`REWRITTEN_TAIL`, on every runtime. Pinned by
`tests/test_launcher_double_dash.py`.

`scripts/host-finalize.sh` (sourced by the launcher before its first verb)
defines two functions.
`_repo_git_from_root REPO ARGS...` runs `git --git-dir=<abs git dir>
--work-tree=REPO ARGS` in a `cd /` subshell, for `ls-remote`,
`remote show` and `fetch`. `_repo_git_push REPO ARGS...` does the same for
every `push`, with `-c core.hooksPath=scripts/push-hooks` (leerie's own
hooks directory, `_HOST_FINALIZE_PUSH_HOOKS`). Its two hooks, `pre-push`
and `reference-transaction`, are one script of shell builtins. Each changes
into `LEERIE_HOOK_WORK_TREE` (`rev-parse --show-toplevel` of REPO), puts
back the operator's `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS` (`LEERIE_HOOK_GCP_SET`,
`LEERIE_HOOK_GCP`), unsets its own variables and execs the operator's hook
of the same name in `LEERIE_HOOKS_DIR` (`_host_finalize_hooks_dir`:
`core.hooksPath`, relative to the top of the work tree, else
`rev-parse --git-path hooks`) with git's arguments and stdin; with no such
executable hook it exits 0. `_host_finalize_pre_push_hook_present` tests
for an executable `pre-push` in that same directory. Every host `fetch`
and `pull` carries `--no-recurse-submodules`: `_repo_git_from_root`'s, the
bring-back, the rebaser repository's and the scratch-ref and PR-base
fetches in `host-finalize.sh`, the bundle fetch of `fetch-branch.sh` and
`ec2-fetch-branch.sh`, the chain's `git fetch origin`, the launcher's
update check and `install.sh`. `gh pr create` runs in a `cd /` subshell
with `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`. The Fly and EC2 seeds list submodules with
`_seed_submodule_dirs` (`scripts/remote/seed-common.sh`, a `foreach` body
that only `printf`s `<displaypath>\0<dir>\0`). Each loop reads the list
from a pipe with `IFS= read -r -d ''`, under `pipefail`, and bundles each
submodule with `git -C` from its own directory. Each bundle is named
`_seed_bundle_name <displaypath>`: the hex of the path's bytes
(`od -An -v -tx1 | tr -d ' \n'`) and `.bundle`. The machine-side scripts
compute the same name with the same pipeline, in the snippet
`_seed_machine_submodules <subs-dir>` prints (`seed-common.sh`), which
all three machine scripts (the Fly seed, the Fly inspect-dir seed, the
EC2 seed) embed and run under `bash`. It reads `git config -z --file
.gitmodules --get-regexp '^submodule\..*\.path$'` with `read -r -d ""`,
and for each submodule whose bundle `<subs-dir>/<hex of prefix+path>.bundle`
exists sets `submodule.<name>.url` to it, runs `git --literal-pathspecs
-c protocol.file.allow=always submodule update --init -- <path>`, and
recurses inside it with `<prefix><path>/`. A submodule without a bundle
stays uninitialised. `.claude` is found with
`find "$USER_REPO/.claude"`. `chain/git_ops.py`'s `_run` starts git from
`/`: with `-C` for a local command, and with the git directory and work
tree for `fetch`, `push`, `ls-remote` and `pull`.

The host-side workers start `claude` outside every checkout and tree.
`config --chat` resolves `claude` with `command -v` from `/` (a relative
result is anchored at `/`), makes a `mktemp -d` directory, refuses one
beneath the checkout, and runs the CLI there with `--add-dir $USER_REPO`
and the checkout's path in its first message. It removes the directory
afterwards and exits with the CLI's status. `run_rebaser` runs its
`claude_p` with `cwd=_host_worker_cwd(repo_root, worktree)` and
`add_dirs=[worktree]`, and names the worktree in the prompt.
Every host-seam `claude_p` (`HOST_SEAM_CAP`: the rebaser and host
recapture) adds `HOST_CLI_ARGS` (`--setting-sources user
--disable-slash-commands --strict-mcp-config`, through
`_host_cli_extra_args(cmd)`, which omits the shared builder's
`--strict-mcp-config` and raises `RuntimeError` if `DISALLOWED_TOOLS` stops
denying any of `HOST_CLI_DENIED_TOOLS` = `Agent`, `Task`, `Skill`). Its
`--settings` is `_host_cli_settings(hook_settings)`: the hook settings with
`HOST_CLI_ENV_PIN` (`CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD=0`) merged
over its `env`, and the same pin goes into `env_extra`. `config --chat`
passes the same flags (DESIGN §6 *The host never runs a program the
checkout chose*, part 4; `tests/test_host_cli_loads_nothing_from_the_tree.py`).
`_host_worker_cwd(*trees) -> Path` makes a fresh `tempfile.mkdtemp`
directory (0700) and raises `OSError` when it is one of `trees` or beneath
one; `run_rebaser` removes it after the call. Its own git
(`rev-parse HEAD`, `check_rebaser_worktree_state` and its helpers) runs
with `cwd="/"`. `_invoke` starts an unconfined command (`grants=None`, the
host-side seam) by `_exe_from_root(cmd[0])`: the absolute path PATH finds
from `/`, with relative and empty entries anchored at `/`. Pinned by
`tests/test_host_python_is_isolated.py`. It covers review round 26 I2's
proof, inverted (an asdf-shaped shim of shell builtins and absolute paths
reading `.tool-versions` from its working directory up). It also checks
that a bounded list of shimmed programs is never started inside the
checkout by `--help`, `version`, `config` and `list`, that the prologue
has its shape, that relative paths still resolve, that `ls-remote` starts
`ssh` outside the checkout (with the `-C` control), that the static rule
on `cd` and `foreach` bodies holds, that every host `fetch` and `pull`
carries `--no-recurse-submodules` (a static rule with its planted control,
and the shipped scratch-ref fetch, inverted from review round 27 I5's
proof), that `config --chat` starts its CLI outside the checkout, and that
`chain/git_ops.py` behaves as above. Review round 27's other host proofs,
inverted: `tests/test_host_worker_starts_outside_the_tree.py` (I1, the real
`run_rebaser` with an asdf-shaped `claude` shim and a plant in the run
branch), `tests/test_host_push_starts_only_the_hook_in_the_checkout.py`
(I5, a hooked push starts `ssh` in `/`, and the operator's hook keeps its
working directory, arguments, stdin, environment and veto) and
`tests/test_seed_submodule_list_is_nul_delimited.py` (I4, a submodule path
holding a newline and a tab lists no other repository, and every bundle
name is hex on both sides).

The orchestrator's
source is baked into the image at `/opt/leerie-image/`; on local runs
the launcher mounts its launch's own copy over it
(`-v $_code_dir:/opt/leerie-image:ro`, `_snapshot_leerie_code`, §0.5
*Baked source*), so iterating on `orchestrator/leerie.py` needs no image
rebuild, and an edit or upgrade of the install never reaches a running
run (DESIGN §6 *A launch runs only the leerie code it started with*).

The orchestrator prefers stdlib. Third-party runtime libraries are
permitted only when they replace non-trivial logic with a widely-used
implementation, earn their distribution cost, and are documented here.
Pins live in `requirements.txt`, installed once per image build
(`pip3 install --break-system-packages --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt`).
No `pyproject.toml`, no PyPI release.

Current runtime deps:

- `tenacity` — exponential backoff for transient `claude -p` auth/rate-limit
  errors (§3 *Auth/quota backoff*).
- `tree-sitter` + `tree-sitter-language-pack` — parser core and prebuilt
  grammars (Python, TypeScript, JavaScript, Ruby, Go, Rust, …) powering the
  P6 repo-map (`_build_repo_map`, DESIGN §5½). Prebuilt manylinux wheels,
  no C build needed.
- `boto3` / `botocore` — AWS SDK for the `--runtime ec2` path, needed for
  AWS's credential-resolution chain (env → shared config/creds → SSO →
  instance profile/IMDS). Available only **inside the container image**
  — the host has no pip/venv surface at all, so every host-side EC2 API
  call instead shells out to the **`aws` CLI** via `ec2-provision.sh` /
  `ec2-ssm.sh` / `ec2-ami.sh` / `ec2-defaults.sh` / `ec2-cleanup.sh` (mirroring
  how the Fly path shells out to `flyctl` rather than importing a Go SDK).
  The new image, key-pair, security-group, subnet, snapshot and IAM calls
  obey the same boundary: `aws` CLI, parsed with python3, never boto3. `boto3`/`botocore` are reserved for future
  in-container AWS calls; none exist yet.

`pytest` remains the sole dev dependency, run on the host against the
bind-mounted source, with two of its plugins: `pytest-xdist` (CI runs the
suite `-n 4`; every test is xdist-safe, and `tests/conftest.py` checks
session-wide leaks from the controlling process only) and `pytest-timeout`
(CI bounds each test with `--timeout`, so a hang fails one named test rather
than the whole job). Neither is named in `pytest.ini`: under
`--strict-config` an option a plugin owns is an error where the plugin is
missing, so a host without them still runs the suite, serially and
unbounded. CI also installs `pytest-cov` and `jsonschema`.

### Path A — Claude Code plugin marketplace (primary)

```
/plugin marketplace add enricai/leerie
/plugin install leerie@enricai-leerie
# then inside Claude Code:
/leerie "task description"
```

`marketplace.json` exposes one plugin (the existing `plugin.json`).
Claude Code clones the repo into its plugin directory and registers the
`commands/` and `skills/` entries. `/leerie` then runs the plugin
skill at `commands/leerie.md`, which shells out to the on-disk
`leerie` launcher in the cloned plugin directory — and through it,
to `nerdctl run`. See §0.5 for the launcher's per-mode (terminal vs
plugin) TTY adaptation.

### Path B — `curl | bash` installer (secondary)

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/enricai/leerie/main/scripts/install.sh | bash
```

The script:

1. **Preflight**: verifies `git`/`curl` on `PATH`. Auto-installs `claude` if
   missing via Anthropic's native installer (opt out: `--no-claude-install` /
   `LEERIE_NO_CLAUDE_INSTALL=1`) — a hard stop otherwise, since leerie shells
   out to `claude -p` for all LLM work.
2. **Runtime install**: per `uname -s`. macOS installs Colima via brew and
   starts the VM; Debian/Ubuntu installs and starts the full **rootless**
   containerd stack (containerd, rootlesskit/slirp4netns/uidmap, nerdctl, CNI,
   BuildKit) and verifies reachability via `nerdctl info`; Fedora/RHEL and
   Arch print a hint to `docs/INSTALL.md` and exit non-zero. Opt out entirely
   with `--no-runtime-install` / `LEERIE_NO_RUNTIME_INSTALL=1`.
3. **Clones** `enricai/leerie` to `$LEERIE_HOME` (default `~/.leerie`) —
   shallow for fresh installs, `git pull --ff-only` for upgrades.
4. **Symlinks** `$LEERIE_HOME/leerie` → `~/.local/bin/leerie`.
5. **PATH check**: prints the shell-rc line to add if `~/.local/bin` is
   missing from `$PATH` (never edits it silently).
6. **Verifies** via `leerie version` (fast path, no container startup).

Supports `--dry-run` (prints actions without executing), `--prefix DIR`
(overrides `LEERIE_HOME`), `--no-runtime-install`
(`LEERIE_NO_RUNTIME_INSTALL=1`), and `--no-claude-install`
(`LEERIE_NO_CLAUDE_INSTALL=1`).

### `version`

`leerie version` reads `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`'s `version`
field — single source of truth. Two parallel readers:

- **Orchestrator** (`_read_version()` in `leerie.py`): stdlib `json` load.
  Exercised by `tests/test_version_flag.py`.
- **Launcher** (bash `awk` extraction): used by the fast path that
  short-circuits container startup. Both readers return the same value
  on the same `plugin.json`, and `tests/test_version_flag.py` guards
  the canonical surface.

`install.sh` uses `leerie version` as its end-to-end smoke test — and
because the fast path doesn't require a running container, the smoke
test runs the moment the symlink is in place.

### Stale-install warning

The installed checkout at `$LEERIE_REPO` is never updated by running
`leerie`; only re-running `install.sh` (or a manual `git pull`) advances it,
so an install can sit arbitrarily far behind `origin` while the operator
believes they're running current code.

`_warn_if_leerie_stale()` runs in the host preflight and **warns, never
blocks**:

- Skips silently when `$LEERIE_REPO` isn't a git checkout, HEAD is detached,
  or the branch has no upstream.
- Compares `git rev-list --count HEAD..@{upstream}`; on non-zero, reports
  both `plugin.json` versions (local and upstream) plus the update command.
- Fetches at most once per 24h (gated by an mtime stamp file, `timeout 5`,
  backgrounded, non-fatal) since a never-fetched checkout's cached
  remote-tracking ref is otherwise as stale as the checkout itself.
- Every git call is `|| true`-guarded — offline/slow-network must never
  fail a run.

### In-repo tee-log warning (N5)

Operators commonly run `leerie task | tee leerie-<task>.log`, and the log
lands in `$USER_REPO` by default — which is bind-mounted whole into every
worker's container at `/work`. A worker can then `cat`/`grep` its own
orchestration log, including gate vocabulary and internal check names,
defeating judge independence.

`_warn_if_log_in_repo()` runs immediately after the stale-install warning,
before host preflight. It globs `"$USER_REPO"/leerie-*.log`, and for each
match logs a warning naming the file plus the bind-mount risk. **Detection
and warning only** — it never blocks the run; relocating the default log
destination and teeing the launcher's own output there is `--log-file`
(N5b), documented below.

Mirrors `_warn_if_leerie_stale()`'s detection-and-warn shape and is tested
the same way (`tests/test_log_in_repo_warning.py`, extracting the function
verbatim from the launcher).

---

### `config`

Launcher bash case arm: `config)`. `leerie config` is a host-only fast
path — it exits before `nerdctl run` and never starts a container. It is
listed alongside `version` in the ownership-guard skip-list so it never
claims a state directory. Four sub-modes:

- **bare (`leerie config`)**: prints effective build/lint/test config for
  `$USER_REPO` with `[config]` / `[inference]` provenance per axis (reads
  `.leerie/config.toml` if present, otherwise infers). Also prints any
  non-comment `key = value` lines from `leerie.toml` when that file exists.
- **`leerie config --init`**: creates `.leerie/` and writes
  `.leerie/config.toml` with auto-detected BLT values (uncommented) and a
  commented `setup_packages` example. Refuses with exit 1 if `config.toml`
  already exists. Prints the path and suggests `git add .leerie/`.
- **`leerie config --chat`**: runs interactive `claude` (NOT `claude -p`)
  with `--system-prompt-file $LEERIE_REPO/prompts/config_chat.md` and
  `--add-dir $USER_REPO`, from a temporary directory of its own (§0, *The
  host never runs a program the checkout chose*). It also passes the
  host-CLI containment: `--setting-sources user --disable-slash-commands
  --strict-mcp-config --disallowedTools Agent,Task,Skill --settings
  '{"env":{"CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD":"0"}}'`, with that
  variable unset in its environment. The first message follows `--`,
  because `--add-dir` takes every word up to the next option. No container started.
  Exits 1 if `prompts/config_chat.md` is missing or `claude` is not on
  PATH; otherwise exits with the session's status.
- **`leerie config --recapture [--force]`**: host-only. Calls
  `run_recapture_deps()`, which consolidates across all finished runs with
  `logs/` under the state dir (or just `--run-id` if given). Without
  `--force`, runs already carrying a `dep_capture.done` sentinel are skipped
  and the write is a never-clobber **union**. `--force` drops the sentinel
  and switches to a wholesale **replace** (`capture_repo_deps(replace=True)`)
  — an empty capture leaves the config untouched. Each run's `State` is
  flocked (skipped, not fatal, on `StateLockedError`). Exits 1 if no runs
  directory or no finished run found. `orchestrator/leerie.py`'s sole
  third-party import on this path (`tenacity`) is deferred into `claude_p()`
  rather than module scope, since the host `python3` isn't guaranteed to
  have `requirements.txt` deps (§0). The seam runs `python3 -I` and calls
  `admit_operator_import_paths([checkout])` after loading the module, so a `tenacity`
  in the operator's user site or on an absolute `PYTHONPATH` entry is found
  (§0 *Python runtime*).

All four sub-modes share an inline BLT inferrer (`_config_read_key`,
`_infer_axis`, `_axis_source`) implemented directly in launcher bash so the
verb needs no container or orchestrator import. `_infer_axis` is a
deterministic file table of its own: a starting file for the operator to
edit, host-side where no worker runs. A run does not use it (a run reads an
undeclared axis from the repository, `_discover_blt`), so there is no
parity with the orchestrator to guard. `tests/test_config_verb.py` runs
per-mode unit tests against a self-contained bash harness.

Maps to `DESIGN.md`: §6½ *Declared BLT commands* (the `.leerie/config.toml`
format and resolution); §6½ *Per-repo container image* (`setup_packages`,
`prompts/config_chat.md` for the interactive session).

---

## 0.5. Container shape

Leerie runs entirely inside a single container per run (DESIGN §6 *Worker
subtree termination*). The orchestrator is PID 1 in the container;
every `claude -p` worker it spawns is a child process in the same PID
namespace; every Bash tool call those workers make lands in the same
namespace too. When PID 1 exits, the kernel reaps the namespace —
which is the abnormal-exit cleanup guarantee.

### Runtime requirements per OS

| OS | Container engine | CLI | VM? |
|----|------------------|-----|-----|
| macOS (arm64 or x86_64) | containerd inside a Colima-managed Linux VM | `nerdctl` host-side shim (`colima nerdctl install`) | Yes — managed by Colima |
| Linux (Debian/Ubuntu) | rootless containerd (native) | `nerdctl` from upstream (+ CNI/BuildKit/RootlessKit) | No |
| Linux (Fedora/RHEL, Arch) | rootless containerd (manual) | `nerdctl` — set up by hand per `docs/INSTALL.md` | No |

The launcher detects `uname -s` and runs the right preflight. macOS:
requires `colima` on `PATH`, checks `colima status`, auto-installs the
`nerdctl` shim if missing, then checks `nerdctl info`. Linux: if `nerdctl`
is missing and auto-install isn't opted out, `runtime_install_linux`
(`scripts/runtime-install.sh`) stands up the full rootless stack on
**Debian/Ubuntu** (containerd + rootless prerequisites via apt, nerdctl/CNI/
BuildKit, the rootless setuptool) and verifies `nerdctl info`. Before the
setuptool first starts containerd, `_runtime_linux_containerd_config` writes
`${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/containerd/config.toml` as `version = 2`
and `[plugins."io.containerd.metadata.v1.bolt"]` `content_sharing_policy =
"isolated"` when no file is there (nothing under `--dry-run`; an existing
file is never edited; DESIGN §6 *The content store*). **Fedora/RHEL
and Arch** aren't auto-installed yet — the launcher prints a hint to
`docs/INSTALL.md` "Rootless mode" and exits non-zero. Pass
`--no-runtime-install` (`LEERIE_NO_RUNTIME_INSTALL=1`) to skip the
Debian/Ubuntu auto-install and fall back to the hint.

`brew install nerdctl` does NOT work on macOS — the Homebrew formula
has `Requires: Linux` because the nerdctl binary talks directly to a
containerd Unix socket. Colima's `colima nerdctl install` is the
supported macOS path; it drops a host-side shim on `$PATH` that
proxies every invocation to nerdctl inside the VM.

### Image build

`Dockerfile` at the repo root. Built locally on first run
(`nerdctl --namespace leerie image inspect "$IMAGE_TAG"` miss → `nerdctl --namespace leerie build`; the namespace `LEERIE_IMAGE_NS`, §0.5 per-repo image table).
`IMAGE_TAG=leerie:<VERSION>` so a leerie upgrade triggers a fresh build
once and reuses the layer cache thereafter. The first build took 18
minutes on a fresh host (measured 2026-11-03); subsequent runs < 3s.

Base layers (top-down):

- `debian:13-slim` — minimal, predictable, glibc-based.
- `apt-get install`: `ca-certificates`, `curl`, `git`, `openssh-client`,
  `python3`, `python3-pip`, `python-is-python3` (a system `python`, which
  an unpinned mise `python` shim falls through to; without it a bare
  `python` fails with "No version is set for shim: python"),
  `build-essential`, plus dev libraries
  (`zlib1g-dev`, `libyaml-dev`, `libreadline-dev`, `libffi-dev`,
  `libssl-dev`, `libpq-dev`, `libsqlite3-dev`, `libgdbm-dev`,
  `default-libmysqlclient-dev`) covering native-extension compilation:
  `node-gyp` (sharp, bcrypt), Ruby C gems (`nokogiri`, `pg`, `sqlite3`,
  `mysql2`, `ffi`), Python C extensions.
- `libc6` + `chromium` + `chromium-driver` + `fonts-liberation` — headless
  Chrome for browser-based testing, installed from Debian's own repos so
  browser/chromedriver stay in sync (Selenium Manager has nothing to
  download at runtime). `libc6` is upgraded in the same transaction since a
  lagging base-image glibc otherwise makes chromium fail with
  `undefined symbol: localtime64_r`. `/home/leerie/.cache/selenium` is
  pre-created (chowned to `leerie` at runtime). Workers run as non-root
  `leerie`, so Chrome's SUID sandbox is disabled via baked flags in
  `/etc/chromium.d/leerie-container-flags`.
- `postgresql-common` (its `/etc/postgresql-common/createcluster.conf` set
  to `create_main_cluster = false`, checked by `grep -qx`) then
  `postgresql` — the server binaries `scripts/sandbox-db.sh` starts a
  command's private cluster from (DESIGN §6½ *A database server in the base
  image*); the step fails unless the newest `/usr/lib/postgresql/<major>/bin`
  has an executable `initdb`. No cluster in the image, nothing chowned
  (rootless, rootful and Fly/EC2 alike: `initdb` writes only the confined
  command's own `/tmp`).
- `/etc/mise/config.toml` written by `scripts/mise-system-config.sh`
  (copied to `/usr/local/lib/leerie/`): `[settings]
  idiomatic_version_file_enable_tools` = every tool whose first backend in
  `mise registry` is `core:` (13 on mise 2026.5.4: bun, deno, dotnet,
  elixir, erlang, go, java, node, python, ruby, rust, swift, zig); the
  script fails the build when the list lacks `node`. No
  `MISE_IDIOMATIC_VERSION_FILE_ENABLE_TOOLS` ENV (DESIGN §6½ *A
  repository's runtimes are the ones mise discovers*).
- LTS Node baked via `mise install --system node@lts` (leerie's own: the
  `claude` CLI is installed with it), with a stable
  `.../installs/node/lts-current` symlink so `ENV PATH` doesn't need the
  concrete version. It is the fallback Node mise's resolver uses when a
  repo declares none of its own (DESIGN §6½). No other runtime is baked.
- corepack's shims for the baked LTS Node made at build by
  `<lts>/bin/corepack enable --install-directory <lts>/bin` (in the
  `lts-current` step), with mise's implicit enable off
  (`MISE_NODE_COREPACK=false`): mise's enable writes next to the first
  `corepack` on `PATH`, the baked Node's, whatever version it installed
  (DESIGN §6 *Each Node version's corepack shims go in its own `bin`*). A
  repo's `package.json` `packageManager` field still selects its own
  pnpm/yarn (no globally pinned pnpm baked). `npm install -g
  '@anthropic-ai/claude-code@>=2.1.289'` installs the `claude` CLI
  (leerie enforces ≥2.1.22 at runtime for `--json-schema`, and ≥2.1.289
  only under `--dangerously-force-strict-output` — §2½ *Forced constrained
  decoding*; the image pin covers both that and the ≥2.1.219 `claude -p`
  mid-stream-drop fix — §3 "Transient transport disconnect").
- A pinned JS-API `typescript` (`ARG BUNDLED_TYPESCRIPT_VERSION=5.9.3`,
  the registry tarball fetched with `curl` and checked against its npm
  `dist.integrity` sha512 before extraction) at
  `/opt/leerie-vendor/node_modules/typescript` — `BUNDLED_TYPESCRIPT` in
  `leerie.py`, the fallback `scripts/load-typescript.cjs` loads when the
  tree's own `typescript` has no compiler API (DESIGN §8 *Delivery
  detection*). Outside `/opt/leerie-image` because local runs mount the
  launch's copy of leerie's code over that path. Root-owned and world-readable (`a+rX`), read-only by
  every runtime: rootless (root-owned is readable to the remapped user),
  rootful `runuser -u leerie` and Fly/EC2 only ever read it, so no chown
  applies.
- `ENV PATH` order is load-bearing: `/opt/leerie-vendor/bin` :
  `<MISE_DATA_DIR/shims>` : `<LTS Node bin>` : `$PATH` :
  `/home/leerie/.local/bin` (DESIGN §6½ *A repository's pinned runtime is
  the one its commands run*). `/opt/leerie-vendor/bin` holds one entry, the
  `claude` link to `<LTS Node bin>/claude` made in the CLI's install step
  (`ec2-bake.sh` makes the same link), so the worker CLI never resolves
  through a mise shim. `MISE_DATA_DIR/shims` comes next, ahead of every
  concrete install's `bin`, so bare `node`/`npm`/`pnpm`/`corepack`/`python3`
  are the version the caller's cwd pins; the LTS Node's `bin` follows as the
  unpinned fallback (and the only `node` before any `mise reshim` in a fresh
  `MISE_DATA_DIR`). No `/usr/local/share/mise/shims` entry: `mise install
  --system` makes no such directory. A tool a setup hook puts in
  `/home/leerie/.local/bin` comes last, so it can never shadow a baked-in
  binary. Pinned by
  `tests/test_dockerfile_path.py` and `tests/test_pinned_runtime_runs.py`
  (whose real-container test, opt-in through
  `LEERIE_TEST_CONTAINER_IMAGE`, runs `_run_mise_install` and confined
  measurements on that image with this checkout's PATH).
- Non-root `leerie` user created with `--build-arg HOST_UID/HOST_GID`
  matching the host user, so container writes into `/work` and
  `/leerie-state` keep the host user's ownership.
- `git config --system --add safe.directory '*'` (in `/etc/gitconfig`):
  the container is single-tenant with `/work` its only repo, so
  blanket-allow is the standard mitigation for Colima/virtiofs presenting
  a mismatched gid that would otherwise trip git's CVE-2022-24765 check on
  worker `git -C <worktree-subdir> ...` calls.
- `WORKDIR /work`, `ENTRYPOINT ["/opt/leerie-image/scripts/container-entry.sh"]`.
  **No `USER leerie` directive** — ENTRYPOINT runs as PID 1 at the
  slice-owning identity so it can create `/sys/fs/cgroup/leerie.slice` and
  start the **cgroup broker** in the exec that drops privilege via `runuser
  -u leerie -- ...` (skipped in rootless mode — DESIGN §6 *Rootless
  exception*). See DESIGN §6 *Memory containment* for the full mechanism.

### Per-repo derived image (local nerdctl)

After the base image is confirmed present, the launcher decides the
repository image's Dockerfile (DESIGN §6½ *Per-repo container image*, *A
generated Dockerfile is leerie's output, never the repository's*). It reads
the first line of the checkout's `.leerie/Dockerfile` (`IFS= read -r -n 256`;
a link there was refused at the start, `_checkout_config_links`):

- absent: generate (below);
- not `LEERIE_GENERATED_SENTINEL` (`# leerie-generated: do not edit
  (regenerated from .leerie/config.toml)`): the repository's own,
  `_REPO_DF_OWN=true`, nothing generated; when `.leerie/config.toml`'s
  `setup_packages` is non-empty, logs `note: the repository's own
  .leerie/Dockerfile is built as written; .leerie/config.toml's
  setup_packages is not read while it is there`;
- the sentinel, and `_checkout_file_tracked ".leerie/Dockerfile"` holds
  (committed, or a submodule's): `remote_log "error: .leerie/Dockerfile is
  committed, and its first line is leerie's mark …"`, naming `git rm
  .leerie/Dockerfile` and deleting the first line as the two ways out, and
  `exit 1`, before any build;
- the sentinel, untracked: a `warning:` that the file is one an earlier
  leerie generated, is not read and can be removed; generate.

Generation runs only when `.leerie/config.toml` exists and
`_leerie_should_generate_dockerfile` holds. It writes
`$_REPO_BUILD_DIR/generated.Dockerfile` (`_repo_build_dir` first; never a
path in the checkout), sentinel first, and keeps its bytes in
`$_REPO_DF_GEN` (empty when nothing was generated), which outlives the
build directory: `_repo_image_prepare` writes it back on each call, for the
local build and for Fly (`_set_fly_per_repo_image`). The build block runs
when `$_REPO_DF_OWN` is `true` or `$_REPO_DF_GEN` is non-empty. The
launcher writes nothing under the checkout's `.leerie/`. The relevant bash
surface:

| Function / variable | Location in `leerie` | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `_leerie_repo_id` | after base-build block | Sanitized repo identifier from `git remote get-url origin` (or `basename $USER_REPO` fallback); lowercase, `[a-z0-9._-]` only, `/` → `-` |
| `_leerie_checkout_id` | after base-build block | 12 hex characters of the sha256 of `$USER_REPO` (the path `.owner` records), computed with `python3 -I` |
| `_repo_image_digest <tag>` | after base-build block | The digest of the image `<tag>` names: `nerdctl --namespace $LEERIE_IMAGE_NS image inspect -f '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}'` after its `@` (`sha256:<hex>`, which `nerdctl run` takes); empty when the tag names no image |
| `resolve_repo_image_tag()` | after base-build block | Returns `leerie-repo/<repo-id>-<checkout-id>:<LEERIE_VERSION>` (`_leerie_repo_id`, `_leerie_checkout_id`) when a Dockerfile is present (real or to-be-auto-generated), empty string otherwise. Two checkouts whose `<repo-id>` collide never share a name |
| `LEERIE_IMAGE_NS` | `scripts/dockerfile-frontend.sh` | `"leerie"`: the containerd namespace leerie keeps its images in and runs its containers in, which no BuildKit worker may read (DESIGN §6 *No build consumes what another build left in BuildKit*). Every `nerdctl` command the launcher runs on its images or containers names it (`--namespace "$LEERIE_IMAGE_NS"`): the base build and its `image inspect`, `_repo_image_digest`, `_check_repo_image`, both builds of `build_repo_image`, the `.dockerfile-hash` base id, `nerdctl run` (all three forms), `_kill_container_from_cidfile`, `_remove_launch_container`, `_reap_dead_launch_containers`' `ps`, `inspect` and `rm`, `leerie_reap_old_images`' `images` and `image rm` (through its `$_ns`, which is `$LEERIE_IMAGE_NS` except with `worker`); and `build-push.sh --local-build`'s build, inspect, smoke run and push with nerdctl. A command on a run's container by its id (`_is_local_container`, `_reap_orphaned_container`, `stop`, `kill`, prune's liveness probe) uses `_container_ns` |
| `_container_ns <run-id>` | before `_reap_orphaned_container` | Prints the first of `$LEERIE_IMAGE_NS` and `default` in which `nerdctl --namespace <ns> inspect <run-id>` succeeds (`default`: a run an earlier leerie launched); returns 1, printing nothing, when neither does. `_is_local_container` is `_container_ns` succeeding; `_reap_orphaned_container` inspects and kills in its namespace; `stop`/`kill` use it, else `$LEERIE_IMAGE_NS`. The reaper, `stop` and `kill` follow their `kill`/`stop` with `nerdctl --namespace <ns> rm -f <run-id>`: `--rm` is the client's, and a dead client's container would stay `Exited`, holding its image. `prune`'s Python liveness probe tries the same two (`LEERIE_PRUNE_CONTAINER_NS="$LEERIE_IMAGE_NS default"`) |
| `leerie_buildkit_resolve` | `scripts/dockerfile-frontend.sh` | Finds the BuildKit daemon `nerdctl --namespace $LEERIE_IMAGE_NS build` uses, as nerdctl 2.3.5 finds it: `$BUILDKIT_HOST`, else the first of `unix://<dir>/buildkit-$LEERIE_IMAGE_NS/buildkitd.sock`, `…/buildkit-default/…` and `…/buildkit/…` (`<dir>` = `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, or `/run/user/<uid>` when unset; `/run` as root and on Darwin) for which `buildctl --addr <a> debug workers --format '{{json .}}'` succeeds (its stdout and stderr together; the first line that parses as JSON is the workers' list) — run through `_leerie_on_buildkit_side`, which on Darwin is `colima ssh -- sudo …` (not measured on macOS). Sets `LEERIE_BUILDKIT_HOST` to it and `LEERIE_BUILDKIT_WORKER_NS` to the space-separated, de-duplicated `org.mobyproject.buildkit.worker.containerd.namespace` labels of its workers (host `python3 -I -S`); returns 1 when no daemon answers, or the first that answers has no such label or one that is not a containerd namespace name (`[A-Za-z0-9]+([._-][A-Za-z0-9]+)*`), with why in `LEERIE_BUILDKIT_RESOLVE_ERROR`: the addresses asked, buildctl's last line of output, and the remedy (start buildkitd, or set `BUILDKIT_HOST`), or which daemon answered without a usable containerd worker. A set `LEERIE_BUILDKIT_HOST` returns 0 at once |
| `leerie_buildkit_check` | `scripts/dockerfile-frontend.sh` | Returns 1, with the reason in `LEERIE_BUILDKIT_REFUSAL` (holding `LEERIE_BUILDKIT_RESOLVE_ERROR`), when `leerie_buildkit_resolve` fails or a namespace in `LEERIE_BUILDKIT_WORKER_NS` is `$LEERIE_IMAGE_NS`; else 0. Called before a repository build (the launcher, with `leerie_sweep_worker_images`), at the top of `build_repo_image` (`_repo_build_fail` on 1), and before `build-push.sh --local-build`'s nerdctl build (exit 1) |
| `leerie_sweep_worker_images` | `scripts/dockerfile-frontend.sh` | For each namespace in `LEERIE_BUILDKIT_WORKER_NS`: lists `nerdctl --namespace <ns> images --format '{{.Repository}}:{{.Tag}}'`, runs `nerdctl --namespace <ns> image rm <name>` (never `-f`) on each name matching `leerie-repo/*` or `docker.io/leerie-repo/*`, lists again, and returns 1 with the reason in `LEERIE_BUILDKIT_REFUSAL` when a listing fails, or naming what is left and each container that holds it (`nerdctl --namespace <ns> ps -a --format '{{.ID}}|{{.Image}}|{{.Status}}'`, its image the name, with or without `docker.io/`), with its status and remedy: `Up…` → end its run (`leerie stop <run-id>`) or let it end; otherwise → `nerdctl --namespace <ns> rm <id>`. No `image rm` advice. Called after `leerie_buildkit_check`, before a repository build: by the launcher (`_repo_build_fail` on 1) and by `build-push.sh --local-build` with nerdctl (exit 1) |
| `check_command_line(argv, state_root=None)` | `orchestrator/leerie.py` | `_parse_command_line(_leerie_arg_parser(), argv)`, then 0; argparse exits 2 with its usage and message on a line it refuses. When the line is `resume` naming a run (positional or `--run-id`) and `state_root` is given, the check also runs `resolve_run_id(Path(state_root), <run-id>, resumable_only=True)`, which `die()`s (status 1) with `run-id … does not match any known run. Available: …` when no run under `<state_root>/runs/` has that ID. The launcher passes `$LEERIE_STATE_HOST_DIR` as `state_root` only when `RUNTIME=local` (an empty argument otherwise, read as None), and the program calls `check(sys.argv[4:], state_root=sys.argv[3] or None)`. `_leerie_arg_parser()` builds `main()`'s parser and nothing else; `_parse_command_line(ap, argv)` pops `resume`/`list` and `resume`'s positional run-id (`_extract_resume_run_id`) and returns `(args, run_id, is_resume, is_list)`, which `main()` uses too. The launcher runs it after the `--inspect-dir` translation and the `REWRITTEN_ARGS` pass (moved, with the `skip_repo_map` resolution, ahead of the base build) and before the base build: `python3 -I -S -B -c` on `$_code_snapshot/orchestrator/leerie.py` (the launch's snapshot, `_snapshot_leerie_code`), with the state-root argument, then `REWRITTEN_ARGS` and `REWRITTEN_TAIL`; `exit $?` on a non-zero status; an exception loading the module exits 0 (DESIGN §6 *A command line is refused before any image step*). The program reads the module's bytes, and loads the code object kept at `$HOME/.cache/leerie/bytecode/<sha256(importlib.util.MAGIC_NUMBER + source)>` (`marshal`; the entry's mtime touched); a missing or unreadable entry is compiled (`compile(data, src, "exec", dont_inherit=True)`) and written there (directory 0700, a `.<pid>.tmp` file `os.replace`d), and every other entry but the three most recently used is removed. The code runs in a `types.ModuleType("leerie_orch")` with `__file__` the source path, registered in `sys.modules` |
| `leerie_lock <file> <what> [mode]` | `scripts/dockerfile-frontend.sh` | Takes an exclusive lock on `<file>` (`mkdir -p` of its directory) and returns once it is held, the holder's PID in `LEERIE_LOCK_HOLDER`; returns 0 with no lock and an empty holder when `<file>` is empty. `[mode]`: empty, exclusive; `shared`, `LOCK_SH` instead of `LOCK_EX`; `try`, exclusive, the holder exiting at the first `BlockingIOError` (so `leerie_lock` returns 1 at once) and nothing logged. The holder is `python3 -I -S -c "$_LEERIE_LOCK_PY" <file> <ready> $$ <mode>`, backgrounded with no stdio: `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX \| LOCK_NB)` (`LOCK_SH` for `shared`) every 0.2 s until held, exiting if the launcher (`$$`) is gone; then writes `<file>.ready.$$.$RANDOM`, which the shell polls every 0.1 s (logging "waiting for `<what>`..." once, after 2 s; returns 1 if the holder dies first) and removes; then exits within 0.5 s of the launcher's end, or at SIGTERM (status 0). No descriptor of the shell's holds the lock (DESIGN §6 *A host-wide image step runs once, under a host lock*) |
| `_leerie_version_older <a> <b>` | `scripts/dockerfile-frontend.sh` | Returns 0 when both match `^[0-9]{1,9}([.][0-9]{1,9})*$` and `<a>` is less than `<b>` comparing part by part as decimal numbers (a missing part is 0); else 1 |
| `_leerie_own_image <name>` | `scripts/dockerfile-frontend.sh` | Returns 0 when `<name>` with its last `:<tag>` removed is `leerie`, `docker.io/library/leerie`, `leerie-repo/<one or more characters>` or `docker.io/leerie-repo/<…>`; else 1 |
| `_leerie_own_base <name>` | `scripts/dockerfile-frontend.sh` | Returns 0 when `<name>` with its last `:<tag>` removed is `leerie` or `docker.io/library/leerie` (the base's copy, `ensure_base_in_worker_ns`); else 1 |
| `leerie_reap_old_images <hold dir> [worker]` | `scripts/dockerfile-frontend.sh` | Returns 0 at once for an empty `<hold dir>`. Its namespaces: `$LEERIE_IMAGE_NS`; with `worker`, each namespace in `$LEERIE_BUILDKIT_WORKER_NS` other than `$LEERIE_IMAGE_NS`. Lists each with `nerdctl --namespace <ns> images --format '{{.Repository}}:{{.Tag}}\|{{.Size}}'` (a warning when one fails, and that namespace is skipped). Its candidates are the names whose tag (after the last `:`) `_leerie_version_older` than `$LEERIE_VERSION` and that `_leerie_own_image` accepts (in `$LEERIE_IMAGE_NS`) or `_leerie_own_base` accepts (with `worker`). For each candidate tag `<v>`, once across the namespaces: `leerie_lock <hold dir>/<v>.lock "" try`; when that returns 1, logs `kept leerie <v>'s images: a launch of leerie <v> is using them` and removes none of them; else runs `nerdctl --namespace <ns> image rm <name>` (never `-f`, output discarded) on each candidate with that tag, in its own namespace, a success recorded as `<name> (<size>)` (`<name> in <ns> (<size>)` outside `$LEERIE_IMAGE_NS`) and a failure (containerd's refusal of an image a container uses) as kept, then `leerie_unlock`. Logs one line naming every removed name with its listed size (`removed images of older leerie versions: …`) and one naming every kept name (`kept images of older leerie versions a container still uses: …`), each only when not empty. Always returns 0. Never touches another namespace or name; never resolves the worker namespaces itself (DESIGN §6 *An image no launch can use any more is removed by leerie*) |
| the image hold (`# --- hold this version's images; remove older versions'`) | before the base-build block | `RUNTIME=local` only. When `$LEERIE_VERSION` is non-empty and only `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`: `leerie_lock "$_leerie_host_dir/image-holds/$LEERIE_VERSION.lock" "another launch's removal of leerie <v>'s images" shared` (exit 1 with an error when it fails), its holder's PID in `_image_hold_holder` (empty when no hold was taken). Every EXIT trap from there on (the snapshot's, the repository build's, the two `$STAGE` traps and the container arm's) runs `leerie_unlock "${_image_hold_holder:-}" || true` (last, or, in the early `$STAGE` trap, just before its `rm -rf "$STAGE"`), so the holder never outlives the launcher; its own check of the launcher's PID is the backstop for a SIGKILL. Then `leerie_reap_old_images "$_leerie_host_dir/image-holds"`. Both run before the base block's first `image inspect` |
| `leerie_unlock <holder>` | `scripts/dockerfile-frontend.sh` | `kill` and `wait` the holder; nothing for an empty one |
| `_leerie_image_lock` | before the base-build block | `$_leerie_host_dir/image.lock` (the host-wide directory, resolved there now). The base build takes it when `image inspect "$IMAGE_TAG"` fails and inspects again under it, building only when still absent; the per-repo block takes it around `leerie_sweep_worker_images`, `leerie_reap_old_images … worker`, `ensure_base_in_worker_ns` and `ensure_frontend_in_worker_ns` |
| `leerie_containerd_config` | `scripts/dockerfile-frontend.sh` | Prints `/etc/containerd/config.toml` as root, else `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/containerd/config.toml` (rootless containerd's `/etc/containerd`); nothing on Darwin |
| `leerie_content_sharing_check` | `scripts/dockerfile-frontend.sh` | Returns 0 when `leerie_containerd_config` prints nothing or its file has a line matching `^[[:space:]]*content_sharing_policy[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*["']isolated["']`; else 1, with `LEERIE_CONTENT_SHARING_HINT` naming the file, the two lines and the restart (`systemctl --user restart containerd`, `systemctl restart containerd` as root) and that it stops every running container. Called after `leerie_buildkit_check` before a repository build, by the launcher (`remote_log "warning: …"`) and `build-push.sh --local-build` with nerdctl (`build-push: warning: …` on stderr); never a refusal (DESIGN §6 *The content store*) |
| `ensure_base_in_worker_ns` | after base-build block | The base's id, `nerdctl --namespace $LEERIE_IMAGE_NS image inspect -f '{{.Id}}' "$IMAGE_TAG"`; `_repo_build_fail` when it is empty. For each namespace in `LEERIE_BUILDKIT_WORKER_NS` whose `image inspect -f '{{.Id}}' "$IMAGE_TAG"` is not that id (absent, or an older base under the same tag), copies the base there through a file in the launch's build directory (`_repo_build_dir`; `$_REPO_BUILD_DIR/base.tar`): (1) `_base_archive_bytes` sums the base's manifest layers' and configuration's sizes (`image inspect --mode native`), plus `BASE_ARCHIVE_SLACK_BYTES` (1 MiB: the archive's headers, index and manifests); `_free_bytes <dir>` is the free space `df -Pk` reports for the directory; `_repo_build_fail` when either cannot be read or the free space is smaller, naming both. (2) `nerdctl --namespace $LEERIE_IMAGE_NS save -o <file> "$IMAGE_TAG"`, (3) `nerdctl --namespace <ns> load -i <file>`, the file removed after the load whatever it returned; `_repo_build_fail` with nerdctl's own output (`_terminal_safe`) when either fails. (4) The id in `<ns>` read again: `_repo_build_fail` unless it is the base's id. Never streamed (`save | load`): nerdctl 2.3.5's `save` exits before a slow reader has the archive's tail (DESIGN §6 *The base a repository's build reads is where BuildKit reads it, with the base's id, or the launch stops*). No retry. Called before `build_repo_image`, under the host's image lock |
| `ensure_frontend_in_worker_ns` | `scripts/dockerfile-frontend.sh` | Calls `leerie_buildkit_resolve` (a warning and return 0 when it fails), then for each namespace in `LEERIE_BUILDKIT_WORKER_NS` pulls `$LEERIE_DOCKERFILE_FRONTEND` into it (`nerdctl --namespace <ns> pull -q`, with the operator's Docker config) unless `nerdctl --namespace <ns> image inspect` finds it, so the pinned frontend survives a prune of BuildKit's cache and a later build needs no network for it (DESIGN §6 *Residuals*). Best-effort/non-fatal (a warning on failure; BuildKit then resolves the frontend itself). Called before the base build and before `build_repo_image` |
| `leerie_prune_cache_mounts <ns>` | `scripts/dockerfile-frontend.sh` | Returns 1 unless `$LEERIE_BUILDKIT_HOST` and `<ns>` are set; else `_leerie_on_buildkit_side buildctl --addr $LEERIE_BUILDKIT_HOST prune --filter 'type==exec.cachemount,description~="<ns>/"'`, output discarded, its status returned. Called after every build that drew `<ns>`, whatever its status: the base build and both of `build_repo_image`'s (a warning naming `<ns>` on failure), and `build-push.sh --local-build`'s with nerdctl (a warning on failure; not for docker or `--dry-run`) (DESIGN §6 *Residuals*) |
| `leerie_cache_mount_ns` | `scripts/dockerfile-frontend.sh` | Prints `leerie-<32 hex>`, 16 bytes of `/dev/urandom` (`od -An -N16 -tx1`); returns 1, printing nothing, when it did not read 16 bytes. Every build leerie runs is given `--build-arg BUILDKIT_CACHE_MOUNT_NS=<its output>`, a fresh value per build, which the pinned frontend puts in front of every cache mount's id, so no two builds share a mount, even at the same time (DESIGN §6 *No build consumes what another build left in BuildKit*). A caller assigns it to a variable first and fails the build when it returns 1, so no build runs with an empty namespace |
| `_build_job <cmd> [args...]` | after base-build block | Runs `<cmd> <args> 2>&1 \| _terminal_relay >&2` (stdin `/dev/null`) as a background job in a process group of its own (`set -m` around the `&`, `set +m` after), the job's first command `trap '' TTOU TTIN`, which the pipeline inherits (with `stty tostop`, a write to the terminal from a group that is not its foreground one stops the group otherwise); records its PID in `$_BUILD_JOB_PID`, and waits for it with `trap '_build_job_die INT' INT`, `… TERM`, `… HUP` (set before `set -m`) and `trap '_build_job_stop' TSTP` (set after `set +m`, which replaces a TSTP trap) set; the caller's traps for the four, read with `trap -p INT TERM HUP TSTP`, are put back after. `_build_job_die <SIG>` runs `_repo_build_done`, then `trap - <SIG>; kill -<SIG> $$`, so the launcher dies of the signal with the build ended and the directory gone, even when a second signal arrives before an EXIT trap would run (DESIGN §6 *A repository image's build directory lives only as long as its launch*). `_build_job_stop` returns at once with no job; else `kill -STOP -- -$_BUILD_JOB_PID`, sets `$_BUILD_JOB_STOPPED`, then `trap - TSTP; kill -TSTP $$`. The wait is a loop: after each `wait`, when `$_BUILD_JOB_STOPPED` is set it is cleared, the TSTP trap set again and `kill -CONT -- -$_BUILD_JOB_PID` sent; when `wait` returned more than 128 and `kill -0` finds the job, it waits again. Then it clears the PID and returns `<cmd>`'s status (`${PIPESTATUS[0]}`). `_build_job_end` kills that group (`kill -KILL -- -$_BUILD_JOB_PID`) and waits for it; `_repo_build_done` calls it first. `build_repo_image`'s two builds and `_fly_push`'s `build-push.sh` run through it (DESIGN §6 *A repository image's build directory lives only as long as its launch*: no build of a repository image outlives the launch) |
| `REPO_IMAGE_LAYOUT` | after base-build block | `"worker-root-2"` (the first layout built without rewriting the repository's Dockerfile): the repository image's layout (DESIGN §6 *The orchestrator's root is leerie's; a repository's root is only a confined process's*), part of `.dockerfile-hash`, so an image built in an older layout is rebuilt |
| `_repo_build_dir` / `_repo_build_prepare` / `_repo_build_done` / `_repo_build_fail <msg>` | after base-build block | `_repo_build_dir` makes `$_REPO_BUILD_DIR` (`mktemp -d $LEERIE_STATE_HOST_DIR/.image-build/b.$$.XXXXXX`, named for the launcher's PID, which `_sweep_stale_builds` reads; never `/tmp`, never the checkout); `_repo_build_prepare` makes it and `$_REPO_BUILD_CTX` beneath it, the build context: `git --literal-pathspecs -C $USER_REPO archive HEAD -- <paths>` extracted there, `<paths>` the NUL-separated list `_repo_image_dockerfile` wrote to `$_REPO_BUILD_DIR/context-paths` (nothing exported when it is empty, or for a repository with no commit; `_repo_build_fail` when the list is absent), then `_repo_context_retime $_REPO_BUILD_CTX`, then `$_REPO_CTX_SHA=$(_repo_context_sha $_REPO_BUILD_CTX)`. Never the checkout directory: no untracked file reaches a build. `_repo_build_done` first ends a running build (`_build_job_end`), then removes it and clears `$_REPO_CTX_SHA`; `_repo_build_fail` logs, removes it and exits 1 |
| `_repo_context_retime <dir>` | after base-build block | Sets the access and modification time of `<dir>` and of every entry beneath it (a link itself, never its target: `follow_symlinks=False`) to one value, in nanoseconds: now less `secrets.randbelow` of 365 days (host `python3 -I -S`). One value for all, so the entries keep the relative order `git archive` gave them; in the past, so no tool sees a future time or one before 1980. `_repo_build_fail` when it fails (DESIGN §6 *No build consumes what another build left in BuildKit*: BuildKit's context snapshot skips a file whose size, mode, owner and time match, without reading it) |
| `_sweep_stale_builds` | before the per-repo image block, after the base build | Run once per launch, backgrounded with no stdio (`( _sweep_stale_builds ) </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &`), before the first build directory is made. For each `$LEERIE_STATE_HOST_DIR/.image-build/b.*` entry of any type: `rm -rf` when its name is `b.<digits>.<rest>` and `kill -0 <digits>` fails; else when `find <entry> -maxdepth 0 -mmin +1440` lists it (a name without a PID, from before this rule, or a PID a live process reuses). The same rule as `_sweep_stale_stages` (DESIGN §6 *A repository image's build directory lives only as long as its launch*). Right after it the launcher sets `trap '_repo_build_done' EXIT`, and all three `$STAGE` EXIT traps set later (the one after `mktemp`, the container arm's re-set before `nerdctl run`, and the local run's) call `_repo_build_done` too, so a directory a Fly launch makes in `ensure_image` goes too, and no EXIT trap set later leaves one. No TERM or HUP trap is set while a build runs: bash runs the EXIT trap on both at once, where a TERM trap waits for the foreground build to end |
| `_repo_context_sha <dir>` | after base-build block | sha256 (host `python3 -I -S`) over a walk of `<dir>` in path order: for each entry its relative path and `l<link target>`, `d`, or `f`/`x` (executable bit) and the sha256 of its bytes, each length-prefixed. No times, no owners (DESIGN §6 *A repository image is the one built from what it reads*) |
| `_repo_image_dockerfile <dir> [<generated>]` | after base-build block | Copies `$USER_REPO/.leerie/Dockerfile` — or, given `<generated>`, that file (leerie's generated one in the build directory) — read beneath the checkout (beneath `<generated>`'s directory) with `O_NOFOLLOW`, regular file, ≤ 1 MiB, byte for byte to `<dir>/repo/Dockerfile` (host `python3 -I`; the directory holds nothing else: it is the first build's Dockerfile directory). Never edits it: no stage is found, named or added, no parser directive moved (DESIGN §6 *One image, two roots*). Prints the sha256 of the bytes it read: the one digest of `.leerie/Dockerfile` the launcher keys an image on, so the launcher reads the file nowhere else by its path. Writes `<dir>/context-paths`: from `git ls-tree -r -z HEAD` (run from `/`; a link's target read with `git cat-file --batch`), for each `COPY`/`ADD` source of an instruction without `--from` (`ONBUILD`'s too; JSON or shell form; a shell-form word `heredoc_word()` takes and an `ADD` URL left out) and each `RUN --mount` of type `bind` (the default) without `from=` (source default `.`): the path when HEAD has it as a file or directory, and, for a path through a committed link (the source itself, or a directory on its way), each link and the path it resolves to within the tree, followed as BuildKit follows a source's links (at most 40 hops; a target that is absolute or climbs past the top adds nothing past the link); a part with `$`, or a wildcard (`*?[\`) before the last part, cuts the path there; a wildcard in the last part matches that directory's names in HEAD by Go's `filepath.Match`; an empty path or a `..` part makes the list `.` alone; `.dockerignore` added when HEAD has it; sorted. Instructions are lexed as BuildKit lexes them: a leading byte-order mark dropped from line 1 once; the parser directives at the top read for `escape` alone (`escape_directive()`: from line 1, each line a whole `#\s*key\s*=\s*value` with a key BuildKit knows — `syntax`, `escape`, `check` — until the first that is not; an `escape` other than `\` or `` ` `` is read as `\`, and the build fails by itself), which sets the continuation character; any whitespace after the instruction word; a comment or empty line inside a continuation skipped; continuations joined with no separator; whitespace is Go's `unicode.IsSpace` set (`GO_WS`: Python's `str.isspace` less `\x1c`–`\x1f`); BuildKit heredoc bodies skipped: on a `RUN`/`COPY`/`ADD` not in JSON form, `shell_words()` splits the joined line on `GO_WS` as BuildKit's `ProcessWords` does for `heredocsFromLine` (escape `\`, quotes and escapes kept raw, an empty environment) and `heredoc_word()` takes a word as a heredoc only when the whole word matches `^(\d*)<<(-?)([^<]*)$` with a non-empty rest, its name that rest unquoted with unset variables kept; a `<<-` body's terminator may be tab-indented. This reading makes only the context list. Exits non-zero only when the file cannot be read so |
| `_repo_image_wrap <out> <base> <worker>` | after base-build block | Writes leerie's own Dockerfile for the second build to `<out>` (making its directory), no repository text in it: a comment, `FROM <base> AS leerie-baseenv` + `RUN ["/bin/sh", "-c", "env -0 > /.leerie-base-env"]`, `FROM <worker> AS leerie-stage` + `USER root` + `COPY --from=leerie-baseenv /.leerie-base-env /.leerie-base-env` + `RUN ["/bin/sh", "-c", "env -0 > /.leerie-worker-env"]`, then the default target `FROM <base>` + `COPY --from=leerie-stage / /opt/leerie-worker-root/`. `<worker>` is `leerie-worker` locally (the named context) and `registry.fly.io/<APP>@<digest>` on Fly |
| `_repo_layout_digest <layout>` | after base-build block | Prints the manifest digest (`sha256:<64 hex>`) of the one image the OCI layout's `index.json` lists (host `python3 -I -S`); prints nothing and returns 1 unless it lists exactly one |
| `_repo_image_prepare` | after base-build block | `_repo_build_dir`, removes a context, the `repo/`, `wrap/` and `worker/` directories and `generated.Dockerfile` made earlier; when `$_REPO_DF_GEN` is non-empty writes it (`printf '%s\n'`) to `$_REPO_BUILD_DIR/generated.Dockerfile` and copies that with `_repo_image_dockerfile $_REPO_BUILD_DIR $_REPO_BUILD_DIR/generated.Dockerfile`, else the checkout's with `_repo_image_dockerfile $_REPO_BUILD_DIR`; sets `$_REPO_DF_SHA` to the digest it printed; then `_repo_build_prepare` (`$_REPO_CTX_SHA`). `_repo_build_fail` on any failure. |
| `_check_repo_image <tag>` | after base-build block | In `$LEERIE_IMAGE_NS`: the image's `RootFS.Layers` are `$IMAGE_TAG`'s plus exactly one, and its `.Config` equals the base's apart from `.Config.Image`; else removes the image and returns 1 |
| `LEERIE_REGISTRY_AUTH_CONFIG` | `scripts/dockerfile-frontend.sh` | `'{"auths":{"leerie.invalid":{}}}'`: the `config.json` of a repository build's Docker config. A config with no auth entry, credential store or helper (an empty directory, `{}`, `{"credsStore":""}`, `{"auths":{}}`) makes buildctl use the platform's default credential helper when it is on PATH; this one entry, for a name no registry can have and with no credential, does not (DESIGN §6 *A repository's build carries no operator credential*) |
| `build_repo_image <tag> [soft]` | after base-build block | Two builds (`_repo_build_fail` when `$_REPO_BUILD_DIR/repo/Dockerfile` is absent, and on any failure; with `soft`, a failure of the first build returns 1 instead, for the generated file's fallback), after `leerie_buildkit_check` (`_repo_build_fail "$LEERIE_BUILDKIT_REFUSAL"` on 1) and `_repo_build_prepare`, each through `_build_job`. Each is `DOCKER_CONFIG=$_REPO_BUILD_DIR/registry-auth DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG='' _build_job nerdctl --namespace $LEERIE_IMAGE_NS build --buildkit-host $LEERIE_BUILDKIT_HOST …`, the directory made anew with mode 0700 (`rm -rf`, `mkdir -m 0700`) before the first and holding only `config.json`, `LEERIE_REGISTRY_AUTH_CONFIG` (`{"auths":{"leerie.invalid":{}}}`: one auth entry with no credential, so buildctl looks for no default credential helper on PATH), written with `printf` (`_repo_build_fail` when either fails), so neither build pulls with the operator's registry credentials (DESIGN §6 *A repository's build carries no operator credential*); `--namespace` keeps the image out of every namespace a BuildKit worker reads, and `--buildkit-host` runs it on the daemon `leerie_buildkit_check` vetted. Below, `nerdctl build` stands for that prefix. Both are given `--no-cache`, `--build-arg BUILDKIT_SYNTAX=$LEERIE_DOCKERFILE_FRONTEND` and `--build-arg BUILDKIT_CACHE_MOUNT_NS=<ns>`, `<ns>` a fresh `leerie_cache_mount_ns` for each build (`_repo_build_fail` when it fails) (DESIGN §6 *No build consumes what another build left in BuildKit*, *A repository's parser directives are its own build's; its frontend is leerie's*). (1) The repository's file as it is: `nerdctl build --no-cache --build-arg BUILDKIT_SYNTAX=<frontend> --build-arg BUILDKIT_CACHE_MOUNT_NS=<ns> --build-arg BASE_IMAGE=<IMAGE_TAG> --build-arg HOST_UID/GID -o 'type=oci,"dest=$_REPO_BUILD_DIR/worker",tar=false' -f $_REPO_BUILD_DIR/repo/Dockerfile $_REPO_BUILD_CTX` — no `--target`, so BuildKit builds the file's own default target, its final stage; the destination CSV-quoted (a `"` doubled), so a state root with a comma is one field. `_repo_layout_digest` must find exactly one image in the layout. (2) Leerie's: `_repo_image_wrap $_REPO_BUILD_DIR/wrap/Dockerfile <IMAGE_TAG> leerie-worker`, then `nerdctl build --no-cache --build-arg BUILDKIT_SYNTAX=<frontend> --build-arg BUILDKIT_CACHE_MOUNT_NS=<ns> --build-context leerie-worker=oci-layout://$_REPO_BUILD_DIR/worker -t <tag> -f $_REPO_BUILD_DIR/wrap/Dockerfile $_REPO_BUILD_DIR/wrap` (nerdctl reads the layout's `index.json` and pins its digest; `oci-layout://<path>@<digest>` is not accepted by nerdctl 2.3.5, which opens `<path>@<digest>/index.json`). The layout is removed after the second build, then `_check_repo_image`. Both builds' output goes through `_terminal_relay` (`_build_job`). The image lands in `$LEERIE_IMAGE_NS`, where `nerdctl run`/`image inspect` read it (nerdctl exports it from BuildKit and loads it there, the worker reading another namespace); `ensure_base_in_worker_ns` and `ensure_frontend_in_worker_ns` must have run first (the first build's `FROM $BASE_IMAGE`, and the frontend); the layout is read from the client, so it needs no namespace. |
| `REPO_IMAGE_TAG` | after base-build block | Set to `resolve_repo_image_tag()` output when a Dockerfile exists; empty string otherwise |
| `REPO_IMAGE_REF` | after base-build block | The digest of the repository image this checkout built (recorded in `.dockerfile-hash`), which `nerdctl run` runs; empty string when there is no repository image |
| `$LEERIE_STATE_HOST_DIR/.dockerfile-hash` | after base-build block | Stores `<LEERIE_VERSION>:<REPO_IMAGE_LAYOUT>:<base image id>:<sha256>:<context sha256>` of the last-built Dockerfile and its context (`$_REPO_DF_SHA`, `$_REPO_CTX_SHA`: the reuse block runs `_repo_image_prepare` first), then a space and the digest of the image built (`_repo_image_digest`, after `build_repo_image`); rebuild fires on mismatch, on image absence, or when the tag's digest is not the recorded one |

**Rebuild triggers** (checked in order, under the checkout's lock, `leerie_lock $LEERIE_STATE_HOST_DIR/.image-build.lock`, taken before `.dockerfile-hash` is read and released after it is written, `_repo_build_fail` when it cannot be taken): (1) `_repo_image_digest "$REPO_IMAGE_TAG"` is empty (no image), OR (2) `<LEERIE_VERSION>:<REPO_IMAGE_LAYOUT>:<base image id>:<sha256>` differs from the stored hash, OR (3) that digest differs from the stored one (the tag names an image this checkout did not build, or none was recorded) — else skipped, and `REPO_IMAGE_REF` is the stored digest. After a build, `REPO_IMAGE_REF` is the new image's digest, recorded with the hash (`_repo_build_fail` when it has none). Before a build fires, `leerie_buildkit_check` and `leerie_sweep_worker_images` run (`_repo_build_fail "$LEERIE_BUILDKIT_REFUSAL"` on 1), then, when `${RUNTIME:-}` is `local`, `leerie_reap_old_images "${_leerie_host_dir:+$_leerie_host_dir/image-holds}" worker` removes older versions' base copies from the worker namespaces, `ensure_base_in_worker_ns` copies the base into each namespace BuildKit's workers read (idempotent by image id) so `FROM $BASE_IMAGE` resolves locally, or stops the launch when the copy there does not end with the base's id, and `ensure_frontend_in_worker_ns` pulls the frontend there. No other build runs before the decision: the launch whose key and digest match runs none. `build_repo_image <tag>` builds the file, whoever wrote it; a failure stops the launch (`_repo_build_fail`), with no fallback (DESIGN §6½ *The repository image holds no dependency*). The stored line is `<key> <digest>`; a third field an earlier leerie wrote (`apt-only`) is read and ignored. The base image's own build (`nerdctl --namespace $LEERIE_IMAGE_NS build [--buildkit-host $LEERIE_BUILDKIT_HOST] --no-cache --build-arg BUILDKIT_SYNTAX=$LEERIE_DOCKERFILE_FRONTEND --build-arg BUILDKIT_CACHE_MOUNT_NS=<ns> --build-arg HOST_UID/HOST_GID -t $IMAGE_TAG $LEERIE_REPO`, when `nerdctl --namespace $LEERIE_IMAGE_NS image inspect $IMAGE_TAG` fails, after `ensure_frontend_in_worker_ns`, `--buildkit-host` when that resolved the daemon; with the operator's Docker config, leerie's own Dockerfile naming only public images) is given `--no-cache`, the pinned frontend and a cache-mount namespace of its own (`<ns>` a fresh `leerie_cache_mount_ns`; exit 1 when it fails), so leerie's base is never built from a step another build cached, nor by a frontend another build chose, nor with a cache mount another build holds.

**The image's two roots.** Everything outside `/opt/leerie-worker-root` is `$IMAGE_TAG`'s, so the entrypoint, the orchestrator, the cgroup broker and `container-entry.sh` run in leerie's root. `/opt/leerie-worker-root` holds the worker stage whole, with `/.leerie-worker-env` and `/.leerie-base-env` at its top; the shim builds a confined process's root from it (`scripts/landlock_exec.py --worker-root`, §6 *Worker confinement* below). `apply_worker_env` takes from the worker stage's environment only a variable the confined command's environment does not set, so a store variable leerie set is the run's whatever the stage says.

**Auto-generation triggers**: when no `.leerie/Dockerfile` exists, the launcher generates one (atomic write via temp file + `mv`) when `.leerie/config.toml` declares `setup_packages` (`_leerie_should_generate_dockerfile <repo> <setup_packages>`), and only then: no lockfile and no manager triggers a build (DESIGN §6½ *The repository image holds no dependency*). A committed Dockerfile always takes precedence. When `.leerie/config.toml` holds a `language_installs` or `bake_language_deps` line (keys an earlier leerie read), the launch logs `note: .leerie/config.toml's language_installs and bake_language_deps are no longer read: …`, once, and reads neither.

**`nerdctl run` image arg**: `nerdctl --namespace $LEERIE_IMAGE_NS run … "${REPO_IMAGE_REF:-$IMAGE_TAG}"` — the repository image by the digest this checkout built, never by its tag; falls back to the base image transparently when no repo Dockerfile is present.

**Generator inputs.** The generated file is the sentinel line, `ARG BASE_IMAGE`, `FROM $BASE_IMAGE`, `USER root` and one apt `RUN` line installing the `setup_packages` words. Each word must match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9+.-]+$` (split with `read -r -a`, no pathname expansion), else the launch stops naming it. No `COPY`, no `WORKDIR`, no `ENV`, and no dependency layer: the image holds no dependency (DESIGN §6½ *The repository image holds no dependency*). Every install the run needs is its provision recipe's, run by the orchestrator in each tree it measures and by a worker in its own, into the run's stores, and the `PROVISION_RECIPE:` block in the implementer's and conformer's prompts (`_format_provision_recipe_section`) carries every `install` and `build` entry of the recipe.

**`capture_repo_deps` contract:** The `dep_capture` worker always runs at
finalize time, even with a committed `.leerie/Dockerfile` — it captures
`setup_packages` only. On success it writes the `dep_capture.done`
sentinel and sets `dep_capture_done = True` in `state.json`. It writes
nothing in the user's checkout: it records the capture in the run's
`captured-deps.json`, and only the operator's `leerie config
--apply-capture <run-id>` applies it (`apply_captured_deps`).

### Registry publish path (fly.io / remote Machines)

Fly.io Machines pull an image from a registry rather than using a
locally-built image. The `HOST_UID/HOST_GID` coupling exists only for
local bind-mounts (so files written by the container into `/work` keep
the host user's ownership). Remote Machines have no such bind-mount, so
the Dockerfile's defaults (`ARG HOST_UID=501 / HOST_GID=20`) are used
as-is — no UID matching required.

**Baked source.** The Dockerfile's `COPY` instructions bake
`orchestrator/`, `scripts/`, `prompts/`, and `.claude-plugin/` into the
image at `/opt/leerie-image/`, so a Fly Machine that pulls it can run the
orchestrator with no bind mount. Local runs mount the launch's own copy
of the four directories over it (`-v $_code_dir:/opt/leerie-image:ro`), so
development iteration works without rebuilding; the install directory
itself is never mounted (DESIGN §6 *A launch runs only the leerie code it
started with*):

- `_snapshot_leerie_code SRC DEST` (launcher, every runtime, before the
  command-line check and so before any image step; `DEST` is
  `$_code_snapshot`, `mktemp -d ~/.cache/leerie/cfg-<pid>-code-XXXXXX`):
  `orchestrator/`, `scripts/`, `prompts/` and `.claude-plugin/` of `SRC`
  (`$LEERIE_REPO`) into `DEST`, and sets `LEERIE_COMMIT` (no longer read
  at launcher start). When `SRC/.git` exists, `HEAD` is read once (`rev-parse --verify -q
  'HEAD^{commit}'`, its stderr in `DEST/.git-err`, removed). Unresolved (git
  cannot read the checkout, e.g. its `safe.directory` refusal, or there is
  no commit), the launch logs "git cannot read the leerie checkout at SRC
  (<git's first stderr line>); taking it as a copy, with no commit
  recorded" and takes the non-git shape below. Resolved, and
  when `git --no-optional-locks status
  --porcelain --untracked-files=all -- <dirs>` is empty, `git archive
  <HEAD> -- <dirs> | tar -xf - -C DEST` and `LEERIE_COMMIT=<short HEAD>`.
  When the status is not empty: with the index lock
  (`rev-parse --git-path index.lock`) absent and `_leerie_checkout_state`
  (HEAD and `ls-files -s --debug -- <dirs>`: each entry's blob id and the
  file status it records, so a flip to another commit and back reads as a
  change) read, `_leerie_worktree_tree` twice
  (`GIT_INDEX_FILE=<private> read-tree HEAD; add -A -- <dirs>;
  write-tree`, the private indexes in `DEST/.idx`, removed before the
  archive is extracted, and with `DEST` on any other exit); the two ids equal, the lock still absent and the state
  unchanged, or it returns 1 ("changed while this launch read it");
  `git archive <tree>` and `LEERIE_COMMIT=<short HEAD>-dirty.<tree:12>`.
  No `SRC/.git` (not a git checkout), or `HEAD` unresolved: `cp -pR` of each directory, then `diff
  -r -q` of each against `SRC`, a difference returns 1 ("changed while
  this launch copied it"); `LEERIE_COMMIT` empty. Then the snapshot's
  `plugin.json` version (the same `awk` extraction as `LEERIE_VERSION`)
  must equal `LEERIE_VERSION`; otherwise it returns 1 naming both
  versions. A return of 1 exits the launch 1. `$_code_snapshot` is
  removed by the EXIT traps until `$STAGE` exists (`_code_snapshot_done`;
  the trap the repository-image block sets removes it too), then the
  local runtime `mv`s it to `$_code_dir` = `$STAGE/leerie-code`, which
  lives and dies with `$STAGE` (its EXIT trap, `_sweep_stale_stages`, which
  also takes a `cfg-<pid>-code-*` a SIGKILL left); a remote runtime
  removes it.
- `_bring_back_ran_run` and the post-exit `host_finalize` source
  `$_code_dir/scripts/host-finalize.sh`, not the install's. The file
  takes leerie's code from the tree it was sourced from,
  `_HOST_FINALIZE_CODE` (`${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}/..`), never
  `$LEERIE_REPO`: the rebaser seam and `host_apply_captured_deps` load
  `$_HOST_FINALIZE_CODE/orchestrator/leerie.py`, whose `PROMPTS` are that
  tree's `prompts/`.

`scripts/remote/build-push.sh` provides the build-and-push path. By
default it uses Fly's remote builder (no host Docker daemon required):

```bash
# Default: Fly's remote builder builds + pushes (recommended):
./scripts/remote/build-push.sh --app <fly-app-name> --push

# Verify the baked source works inside a Machine:
flyctl machine run registry.fly.io/<fly-app-name>:<VERSION> \
  --app <fly-app-name> \
  -- python3 /opt/leerie-image/orchestrator/leerie.py version
```

Internally, the remote-builder path runs:

```bash
flyctl deploy --build-only --push --remote-only --depot=false --no-cache \
  --build-arg BUILDKIT_SYNTAX=<LEERIE_DOCKERFILE_FRONTEND> \
  --build-arg BUILDKIT_CACHE_MOUNT_NS=<leerie_cache_mount_ns> \
  --app <fly-app-name> \
  config <tmp-fly.toml> \
  --dockerfile <DOCKERFILE> \
  [--build-arg KEY=VAL ...] \
  --image-label <LABEL>
```

run from `<CONTEXT>` (flyctl's build context is its working directory).
`<DOCKERFILE>` defaults to `$LEERIE_REPO/Dockerfile`; `--dockerfile <path>`
overrides it (used by `ensure_image()` for per-repo images). `--build-arg
KEY=VAL` is repeatable. `--context DIR` sets `<CONTEXT>` (default
`$LEERIE_REPO`; on `--local-build` it is the `nerdctl`/`docker build`
context too): `ensure_image()` passes the committed tree for the
repository's stage and, for the wrap, `$_REPO_BUILD_DIR/wrap`, which holds
only leerie's Dockerfile (it copies nothing from a context). No build is
given a target: each builds its file's default target. Every build is
given `--no-cache`, on the remote builder (`flyctl deploy --no-cache`) and
on `--local-build` (`nerdctl`/`docker build --no-cache`): Fly's remote
builder is one per organization, shared by every app in it (DESIGN §6
*No build consumes what another build left in BuildKit*). Every build is
also given `--build-arg BUILDKIT_SYNTAX=$LEERIE_DOCKERFILE_FRONTEND`
(sourced from `scripts/dockerfile-frontend.sh`), ahead of the caller's
`--build-arg`s, on both builders: the frontend is leerie's, never a
`# syntax=` line's (DESIGN §6 *A repository's parser directives are its
own build's; its frontend is leerie's*). After it each build is given
`--build-arg BUILDKIT_CACHE_MOUNT_NS=<ns>`, a fresh `leerie_cache_mount_ns`
for each builder's build (exit 1 when it fails), so no two builds share a
cache mount (DESIGN §6 *No build consumes what another build left in
BuildKit*). A caller's `--build-arg` naming either, in any letter case
(`BUILDKIT_SYNTAX`, `buildkit_cache_mount_ns=x`, …), exits 1 before any
build. `--no-run` keeps
`--local-build` from starting a container from the image (its entrypoint
check and version smoke test): `ensure_image()` passes it for the
repository's own stage, which only ever runs as a confined process's root
(DESIGN §6 *One image, two roots*).

The image is pushed under exactly `--tag` (default
`registry.fly.io/<APP>:<VERSION>`): `<LABEL>` is that tag's part after
its last `:`. Fly's remote builder pushes only `registry.fly.io/<APP>:<LABEL>`,
so in that mode a tag whose repository is anything else, or whose label is
not `[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,127}`, exits 1 before anything runs
(review round 29, isolation F1: the label was `$LEERIE_VERSION` whatever
`--tag` said, so a repository image was pushed over the base tag).

After a successful push, with `--push`:

- `--digest-file PATH` writes the digest the registry holds under the tag
  (`registry_image.py digest`), one line, `sha256:<hex>`.
- `--layout-base REF` requires `registry_image.py layout REF
  <repository>@<digest>` to pass, else exits 1 and writes no digest.

The registry password is `flyctl auth token` when the tag's host is
`registry.fly.io`, and empty otherwise. `--dry-run` prints the
`registry_image.py` commands instead. Either flag without `--push` exits 1.

The `<tmp-fly.toml>` is a copy of the repo's `fly.toml` with the `[build]
image = "..."` line stripped — that line tells flyctl "fetch the existing
image", which makes `flyctl deploy --build-only` skip the build step and
fail with "Could not find image"
([flyctl#1686](https://github.com/superfly/flyctl/issues/1686)).

**Opt-in: `--local-build`** (or `LEERIE_LOCAL_BUILD=1`). Builds with
host `nerdctl`/`docker` and pushes from the host. Requires a working
Docker daemon authenticated to `registry.fly.io`. Does NOT work with
nerdctl-in-Colima on macOS — nerdctl reads `~/.docker/config.json`
but cannot resolve `credsStore: desktop` (no access to macOS
Keychain from inside the Lima VM). Documented in INSTALL.md for
completeness; most users should leave it off. With nerdctl, every
command on the image names `--namespace $LEERIE_IMAGE_NS` (build,
`inspect`, the smoke `run --rm`, `push`), and the build is given
`--buildkit-host $LEERIE_BUILDKIT_HOST` after `leerie_buildkit_check`
and then `leerie_sweep_worker_images` (exit 1 on either's refusal,
`build-push: $LEERIE_BUILDKIT_REFUSAL`; not run under `--dry-run`), and after it, whatever its status, `leerie_prune_cache_mounts` (a warning on failure); docker gets none of these. Its
builds keep the operator's Docker config: the repository's stage pulls
leerie's base from `registry.fly.io` (DESIGN §6 *A repository's build
carries no operator credential*, *Fly*).

#### Auto-publish on first remote run (`ensure_image()` in the launcher)

A remote run requires the image at `$FLY_IMAGE_TAG` to already exist in
`registry.fly.io`, or `flyctl machine run` fails at provision time with
an unfriendly "manifest unknown" error. `ensure_image()` in the
launcher's `RUNTIME=fly` branch closes that gap, run before
`provision_machine`. Two variants:

`ensure_image` sets `FLY_IMAGE_REF` to `<repository>@<digest>` (the tag's
part before its last `:`, and the digest pushed or cached), and the
launcher hands that to `provision_machine` as `FLY_IMAGE_TAG`: a machine
starts from the digest leerie pushed, never from a tag (DESIGN §6½
*Per-repo container image*, Fly). Helpers: `_fly_cache_get <cache-file>
<tag>` prints the digest and base digest of the last line for `<tag>`;
`_fly_digest_ok` accepts only `sha256:<64 hex>`; `_fly_push <build-push>
<cache-dir> <tag> <args...>` runs build-push.sh with `<args> --tag <tag>
--digest-file <file>` (the file under the cache directory) through
`_build_job` and sets `_FLY_PUSHED` to the digest it reported.

**Base image path** (no `.leerie/Dockerfile`):

1. Cache check: if `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/leerie/published-tags.txt` has a
   digest for `$FLY_IMAGE_TAG`, start from it and skip everything.
2. Auto-create the Fly app if it doesn't exist. `flyctl apps list
   --json` is parsed for a name match; on miss, `flyctl apps create
   $LEERIE_FLY_APP` is invoked. Idempotent — "already exists" is a
   silent success.
3. Invoke `scripts/remote/build-push.sh --app $LEERIE_FLY_APP --push`.
   `--local-build` is forwarded if `LOCAL_BUILD=true` (set by the
   `--local-build` CLI flag or `LEERIE_LOCAL_BUILD=1` env var).
   build-push.sh handles the actual remote-vs-local mode dispatch.
4. On success, append `<tag> <digest>` to the cache.

**Per-repo derived image path** (`.leerie/Dockerfile` present):

The relevant bash surface:

| Function / variable | Location in `leerie` | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `_set_fly_per_repo_image()` | before `resolve_fly_image_tag()` call in the `RUNTIME=fly` block | When `$_REPO_DF_OWN` is `true` or `$_REPO_DF_GEN` is non-empty, writes leerie's Dockerfile for it and its context (`_repo_image_prepare` on the base tag), computes the tag from `$_REPO_DF_SHA` and `$_REPO_CTX_SHA`, sets `LEERIE_FLY_IMAGE` + context vars; no-op when absent. The launcher removes the build directory after `ensure_image` (`_repo_build_done`) |
| `_FLY_REPO_DF_SHA` | module-level (set by `_set_fly_per_repo_image`) | The digest of the Dockerfile bytes the per-repo tag names (`$_REPO_DF_SHA`); `ensure_image` makes leerie's Dockerfile again on the base's digest and requires the same digest. Empty string when no per-repo Dockerfile |
| `_FLY_REPO_CTX_SHA` | module-level (set by `_set_fly_per_repo_image`) | The digest of the build context the per-repo tag names (`$_REPO_CTX_SHA`); `ensure_image` requires the same digest of the context it makes again |
| `FLY_IMAGE_REF` | module-level (set by `ensure_image`) | `registry.fly.io/<APP>@<digest>`, what the machine starts from |
| `_FLY_BASE_TAG` | module-level (set by `_set_fly_per_repo_image`) | Base Fly tag (`registry.fly.io/$APP:$VERSION`); the repository image is built `FROM` its digest |

Before `resolve_fly_image_tag()` is called, `_set_fly_per_repo_image()`
finds a Dockerfile to build (the repository's own, or the one the launch
generated), takes the first 12 hex chars of the sha256
of `$_REPO_DF_SHA:$_REPO_CTX_SHA` (the Dockerfile bytes leerie's Dockerfile
was made from, and the context they read), and sets
`LEERIE_FLY_IMAGE=registry.fly.io/$APP:$VERSION-$HASH`, which
`resolve_fly_image_tag()` returns via the existing override hook.
`ensure_image()` then:

1. Cache check: the per-repo tag's line records a digest, a base digest
   and the layout, the base tag's line records that same base digest, and
   the layout is `REPO_IMAGE_LAYOUT` — start from the per-repo digest and
   skip everything.
2. Ensure the base image is published: on no cached base digest, push the
   base tag first (`_fly_push`) and append `<base-tag> <digest>`.
3. Build and push the per-repo image in its two builds (DESIGN §6 *One
   image, two roots*): `_repo_image_prepare` (the Dockerfile copied again
   and its context; exit when `$_REPO_DF_SHA` is not `$_FLY_REPO_DF_SHA`
   or `$_REPO_CTX_SHA` is not `$_FLY_REPO_CTX_SHA`, what the tag names),
   then `_fly_push` with `--dockerfile $_REPO_BUILD_DIR/repo/Dockerfile
   --context $_REPO_BUILD_CTX --build-arg BASE_IMAGE=<base ref> --no-run`
   and the tag `<per-repo-tag>-repo` (the repository's file as committed);
   then `_repo_image_wrap $_REPO_BUILD_DIR/wrap/Dockerfile <base ref>
   registry.fly.io/$APP@<that digest>` and `_fly_push` with `--dockerfile
   $_REPO_BUILD_DIR/wrap/Dockerfile --context $_REPO_BUILD_DIR/wrap
   --layout-base <base ref>` and the per-repo tag; then `_repo_build_done`
   (on failure too). `--layout-base` applies `_check_repo_image`'s rule to
   the registry's copy.
4. Append `<per-repo-tag> <digest> <base digest> <REPO_IMAGE_LAYOUT>` to
   the cache.

The launch wrapper sets `LEERIE_REPO_IMAGE=1` in the orchestrator's
environment when `_FLY_REPO_DF_SHA` is set (locally, `nerdctl run -e
LEERIE_REPO_IMAGE=1` when `REPO_IMAGE_REF` is; the name is on the `LEERIE_*`
auto-forward deny-list). `_require_worker_view` dies when it is "1" and the
image has no `/opt/leerie-worker-root`.

A rebuild fires automatically when the Dockerfile content or the leerie
version changes, since either changes the tag and causes a cache miss, and
when the base digest cached now is not the one the image was built on.

Results are cached at `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/leerie/published-tags.txt`
(default `~/.cache/leerie/published-tags.txt`), one line per image pushed:
`<tag> <digest>`, and `<tag> <digest> <base digest> <layout>` for a
repository image; the last line for a tag wins. A line without a digest (written
before digests were recorded) is not a hit. It's a *positive* list only —
a missing entry means "probe", not "absent".

Flags:

| Flag | Env | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--no-auto-publish` | `LEERIE_NO_AUTO_PUBLISH=1` | off | Skip the probe entirely; trust the operator to have published the image. The run still proceeds; if the tag is missing, `provision_machine` fails as before. |

The flag is consumed by the launcher and not forwarded to the
orchestrator (same convention as `--no-runtime-install`).
