Returns rc=2 + `remote_log` error on unknown verb (bash-side assert; Python heredoc has its own `sys.exit(2)` backstop). |

The wave loop's tag-write step (`update_run_json … chain_id "$_ch_id"
wave_idx "$_wave_idx"`) fires BEFORE the failure-pause check so
runs that paused on failure still get tagged and are therefore
discoverable by `leerie resume <chain-id>` / `kill <chain-id>` /
etc. The `_ch_wave_pids` / `_ch_wave_child_pids` arrays reset at
the top of every wave iteration (above the `_wave_already_done`
check) so the SIGINT trap handler never sees stale entries from a
prior wave.

##### Resuming a chain via `chain --chain-id <uuid>`

`leerie chain --chain-id <prior-uuid> --wave …` pins the chain_id to a
prior chain's UUID instead of minting fresh. The wave loop's
`_wave_already_done` check then matches the prior chain's runs and skips
fan-out for already-pushed waves, advancing `current_base` through any
wave-staging branches already pushed to origin — the load-bearing recovery
path after `leerie resume <chain-id>` unpauses every paused run: the user
re-submits with `--chain-id <prior-uuid>` and the chain picks up at the
first not-yet-done wave.

The launcher normalizes the user-supplied chain_id to lowercase via `tr
'[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'` after UUID format validation (`UUID_PATTERN` is
case-insensitive, `grep -qiE`, so uppercase input passes validation; but
the wave-loop helpers compare `run.json`'s `chain_id` case-sensitively, and
`uuid.uuid4()` always emits lowercase). Without normalization, uppercase
`--chain-id` input would silently bypass idempotency and fork the chain
into two chain_ids — the v8 audit's S1 finding.

##### Synth-merge idempotency probe

Before invoking `chain.git_ops.synth_merge_branches` for wave N → N+1,
the wave loop probes origin via `git ls-remote --exit-code origin
leerie/stage/<chain-id>-wave-<N+1>`. If the stage branch already exists
(e.g. the user manually resolved a prior synth-merge conflict and
pushed), the wave loop fetches + checks out the existing branch instead
of re-running synth-merge — otherwise `synth_merge_branches`'s `git
checkout -B` would force-recreate the stage branch from `$current_base`,
discarding the resolved state and re-conflicting the same way.

#### Synth-merge between waves

After every wave-N job's `host_finalize` has pushed its branch to
origin, the wave loop runs synth-merge to build the next wave's
base branch:

```bash
python3 -c "
from chain.git_ops import synth_merge_branches, SynthMergeConflict
synth_merge_branches('$USER_REPO', '$current_base',
                     ['leerie/runs/...', ...],
                     'leerie/stage/<chain-id>-wave-<N+1>')
"
```

`synth_merge_branches` runs in `$USER_REPO`, does `git fetch
origin` + `git checkout -B <stage> origin/<base>` + sequential
`git merge --no-ff --no-edit origin/<branch>`. Conflicts raise
`SynthMergeConflict`; the wave loop catches and pauses the chain
with a clear message for manual resolution. The function works
unchanged from its v3 form — branches are on origin (each wave-N
job's `host_finalize` pushed it), so the `origin/<branch>`
references resolve.

After synth-merge, the wave loop pushes the stage branch to origin
so wave-N+1 workers can see it as their starting base.

#### Idempotent resume

If the user Ctrl-Cs mid-chain or any job fails, the wave loop exits
non-zero with a resume hint: `leerie resume <chain-id>` resumes every
paused run, then re-invoking `leerie chain --wave ...` picks the chain
back up (the idempotency check above skips waves whose runs are already
`pushed_at`). `pushed_at` is the canonical "this run is done, don't
re-spawn" sentinel — the same one `host_finalize` uses for push
idempotency, set after `git push -u origin <branch>` succeeds.

#### chain.git_ops surface (laptop-side)

`chain/git_ops.py` provides the git operations invoked by the wave
loop. Workers never invoke this module; all GitHub credential
touches happen on the laptop using its existing `gh auth` and
`~/.git-credentials`.

| Function | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `synth_merge_branches(repo, base_branch, dep_branches, stage_name)` | Build a stage branch by merging each dep branch into a fresh checkout of `base_branch`; raises `SynthMergeConflict` on any conflict. Used by the wave loop between waves. Passes `-c user.email=leerie-chain@bot.invalid -c user.name=leerie-chain` to `git merge` defensively so the merge commit succeeds even when the laptop's global git identity is unset (otherwise the merge would fail with "Committer identity unknown"). |
| `create_stage_branch(repo, chain_id, base_branch)` | Create (or check out, idempotently) the `stage-<chain_id>` branch off `base_branch`. |

Maps to `DESIGN.md`: §19 *Chain orchestration*.

### Run-group verbs

Run-group orchestration launches N ordinary single-repo leerie runs
together as a coordinated unit, sharing a `group_id` (DESIGN.md §20).
Each member is an unchanged, fully isolated run with its own
basename-keyed state directory, its own run branch, its own PR, and
its own resume record. The group layer adds a shared brief,
read-only cross-repo visibility via `--inspect-dir`, deploy-ordering
notes, and group-scoped verbs — nothing else.

**Contrast with chains (§19):** chain-scoped verbs scan ONE state
directory for `chain_id`; group-scoped verbs must scan ACROSS the set
of member state directories (one per member repo basename). The two
subsystems are complementary in design spirit but do not share
discovery machinery — `_chain_runs_filter` (`leerie:191`) assumes a
single `$LEERIE_STATE_HOST_DIR` and cannot be reused directly.

#### `group_id` in `run.json`

`group_id` is an optional string field in `run.json`. The orchestrator
writes it at run start when `--group-id` is supplied (`_write_run_json` in
`_run_phases`' fresh-run branch), into the run it resolved, so the field
appears in `run.json` when the run begins and only in a run of that group
(DESIGN §6 *Which run the container ran*). On Fly and EC2 the `group`
launcher arm also writes it into the host-side `run.json` after the members
exit (the pointer tag-back below).
`_validate_run_json`
(`orchestrator/leerie.py:1994`) does not add any invariant check on
`group_id` — it is informational and orthogonal to the push/pause/kill
state machine. The field is accepted by the validator without error
because validators only check fields they know about (unknown keys pass
through).

#### Launcher `group` verb

```
leerie group \
  --repo <path> "<prompt>" \
  --repo <path> "<prompt>" \
  [--brief <file>] \
  [<per-member-flags>]
```

Modeled on the `chain` arm (`leerie:2033`). The `group` arm parses repeated
`--repo <path> "<prompt>"` pairs and an optional `--brief <file>`; fails
fast if any repo path is not a git repository (mirrors the chain
prompt-file check at `leerie:2136`); mints a `_group_id` (UUID, same
mechanism as `chain`'s `_ch_id`); then per member builds the prompt as
`<brief>\n\n<member prompt>`, appends `--inspect-dir <sibling-repo>` for
every other member, and backgrounds:

```bash
# resolved once, before any cd, to an absolute path:
_grp_self_cmd="${LEERIE_SELF_CMD:-$_grp_leerie_dir/$(basename "$0")}"
( cd <repo> && "$_grp_self_cmd" "<prompt>" <flags> \
    --group-id "$_group_id" ) &
```

(mirrors `leerie:2237-2246` for chains). Each `cd` makes the member resolve
its own `USER_REPO` and basename-keyed state directory independently. The
self-command **must** be absolutized *before* the `cd`: a relative `$0`
(e.g. `./leerie`) would not resolve once the subshell has `cd`'d into the
member repo — unlike chains, which never `cd`. Finally, waits for all
members (`wait`) and runs the Fly/EC2 pointer tag-back (below).

**State-dir guard (mandatory).** The arm rejects or per-member-namespaces
any `--state-dir` / `LEERIE_STATE_DIR` override in the calling environment,
before any member is backgrounded. These override `_state_dir_default`
(`:431`) and would pin every member to one shared state directory, causing
a `.owner` collision on member 2. Chains (one repo) forward these safely;
groups (N repos) must not.

Per-member flags are forwarded like `_ch_passthrough` for chains.
`LEERIE_SELF_CMD` is the same test seam used by chain verbs — it still
takes precedence in `_grp_self_cmd`, so tests substitute a stub binary
via `LEERIE_SELF_CMD`.

#### Group tag-back (Fly and EC2 only)

A local member is not tagged by the launcher: its orchestrator wrote
`group_id` into its run's `run.json` at run start. The `group` arm reads no
run id and scans no state directory for runs.

On Fly and EC2, after `wait`, the arm writes `group_id` into the host-side
`run.json` of each member's own run, through `update_run_json … group_id
"$_grp_id"`. That covers the time before the machine's copy, which carries
the orchestrator's `group_id`, is synced back. The run is found from the
member's basename-keyed state dir by that member launcher's own pid (`$!`):
first its `remote/<pid>.json` pointer, then the `fly-machine.json` whose
`launcher_pid` is that pid. When neither exists (a local member), nothing
is written.

#### Group-scoped verbs

| Verb | Behavior |
|------|----------|
| `leerie group --repo <path> "<prompt>" [--repo ...] [--brief <file>] [--group-id <uuid>]` | Fan-out launcher. Mints a fresh `group_id` unless `--group-id <prior-uuid>` is supplied. Fans out one backgrounded member invocation per `--repo` and waits; on Fly and EC2, then runs the pointer tag-back. |
| `leerie status <group-id>` | Iterates member state dirs (derived from the group's member repos or a group-manifest the launcher drops), filters `run.json` by `group_id`, renders one row per matched run (run_id, status, branch, notes). Same field-derived status as chain `status`. |
| `leerie stop <group-id>` | Discovers running Fly members across all member state dirs; invokes `leerie stop <run-id>` per discovered run. Fly-runtime only (pauses machines). |
| `leerie resume <group-id>` | Discovers paused members across all member state dirs; invokes `leerie resume <run-id>` per discovered paused run. |
| `leerie kill <group-id>` | Discovers non-destroyed members across all member state dirs; invokes `leerie kill <run-id>` per discovered run. Idempotent. |
| `leerie finalize <group-id>` | Discovers members not yet pushed across all member state dirs; invokes `leerie finalize <run-id>` per discovered run. |
| `leerie list --groups` | Iterates across all leerie state dirs under `$HOME/.leerie/`, groups `run.json` files by `group_id`, renders one row per group (group_id, status, member count). |

These verbs are dispatched by UUID detection (same `8-4-4-4-12` hyphen
pattern as chain verbs). A UUID that matches a `group_id` across member
state dirs is a group-scoped dispatch.

#### `_group_runs_filter`

The group-scoped verb implementations build on `_group_runs_filter`,
a private launcher helper that scans a **set** of state directories
(one per member repo basename) for `run.json` files tagged with a
given `group_id`. Signature:

```
_group_runs_filter <group_id> <verb> <state_dir_1> [<state_dir_2> ...]
```

Emits matching run-ids one per line, filtered by the same per-verb logic as
`_chain_runs_filter` (`stop` / `kill` / `finalize` / `resume` / `running`).
Key difference: `_chain_runs_filter` iterates one directory
(`$LEERIE_STATE_HOST_DIR/runs/*/run.json`); `_group_runs_filter` iterates
`<state_dir_N>/runs/*/run.json` for each supplied directory.

#### Deploy-ordering notes

When a member's planner declares a cross-repo prerequisite as
`requires.extent: external` (DESIGN.md §5), those entries accumulate
in `State.data["external_preconditions"]` (written at plan time,
`orchestrator/leerie.py:9727`). The entry shape is:
`{tag, reasons:[{sid, reason}], originating_subtasks}`.

The deploy-note plumbing threads `external_preconditions` from State
into the finalize path at three points, so the note survives regardless
of which finalize path fires:

1. **`_compose_pr_via_llm` payload** (the `pr_writer` call runs with
   `cwd=_payload_only_cwd(st)`, an empty `<run_dir>/payload-only/`, and
   `allowed_tools=PAYLOAD_ONLY_TOOLS` (`"Read"`), never in `repo_root`):
   added as a field in the JSON payload passed to `pr_writer`, alongside
   `task`, `commit_log`, etc. The pr_writer prompt renders a
   "⚠ Deploy-ordering" section when the field is non-empty.
2. **`compose_pr_body` fallback** (`orchestrator/leerie.py:2119`): the
   deterministic Python fallback PR body renders the same section from
   state, covering the case where the `pr_writer` LLM worker fails or is
   skipped.
3. **`host-finalize.sh` bash fallback**: the pure-bash deterministic PR
   body (the LLM-less host-side finalize path, used when neither
   `pr_body` nor the Python fallback reached `run.json`) renders the
   identical section via `jq` — byte-for-byte matching the Python
   renderer's shape (`- **<tag>** — <reason>`, reasons `"; "`-joined,
   nothing emitted when absent/empty). No `run.json` persistence is
   needed — `external_preconditions` is already a `STATE_FIELDS` key.

#### Run-summary cost line

Both deterministic renderers also emit a `- Cost:` line in the
`## Run summary` block (after `- Workers:`), sourced from `state.json`'s
`telemetry` block: `- Cost: $X.XX (N calls, I in / O out tokens)`.
Rendered only when the telemetry block is present (omitted on
pre-classify orphans), matching the deploy-note guard.
`compose_pr_body` and the `host-finalize.sh` `jq` fallback both produce
2-decimal, thousands-grouped output and are format-identical except for
a sub-cent rounding difference on an exact half-cent `cost_usd` that
never arises on a real summed cost. No `run.json` persistence is needed
— `telemetry` is already a `STATE_FIELDS` key.

**Key design note:** `reason` in `external_preconditions` is
unstructured free text (`required` is only `[tag, extent]`,
`orchestrator/leerie.py:731`). The group launcher, not the planner,
knows which sibling repos are group members — so the deploy note
identifies sibling members by injected group membership, not by
parsing planner free-text.

#### Planner steering (`prompts/planner.md`)

When a group member's planner receives a group brief (a shared context
block prepended by the launcher, marked `## Group brief` or similar),
`prompts/planner.md` directs it to: (1) **read the sibling's contract** —
`Read`/`Grep`/`Glob` under `/inspect/<name>/` to locate the sibling's API
surface, types, schema, or interface files, not just the brief; (2)
**honor the interface** — subtasks must conform to the sibling's actual
types/field names/endpoints as found in the code; (3) **declare the
dependency** — add a `requires` entry with `extent: "external"` whose
`reason` names the sibling repo and the specific contract item, for every
subtask depending on a sibling-owned contract.

This is advisory steering per DESIGN.md §12 ("prompts advisory, code
enforces"): the write-confinement guarantee stays code
(`_filter_offtree_subtasks`), not the prompt. The instruction lifts
reliable cross-repo-aware planning from emergent to dependable.

The planner prompt also documents the runtime asymmetry: inspect-dir
read-only is kernel-enforced locally (`:ro` bind-mount) but
convention-enforced on Fly (`chown leerie:` in `seed-repo.sh`). The
practical guarantee is the same for planning — acting workers that get
`/inspect/` do not receive `--add-dir` on Fly either — but the
mechanism differs.

#### No new schema, state, or cap changes

This is the point of the lean shape (DESIGN.md §20 *Why the lean
shape*). The following are explicitly unchanged:

- `STATE_FIELDS` / `state.json` schema — `group_id` lives in
  `run.json` (the per-run sidecar), not in `state.json`.
- Subtask schema and planner schema — group members are ordinary runs.
- `DEFAULT_CAPS` — no new per-member cap; each member consumes from
  its own run's cap budget.
- `_filter_offtree_subtasks` (DESIGN.md §12) — the existing guard
  enforces write-confinement for siblings seeded as inspect-dirs,
  unchanged.
- Branch helpers (`new-worktree.sh`, `setup-run.sh`, `integrate.sh`,
  `finalize.sh`, `host-finalize.sh`) — each member's finalize runs
  its own existing `host_finalize` against its own repo.

Maps to `DESIGN.md`: §20 *Run groups (multi-repo)*.

## 2½. Configuration reference

Complete reference for every CLI flag, environment variable, and
`leerie.toml` key the orchestrator and launcher read. Moved here from
the README (2026-08-21) to keep the README a quickstart entry point;
see the README's *Configuration* section for a pointer back to this
table.

### CLI flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|------|---------|-------------|
| `task` (positional) | — | The task description (literal string, or path to a `.txt`/`.md` file). Required unless the `resume` / `list` verbs or `--phase` is given. |
| `resume` (verb) | off | Resume an interrupted run. Auto-picks if exactly one run exists; pass the run-id if multiple. |
| `--run-id ID` | — | Select a specific run by id (e.g., for `resume` or `--phase` when multiple runs are in flight). |
| `list` (verb) | off | Enumerate in-flight and completed runs in this repository (run id, started, status, cost, branch). |
| `--no-push` | off | Skip the default push + PR at finalize. The run completes with the run branch local-only; your working branch is unchanged. Overrides `LEERIE_NO_PUSH` / `leerie.toml`. Sticky: a `resume` continues it (§2½ *Run choices on resume*). |
| `--push` | off | Push and open the PR at finalize even though the run recorded `no_push` (or `LEERIE_NO_PUSH` / `leerie.toml` says not to). The way to push a run started with `--no-push`: `leerie resume <id> --push`. `--no-push` wins when both are given. |
| `--no-verify` | off | Pass `--no-verify` to the finalize `git push` only (skips pre-push hooks). Worker commits inside worktrees still run all hooks. The user's explicit override per CLAUDE.md's hooks principle. |
| `--answers FILE` | — | JSON object of pre-supplied clarification answers (keyed by question `id`; may include `source_of_truth`). |
| `--clarify` | off | Opt into surfacing intent questions to the user. Default: questions are dropped after the classifier's codebase→research filter, and the implementer makes a documented best-effort decision. Also `LEERIE_CLARIFY` env var or `clarify = true` in `leerie.toml`. |
| `--max-workers N` | `2000` | Cap on total `claude -p` invocations across the run. Also `LEERIE_MAX_WORKERS` env var or `max_workers` in `leerie.toml`. |
| `--max-parallel N` | `5` | Cap on concurrent workers within a wave. Per-worker cgroup containment keeps an OOM inside one worker's cgroup; users on smaller VMs can opt down. Also `LEERIE_MAX_PARALLEL` env var or `max_parallel` in `leerie.toml`. |
| `--worker-memory-max SIZE` | auto | Per-worker cgroup memory cap (e.g. `4G`, `512M`). Bounds RAM the worker subtree may consume; OOMs stay inside the worker cgroup rather than cascading to sshd / orchestrator. Auto-derived when unset from the shared `leerie.slice` budget (`/proc/meminfo` only when no slice budget is readable). Raised automatically when the repo's own build/lint/test command declares a Node heap via `--max-old-space-size`; if you pin an explicit value **below** that declared heap plus headroom, leerie refuses at startup rather than issuing a cap that guarantees an in-cgroup OOM. Also `LEERIE_WORKER_MEMORY_MAX` (never `leerie.toml`). |
| `--worker-timeout SEC` | `5400` (90 min) | Global per-worker wall-clock ceiling. Setting it **bypasses** the measured per-worker table (`TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_PER_WORKER`), which otherwise lowers the ceiling for fast worker types — e.g. `classifier` to 1236 s — using a duration distribution measured on one host. Raise it when a worker is being killed at a ceiling derived on a faster machine. A bypass rather than a bound, so an explicit value wins outright in both directions; explicitly passing the default counts as setting it. Also `LEERIE_WORKER_TIMEOUT` or `worker_timeout_sec` in `leerie.toml`. |
| `--max-rate-limit-wait SEC` | `21600` (6 h) | Longest rate-limit reset `main()` will sleep through before it stops auto-resuming and takes the `out_of_credits` disposition instead (worktree-only cleanup, resume hint, `EXIT_LOCKED`). The five-hour session window is bounded and worth waiting out; the weekly window resets at a fixed per-account instant that can be days away, and sleeping on it holds the run-directory flock and blocks every other run on the repo. Keyed on the **computed wait**, never on `rateLimitType`, so a renamed limit type cannot silently disable it. Also `LEERIE_MAX_RATE_LIMIT_WAIT` or `max_rate_limit_wait_sec` in `leerie.toml`. |
| `--confidence-rounds N` | `8` | Evidence-gate rounds the planner and implementer may run before exiting blocked (DESIGN §8). Overrides `LEERIE_CONFIDENCE_ROUNDS` and `leerie.toml`. |
| `--skip-smoke` | off | Skip the live `claude -p` preflight smoke test. |
| `--source-of-truth VALUE` | `both` | `codebase` / `research` / `both`. Overrides `LEERIE_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH` and `leerie.toml`. |
| `--runtime VALUE` | `local` | `local` / `fly` / `ec2`. Execution backend for per-subtask worker containers. Overrides `LEERIE_RUNTIME` (never `leerie.toml`). `--runtime ec2` provisions an EC2 instance, seeds it, and runs the orchestrator on it, mirroring `--runtime fly`; see `docs/INSTALL.md` "EC2 runtime" (bakes and reuses a tagged AMI on first use unless `--ec2-ami` names one). |
| `--aws-region VALUE` | none | AWS region leerie itself uses when provisioning `--runtime ec2` machines. Distinct from the AWS SDK's own `AWS_REGION` credential-chain var. Also `LEERIE_AWS_REGION` env var (never `leerie.toml`). |
| `--aws-profile VALUE` | none | AWS profile leerie itself uses when provisioning `--runtime ec2` machines. Distinct from the AWS SDK's own `AWS_PROFILE` credential-chain var. Also `LEERIE_AWS_PROFILE` env var (never `leerie.toml`). |
| `--ec2-ami VALUE` | `ensure_ami()` bake/reuse (optional override) | AMI id for the `RunInstances` call. Also `LEERIE_EC2_AMI` env var (never `leerie.toml`). |
| `--ec2-instance-type VALUE` | `m5.xlarge` (optional override) | EC2 instance type (e.g. `t3.large`). Also `LEERIE_EC2_INSTANCE_TYPE` env var (never `leerie.toml`). |
| `--ec2-key-name VALUE` | leerie-tagged key pair (optional override) | EC2 key-pair name for SSH access. Also `LEERIE_EC2_KEY_NAME` env var (never `leerie.toml`). |
| `--ec2-security-group VALUE` | leerie-tagged group (tcp/22 from launcher egress `/32`) (optional override) | Security group id to attach. Also `LEERIE_EC2_SECURITY_GROUP` env var (never `leerie.toml`). |
| `--ec2-subnet-id VALUE` | default-VPC public subnet (optional override) | Subnet id to launch into. Also `LEERIE_EC2_SUBNET_ID` env var (never `leerie.toml`). |
| `--ec2-instance-profile VALUE` | none (optional) | IAM instance profile name passed as `--iam-instance-profile` to `RunInstances`. Also `LEERIE_EC2_INSTANCE_PROFILE` env var (never `leerie.toml`). |
| `--inspect-dir PATH` | none | Extra directory the inspect-bucket workers (classifier, planner, reconciler, plan_overlap_judge, provision, artifact_registry) may read; forwarded to `claude -p` as `--add-dir`. Repeatable. Also `LEERIE_INSPECT_DIRS` (colon-separated); no `leerie.toml` key. |
| `--model ALIAS` | per-worker (every worker → `sonnet`, except `pr_reviewer`, `intent_resolver`, `plan_item_checker` → `opus`) | `sonnet` / `opus` / `haiku`. Sets every worker this run; without it the per-worker defaults apply. |
| `--model-<worker> ALIAS` | per-worker default (every worker → `sonnet`, except `pr_reviewer`, `intent_resolver`, `plan_item_checker` → `opus`) | Per-worker override. `<worker>` is any `WORKER_TYPES` entry (listed under `LEERIE_MODEL_<WORKER>` below). Overrides `--model`, `LEERIE_MODEL`, and `leerie.toml`. |
| `--effort LEVEL` | per-worker (judgment: `medium`; implementer/conformer: `low`; `pr_reviewer`, `intent_resolver`, `plan_item_checker`: `high`) | `low` / `medium` / `high` / `xhigh` / `max`. Reasoning-depth dial forwarded to `claude -p --effort`. Pins judgment workers to a consistent depth across runs to reduce same-job variance (e.g. planner subtask-count drift); implementer/conformer are pinned to `low` for cost/latency. §2 "Effort selection". |
| `--effort-<worker> LEVEL` | per-worker default (judgment workers → `medium`; implementer/conformer → `low`; `pr_reviewer`, `intent_resolver`, `plan_item_checker` → `high`) | Per-worker override. `<worker>` is one of the orchestrator workers (same set as `--model-<worker>`). Overrides `--effort`, `LEERIE_EFFORT`, and `leerie.toml`. |
| `--judge-model ALIAS` | `sonnet` | Model alias for the post-run judge skill (absent from `MODEL_DEFAULT_PER_WORKER`, falls through to the global `MODEL_DEFAULT`). Also `LEERIE_MODEL_JUDGE` or `model_judge` in `leerie.toml`. |
| `--heal-model ALIAS` | `sonnet` | Model alias for the post-run self-heal skill. Also `LEERIE_MODEL_HEAL` or `model_heal` in `leerie.toml`. |
| `--heal-max-rounds N` | `10` | Maximum heal-loop iterations per `call_type`. Also `LEERIE_HEAL_MAX_ROUNDS` or `heal_max_rounds` in `leerie.toml`. |
| `--heal-success-threshold RATE` | `0.9` | Pass-rate threshold for the heal-loop SUCCESS verdict. Also `LEERIE_HEAL_SUCCESS_THRESHOLD` or `heal_success_threshold` in `leerie.toml`. |
| `--verbosity LEVEL` | `stream` | `quiet` / `normal` / `stream` / `debug`. Controls inline per-worker activity output; full per-worker stream is always saved to `<state-root>/runs/<run-id>/logs/transcripts/<sid>.log` (where `<state-root>` is the resolved state directory — default `$HOME/.leerie/<basename>/`). |
| `-v` / `-vv` | `0` (off) | Shortcuts that anchor to `normal`: `-v` = `stream`, `-vv` = `debug`. With no `-v` and no `--verbosity`, falls through to `LEERIE_VERBOSITY` / `leerie.toml` / default `stream`. |
| `-q` / `-qq` | `0` (off) | Shortcuts that anchor to `normal`: `-q` = `normal` (pre-streaming behavior), `-qq` = `quiet`. With no `-q` and no `--verbosity`, falls through to the same chain as `-v`. |
| `--judge-dir DIR` | `judge-out` | Subdirectory name under the run dir for LLM judge output. Also `LEERIE_JUDGE_DIR`; no `leerie.toml` key. |
| `--heal-dir DIR` | `heal-out` | Subdirectory name under the run dir for LLM self-heal output. Also `LEERIE_HEAL_DIR`; no `leerie.toml` key. |
| `--phase PHASE` | — | Run a post-run skill phase (`judge` or `heal`) against an existing run's captured LLM calls instead of starting a new run. Use `--run-id` to select when multiple runs exist. |
| `--report [RUN_ID]` | — | Print a read-only telemetry report for a run: per-call-type token/cost/latency/failure breakdown plus memory peak. Pass a run id, or omit to auto-pick when exactly one run exists. Exits without running orchestrate. |
| `--status STATE` | — | With `list`, restrict the table to runs whose derived status matches STATE. One of: `seed-failed`, `corrupt-sidecar`, `in-progress`, `done`, `done-pushed-no-pr`, `done-pushed-pr`, `push-failed`, `pr-failed`, `paused`, `killed`, `sync-failed`, `incomplete`, `other-leerie`. |
| `--skip-overlap-judge` | off | Skip the phase 2¾ plan-overlap judge (DESIGN §5). Auto-skipped on single-planner runs; this flag disables it on multi-planner runs. Also `LEERIE_SKIP_OVERLAP_JUDGE` (never `leerie.toml`). |
| `--skip-budget-check` | off | Skip the post-schedule budget-feasibility preflight (DESIGN §13). The runtime backstop in `State.bump_workers()` still fires. Also `LEERIE_SKIP_BUDGET_CHECK` (never `leerie.toml`). |
| `--skip-repo-map` | off | Skip the P6 repo-map structural context (DESIGN §5½ (P6)): suppresses `_build_repo_map()` and the ranked subgraph injection into planner/splitter context; the planner degrades gracefully to the prior grep/glob-only path. Use on repos where tree-sitter cannot parse the primary language. Also `LEERIE_SKIP_REPO_MAP` or `skip_repo_map` in `leerie.toml`. |
| `--skip-adherence-check` | off | Skip the instruction-adherence gate: the deterministic prescribed-command-coverage floor and the `adherence_judge` worker in `phase_adherence_gate` (a whole-plan gate, "Phase 2⅞", run after `phase_overlap_judge` and before `_schedule()`). A plan that diverges from an explicitly prescribed procedure is not caught before `phase_execute` spends. Also `LEERIE_SKIP_ADHERENCE_CHECK` (never `leerie.toml`). |
| `--skip-classification-check` | off | Skip `phase_classification_gate` (DESIGN §8) entirely: `classification_judge` never spawns and the classifier's own category set stands. The escape hatch for a gate that will not converge — it runs before any provision/plan spend and `die()`s on exhaustion, so a stuck gate otherwise takes the whole run. A miscategorized set produces the wrong planners, so prefer refining the task description first. Also `LEERIE_SKIP_CLASSIFICATION_CHECK` (never `leerie.toml`). |
| `--stop-on-blocked` | off | Stop the run and wait for `accept-blocked` when a subtask is still blocked after its re-drives from the shared budget, instead of settling it `unconverged`. Accepted on start and `resume`. Also `LEERIE_STOP_ON_BLOCKED` or `stop_on_blocked` in `leerie.toml`. |
| `--stop-on-repo-change` | off | Stop the run when the real checkout changes mid-run (new/edited files, or — even during execute — a commit, HEAD move or branch change), instead of logging a WARNING and continuing (DESIGN §12 L4). Accepted on start and `resume`. Also `LEERIE_STOP_ON_REPO_CHANGE` or `stop_on_repo_change` in `leerie.toml`. |
| `--skip-integration-check` | off | Skip the `integration_judge` behavioral-defect gate (DESIGN §8) entirely: no worker spawn for any subtask in this run. Independent of the accept-integration/audit-key mechanism, which only accepts a finding the judge already produced. Also `LEERIE_SKIP_INTEGRATION_CHECK` (never `leerie.toml`). |
| `--skip-acceptance-check` | off | Skip the held-out acceptance tests (DESIGN §8 *Held-out acceptance tests*): no `acceptance_writer` sets are written after the defect-scope audit and the post-integration acceptance gate does not run. Also `LEERIE_SKIP_ACCEPTANCE_CHECK` (never `leerie.toml`) in leerie.toml. |
| `--dangerously-skip-permissions` | off | Pass `--dangerously-skip-permissions` to every `claude -p` worker, including judgment workers that run in the real repo cwd. Waives DESIGN §12 read-only enforcement. Also `LEERIE_DANGEROUSLY_SKIP_PERMISSIONS` (never `leerie.toml`). |
| `--pr-template NAME` | none | When the target repo has multiple PR templates in `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/`, pick this one by basename (with or without `.md`). Also `LEERIE_PR_TEMPLATE` or `pr_template` in `leerie.toml`. |
| `--pr-base-branch BRANCH` | `working_branch` | Override the final branch this run's PR merges into (passed to `gh pr create --base`). The diff fork-point used to compute the PR diff is unaffected and always stays `working_branch`. Also `LEERIE_PR_BASE_BRANCH` or `pr_base_branch` in `leerie.toml`. |
| `--pr-writer-model ALIAS` | `sonnet` | Model alias for the finalize-time PR title + body writer. Also `LEERIE_MODEL_PR_WRITER` or `model_pr_writer` in `leerie.toml`. |

### Launcher verbs

These bare subcommands are handled by the bash launcher before the
container starts. A summary appears in the `leerie --help` epilog.

**`--help` / `-h` (no container required):** the launcher scans argv for an
exact `-h`/`--help` (stopping at `--`) right after resolving `LEERIE_REPO`,
before any state-dir, runtime, preflight, or provisioning work, and `exec`s
`python3 -I -B orchestrator/leerie.py --help` on the host; when `$1` is
`prune` it prints `prune`'s own usage (`_prune_usage`, also the `prune`
arm's) and exits 0 instead. No help answer resolves, checks or creates the
state root. Forwarding help
into the container ran the full run path first (including a machine
provision on `--runtime fly|ec2`) and then let the post-run finalize block
treat the exit 0 as a finished job. Pinned by
`tests/test_launcher_help_fast_path.py`.

**`list` and `--report` (no container required):** both only read
`<state-root>/runs/*`, so the launcher's `_exec_readonly_on_host` runs
`LEERIE_STATE_DIR=$LEERIE_STATE_HOST_DIR python3 -I -B orchestrator/leerie.py`
on the host. It is called at the end of the `list)` arm (so the
`list --runtime fly` view, `list chains` and `list --groups` keep their own
handling) and from a `--report` scan placed after the state-dir ownership
check. The argv is allowlisted (`list`, `--report [ID]`, `--run-id`,
`--runtime`, `--status`, and the launcher-only `--state-dir`, which is
dropped because it is already folded into `LEERIE_STATE_HOST_DIR`); any other
token, or no `python3`, returns and the invocation takes the container path
unchanged. An allowlist is used instead of a copy of the `REWRITTEN_ARGS`
launcher-only-flag filter so it cannot leak a launcher-only flag into the
orchestrator's strict argparse or drift from that list. Through the
container these verbs also ran the push preflights and the post-run finalize
block, which reported on a job that never ran. Pinned by
`tests/test_launcher_readonly_host_path.py`.

**bash 3.2 parse constraint:** a heredoc nested in `$( ... )` must not
contain an apostrophe, because macOS `/bin/bash` 3.2 scans the substitution for
quotes without understanding heredocs and a stray one inverts the quote parity
of everything after it. Pinned by `tests/test_launcher_bash32_parse.py`.

**Per-repo configuration (no container required):** `leerie config` is
a host-only fast path — it exits before `nerdctl run` and never starts
a container.

| Verb | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `config` | Print the effective build/lint/test config for this repo, with `[config]` or `[inference]` provenance for each axis. Also shows `leerie.toml` operational knobs when present. |
| `config --init` | Create `.leerie/config.toml` with auto-detected BLT commands (uncommented) and a commented `setup_packages` example. Errors if the file already exists. Prints the path and suggests `git add .leerie/`. |
| `config --chat` | Open an interactive `claude` session with a config-generation system prompt and `--add-dir` pointing at the current repo. The model can read the repo and write `.leerie/config.toml` (and optionally `.leerie/Dockerfile`). |
| `config --recapture` | Host-only (no container). Consolidates across **all** finished runs' logs (not just the newest) via the dep_capture LLM worker and **records** each run's capture in that run's `captured-deps.json`, for `config --apply-capture`. Never-clobber union when applied: already-captured runs (sentinel present) are skipped and only new packages are added. |
| `config --recapture --force` | Re-runs the worker over runs already captured (drops the `dep_capture.done` sentinel) and records a capture that, when applied, **wholesale-replaces** the persisted `setup_packages` — packages no longer captured are dropped. An empty capture leaves the existing config untouched (never blanks a good config). Use to re-derive deps from current run history. |
| `config --apply-capture <run-id>` | Host-only. Applies `<state>/runs/<run-id>/captured-deps.json` to `.leerie/config.toml` and logs the change as a unified diff (`host_apply_captured_deps` → `apply_captured_deps`); the only way a capture reaches the config (DESIGN §6½ *The operator applies a capture*). A capture `_capture_problems` refuses is kept and nothing is written (exit 1); so is one whose merge (any entry without `replace`) would keep a value `.leerie/config.toml` already holds that fails: `_config_capture_problems(cfg)` runs `_capture_problems` on its `setup_packages` items (`_split_setup_packages`), and the message names each failing entry. |

**Lifecycle (remote mode):**

| Verb | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `stop <run-id> [--runtime local\|fly\|ec2]` | Pause a run — a remote Fly machine, an EC2 instance (`stop-instances`, preserving the root EBS volume), or a local container. Resumable via `resume` (EC2 `resume` calls `resume_instance()` and re-resolves the reassigned public IP). |
| `kill <run-id> [--force]` | Destroy a remote machine permanently. `--force` skips confirmation. Also accepts `--machine-id <id> [--app <app>]` for orphan cleanup. |
| `finalize <run-id> [--force] [--no-verify] [--no-push] [--runtime local\|fly\|ec2]` | Finalization fast-path: get the run branch onto the host, then push + open PR. What "get it onto the host" means is runtime-dependent. **Fly/EC2:** collect un-integrated subtask branches on the machine and fetch the run branch; without `--force`, requires the orchestrator to be dead, and `--force` SIGTERMs a live one first (Fly only — the EC2 arm refuses it, since the force path is flyctl-transport). **Local:** there is nothing to fetch (the state root is bind-mounted and the branch is already in the user's repo), so it skips straight to `host_finalize`; `--force` is refused, because it exists to stop a *detached* orchestrator and a local run's exits with its container. Runtime is auto-detected from the run dir: `fly-machine.json` → fly, `ec2-instance.json` → ec2, **neither → local**. That last case also means a Fly/EC2 run whose sidecar has been deleted resolves to **local**: if its branch was never fetched to the host it reports "has no run branch in `$USER_REPO`" rather than reaching flyctl, and if the branch is already present it simply finalizes from it. Pass `--runtime fly` explicitly to override. `--no-push` finalizes without pushing: after the fetch the verb stops before `host_finalize`, on every runtime; without it the push follows the run's `run.json.no_push`. |
| `re-seed <run-id> [--force]` | Mid-run host→machine re-rsync of dirty delta. `--force` bypasses the safety check that refuses to clobber machine-side uncommitted edits. |
| `status <run-id\|chain-id\|group-id>` | Render run/chain/group state from `run.json`. |
| `attach <run-id\|chain-id>` | Poll `run.json` files every 5s. |
| `accept-blocked <run-id> <subtask-id> [--force]` | Accept a blocked subtask so `resume` skips it. `--force` also settles one abandoned mid-flight (e.g. after a crash), where neither status field records it as blocked. |
| `accept-integration <run-id> <subtask-id>` | Accept a recorded `integration_judge` finding for a subtask so `resume` stops re-invoking the judge for it. |
| `accept-heldout <run-id> <set>[/<case>] ...` | Accept held-out cases of a run as not required by its task: `<set>` is a held-out set number, `<set>/<case>` one case of it by the name the PR's `## Still failing when the run ended` section shows (or its whole ID, `<file> :: <title>`). `resume` then stops counting them as unfinished work, and the PR lists them under `## Held-out cases accepted by the operator`; a finished run's outcome is decided again and its open PR updated. See "Operator-accepted held-out cases" below. |
| `chain [--chain-id <uuid>] --wave <files> [--wave <files>] ...` | Submit or resume a multi-run chain. `status`/`kill`/`resume`/`finalize`/`attach <chain-id>` and `list --chains` also operate on chains (see "Chain verbs" below). |
| `group --repo <path> "<prompt>" [--repo ...] [--brief <file>] [--group-id <uuid>]` | Fan-out launcher for N single-repo runs sharing a `group_id`. `status`/`kill`/`resume`/`finalize <group-id>` and `list --groups` also operate on groups (see "Run-group verbs" below). |
| `version` | Print `leerie <version>` and exit. |

`resume` and `list` are documented in the "CLI flags" table above (they interact with the `task` positional and `--run-id`/`--phase`); the rest of the bare verbs are listed here.

**Resume modifiers (used with `resume`):**

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--shell` | Drop into a bash shell at `/work` on the machine instead of tailing the orchestrator log. |
| `--auto-finalize` | On clean orchestrator exit, automatically run `leerie finalize`. |
| `--no-re-seed` | Skip the automatic re-seed of dirty delta on resume. |

**Build and runtime:**

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--state-dir PATH` | Override the per-repo state directory. Also `LEERIE_STATE_DIR` env var; no `leerie.toml` key. Never at, inside or above the checkout. |
| `--fly-app NAME` | Fly.io app name (required for `--runtime fly`; globally unique). Also `LEERIE_FLY_APP` env var. |
| `--fly-disk-gb N` | Provision a Fly volume of N GB mounted at `/home/leerie`. Also `FLY_VM_DISK_GB` env var. |
| `--no-runtime-install` | Skip auto-install of container runtime (Colima / nerdctl / containerd). Also `LEERIE_NO_RUNTIME_INSTALL`. |
| `--no-auto-publish` | Skip the image-publish probe on startup. Also `LEERIE_NO_AUTO_PUBLISH`. |
| `--local-build` | Force local `nerdctl build` instead of the Fly remote builder. Also `LEERIE_LOCAL_BUILD`. |

### Environment variables and `leerie.toml` keys

Source of each setting: the env var (and its flag) is the operator's. The
`leerie.toml` key column names the key a repository's `leerie.toml` may set,
the repository's own fact or preference, which the operator's flag and env
var override. `—` means no `leerie.toml` key; `— (operator only)` marks a
setting that carries the operator's authority, and a `leerie.toml` that sets
its key stops the launcher, naming this env var or flag (§2 *Repository
configuration chooses no operator authority*). The checkout's
`.claude/settings*.json` count as the operator's only while git does not
track them (same section).

| Env var | `leerie.toml` key | Description |
|---------|---------------------|-------------|
| `LEERIE_STATE_DIR` | — | Override the per-repo run state directory. A location, so no `leerie.toml` key: a `state_dir` there stops the launcher (§2 *Repository configuration names no location*). Never at, inside or above the checkout. Unset → default `$HOME/.leerie/<basename>/` (outside the repo; no `.gitignore` entry needed in target projects). Cross-repo basename collisions are caught at use time via an `.owner` sidecar inside the dir. Set once in your shell profile for a global directory across all repos. |
| `LEERIE_HOST_DIR` | — | Launcher-only: the host directory mounted at `/leerie-host`, where the host-wide build semaphore keeps its slot files (DESIGN §6 *A host-wide build semaphore*). Unset → `~/.leerie/.host`, which must stay the default: the semaphore bounds only runs that share one directory, so repoint it only for a run that must be isolated from the host's other runs (a bench that must never touch `~/.leerie`). Must be absolute (`~/` expands); a relative path is refused. Not forwarded into the container: there the launcher sets `LEERIE_HOST_DIR=/leerie-host`, the mount point `_build_sem_dir` reads. |
| `LEERIE_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH` | `source_of_truth` | Sticky source-of-truth preference (`codebase` / `research` / `both`). Overridden by `--source-of-truth`. Unset → default `both`. |
| `LEERIE_RUNTIME` | — (operator only) | Execution backend for per-subtask worker containers (`local` / `fly` / `ec2`). Overridden by `--runtime`. Unset → default `local`. |
| `LEERIE_MODEL` | `model` | Model alias applied to every worker. Overridden by `--model` and per-worker overrides. Unset → every worker defaults to `sonnet`, except `pr_reviewer`, `contradiction_judge`, `intent_resolver` and `plan_item_checker` → `opus`. |
| `LEERIE_MODEL_<WORKER>` | `model_<worker>` | Per-worker override (e.g. `LEERIE_MODEL_IMPLEMENTER=opus`). Overridden by `--model-<worker>`. `<worker>` ∈ every `WORKER_TYPES` entry: `classifier`, `planner`, `reconciler`, `plan_overlap_judge`, `satisfied_probe`, `provision`, `implementer`, `integrator`, `conformer`, `fit_judge`, `splitter`, `adherence_judge`, `classification_judge`, `wiring_judge`, `provision_judge`, `task_coverage_judge`, `artifact_registry`, `integration_judge`, `no_work_judge`, `delivery_judge`, `defect_scope_auditor`, `rebaser`, `acceptance_writer`, `set_auditor`, `surrogate_fixer`, `ci_checks`, `scope_judge`, `pr_reviewer`, `contract_extractor`, `falsifier`, `verifiability_classifier`, `delivery_ratchet`, `forbidden_command_extractor`, `observability_judge`, `contradiction_judge`, `intent_resolver`, `plan_item_checker`. Unset → every worker → `sonnet`, except `pr_reviewer`, `contradiction_judge`, `intent_resolver` and `plan_item_checker` → `opus`. |
| `LEERIE_EFFORT` | `effort` | Reasoning-depth dial forwarded to `claude -p --effort` (`low` / `medium` / `high` / `xhigh` / `max`). Applies to every worker; overridden by `--effort` and per-worker overrides. Unset → judgment workers `medium`, implementer/conformer `low`, `pr_reviewer` `high`, everything else inherits Claude default. |
| `LEERIE_EFFORT_<WORKER>` | `effort_<worker>` | Per-worker override (e.g. `LEERIE_EFFORT_PLANNER=max`). Overridden by `--effort-<worker>`. Same worker set as `LEERIE_MODEL_<WORKER>`. Unset → judgment workers `medium`; `pr_reviewer` `high`; implementer/conformer `low`; `satisfied_probe` unset. |
| `LEERIE_CONFIDENCE_ROUNDS` | `confidence_rounds` | Evidence-gate rounds per worker (positive integer). Overridden by `--confidence-rounds`. Unset → default `8`. |
| `LEERIE_INSPECT_DIRS` | — | Extra directories the inspect-bucket workers (classifier, planner, reconciler, plan_overlap_judge, provision, artifact_registry) may read; forwarded as `--add-dir`. Colon-separated. A location, so no `leerie.toml` key. Overridden by `--inspect-dir` (repeatable). Unset → none. |
| `LEERIE_VERBOSITY` | `verbosity` | Inline-output verbosity (`quiet` / `normal` / `stream` / `debug`). Overridden by `--verbosity`. `-v` / `-vv` / `-q` / `-qq` shortcuts override both. Unset → default `stream`. |
| `LEERIE_NO_PUSH` | `no_push` | Sticky opt-out from push + PR at finalize (truthy → skip). Overridden by `--no-push`. `--no-verify` has no env/TOML mirror — it is a per-invocation override only. Unset → default `false` (push + PR happen). |
| `LEERIE_SKIP_FRESHNESS_CHECK` | — | Truthy → skip host preflight step 5, the stale-base refusal (`host_base_freshness_check` — DESIGN §6 *A fresh run refuses a stale base*): a fresh run whose HEAD is strictly behind its remote upstream — or, with no usable upstream, behind a same-named origin branch — refuses to start, because it would re-solve merged work and its finalize rebase can land the older solution over the newer one (measured). Env-only, mirroring `LEERIE_SKIP_PREPUSH_PREFLIGHT` — an argv flag would leak into the orchestrator's argparse passthrough. Fresh runs only; resume never runs the check. |
| `LEERIE_RUN_END_GRACE_S` | — | Launcher-only, local runtime: how many seconds the launcher keeps waiting on the container runtime once its run has recorded its end (`orchestrator.exit_code`). Past that, it finishes from the run directory when the host's `/proc` shows no process of the container is left. It is also the bound on the container's removal after such a finish (DESIGN §6 *A launch's host-side work starts when its run has ended*). It never bounds a run that has not ended. Unset or not digits → `60`. |
| `LEERIE_CLARIFY` | `clarify` | Sticky opt-in to surfacing intent questions to the user (truthy → on). Overridden by `--clarify`. Unset → default `false`. |
| `LEERIE_MODEL_JUDGE` | `model_judge` | Model alias for the post-run judge skill. Overridden by `--judge-model`. Unset → default `sonnet` (absent from `MODEL_DEFAULT_PER_WORKER`, falls through to the global `MODEL_DEFAULT`). |
| `LEERIE_MODEL_HEAL` | `model_heal` | Model alias for the post-run self-heal skill. Overridden by `--heal-model`. Unset → default `sonnet`. |
| `LEERIE_HEAL_MAX_ROUNDS` | `heal_max_rounds` | Maximum heal-loop iterations per `call_type`. Overridden by `--heal-max-rounds`. Unset → default `10`. |
| `LEERIE_HEAL_SUCCESS_THRESHOLD` | `heal_success_threshold` | Pass-rate threshold for the heal-loop SUCCESS verdict. Overridden by `--heal-success-threshold`. Unset → default `0.9`. |
| `LEERIE_JUDGE_DIR` | — | Subdirectory name under the run dir for LLM judge output. Overridden by `--judge-dir`. Unset → default `judge-out`. |
| `LEERIE_HEAL_DIR` | — | Subdirectory name under the run dir for LLM self-heal output. Overridden by `--heal-dir`. Unset → default `heal-out`. |
| `LEERIE_MAX_WORKERS` | `max_workers` | Total worker-invocation budget. Overridden by `--max-workers`. Unset → default `2000`. |
| `LEERIE_MAX_PARALLEL` | `max_parallel` | Concurrent workers per wave. Overridden by `--max-parallel`. Unset → default `5`. |
| `LEERIE_WORKER_MEMORY_MAX` | — (operator only) | Per-worker cgroup memory cap (e.g. `4G`, `512M`). Overridden by `--worker-memory-max`. Unset → auto-derived from the shared `leerie.slice` budget (`/proc/meminfo` only as a fallback), and raised automatically when the repo declares a Node heap — see the `--worker-memory-max` row above. |
| `LEERIE_WORKER_PIDS_MAX` | — (operator only) | Per-worker cgroup PID cap (positive integer). Overridden by `--worker-pids-max`. Unset → default `2048`. |
| `LEERIE_WORKER_TIMEOUT` | `worker_timeout_sec` | Global per-worker wall-clock ceiling in seconds. Overridden by `--worker-timeout`. Setting it at any tier bypasses the measured per-worker timeout table — see the `--worker-timeout` row above. Unset → default `5400` and the table applies. |
| `LEERIE_MAX_RATE_LIMIT_WAIT` | `max_rate_limit_wait_sec` | Longest rate-limit reset to sleep through, in seconds. Overridden by `--max-rate-limit-wait`. Unset → default `21600` (6 h). Beyond it, the run pauses resumably rather than sleeping — see the `--max-rate-limit-wait` row above. |
| `LEERIE_DANGEROUSLY_SKIP_PERMISSIONS` | — (operator only) | Waive §12 read-only enforcement on judgment workers (truthy → on). Overridden by `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. Unset → default `false`. |
| `LEERIE_DANGEROUSLY_ALLOW_UNCAPPED` | — (operator only) | Run workers uncapped when the cgroup broker probe fails, with a loud warning instead of a fatal error (truthy → on). Overridden by `--dangerously-allow-uncapped`. Unset → default `false`. |
| `LEERIE_DANGEROUSLY_FORCE_STRICT_OUTPUT` | — (operator only) | Force constrained decoding through the per-run loopback proxy (truthy → on). Overridden by `--dangerously-force-strict-output`. Unset → default `false`. |
| `LEERIE_SKIP_OVERLAP_JUDGE` | — (operator only) | Skip the phase 2¾ plan-overlap judge on multi-planner runs (truthy → skip). Overridden by `--skip-overlap-judge`. Unset → default `false`. |
| `LEERIE_SKIP_ACCEPTANCE_CHECK` | — (operator only) | Skip the held-out acceptance sets and gate (truthy → skip). Overridden by `--skip-acceptance-check`. Unset → default `false`. |
| `LEERIE_SKIP_BUDGET_CHECK` | — (operator only) | Skip the post-schedule budget-feasibility preflight (truthy → skip). Overridden by `--skip-budget-check`. Unset → default `false`. |
| `LEERIE_SKIP_REPO_MAP` | `skip_repo_map` | Skip the P6 repo-map structural context injection (truthy → skip). Overridden by `--skip-repo-map`. Unset → default `false`. |
| `LEERIE_SKIP_ADHERENCE_CHECK` | — (operator only) | Skip the instruction-adherence gate (deterministic command-coverage floor + `adherence_judge`) (truthy → skip). Overridden by `--skip-adherence-check`. Unset → default `false`. |
| `LEERIE_SKIP_CLASSIFICATION_CHECK` | — (operator only) | Skip the `classification_judge` category-set gate entirely (truthy → skip). Overridden by `--skip-classification-check`. Unset → default `false`. |
| `LEERIE_STOP_ON_BLOCKED` | `stop_on_blocked` | Halt on a subtask still blocked after its re-drives rather than settling it `unconverged` (truthy → halt). Overridden by `--stop-on-blocked`. Unset → default `false`. |
| `LEERIE_STOP_ON_REPO_CHANGE` | `stop_on_repo_change` | Halt when the real checkout changes mid-run rather than warning and continuing (truthy → halt). Overridden by `--stop-on-repo-change`. Unset → default `false`. |
| `LEERIE_SKIP_INTEGRATION_CHECK` | — (operator only) | Skip the `integration_judge` behavioral-defect gate entirely (truthy → skip). Overridden by `--skip-integration-check`. Unset → default `false`. |
| `LEERIE_SKIP_SATISFIED_CHECK` | — (operator only) | Skip the plan-time `satisfied_probe` (truthy → skip). Overridden by `--skip-satisfied-check`. Unset → default `false`. |
| `LEERIE_SKIP_BASE_BASELINE` | — (operator only) | Skip the base-tree health baseline (truthy → skip). Overridden by `--skip-base-baseline`. Unset → default `false`. |
| `LEERIE_SKIP_COVERAGE_CHECK` | — (operator only) | Skip the required-items coverage review and the phase-5 delivery gate (truthy → skip). Overridden by `--skip-coverage-check`. Unset → default `false`. |
| `LEERIE_SKIP_COMPLETENESS_CHECK` | — (operator only) | Make the conformer's `solution_defects` axis advisory (truthy → skip). Overridden by `--skip-completeness-check`. Unset → default `false`. |
| `LEERIE_PR_TEMPLATE` | `pr_template` | PR template basename for repos with multiple templates. Overridden by `--pr-template`. Unset → alphabetically first `.md`. |
| `LEERIE_PR_BASE_BRANCH` | `pr_base_branch` | Final branch this run's PR merges into. Overridden by `--pr-base-branch`. Unset → default `working_branch`. |
| `LEERIE_MODEL_PR_WRITER` | `model_pr_writer` | Model alias for the finalize-time PR writer. Overridden by `--pr-writer-model`. Unset → default `sonnet`. |
| `LEERIE_MODEL_DEP_CAPTURE` | *(none)* | Model alias for the finalize-time dep_capture worker. Env var only — no per-worker CLI flag and no `leerie.toml` key (it still honors the global `model` key / `--model`). Unset → default `sonnet`. |
| `LEERIE_CAPTURE_DEPS` | `capture_deps` (`.leerie/config.toml` only — not `leerie.toml`) | Enable finalize-time dependency capture (truthy → on). Precedence: `LEERIE_CAPTURE_DEPS` > `.leerie/config.toml` > default `true`. Set to `false` / `0` to disable entirely. |
| `LEERIE_WORKER_DEBUG` | — | Enable debug-level logging injection (`DEBUG=*`, `ANTHROPIC_LOG=debug`) into worker processes. Truthy → on. |
| `LEERIE_FLY_APP` | — | Fly.io app name (globally unique). Required when `--runtime fly`. Set via env or `--fly-app`. Launcher-only. |
| `LEERIE_REGION` | — | Fly region used by per-job `--runtime fly` machines (including those spawned by `leerie chain`). Unset → default `iad`. Launcher-only. |
| `LEERIE_AWS_REGION` | — (operator only) | AWS region leerie itself uses when provisioning `--runtime ec2` machines — distinct from the AWS SDK's own `AWS_REGION` credential-chain env var. Overridden by `--aws-region`. Unset → default `None` (region selection left to the AWS credential chain). |
| `LEERIE_AWS_PROFILE` | — (operator only) | AWS profile leerie itself uses when provisioning `--runtime ec2` machines — distinct from the AWS SDK's own `AWS_PROFILE` credential-chain env var. Overridden by `--aws-profile`. Unset → default `None`. |
| `LEERIE_EC2_AMI` | — (operator only) | AMI id for the `--runtime ec2` `RunInstances` call. Overridden by `--ec2-ami`. Optional override; default: `ensure_ami()` bake/reuse. Launcher-only. |
| `LEERIE_EC2_INSTANCE_TYPE` | — (operator only) | EC2 instance type (e.g. `t3.large`). Overridden by `--ec2-instance-type`. Optional override; default: `m5.xlarge`. Launcher-only. |
| `LEERIE_EC2_KEY_NAME` | — (operator only) | EC2 key-pair name for SSH access. Overridden by `--ec2-key-name`. Optional override; default: leerie-tagged key pair. Launcher-only. |
| `LEERIE_EC2_SECURITY_GROUP` | — (operator only) | Security group id to attach. Overridden by `--ec2-security-group`. Optional override; default: leerie-tagged group (tcp/22 from launcher egress `/32`). Launcher-only. |
| `LEERIE_EC2_SUBNET_ID` | — (operator only) | Subnet id to launch into. Overridden by `--ec2-subnet-id`. Optional override; default: default-VPC public subnet. Launcher-only. |
| `LEERIE_EC2_INSTANCE_PROFILE` | — (operator only) | IAM instance profile name for `RunInstances`. Overridden by `--ec2-instance-profile`. Optional; default: optionally a leerie-tagged SSM profile. Launcher-only. |
| `LEERIE_EC2_SSH_KEY_FILE` | — | Private key ssh uses for the EC2 instance. Unset → leerie's own key at `~/.leerie/.ec2-keys/<account>/<region>/leerie-ssh.pem` when `LEERIE_EC2_KEY_NAME` is unset; set it to the private half of an explicit `LEERIE_EC2_KEY_NAME`. Launcher-only. |
| `LEERIE_EC2_SSH_CIDR` | — | CIDR admitted on tcp/22 by leerie's default security group. Unset → the launcher's egress IPv4 as a `/32`; `0.0.0.0/0` is refused. Launcher-only. |
| `LEERIE_EC2_IAM_RETRY_S` | — | Seconds between `run-instances` retries while EC2 rejects a just-created instance profile. Unset → `5`. Launcher-only. |
| `LEERIE_EC2_IAM_RETRY_BUDGET_S` | — | Total seconds to keep retrying that rejection before failing. Unset → `120`. Launcher-only. |
| `LEERIE_EC2_AMI_WAIT_S` | — | Seconds to wait for a baked AMI to become `available`. Unset → `3600`. Launcher-only. |
| `LEERIE_EC2_BAKE_BASE_AMI` | — | Stock AMI the bake starts from. Unset → the public SSM parameter `/aws/service/debian/release/13/latest/amd64`. Launcher-only. |
| `LEERIE_EC2_BAKE_SSH_RETRIES` | — | SSH reachability attempts on the bake instance. Unset → `60`. Launcher-only. |
| `LEERIE_EC2_BAKE_POLL_S` | — | Seconds between bake polls (SSH reachability, instance state, image state). Unset → `5`. Launcher-only. |
| `LEERIE_EC2_BAKE_WAIT_TRIES` | — | Instance-state polls (running, stopped) before the bake gives up. Unset → `120`. Launcher-only. |
| `LEERIE_SEED_TIMEOUT_S` | — | Timeout in seconds for `seed_auth` / `seed_repo` bulk transfers over `flyctl ssh console`. Unset → default `600` (10 min). Launcher-only. |
| `LEERIE_PROGRESS_INTERVAL_S` | — | Heartbeat cadence in seconds for "still streaming" lines during bulk transfers. Set to `0` to suppress. Unset → default `10`. Launcher-only. |
| `LEERIE_MACHINE_START_TIMEOUT` | — | Timeout in seconds for Fly machine start. Unset → default `120`. Launcher-only. |
| `LEERIE_PAUSE_NOTIFY_CMD` | — | Shell command to `eval` when a Fly machine pauses on failure. Unset → no notification. Launcher-only. |
| `LEERIE_NO_RUNTIME_INSTALL` | — | Skip auto-install of container runtime (truthy → skip). Also `--no-runtime-install`. Launcher-only. |
| `LEERIE_NO_AUTO_PUBLISH` | — | Skip image publish probe (truthy → skip). Also `--no-auto-publish`. Launcher-only. |
| `LEERIE_LOCAL_BUILD` | — | Force local image build instead of Fly remote builder (truthy → local). Also `--local-build`. Launcher-only. |
| `LEERIE_NONINTERACTIVE` | — | Suppress interactive prompts in runtime-install and auth flows (truthy → non-interactive). Launcher-only. |
| `FLY_VM_DISK_GB` | — (operator only) | Provision a Fly volume of this many GB. Also `--fly-disk-gb`. Launcher-only. |
| `CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE` | — | **Claude Code CLI variable**, not consumed by leerie. Set to `70` to backstop worker auto-compaction. |

### Precedence

- **Source-of-truth** (highest first): `--source-of-truth` →
  `LEERIE_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH` → `leerie.toml` → default `both`.
- **Model** (per worker, highest first): `--model-<worker>` →
  `--model` → `LEERIE_MODEL_<WORKER>` → `LEERIE_MODEL` →
  `model_<worker>` in `leerie.toml` → `model` in `leerie.toml` →
  per-worker default → global default (every worker resolves to
  `sonnet` today, except `pr_reviewer`, `intent_resolver` and
  `plan_item_checker`, which resolve to `opus`). To opt a specific worker into Opus-grade reasoning,
  set `LEERIE_MODEL_<WORKER>=opus` or pass `--model-<worker> opus`.
- **EC2 knobs** (`ec2_ami`, `ec2_instance_type`, `ec2_key_name`,
  `ec2_security_group`, `ec2_subnet_id`, `ec2_instance_profile`; highest
  first): `--ec2-<knob>` → `LEERIE_EC2_<KNOB>` → the zero-config default from `ec2-defaults.sh` / `ec2-ami.sh`. None
  is required.
- **Confidence rounds** (highest first): `--confidence-rounds` →
  `LEERIE_CONFIDENCE_ROUNDS` → `confidence_rounds` in
  `leerie.toml` → default `8`.
- **Verbosity** (highest first): `--verbosity` → `-v`/`-vv`/`-q`/`-qq`
  shortcuts (anchored to `normal`, not to the resolved default) →
  `LEERIE_VERBOSITY` → `verbosity` in `leerie.toml` → default
  `stream`.

See §2 above for the rationale behind these orders and the full
validation contract.

### Run choices on resume

DESIGN §6 *A resumed run continues under the choices it was started with*.
Every flag and knob in this section has exactly one class:

- **sticky** — a choice about what the run does or where its result goes.
  The fresh run records it in `state.json` under the key in the first
  column. `main()` continues it on `resume` (`_continue_run_choices`)
  before anything reads it. A flag in the second column given on the
  resume's command line overrides it, and the override is appended to
  `run_choice_overrides`. The resume's environment and `leerie.toml` never
  override a recorded value. They count only for a run recorded before the
  key existed (`no_push` first falls back to `run.json.no_push`).
  `run_caps`, `models` and `efforts` are continued per entry:
  `--model-planner opus` on a resume changes only the planner, and
  `--model` changes every model. An overridden entry takes its value from
  the command line alone (its own flag, else the global one): a worker's
  own env var such as `LEERIE_MODEL_JUDGE`, which outranks `--model` on a
  fresh run, does not reach a recorded run through an override.
- **per-invocation** — belongs to the invocation or to the host it runs on.
  Each invocation resolves it again (CLI → env → `leerie.toml` → default).
- **sidecar** — recorded by the launcher or the fresh run in a sidecar
  (`run.json`, `fly-machine.json`, `ec2-instance.json`) and read back from
  there on `resume`. This mechanism does not handle these.

`RUN_CHOICES_STICKY` (with `RUN_CAPS_STICKY`), `RUN_OPTIONS_PER_INVOCATION`
and `RUN_OPTIONS_SIDECAR` in `orchestrator/leerie.py` hold the same three
classes for the orchestrator's own options. `tests/test_run_choices_on_resume.py`
fails when a flag or knob in this §2½ or an orchestrator option has no row
here, when this table and the code give an orchestrator option different
classes, or when `main()` reads a sticky choice before the continuation.

The push choice has a second record, `run.json.no_push`. It is the record
the host reads. Its one writer, `_record_run_push_choice`, writes
`args.no_push` (the continued choice) or `true` while the run has nothing
to push; `main()` calls it on every non-`--phase` invocation, after the
continuation. The launcher resolves its
own `NO_PUSH` as follows: `--no-push`, then `--push`,
then (on `resume`) `run.json.no_push` of the run it resumes — the id on
the command line, or for a bare `resume` on the local runtime the one the
launcher gets by loading `orchestrator/leerie.py` host-side and calling its
`resolve_run_id(<state root>, None, resumable_only=True)` —
then `LEERIE_NO_PUSH`
and `no_push` in `leerie.toml`. `--no-push` wins over `--push` in both the
launcher and the orchestrator. On a fresh run the launcher hands a resolved
`NO_PUSH=true` to the orchestrator as `--no-push`, on every runtime (one
block, before the runtime branches), because neither the container nor a
remote machine sees the host's `LEERIE_NO_PUSH`. On a resume it adds
nothing: only the resume's own `--no-push` / `--push` reach the
orchestrator, which continues its record. No host-side reader rewrites
`run.json.no_push` (DESIGN §6 *One push choice per run, on every runtime*).

|--------|-------|-----------------------------|-------|-----|

| `clarify` | `--clarify` | `LEERIE_CLARIFY` / `clarify` | sticky | what the run asks |

### Worker types

Leerie spawns the thirty-three `claude -p` worker types in `WORKER_TYPES`.
Each is a separate subprocess; there is no in-session agent nesting. (The
table predates `task_coverage_judge`, `integration_judge` and `rebaser`,
which are specified in their own sections.)

| Worker | Prompt source | Default model | Runs per task | Returns |
|--------|---------------|---------------|---------------|---------|
| `classifier` | `prompts/classifier.md` | sonnet | 1 | category set + intent questions |
| `classification_judge` | `prompts/classification_judge.md` | sonnet | 0 or 1 (phase 1½, adversarial re-check of the classifier's category set) | `{categories_reviewed[], miscategorizations[], rationale}` — independent verification the classifier's category set covers the task. DESIGN §8 *Independent adversarial verification* |
| `no_work_judge` | `prompts/no_work_judge.md` | sonnet | 0 or 1 (phase 1½, only when the gate converges with `likely_already_satisfied` + evidence; suppressed by `--skip-satisfied-check`) | `{confirmed: bool, evidence: str, checked?[]}` — independently re-verifies the classifier's already-satisfied claim against the current checkout (SATISFIED_PROBE_TOOLS scope); only `confirmed: true` with non-empty evidence routes to `_finish_no_work_run` — held first as `no_work_pending` when `_acceptance_can_check(st)` holds; a dispute with non-empty evidence persists `state.data["no_work_dispute"]` (consumed by `phase_plan`'s ctx — DESIGN §8 *A dispute's evidence is planning input, not log noise*) and falls through to planning; everything else falls through with nothing persisted. DESIGN §8 *The healthy-path consumer* |
| `defect_scope_auditor` | `prompts/defect_scope_auditor.md` | sonnet | 0–6 (phase 2, after the artifact registry, only when categories include `bug-fixing`; when the first answer is `applicable: false`, further independent samples up to `caps["applicability_samples"]` (3) votes — the first `applicable: true` is used, false stands only when every vote says so, a crashed sample is no vote and is drawn again within two extra attempts, budget exhaustion propagates — DESIGN §5 *`applicable: false` is honoured only when three samples agree*; plus one call on the one-shot empty-enumeration re-ask below; the first answer's check loop re-asks, within `judgment_check_rounds` (3) calls, while a site's `sweep` matches nothing or is over the sweep limits — `_site_sweep_issues` — or its `reading` is inconsistent — `_reading_issues`) | `{applicable, defect_shape?, reading: {kind: "one_reading"\|"narrow_or_broad", narrow, broad}, sites: [{file, symbol, line_hint?, role, note?, extent: "one_place"\|"pattern", sweep?, reading?: "both"\|"broad_only"}], chokepoint?: {exists, file?, symbol?, rationale?}, ground_truth?: {data_dependent, inputs: [{path, kind: "file"\|"directory", role, resolved_path}], repro_command}, rationale?}` — enumerates every site implementing the task's defective decision idiom on the base tree (roles: decision_site/producer/consumer/bypass) and whether a single-point fix exists; an unconfirmed-cause symptom report with multiple candidate mechanisms IS applicable (shape = the violated behavioral contract, sites = the candidate mechanisms — DESIGN §5 *The applicability trigger includes unconfirmed-cause reports*, measured after 2/2 live declines on a task whose report named multiple candidate mechanisms while each run's plan carried at most one); `ground_truth` is the report's evidence basis (DESIGN §5 *Report-named ground truth is extracted and mechanically checked* / *Resolution is the auditor's judgment*): report-named external input paths verbatim plus the report's own repro command, each input also carrying the schema-REQUIRED `resolved_path` (null = unfound; an attestation the gate's presence check depends on must not be skippable by omission — the `change_shape` precedent; `repro_command` is required for the same reason) — the in-container location the AUDITOR verified it reachable at (the verbatim path when it exists; a mounted /inspect location it confirmed by reading; null when unfound — never invented, the sites' no-fabrication bar; identity between a host path and a mounted copy is semantic judgment, deliberately NOT a Python path heuristic). `phase_defect_scope_audit` existence-checks mechanically (`_check_ground_truth_inputs`, resolved-path-first with verbatim fallback), logging any absence loudly with the `--inspect-dir` remediation and persisting per-input `present`/`resolved_path` on the state; an `applicable: true` result with empty `sites` is re-asked ONCE with a corrective message naming the misfiling (`_REASK_EMPTY_SITES_MSG` — measured: a live audit returned its full 8-site enumeration embedded as JSON text inside `defect_shape` with `sites: []`; the second answer is honored either way, still fail-open — DESIGN §5 *An applicable audit with zero sites is re-asked once*); persisted to `state.data["defect_scope"]`, injected into every planner's ctx (each covering subtask states its site-scoped done-state plus the shape as the campaign contract it serves — informational per DESIGN §9, not a gate), held by the bug-fixing planner's loop to the typed site claims (`_check_site_claims`). Best-effort/non-fatal on the artifact-registry model. DESIGN §5 *Defect-scope audit* |
| `delivery_judge` | `prompts/delivery_judge.md` | sonnet | 0–6 per pack (phase 5 delivery gate: `_d1_judge_packs` cuts the judge-bound items into root-ancestor packs of at most `d1_pack_items` (20) items, a group over 30 chunked at 30; per pack 1 on a clean first pass, 3 when its first sample flags something or leaves an item unknown, plus per sample at most one follow-up (two when it inspected none of its pack) for the items it left uninspected (`_delivery_uninspected`, `_delivery_reask_chunks`), ×2 when a recheck runs after the final-conformer pass; 0 when `required_items` is empty, `--skip-coverage-check`, staging/`working_branch` absent, or every item is `external` or settled by the untouched-paths check with no contract asked) | `{verdicts: [{item_index, met, parts[{requirement, kind: static|behavioral|test_outcome, status: met|unmet|not_inspected, cites[{path, line_start, line_end, quote}]}], evidence}], contract?: {verdict: "met"|"unmet"|"conflict"|"unverifiable", evidence, conflicting_contracts?[]}, rationale?}` — verifies each required item against the integrated staging tree, and — when the run carries an applicable defect audit with non-empty sites — additionally returns the typed finding-level contract verdict (DESIGN §8 *The gate judges the finding, not only the items*; budget +12 turns when asked); `unverifiable` is the honesty verdict for a data-triggered contract whose report-named ground-truth inputs are absent in-container (the payload states which, from the audit's mechanically-checked `ground_truth`; bench-measured 2/2 flips from a silent `met` on a live run's verbatim payload), and the orchestrator enforces it mechanically — `_downgrade_ungrounded_met` records a `met` majority as `unverifiable` (raw claim preserved in `judge_claimed`) whenever the audit says `data_dependent` and every named input is absent; `unverifiable` never routes to the conformer (nothing on the tree to fix) but persists, steers via `prior_delivery_residual`, and is stated loudly at whichever gate half records it — the pre-pass (the final-tree conformance pass still follows) or, when a recheck forced by the pre-pass's unmet items or unmet contract lands unverifiable, the recheck directly before finalize (`_log_contract_unverifiable` at both call sites — the data-absence narrative and `--inspect-dir` remediation only when the audit's own record established the case, data-dependent with named inputs absent, mirroring `_check_ground_truth_inputs`' warning gate; any other voted unverifiable states the judge's evidence instead); the PRESENT case is the converse duty (DESIGN §8, same paragraph): when every input resolves present and the audit carries a repro command, the availability section names the resolved locations and the judge is directed that the record's repro evidence DECIDES the contract — a met resting only on synthetic fixtures while the repro was never run must state why in-tree evidence suffices, else return an ACTIONABLE unmet naming the unexecuted repro (bench-measured 2/2 on the live recheck payload), which rides the ordinary final-conformer route (an acting worker with execution rights) and shows in the recheck's fresh digest; planners are correspondingly directed (prompts/planner.md `defect_scope` section) that resolved-present inputs mean the plan carries a repro-executing acceptance subtask; the payload carries an executed-commands digest (BLT-verb-matched Bash invocations + verbatim result tails from the per-worker logs; the verb set is widened by the lead verbs of the audit's `repro_command` when one exists — DESIGN §8, measured: a node-led repro on a pnpm-verbed repo would never enter the record the repro-decides rule reads) so execution-shaped items are judged from records, not impossible re-runs (TREE_READER_TOOLS scope, cwd = staging; per-call turn budget derived from the pack's item count, `min(30 + 6*len(pack), 90)` — a fixed 30 was measured crashing 4/4 attempts at turns=31 on 9- and 6-item lists, DESIGN §8 *The judge's turn budget scales with the item count*); `_delivery_judge_unmet` majority-votes (2-of-3) per `item_index`, confirmed-unmet items route into the final-conformer pass via `_format_unmet_required_items_section` and are re-judged after it; residuals persist to `state.data["delivery_gate"].unmet_after` (contract verdicts to `.contract_before` / `.contract_after`) and never block finalize; a fresh same-task run's planners receive the most recent COMPLETED run's residual as ctx `prior_delivery_residual` (completion = the run's own orchestrator.exit_code is "0"; `finished_at` is a discovery sentinel the die() path also writes and does not qualify).
