  `<run>/sysprompt`, leerie's install `ROOT`, the realpath of the
  `claude` that `env["PATH"]` finds, `env["HOME"]` (realpath; left out
  when it holds `SHARED_TMP`) and the CLI configuration template
  `<run>/claude-config/` (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_TEMPLATE`, linked from each
  worker's configuration). `<run>/worktrees/.stores/stores/` (the run's stores) is never
  granted. The cwd, for a
  committing worker (`schema_key` in
  `_COMMITTING_WORKERS`: implementer, conformer, integrator,
  acceptance_writer, surrogate_fixer, falsifier, rebaser): `rw` it and
  `_tree_git_dirs(cwd, run_dir)`'s write list, `ro` its read list or, for
  a clone (both empty), `<run>/repo/objects`. `_tree_git_dirs` (from
  `_git_dirs(tree)`; `([], [])` when it is None): a common
  dir in `<run>/tree-repos/` (`TREE_REPOS_DIRNAME`) → write it whole, read
  `<run>/repo/objects`; the run repository itself (a committing tree I6
  never makes) → `die()` naming the tree, before any spawn, so no grant to
  the run repository's `refs/`, `objects/` or `logs/` exists; a git dir
  inside the tree (a clone) → nothing. For any other worker: `rw` the
  cwd when `_bash_unrestricted(allowed_tools)` (bare `Bash` in the list),
  else `ro` (the shared planning worktree and the payload-only directory
  included: no worker there has a shell); `ro` `<run>/repo` and
  `_tree_repo_read(cwd, run_dir)` — the common dir (`_git_dirs(tree)`:
  `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir --git-common-dir`,
  resolved, or None) when it is in `<run>/tree-repos/`, else nothing
  (never a `die()`: no write is granted). `_RUN_NOTES_READERS`
  (implementer, conformer, integrator): `ro` `<run>/subtasks`,
  `<run>/task.md`, `<run>/notes`, and `<run>/task-files` when it is a directory (`TASK_FILES_DIRNAME`). `notes_id`: `rw` `<run>/notes/<id>/`
  (created). `selfcheck_dir`: `ro` it, `rw` its `run/` (created) and
  `rw` `_selfcheck_copies(run_dir, <its name>)` (made 0700,
  `_mkdir_private`). The
  tree's own stores (DESIGN §6 *A worker started in a tree leerie installed
  for runs on that tree's stores*): when `_installed_tree_stores(cwd)` is
  not None, that directory (made 0700) is added to `rw` when the cwd is
  (a committing worker, or bare `Bash`), else to `ro`. Last,
  `_apart(paths, state_root)` replaces any path that contains the state
  root by `_beside(path, state_root)` (`_around`), then any that contains
  the host directory (`_host_dir()`: the realpath of `$LEERIE_HOST_DIR`
  when it is a directory, else None) the same way — no grant covers
  either whole; `_reads_outside`'s paths, which never do, are not passed
  through it.
- `_beside(top, root)` — at each directory from `top` down to `root`'s
  parent, every entry except the one on the way to `root` and except a
  symlink resolving onto that path or beneath `root`. `_reads_outside(root,
  *, tmp=True)` is `_beside(Path("/"), root)`; with `tmp=False` (every
  worker) `SHARED_TMP` is left out too: `_beside(Path("/"), SHARED_TMP)`
  when the root lies beneath it, else every path whose realpath is
  neither beneath nor above it. Either way the host directory
  (`_host_dir()`, the build slots) is then taken out by `_around`: a
  read-only descriptor can `flock` a slot (DESIGN §6 *A host-wide build
  semaphore*). Either way every path whose realpath is `_DEV`
  (`Path("/dev")`) or beneath it is then left out: no read grant covers
  `/dev` (DESIGN §6 *No confined process holds or can open the operator's
  terminal*). `_WORKER_DEVICES = ("/dev/null", "/dev/zero", "/dev/full",
  "/dev/random", "/dev/urandom", "/dev/tty", "/dev/shm")`, written, are
  the only paths of `/dev` a grant names; no pseudo-terminal (`/dev/ptmx`,
  `/dev/pts`), which the shim grants with an isolated process's own
  `devpts` (`PRIVATE`). `_measurement_grants` ends the same way (`_apart`).
- `_confined_argv(grants, cmd, *, sandbox=None, report_fd=None, cli=False,
  worker_root=True)` — `[sys.executable, "-I", "-S", LANDLOCK_SCRIPT,
  <--isolate | --sandbox …>, --rw…, --ro…, "--", *cmd]` (§ *Isolation and
  the held-out sandbox (I3)* below); with `--isolate`, `--link-root
  <grants.link>` when `grants.link` is set.
- `WORKER_ROOT = Path("/opt/leerie-worker-root")`; `_worker_root() -> str |
  None` — its path when it is a directory (`lstat`, not a link), else
  None (DESIGN §6 *The orchestrator's root is leerie's; a repository's
  root is only a confined process's*).
- `_worker_home_extras(worker_root, home=Path("/home/leerie"), limit=20) ->
  list[str]` — the entries beneath `<worker_root>/home/leerie` the
  container's `home` lacks, named `/home/leerie/<rel>`: walks by name
  beneath the worker root without following a link (`_listdir_beneath`,
  `_dir_beneath_exists`; a linked `home` or `home/leerie` is not walked),
  descends a directory both have unless the container's is a
  mount point (an auth or cache mount owns it), unreadable directories
  skipped; at most `limit`.
- `_require_worker_view() -> None` — first `die()`s when `REPO_IMAGE_ENV`
  (`LEERIE_REPO_IMAGE`) is "1" and `_worker_root()` is None: the launcher
  started the run on a repository image that has no worker root. Then
  `die()`s, naming them, when `_worker_home_extras(WORKER_ROOT)` finds any
  path, telling the operator to install beneath `/opt` or `/usr/local`.
  Then nothing without `_worker_root()` or
  without `_isolated()` (a command enters the view only through the
  isolation); else runs `_confined_argv(WorkerGrants(rw=("/dev/null",), ro=("/",)),
  ["test", "-e", "/.leerie-worker-env"])` (`_WORKER_ENV_MARK`) from `/`,
  60 s, and `die()`s naming the shim's stderr and the rebuild when it
  exits non-zero.
- `claude_p(…, notes_id=None, selfcheck_dir=None)` computes `grants` once
  per call, after `_confined_cli_env` has put the worker's own
  `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`/`TMPDIR`/`TMP`/`TEMP`/`CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR` in its environment (None only
  when `caps[HOST_SEAM_CAP]`), passes it to
  `_invoke_admitted` → `_invoke(…, *, grants)` (keyword-only, no default);
  `_invoke` spawns `_confined_argv(grants, cmd)` (inside the spawn gate
  when there is one), or `cmd` itself for `None`. The staged stdin prompt
  is written under `<run>/stdin/` (`mkstemp(dir=…)`), not the system temp
  directory. For a worker with bare `Bash` (`_bash_unrestricted`, not in
  `NOTICE_FREE_WORKERS`), `claude_p` then appends
  `_confined_writes_notice(grants, cwd=, env=)`: "your processes can write
  only these: …" listing every path of `grants.rw` but `_WORKER_DEVICES`,
  the working directory, `$TMPDIR` and `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` named as such
  and first, then "`/tmp` and every other path are not writable; put
  scratch files in $TMPDIR." `scripts/worker-guard.py` appends the same for
  the Fly integrator, from its own grant. `_worker_guard` carries no write
  notice: it has no grant. `preflight`'s smoke test passes
  `_worker_grants(…, schema_key="smoke", cwd=<smoke dir>, env=…)` over
  `os.environ` with `_confined_cli_env(run_dir, "smoke")` laid on it, the
  same as its `_invoke`'s `env_extra`.
  `_run_implementer` passes `notes_id=sid`; `_redrive_drive`
  `notes_id=members[0]` and `selfcheck_dir` (its `bin/`'s parent).
- `HOST_SEAM_CAP = "_host_seam"` — a key set True only on the caps
  `_resolve_host_seam_settings` returns (`run_rebaser`,
  `run_recapture_deps`), read only by `claude_p`.
- Notes: `NOTES_DIRNAME = "notes"`; `_notes_dir(leerie_dir, sid)`,
  `_criteria_path` (`notes/<id>/criteria.md`), `_checkpoint_path`
  (`notes/<id>/checkpoint.md`), replacing `criteria/<id>.md` and
  `checkpoints/<id>.md` (the run directory and `setup-run.sh` make
  `notes/`). The self-check's call log is
  `<run>/selfcheck/<group>/run/calls.ndjson` (`log`); its copies are made
  in `<run-dir>/worktrees/.selfcheck/<group>/` (`snap_root`,
  `_selfcheck_copies`).
- Fly: `scripts/worker-guard.py <tools> <repo> <state.json> <wid>` also
  names the worker's `_confined_cli_env(run_dir, <wid>)` (exiting 1
  without a `<wid>`: no confined CLI runs without its own directories), with
  `_worker_cache_env`'s caches, in `guard_env`, and prints `guard_confine`
  (the shim argv for `_worker_grants(run_dir=<state.json's dir>, state,
  "integrator", staging, …)` over that environment), exiting 1 when the ABI
  is too low; `collect-subtrees.sh` passes `integrator-<sid>`, prefixes
  `claude -p` with it and skips the branch without it. `guard_env` also
  names `CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL_PREFIX=<WORKER_SHELL>`, and `guard_settings` is
  `_confined_cli_settings(<the hook>, run_dir=<state.json's dir>,
  repo_root=<the run directory's third parent>)`, which `collect-subtrees.sh`
  passes with `--setting-sources ""`.
- **The CLI's own git** (DESIGN §6 *The CLI's own git runs on leerie's
  terms*). `CLI_GIT_BIN = ROOT / "scripts" / "cli-bin"` (only `git`, a
  `/bin/sh` script), `WORKER_COMMAND_ENV = "LEERIE_WORKER_COMMAND"`,
  `CLI_GIT_ENV = "LEERIE_CLI_GIT"`, `REAL_GIT_ENV = "LEERIE_REAL_GIT"`.
  `_cli_git_env(tree, path) -> dict`: `PATH` = `CLI_GIT_BIN` then `path`
  without it, `LEERIE_REAL_GIT` = realpath of the `git` that `path` finds
  (else `/usr/bin/git`), `LEERIE_CLI_GIT` = `{"args": _tree_git_args(tree),
  "env": {}}` as JSON. `_invoke`, for every spawn with a grant: drops
  `LEERIE_WORKER_COMMAND` from the worker's environment, calls
  `_ready_tree_for_worker(cwd)` (logged when it put anything back), and lays
  `_cli_git_env(cwd, <its PATH>)` over the environment.
  `_ready_tree_for_worker(tree) -> list[str]`: `_restore_settings(tree)`,
  then `".git"` when `_restore_git_pointer(tree)` rewrote it.
  `_restore_git_pointer(tree) -> bool`: for a worktree located by
  `_run_tree_location` (not a ref-less clone, whose git dir is its common
  dir), leaves a regular `.git` whose `gitdir:` resolves to the
  administrative directory; else removes what is there (`_remove_beneath`)
  and writes `gitdir: <admin>\n`
  with `_write_beneath(tree, tree/".git", …, mode=0o644, make=False)`.
  `scripts/cli-bin/git`: `exec "$LEERIE_REAL_GIT" "$@"` when
  `LEERIE_WORKER_COMMAND=1`, else `exec /usr/bin/python3 -IS
  <scripts>/cli-git.py "$@"`. `scripts/cli-git.py`: `nest()` (126 and no
  git on failure), then `execve(LEERIE_REAL_GIT, [real, *spec["args"],
  *argv[1:]], env | spec["env"])` with `LEERIE_CLI_GIT` removed; 126 on an
  unreadable spec, 127 when the exec fails. `worker-shell.py` sets
  `LEERIE_WORKER_COMMAND=1` in the command's environment. A ref-less
  clone's committing worker reads `_clone_git_dir(cwd)` (`_worker_grants`).
  `worker-guard.py` calls `_ready_tree_for_worker(<staging>)` and adds
  `_cli_git_env(<staging>, <PATH>)` to `guard_env`.
  Settings pin (review round 23): `_CLI_PINNED_NAMES = ("PATH",
  SHELL_PREFIX_ENV, WORKER_COMMAND_ENV, CLI_GIT_ENV, REAL_GIT_ENV)`.
  `_confined_cli_settings` passes every layer below leerie's own through
  `_lower_layer_part(layer) -> dict`, which keeps only
  `_LOWER_LAYER_KEYS` (the CLI's credential helpers: `apiKeyHelper`,
  `awsCredentialExport`, `awsAuthRefresh`, `gcpAuthRefresh`),
  `permissions` cut to `_LOWER_LAYER_PERMISSIONS` (`deny`, `ask`; the key
  left out when nothing is left) and `env` cut to `_LOWER_LAYER_ENV` —
  endpoint (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL`,
  `ANTHROPIC_VERTEX_BASE_URL`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`,
  `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_BEDROCK_AUTH`,
  `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_VERTEX_AUTH`, and Foundry's `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY`,
  `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_FOUNDRY_AUTH`, `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL`,
  `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_RESOURCE`), credentials (`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`,
  `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS`,
  `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_API_KEY`), Vertex's project and region
  (`ANTHROPIC_VERTEX_PROJECT_ID`, `CLOUD_ML_REGION`) and model mapping
  (`ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL`, `_OPUS_MODEL`, `_HAIKU_MODEL`,
  `_FABLE_MODEL`, `ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL`,
  `ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL_AWS_REGION`) — and names starting with one
  of `_LOWER_LAYER_ENV_PREFIXES` (`AWS_`, `VERTEX_REGION_CLAUDE_`); none of
  them is a `_CLI_PINNED_NAMES` name or `LEERIE_*`. Each is a name the
  installed CLI (2.1.317) defines: its settings schema lists the four
  helpers as its credential helpers, and the environment names are those
  its Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry and gateway setups read; the CLI's
  provider switches that no documented setup sets are left out. So
  a worker's tool scope is its argv alone (DESIGN §6 *The CLI reads no
  settings file*, §12 *L1*).
  `_cli_pinned_env(worker_env) -> dict`: each name's value in
  `worker_env`, `WORKER_COMMAND_ENV` as `""`. `_pin_cli_settings(cmd,
  pinned) -> list`: `cmd` with `pinned` laid over its `--settings` JSON's
  `env` (unchanged without `--settings`); `_invoke` applies it after
  `_cli_git_env` for every spawn with a grant, and `worker-guard.py` to
  `guard_settings` with its own `guard_env`.
- **A worker's commands in a nested domain** (DESIGN §6 *A worker's
  commands cannot reach its CLI*). `WORKER_SHELL = ROOT / "scripts" /
  "worker-shell.py"` (executable, `#!/usr/bin/python3 -IS`),
  `SHELL_PREFIX_ENV = "CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL_PREFIX"`. `_invoke` sets
  `SHELL_PREFIX_ENV` to `WORKER_SHELL` in the environment of every spawn
  with a grant (never with `grants=None`), and `_confined_cli_settings`
  puts it in the settings' `env`, the top layer. `scripts/worker-shell.py
  COMMAND [ARGS…]`: loads `landlock_exec.py` beside it by path, calls
  `nest()`, pops `LEERIE_WORKER_VIEW`/`LEERIE_WORKER_ROOT` from its
  environment and, when both were set and the command is not leerie's
  hook (`_is_leeries_hook`: one argument, either exactly `"<sys.executable>
  -I <dir>/tree-reader-hook.py"` or `"<sys.executable> -I
  <dir>/forbidden-command-hook.py "` then base64 characters only), calls
  `enter_worker_view(view, worker_env_changes(root))` (126 when it raises),
  then `execv("/bin/bash", ["/bin/bash", "-c", COMMAND, *ARGS])`; 126 when
  `nest()` raises (the command does not run), 127 when the exec fails, 2
  without a command. `landlock_exec.nest()`: a ruleset handling
  `HANDLED` with one rule allowing `HANDLED` beneath `/`, no scope, then
  `PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS` and `landlock_restrict_self`; raises `OSError`
  naming the failed step.
- Every worker also gets `ro` `<run>/mise-tools.toml` (`MISE_TOOLS_NAME`,
  written by `_discover_tools`).
- **Measurements** (DESIGN §6 *Leerie's runs of the repository's commands
  are confined too*). `WorkerGrants(rw, ro, env=())`: `env` is the
  `(name, value)` pairs the grant names, laid over the command's
  environment last; a worker's grant leaves it empty.
  `_measurement_grants(st, tree, kind=MEASURE_KIND) -> WorkerGrants`,
  kinds `MEASURE_KIND = "measure"`, `SETUP_HOOK_KIND = "setup_hook"`,
  `TOOLCHAIN_KIND = "toolchain"`, `INSTALL_KIND = "install"` (every
  install leerie runs on a repository's code: `MEASURE_KIND`'s paths and
  `env` unchanged, with `egress` True; DESIGN §6 *An install reaches its
  inputs*); no grant's `env` holds a store variable (they are
  `_leerie_stores`' and `_tree_store_env`'s); `MEASUREMENT_KINDS` is the four, the only `kind`
  values `_measurement_grants` accepts (`ValueError` otherwise). `die()`s when `st` has no `run_dir`, or
  when the tree holds or lies beneath one of `_MEASURE_PRIVATE`
  (`state.json`, `acceptance`, `logs`, `workers`, `tree-stores`, `stores`, `tmp`,
  `repo-settings`, `tree-repos`, `repo`, `measure` under the run
  directory). A tree beneath
  `<run>/worktrees/` is taken at its git toplevel. `rw`:
  `_WORKER_DEVICES`, the tree, `_measure_dir(st, tree)`, the run's
  stores `<run>/worktrees/.stores/stores/` (`RUN_STORES_DIRNAME`, made 0700), the tree's
  private temp directory `_private_tmp(<measure-dir>)`; setup-hook kind
  adds `MISE_DATA_DIR` (default `~/.local/share/mise`) and `~/.local/bin`
  (both made first), toolchain kind `MISE_DATA_DIR` and the toolchain home
  layer `_toolchain_home()` (`$LEERIE_TOOLCHAIN_HOME`, `TOOLCHAIN_HOME_ENV`,
  realpath; none when unset) — a toolchain path beneath the state root is
  never granted. `ro`:
  `_reads_outside(state_root, tmp=False)` (no grant names `/tmp`: an
  isolated command's own is the shim's), leerie's install `ROOT`, `os.environ["HOME"]` (realpath;
  left out when it holds `SHARED_TMP`),
  `<run>/mise-tools.toml` and `_measured_git_reads(tree, run_dir)`
  (`git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir --git-common-dir`:
  common dir the run repository → it whole; a tree repository → it and
  `<run>/repo/objects`; a git dir inside the tree (a clone) →
  `<run>/repo/objects`; a git dir elsewhere outside the run directory → it
  and its common dir; else nothing). `rw` also, for a tree whose parent
  is `<run>/worktrees/`, `<run>/worktrees/.stores/tree-stores/<tree>/`
  (`TREE_STORES_DIRNAME`, made; what `_tree_store_env` names). `env`: `TMPDIR`/`TMP`/`TEMP` and
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` → the private temp directory (remade on every call),
  `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` → `<private-tmp>/run` (no `GNUPGHOME`: the private
  home's `~/.gnupg` is the command's own, DESIGN §6 *Every confined process
  has its own home*), `XDG_STATE_HOME` →
  `<measure-dir>/state`, `MISE_STATE_DIR` → `<measure-dir>/mise-state`
  (emptied first for the toolchain kind), and, for the kinds that write
  `MISE_DATA_DIR` (toolchain, setup hook), `MISE_CACHE_DIR` →
  `<MISE_DATA_DIR>/<MISE_CACHE_NAME>` (`"cache"`; inside the granted data
  directory, shared with every run: mise's install lock and `incomplete`
  markers live there — DESIGN §6 *One toolchain install at a time on a
  host*); no store variable (leerie's environment and
  `_tree_store_env` set them). No grant names `/tmp` (the shim gives the
  command its own, DESIGN §6 *Every confined process has its own `/tmp`,
  `/dev/shm` and IPC*); the worker-tree distinction (`_is_worker_tree`,
  `_declare_worker_tree`, `_WORKER_TREES`, `_TMP_GRANTED_TREES`) is
  deleted.
- `_argv_outside_grant(argv, grants) -> str | None` —
  the first element of `argv` that is an absolute path that exists and
  whose realpath lies beneath no realpath of `grants.rw` or `grants.ro`;
  None when every one does. `_run_streaming` and `_ts_script_run` `die()`
  on one before spawning (DESIGN §6 *Leerie's runs of the repository's
  commands are confined too*). `_redrive_ast_hits` writes each base copy
  under the grant's `TMPDIR` (`tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=…)`), the
  tree's private temp directory, never `<run>/tmp/`. New directories (the tree's stores,
  `mise-state/`) are made by `_mkdir_private`. `_cache_vars(cache)` (every
  `_STORE_VARS` variable → `cache/<name>`,
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME` → `cache/xdg`, then `_with_pnpm_spellings`) serves
  `_worker_cache_env(env, run_dir, cache=None)` only (`cache` default
  `<run>/worktrees/.stores/cache/`). `_invoke`
  passes `_granted_cache_dir(grants, leerie_dir)` — the held-out set when
  the grant's `rw` names it, else the fixers' — so the variables follow the
  grant. Paths through `_around`, as a worker's.
- `_measure_dir(st, tree) -> Path` — `<run>/measure/<tree-name>-<id>/`
  (`MEASURE_DIRNAME`) with `_MEASURE_SUBDIRS` (`mise-state/`, `reports/`,
  `coverage/`) made 0700 by `_mkdir_private` (a link or file in their
  place is removed). `<id>`: 16 hex digits read from, or first written to,
  `<id-dir>/leerie-measure-id` (`_MEASURE_ID_FILE`), `<id-dir>` from
  `_measure_id_dir(run_dir, tree, dirs)`: the administrative directory
  `_run_tree_location` names for a tree in the run's `worktrees/` (never
  the tree's own `.git`), or the git dir when it is in `<run>/repo/`; read
  (`_read_beneath`) and written (`_write_beneath`, mode 0644; a write that
  fails leaves a fresh id per call) from the run directory down; else
  `sha256(<tree realpath>)[:16]`. When
  a new id is written (a new tree at that path), `<run>/worktrees/.stores/tree-stores/<tree>/`
  is moved aside to `.gone/` too. A
  sidecar `<run>/measure/<tree-name>-<id>.tree` (JSON `{tree, id_file,
  tmp}`) records the owner and its private temp directory;
  `_sweep_measure_dirs(root)` (every call) moves aside to
  `<run>/measure/.gone/` each directory whose tree is gone or whose id
  file is missing, unreadable through `_read_beneath`, or names another
  id, removes its sidecar's `tmp` (when
  directly beneath `PRIVATE_TMP_ROOT`), and removes `.gone/` in a daemon
  thread (`_rmtree_owned`).
- Private temp directories (DESIGN §6 *A confined command's scratch is
  short and private*): `SHARED_TMP = Path("/tmp")`, `PRIVATE_TMP_ROOT =
  SHARED_TMP / "l"`. `_private_tmp(key) -> Path` — `_own_private_dir` on
  `PRIVATE_TMP_ROOT` and on `PRIVATE_TMP_ROOT / sha256(str(key))[:16]`,
  recorded in `_PRIVATE_TMPS` (path → creating pid); the first one
  registers `atexit` `_remove_private_tmps` (the creating pid's only).
  `_release_run_dir` first calls `_remove_trees_private_tmps(<run>/measure)`,
  which removes (`_rmtree_owned`) the `tmp` each sidecar names directly
  beneath `PRIVATE_TMP_ROOT`.
  `_own_private_dir(path)` — `mkdir(0o700)`, then `die()` unless `lstat`
  shows a directory owned by `os.geteuid()` (a link or another user's is
  refused), `chmod 0o700` when its mode differs. `_mkdir_private(path,
  top)` — every missing directory from below `top` down to `path`,
  `mkdir(0o700)`; used for the measurement directory, the tree's stores,
  `mise-state/`, `_worker_dirs`' `config` (via its staging sibling) and
  `tmp`, `_cache_vars`' `xdg`/`pnpm-store` (bounded at the run
  directory), a worker's notes directory; the self-check's `run/` is made
  0700.
- The run's execution lock and `_held_out_section` (formerly the run's
  `/tmp` lock): § *Isolation and the held-out sandbox (I3)* below.
- `_use_run_tmp(st) -> Path` — `<run>/tmp/` made 0700, set as
  `tempfile.tempdir` and `os.environ["TMPDIR"]`, the temp directory before
  it kept once in `_SYSTEM_TEMP_DIR` (`_system_temp_dir()`, where
  preflight's smoke test makes its working directory); `_run_phases`'
  second statement, after the run-id log line.
- `_run_streaming(cmd, *, grants, …)` and `_run_contained(argv, *,
  grants, sandbox=None, …)`: `grants` keyword-only, no default. The spawn
  is `_confined_argv(grants, cmd, sandbox=…)` (inside the spawn gate
  when there is one), under `_exec_lock().shared()` (the run's; it has no host level),
  with environment `{**_repo_command_env(env), **dict(grants.env)}`.
  `_run_streaming` first `die()`s when `log_path` is a registered worker
  transcript (`_is_worker_transcript`; DESIGN §8 *What a worker ran is
  read from its own transcript*).
  `_measure_blt(axis, cmd, tree, *, grants, …)` passes its caller's.
  Callers derive the grant for the tree they run in: `_ensure_worktree_deps`
  (`INSTALL_KIND` for a recipe `install` entry, `MEASURE_KIND` for a
  `build` entry, each derived at the first entry of its kind),
  `_measure_axes`, `_capture_failing_test_ids`,
  `_ci_run(argv, *, tree, rec, st, caps, label, kind=MEASURE_KIND)`
  (`_ci_prepare` passes `INSTALL_KIND` for a check's prerequisites;
  every check runs `MEASURE_KIND`),
  `_acceptance_parse_probe`, `_run_acceptance_file`, `_cov_contained`
  (the tree's git toplevel; `kind=MEASURE_KIND`, `INSTALL_KIND` from
  `_install_settles`), `_settle_by_execution`, `_run_setup_hook`
  (`SETUP_HOOK_KIND`), `_run_mise_install` (`TOOLCHAIN_KIND`, one grant for
  `mise install`, `_enable_corepack_shims`' enables and `mise ls --current
  --json`, the latter through
  `_run_proc(_confined_argv(…))`). The AST scripts take `grants` too:
  `_ts_resolvable(tree, *, grants)`, `_redrive_ast_hits(staging, base,
  head, *, grants)`, via `_redrive_ast_available(staging, *, grants)` and
  `_redrive_escalation_gate(staging, base, head, *, grants)`. They spawn
  synchronously (`_ts_script_run`), so they cannot wait for the execution
  lock: every coroutine that calls one holds `_exec_lock().shared()`
  around the call (the falsifier's `_ts_resolvable`, the re-drive's `_redrive_ast_available` and
  `_redrive_escalation_gate`), and `_ts_script_run` `die()`s, before
  spawning, when its context holds neither level (`_exec_lock_held()`).
  The falsifier's AST facts (`_probe_case_facts_placed`) are not among
  them: its probe is never on disk in the tree, so the facts script runs
  in a held-out sandbox through `_run_streaming`, the probe placed.
- Reports a measured command writes are under `_measure_dir(st, tree)`:
  `_capture_failing_test_ids`' `reports/<label>-<i>-…` (read with

  `_runner_report_failing_ids(kind, report, tree)`,

  `_parse_runner_report(kind, report, tree)` (JUnit through

- `committing_worker_started`: `claude_p` sets it (and saves) before

### Leerie's writes where confined code writes

DESIGN §6 *Leerie never writes through a path confined code shaped*. One
family in `leerie.py`, each walking from an anchor no confined process can
replace (the run directory, or a grant's own root) without following a
link:

- `_open_dir_beneath(anchor, path, *, make=False, dir_mode=0o777,
  replace=False) -> int` — each component `O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW`
  (`_DIR_NOFOLLOW`) at the previous descriptor; `make` makes a missing one,
  `replace` removes a link or file in a directory's place (leerie's layout
  only). `OSError` (ELOOP/ENOTDIR) on a link otherwise, and (EINVAL) when
  `path` is not lexically beneath `anchor` (`_beneath_parts`). `_dir_beneath` is its
  context manager.
- `_write_beneath(anchor, path, data, *, mode=None, make=True)` — a fresh
  `.leerie-<hex>` made `O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW` in the directory's
  descriptor, written, `fchmod` to `mode` (default the replaced regular
  file's mode, else 0o666 less the umask), renamed over `path.name`.
- `_read_beneath(anchor, path, *, limit) -> bytes` (`O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK`; a
  non-regular file raises, so does one over `limit`; § *Leerie's reads of a
  repository's content* below), `_lexists_beneath(anchor, path) -> bool` (a
  link or non-directory on the way counts as taken), `_unlink_beneath`,
  `_remove_beneath` (a directory through `_rmtree_owned` of
  `/proc/self/fd/<dirfd>/<name>`), `_rmdirs_beneath` (`os.removedirs` up to
  the anchor), `_copy_beneath(src, anchor, dst, *, src_anchor=None, limit=None)`
  (with `src`'s mode; `src_anchor` reads `src` through `_read_beneath`
  within `limit`), `_copytree_beneath(src, anchor, dst, *, ignore=None,
  src_anchor=None, limit=None)` (links copied as
  links).
- `_add_dir_bits_beneath(anchor, rel, bits)` — the owner bits on `anchor`
  and each directory down to `rel` through `O_PATH|O_NOFOLLOW` descriptors
  and `chmod("/proc/self/fd/N")`; a link ends the walk (by path, each
  component `lstat`ed, where `os.O_PATH` is absent). Used by
  `_writable_dirs_to`, `_restore_write_bits` and `_rmtree_owned`.
- `_mkdir_private(path, top)` — `_open_dir_beneath(top, path, make=True,
  dir_mode=0o700, replace=True)`; a `path` not beneath `top` is left alone.

Callers: `_restore_tracked_content`, `_remove_new_untracked`,
`_restore_settings`, `_measure_dir_at`, `_sweep_measure_dirs`,
`_capture_failing_test_ids`, `_vitest_run`, `_measure_subtask_coverage`,
`_overlay_other_side`, `_try_json_key_merge`, `_move_view`,
`_drop_lying_index`, `_redrive_ast_hits`, `_stage_worktree_extras`,
`_place_set`/`_unplace(copied, wt)`, `_copy_task_references(st, wt, task)
-> (copied, refs)` (the writer's, the set auditor's and the surrogate's
checkouts), `_checkout_ignorable`/`_checkout_ignore`,
`_falsifier_place_leads` (leads written mode 0444; the `rglob` chmods
before removal are gone, `_rmtree_owned` gives the bits),
`_falsifier_gates`, `_falsifier_save_probe`, `_collect_acceptance_set`.
`_rescue_integrator_work`'s throwaway index is in
a `tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="leerie-rescue-")` directory, not the tree's
git directory. Tests: `tests/test_leerie_writes_never_follow_links.py`
(the primitives; review round 21's R1, R2 and R5 proofs inverted; the rule
that every function calling a raw write primitive is classified, and the
converted functions call none).

### Leerie's reads of a repository's content

DESIGN §6 *Leerie never reads through a link a repository holds*. The
read side of the family above, anchored at the repository's root (`/work`,
a worker's tree, a tree repository, a measurement's tree, a subtask's
notes directory):

- `_read_beneath(anchor, path, *, limit: int) -> bytes` — the regular
  file reached without a link; `limit` has no default. After the open,
  `fstat` on the descriptor: a file over `limit` bytes is refused
  (`OSError` `EFBIG`, which every caller already treats as unreadable), and
  the read takes at most `limit + 1` bytes in 1 MiB chunks, refusing the
  file if it grew past `limit`. `_read_head_beneath(anchor, path, *,
  limit)` returns at most the first `limit` bytes instead, for a caller
  that uses only the start (`_read_file_safely`, the binary probe in
  `_introduced_conflict_markers`). DESIGN §6 *No read is unbounded*.
- The limits, by what the file is: `READ_LIMIT_CONFIG = 1 MiB`
  (configuration, manifests, version pins, CI files, git's admin files, a
  checkpoint, a `.gitignore`, a measurement's id file), `READ_LIMIT_TEXT =
  16 MiB` (text read whole: a task file or reference, a source file parsed
  or counted, a README, a held-out or test file copied out of a tree) and
  `READ_LIMIT_LARGE = 256 MiB` (a measurement's own report: a JSON test
  report, a coverage map or summary; a copy of the operator's untracked
  files into the planning worktree).
- `_read_text_beneath(anchor, path, *, limit, errors="replace") -> str` —
  `_read_beneath` decoded as UTF-8 (`errors="strict"` where the caller
  parses JSON or TOML and treats a decode error as unreadable).
- `_no_link_beneath(anchor, path) -> bool` — exists, and neither it nor a
  directory on the way is a link; `_dir_beneath_exists(anchor, path)`;
  `_link_on_the_way(anchor, path) -> bool`;
  `_listdir_beneath(anchor, path) -> list[str]` (the directory reached
  without a link; `OSError` otherwise); `_glob_beneath(anchor, pattern)
  -> list[Path]` (`anchor.glob`, sorted, filtered by `_no_link_beneath`).
- `_copy_beneath(..., src_anchor=, limit=)` and `_copytree_beneath(...,
  src_anchor=, limit=)` read the source beneath `src_anchor`, each file
  within `limit` (required with `src_anchor`: a `TypeError` without it).

The PR template is a git blob: `_find_pr_template(git_dir, rev,
override=None) -> (rel, text, truncated) | None` lists
`_PR_TEMPLATE_SINGLE_LOCATIONS`, then each of `_PR_TEMPLATE_MULTI_DIRS`,
with `git ls-tree -z --full-tree <rev> -- <path>` in the run's own
repository (`_committed_blobs`, regular blobs only: mode 100644/100755),
and reads the chosen blob with `git cat-file blob`
(`_committed_text`, capped at `PR_WRITER_TEMPLATE_MAX_BYTES`).
`_compose_pr_via_llm(st, caps, models, efforts, pr_template_override)`
calls it with `_run_repo(st)` and `_diff_base(st)`; with no `base_sha` the
worker gets no template.

Converted readers: `_read_toml_key` (anchored at the repository root:
the file's parent, or its grandparent for `.leerie/config.toml`),
`_write_config_toml_keys` (read beneath, written with `_write_beneath`),
`_settings_file(path, *, root=None)` (the repository's `.claude` settings
with `root`), `_gather_provision_fixtures`, `_read_file_safely(root, path,
budget)`, `_sample_workspace_manifests`, `_gather_dep_manifests`,
`_workspace_globs`, `_parse_repo_file(root, path)`,
`_extract_symbol_ranges(root, path)`, `_subfile_split`,
`_peel_oversized_file`, `_is_same_document(root, path, text_len, text)`,
`_glob_task_references` (matches reached through a link dropped),
`_d1_report_sources`, `_task_file_text` (`resolve_task_argument`; a path
outside the working directory is the operator's),
`_js_runner_scoped_templates`, `_package_json_name`,
`_package_json_scripts`, `_ci_safe_rel`
(lexical, never resolved), `_ci_config_files`, `_ci_check_problems`,
`_ci_strict_problems`, `_ci_coverage_pcts`, `_prisma_project`, `_prisma_reset_scripts`,
`_prisma_mock_hits`, `_go_test_func_names(root, path)`,
`_binary_install_source`, `_validate_checkpoint(path, worktree_root=None,
notes_dir=None)` (read beneath `notes_dir`, which the gate passes as
`_notes_dir(leerie_dir, sid)`), `_introduced_conflict_markers`,
`_restore_git_pointer`, `_admin_dir_of`, `_run_tree_location`,
`_stage_worktree_extras`, `_copy_task_references`,
`_verify_set_audit_case`, `_category_evidence_found`
(`follow_symlinks=False`). The launcher, after its `--help` scan and
before any verb but `version`, exits 1 when `_checkout_config_links`
names a link among `leerie.toml`, `.leerie`, `.leerie/config.toml`,
`.leerie/Dockerfile`, `.claude`, `.claude/settings.json` and
`.claude/settings.local.json` in `$USER_REPO` (the last three are read by
`detect_bedrock_mode` and `bedrock_preflight`). Tests: `tests/test_leerie_reads_never_follow_links.py` (the
primitives; review round 26 I1's proof inverted, the credentials file and
`/proc/self/environ`; the converted readers; the rule that every function
calling a raw read primitive is classified, and the converted functions
call none and, but for three existence-only ones, use no `.is_file()`,
`.is_dir()`, `.exists()`, `os.path` probe or copy without `src_anchor=`).

## 4. Phase walkthrough (`leerie.py`)

| Phase | Function(s) | What it does |
|-------|-------------|--------------|
| Preflight | `preflight` | disk headroom on the state-dir filesystem (N30 — see "Disk headroom" above), git identity, clean working tree, external `leerie` branch collision (DESIGN §6 *External collision hazard*), `claude` CLI version, live `claude -p` smoke test. The smoke test uses the shared contained argv (`_contained_claude_argv`, so tool denies + `--strict-mcp-config` apply), `SMOKE_MAX_TURNS`=5 against a measured happy path of 3, and the **resolved `classifier` model** — the tier the run's first worker actually spawns with. It runs in an **empty cwd with no repository ancestor** — a stable path under the system temp dir, named from a hash of the state root (the CLI resolves project context by walking UP from cwd, so a directory under `<repo>/.leerie` would reload the very CLAUDE.md this avoids). Not cleaned up: it is empty by construction and two runs of one state root share it. It validates the CLI, not the repo. A client-side context refusal is classified via `_is_context_overflow` and **raises `ContextOverflow`** (resumable `EXIT_LOCKED` pause) rather than printing a bare `Prompt is too long`. Run-id collisions are detected at two points: filesystem side in `State.__init__`; git side in `setup-run.sh`'s branch-creation step, which repeats the check as defense-in-depth for `resume`. Smoke test bypassed by `--skip-smoke`; preflight skipped entirely on `resume` |
| 1 Classify | `phase_classify`, `_d1_units`, `_d1_split_spans`, `_d1_split_sections`, `_d1_report_paths`, `_d1_report_sources`, `_d1_render`, `_d1_coverage_holes`, `_d1_closure` | one classifier worker → categories + questions + requirement-coverage items (DESIGN §8 *Requirement coverage*). The user prompt carries the task cut into spans `[S1]`… (`_d1_split_spans`: a heading line, a blank line, or a list item at any indent opens a span; a fenced block stays whole; `[Sx < Sy]` marks a nested item and its `parent`; a re-classify from the classification gate passes its feedback as `phase_classify`'s `review_note`, shown after the cut task and never cut with it, so coverage accounts for the user's task, not the orchestrator's note) and each report from `_d1_report_sources` — a `_glob_task_references` hit with a `.md`/`.markdown`/`.mdx` suffix that the repository does not track (`_checkout_file_tracked`), at most `D1_REPORT_MAX_BYTES` (256 KiB) — cut at headings into sections `[R1]`… (`_d1_split_sections`). The check chains `_d1_coverage_holes` after `check_classifier_output`; `D1_REPORT_WITHOUT_REQUIREMENT` is raised only on the first check of the call. After the loop it writes `required_items`, `requirement_coverage` and `needs_human_verification`; residual holes are logged, never fatal. Returned categories are filtered against the 9-name whitelist in `CATEGORIES` (mirrors DESIGN §4); `die()` if none survive. On a fresh (non-resumed) run, `run.json`'s identity fields (`run_id`, `branch`, `working_branch`, `pr_base_branch`, `started_at`, `task`) are written immediately BEFORE this phase runs — not after, as originally implemented — so any early-exit path reachable from classification (including the classification gate's no-work routing, below) sees a fully-identified `run.json` rather than one carrying only `_finish_no_work_run`'s own `{finished_at, no_push, no_verify}` (DESIGN §8 *Reaching the cleared-but-empty state from classification*) |
|   • Classification gate | `phase_classification_gate` | independent adversarial verifier of the classifier's category set (DESIGN §8 *Independent adversarial verification*). One `classification_judge` worker attacks the chosen categories against the task + codebase; a non-empty `miscategorizations` array (a missing category the work requires, or a spurious one) re-drives `phase_classify` via `_run_checked_loop` (bounded by `judgment_check_rounds`, and cut short earlier by `_run_checked_loop`'s own oscillation guard when a round's issues repeat an earlier round's exactly — DESIGN §8 *The CRITIC retry pattern's oscillation guard*). Skipped entirely by `--skip-classification-check`, which returns `False` without spawning the judge and without writing the audit key — a bypass is not a clean-pass judgment, matching every sibling skip path. Across rounds, the gate accumulates a `judge_confirmed` set — every category the judge has reviewed without objection or explicitly asked to add — and passes it into the re-invoked `phase_classify`, so `check_classifier_output`'s `SAME_WORK_RISK`/`TEST_OWNERSHIP_RISK`/`CATEGORY_NO_DIR` self-checks never strip a category the judge has already vetted. `CATEGORY_NO_DIR` honours it for the same reason as the two RISK advisories, but on a **single** category rather than a pair, and for `infrastructure` as well as `documentation`. Separately, what counts as evidence for a category is `CATEGORY_EVIDENCE` + `_category_evidence_found`: directories matched case-insensitively at the root **or one level down** (`src/infrastructure/`), root marker files by case-folded stem (`cdk.json`, `readme`), and root globs (`*.tf`). Suppression is empty-handed on the initial classify, so a signal that mis-describes a correct classification fires before any judge runs — measured at 27 firings across 19 runs, all false. `_category_evidence_summary` derives the advisory text from the same table so the remedy it names cannot drift from the rule. The set is monotone except under an evidenced retraction (DESIGN §8 *`judge_confirmed` is monotone except under an evidenced retraction*): a narrower later round does not retract an earlier confirmation, but an **evidenced** `spurious_category` does — `_check` applies `judge_confirmed.difference_update(spurious)` and will not re-add a category the same round called spurious. `_gating_spurious_categories` is the single definition of "concretely objected to", shared by `_check` and the feedback builder; a vague entry (empty `concrete_work_evidence`) neither gates nor retracts. `_on_feedback` names the drop list outright in the re-classify prompt and `die()`s rather than emit a keep-list and drop-list that intersect — the failure mode of the contradiction is not a wrong answer but an unsatisfiable instruction that silently burns the round budget. On exhaustion, `die()`s with the residuals named and the **actual** number of re-classify rounds that ran (tracked by the gate, not read off the cap: `_run_checked_loop` fires feedback only while `rnd < max_rounds - 1`, so a 3-round budget re-classifies at most twice, and once when the oscillation guard aborts early) — UNLESS `st.data["likely_already_satisfied"]` is `True` with non-empty evidence, in which case it routes to `_finish_no_work_run` (the same terminal state `_detect_no_work` produces post-plan; DESIGN §8 *Reaching the cleared-but-empty state from classification*) and returns `True` — except that when `_acceptance_can_check(st)` holds, a confirmation is held as `no_work_pending` (and `False` returned) until `_settle_pending_no_work` decides it on the held-out sets (see the `no_work_pending` state row) — signaling the caller (`_run_phases`) to stop the pipeline. Gates before provision/plan spend. Runs inside the `plans_after_classify` checkpoint block (DESIGN §6 "Resumable planning"), so a resume past classify skips it. Persists to `state.data["classification_coverage_gate"]`. **On the CONVERGED path** (gate clean), `_confirm_no_work_on_converged_gate` consults the same `likely_already_satisfied` signal — but through an independent `no_work_judge` (read-only, `SATISFIED_PROBE_TOOLS`, current-checkout-only) rather than raw trust: only `confirmed: true` with non-empty evidence routes to `_finish_no_work_run` (audit record in `state.data["no_work_confirmation"]`, returns `True`); a dispute, crash, timeout, or empty evidence falls through to planning unchanged — a dispute with non-empty judge evidence additionally persists both halves of the disagreement to `state.data["no_work_dispute"]`, which `phase_plan` injects into every planner's ctx so the plan targets the disputed residual rather than re-deriving the task (DESIGN §8 *A dispute's evidence is planning input, not log noise*) — and `skip_satisfied_check` suppresses the consult entirely (DESIGN §8 *The healthy-path consumer*). |
|   • Provision | `phase_provision` | per-repo dep **detection** (DESIGN §6½ *The repository image holds no dependency*). Always runs, for every task whatever its categories (DESIGN §6½: every measurement installs from the recipe). Five steps: `_discover_tools` (the `tool_discovery` worker → `<run>/mise-tools.toml`, `MISE_GLOBAL_CONFIG_FILE`) → `.leerie-setup.sh` hook if present → `mise install` in a throwaway checkout of the planning commit (steps 2–4; reads `.tool-versions` natively; `.nvmrc` / `.python-version` / `.ruby-version` / `rust-toolchain.toml` via image-set `MISE_IDIOMATIC_VERSION_FILE_ENABLE_TOOLS`) → version capture via `mise ls --current --json` → `_detect_recipe_from_lockfiles()` table-first, falls back to a `provision` worker on table miss. The recipe is **persisted to `st.data["provision"]["recipe"]` and injected into implementer/conformer prompts as a `PROVISION_RECIPE:` block**, every `install` and `build` entry (never run by the orchestrator at `repo_root`, which would clobber the host's bind-mounted checkout). The tools file's env var `MISE_GLOBAL_CONFIG_FILE` is exported to `os.environ` so all downstream worker subprocesses inherit it. `mise install` and `.leerie-setup.sh` run through `_run_streaming` so their output is visible live. Skipped on `resume` when `st.data["provision"]["recipe"]` is already present (key-presence, not truthiness — an empty recipe is a valid completed state; DESIGN §6 "Resumable planning"); the env var is re-exported from persisted state on resume. |
|   • Provision gate | `phase_provision_gate` | independent adversarial verifier of the detected install recipe (DESIGN §8, §6½). One `provision_judge` worker attacks `st.data["provision"]["recipe"]` against the image/runtime — catching the semantic gaps the deterministic `_normalize_pip_installs` / `_validate_provision_recipe` miss (a `pip install` missing `--break-system-packages` on the externally-managed Debian image, a package manager that doesn't match the lockfiles present). A non-empty `recipe_failures` array `die()`s immediately with the judge's concrete `fix` named — **detect-and-die, single pass** (no re-drive: a table recipe re-emits identically and an LLM recipe would re-produce the same defect, so re-driving only burns rounds before dying anyway; a broken recipe is fatal, matching `phase_provision`'s own recipe-validation die). A `provision_judge` `WorkerError` degrades (the deterministic checks already ran). Skipped when no recipe was detected (`kind: none`); runs inside the `plans_after_classify` checkpoint block so a resume past classify skips it. Persists to `state.data["provision_recipe_gate"]`. |
|   • Clarify *(optional)* | `gather_answers` | source-of-truth is satisfied non-interactively from the resolved preference (default `both`), **unconditionally** — never gated on the classifier's `needs_source_of_truth`, which records only whether the question was relevant. Every consumer **that holds a `State`** reads the value through `_effective_source_of_truth(st)` — `phase_plan`, `phase_reconcile` (inside the `_check_unresolvable` closure, sourcing the phase-2½ abort message), `_write_plan` and `_compose_pr_via_llm` — and none may fall back to a hardcoded tier. That list is **derived, not maintained**: `tests/test_effective_sot_consumers.py` resolves every `_effective_source_of_truth(...)` call site to its enclosing module-level function and fails if this sentence omits one. It exists because the hand-written list drifted inside the very commit that introduced it — the `phase_reconcile` reader was added as a deliberate design step and the prose still said three, which is the enumeration-vs-derivation failure recorded four times over in CLAUDE.md. The two readers that cannot are `compose_pr_body` (takes a plain `state: dict`, the deterministic PR-body fallback) and `scripts/host-finalize.sh`'s `jq`; both read the recorded answer directly and render `n/a` when absent. Intent questions from the classifier are dropped by default; pass `--clarify` to surface them. With `--clarify` + interactive: collect; with `--clarify` + non-interactive: write `pending-questions.json`, exit code 10 (DESIGN §11). The asking and the deferral are `_ask_questions(st, pending)` and `_defer_questions(st, pending)`, shared with `_stop_for_intent_questions`, whose intent conflicts are asked whether or not `--clarify` is set (DESIGN §11 *Intent conflicts are settled with evidence, else asked*) |
| 2 Plan | `phase_artifact_registry`, `phase_defect_scope_audit`, `_settle_scope_reading`, `phase_acceptance_write`, `phase_plan` | **First: `phase_artifact_registry`** runs a single read-only `artifact_registry` worker (after classify, before any planner) that emits a small canonical `{description, tag, path}` vocabulary for the artifacts the task will plainly create (DESIGN §5 *Artifact-registry worker*). |   • Reconcile *(when needed)* | `phase_reconcile` | compute set of `requires` capability tags with no matching `provides` across merged planner output. **Before matching, two mechanical passes run: (a) `_promote_external_collisions(plans)` rewrites any `extent: external` entry whose tag is in some plan's `provides` to `extent: in_plan` (the in-plan producer wins); (b) `_collect_external_preconditions(plans)` extracts every remaining `extent: external` entry into a deduped list `{tag, reasons[], originating_subtasks[]}` that bypasses the reconciler and is persisted by `_write_plan`. Both passes are re-run after `_apply_reconciler_output` so any `extent: external` entries on reconciler-added connector subtasks also flow through the same machinery (collision-promoted if a provider now exists; otherwise added to the persisted preconditions list). If empty: short-circuit (no worker spawn, plan unchanged). Else: spawn one reconciler worker. Its per-subtask input view (`subtask_views`) carries `id`, `title`, `intent`, **`scope_note`**, `depends_on`, `files_likely_touched`, `provides` and the `in_plan` `requires` tags — `scope_note` because `prompts/reconciler.md` scopes `conditional_drop` to signals in the consumer's `intent`/`scope_note` and shipping only half of that surface disables the rule for whichever half the planner used. `tests/test_reconciler_payload_fields.py` derives the required field set from the prompt text so a newly-named signal cannot drift. Including `scope_note` grows `subtask_views` meaningfully, but the payload is deliberately **uncapped** — it travels over stdin, so `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` no longer bounds it (see "User prompt transport") and nothing truncates it. The nearest real ceiling is the ~224K-token client-side refusal that applies under `--dangerously-force-strict-output` (`ContextOverflow`), so a future field added here should be sized against that, not assumed free. The worker emits eight actions — five *resolution* (renames / add_provide / added_subtasks / conditional_drop / drop_require), two *cycle-breaking-only* (dependency_edges / merged_subtasks; `drop_require` also plays a cycle-breaking role), and one *escape hatch* (unresolvable). **Wire shape vs internal shape:** the four `{sid, tag, reason}` ops travel as one `op`-discriminated `tag_ops` array and a new subtask's `requires` travels in a sibling `added_requires` keyed by sid — both forced by grammar compilation (see §7). `_expand_reconciler_output` fans that into the eight arrays named here before any consumer runs, so every apply step and state field below uses the action names, not the wire names. If `unresolvable` is non-empty, dead-subtask elimination (`_prune_dead_subtasks`) first removes fully-speculative subtasks whose every `in_plan` requires is unresolvable when ≥1 domain has 0 subtasks (see "Phase 2½ checks" below); if entries remain after pruning, `die()` with the reconciler's diagnosis (DESIGN §5). Otherwise, the orchestrator applies the seven action arrays mechanically. After applying, runs an **acyclicity gate** (Tarjan's SCC over the post-mutation graph); on cycle, deep-copies the pre-mutation plans, computes a recommended cycle-resolution per SCC from structural signals, respawns the reconciler once with a structured retry prompt + bounded "must-include" set of acceptable operations, and re-runs the gate. If still cyclic, `die()` with the SCC + offending mutations enumerated. See "Phase 2½ checks" and "Cycle-resolution retry loop" below. |
|   • Overlap judge *(when 2+ planners)* | `phase_overlap_judge` | spawn one `plan_overlap_judge` worker against the reconciled plan to detect cross-planner **surface collisions** — two subtasks producing the same exported artifact (same component / function / primitive) with incompatible APIs. Schema in `SCHEMAS["plan_overlap_judge"]`. Output: zero or more `collisions`, each with `resolution ∈ {merge, drop_a, drop_b, unresolvable}` and (when `resolution=merge`) a non-empty `merge_feasibility` statement that becomes the merged subtask's unified intent. Orchestrator applies actions mechanically through `_apply_overlap_collisions` with the **anchor-survivor rule**: when one sid appears in 2+ non-`unresolvable` collisions (computed by `_compute_overlap_anchors`), it is the structural anchor of the cluster and survives every merge it participates in — overriding `_apply_overlap_merge`'s default lex-smaller rule (the default is a determinism device with no semantic content). Rationale: membership is bare appearance count and carries no semantic claim — a sid the judge dropped twice is an anchor too, it just never survives to use the hint — but a sid the judge kept returning to is a better merge tie-break than alphabetical order. Do **not** read it as "the broader subtask that absorbs each partner": that is false on 20 of the 64 two-collision combinations (DESIGN §5). Pairs that lack a shared endpoint use the lex-smaller default unchanged. Per-pair: `merge` → `_apply_overlap_merge` (with optional `survivor_hint=anchor_sid` when applicable; union of fields, intent concatenation, downstream `depends_on` rewrites); `drop_*` → `_apply_overlap_drop` (mirrors `conditional_drops` apply step); `unresolvable` → `die()` at plan time with both sids + artifact + judge's reason. The validator also die()s on the keep-and-delete contradiction (`_contradictory_drop_sids`: a `drop_*` whose dropped sid *survives* another collision — kept as a merge endpoint or as the non-dropped side of another `drop_*`. One claim deletes it, another keeps it; no apply order satisfies both. Deliberately **not** anchor membership — a sid dropped by several collisions is an anchor by appearance but is coherent multi-drop output, applied as a cluster by `_apply_multidrop`). **Per-resolution cycle avoidance:** before applying each `merge` / `drop_*`, `_apply_overlap_collisions` tentatively applies it to a copy (`_would_cycle_after`) and, if it would introduce a dependency cycle, skips it (`skipped_would_cycle`) — keeping both subtasks separate for the integrator instead of `die()`ing the run; the final post-merge Tarjan gate is retained only as a never-fires backstop. **Cheap-skip** when fewer than 2 planners produced subtasks, or total subtask count < 2 (no possible cross-planner collision). **Python backstop** asserts every `merge` carries non-empty `merge_feasibility` — caught at `_validate_overlap_judge_output` before any apply. Opt-out via `--skip-overlap-judge` (mirrors `--skip-smoke`; env `LEERIE_SKIP_OVERLAP_JUDGE`; `leerie.toml` `skip_overlap_judge`). Persists full judge output to `state.data["plan_overlap_judge"]` and post-apply mutations to `state.data["plan_overlap_applied"]` for audit. See "Phase 2¾ checks" below. |

It never re-plans and never `die()`s. The deterministic `check_required_items_coverage` floor was DELETED: it required one subtask's `title + success_criteria_seed` token set to be a SUPERSET of a required item's and passed **0 of 102 items** across every run that ever carried `required_items`, while violating CLAUDE.md's prohibition on inferring meaning from prose. The judge is retained but non-terminal — on identical input it returned a different finding set 85% of the time (n=20) with an empty intersection across samples. Contrast `wiring_judge` (99% true, 69/70) and `plan_overlap_judge` (deterministic backstops), which keep their authority. The gate's authority rests on the typed item accounting, not the judge. | 3 Schedule | `_detect_no_work`, `_warn_cross_planner_file_overlap`, `_warn_layer_gaps`, `_warn_provider_subset_subtasks`, `_warn_test_subtask_missing_producer_edge`, `_filter_offtree_subtasks`, `_filter_satisfied_subtasks`, `_schedule`, `phase_wiring_gate`, `check_plan_wiring`, `_validate_plan` | **First: `_detect_no_work(plans)` short-circuits when every plan has `status: "ready"` and empty `subtasks` (DESIGN §8 *The cleared-but-empty terminal state*)** — `_finish_no_work_run` records `no_work_required=true` + per-domain bases in state.json, writes `finished_at` to state.json + run.json (`no_push=True`), logs the summary, and skips phases 4–6. Otherwise: warn on cross-planner file overlap; warn on layer gaps (DESIGN §5 *Migration-surface completeness*); warn on provider-subset subtasks (a subtask whose entire `files_likely_touched` is a subset of an ordered predecessor's; advisory only); warn on under-wired test subtasks (`_warn_test_subtask_missing_producer_edge` — a `test-`-prefixed subtask declaring no `requires`/`depends_on` while the plan has producing subtasks; advisory only, scoped to the `test-` prefix — `phase_wiring_gate`'s constrained repair is the actual enforcer of this class); soft-drop subtasks whose `files_likely_touched` resolves outside the run's repo root, recorded in `state.data["dropped_subtasks"]`. **Then `_filter_satisfied_subtasks(plans, repo_root, st, caps, models, efforts, protect=)`** (after which `_finish_if_every_fix_already_on_head(st, caps, fix_ids_before, plans)` ends the run via `_finish_no_work_run` when every subtask flagged `fixes_reported_symptom` before the sweep was dropped by it and `_acceptance_passes_on_head(st, caps)` — some held-out set was measured on HEAD and none of the MEASURED sets fails; any error proceeds with the plan: DESIGN §8 *A plan whose fixes are all already on HEAD ends as no work*) spawns one read-only `satisfied_probe` worker per surviving subtask (bounded by `max_parallel`), each evaluating that subtask's `success_criteria_seed` against the base tree; subtasks the probe marks `satisfied` are soft-dropped (`reason: "already_satisfied"` + evidence, DESIGN §8 *Already-satisfied subtask elimination*) unless the falsifier shows the criterion unmet on the base first (`_falsify_satisfied_drops(st, caps, models, efforts, base_sha, subtasks, dropped, cache)`, DESIGN §8 *A subtask is dropped as already satisfied only when the falsifier cannot show its criterion unmet on the base*): every `already_satisfied` candidate whose cache entry has no `falsifier` record is one item `_satisfied_falsifier_item(s)` — `{item: <intent>, parts: [<success_criteria_seed>], source_ref: "subtask <sid>"}` (the seed alone as `item`, no parts, when the intent is blank) — and all of them go to one `_falsify_items(..., sha=base_sha, base_claim=True, names={i: "base-<sid>"}, probes_root=<run_dir>/satisfied-probe/probes, persist=None)` call; a subtask with a confirmed sample is taken out of `dropped` (logged, kept), one with none stays dropped. The outcome `{confirmed, samples}` is written to `satisfied_probe_cache[sid]["falsifier"]` and saved; a cached outcome is reused (a confirmed one keeps the subtask without a run). A falsifier that is skipped (`_falsify_items` returns `skipped`), raises, or records no outcome for a subtask leaves its drop standing, uncached, with a log line; a `satisfied: false` verdict whose typed fields agree (`unsatisfied_reason == "artifact_missing"`, `equivalent_coverage_exists == true`, and an **explicit** `sibling_invalidation_risk == false`) is soft-dropped the same way with `reason: "equivalent_coverage"` — any other combination, or any field absent, keeps the subtask, so the sibling channel stays keep-only by construction (DESIGN §8 *A "not satisfied" verdict carries a typed reason*). Each probe's payload carries a `surviving_siblings` array (every other subtask's `provides`/`files_likely_touched`) so a probe can decline a drop a still-pending sibling would invalidate (DESIGN §8 *The sibling-invalidation case*) — context for a *keep* decision only. Skipped when `state.data["skip_satisfied_check"]`. If this empties every `status: "ready"` plan, the gate routes to `_finish_no_work_run` via a synthesized `no_work_map`, preceded by `_mark_dispute_unacted(st)`, as at the empty-plans (`_detect_no_work`) exit. The sweep's `protect` is `_fix_ids_held_out_sets_protect(st, caps, fix_ids_before)`: the ids flagged `fixes_reported_symptom`, when held-out sets exist, some were measured on HEAD (`_acceptance_results_on_head`), and `_acceptance_any_fails` holds — the settle's rule — else empty, and empty without running the sets when `skip_satisfied_check` is set (there is no sweep to protect from); when the planning worktree's HEAD (ensured by the caller, not again here) equals `acceptance.validity_base` (every set failed there during validation) it returns the ids without running the sets; protected subtasks are never offered to the probe and so never dropped (DESIGN §8: executed evidence outranks the probe; any error protects nothing). Both soft-drop filters vanish subtask ids, so each calls `_remap_vanished_deps(surviving, {sid: [] for sid in dropped})` (DESIGN §5 *Id-vanishing operations*) to prune dangling `depends_on` references, and — since a drop also orphans the **tag channel** — calls `_prune_orphaned_requires(plans, dropped_provides)` once over all plans to remove inbound `requires` tags whose only provider was dropped. The probe's tool allowlist is a base-tree-only subset (`SATISFIED_PROBE_TOOLS` in `orchestrator/leerie.py`) — no `git log` / non-HEAD ref, since a worktree shares the repo's full ref DB. In this first pass a defect is repaired only when `kind == "missing_requires"`, the sid is in the plan, the edge isn't already declared, and the edge doesn't close a cycle (trialled via `_would_cycle_after`, cumulative across trials); `_fanin_and_fallback` then works the residual of every kind but `missing_provides` (a warning), so `broken_by_merge`, `broken_by_drop` and `orphaned_dependent` edge requests are ordered there too. `tag_or_dep` resolves against **both** dependency channels, first match wins: (a) **tag channel** — one in-plan provider → append to `requires`; (b) **id channel** — `tag_or_dep` names a surviving subtask id → append to `depends_on` via `_add_depends_on_edge`; (c) **single-cluster fan-out** — several providers sharing one `_cofile_cluster` (§5½ (P1) *Sub-file*) → append the `requires` tag, ordering behind the whole cluster. Each repair records its `channel`. After the repair loop, `_filter_defects_already_ordered(plans, defects) -> (surviving, notes)` re-checks the unrepaired residual against the plan's actual ordering — resolved through `_build_predecessor_graph` (so `requires` edges with `extent: in_plan` count, not just `depends_on`) — dropping a defect only when **every** producer (never just one) is a direct predecessor of the sid; transitive-only orderings don't count. Scoped to `kind == "missing_requires"`; `broken_by_drop`/`broken_by_merge` findings pass through untouched, since ordering can't refute a claim that the work itself is gone. Before any repair, `_filter_provably_false_wiring_defects` discards findings the plan itself contradicts: a `broken_by_*` whose capability is still provided, or whose capability was provided by a subtask dropped `already_satisfied` or `equivalent_coverage` (same base-tree premise). Before that loop, `_expand_multi_value_wiring_defects` splits a `missing_requires` defect whose `tag_or_dep` names several comma-joined values into one defect per value (the schema types the field as a bare string, so a comma-joined list is schema-valid but resolves nothing under exact lookup) — conservative: only `missing_requires`, only when the string doesn't already resolve whole, only when every part resolves to a surviving id or provided tag. When any repair lands, `_run_phases` re-runs `_schedule(plans)` and rewrites `state.data["plan_snapshot"]`. It reads `state.data["dropped_subtasks"]` for its `broken_by_drop`/`broken_by_merge` reasoning, so it must run post-drop. Its resume skip is keyed on the **presence of `state.data["wiring_gate"]`** (written only when the gate passes) — **not** `plan_snapshot`, which is written before the gate runs and so is present even on a died gate; keying on the snapshot would let `resume` silently bypass a gate the run had already failed. A `WorkerError` degrades (the deterministic check below still guards the structural channel). (2) The deterministic `check_plan_wiring(subtasks)` replays `_validate_plan`'s own provider-existence + `depends_on`-existence logic and `die()`s with a wiring-specific message before the generic `_validate_plan` die; it runs outside the `plan_snapshot` if/else on every path, including a budget-check resume, as the cheap structural backstop. |

A RED base logs a loud provisioning warning and writes `run.json.health.base_suite`. Runners are matched by `_acceptance_runner` on the basename of each word `_shell_scan` finds, at any depth (falling back to `_rough_words(_strip_comments(cmd))` — words split at unquoted blanks and operator characters, quotes and `$'…'` handled, where `shlex` fails on `$'…'`; with every comment — a `#` starting an unquoted word — removed up to its newline by `_strip_comments`, which tracks quotes, `$'…'`, escapes (a line continuation leaves a word boundary as it was), `${…}`, `$$`, substitution parens, and whether it is inside a backtick body (only there does a backtick end a comment); so a quoted `'#x'`, a mid-word `#` and `$(echo u)#sub` are not comments and a runner on a later line is still found — when the scan cannot close the command, such as an unparenthesised `case` pattern inside `$(…)`, so the runner's exit codes still apply), so a runner wrapped in `make`/`tox` is not recognised. `_parse_runner_report(kind, path)` returns `{executed, collection_error, cases{id: status}}` from `_runner_report_cases(kind, path, tree=None)` — every case as `{id, file, status}`, status `passed` / `failed` / `skipped` / `load_error` (JUnit: a case whose `<error>` has pytest's fixed `message="collection failure"` is a `load_error` — whatever its `classname`, which `--junit-prefix` fills in — a `<failure>` or `<error>` case `failed`, a setup error included; jest-compatible JSON: a suite with `testExecError`, or failed with no assertion results, is a `load_error`, assertions passed/failed as such and any other status skipped; `rspec-json`: `examples[].status`, pending skipped, `summary.errors_outside_of_examples_count > 0` a `load_error`; `minitest-json`: `cases[].status`, `error` counting as failed; `go-json`: `Test` events' pass/fail/skip, a package that failed with no test event a `load_error`; `libtest-json`: `type: test` events' ok/failed/ignored; executed = passed + failed) or None when there is no readable report of a known kind. `_runner_report_failing_ids` (B*'s IDs) is derived from the same cases. With a report: a collection error is no verdict unless `failure_mode == "import"`, when it FAILS. `_write_acceptance_set` passes `"import"` only after checking it: a non-`.py` file declared `"import"` is never run (logged and dropped alone, so the set survives on its other files), and a `.py` one is passed as `"import"` only if `_acceptance_parse_probe(st, caps, tree, rel, targets, log_path, label)` returns True. It names a throwaway file beside the declared one with `_acceptance_probe_rel` — the first of: the declared name with `_leerie_probe_<sha256(rel)[:12]>` after its stem, `leerie_probe_<…>_` before it, then the short `test_leerie_probe_<…>` / `leerie_probe_<…>_test` (candidates over `_PROBE_NAME_MAX` = 200 bytes skipped) that the repo's test globs (`resolve_test_file_globs`, `_is_test_file`) accept, else the first candidate anyway (a `{files}` template renders any name; for `{test_files}` `_acceptance_cmd` then renders nothing) — writes a `unittest.TestCase` there whose body first writes a marker under the tree's `<measure-dir>/reports/` and then compiles each target's bytes (targets: the file plus every other new `.py` file the writer created), runs it through `_acceptance_cmd` and `_run_streaming` (the project's own command, so its interpreter), and deletes it. The body writes the marker `ran` first and `ok` after every target compiled. It returns `(verdict, reason)`: True on exit 0 with `ok`; False with `ran` alone — a target did not compile ("does not parse"); None otherwise, with a reason naming which — the marker directory is not writable (checked by the orchestrator writing the marker path first, since the probe runs as the same user), the parse check passed but the run failed after it (`ok`, non-zero: a teardown error, a threshold, or another test the command ran), the command could not be run (exit 126/127), the container's limits killed it (fork exhaustion), the command collected or selected no test (no marker, exit 0 or the runner's `_RUNNER_NOTHING_COLLECTED_EXIT`, pytest's 5: the probe was deselected or skipped), it failed before reaching the check (no marker, any other non-zero exit: a conftest, plugin or package import — such as a conftest importing the entry point an import defect lacks), there is no command for the probe's name, or an exception or timeout. The writer logs the reason. Short of True, the file is validated as `"assertion"`, and the log gives the probe's reason. Back in `_run_acceptance_file`'s report rules: zero executed is no verdict; otherwise the exit code decides. Without a report: one of the invoked runner's `_RUNNER_NO_VERDICT_EXITS` (pytest: 2/3/4/5) is no verdict — not `_measure_blt`, whose unmeasurable test matches `No such file or directory` anywhere in the output, which a failing missing-file defect test also prints. Every evaluation (`_evaluate_acceptance_sets(..., confirm=True)`, the default) confirms a failing set file under B*'s blocks while the set is placed: `_confirm_still_failing(candidates, run_final, caps, label=)` takes `_confirm_hold()` (the confirm lock, `_confirm_lock`; nothing inside an evaluation's exclusive hold), waits on `_confirm_gate`, then reruns the failing files serially `confirm_pairs` times (`confirm_pairs_escalated` after a gate timeout) inside `confirm_budget_sec`; a file is `confirmed` only if every required rerun ran, had a verdict and failed it — or the budget alone cut the vote short and every rerun that finished failed it (`seen_failing=True`: the first run failed it; each rerun's files share one deadline, and a rerun the deadline cuts returns a `_RerunCut` carrying the files it finished) — else `resource_affected` — the result keeps only confirmed files in `failing_files` (those the budget cut short also in `budget_short_files`), lists the rest as `resource_affected_files`, and a set whose failures were all resource-affected is `unmeasured` (no evidence either way). `_acceptance_any_fails` (which replaced `_acceptance_majority_fails`) is True when any MEASURED set (`_acceptance_measured`) failed; with no measured set the gate records no evidence and does not repair. When any measured set fails it runs at most two repair rounds — a `conformer` call at `EFFORT_ACCEPTANCE_REPAIR = "high"`, `sid=acceptance-repair-r<n>`, whose prompt carries `_format_acceptance_task_section(task, required_items)` (the task text and each required item as `{item_index, item, parts?}` — `parts` the classifier's, verbatim; not held-out data) and then `_format_acceptance_failures_section` (the failing files' declared case names from the shown sets only — `_acceptance_shown_indices(sets)`; decided by whether a shown set fails (an unmeasured set is no failure), not by whether names were found: when no shown set fails, the section says every failing test is one the conformer is not shown; when a shown set fails without declared names, it says the failing cases were not named; when named and unnamed failing files mix, `(other failing tests declared no case names)` follows every name, the import-failure list included — those of files the set's `modes` marks `"import"` listed apart, as having failed to load against the UNFIXED tree — a fact validation observed, never a claim about the current tree — the two highest-indexed valid sets are never shown when four or more are valid — plus the defect contract; never runner output or test source) — re-evaluating every set after each round and saving state after each (an errored round too — re-evaluated when the staging HEAD is not the commit the current verdict was measured on, or cannot be read: a worker can commit and then fail, and an interrupted earlier attempt at the same round can have committed before a resume). Every evaluation of staging's HEAD goes through a local `_measure(label)` that reads the staging HEAD sha first and evaluates `rev=` that sha (the pre-repair control below evaluates `before_sha` directly), so each verdict is recorded with the commit it describes (`gate.initial_sha`, `gate.rounds[].sha`; a retry that replaces a round's results replaces its sha too). A round whose own evaluation measures nothing while the verdict before it measured is measured once more inside the loop (`gate-r<n>-retry`, recorded as `rounds[].retried`), so a one-off install failure does not stop the rounds on a verdict that cannot fail; the post-loop retry below is skipped for a commit a round already retried. Rounds run for at most `caps["acceptance_repair_rounds"]` (default 2), rounds already recorded before a resume counting against the cap; each round first checks the latest verdict (the last round with non-empty `results` — an errored round carries them only when it committed — else `gate.initial`) and stops once it passes, so a resume after a passing round runs no further round. A recorded `gate.before_sha` sends a resumed gate into this repair branch whatever the verdicts, so the rollback check below always runs on commits a repair made. With fewer than four valid sets nothing is held back: that is logged, and the section then does not tell the conformer of tests it is not shown. Each round's `bump_workers` is inside the round's `try`, so an exhausted worker budget ends the repair like any worker failure (`rounds[].error`) and the rollback check still runs — the gate's caller already treats any gate exception as advisory. With no readable staging HEAD (`_branch_head_sha`, which returns `""` on any failure, an `OSError` spawning git included — a change shared by its other callers, which already treated `""` as unknown) there is no rollback target and no round runs. A round's worker failure of any `Exception` type — not only `WorkerError`/timeout, since `claude_p` lets an `OSError` spawning the worker through — ends the repair like the others, and the rollback check still runs. After the rounds, when staging's HEAD moved (or cannot be read), the repair is rolled back if the repo's `tests` axis passed before the rounds (`gate.pre_tests_passed`; a measurement that raises counts as unmeasured) and fails after them **and the failure is confirmed** by `_acceptance_confirm_red_axis(st, caps, staging, before_sha, test_cmd, log_path=...)` → `(reason, record)`, the record saved as `gate.post_tests_confirm`: the failing IDs on staging (`_ratchet_test_ids`, so a forbidden command is replaced as at final) go through `_ratchet_exec` against `before_sha` with an empty failing set before (the axis passed there), and only a non-empty `new` confirms (`{new, resource_affected}`); with no per-test report the axis is measured once more with `memo=False` (`label_prefix="acceptance-post-again"`) and a second red confirms (`{no_report: true, reproduced}`); unconfirmed, the repair is kept and logged (DESIGN §8: one flaky red run used to reset every round); a confirmation that raises falls back to the red run (`{error}`), or if `initial` was measured and the latest verdict measures nothing — and a retry of the repaired tree (`label="gate-retry"`; when it measures, it replaces the last round's results and no rollback follows) measures nothing too while the pre-repair tree does (`_evaluate_acceptance_sets(..., rev=before_sha)`, `label="gate-before"`; when neither measures, the failure is the environment's and the repair is kept, with a log line): `gate.rolled_back` and `gate.rollback_reason` (`turned the test axis red` / `left the held-out sets unmeasurable`) are saved, then `_restore_tree(staging, gate.before_sha)` resets and confirms HEAD is there (up to three attempts a second apart, a spawn `OSError` on the reset or an unreadable HEAD after it counting as not yet decided) — on success the verdict becomes `initial`; on failure `gate.rollback_failed`, a WARNING, the verdict stays the repair tree's (that tree ships), and `gate.residual` is created if absent and carries `rollback_failed: true`, which `_prior_delivery_residual` forwards to the next run's planner with `unmeasured_final`. A resume that finds `rolled_back` recorded repeats the (idempotent) rollback — its verdict then `initial` on success, the repair tree's on failure — running no round and no measurement — both persisted before the first round, so a resume mid-repair compares against the pre-repair tree rather than re-measuring an already-repaired one. Logged and recorded set counts (`residual.failing_sets`/`total_sets`, `acceptance_dispute`) are over measured sets only. **Before the residual**, when `gate.audited` is unset, `_acceptance_audit_and_rewrite(st, caps, models, efforts, staging, final, final_sha)` (DESIGN §8 *A set that keeps failing is audited, and rewritten once*; any exception is logged and leaves `final` as it was; `gate.audited` saved after) takes each measured failing set not `broken` and under `acceptance_rewrite_rounds`, in index order: (1) `_acceptance_mechanical_findings(repo, own, set)` on the own start's JS/TS import graph (`_js_source_graph`: `git ls-tree`/`cat-file --batch`, `tsconfig.json` `paths` aliases via `_ts_path_aliases`, test files by `_JS_TEST_PATH_RE`, support modules by `_JS_SUPPORT_PATH_RE` imported only by tests/support) — M1 a line matching `_M1_POSITIONAL_MOCK_READ_RE`, M2 a named import from a production module no other production module's source names; (2) `_acceptance_audit_on_rev` — `_acceptance_tree` makes `<run_dir>/worktrees/acceptance-audit` at the verdict's sha (deps, and a test DB in a Prisma repo), `_acceptance_audit_in` places the set, reads its failing cases with messages (`_acceptance_case_failures`: `_run_acceptance_file(validating=True)`, `observed["failure_messages"]` from JUnit `<failure>`/`<error>` and jest `failureMessages`), copies the task's files in, builds the payload (`_repo_test_harness(repo, rev, _set_production_imports(graph, set))` — up to 40 newest neighbour tests by `_git_recency`, 8 support helpers with `_JS_EXPORT_RE` names, 5 exemplars — then TASK, references, contract, set files, failing cases) and runs `set_audit_samples` `set_auditor` samples (`bump_workers` each; a sample's `WorkerError`/timeout is no finding), keeping the union of `_verify_set_audit_case`-backed `set_defect` cases; (3) only when neither fired, the surrogate witness — `_acceptance_surrogate` once per gate (`_acceptance_writer_checkout` at the own start in `worktrees/acceptance-surrogate`, report copied in and removed after, deps, test DB, one `surrogate_fixer`; abstains when it fails or leaves no change), `_acceptance_run_placed` runs the set there with B* confirmation, and a confirmed failing file is a trigger whose note also carries `_acceptance_audit_in`'s findings on that tree. A trigger bumps `rewrite_rounds` and records `rewrite.triggers` (saved), then `_acceptance_rewrite_set` calls `_write_acceptance_set(..., rewrite_of=set, note=_rewrite_note(triggers))` in `worktrees/acceptance-rewrite-<k>` (the set's files placed after the untracked snapshot, the note appended), and once more (`attempt=2`) when the result has `declared_defect: false`. A valid result replaces the set's `_SET_FIELDS` (the original kept under `rewrite.original`), is re-evaluated on the same sha, and if it still fails is audited again; otherwise the original is kept (`kept_original`, `reason`). `broken: true` when that re-audit counts a finding, or when the original's audit did and the rewrite was not kept. `rewrite.result` replaces the set's entry in `final`. The surrogate clone and its database are removed at the end. A residual is recorded in `acceptance.gate.residual` and the run ships (non-blocking); `phase_finalize` always runs Delivery gate routing (DESIGN §8 *Grouped judging at coverage item counts*): `_delivery_judge_unmet` never judges an item typed `verifiability: "external"`; an item with `untouched_paths` is settled by `_d1_untouched_verdict` — `git -C <staging> diff --name-only <own start>..HEAD -- <pathspecs>` (own start = `_acceptance_own_start`; a path containing `*`, `?` or `[` becomes `:(glob)<p>`; an absolute, `..`-bearing or non-`[A-Za-z0-9_./*?[]-]` path, an unknown own start or a git error returns `None` and the item is judged); the rest go to `_d1_judge_packs` and one `delivery_judge` prompt per pack, run concurrently under `max_parallel`, the defect contract asked of the first pack only. |
| 6 Finalize | `phase_finalize` → `finalize.sh`, `cleanup.sh`; launcher then pushes on host | verify the run branch is non-empty; run `cleanup.sh --run-id <id>` (worktrees only — finalize deletes no branch: the per-subtask branches are refs of the run's own repository, never brought back to the user's, and go with the run directory at `leerie prune`; DESIGN §6 *Branch cleanup at finalize*); record `finished_at` in `run.json` (the run branch is **kept** as the PR head; state dir is kept as audit). **The push + PR step has moved to the host launcher** (DESIGN §6 *Finalization*). A successfully finalized run (`finished_at` set AND `current_phase` == "phase 6: finalize") is **terminal on resume** — the orchestrator returns without re-executing phases 4→5→6, preventing a concurrent `decide_teardown` race.
