Before it returns, `_compose_pr_for_a_push_chosen_after_finalize(st, no_push, caps, models, efforts, pr_template_override)` runs `_compose_pr_via_llm` when the resume continues the run with a push (`args.no_push` false, after `_continue_run_choices`) and `run.json` holds neither `pushed_at` nor `pr_title` (a run the host already pushed had its PR composed under the choice that pushed it; a later resume does not run `pr_writer` again) — a push chosen after finalize (`leerie resume <id> --push` of a finished `--no-push` run) gets its PR written by `pr_writer`, not the fallback (DESIGN §6 *One push choice per run, on every runtime*); otherwise it does nothing. Pinned by `tests/test_resume_push_writes_pr.py`. **`current_phase` is stamped `"phase 6: finalize"` only *after* `finalize.sh` returns 0** (the non-empty-branch check passes), not on phase entry: the `die()` on a `finalize.sh` failure sets `finished_at` via the `except SystemExit` handler, so stamping the phase before the check would make a *died* finalize byte-identical to a *succeeded* one, and the resume completion guard would mistake it for terminal and hand the host launcher an empty run branch to push (which then fails at `gh pr create` with "No commits between …"). Stamping after the check keeps a died finalize resumable — `current_phase` stays at its pre-finalize value, the resume guard falls through, and `resume` re-runs `finalize.sh`'s non-empty check. |
| Post-run Judge | `phase_judge`, `_judge_capture` | standalone post-run phase (not part of main orchestrate flow): reads `calls.ndjson`, runs one `_judge_capture()` per record in parallel under `asyncio.Semaphore(max_parallel)`, writes per-record verdicts to `<judge-dir>/<call_id>.json` and a summary `INDEX.json`; uses `prompts/judge.md` rubric. Each `judge` call runs with `cwd=_payload_only_cwd(st)` and `allowed_tools=PAYLOAD_ONLY_TOOLS` — the record is its whole input, and the user's checkout is never its cwd (DESIGN §8 *A worker that does not commit never runs in a tree leerie measures*) |
| Post-run Heal | `HealState`, `_heal_baseline`, `_heal_apply_patch`, `_heal_replay_patched`, `_request_patch`, `phase_heal` | `_request_patch`'s `patch_generator` runs payload-only (`_payload_only_cwd(st)`, `PAYLOAD_ONLY_TOOLS`); heal-loop phases: `HealState` persists failing_samples / baseline / history / best_so_far at `<heal-dir>/<call_type>/state.json`; `_heal_baseline(call_type, failing_records, n, heal_dir, caps, st, models)` runs n unpatched replays per record + judge, writes baseline verdicts + state; `_heal_apply_patch(call_type, iter_n, patch_text, anchor_match, heal_dir, failing_records)` materialises patched prompts under `iter-<N>/patched-prompts/`; `_heal_replay_patched(call_type, iter_n, n, heal_dir, caps, st, models)` runs n patched replays per record + judge, appends iteration record to state.history; `_request_patch(state, iter_n, st, caps, models)` invokes the `patch_generator` worker (schema `SCHEMAS["patch_generator"]`, SID `heal-patch-<call_type>-iter<N>`, prompt from `prompts/patch_generator.md`) and returns `(anchor, replacement)` — raises `ValueError` if the returned anchor is not a literal substring of the resolved prompt body (code-enforced per the prompts-are-advisory principle); `phase_heal(call_type, failing_records, heal_dir, caps, st, models, request_patch_fn=None, n, config)` drives the full baseline→loop→report cycle; `request_patch_fn` defaults to the real `_request_patch` when `None`, or accepts a sync/async 2-arg stub for testing |

`phase_classify` runs before `gather_answers` because the question set depends
on the classification.

Between Phase 3 and Phase 4, `_write_plan()` persists the merged plan
(`<state-root>/runs/<run-id>/plan.json`, carrying the full task text
under its top-level `"task"` key) and per-subtask spec files
(`<state-root>/runs/<run-id>/subtasks/<id>.json`). It also writes
`<state-root>/runs/<run-id>/task.md`, the task text verbatim as plain
markdown. Each spec file carries `_task_ref` — the path to `task.md` —
plus `_task_ref_bytes`, its size, rather than a second copy of the task
text: inlining the full task into every subtask spec was measured to
bloat briefs significantly on large task documents, spilling past the
CLI's Read cap.

`_task_ref` points at `task.md` and **not** at `plan.json`, which is by
construction the task text plus every subtask body — strictly larger
than any single brief it replaced — so referencing it relocates the
Read-cap failure instead of removing it. Format carries the rest: the
cap is 25,000 **tokens**, and markdown measures meaningfully more
bytes/token than JSON, so the same text can sit over the cap inside
`plan.json` but under it as markdown. On large task documents that
alone isn't enough; the implementer prompt's `offset`/`limit` guidance,
keyed on `_task_ref_bytes`, is what keeps the read from failing. The
conformance phase derives its build/lint/test commands via
`_infer_build_lint_test(repo_root)` for any axis `.leerie/config.toml` does
not declare: the commands the `blt_discovery` worker read from the
repository this run (`_DISCOVERED_BLT`), empty strings before phase 1½
and for an axis the repository has no step for. There is no table of
files to commands (DESIGN §6½ *A repository's build, lint and test
commands are read from it*).

**Build/lint/test discovery.** `_discover_blt(st, caps, models, efforts,
repo_root, recipe)`, called by `phase_provision` after the recipe is
validated and normalized and before it is recorded (so a resume skips the
phase only when both are). Spawns `blt_discovery`
(`prompts/blt_discovery.md`, `SCHEMAS["blt_discovery"]`: `build`, `lint`,
`test`, each `{command, evidence}`, `command` empty for no step) with
`_blt_discovery_user_prompt(recipe)` (the recipe's non-`none` steps,
`(<working_dir>) <argv>` one per line, or `(none)`), `cwd=_judgment_cwd(st)`,
`INSPECT_TOOLS`, `max_turns=30`, `autonomous=False`, through
`_run_checked_loop` with `check=_blt_command_issues(result, repo_root,
bin_paths, PATH)`: per non-empty command, `SHELL_OPERATOR` when it holds
any of `_BLT_SHELL_OPERATORS` (`&&`, `||`, `|`, `;`, `>`, `<`, backtick,
`$(`), `UNPARSEABLE` when `shlex.split` fails, `NO_PROGRAM` when nothing
but `NAME=value` words remain or the program is `cd`, else
`_recipe_program_issues` on the words. An axis whose command still has an
issue after the rounds is logged and left empty. The three commands are
recorded at `st.data["provision"]["blt"]`, set as `_DISCOVERED_BLT`, and
logged; a worker with no answer records three empty commands. Then
`_resolve_memory_caps(caps, repo_root)` resolves the memory ceiling and
demand again: the declared Node heap is read from the scripts those
commands run, which the start-of-run resolution could not see.
`_resume_provision_env` sets `_DISCOVERED_BLT` from `provision.blt` on
`resume`. Pinned by `tests/test_blt_discovery.py`.

**Declared BLT commands (`.leerie/config.toml`).** A repo may commit
`.leerie/config.toml` with explicit `build`, `lint`, and/or `test` keys
that override the corresponding axis read from the repository. Missing
keys fall through to `_infer_build_lint_test()`. An empty-string value
means "not applicable" (the same convention) and is preserved rather than
replaced. The file also accepts a `setup_packages` key (comma-separated
apt package names) that triggers per-repo Dockerfile auto-generation
(§6½ *Auto-capture of repo dependencies*); not consumed by BLT resolution.

Resolution: **`_load_blt_config(repo_root)`** reads `.leerie/config.toml`
via `_read_toml_key()` for each of `build`/`lint`/`test`/`setup_packages`,
returning `None` when absent or a dict of only the present keys.
**`resolve_blt(repo_root)`** calls it; for each axis, uses the declared
value if present (including empty string), else falls through to
`_infer_build_lint_test()`. This is the function `_run_conformance_phase`
and `_run_final_conformance` both call — neither calls
`_infer_build_lint_test` directly.

`.leerie/config.toml` format (flat key = value, same parser as `leerie.toml`):

```toml
build = "make build"
lint  = "ruff check ."
test  = "pytest -x"
# setup_packages = "libvips-dev fonts-noto"
```

`plan.json` carries `{task, waves, subtasks, preconditions}`. The
`preconditions` array is the deduped list of `extent: external` `requires`
entries collected during phase 2½ (see DESIGN §5 `requires.extent`); each
entry is `{tag, reasons: [{sid, reason}, …], originating_subtasks: [sid, …]}`.
It is the human-facing surface for prerequisites the planners identified
but explicitly declared out-of-graph. The launcher / integrator surface
this list in the PR description so the human running the change sees what
must be true in the environment before the change is safe to ship.

Maps to `DESIGN.md`: §3.


### Isolation and the held-out sandbox (I3) — `scripts/landlock_exec.py --isolate` / `--sandbox`

DESIGN §6 *Every confined process has its own `/tmp`, `/dev/shm` and IPC,
and sees every other mount read-only*, *A confined process has its own
network; the outside is reached only through leerie's proxy*, *A held-out
evaluation runs alone, in a world that dies with it (I3)*, *No database
server leerie starts is ever unconfined*.

**The shim** (`scripts/landlock_exec.py`, stdlib only, single-threaded
until it execs):

```
landlock_exec.py [--isolate [--egress SOCK] [--forward PORT=SOCK]...
                  [--worker-root DIR [--cli]]]
                 [--rw PATH]... [--ro PATH]... -- CMD
landlock_exec.py --sandbox --view TREE [--place SRC=REL]...
                 [--replace SRC=REL]... [--remove REL]...
                 [--report PATH --report-fd N] [--worker-root DIR]
                 [--rw PATH]... [--ro PATH]... -- CMD
```

Without either flag it behaves as before (Landlock, seccomp, `run`).
`--isolate` and `--sandbox` exit 126, naming the step and its errno,
without running CMD when any step fails (`leerie: cannot isolate the
command, so it does not run: <step>: <errno>`). Functions, in call order:

- `enter_namespaces(*, sandbox: bool) -> None` — `unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER)`;
  `/proc/self/setgroups` ← `deny`; `uid_map` and `gid_map` ← `"<id> <id>
  1"` (the caller's own ids); then `unshare(CLONE_NEWNS | CLONE_NEWIPC |
  CLONE_NEWNET)` (step `unshare(mount/IPC/net)`), plus `CLONE_NEWUTS |
  CLONE_NEWPID` with `sandbox` (`unshare(mount/IPC/net/UTS/PID)`). Then
  `loopback_up()`, for both.
- `pivot_to_owned_root(carry_ro, carry_rw, *, sandbox) -> list[str]` —
  `/` made `rprivate`; a tmpfs (mode 0755, `nosuid,nodev`) mounted on
  `/tmp` as the new root, holding, for each entry of the old root, a
  directory with the entry `rbind`-mounted (a directory), an empty file
  with it bound (a file), the same symlink (a symlink), or an empty
  directory (`tmp` and `dev`: the container's `/dev` is never bound into
  the new root); `pivot_root(new, new/.oldroot)`; then
  `private_mounts("/.oldroot/dev")`; then each grant beneath `/tmp` (not `/tmp` itself)
  bound from `/.oldroot<path>` onto the same path in the new `/tmp` —
  except, in a sandbox, a write grant, which becomes an empty copy of its
  subdirectories (`_skeleton`: a held-out run gets a fresh private temp
  directory, `run/` included); then `/.oldroot` detached
  (`umount2(MNT_DETACH)`) and removed, and `chdir` back. Returns the
  carried write grants' mount points.
- `private_mounts(old_dev: str) -> None` — tmpfs on `/tmp` (`mode=1777`,
  `nosuid,nodev`), then `private_dev(old_dev)`.
- `private_dev(old_dev: str) -> None` — DESIGN §6 *No confined process
  holds or can open the operator's terminal*. A tmpfs on `/dev` (`DEV`;
  `mode=0755`, `nosuid,nodev,noexec`); for each of `DEV_NODES = ("null",
  "zero", "full", "random", "urandom", "tty")` that is a character device
  in `old_dev`, an empty file bound over from it (`MS_BIND`; a user
  namespace cannot `mknod`); the `DEV_LINKS` symlinks `fd ->
  /proc/self/fd`, `stdin`/`stdout`/`stderr -> /proc/self/fd/0..2`, `ptmx
  -> pts/ptmx`; directories `shm` and `pts`; tmpfs on `/dev/shm`
  (`mode=1777`, `nosuid,nodev`); `devpts` on `/dev/pts`
  (`newinstance,ptmxmode=0666,mode=620`, `nosuid,noexec`). A failure is
  step `make /dev: …`, `tmpfs /dev`, `bind /dev/<name>`, `tmpfs /dev/shm`
  or `devpts /dev/pts`. `readonly_mounts` makes `/dev` and each bound node
  read-only (a node on a read-only mount still writes).
- `bind_grants(rw: list[str], link_root: str | None = None) ->
  tuple[list[str], list[str]]` (`--isolate`; DESIGN §6 *The write grants on
  one mount are one mount*) — of the `rw` paths that exist and are not
  beneath `/tmp` or `/dev` (`_bindable`), each strictly beneath
  `link_root` (`--link-root DIR`, absolute, not `/`, only with
  `--isolate`) is bound with the others there: `link_root` bound onto
  itself once (`MS_BIND | MS_REC`, step `bind grant <path>`), then
  `_shield(link_root, grants)`: every entry beneath it that is no grant,
  beneath none and leads to none bound onto itself (`MS_BIND | MS_REC`,
  step `bind <path>`; a symbolic link skipped, an entry gone `ENOENT`
  skipped, a directory that cannot be listed step `list <path>`), the
  directories leading to a grant walked. Every other grant is bound onto
  itself apart. Returns `(grants, roots)`: the grants, and `[link_root]`
  when it was bound. `isolate(..., link_root=)` passes it through.
- `private_home(home, layers, size, grants) -> None` (`--home DIR
  --home-bytes N [--home-layer DIR]...`, with `--isolate` or `--sandbox`;
  DESIGN §6 *Every confined process has its own home*) — called by
  `isolate(..., home=, home_layers=, home_bytes=)` right after
  `pivot_to_owned_root`, before the grants are bound or overlaid; `home` is
  then in `roots` (its own mount kept writable, what is beneath it judged
  apart). Refuses (`IsolationError`) a `home` that is not a directory, a
  layer or home path holding `,`, `:` or a backslash, and a mount beneath
  `home` (`/proc/self/mountinfo`). Mounts a `tmpfs` (`size=N,mode=0700`,
  `nosuid,nodev`) on `_HOME_UPPER` (`/tmp/.leerie-home`), makes `u/` (the
  home's mode) and `w/` in it, binds `home` recursively at `_HOME_REAL`
  (`/tmp/.leerie-home-real`), mounts `overlay` on `home` with
  `lowerdir=<each existing layer not beneath home>:<home>`,
  `upperdir=_HOME_UPPER/u`, `workdir=_HOME_UPPER/w`, `userxattr`; binds
  every `rw`/`ro` grant strictly beneath `home` from `_HOME_REAL/<rel>`
  over the overlay (`MS_BIND | MS_REC`; a missing source or a link
  skipped); then detaches `_HOME_REAL` and `_HOME_UPPER` (`MNT_DETACH`)
  and removes both directories. With `--home-upper DIR` (`--isolate`
  only; `upper=` here) no `tmpfs` is made: `upperdir=DIR`,
  `workdir=DIR.work` (both must be directories and nameable, else
  `IsolationError`), and only `_HOME_REAL` is detached; such a home is not
  watched (`_watch_home(..., watch=False)`). `main()` and `run_sandbox` add `home` to
  the Landlock write grants (`_watch_home`) and set `_HOME_WATCH =
  HomeWatch(home, N)`: `_wait_signal(watched)` (every wait in `run`,
  `run_as_init` and `run_sandbox`) samples it and waits with
  `sigtimedwait(…, HOME_SAMPLE_SEC = 0.2)`; a sample with `f_bavail *
  f_frsize < HOME_FULL_MARGIN` (1 MiB) marks it full; `_home_full()`
  samples once more after the command and its descendants have ended and,
  when full, the shim exits through `_refused(HomeWatch.finding())` ("the
  command filled its home <home> (<N> MiB, its private overlay's
  limit)…"), so the caller raises `ConfinementRefused`. The AppArmor
  profile allows `mount fstype=overlay overlay -> /home/*/` and `mount
  fstype=tmpfs options=(rw, nosuid, nodev) tmpfs -> /tmp/.leerie-home/`.
  `overlay_grants(rw, view) -> list[str]` (`--sandbox`) — `view` first,
  then each other `rw` directory outside `/tmp` and `/dev`: an overlay on
  it, `lowerdir=<it>,upperdir=/tmp/.leerie-overlay/<n>/u,
  workdir=/tmp/.leerie-overlay/<n>/w,userxattr` (made 0700); a failed
  overlay is a failed step (exit 126, naming the path), never a fallback.
- `build_worker_view(worker_root: str) -> list[str]` (`--worker-root`,
  after `bind_grants`/`overlay_grants`) — DESIGN §6 *The orchestrator's
  root is leerie's; a repository's root is only a confined process's*.
  Makes `WORKER_VIEW = "/.leerie-worker-view"` (0755) in the new root and,
  for each name in the worker root's top level and `/`'s (but the view):
  `opt` (when the worker root's is a directory) → a directory holding each
  entry of both `/opt`s but those beneath `worker_root`, a `leerie-*`
  entry the container has from the container, any other from the worker
  root; `etc` (when the worker root's is a directory) → a directory
  holding each entry of the worker root's `/etc`, but each name in
  `CONTAINER_ETC_FILES` (`hosts`, `hostname`, `resolv.conf`) from the
  container's `/etc` when it has it; a name in `CONTAINER_ENTRIES` (`dev`, `proc`, `sys`, `run`, `tmp`,
  `home`, `work`, `inspect`, `leerie-state`, `leerie-host`) or absent from
  the worker root → the container's (when it has it); else the worker
  root's. Each entry by `_bind_entry(src, dst)`: a link copied as a link,
  a directory `rbind`-mounted, anything else bound as a file. Lists and
  stats only. Returns the view entries taken from the worker root (and the
  view's `/opt`), which `isolate` returns for the caller to add to `ro`. A
  failure is step `build the worker view`. `isolate` then adds `WORKER_VIEW
  + k` for each kept mount point to `keep`, and the view's own `/tmp`,
  `/dev/shm` and `/dev/pts` to the private mounts `readonly_mounts` skips.
- `readonly_mounts(keep: list[str], private=PRIVATE, roots=()) -> int` —
  every `/proc/self/mountinfo` entry not already `ro`, not in `keep` or
  beneath one, not exactly one of `roots` (`bind_grants`'s, and with a
  worker view `WORKER_VIEW + root` too), and not one of `private` (`/tmp`,
  `/dev/shm`, `/dev/pts`), remounted `MS_REMOUNT | MS_BIND | MS_RDONLY`
  with its locked flags (`nosuid`, `nodev`, `noexec`, `noatime`,
  `nodiratime`, `relatime`) kept; a refused remount is a failed step.
  A carried read-only grant beneath `/tmp` is remounted read-only too.
- `place(pairs: list[tuple[str, str]], view: str) -> None` (`--sandbox`,
  after `readonly_mounts`) — each `SRC` (read by the shim, still
  unconfined) written at `<REL>` beneath an `O_DIRECTORY` descriptor of
  the view by `_place_one(view_fd, src, rel)`: every directory of `REL`
  made with `mkdirat` when absent and opened `O_NOFOLLOW | O_DIRECTORY`
  from its parent's descriptor, the file created `O_CREAT | O_EXCL |
  O_NOFOLLOW`, mode `0444`. Refused (exit 126, step `place …`) when `REL`
  is absolute, empty or holds `.`, `..` or an empty component, or when
  placing fails for any reason but the three below. `PlacementTaken`
  (`_taken`, the taken descriptor, never a refusal) when `_place_one`
  fails `EEXIST`, `ENOTDIR` or `ELOOP` (`_TAKEN_ERRNOS`): the view already
  has a file there (a set is never placed over the tree's own file, the
  rule `_place_set` held), or a link or a non-directory is on its path
  (review round 21, isolation R6: a committed `tests -> <worker tree>`
  link sent the file onto disk in the worker's tree, because the
  placement followed it, with every mount still writable; review round
  39, isolation R1: reported as a refusal, the same link stopped the run
  with exit 78 on every `resume`).
  `tests/heldout_sandbox_emulator.py` refuses the same paths.
  `over` (`--replace` pairs) and `remove` (`--remove` paths), keyword
  arguments of `place`, after the pairs and validated the same way: an
  existing test's base form (DESIGN §8). `_place_one(…, over=True)`
  writes over a regular file at `REL` with `O_WRONLY | O_TRUNC |
  O_NOFOLLOW` (creating it as above when absent); `_place_one(view_fd,
  None, rel)` deletes the regular file at `REL` with `unlinkat`, and is a
  no-op when it or a directory on its way is absent (none is made).
  `_regular_at` reads `REL` with `fstatat(AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW)`: anything
  but a regular file there fails `EEXIST`, so a link, a directory or a
  device at `REL` is `PlacementTaken` too.
- `loopback_up() -> None` (both) — `SIOCGIFFLAGS` and `SIOCSIFFLAGS`
  (`IFF_UP`) on `lo`; a failure is step `bring up lo`.
- `join_session_keyring() -> None` — `keyctl(KEYCTL_JOIN_SESSION_KEYRING,
  NULL)`: an anonymous session keyring of its own.
- `install_seccomp() -> None` — after `PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS`, a BPF filter
  (`seccomp_program(arch)`, `SECCOMP_TABLES = {"x86_64": …, "aarch64":
  …}`, the arch from `os.uname().machine`): an `AUDIT_ARCH_*` other than
  the table's → `SECCOMP_RET_KILL_PROCESS`; on x86_64 a syscall number at
  or above `0x40000000` (x32) → `EPERM`; `unshare`, `setns`, `mount`,
  `umount2`, `pivot_root`, `open_tree`, `move_mount`, `fsopen`,
  `fsconfig`, `fsmount`, `fspick`, `mount_setattr`, `add_key`,
  `request_key`, `keyctl` → `EPERM`; `clone3` → `ENOSYS`; `clone` with
  `args[0] & CLONE_NEW_MASK` (`0x7E020000`) → `EPERM`. Numbers: x86_64
  272, 308, 165, 166, 155, 428–433, 442, 248–250, `clone` 56, `clone3`
  435; aarch64 97, 268, 40, 39, 41, 428–433, 442, 217–219, `clone` 220,
  `clone3` 435. Installed by every confined process, with or without
  isolation (it needs no namespace); an architecture with no table is a
  failed step (exit 126).
- `confine(rw, ro)` — unchanged, plus from `abi() >= 6` the ruleset's
  `scoped` field `LANDLOCK_SCOPE_ABSTRACT_UNIX_SOCKET |
  LANDLOCK_SCOPE_SIGNAL` (the attribute grows to `handled_access_fs`,
  `handled_access_net` = 0, `scoped`, with its size passed). With
  isolation the shim adds `/tmp`, `/dev/shm` and `/dev/pts` to `rw`; a
  grant of `/tmp` or `/dev/shm` itself names the private one.
- `run(cmd, relay=None, enter=None)` (`--isolate`, and no flag) — unchanged:
  subreaper, `/proc` walk, `end_descendants`; the child calls
  `_before_exec(enter)` just before `execvp`, as `run_as_init`'s does.
  `_before_exec`: `("view", WORKER_VIEW, changes)` →
  `enter_worker_view(view, changes)`: `os.chroot(view)`, `chdir` to the same
  working directory, `prctl(PR_CAP_AMBIENT, PR_CAP_AMBIENT_CLEAR_ALL)`,
  `apply_worker_env(os.environ, changes)`; `("cli", WORKER_VIEW,
  worker_root)` → `keep_chroot_across_exec()` (`capget`, `CAP_SYS_CHROOT`
  (18) added to the inheritable set, `capset`, `prctl(PR_CAP_AMBIENT,
  PR_CAP_AMBIENT_RAISE, 18)`) and `LEERIE_WORKER_VIEW` / `LEERIE_WORKER_ROOT`
  (`VIEW_ENV`, `WORKER_ROOT_ENV`) set in its environment. Either failing
  prints `leerie: cannot start the command in the repository's root, so it
  does not run: …` and `_exit(126)`. Runs after `confine` and the seccomp
  filter, so nothing from the worker root runs before the command is
  confined.
- `worker_env_changes(worker_root) -> (dict, list)` — reads
  `<root>/.leerie-worker-env` and `<root>/.leerie-base-env`
  (`_read_env_file`: `O_NOFOLLOW`, a regular file, at most 1 MiB, split on
  NUL into `k=v`; `{}` otherwise); returns the variables whose worker value
  differs from the base's, less `_ENV_KEPT_OUT` (`PATH`, `HOME`, `TMPDIR`,
  `PWD`, `OLDPWD`, `SHLVL`, `_`, `HOSTNAME`, `NO_PROXY`, `no_proxy`,
  `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY`), `PROXY_VARS` and names starting `LEERIE_`,
  `CLAUDE` or `ANTHROPIC_`; and the worker `PATH`'s entries the base `PATH`
  lacks, in order. `apply_worker_env(env, changes)`: each variable set when
  `env` lacks it or its value starts with `/opt/`; the `PATH` entries put
  first.
- `--sandbox` forks after the mounts: the child is PID 1 of the new PID
  namespace: `join_session_keyring`, every fd but 0–2, `report_fd` and
  the status pipe closed, `install_seccomp`, `confine`, then
  `run_as_init(cmd, report, report_fd, status_w)` — stop-signal handlers
  installed (an init receives only handled signals; the watched signals
  blocked since before the fork, so none is lost), fork + exec CMD (signal
  mask and `PYTHON_IGNORED_SIGNALS` restored; the report fd and the
  status pipe `O_CLOEXEC`); wait for CMD or a stop signal;
  `kill(-1, SIGTERM)`, `END_GRACE_SEC` (`STOP_GRACE_SEC` when stopped),
  `kill(-1, SIGKILL)`, reap until `ChildProcessError`; copy `report`
  (when it exists, at most `REPORT_MAX_BYTES = 64 << 20`) to `report_fd`
  from offset 0 and truncate it there; write `E<code>` or `S<signal>` to
  the status pipe; `_exit(0)`. The outer shim waits for it, forwards a
  stop signal to it (SIGTERM), reads the status and exits as CMD did
  (`_die_of` for a signal); no status (PID 1 was killed) → exit 1.
  `report_fd` is a regular file leerie opened, never a pipe: a runner
  report can exceed a pipe's buffer, and nothing reads it until the
  command exits.
- `isolation_error() -> str | None` — runs the shim itself, `--isolate
  --ro / -- true`, in a child process; None when it exits 0, else the last
  line of its stderr (the step and errno). Tests use it to skip on a host
  that cannot build one (the host's user-namespace restriction).
- `isolate(rw, ro, *, sandbox=False, view=None, place_pairs=(),
  sockets=())` — the steps above in order (`sockets`: the relays' unix
  sockets, each one's directory, when beneath `/tmp`, carried in
  read-only as a `--ro` grant beneath `/tmp` is), then `chdir` to the
  caller's cwd again (it was
  resolved before the binds and overlays, so it named the directory
  beneath them); returns `(n, view_ro)` — with `worker_root` (`isolate(…,
  worker_root=None)`), `build_worker_view`'s grants. `run_sandbox(cmd, rw,
  ro, view, place_pairs, report, report_fd, worker_root=None)` — `isolate`
  (with `worker_root`: `view_ro` added to `ro`, and PID 1's command entered
  with `("view", …)`), the status pipe, the fork of PID 1 with the
  watched signals still blocked (a stop forwarded before PID 1 has its
  handlers waits, pending), and the outer wait. `_parse(argv)` — the
  options, or a usage error (exit 2): `--isolate` and `--sandbox`
  exclusive, `--sandbox` needs `--view`, `--view`/`--place`/`--replace`/
  `--remove`/`--report` need `--sandbox`, `--report` and `--report-fd` together, `--egress
  SOCK` (absolute) and `--forward PORT=SOCK` (1–65535, absolute) need
  `--isolate`, `--worker-root DIR` (absolute, not `/`; normalized) needs
  `--isolate` or `--sandbox`, `--cli` needs `--isolate` and
  `--worker-root`.
- **The relay** (`--isolate` with `--egress` or `--forward`): after
  `isolate` and `join_session_keyring`, one `relay_listener(port) ->
  socket` per target on the namespace's `127.0.0.1:<port>`
  (`SO_REUSEADDR`, backlog 128; a refused bind is step `relay listen
  127.0.0.1:<port>`) — each `--forward` port first, then `--egress` on
  port 0 (the kernel's pick). With `--egress`, `os.environ` gains
  `proxy_env(port)`: `HTTPS_PROXY`, `HTTP_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY`,
  `https_proxy`, `http_proxy`, `all_proxy` = `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`
  (`PROXY_VARS`), `NO_PROXY` = `no_proxy` = `localhost,127.0.0.1,::1`
  (`NO_PROXY_VALUE`), `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1`. Then `confine`, then
  `start_relays(relays)`: one `fork` (so the relay is confined like the
  command, a child of the shim, ended by `end_descendants` with it);
  the child (`serve_relays`) closes stdin and runs a thread per listener
  accepting connections, a thread per connection (`_relay_one`) that
  connects an `AF_UNIX` stream to the target and pumps both ways
  (`_pump`, 64 KiB reads, `shutdown(SHUT_WR)` on EOF); the shim closes
  the listeners and runs the command (`run`).

**The orchestrator side.**

- `WorkerGrants.egress: bool = False` (the fourth field): `True` from
  `_worker_grants` (every worker) and from `_measurement_grants` for
  every kind but `MEASURE_KIND` (`INSTALL_KIND`, `SETUP_HOOK_KIND`,
  `TOOLCHAIN_KIND`); `_heldout_grants` keeps
  `_measurement_grants(st, tree)`'s `False`.
- `ISOLATE_ENV = "LEERIE_ISOLATED"`. `_require_heldout_sandbox(run_dir)` sets
  `os.environ[ISOLATE_ENV] = "1"` after its checks pass, so every later
  confined spawn in this process and its children (`worker-guard.py`)
  isolates; `_isolated() -> bool` reads it.
- `HeldOutSandbox(view: str, place: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = (),
  report: str | None = None, replace: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = (),
  remove: tuple[str, ...] = ())` (NamedTuple; `place` and `replace` pairs
  are `(absolute source, path relative to view)`; `replace` and `remove`
  carry an existing test's base form, DESIGN §8).
- `_confined_argv(grants, cmd, *, sandbox: HeldOutSandbox | None = None,
  report_fd: int | None = None) -> list[str]` — `[sys.executable, "-I",
  "-S", LANDLOCK_SCRIPT]`, then `--sandbox --view <view>`, one `--place
  SRC=REL` per pair, one `--replace SRC=REL` per `replace` pair, one
  `--remove REL` per `remove` path, and `--report <report> --report-fd <report_fd>` (both
  or neither) when `sandbox` is given, else `--isolate` when `_isolated()`
  — followed, when `grants.egress`, by `--egress
  <_egress_server().socket_path>` and, while `_STRICT_PROXY` is live,
  `--forward <its port>=<_egress_server().forward(its port)>`; with
  `worker_root` True and `_worker_root()` a path, `--worker-root <path>`
  (after the sandbox options, or after the isolation ones when isolated;
  plus `--cli` when `cli`); `_home_argv(grants)` (sandboxed or isolated);
  then `--rw`/`--ro` from `grants` and `-- cmd`.
  `_invoke` passes `cli=True` (it starts a worker's CLI), and so does
  `scripts/worker-guard.py`'s `guard_confine`; `_require_heldout_sandbox`'s
  probe passes `worker_root=False` (it checks the shim's own machinery, in
  leerie's root). A `sandbox` with
  `_isolated()` False is still emitted: a held-out file never runs outside
  a sandbox, and the shim refuses (126) where it cannot build one.
- `_run_streaming(cmd, *, grants, sandbox: HeldOutSandbox | None = None,
  …)` — with `sandbox`, opens an unlinked report file in `<run>/tmp/`
  (`tempfile.TemporaryFile`), passes it in `pass_fds`, spawns
  `_confined_argv(grants, cmd, sandbox=…, report_fd=…)`, and after the
  command exits copies the file's content to `sandbox.report`'s path
  outside (the caller's report path, which no other process wrote; an
  empty file writes nothing). The evaluation's grant is
  `_heldout_grants(st, tree)`: `_measurement_grants(st, tree)` unchanged
  (the sandbox overlays every `rw` path, the run's stores among them, so
  the evaluation's writes there vanish with it). Callers passing it, each through `_run_acceptance_file(…,
  place=)`, the parse probe, `_capture_failing_test_ids(…, place=)` (the
  falsifier's confirm runs) or `_probe_case_facts_placed`:
  - `_run_acceptance_file(st, caps, tree, rel, log_path, label, *,
    validating=False, failure_mode="assertion", observed=None,
    cases_out=None, place: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = (),
    suite: dict | None = None)` —
    `HeldOutSandbox(view=tree, place=place, report=<its report path when
    the runner has one>)`; `_acceptance_cmd(st, [rel], tree, placed=
    {rel: src for src, rel in place})`, or with `suite` (the run's browser
    channel) `_browser_suite_cmd(suite, [rel])` and `_browser_suite_env(suite)`
    laid over the run's environment after the path overlay (DESIGN §8 *A
    probe is re-run through the channel that confirmed it*). Its
    `env_extra` is gone: the database is the wrapper's (*The per-command
    database*).
  - `_acceptance_run_placed(st, caps, wt, sets, label, *, confirm=True)`
    — per set, the `place` pairs of every file whose path `wt` does not
    already have by the shim's rule (`_lexists_beneath`: a file there, or a
    link or a non-directory on its way: `path_in_use`, the set
    unmeasured), handed to every run, confirm rerun and
    discovery rerun (`_acceptance_discover(…, place, note, …, suite=)`, the
    positional slot `env_extra` had); nothing is copied, no section held
    across the loop. Each set's channel is `_acceptance_set_suite(st, set)
    -> dict | None | False`: None (the test command) unless the set has
    `via_browser_suite`, then `_browser_suite(st)`, or False when that is
    None — the set is then `{passed: False, unmeasured: True,
    failing_files: [], unmeasured_reason: "no_browser_suite"}` and nothing
    runs; the channel is passed as `suite=` to every run, confirm rerun and
    discovery rerun of the set. `_evaluate_acceptance_sets_inner`, when
    `_browser_suite(st)` is set and some set's channel is it, runs
    `_ci_prepare(wt, [_browser_suite_rec(suite)], st, caps,
    "acceptance-<label>")` in the evaluation worktree after its
    dependency install. The writer's validation runs its own files where the
    writer wrote them (no `place`), in the same sandbox.
  - `_acceptance_parse_probe` — the probe's source is written to a
    `tempfile.mkstemp` file of leerie's own (removed after) and placed at
    the probe's path (`None` with "the parse check's name is taken" when
    `_lexists_beneath` finds that path taken); its marker is the sandbox's `report`, so
    "ran"/"ok" come back through the descriptor.
  - `_acceptance_case_failures(st, caps, wt, set_, log_path, label)` —
    the set's files as `place`; `_acceptance_audit_in` checks no set path
    is taken in `wt` (else `skipped`), captures the failing cases that way,
    and only then `_place_set`s the set on disk for the `set_auditor`
    worker, which reads it (a held-out-side worker in a tree no worker
    commits from), removing it after.
  - `_acceptance_cmd(st, files, tree=None, placed: Mapping[str, str] |
    None = None)` reads a placed file's Go test names from its source, and
    `_vitest_exact_selection(cmd, files, tree, extra=())` /
    `_vitest_filter_colliders(tree, files, extra=())` count the placed
    paths as the tree's files.
- `_require_heldout_sandbox(run_dir: Path) -> None` — in
  `_require_confinement`, after `_require_landlock` and `_require_state_root_apart`, on every
  runtime: makes
  `<run-dir>/sandbox-probe/` (`_SANDBOX_PROBE_DIRNAME`) with `view/`, a set
  file outside it and `ro.txt`, and a marker file in the container's
  `/tmp` and `/dev/shm`; runs `_confined_argv(WorkerGrants(rw=("/dev/null",
  view), ro=("/",)), [python, -I, -S, SANDBOX_PROBE_SCRIPT, ro.txt,
  probe/placed.txt, <markers>], sandbox=HeldOutSandbox(view, place=((set,
  "probe/placed.txt"),), report=<view>/report.json), report_fd=<an unlinked
  temp file in the probe directory>)` (`subprocess.run`, `pass_fds`, 60 s).
  `scripts/sandbox_probe.py` (stdlib) writes `report.json` in its cwd:
  `ipc_ns` (`/proc/self/ns/ipc`), `interfaces` (`socket.if_nameindex()`),
  `tmp_private` and `shm_private` (the markers absent), `erofs`
  (`os.utime(ro.txt)` → True on EROFS, else the errno name), `add_key`
  (True on EPERM), `placed` (the placed file read in the view), and, when
  `_confined_home()` is non-empty (the grant then names it and the
  toolchain layer, and the probe gets a fifth argument
  `.leerie-probe-<nonce>`), `home_written` (that file written in `$HOME`:
  True, else the error); a `home_written` other than True, or the file
  found in the real home afterwards (then removed), is a failed property
  ("its home is not writable", "a write to its home reached the real
  home"). The `_SANDBOX_FIXES` entry for `home .* is mounted beneath it` or
  `overlay /home…: EINVAL` comes before the generic overlay one and names a
  mount beneath the home. A non-zero
  exit or no report → `die()` with the shim's stderr and
  `_sandbox_fix(stderr) -> str`, the first of `_SANDBOX_FIXES` (regexes
  over the shim's own step and errno names, most specific first) that
  matches: no seccomp table → the architecture; `unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER):
  EPERM` → `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined`; `unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER):
  EINVAL|ENOSPC|EUSERS|ENOSYS` → no unprivileged user namespaces; `write
  setgroups: EACCES` → the host's restriction, the process not under the
  profile; `overlay …: EINVAL` → the state root's filesystem; any other
  `: EACCES` → the `leerie-container` profile, with its two load
  commands. `LEERIE_RUNTIME=fly` adds that Fly runs do not start. A report
  missing a property → `die()` naming each (`_sandbox_probe_failures(got,
  placed_on_disk)`, which also fails a placed file found on disk). The
  probe directory and the markers are removed either way; then
  `_require_egress_relay()`; on success `os.environ[ISOLATE_ENV] = "1"`.
  `_SANDBOX_FIXES` maps `unshare(mount/IPC/net…): EPERM|EINVAL|ENOSPC`,
  `bring up lo` and `relay listen` to the runtime's network-namespace
  fix (ahead of the overlay and `EACCES` entries).
- `_require_egress_relay() -> None` — binds a listener on the
  orchestrator's `127.0.0.1:0`, then runs `[python, -I, -S,
  LANDLOCK_SCRIPT, --isolate, --egress, <socket>, --rw, /dev/null, --ro,
  /, --, python, -I, -S, -c, _EGRESS_RELAY_PROBE, <port>]` (60 s): the
  probe sends `CONNECT 127.0.0.1:<port>` to `HTTPS_PROXY` and connects to
  `127.0.0.1:<port>` directly, printing `{"proxy": <status line>,
  "outer_loopback": <errno name or "reached">}`. `die()`s (naming each
  failure and `_sandbox_fix(stderr)`) unless the exit is 0, the status
  line starts `HTTP/1.1 403` and the direct connection is
  `ECONNREFUSED`. That refusal is pre-marked as logged
  (`_EgressProxy._refused`). `tests/conftest.py`'s autouse
  `_no_real_heldout_sandbox` stubs it (opt-out
  `@pytest.mark.real_heldout_sandbox`, registered in `pytest.ini`) and
  clears `ISOLATE_ENV` before and after every test; in every Python child
  a test starts too, by putting `tests/no_real_heldout_sandbox_site/`
  (whose `sitecustomize` stubs it in each `orchestrator/leerie.py` the
  child executes) first on `PYTHONPATH` (pinned by
  `tests/test_no_real_heldout_sandbox_site.py`).
- **The execution lock** (replaces the run's `/tmp` lock): `_TmpLock` →
  `_ExecLock`, `_tmp_lock()` → `_exec_lock()`, `_TMP_LOCKS` →
  `_EXEC_LOCKS`, `_TMP_EXCLUSIVE` → `_EXEC_EXCLUSIVE`; the same semantics
  (`readers`, `writer`, `writers_waiting`, waiter futures; `shared()` —
  passes through when `_EXEC_EXCLUSIVE` is set, else waits while a writer
  holds or waits; `exclusive()` — yields False when nested, else waits for
  no writer and no reader, sets `_EXEC_EXCLUSIVE` in the holder's context,
  yields True; one per running loop, a weak-key dictionary). The lock is
  the run's alone: no level of it spans runs (DESIGN §6 *There is no host
  level*). `shared(worker=True)` also counts the holder in `workers`.
  `exclusive()` that must wait logs before waiting — `execution lock:
  held-out evaluation waits for <readers> shared holder(s) of this run
  (<workers> worker(s))<, behind another evaluation>` — and, once it holds
  the lock, `execution lock: held-out evaluation waited <s>s`; an
  `exclusive()` that need not wait logs nothing. Shared
  holders: `_run_streaming` (its whole spawn), the callers of
  `_ts_script_run` (synchronous: it checks `_exec_lock_held()` and
  `die()`s without it), the `mise ls` spawn, and `_invoke` (so
  `_invoke_admitted`, which delegates to it) from before the worker's
  spawn until its process has exited and been reaped (an
  `AsyncExitStack` closed in its `finally`, and on every path that fails
  before it). A shared holder's own nested `shared()` passes through
  (`_EXEC_SHARED`, set in the holder's context), so a command run under a
  hold never waits behind an evaluation that waits for that hold;
  `exclusive()` called where `_EXEC_SHARED` is set `die()`s (`invariant:
  a held-out evaluation started while its own caller holds the execution
  lock shared`). A shared hold is taken after every semaphore its holder
  takes (`_blt_slot`, memory admission, `_confirm_hold`), and a host
  build slot after the hold (`_build_class_slot`, `_held_out_section`;
  DESIGN §6 *The run's execution lock, then a host build slot,
  everywhere*). Inside an exclusive hold the three gates pass through
  instead of waiting (`_EXEC_EXCLUSIVE` set: the holder is alone in the
  run, and holds its own slot), and nothing reachable inside
  `_held_out_section` takes a raw one (`_blt_semaphore`,
  `_acquire_build_slot`, `_confirm_lock`, a `Semaphore`) or spawns a worker
  (`tests/test_exec_lock.py`, by rule over the module, stopping at the
  three pass-through gates, whose pass-through it executes); and nothing
  reachable inside a `_build_class_slot` hold takes a slot, a section, a
  semaphore or a worker (the same test), so the lock and the slots cannot
  deadlock. `_held_out_section(st)` — `exclusive()`, then, for the
  outermost section only, `_host_build_slot(st, label="held-out
  evaluation", take=<outermost>)` inside it, around one logical
  evaluation (held by `_run_acceptance_file`,
  `_acceptance_parse_probe`, `_capture_failing_test_ids` (with `place`) and
  `_probe_case_facts_placed` around their spawn, and by `_falsifier_gates`
  from the probe's placement check through its facts read, so the first
  run, the B\* reruns and the facts read are one hold — those three
  callees' own sections nest; `_falsify_items` has no confirm lock of its
  own: its samples queue on the execution lock; the section replaces
  `_blt_semaphore` for a held-out run; `_acceptance_run_placed` no longer holds it
  across its loop, since nothing is placed on disk), no `/tmp` inventory;
  `_exec_lock().shared()` called for a worker while `_EXEC_EXCLUSIVE` is
  set `die()`s (`invariant: a worker spawned inside a held-out
  evaluation`); a command passes through as before.
- **The gates that pass through inside an evaluation**:
  `_blt_slot(caps)` — async context manager: the BLT semaphore
  (`_blt_semaphore(caps)`), or nothing when `_EXEC_EXCLUSIVE` is set;
  `_build_class_slot(st, *, label)` — yields None without taking a host
  slot when `_EXEC_EXCLUSIVE` is set (the evaluation took one once it held
  its `exclusive()`); otherwise `_exec_lock().shared()` and then
  `_host_build_slot(st, label=label)` (`_acquire_build_slot`, its fd
  closed on exit; `take=False` yields None and takes nothing).
  `_capture_failing_test_ids` takes `_held_out_section` for a held-out
  file and `_build_class_slot` for any other run, never both;
  `_confirm_hold()` — async context
  manager: `_confirm_lock()`, or nothing when `_EXEC_EXCLUSIVE` is set.
  Every former `async with _blt_semaphore(caps)` and `async with
  _confirm_lock()` uses them (`_measure_axes`,
  `_capture_failing_test_ids`, `_confirm_new_failures`,
  `_confirm_still_failing`, `_intermittent_discovery`,
  `_acceptance_discover`, `_settle_by_execution`).
- **Deleted**: `WorkerGrants.shared_tmp`, `_confined_argv(…,
  shared_tmp=)`, `_argv_outside_grant(…, shared_tmp=)`,
  `_measurement_grants`' `shared_tmp`, `_TMP_GRANTED_TREES`,
  `_is_worker_tree`, `_declare_worker_tree`, `_WORKER_TREES`,
  `_tmp_inventory`, `_remove_created`, `PRIVATE_TMP_ENV` and the
  Dockerfile's `ENV LEERIE_PRIVATE_TMP=1`, `_place_set` on the evaluation
  path (the self-check keeps it for shown sets in its own copy), and the
  unconfined cluster: `_start_test_db_cluster`, `_pg_server_bin`'s
  unconfined use, `_test_db_session`'s cluster, `_create_test_db`'s
  unconfined `prisma db push` and `_drop_test_db`. `_reads_outside(root,
  tmp=False)` keeps leaving the container's `/tmp` out of every grant
  (the shim grants the private one), and `/dev` (round 33). `_WORKER_DEVICES` keeps `/dev/shm`
  (the shim maps it to the private one).
- `_confined_writes_notice` names `/tmp` as the worker's private scratch,
  gone when its session ends, and no longer says `/tmp` is not writable —
  when `_isolated()`; an unisolated worker (a test, a host harness) has no
  `/tmp`, and the notice says so as before.
- `_run_contained(argv, *, grants, sandbox=None, …)` passes `sandbox` to
  `_run_streaming`.

**The egress proxy** (DESIGN §6 *A confined process has its own
network*):

- `_EgressProxy(directory: Path)` — `socket_path` = `directory /
  EGRESS_SOCKET_NAME` (`"egress.sock"`); `start()` runs
  `asyncio.start_unix_server(_handle, path=…, limit=_EGRESS_HEAD_MAX
  (64 KiB), backlog=256)` on a new event loop in a daemon thread
  (`leerie-egress`), waiting `_EGRESS_START_TIMEOUT_SEC` (30) for it and
  raising `OSError` on failure. `_handle` reads the request head
  (`readuntil(b"\r\n\r\n")`): `CONNECT host:port` (`_egress_target`, an
  IPv6 literal bracketed) → `_connect`, then `HTTP/1.1 200 Connection
  Established` and a two-way splice; an absolute `http://` request →
  `_connect(host, port or 80)`, the request line rewritten to origin form,
  `Proxy-Connection`, `Proxy-Authorization`, `Connection` and
  `Keep-Alive` dropped (`_EGRESS_HOP_HEADERS`), `Connection: close`
  added, then the splice; anything else → 400. `_connect(host, port)` —
  `loop.getaddrinfo`; each address checked by `_egress_refusal(addr,
  _own_addresses())` (loopback, link-local, unspecified, multicast — an
  IPv4-mapped IPv6 address unwrapped — or the container's own); none left
  → 403 `refused host:port (<why>)`, logged once per destination
  (`egress: refused …`); else connect (`_EGRESS_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SEC`, 30)
  to each allowed address in turn → 502 when none answers. When
  `_egress_proxy(host)` (DESIGN §13, the container's proxy variables)
  names an upstream proxy, `_via_upstream` tunnels through it with
  `CONNECT` (and `Proxy-Authorization: Basic`) — a plain request too,
  over a `CONNECT` to its port — and a name only that proxy can resolve
  is allowed. Counters `connections`, `refusals`. No
  payload is logged. `forward(port) -> str` — a further unix server,
  `fwd-<port>.sock` in the same directory, piping each connection to the
  orchestrator's `127.0.0.1:<port>`; made once per port.
- `_own_addresses() -> set[str]` — the `/32 host LOCAL` entries of
  `/proc/net/fib_trie` and every address in `/proc/net/if_inet6`.
- `_egress_server() -> _EgressProxy` — this process's proxy (module
  `_EGRESS`, under `_EGRESS_LOCK`), started on first use in
  `_new_private_tmp("egress-")`; a forked child starts its own; a start
  failure `die()`s.
- `_new_private_tmp(prefix: str) -> Path` — `_own_private_dir(PRIVATE_TMP_ROOT)`
  then `tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=prefix, dir=PRIVATE_TMP_ROOT)`
  (`/tmp/l/<prefix><random>/`, 0700, made by this call so no existing path
  is ever reused), registered in `_PRIVATE_TMPS` and removed at exit like
  `_private_tmp`'s. Every proxy instance has its own directory, so none
  binds another's `egress.sock`.
- What honours the proxy variables in the image (measured 2026-11-01,
  rootless and rootful): the table below. A tool that does not loses
  direct egress.

| tool | through the proxy |
|---|---|
| `claude -p` (CLI 2.1.311): the API, `WebFetch`, its Bash tool's commands | yes (a haiku worker: 4 turns, `is_error: false`, 15 proxy connections) |
| `curl`, `git` over https, `pip`, Python's `urllib` | yes |
| `npm`, `pnpm` (its own self-download and `dlx` included), `yarn`, `corepack` | yes |
| Node's `fetch` and `https` | yes, with `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1` (without it: `EAI_AGAIN`) |
| `mise` (`ls-remote`, a tool's download), `uv` through `mise exec` | yes |
| `git` over ssh, any raw socket or UDP | no: no route, no resolver |
| `wget`, `cargo`, `go`, `bun`, `deno` | not in leerie's image; unmeasured |

**The per-command database** (`scripts/sandbox-db.sh`): `sandbox-db.sh
<pkg-dir> <db-name> -- CMD...`, run as the confined command itself (inside
its isolation or sandbox, under its grant). It refuses (exit 125) a name
not matching `^leerie_[0-9a-f]{16}_test$`; `initdb -D /tmp/leerie-pg/data
--auth-local=trust --auth-host=trust -U <user>` from the newest complete
`/usr/lib/postgresql/<major>/bin` (else `PATH`); `pg_ctl start` with `-c
listen_addresses=127.0.0.1 -c port=5432 -c
unix_socket_directories=/tmp/leerie-pg -c fsync=off` (the loopback of the
command's own network namespace); `createdb`; `DATABASE_URL` =
`DIRECT_URL` = `postgresql://<user>@127.0.0.1:5432/<db-name>`;
`<pkg-dir>/node_modules/.bin/prisma db push --accept-data-loss` (in
`<pkg-dir>`; the push the orchestrator used to make, generate included)
with `PRISMA_USER_CONSENT_FOR_DANGEROUS_AI_ACTION` on that one command;
then `exec CMD` with both URLs exported. Without server binaries, as
root, or when any step fails (the directory, `initdb`, the start,
`createdb`, no installed `prisma`, the push), it execs CMD unchanged,
saying so in one line. Everything it prints goes to stderr: CMD's stdout
is CMD's own (a worker's is its event stream). The shim ends the server
with the command. Leerie composes the prefix with `_test_db_argv(st, tree,
key) -> list[str]` — `["bash", SANDBOX_DB_SCRIPT, <tree>/<project dir>,
leerie_<sha256(f"{run_id}:{key}:{tree}")[:16]>_test, "--"]`, `[]` outside
a Prisma repo whose datasource is PostgreSQL or when the URL is refused
(logged) — after checking the URL the script will compose
(`_test_db_url(name)`; `_test_db_url_refusal(url, direct_url)`: postgres
scheme, host and port exactly `TEST_DB_HOST, TEST_DB_PORT = "127.0.0.1",
5432` and no query, parameters or fragment, the name rule
(`_TEST_DB_NAME_RE`), DIRECT_URL == DATABASE_URL). Callers put it in front
of the command instead of entering `_test_db_session`: every held-out run
(`_run_acceptance_file`, key `<label>:<rel>`), CI parity's checks that
`require` a database (`_ci_run`, key `ci-<label>`), the falsifier's
confirm runs (`_capture_failing_test_ids(…, db=True)`, which replaces its
`env_extra`); a worker that needs one for its session — the writer, the
surrogate fixer, each falsifier sample, the re-drive implementer when it
has shown sets or shown probes (`_redrive_drive(…, db=)`) — is spawned through
`claude_p(…, db=True)`, which puts the prefix (keyed by the worker's sid)
in front of the `claude` argv, so its `DATABASE_URL` names its own
cluster, and the re-drive's self-check, which runs inside that worker,
uses it through its environment (`_selfcheck_prepare(st, caps, staging,
shown, label)`, `db_url` gone, `config.json`'s `env` empty).

A database that is promised is required. `_test_db_argv(st, tree, key, *,
require: bool = False)` with `require` appends `["bash",
REQUIRE_TEST_DB_SCRIPT, _test_db_url(name), "--"]` after the wrapper
(`scripts/require-test-db.sh <url> -- CMD`), which exits
`TEST_DB_ABSENT_EXIT` (3) with one stderr line unless `DATABASE_URL` is
exactly that URL, and otherwise `exec`s the command. `async _test_db_present(st, tree, key, *, log_path)
-> bool` runs `_test_db_argv(…, require=True) + ["true"]` once in `tree`
through `_run_streaming` (`_measurement_grants(st, tree)`, 300 s): True
only on exit 0; False outside a Prisma/PostgreSQL repo, on any other
exit, a timeout or a spawn failure (logged). `_write_acceptance_set`
sets `has_db = await _test_db_present(st, wt, f"{name}-db-check", …)`
after the writer's install, adds `_prisma_real_db_section` only when it
is True, and spawns the writer with `claude_p(…, db=has_db,
db_required=has_db)`; `claude_p(…, db_required=True)` composes its prefix
with `require=True`, so a writer whose own database did not come up
exits 3 before `claude` starts instead of running on a prompt that names
a database it lacks. The set's validation runs keep `require=False`.

**The launcher and the runtime** (`leerie`, `scripts/runtime-install.sh`,
`scripts/apparmor/leerie-container`):

- `SECOPT=(--security-opt seccomp=unconfined)` on every local `nerdctl
  run` (rootless, rootful, Colima), replacing `ROOTLESS_SECOPT`.
- `APPARMOR_OPT=(--security-opt apparmor=leerie-container)` when the
  runtime's kernel lists `apparmor` in `/sys/kernel/security/lsm`
  (`_RUNTIME_LSM_FILE`; on macOS, read through `colima ssh`;
  `runtime_has_apparmor`: the file read into a variable, then `case
  ",$lsm," in *,apparmor,*`); the profile must then be loaded —
  `runtime_apparmor_current` reads the names under
  `/sys/kernel/security/apparmor/policy/profiles/*/name`
  (`_RUNTIME_AA_PROFILES_DIR`; readable without root; `…/apparmor/profiles`
  is not) into a variable, matches a whole line with `case`, and compares
  the installed file `$LEERIE_APPARMOR_DEST`
  (`/etc/apparmor.d/leerie-container`) with the repo's by value. Neither
  probe is a pipeline (DESIGN §6 *The launcher's detection gives the
  kernel's answer*); the three path variables are set when the file is
  sourced so a test can point the real probes at a fixture
  (`tests/test_runtime_probes_pipefail.py`, which also rejects a pipe into
  an early-exit consumer in every shell file run under `pipefail`). Missing or
  stale: with a terminal and without `--no-runtime-install`, run
  `runtime_install_apparmor`; else exit 1 printing
  `runtime_apparmor_hint`'s two commands. The block is guarded by
  `declare -F runtime_has_apparmor` (an install without
  `scripts/runtime-install.sh` passes no profile and fails at preflight).
- `runtime_install_apparmor` (`scripts/runtime-install.sh`) — Linux: `sudo
  install -m 0644 "$LEERIE_REPO/scripts/apparmor/leerie-container"
  /etc/apparmor.d/leerie-container && sudo apparmor_parser -r -W
  /etc/apparmor.d/leerie-container`; Colima: the same through `colima ssh
  -- sudo tee /etc/apparmor.d/leerie-container` (the file on stdin) and
  `colima ssh -- sudo apparmor_parser -r -W …`; run by the launcher
  whenever the profile is missing or stale (scripts/runtime-install.sh:
  `runtime_has_apparmor`,
  `runtime_apparmor_current <src>`, `runtime_apparmor_hint <src>`,
  `runtime_install_apparmor <src>`; the first two read the containers'
  kernel through `_runtime_on_kernel`, and the last two branch on
  `uname -s`).
- `scripts/apparmor/leerie-container` — `abi <abi/4.0>`, profile
  `leerie-container flags=(attach_disconnected,mediate_deleted)`:
  `nerdctl-default`'s rules (network, capability, file, umount, the signal
  and ptrace peers renamed to itself, every `/proc` and `/sys` deny) plus
  `userns,`, `mqueue,`, `io_uring,`, `pivot_root,`, `remount /,`,
  `remount /**,`, `mount options=(rw, rprivate) -> /,`, `mount
  fstype=tmpfs options=(rw, nosuid, nodev) tmpfs -> /tmp/,` and `->
  /dev/shm/,`, `mount fstype=tmpfs options=(rw, nosuid, nodev, noexec)
  tmpfs -> /dev/,` (`private_dev`; its nodes are bound by the bind rule
  below), `mount fstype=devpts options=(rw, nosuid, noexec) devpts
  -> /dev/pts/,`, `mount options=(rw, bind) /dev/pts/ptmx -> /dev/ptmx,`
  (0.43.0's shim; this one makes no such mount),
  `mount fstype=overlay overlay -> /leerie-state/**,`, `mount options=(rw,
  bind) -> /**,` and `mount options=(rw, rbind) -> /**,` (the staged root
  under `/tmp`, the carried grants, `bind_grants`'s binds and `_shield`'s). The
  profile keeps every allow rule of a released profile (DESIGN §6 *The
  profile only grows*): `tests/test_launcher_secopt.py`'s
  `RELEASED_0_43_0_RULES` lists 0.43.0's allow rules verbatim, and
  `test_profile_keeps_every_rule_a_released_shim_needs` asserts each is a
  line of the profile. A release that adds a rule extends the list; none
  removes from it but a change carrying its own migration.
- `container-entry.sh` and the image: no change but the removed `ENV`.
- Tests: `tests/test_landlock_isolation.py` (every channel of the
  measured design's §1.2 closed, in a real sandbox; skipped where
  `isolation_error()` is not None), `tests/test_heldout_sandbox_preflight.py`
  (the die messages from the shim's measured failure lines, `_sandbox_fix`,
  the argv, the order of the confinement check every entry runs
  (`_require_confinement`), and the real gate where it can run),
  `tests/test_seccomp_filter.py` (both tables executed by a BPF
  interpreter, the real filter on the host, Node's worker threads under
  it), and `tests/test_launcher_secopt.py` (replacing
  `tests/test_rootless_seccomp.py`: the launcher's block executed with the
  runtime stubbed, the runtime-install helpers, the profile compiled with
  `apparmor_parser -Q` and its rules); `tests/test_exec_lock.py` (the execution lock: evaluations,
  measurements and real `_invoke` workers ordered, the worker guard, two
  runs' locks independent, the logged wait, and deadlock-freedom by rule over the
  module), `tests/test_heldout_sandbox_callers.py` (every held-out runner
  hands `_run_streaming` a sandbox in a section, the set never on disk,
  the report back through the descriptor; the per-command database: the
  URL refusal, `_test_db_argv`, the held-out, CI, worker and falsifier
  wrappers, no server or `prisma` run by leerie, the push confined),
  `tests/test_heldout_isolation.py` (review round 20's H1 and H2 proofs, F1
  and a fixed `/tmp/<name>` per command, each asserted closed in a real
  sandbox; skipped where the shim lacks `isolation_error()` or it is not
  None), `tests/test_confined_inputs.py` (an AST script without the lock
  stops the run; every caller holds it, by rule).

---

## 5. Deterministic enforcement points

All in `leerie.py`, in execution order. This is the concrete catalogue behind
`DESIGN.md` §12 ("prompts advisory, code enforces").

### Preflight (before any LLM work)
| Check | Catches |
|-------|---------|
| `resolve_source_of_truth()` at startup | invalid value in `leerie.toml`, `LEERIE_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH`, or `--source-of-truth` — caught before any worker spawns, not mid-planner |
| `resolve_runtime()` at startup | invalid value in `LEERIE_RUNTIME` or `--runtime` — caught before any worker spawns |
| `resolve_models()` at startup | invalid model alias in `leerie.toml`, any `LEERIE_MODEL[_*]` env var, or any `--model[-*]` CLI flag — caught before any worker spawns |
| `git user.email` / `user.name` set | commits would fail silently without identity |
| working tree clean | dirty tree → ambiguous diffs, corrupt merge history |
| `claude --version` ≥ `MIN_CLAUDE_CLI` (currently `(2, 1, 22)`) | CLI too old for `--json-schema` (introduced for `claude -p` in v2.1.22) — replaces the cryptic "unknown option" message a stale CLI used to produce |
| `claude --version` ≥ `MIN_CLAUDE_CLI_STRICT_OUTPUT` (currently `(2, 1, 289)`), only when `--dangerously-force-strict-output` is on | a CLI on which strict decoding turns leaked tool-call markup into a schema-valid payload with its fields emptied (DESIGN §7) |
| `gh auth status` + `origin` remote (launcher bash, before container) | finalize would fail at push/PR after the full run already ran. Short-circuited when `--no-push` is passed (env / TOML mirrors). |
| `_require_landlock()` (in `_require_confinement`, on every invocation that runs workers or commands — fresh, `resume`, `--phase`) | a kernel that cannot confine a worker (Landlock ABI below `MIN_ABI`) |
| `_require_state_root_apart()` (in `_require_confinement`, after `_require_landlock`) | a state root reachable under a second name through the checkout's mount, or holding the checkout (DESIGN §6 *No host path comes from a repository*) |
| `_require_heldout_sandbox()` (in `_require_confinement`, after `_require_state_root_apart`) | a runtime that cannot build the held-out sandbox or the isolation every confined process gets — seccomp refusing a user namespace, the `leerie-container` AppArmor profile not applied, the host's user-namespace restriction, no seccomp table for the architecture, Fly's guest kernel — named in the `die()` (§ *Isolation and the held-out sandbox (I3)*) |
| live `claude -p` smoke test | auth failure or network problem |
| live `claude -p` smoke test — client-side context refusal | `ContextOverflow` -> resumable `EXIT_LOCKED` pause naming the remedy, not a bare `Prompt is too long` |

Run-id collisions are detected at two natural collision points:

| Check | Where | Catches |
|-------|-------|---------|
| `State.__init__` refuses if the run dir is locked by another process | container start | Another orchestrator already owns this `<state-root>/runs/<run-id>/` |
| `setup-run.sh` preserves an existing `leerie/runs/<run-id>` branch instead of creating it | wave-execute phase | A pre-existing branch with the same name (treated as a resume; the run picks up wherever the branch was left) |

The run-id is the container/machine ID (DESIGN §6), known at container creation time. No temporary directory or rename is needed.

`--skip-smoke` bypasses only the live smoke test (used by the test harness); the CLI version check and the `gh` check still run because they are local and read-only, and skipping them would defer a confusing failure to mid-run.

### Phase 1 checks — `phase_classify`
| Check | Catches |
|-------|---------|
| classifier-returned categories filtered against the 9-name whitelist `CATEGORIES` (mirrors DESIGN §4) | classifier hallucinating a category outside the nine |
| `die()` if no category survives the filter | a run with no valid domain for any planner |

### Phase 2½ checks — `phase_reconcile`
| Check | Catches |
|-------|---------|
| **dead-subtask elimination** (runs *before* `_check_unresolvable`) | subtasks whose *every* `in_plan` requires tag is in the reconciler's unresolvable set, when at least one domain has 0 subtasks. `_prune_dead_subtasks(plans, unresolvable_entries)` removes fully-speculative subtasks mechanically (mirrors dead code elimination after constant folding — DESIGN §5 *Dead-subtask elimination*). Prunes downstream `depends_on` references to pruned sids (same pattern as `conditional_drops`). Strips pruned entries from `output["unresolvable"]` before `_check_unresolvable` runs. If all unresolvable entries were pruned, `_check_unresolvable` returns immediately and the run proceeds. If some remain, `die()` as before. Pruned sids are recorded in `state.data["speculative_collapse_drops"]`. |
| **external-twin demotion** (runs *after* `_prune_dead_subtasks`, *before* `_check_unresolvable`) | an `unresolvable` entry whose tag another subtask already declared `extent: external`. `_demote_unresolvable_with_external_twin(plans, unresolvable_entries, external_preconditions)` matches first on the exact tag, then on `_tag_key` (lowercase, split on `-`/`_`, singularize tokens over 3 chars, compare as a set). A hit rewrites the consumer's `requires` entry to `extent: external` with the twin's `reason` attributed to its source sid, drops the entry from `output["unresolvable"]`, records it in `state.data["external_twin_demotions"]`, and refreshes `state.data["external_preconditions"]` via `_collect_external_preconditions` so `_write_plan` persists the rescued entry into `plan.json`'s `preconditions`. **Placement is the safety property** — running after the reconciler's verdict means it can only convert a `die()` into a deploy note, never preempt a resolution the reconciler would have made. The normalized pass is set equality after singularization, never partial token overlap (DESIGN §5 *The external twin*). |
| reconciler's `unresolvable` array non-empty → `die()` with the worker's diagnosis | genuine gaps where no planner produced a needed capability *in the build graph* and no plausible connector subtask can be inferred. Restricted to `extent: in_plan` entries — `extent: external` entries are filtered out before the unresolved set is computed and surface as `preconditions` in `plan.json` rather than as failures. Each unresolved `(sid, tag)` pair is annotated with the consuming subtask's producing planner-domain (from `_compute_unresolved_requires`) so the abort message can render `domain/sid` — naming the planner-domain whose plan held the dangling dependency. The message itself is rendered by `_unresolvable_die_message(unresolvable, sid_domain, source_of_truth)`, a module-level pure function (extracted from the closure so it is testable at all). Its remediation text names both repairs explicitly (satisfy the criterion inside the fence, or move it to whatever owns that surface) and flags widening the scope fence as usually wrong — `domain/sid` alone is *not* the remediation lever. A final paragraph about narrowing `--source-of-truth` is emitted **only when `_effective_source_of_truth(st)` is not `codebase`** — it addresses research-surfaced phantom prerequisites under `both`/`research` and is a non-sequitur otherwise (DESIGN §11 records narrowing the preference as *historically* the escape hatch, superseded by `requires.extent: external`). |
| reconciler output validated against `SCHEMAS["reconciler"]` | malformed reconciler response (caught by `claude_p`'s schema gate; structurally invalid output is retried once, then escalated) |
| **size gate** on `added_subtasks` (runs *before* the acyclicity gate) | a reconciler-added subtask emitted with `size: large`. The reconciler-authored subtasks carry `_added_by_reconciler: true` (set in `_apply_reconciler_output`); `_find_oversized_added_subtasks` collects every offender. On detection, leerie tries one size-resolution retry (see "Size-resolution retry loop" below); if the retry still emits `size: large`, `die()` with the offending sids enumerated. The downstream `_validate_plan` size check (line "no `size: large` subtasks" under "Plan validation") is the final backstop and only fires for planner-authored `large` after this retry exhausts; its error message names "planner" vs "reconciler" via the `_added_by_reconciler` flag so the user knows which prompt misbehaved. |
| **acyclicity gate** (Tarjan SCC over the post-mutation graph; runs *before* the unresolved-requires re-check) | a rename / added_subtask / dependency_edge that closes a dependency cycle. Each individual reconciler mutation can be locally correct yet jointly cycle-creating — e.g. two renames whose targets each provide what the other side requires. Tarjan localizes the SCC; edge attribution names which mutation closed each edge. On detection, leerie tries one cycle-resolution retry (see "Cycle-resolution retry loop" below); if the retry still cycles, `die()` with the SCC + offending mutations enumerated. |
| **must-include constraint** (apply-step enforcement on retry output) | a retried reconciler output that omits any operation from the bounded set leerie required for each named cycle. The retry prompt lists the legal operations per cycle (`drop_require` on either rename, `dependency_edges` in either direction, `merged_subtasks` in either direction); if the revised output doesn't include at least one for each cycle, `die()` with the missing-cycle diagnostic — surfaces "model defied a structural constraint" cleanly, never a silent cycle. |
| **unresolved-requires retry loop** (recompute unresolved set after applying reconciler output) | the reconciler's renames/added_subtasks/add_provide ops didn't actually close every gap. Common cause: model invented a new tag in `added_subtasks` and forgot to rename the original consumer's tag to match. On first detection, leerie tries one retry with a structured prompt that surfaces string-similarity hints from the post-mutation `provides` namespace. If the retry still leaves unresolved tags, `die()` with the structured report. |
| **unresolved-retry must-include constraint** (apply-step enforcement on retry output) | a retried output that omits any operation addressing the named unresolved entries. Legal addressing: `rename` on the (sid, tag), `add_provide` covering the tag, `added_subtask` whose provides includes the tag, `conditional_drop` on the consumer sid, `drop_require` on the (sid, tag) (consumer's `requires` is over-specified — an aggregate or coarser synonym of what the consumer itself provides, not a real cross-subtask dependency; the consumer stays in the plan, only the bad edge goes), or `unresolvable` on the (sid, tag). |
| **conditional_drops** apply step (DESIGN §5 resolution action; the worker emits it as `op: "conditional_drop"` in `tag_ops`) | a planner-emitted consumer subtask whose own `intent` declares it conditional on an unresolvable `extent: in_plan` precondition (signals like "no-op if X", "conditionally add", "drop if Y", "otherwise this subtask is dropped"). The apply step removes the named sid from its plan, prunes downstream `depends_on` references to that sid, and records the drop in `state.data["conditional_drops"]` (keyed by sid → `{reason, from_unresolved_tag}`). Distinct from `state.data["dropped_subtasks"]`, which records off-tree soft-drops from `_filter_offtree_subtasks` (phase 3) — same shape of audit signal, different cause. The apply step `die()`s if the target sid carries `_added_by_reconciler: true` (the op is restricted to planner-authored consumers — a reconciler-added subtask has no planner prose to convert into a structured drop). |
| **dropped_requires** apply step (DESIGN §5 resolution action — also a cycle-breaking op; the worker emits it as `op: "drop_require"` in `tag_ops`) | a consumer's `requires` entry that was over-specified by its planner — an aggregate, coarser synonym, or authoring-time decision the same subtask itself records, rather than a code artifact another subtask produces. The apply step removes the named `(sid, tag)` `extent: in_plan` entry from the consumer's `requires` list. The consumer itself stays in the plan (unlike `conditional_drops`, which removes the whole subtask) — only the bad edge goes. Apply mechanics are identical whether the op is emitted as a resolution (unresolved-tag retry, addressing an over-specified self-reference) or a cycle-breaker (the over-specified entry was what closed the cycle). Silent no-op on missing sid/entry, mirroring `renames`. |
| post-unresolved-retry cycle gate re-run | the retry's revised output reintroduces a cycle (e.g., a rename closes a loop). Same Tarjan check as the primary acyclicity gate; on cycle, `die()` with the SCC report. |

**Size-resolution retry loop.** When the size gate fires on the first
reconciler attempt (any `added_subtask` with `size: large`),
`phase_reconcile` deep-copies the pre-mutation plans, reverts the failed
mutations, builds a retry prompt (`_build_size_retry_prompt`) naming each
offending sid, its `provides`/`requires`/`depends_on`, and the explicit
decomposition rule ("emit one subtask per `provides` tag, or smaller
groupings that share state"), then respawns the reconciler once. Maximum
two attempts total — mirrors the cycle-retry shape; one extra reconciler
spawn on oversize runs only. No recommendation heuristic is computed
(unlike the cycle loop): the mechanical guarantee is rendered directly
into the retry prompt (and documented in `prompts/reconciler.md` on the
first attempt) — the retry is the enforcement. The size gate runs
*before* the acyclicity gate because oversize authoring is an upstream
defect — a `large` subtask bundling several capabilities is also more
likely to produce a cycle, so splitting first gives the cycle gate a
cleaner graph.

**Retry composition (snapshot refresh).** When multiple retries fire on
the same run (e.g., size retry succeeds and then the cycle gate fires),
each successful retry refreshes `pre_plans_snapshot` to the post-retry
state, so the next retry's revert restores the most recent good state
rather than undoing an already-successful split. The unresolved retry
doesn't refresh — it's the last gate before `phase_reconcile` returns.

**Cycle-resolution retry loop.** When the acyclicity gate fires on the first
reconciler attempt, `phase_reconcile` deep-copies the pre-mutation plans,
reverts the failed mutations, computes a *recommended* operation per SCC
from structural signals (in `_recommend_cycle_resolution`), builds a
retry prompt (in `_build_cycle_retry_prompt`) that names the SCC, the
mutations that closed each edge, the structural signals, the
recommendation, and the bounded "must-include" set of acceptable
operations, then respawns the reconciler worker once with that prompt.
Maximum two attempts total — mirrors the schema-fail retry shape at
`leerie.py: claude_p()`. Cost: one extra reconciler spawn on cycling
runs only; non-cycling runs pay nothing extra.

The recommendation heuristic is deterministic:

1. **Exactly one edge in the SCC is a planner-declared `depends_on`** →
   `drop_require` on the rename that closes the reverse direction
   (planner ordering wins).
2. **Else SCC members share `files_likely_touched`** → `merged_subtasks(into,
   from)`, `into` = smaller subtask by `success_criteria_seed` length
   (tie-break: lexicographic sid).
3. **Else** → `drop_require` on the rename whose `from` tag had no
   planner-declared producer pre-reconcile (speculative rename).
4. **Tie-breaker of last resort** → drop the lexicographically later rename.

The retry prompt presents the recommendation as the answer, not one of
several options, and explicitly forbids `unresolvable` for cycle
resolution — the mechanical floor (gate + must-include) is the
guarantee; the recommendation primes the model toward it.

**Unresolved-requires retry loop.** Symmetric architecture, fired by a
different gate: when post-mutation `_compute_unresolved_requires` is
non-empty (cycle gate already clear), `phase_reconcile` deep-copies the
pre-mutation plans, computes a string-similarity recommendation per
unresolved entry (`_recommend_unresolved_resolution`), builds a retry
prompt (`_build_unresolved_retry_prompt`) naming the unresolved `(sid,
tag)` pairs, top-3 candidate `provides` ranked by Jaccard, the
recommendation (if any), and the must-include set, then respawns the
reconciler once (max two attempts). Two guards filter candidates before
scoring — a self-loop guard (skip the consumer's own sid) and an
extent-aware guard (`in_plan` only). Cases (first match wins):

1. Unique top match, Jaccard ≥ 0.5 → `rename(sid, from=tag, to=top.tag)`.
2. Top match, Jaccard ≥ 0.7 (even if not unique) → same.
3. Else → no recommendation; model picks unaided (the common case).

`unresolvable` IS valid for this retry (unlike the cycle retry's strict
forbid) — if no real producer exists, surfacing that cleanly is right.
The mechanical floor (must-include validator + post-retry unresolved +
cycle re-check) catches every malformed revision; the recommendation is
best-effort.

### Phase 2¾ checks — `phase_overlap_judge`
| Check | Catches |
|-------|---------|
| **deterministic duplicate-provider floor** (`check_duplicate_providers(plans) -> list[str]`, `DUPLICATE_PROVIDER` / `DUPLICATE_PROVIDER_NO_OVERLAP`) — runs **before** the cheap-skip and independently of `--skip-overlap-judge`, so it fires on every path including single-planner runs and a `plan_overlap_judge` `WorkerError` | Two tiers over the same tag→providers map (`_iter_duplicate_provider_pairs`, which yields `(sid_a, sid_b, tag, shared_files, kind)` where `kind ∈ {"overlap", "no_overlap"}`). **`DUPLICATE_PROVIDER`** — same **`provides` tag** *and* intersecting `files_likely_touched`: duplicate work on one file; routed into the M11 auto-merge below. **`DUPLICATE_PROVIDER_NO_OVERLAP`** — same tag, no shared file: advisory only, never auto-merged (folding is right for duplicate work and wrong for a mis-declared tag, and the synthesizer cannot tell them apart). Pure set logic (DESIGN *Language-to-JSON*). Path comparison is `_paths_designate_same_file` (component-wise, absorbing a repo-root prefix on either side), not raw string equality. **Three load-bearing exclusions:** (1) pairs sharing a non-`None` `_cofile_cluster` (§5½ (P1) *Sub-file*); (2) pairs sharing a non-`None` `_newfile_owner_id` — multi-file splitter chunks, which inherit the parent's `provides` verbatim and are not covered by (1) since only `_cofile_child` sets a cluster; (3) **no-overlap tier only** — pairs ordered by transitive `depends_on`/`requires` (`_transitive_predecessors` over `_build_predecessor_graph`), the legitimate shared-umbrella-tag chain. Exclusion (3) deliberately does **not** apply to the overlap tier (DESIGN §5). |
| **duplicate-provider merge routing** (`_duplicate_provider_merge_collisions(plans) -> list[dict]`, applied via `_apply_overlap_collisions`) — M11: the floor's detections are resolved, not just logged | mirrors the floor's detection logic, synthesizes one `resolution: "merge"` collision per flagged pair, and feeds them through the **same** `_apply_overlap_collisions` the judge's output uses (its `_would_cycle_after` guard, `skipped_redundant` dedup, anchor + transitive `survivor_of` cluster resolution). Runs above every cheap-skip, so single-planner and `--skip-overlap-judge` runs still get collisions resolved. Safe for the 3+-participant case because the merge chase carries every absorbed subtask's intent forward — a triangle of duplicate-provider pairs collapses to one survivor with the closing edge `skipped_redundant`. Persists to `state.data["duplicate_provider_merge_applied"]`, absent when nothing merged. |
| **cheap-skip when impossible** (fewer than 2 planners contributed subtasks, OR total subtask count < 2) | spurious worker spawn on single-planner / trivial runs. Log line `phase 2¾: overlap-judge skipped (single planner)` or `… (< 2 subtasks)`. |
| judge output validated against `SCHEMAS["plan_overlap_judge"]` | malformed judge response (retried once, then escalated). |
| **merge-feasibility backstop** (`_validate_overlap_judge_output`) — every `resolution == "merge"` must carry non-empty `merge_feasibility` | the judge skipping that discipline in `prompts/plan_overlap_judge.md` (§12 prompts advisory, code enforces). `die()` with the offending pair (`a_sid`/`b_sid`/`artifact`). |
| **`merge` apply step** (`_apply_overlap_merge`) | collapses the two subtasks: surviving sid is lex-smaller by default, or the `survivor_hint` when applying the anchor-survivor rule. Surviving subtask gets the union of `files_likely_touched`/`provides`/`requires`/`depends_on` (self-refs removed); `title` becomes `"{survivor.title} + {dropped.title}"`; `intent` concatenates survivor + absorbed intent (under an `--- Absorbed intent from {dropped.id} ---` marker) + a trailing merge-feasibility note (DESIGN §5 carry-forward invariant, so an already-once-merged intent chain isn't lost). `success_criteria_seed` becomes `"{survivor.criteria} AND {dropped.criteria}"`. Downstream `depends_on` referencing the dropped sid rewritten to the survivor. Recorded in `state.data["plan_overlap_applied"]`. |
| **`drop_a` / `drop_b` apply step** (`_apply_overlap_drop`) | removes the dropped sid; unions its `provides` into the survivor's (deduped, order-preserving, so downstream `requires` still resolve); drops any survivor `extent: in_plan` requires now self-looping; rewrites downstream `depends_on`. Title/intent/criteria are NOT copied — only capability-graph wiring is unioned. |
| **anchor-survivor rule** (`_apply_overlap_collisions` + `_compute_overlap_anchors`) | shared-endpoint clusters where one sid appears in 2+ non-`unresolvable` collisions (an *anchor*) survive every merge they participate in via `survivor_hint=anchor_sid`, overriding the lex-smaller default. Membership is bare appearance count with **no** semantic claim — a sid dropped twice is an anchor too and simply never uses the hint; do not read it as "the subtask that absorbs its partners" (false on roughly a third of resolution combinations). When both endpoints of a pair are anchors (e.g. a triangle's closing edge), falls through to lex-smaller. A `survivor_of` map rewrites later pairs against earlier survivors; fully-redundant closing edges are recorded `skipped_redundant`. A multi-drop cluster (below) collapses its N collisions into one `multi_drop_*` entry rather than one-per-collision. `_apply_overlap_drop` has a self-loop guard as defense in depth. |
| **keep-and-delete consistency gate** (`_validate_overlap_judge_output` + `_contradictory_drop_sids`) — self-contradictory output die()s before any mutation | a `drop_*` whose `dropped_sid` also *survives* another collision (kept as a merge endpoint or the non-dropped side of another `drop_*`) — no apply order satisfies both. die() names the sid, partner, artifact, and suggested resolution. **The predicate is `_contradictory_drop_sids` (survives-somewhere ∧ dropped-somewhere), NOT `_compute_overlap_anchors`** — conflating the two was the defect this gate was rewritten to remove; a sid dropped by 2+ collisions is an anchor by appearance but not a contradiction (that's the multi-drop shape below, sanctioned output). Gating on anchor membership instead killed runs whose judge output was correct, after full planner spend, unrecoverably. |
