| **duplicate-pair rule** (`check_overlap_judge_output` `DUPLICATE_PAIR` + `_validate_overlap_judge_output` coalescing, keyed on `_collision_effect`) — a pair may repeat only when every row has the same *effect* | one pair colliding on several artifacts (one row listing every path, or one row per artifact — DESIGN §5 *Multi-artifact pair*; the per-artifact form is absorbed as `skipped_redundant`). Effect-identical rows are coalesced keeping every `artifact`/`merge_feasibility`. Rows whose effects **differ** (e.g. swapped-endpoint `drop_a` deleting opposite subtasks, or a `drop`+`merge` on one pair) surface as `DUPLICATE_PAIR` inside the retry loop, terminal at the keep-and-delete gate if unfixed (`tests/test_phase_overlap_judge.py` freezes the full 4×3 matrix). `resolution` alone is the wrong signal — swapped-endpoint rows share a resolution string. Gating on bare pair repetition instead `die()`d coherent output past the retry loop; a real run was killed this way after significant planning spend. |
| **multi-drop cluster apply** (`_apply_multidrop` inside `_apply_overlap_collisions`) — one sid dropped by 2+ collisions applies as a single whole-cluster operation, never by replaying the pairs | one subtask's surface jointly covered by several siblings (DESIGN §5 *Multi-drop*). Replaying pairs through `survivor_of` is **silent corruption** — pair 2 would drop a live sid the judge never named, and `_apply_overlap_drop` discards title/intent/criteria, so the loss is unrecoverable (damage scales with cluster size). Instead: union the dropped subtask's `provides` into **every** named survivor, drop each survivor's now-self-looping requires, remove the dropped subtask once, fan `depends_on` out to **all** survivors (dedup, self-refs removed — mirrors `_remap_vanished_deps`). Guarded by `_would_cycle_after` with a three-tier ladder: `multi_drop_fanout` (acyclic) → `multi_drop_degraded_single` (fan-out would cycle; fall back to `sorted(survivors)[0]`) → `skipped_would_cycle` (both would cycle). Survivors sorted for determinism. Each tier recorded in `state.data["plan_overlap_applied"]`; tier 3 keys on `resolution: "multi_drop"` to attribute it to this bucket rather than a pairwise skip — every `(action, resolution)` shape partitions and sums to `len(applied)`. |
| **`unresolvable` → `die()`** at plan time | genuine API contradictions the judge refuses to auto-merge. Names both sids, the artifact, the reason, and the next step (disambiguate or narrow the task). Message must not suggest `resume`: this precedes `_write_plan()`, so `state.json` has no `waves` key and `_run_phases()` dies on resume. Strictly better than the multi-hour wave-N integrator crash this phase prevents. |
| **per-resolution cycle avoidance** (`_would_cycle_after` inside `_apply_overlap_collisions`) — checked before each `merge`/`drop_a`/`drop_b` apply | a resolution's dependency-union can introduce a transitive cycle absent from the post-reconcile graph. Deep-copies `plans`, applies to the copy, rebuilds the predecessor graph, runs `_tarjan_sccs`; a would-cycle resolution is skipped (next row) and both subtasks kept separate for the integrator. Side-effect-free; sees every earlier-applied resolution. Covers `drop_*` too. |
| **post-merge acyclicity backstop** — Tarjan SCC immediately after `_apply_overlap_collisions` returns | with per-resolution avoidance in place this must never fire; a surviving cycle `die()`s with `_format_cycle_diagnostic`, framed as an orchestrator logic bug, not user-recoverable. Defense-in-depth against future drift, mirroring `_apply_overlap_merge`'s defensive missing-sid `die()`. |
| **`skipped_would_cycle` audit action** | a `merge`/`drop_*` whose apply would close a cycle. Recorded with both sids, artifact, resolution; `survivor_of` is **not** updated on a skip (both endpoints stay live for later collisions). The judge is not re-prompted — a global-graph property outside its pairwise competence. |
| **state persistence** | full judge output → `state.data["plan_overlap_judge"]`; post-apply mutations → `state.data["plan_overlap_applied"]`. Persisted before the phase returns; visible for resume-time replay debugging. |

The complementary `_warn_cross_planner_file_overlap()` check at phase 3
is **kept as-is** — it now serves as a complementary signal for file-
overlap that *doesn't* indicate surface collision (the deliberately-
permissive same-file-different-surface class).

### Plan validation — `_validate_plan` (after scheduling, before persisting the plan)
| Check | Catches |
|-------|---------|
| **budget feasibility** — `check_budget_feasibility()` runs at the same layer, immediately after `_schedule()` and before `_write_plan()`. Estimates remaining `claude -p` calls (implementers + conformers + integrators per wave + finalize), added to `worker_count` already spent, multiplied by `budget_safety_margin`, compared to `max_total_workers`. | a planner output too large for the configured `--max-workers` cap. `State.bump_workers()` is the runtime backstop (raises `WorkerError` mid-execution); this earlier check `die()`s with `EXIT_BUDGET_INFEASIBLE=11` and a recommended `--max-workers` at the cheapest possible moment. Opt-out via `--skip-budget-check` / `LEERIE_SKIP_BUDGET_CHECK` / `leerie.toml`. See §"Budget feasibility preflight" and DESIGN §13. |
| ids match domain prefix (`bugfix-`, `feat-`, `refactor-`, `perf-`, `test-`, `deps-`, `config-`, `docs-`) | cross-domain collisions, audit ambiguity. The prompt receives the prefix directly as `ID_PREFIX = CATEGORY_ABBREV[domain] + "-"`, so it cannot drift from the validator's allowlist. |
| no `size: large` subtasks | planner OR reconciler violated the sizing constraint. Error names the actual author via `_added_by_reconciler` ("planner must split it further" vs. "reconciler must split it further (size-retry exhausted)"). This row is the post-merge backstop for both cases; the reconciler path is exercised through the phase 2½ size gate first. |
| no empty `success_criteria_seed` | implementer has no criteria starting point |
| every `depends_on` id exists | dangling edges silently dropped by the scheduler |
| every `requires` entry is `{tag, extent, reason?}`; `extent ∈ {in_plan, external}`; `reason` non-empty when `extent: external` | malformed planner output (JSON-schema-caught; this is the post-merge re-check) |
| every `requires` entry with `extent: in_plan` has a provider in some `provides` | unresolvable cross-domain dependency (`external` entries are declared out-of-graph) |
| no `files_likely_touched` entry matches `_is_protected_path()` (`.leerie/`, `.git/`, top-level `.claude/` outside the deliverable subtrees; the path compared as `_path_fold(path) + "/"`, where `_path_fold` is `posixpath.normpath`, the `_HFS_IGNORABLE` code points (git's `is_hfs_dotgit` list) removed, then NFKC, casefold and NFKC again) | planner named a protected meta-directory as a deliverable — would fail `check_diff_scope` mid-run. Catching it here gives the planner a corrective-retry round instead of burning an implementer. Coordination artifacts should use `provides`/`depends_on` + the implementer's `artifacts` field (DESIGN §5), not `files_likely_touched`. |

`_warn_cross_planner_file_overlap()` runs immediately after `phase_reconcile`
(before `_validate_plan` and the scheduler) and **logs a warning, never
fails**, when two planners' subtasks share a `files_likely_touched` path. The
reconciler also consumes this signal as one input to the cycle-resolution
heuristic above (shared-file SCC members get a `merged_subtasks`
recommendation); the warning complements rather than replaces it.

`_warn_layer_gaps(plans)` runs at the same layer, two heuristic warnings
(DESIGN §5 *Migration-surface completeness*): (1) a `schema.prisma` path
touched with no subtask touching seed/migration files — database-init gap;
(2) `provides` tags with env/bootstrap/secret/credential keywords but no
subtask touching `.env.example`/env docs — env-contract gap.

`_filter_offtree_subtasks()` runs at the same layer (after
`_warn_cross_planner_file_overlap`, before `_schedule()`) and **soft-drops
any subtask whose `files_likely_touched` resolves outside the run's primary
repo root** — typically a leak into a read-only inspect-dir mount. Drops are
recorded in `state.data["dropped_subtasks"]`. Must run before `_schedule()`
since `phase_execute` iterates `state.data["waves"]` (computed by
`_schedule()`) and a later drop would leave `waves` referencing a sid with no
spec on disk. A soft drop, not `die()`, because resume does not re-run the
planner pipeline and needs `state.data["waves"]`. A dropped subtask whose
`provides` a survivor `requires` is caught by the unresolvable-requires check
above.

### Per-subtask checks — in `_settle_subtask`, every worker result
| Check | Catches | On failure |
|-------|---------|-----------|
| `_validate_result()` — `incomplete-handoff` with missing checkpoint file | session-limit no-op; `--max-turns` with no checkpoint written; **worker reaped mid-turn** (e.g. an OOM-killed backgrounded build before the checkpoint was written) | **Rescued when the worktree holds commits, else Retryable** (`failure_kind="empty_handoff"`). `_settle_subtask` calls `_branch_has_commits_ahead` (True only when the worktree exists, git succeeds, and there are commits ahead of the run branch — distinct from `check_branch_has_commits`'s indeterminate `None`); if there are commits ahead, the worker produced a real deliverable and is settled `complete` (advisory conformance records whatever step didn't finish) instead of discarded — `fail()` would `_reset_subtask_worktree` and destroy the committed diff. Only a genuine no-op (no commits) stays retryable; a gone worktree / git failure is never mistaken for a real deliverable. Confidence gate and dirty-worktree fail are skipped for a rescued result. See DESIGN §9. |
| `_validate_result()` — other cross-field invariants | `handoff` with null `checkpoint_path`; `blocked` with no blocker; `failed` with no summary; `needs-clarification` with no `clarification_question` / invalid `checkpoint_path` | **Terminal** (`failure_kind="broken"`) |
| `check_branch_has_commits()` | `complete` claim, nothing committed *and* no `artifacts` returned. A non-empty `artifacts` array (DESIGN §5 *Artifact passing*) is a substitute deliverable — research-style subtasks pass without commits. | **Settled by execution when verification-only, else re-driven (DESIGN §8 *Settled by execution*).** A no-commits `complete` on a subtask `_verification_only(subtask)` holds for is settled by `_settle_by_execution`: a `pass` settles it `complete` through `_settle_already_satisfied` (`dropped_subtasks` reason `"settled_by_execution"`, the `conformance[sid]` sentinel); an `environment_limit` settles it `unconverged` (`_settle_unconverged(..., kind="environment_limit")`). A claim that is not verification-only is settled by `_settle_nothing_to_change` (below): `complete` on its verify commands passing and the HEAD satisfied-probe shown the implementer's evidence (`dropped_subtasks` reason `"satisfied_by_sibling"` when a sibling's integration merge touched its `files_likely_touched`, else `"satisfied_on_base"`), `unconverged` as `undecidable_no_op` on a `cannot_verify` no passing command answers, or as `no_op_refuted` on a second refuting execution after a re-drive; a probe answering only `cannot_verify` does not block when every `verify` entry has an argv and each passed and every criterion it lists `unverifiable` it also lists `covered_by_execution` (`_execution_answers_cannot_verify`; `decided_by: "execution"`). The probe never settles a claim alone. Any other outcome returns `status: "blocked"` with a typed blocker (`_execution_blocker`, or the unmet check), which the wave-end re-drive takes from the shared budget (§6 *Shared re-drive budget*). |
| dirty worktree check | uncommitted changes that vanish on integration | **Retryable** |
| `check_diff_scope()` | `.leerie/` or `.git/` in the diff; any `.claude/` path except `.claude/agents/`, `.claude/commands/`, `.claude/skills/` (the documented user-deliverable subtrees — never `settings.json` or a top-level `.claude/` file), each compared folded (`_path_fold`; the diff read with `-z`). Also a touched path present at `HEAD` that folds to a different path or directory of `HEAD`'s tree (`git ls-tree -r -z --name-only`), less pairs whose two spellings both were in the run branch's tree (`_fold_collisions(added, tree, before=)`); skipped when the run branch's tree cannot be listed | **Terminal** (protected path, fold collision); scope-volume warning is non-fatal (touched > max(3× expected, 5), or > 15 regardless) |
| `_validate_checkpoint()` — on `incomplete-handoff` | required section missing/empty/whitespace/placeholder-only (`none`/`n/a`/`na`/`tbd`/`nothing`/`unknown`/`todo`/`pending`/`—`/`--`/`-`/`?`, trailing punctuation ignored); a `## Files touched` path no longer exists and isn't flagged `[deleted]` | returns `blocked` |
| `_route_blocker_kind()` — on `status` `blocked` or `failed` from the worker | worker self-report of a blocker or failure, typed `blocker_kind` | **Routed by the kind** (DESIGN §13 *A blocked implementer says why, as a type*): `external_precondition` with a named resource → `accepted_external` only when the code check verifies it (`_verify_external_claim`), otherwise retyped `other` and re-driven — except that the same claim (`check.claim`) returning `unverified` with `reason: "environment"` on the blocked attempt after one that did, with no completed attempt between them, settles `unconverged` (`_settle_unconverged(..., kind="external_unverified")`, reason naming the claim); `environment_limit` → one in-place retry, then `unconverged`; `cannot_reproduce` → settled by execution, else re-driven, and `unconverged` when that execution hits the environment limit; `nothing_to_change` → settled `complete` on evidence when its verify commands (if any) pass and the satisfied-probe, shown the implementer's `criteria_results` locations, finds its criteria met, or answers only `cannot_verify` when every criterion has a command and each passed and every criterion it could not check is one a passing command exercises in full (`_settle_nothing_to_change`, §6 *Sibling-delivered no-op*); `unconverged` at once (`undecidable_no_op`) on any other `cannot_verify`, on a refuting execution after one re-drive (`no_op_refuted`), and when that execution hits the environment limit; else re-driven; every other kind (and a missing one) → `blocked`, re-driven at wave end from the shared budget. A self-reported `failed` is no longer terminal. |

`_validate_result()` accepts `complete` regardless of what
`criteria_results` carries — empty, missing, or `met:false` entries are all
valid (DESIGN §8: the criteria file is informational). An unmet-criterion
self-report is recorded for telemetry and surfaces as a warning, never
affecting terminal status. The criteria-file lock and the
`criteria_revision_proposal` channel were both removed when the criteria
file's load-bearing role retired (DESIGN §9).

### Per-subtask post-work conformance — in `_settle_subtask`, success path only

Triggered only when an implementer's `status: "complete"` has already cleared
every check above (commits present, worktree clean, no protected path
written). None of the other terminal statuses (`incomplete-handoff`,
`needs-clarification`, `blocked`, `failed`) invoke the conformer.
Implements DESIGN §9 *Post-work conformance*.

| Step | Function | Behavior |
|------|----------|----------|
| Discover rules files | `_discover_rules_files(repo_root)` | Existing paths from a fixed, capped allowlist (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.agent.md`, `.cursorrules`, `.windsurfrules`, `docs/CLAUDE.md`, `docs/AGENTS.md`, `docs/CONVENTIONS.md`, `docs/STYLE.md`, `docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md`, `docs/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md`, `docs/UI.md`, `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `docs/DESIGN.md`, `docs/IMPLEMENTATION.md`), deterministic order, never raises, `[]` when nothing matches. The design-system candidates exist so a repo's component/color/banner conventions reach both conformer and implementer (DESIGN §9). |
| Run conformer | `_run_conformer()` | One `claude -p` invocation with `ACT_TOOLS`, `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, `SCHEMAS["conformer"]`. Optional `extra_feedback` appended to the user prompt (Pattern B backgrounding-retry feedback). `WorkerError` → `None` (warning). Output passed through `_expand_conformer_output()` (N29), restoring the flattened wire shape into the four arrays downstream steps expect. |
| Validate output | `_validate_conformance_result()` | Cross-field invariants — a `rule_violations_residual` entry with no `axis` requires `rules_files_read` non-empty (one with an `axis` is leerie's own `build/lint/tests must pass` rule, which the conformer prompt states and no repository file supplies); each `rule_violations_fixed` cites a non-empty `rule`; each `docs_updates`/`tests_updates` cites an existing `path`. Failure → warning, loop breaks. |
| Re-run gates | `_clean_tree_gate` (first, right after the worker), `check_diff_scope` | The clean-tree gate (*Clean-tree gate (I1)*), then the implementer's scope check re-applied to conformer commits. A protected-path violation triggers `_restore_tree(worktree, before_sha)` (*One restore*), recorded as a warning, **not** `failed`/`blocked`. |
| Clobber-survival check | `_clobbered_owned_files(worktree, run_branch, impl_head_sha)` + `_blob_sha` | DESIGN §9 *No clobbering the implementer's work*. `impl_head_sha` snapshotted **once before the round loop** (a per-round HEAD would miss a round-0 clobber). Owned set = `git diff --name-only <run_branch>..<impl_head_sha>`; a clobber is a deletion at HEAD or a blob reverted to base (three-way `_blob_sha` compare via `git rev-parse --verify -q`); a legit conformer edit leaves a distinct third blob, not flagged. Warns always; under `--strict-conformer` also rolls back to the implementer HEAD **and blocks** — a `clobbered_files` flag forces a block even when `_conformance_clean` is True. Not auto-rolled-back in advisory mode (a legitimate revert-to-base is git-indistinguishable from a clobber). The final-tree pass uses `base=` a **snapshot SHA** (`_merge_base_sha(staging, working_branch, staging_before_sha)`), never `run_branch` — the staging worktree has the run branch checked out, so passing that name collapses the two blob lookups and reports every final-conformer edit as `(reverted-to-base)`. The per-subtask call site is correct with `base=run_branch` since a subtask worktree sits on a genuinely different ref. |
| Loop bound | `caps["conformance_rounds"]` (default 3) | Re-runs on malformed output or remaining residuals; exhausting the cap is a warning, not a failure. |
| Loop-continuation predicate | `_conformance_clean(conf_res, baseline)` + `_baseline_red_axes(baseline)` | DESIGN §9 *The signal that continues the loop is a delta, not a verdict*. True (ends loop) when nothing left is this subtask's responsibility. `baseline` is `st.data["conformance"]["_baseline"]` or `None`. **Checked ahead of the red-axis exclusion: `ran && !measured` returns False** — an unmeasurable axis (runner absent, or `_is_fork_exhaustion`) is a third state, not "red at baseline." Then two exclusions keyed on `_baseline_red_axes()` (admits only `_BLT_AXES` names): (1) `ran && !passed` red at baseline doesn't block; (2) a `rule_violations_residual` whose **`axis` field** is red at baseline doesn't block. Everything else blocks — an unlabelled residual, or a failure on an axis green at baseline (a real regression). `axis` is read from the schema field, never inferred from `rule`/`why_not_fixed` prose (*Language-to-JSON*); optional on the schema, absence gates. `baseline=None` reproduces the pre-change absolute-verdict behaviour byte-for-byte. |
| Axis selection | `resolve_blt_scoped(repo_root)` + `_changed_files(worktree, run_branch)` + `_select_subtask_axes(blt, scoped, files, base_ref, mode, test_globs, direct, named_tests)` | DESIGN §9 *Per-subtask scope: a delta proxy, not the suite*, *A subtask runs the tests it names*. Resolved once per subtask before the round loop — the changed-file set is the implementer's diff; conformer commits don't widen scope. `mode` is `st.data["subtask_tests"]`. Under `scoped`, a `test` template `_impact_runner` reads as an impact-analysis runner renders `direct` (`resolve_test_files_scoped`) over the diff's test files and `named_tests`, or defers; the template itself renders only with no `direct`. `resolve_blt_scoped` reads `test_scoped`/`build_scoped` from `.leerie/config.toml`, else infers: the first (diff, affected-tests) element of `_js_runner_scoped_templates(repo_root)` — `npx vitest related --run {files} --passWithNoTests` (a `vitest.config.*` or `vitest.workspace.*` present), `npx jest --findRelatedTests {files} --passWithNoTests` (a `jest.config.*`) — otherwise `_infer_scoped_test_template(_canonical_test_command(repo_root))` — from a canonical test command (declared, else inferred, read without `resolve_blt`'s log lines) that is a bare invocation of a `_SCOPED_RUNNER_PREFIXES` argv prefix (`shlex.split`; only options after it — a word following one of the runner's `_SCOPED_RUNNER_VALUE_OPTS` (pytest's entry is `_PYTEST_VALUE_OPTS`) is that option's value, while selecting options such as `-k`/`-m`/`--tag` are absent from that table and so disqualify — except `go test`'s package patterns): pytest / `python -m pytest` / `python3 -m pytest` (any `python<version>`, `_PYTHON_BIN_RE`) / `py.test`, also behind a `_SCOPED_ENV_WRAPPERS` wrapper and its options (`uv run`, `poetry run`, `pipenv run`, `pdm run`, `rye run`, `hatch run`; `_scoped_unwrap`), kept in the template — for pytest `_scoped_pytest_template` keeps the options (a `_PYTEST_VALUE_OPTS` option with its value) except the suite-level ones in `_PYTEST_SUITE_LEVEL_OPTS` (`--cov-fail-under`, `--max-warnings`, `--junitxml`/`--junit-xml`/`--junitprefix`/`--junit-prefix`) and every `--cov*` option, dropped with their values — when it dropped a `--cov*` option it appends `--no-cov` once (pytest-cov is evidently installed; `--no-cov` also disables a config `fail_under`) — and drops the path positionals, returning not-bare for a node id (`::`), a `_PYTEST_SELECTING_OPTS` option, or a word after a long option in neither `_PYTEST_VALUE_OPTS` nor `_PYTEST_LONG_FLAGS` —, `rspec` / `bin/rspec` / `bundle exec rspec`, `rails test` / `bin/rails test` / `bundle exec rails test` → `<canonical> {test_files}`; `rake test` / `bundle exec rake test` → `[bundle exec ]_RUBY_TEST_LOADER {test_files}` (`ruby -Itest -Ilib -e 'ARGV.dup.each { |f| require File.expand_path(f) }; ARGV.clear'`); `go test` → `go test <its options> {test_packages}`; `cargo test` (no `--`) → `cargo test <its options> --no-fail-fast {test_targets}`; anything else returns `(None, "no_scoped_runner:<argv0 or why>")` — and `npx tsc --noEmit` as `build_scoped` when `tsconfig.json` exists and canonical build isn't already `tsc`-shaped (DESIGN §9; DESIGN §8 *Scoped runners for every runner leerie can read*). Kept separate from `_infer_build_lint_test` so the launcher's mirrored bash inference stays untouched. No lint tier. `_changed_files` uses `git diff -z --name-only` (`-z` avoids git's C-quoting of non-ASCII paths breaking `splitlines()`). `_render_scoped` `shlex.quote`s each path, returns `None` (a `tests` axis is then deferred, a `build` axis falls back to canonical; below) when a `{files}` template has no files — rendering bare would run EVERYTHING. For an impact-analysis template — `_impact_runner(template) -> str | None`, the `_RUNNER_DIRECT_SELECTORS` runner whose word `_shell_scan` finds (`_runner_positions`) with its affected selector after it — `{files}` keeps only the files whose extension is in `_IMPACT_SOURCE_EXTS` (`.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mts`, `.cts`, `.vue`, `.svelte`) before that absence rule (DESIGN §9 *An impact-analysis runner is handed only its own module sources*). A `{test_files}` variant substitutes only `_is_test_file`-matching members with the same absence rule, for runners with no source→test impact analysis (pytest treats a non-test path as an ERROR, exit 4, and poisons the whole invocation); `{test_packages}` substitutes the sorted `./<dir>` (or `.`) of each test-shaped `_test.go` member and `{test_targets}` a `--test <stem>` per `_is_cargo_integration_test` member (a `.rs` file directly under `tests/`), each `None` when there are none (`_SCOPED_PLACEHOLDERS` lists all five). `_is_test_file` matches a `tests/`/`test/`/`spec/` segment or `test_*.py`/`*_test.*`/`*.test.*`/`*.spec.*`; `test_file_globs` in `.leerie/config.toml` replaces the built-ins, read by `resolve_test_file_globs(repo_root)` and passed by `_run_conformance_phase` as `test_globs`. `_render_scoped` also hard-skips an unsubstitutable placeholder (`_UNKNOWN_PLACEHOLDER_RE`, warned once per process via `_warn_unknown_placeholder_once`) rather than shipping a literal brace — an unguarded skew between a newer `.leerie/config.toml` and an older installed orchestrator would otherwise turn every subtask RED. The scan runs against the TEMPLATE with placeholders stripped, never the rendered command (a changed path may legitimately contain braces). Under `scoped`, a `tests` axis whose proxy doesn't resolve is **deferred** — omitted from the returned command map, not replaced by the canonical command (DESIGN §9 *Per-subtask scope*, the absence rule); `build` and `lint` keep the canonical fallback. `full` returns every canonical command, `off` returns `{}`. The scope label is `scoped` if at least one axis used a proxy, else `deferred` when an axis was deferred, else `full` — and `runner_config_changed` whenever `scoped["test"]` is an impact-analysis template and a changed file is that runner's configuration (`_is_runner_config(path, runner)`: its basename matches `_RUNNER_CONFIG_GLOBS[runner]` — vitest `vitest.config.*`, `vite.config.*`, `vitest.workspace.*`; jest `jest.config.*`); then the `tests` axis is `_render_scoped(direct, files + named_tests, ...)` (deduplicated), deferred when it renders nothing. `_run_conformance_phase` passes `direct=resolve_test_files_scoped(repo_root)` and `named_tests` = the subtask's `files_likely_touched` strings. `_deferred_axes(subtask_axes, blt, mode)` names the deferred axes (only ever `tests`, only under `scoped`); `_run_conformance_phase` merges `_DEFERRED_AXIS` (`{ran: False, measured: False, passed: None, command: "", deferred: True, summary: "deferred to the whole-tree pass"}`) for each into every pre/post measurement, so `_apply_measured_axes` overwrites the conformer's self-report on a deferred axis too, and `_format_blt_results_section` renders any axis with `deferred: True` as `deferred to the whole-tree pass (no proxy for this diff)`. |
| Named-test-files template | `resolve_test_files_scoped(repo_root)` + `_js_runner_scoped_templates(repo_root)` | DESIGN §9 *Operands that are already test files take the runner's direct form*. The template every caller holding test files renders through `_acceptance_cmd(st, files, tree)`: the acceptance sets (`_run_acceptance_file`), their parse probe (`_acceptance_parse_probe`), the re-drive self-check (`_run_delivery_redrive`), the coupled tests replacing a forbidden suite (`_scoped_test_replacement`), discovery (`_intermittent_discovery`), B* reruns and `files=` captures (`_capture_failing_test_ids`), the falsifier (`_falsifier_gates`) and the conflicted-area tests (`_integration_test_failures`); the precondition checks `phase_acceptance_write`'s skip, `_acceptance_can_check` and `_falsifier_gates`' skip read it too, and the acceptance writer's real-database note shows it verbatim (`_prisma_real_db_section`). `resolve_blt_scoped` (a diff's affected tests) feeds only `_select_subtask_axes` and `_warn_scoped_degraded_once`. Resolution: a declared `test_files_scoped` (`_load_blt_config` key); else a declared `test_scoped` through `_derive_test_files_scoped(template)` — when `_shell_scan` reads it as one simple command (words only, depth 0, no `$` or backtick in a word, no heredoc) naming exactly one runner of `_RUNNER_DIRECT_SELECTORS` (`vitest`: `related` → `run`, which must be its first non-option word; `jest`: `--findRelatedTests` → `--runTestsByPath`) whose selector and `{files}` each occur once, those two words are replaced in the raw text (`{files}` → `{test_files}`) and the result kept only if it rescans to the same tokens with exactly those two changed; else the declared `test_scoped` as written; else the second (named test files) element of `_js_runner_scoped_templates` — `npx vitest run {test_files} --passWithNoTests` / `npx jest --runTestsByPath {test_files} --passWithNoTests`; else `resolve_blt_scoped(repo_root).get("test")`, already `{test_files}`-tier (or package/target) for every other inferred runner. Over `{test_files}`, `_acceptance_cmd` renders nothing when any file is not `_is_test_file`-shaped, so a source file never reaches the direct form. Its last step is `_vitest_exact_selection(cmd, files, tree or st.repo_root)`: when `_vitest_filter_form` says the command hands the files to vitest as positional filters (vitest named with a first non-option word outside `_VITEST_NON_FILTER_SUBCOMMANDS` = `related`/`bench`/`init`/`list`, or a package-manager script whose `_runner_command` body runs vitest), every file `_vitest_filter_colliders(tree, files)` lists — walked with `node_modules` and `.git` skipped and symlinked directories not followed; `_vitest_filter_selects` is vitest's lower-cased substring rule tried at every ancestor the two paths share — is appended through `_append_runner_flags` as `--exclude <realpath of tree>/<path>`, glob metacharacters escaped (`_VITEST_GLOB_META_RE`). No collider: the command is returned unchanged. Colliders and no placement: `None`, logged. `_acceptance_parse_probe` passes its `tree`. The launcher's `config --init` template documents `test_files_scoped` (commented, with the derivation it overrides) and `config` prints it beside `test_scoped`; undeclared, its provenance reads `derived from test_scoped at runtime` when `test_scoped` is declared, else `inferred at runtime` (the bash arm names the source and never derives a value itself). Pinned by `tests/test_test_files_template.py`. |
| Measure (pre / post) | `_measure_axes(worktree, axes, st, caps, ...)` | Run immediately before the round (feeds `BLT_RESULTS:`) and again after (overwrites the worker's self-report). Memoised via `blt_results`, so the post measurement is free when the round committed nothing (measured, 182/224 rounds). `--subtask-tests off` yields `{}` and skips both; a deferred axis is never run and carries `_DEFERRED_AXIS` in both. Each axis is bounded by `caps["worker_timeout_sec"]` (5400s default) — no tighter per-axis ceiling. |
| Worktree deps | `_ensure_worktree_deps(tree, st, caps, ...)`, from inside `_measure_axes` | DESIGN §6½ *Who runs that install*. Applies the provision recipe's install/build on the FIRST axis actually measured — not at worktree creation, since a config/docs-only subtask (44/91 in the motivating run) correctly skips it. Memoised on the resolved absolute path in module-level `_DEPS_INSTALLED` (per-process fact, not run state). Non-fatal: a failed install leaves every axis `_measure_axes` then measures in that tree unmeasured (below). Returns `bool` — False when an `install` entry exited non-zero, timed out or raised (a failed `build` entry does not count: a fix that breaks the build is evidence the tests then show), True otherwise; a memo hit returns what that install did (module-level `_DEPS_FAILED: dict[str, int]`, the failed subset of `_DEPS_INSTALLED` with its count of failed installs in a row, dropped on a fresh install and on a success), except that a memo hit on a failed install installs again while that count is at most `caps["deps_install_retries"]` (2), logging `"<log_prefix>: the dependency install failed here before — retrying it (<n> of <cap>)"`. `async _retry_failed_baseline(st, caps, *, log_path) -> bool`: when any axis of `conformance._baseline.axes` carries `deps_failed` and the baseline has a `sha`, measures build/lint/tests again in a fresh detached `baseline-retry` helper checkout of that sha (at most `deps_install_retries` times per process, module-level `_BASELINE_RETRIES: dict[str, int]` keyed by the sha), and when its install succeeded (no axis carries `deps_failed`) replaces `_baseline.axes`/`red_axes` and `baseline_failing_ids` and returns True; called at the top of `_confirm_final_test_failures` and of `_refresh_test_id_diff` (which then measures instead of reusing). `_run_final_conformance` re-reads `conformance._baseline` from state after every `_confirm_final_test_failures` call — each round's, and the after-loop confirm of a round that broke before its post-measurement (there keeping the last round's tests-red refinement on the new baseline) — so `_conformance_clean` and the strict `blocked` verdict judge against the re-measured base. `_confirm_final_test_failures` never reuses a prior verdict with `base_install_failed`, and `_refresh_test_id_diff` never reuses such a diff (nor a `stale_for_tree` one after a baseline was replaced). DESIGN §9 *A failed install is no measurement*: `_measure_axes` makes every result it measured after a False unmeasured, whatever the axis and whatever the command's exit: `measured: False`, `passed: None`, `deps_failed: True`, `summary` `"not measured: the dependency install failed — <the command's tail>"`, no `failing_ids` (no report run is taken), never memoised. Every reader judges a result through one predicate, `_axis_measured(ax) -> bool` (`ran` and `measured` and not `deps_failed`; the last clause for a baseline saved in run state before this rule, `measured: True` beside `deps_failed: True`), and `_baseline_red_axes` drops from the saved `red_axes` any axis whose saved result carries `deps_failed` — so on a resume that reuses such a baseline no axis counts red for want of its dependencies. Through it: `red_axes` in `_capture_conformance_baseline` and `_retry_failed_baseline` and `base_red_axes` in `_base_health_payload` exclude it, `_round_axis_regressions` skips it, `_conformance_clean` reads it not clean (ran, not measured), and the PR's final-tree evidence reads "not measured". Readers that name why an axis is unmeasured read `deps_failed` for the reason: `_format_blt_results_section` (`BLT_RESULTS:`), `_format_baseline_section` (`BASELINE:`) and `_format_baseline_green_message` say the dependency install failed rather than that the runner is missing. `_confirm_final_test_failures` returns None for a `tests` result with `deps_failed`, logging that the install failed before its unmeasured check (and `_refresh_test_id_diff`'s `why` reads "the dependency install failed in the tree measured, …"); `_capture_conformance_baseline` records `baseline_failing_ids = None` for one; B\*'s `confirm-base` and the re-drive's `redrive-base` checkouts rerun nothing when it is False (the final diff's verdict gets `base_unavailable` and `base_install_failed`); the held-out acceptance callers (exit-code verdicts) treat it as before. Collapses 263 installs across 161 worker logs into one per worktree. The recipe loop runs inside `_leaves_tree_as_found` (below). |

| Apply (twice per round) | `_apply_measured_axes(conf_res, pre)` then `(conf_res, post)` | Replaces `conf_res["build"\|"lint"\|"tests"]` with the orchestrator's measurement into a NEW dict (raw worker payload stays as-emitted for telemetry). **Both applications are load-bearing.** `post` is the ordinary tail case. `pre` runs as soon as there's a dict — in `_run_conformance_phase` before `_clean_tree_gate` and `_validate_conformance_result` — because four gates `break` before the tail: the I1 unclean-tree rollback, malformed result, protected-path violation, strict-mode clobber. One application precedes all of them; no gate carries its own (in `_run_final_conformance` the unclean-tree exit precedes the apply because it never adopts the round's result). Without it those paths would carry the conformer's *claimed* axes into `_conformance_clean`'s `--strict-conformer` decision — gating on a self-report, the exact thing this phase stopped doing. `pre` is also the *accurate* measurement there, since both exits roll the worktree back toward pre-round state. Pinned by `test_the_overwrite_is_applied_twice_per_round` (shape) and the per-exit `*_still_reports_measured_axes` tests in `tests/test_run_conformance_phase.py` (substance). |
| Round delta | `_round_axis_regressions(pre, post)` | An axis green before the round, red after — a regression the conformer just introduced. Appended to `warnings`, fed into next round's feedback, ANDed into the loop-exit condition so a self-inflicted break earns another round. Never fires when either side is unmeasured, when command strings differ (a carried result is compared on its `whole_command`), or on red→red (inherited debt). |
| BLT-axis observability + feedback | `_emit_bash_axis_warnings()` | Parses the per-worker JSONL conformer log after each round for two feedback-injected patterns: (1) **multi-invocation** — `ran <AXIS>_CMD K times in one round` (progressive testing is legitimate, but a provably-redundant re-run wastes an expensive cycle); (2) **retry-after-backgrounded** — `<AXIS>_CMD auto-backgrounded … followed by another <AXIS>_CMD invocation`, the "retry-instead-of-recover" pattern. Both formatted via `_format_check_feedback()` and passed to the next round. `_BLT_AXIS_RES` holds compiled per-axis regexes (test/build/lint runner invocations); `_count_orphaned_bg_axis` also accepts `BashOutput shell_id=<id>` polls as a valid recovery path. |
| Attach result | — | `res["conformance"]` and `res["conformance_warnings"]` added to the implementer's result; the subtask still returns `complete`. |

The phase is advisory: **no path through it produces a `failed` or `blocked`
subtask status.** Build/lint/test failures, malformed conformer output,
crashes, gate violations, and exhausted rounds all surface as
`conformance_warnings` and non-fatal log lines. Per §12: *discovery* of rule
files, *schema validity* of conformer output, and *protected-path
invariance* are code-enforced; whether the conformer made the right
docs/tests/rule-violation calls is left to the worker.

### Wave-level checks (after integration)
| Check | Catches |
|-------|---------|
| `_scan_conflict_markers()` | unresolved `<<<<<<<` markers in the run-branch worktree after integration — deterministic safety net |

There is no LLM wave-level re-validation. An earlier `validate_wave` ran a
deterministic test-runner fast-path and an LLM validator over per-subtask
criteria with a re-spawn loop; removed when the criteria file's load-bearing
role retired (DESIGN §8, §9). Per-subtask quality is the implementer's
confidence gate; the wave-level safety net is the conflict-marker scan.

### Post-integrator checks (after an integrator handles a conflict)
Verify the integrator honored DESIGN §6's *behavioral* conflict-resolution
contract — the integrator prompt (`prompts/integrator.md`) carries the
behavioral spec (read every involved subtask's intent, preserve each side's
intent, call irreconcilable cases a `design-conflict`); the orchestrator
only checks the outcome.

| Check | Catches |
|-------|---------|
| `check_merge_committed()` | integrator returned `resolved` but left the worktree mid-merge (`MERGE_HEAD` present) or staged-uncommitted — the subtask is backed out (`_back_out_unmerged`, below) |
| `check_integrator_commit()` | integrator merge commit touched `.leerie/` files (`show --name-only -z`, compared folded) — non-fatal warning |
| `_set_integration_subject(staging, sid, pre_sha)` (after `check_merge_committed` passes) | an integrator merge committed under its own message: HEAD, when a two-parent merge whose first parent is `pre_sha`, is re-worded (`commit --amend --no-verify`, tree and parents unchanged) to `leerie: integrate <sid>` with the integrator's message as the body — the subject `_integration_commit` and `_sibling_deliveries` find a subtask's merge by |
| integrator status `design-conflict` / `failed` | unresolvable conflict — the subtask is backed out, the same fallback as a repair round's verdict (DESIGN §6 *When integration cannot succeed*): `_back_out_unmerged(st, staging, sid, pre_sha, reason)` runs `git merge --abort` and `git reset --hard <pre_sha>` (the merge's first parent, read before `integrate.sh`), writes `integration_gate[sid]` `{accepted: false, outcome: "backed_out", fallback_reason, reset_to, merge_commit_sha: ""}` (so a resume skips the sid), records the `risk_register[sid]` `integration_content_loss` entry and `_settle_unconverged(..., kind="integration_backed_out")`; `integrate_wave` records the sid `unconverged` in `results` and continues the wave. Only a reset that does not land on `<pre_sha>` `die()`s |
| `_try_json_key_merge()` (before any integrator) | a conflict confined to `.json` files that merges by key with no key conflict — committed by code, no integrator or judge |
| integrator **crash** (`WorkerError` or `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` from the integrator's `claude_p`, or no result) | infrastructure failure, not a verdict — `_rescue_integrator_work()` captures the in-progress resolution to `refs/leerie/rescue/<run-id>/<sid>/<n>` (`n` = 1 + the highest existing `n` for that sid; a pre-existing flat `…/<sid>` ref from an older leerie makes it `…/<sid>.<n>`, since a ref cannot also be a directory; `git update-ref <ref> <commit> ""` so an existing ref is never overwritten — a failure returns None) **before** the merge is aborted; then `_restart_integration_merge(staging, st, sid, pre_sha)` resets staging to `<pre_sha>` and re-runs `integrate.sh`, and a fresh integrator resolves the same conflict — up to `integrator_crash_retries` (2) retries. A restart that does not land on `<pre_sha>` or does not reproduce the conflict (`integrate.sh` exit ≠ 1) ends the retries. Retries spent → `_back_out_unmerged(st, staging, sid, pre_sha, reason)` with `reason` naming every rescue ref (`integrator crashed N time(s) (<cause>); its resolutions are rescued to <ref>, …`), and the wave continues; no `blocked[sid]`, no `die()` |

`_rescue_integrator_work(staging, sid, run_id) -> str | None` returns the rescue
ref, or `None` when nothing to save or the capture failed. **Not** gated on
`check_merge_committed`: a crashed integrator typically dies mid-resolution
with no merge commit, exactly the case worth rescuing (DESIGN §12). Stages
into a throwaway `GIT_INDEX_FILE` — in the worktree's own git dir
(`rev-parse --absolute-git-dir`; staging is a linked worktree whose `.git` is
a file) — seeded from HEAD (`read-tree` → `add -A` →
`write-tree` → `commit-tree`) because `git stash` refuses a conflicted tree;
the real index/working tree are never touched, untracked files are
captured. Every git failure degrades to `None` — a rescue failure must
never mask the crash. `_run_proc` gained an `env: dict[str, str] | None`
param for this.

### Resume integrity — `_validate_resume_state()`
Enforces (one half of) DESIGN §6's "the run branch is the resume contract"
invariant — state.json's `waves`/`completed_waves` say *which* wave to
resume; the never-reset `leerie/runs/<run-id>` branch holds *the work*
every prior wave produced. Both must be coherent for resume to be safe.

On `resume`: asserts `task` is present and non-empty; asserts `waves`,
`completed_waves`, `subtask_status` are well-formed *if present*. `waves` is
intentionally optional — a run interrupted before scheduling has none, and
per DESIGN §6 "Resumable planning — a per-phase checkpoint cursor, not a
`waves` gate," `_run_phases` walks the planning-phase sequence (classify →
plan → reconcile → overlap-judge → adherence-gate → off-tree/satisfied
filters → schedule) and re-enters at the first phase whose `plans_after_*`
checkpoint key is absent, reusing the last completed phase's persisted
`plans` rather than re-deriving from scratch. Rejects corrupt/hand-edited
state without rejecting a legitimately-early interruption. It is the only
refusal of a state with no planning output: a run that recorded its task
and died inside `phase_classify` (no `categories`, no `plans_after_*`)
re-enters at `phase_classify` (DESIGN §6 *The first phase is a phase like
any other*). A state with no `current_phase` stamp at all is started from
its recorded task by the never-started demotion at the top of
`_run_phases` (preflight, `_preflight_repo`, run identity), not resumed.
Pinned by `tests/test_resume_after_phase1_death.py`, which drives the real
`main()` through a phase-1 death and its resume.

The `except SystemExit` handler in `main()` guards `st.save()` behind
`st.data.get("task")` so that a failed `resume` (which `die()`s before
state was loaded) does not poison the host-side `state.json` with a bare
`{"finished_at": …}` stub — that would block subsequent resume attempts
with "no usable task" instead of the clearer "no state.json".

On `resume`, `main()` continues every sticky run choice the fresh run
recorded — the source-of-truth preference, the models and efforts, the
skip flags, the caps, `no_push` — before `_orchestrate()` reads any of
them (`_continue_run_choices`, §2½ *Run choices on resume*). Only a flag
on the resume's command line overrides a recorded choice; the resume's
env and `leerie.toml` do not.

### Concurrency model
The orchestrator runs on a single `asyncio` event loop. Each `claude -p`
worker is spawned via `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec` (wrapped by
`_run_proc`) with `start_new_session=True`, so each worker is its own
POSIX session and process-group leader. Parallel workers within a wave run
via `_gather_or_cancel` (an `asyncio.gather` wrapper that on the first
exception cancels every other in-flight task and awaits finalization
before re-raising) under an `asyncio.Semaphore(max_parallel)`. `State`
carries no lock — coroutines interleave only at `await` points, never
inside a `st.data[k] = v; st.save()` pair. `State.save()` writes a temp
file then `os.replace()`s for atomicity against a process crash.

Subprocess cleanup is four-layered, addressing two leak classes plus mid-run pressure reduction:

1. **Lifetime descendant tracking (`_DescendantTracker`).** A per-worker
   asyncio task polls `_enumerate_descendants(proc.pid)` every ~0.5s and
   accumulates every PID ever observed as a descendant. On every exit
   path, `stop_and_reap()` SIGKILLs the accumulated set. This is the
   load-bearing fix for Claude Code's Bash tool with `run_in_background:
   true`: the tool wrapper spawns the user command in a detached POSIX
   session and can exit while the command keeps running; by the time
   `claude -p` exits the backgrounded command has reparented to PID 1 and
   is invisible to a post-hoc PPID walk — but the tracker observed it
   mid-flight and has its PID.

2. **Abnormal-exit subtree termination (`_terminate_proc_tree`).** On
   `KeyboardInterrupt`/`SIGTERM`/`RateLimitedExit`/any other
   `BaseException`, `_run_proc`'s and `_invoke`'s catch-all handlers call
   `_terminate_proc_tree(proc)`: SIGTERM to the worker's process group
   (`os.killpg`) AND every descendant via PPID walk, wait
   `_PROC_TREE_GRACE_SEC = 2.0`, then SIGKILL survivors via both
   mechanisms. The PPID walk is needed because Bash-tool subprocesses sit
   in a *different* POSIX session than `claude -p`, so `killpg` alone
   misses them. Exception paths run the tracker reap *after* this,
   catching anything orphaned during the run.

Layers 1 and 2 compose: `_terminate_proc_tree` is broad and synchronous
(kills the attached subtree), the tracker is narrow and historical (kills
only what it observed, including processes that have since reparented
away). Neither alone is sufficient.

3. **Mid-run PID reaping (`_poll_loop` + `_reparented_orphans`).** A
   pressure-gated reducer under the PID-exhaustion-detection backstop
   (below) that proactively reaps orphans before `pids.max` is reached.
   `_DescendantTracker` takes an optional `cgroup_sid`; each `_poll_loop`
   cycle, when set, computes the pressure ratio `pids.current / pids.max`
   via `_cgroup_stat`. Reaping arms at `_PID_REAP_HIGH_WATER = 0.90`, then
   `_reparented_orphans(self._seen, min_age)` SIGKILLs the killable set
   oldest-first until the ratio drops below `_PID_REAP_LOW_WATER = 0.75`.
   `_reparented_orphans(seen, min_age=None) -> list[int]` snapshots `ps
   -eo pid,ppid,etimes` (raises on failure → `[]`, never parses garbage)
   and returns, oldest-first, PIDs from `seen` that are alive, reparented
   to init or the orchestrator (post-`_become_subreaper`), and at least
   `min_age` seconds old. `min_age`'s `None` sentinel resolves
   `_PID_REAP_MIN_AGE_SEC` *at call time* rather than binding once at def
   time, so patching the constant moves the floor.

   **Two-tier age floor (DESIGN §6 *Why a single 60s floor is not
   enough*).** `_poll_loop` selects the floor from the same pressure
   ratio: at or above `_PID_REAP_CRITICAL_WATER = 0.90` it passes
   `_PID_REAP_CRITICAL_AGE_SEC = 5`; below it, `_PID_REAP_MIN_AGE_SEC =
   60`. Without the critical tier the reaper arms at 90% and finds every
   candidate younger than 60s — a disabled reducer. `_PID_REAP_CRITICAL_WATER`
   equals `_PID_REAP_HIGH_WATER` (both 0.90) but stays a separate named
   constant since arming and floor-escalation answer different questions.
   (DESIGN §6 carries the measurement behind the tier.)

4. **Zombie reaping (`_become_subreaper` + `_zombie_reaper`).** Handles
   *zombies* (`<defunct>`, not yet `wait()`ed), which also count against
   `pids.max`; the container PID 1 is not a reaping init, so orphaned
   `git`/`ssh-agent` descendants reparent to it and rot (DESIGN §6
   *Zombie reaping*). `_become_subreaper()` — called once early in
   `main()` — issues `prctl(PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER, 1)` (Linux-guarded, a
   logged no-op elsewhere) so orphans reparent to the orchestrator.
   `_zombie_reaper()` is a background asyncio task, same lifecycle as
   `_memory_sampler`. It is an **allowlist, never a `/proc` scan**:
   `os.waitpid(pid, WNOHANG)`s only PIDs in `_REAPABLE_PIDS`.

   **`ChildProcessError` (ECHILD) does NOT discard the PID (N36).** For a
   live grandchild, ECHILD means "not ours **yet**" — while the worker
   lives the orchestrator isn't the pid's parent yet. Discarding would
   drop it permanently, so when the worker exits and the orphan reparents
   it's no longer on the allowlist and nothing ever waits it. The arm
   instead disambiguates with `_pid_still_exists(pid)` (a `/proc`
   existence check kept in its own function so `_zombie_reaper`'s own
   source never mentions `/proc`): alive → retain and retry; gone →
   discard. Retention is bounded by `_ECHILD_RETRY_MAX_SEC` (60s,
   first-ECHILD timestamps in `_REAPABLE_PID_FIRST_ECHILD`), safe
   only because `_DescendantTracker._poll_loop` re-marks every observed
   descendant every `_DESCENDANT_POLL_SEC` (0.5s), so an aged-out pid is
   re-added with a fresh window (both constants pinned together in
   `tests/test_subreaper.py`). Any other `OSError` discards immediately.

   `_mark_reapable(pids)` populates that set (minus
   `_ASYNCIO_MANAGED_PIDS`), fed from `_DescendantTracker._poll_loop`'s
   `_enumerate_descendants` snapshots — subtrees leerie observed and
   therefore owns. `_orphan_zombie_children()` **no longer exists**: any
   reaper that *discovers* PIDs is wrong, because a PID between `fork()`
   and asyncio's `os.pidfd_open()` is in no registry (DESIGN §6 *Zombie
   reaping*; the scanning design once killed `preflight`'s own `git
   config` PID on 40/40 real runs, fabricating rc=255). `_signal_pids`
   deliberately does not `waitpid` — `_zombie_reaper` is the single
   reaping point. `_reparented_orphans` accepts `ppid in (1,
   os.getpid())` since orphans now reparent to the orchestrator.

**PID-exhaustion detection (`_cgroup_stat` + `_read_stream` probe).** The
above runs at worker *exit*; leaked `run_in_background` subprocesses
accumulate against the worker cgroup's `pids.max` (default
`worker_pids_max = 2048`, resolved `--worker-pids-max` >
`LEERIE_WORKER_PIDS_MAX` > `DEFAULT_CAPS`) *during* the
run. Once hit, every `fork()` in the subtree returns `EAGAIN`, so every
`Bash` tool-call fails and the worker spirals without diagnosing the cause
(DESIGN §6 *Detecting PID exhaustion*). The broker's read-only `stat <sid>`
verb → `OK <pids.current> <pids.max> <pids.events.max>
<memory.events.oom_kill>`; client `_cgroup_stat(sid) ->
tuple[int,int,int,int] | None`. `_read_stream` keeps a bounded
`deque(maxlen=_PID_EXHAUSTION_WINDOW)` of recent tool-result outcomes via
`_tool_result_outcome(event)` (non-tool-result events return `None`, not
counted). When the window holds `≥_PID_EXHAUSTION_ERROR_THRESHOLD` (3)
errors **and the latest result is itself an error** (so a healthy-but-failing
worker's interleaved successes don't re-trigger the probe), it calls
`_cgroup_stat`; if `current >= max` or `pids.events.max` is climbing it
logs the cause, relabels the tool-fail summary, and raises `WorkerError`
routed through `_terminate_proc_tree` + tracker-reap to the callers'
normal handling (implementer → retryable `incomplete-handoff`; conformer →
advisory `None`). `_is_fork_exhaustion(text)` is a cheap `EAGAIN`-string
fast-path; the cgroup probe is authoritative. A window (not a consecutive
counter) is required because tool-results are never adjacent — the
model's assistant turn always sits between them.

**Memory-OOM naming (`_invoke`'s no-envelope path + `_settle_subtask`,
DESIGN §6 *Detecting memory OOM*).** A command that overshoots `memory.max`
is killed with a bare `Killed` — no tool-result error, often no `result`
event before `claude -p` is reaped. `_read_stream` tracks `last_bash_cmd`
(the most recent `Bash` command, first line) alongside the PID-exhaustion
window. In `_invoke`'s `finally`, `final_stat = _cgroup_stat(cgroup_sid)`
is read immediately before `_cgroup_destroy` (the last point a read is
possible). When `envelope is None` and `final_stat[3]` (`oom_kill`) is `>
0`, `_invoke` raises `WorkerError(f"worker {sid} was OOM-killed on
\`{last_bash_cmd}\` (memory.max={cap} GiB) — raise --worker-memory-max or
lower --max-parallel")` instead of the generic message.
`_run_implementer`'s `except WorkerError` threads that text into the
synthesized `incomplete-handoff` envelope's `summary` unchanged.
`_settle_subtask`'s `empty_handoff` handling (rescue and no-commits
branches alike) prefers `res.get("summary")` — the worker's own
diagnostic — over `_validate_result`'s generic message, so a named OOM
survives even when the subtask ultimately terminates via the retry cap.

### Abnormal exit and rate-limit contract (DESIGN §6 *Cleanup on abnormal exit*)

All abnormal exits — Ctrl-C, SIGTERM/SIGHUP, WorkerError, unhandled
exception, or `RateLimitedExit` — route through
`_cleanup_on_abnormal_exit(st, full_purge=False)`. **State.json, the
run branch, per-subtask branches, and implementer checkpoints all
survive**; only worktrees are removed (and re-created idempotently on
`resume` via `scripts/new-worktree.sh`).

Worktree removal has a 240s timeout **shared across the whole loop**, not
re-granted per entry: a single deadline is computed once at loop entry
(`time.monotonic() + 240`), and each `git worktree remove` call gets
whatever budget remains until that deadline (a large worktree can be
hundreds of MB / tens of thousands of files under N-way concurrent disk
contention). Once the shared budget is exhausted, remaining entries skip
the `git worktree remove` call and go straight to the `rm -rf` fallback —
worktrees under one run typically share the same underlying stall (all
removed from the same bind-mounted `.git`), so a fixed *per-entry* 240s
would let one stall cost 240s times the worktree count. Failures are
non-fatal and counted; if any failed, cleanup logs a pointer to
`scripts/cleanup.sh --run-id <id>` to finish manually — best-effort, a
stale worktree is the worst case, not a corrupted run.

Per-worker `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` from `_invoke` (`worker_timeout_sec`,
default 5400s/90min) is caught by both `_run_implementer` (returns an
`incomplete-handoff` envelope, same path as WorkerError) and
`_run_conformer` (logs + returns `None`). Without these catches the
timeout escapes through asyncio cancellation into `main()`'s catch-all and
dumps a multi-KB traceback — including the full `claude -p` command line
— to the terminal.

`RateLimitedExit` is raised by `_detect_session_limit(text)` inside
`_summarize_stream_event` on the verbatim Claude Code subscription message
`"You've hit your session limit · resets <h>:<mm><am|pm> (<IANA TZ>)"`, or
by the same function's `rate_limit_event` branch when the protocol-level
`status` falls outside `{"allowed", "allowed_warning"}` — matching
everything-not-allowed avoids hardcoding a terminal-status guess that
could go stale. The protocol path parses `resetsAt` (Unix timestamp) into
a UTC `reset_at`; the text path parses wall-clock + IANA tz. A **third**
raise site is the `_invoke` no-result-envelope branch: when a stream
truncates with no `result` event *and* a mid-stream `rate_limit_event`
shows `overageDisabledReason in {"out_of_credits", "out_of_overage"}`
(latched via `nonlocal overage_blocked`), `_invoke` raises
`RateLimitedExit(reset_at=None, out_of_credits=True, raw)` — raised here,
not in `_summarize_stream_event`, so the latch survives to the post-stream
check even at quiet verbosity. The latch keys on `overageDisabledReason`,
**not** `overageStatus == "rejected"` (a standing, non-exhaustion state for
orgs with overage disabled) — keying on the latter misclassified unrelated
truncations. An `org_level_disabled` truncation takes the ordinary
`WorkerError` path.

Either source produces a `reset_at: datetime | None` (parse failure →
`None`, never a wrong-time guess). `main()`'s `except RateLimitedExit`:
when `reset_at` is set, cleanup → sleep until the moment + 30s margin →
`os.execv(sys.executable, [sys.executable, __file__, "resume", "--run-id",
<id>])` to re-exec the orchestrator itself (not the launcher, which isn't
baked into the image). `worker_count` persists across the re-exec, so a
repeatedly-limited run still respects `--max-workers`. When `reset_at` is
`None` (unparseable message), sleep a fixed `RATE_LIMIT_RETRY_BACKOFF_SEC`
(300s) and re-exec the same way. **Ceiling:** if the computed
`wait_seconds` exceeds the resolved `max_rate_limit_wait_sec` cap (default
6h; `--max-rate-limit-wait` > `LEERIE_MAX_RATE_LIMIT_WAIT` >
`max_rate_limit_wait_sec` in leerie.toml > `DEFAULT_CAPS`, via
`resolve_max_rate_limit_wait_sec`), neither arm sleeps —
`main()` takes the `out_of_credits` disposition instead (worktree-only
cleanup, best-effort `dep_capture`, resume hint, `EXIT_LOCKED`), because a
weekly-limit reset can be days out and sleeping holds the run-directory
flock. Keyed on the computed wait, never on `RateLimitedExit.limit_type`
(carried from the `rate_limit_event`'s `rateLimitType` and used only in the
pause message), so a renamed limit type cannot silently disable it. Both clock-based arms route through
`_sleep_then_reexec(st, wait_seconds, reason) -> int | None`: `None` when
`os.execv` succeeds (return unreachable), else an exit code — `130`
(Ctrl-C), `128 + signum` (SIGTERM/SIGHUP), `EXIT_LOCKED` (75, the
should-never-happen `os.execv` failure). The caller sets `abnormal = False`
(the helper already ran cleanup).

The `out_of_credits=True` arm does **not** auto-resume — no reset clock
(clears only on top-up/billing cycle). `main()` runs
`_cleanup_on_abnormal_exit` directly, logs a `leerie resume <id>` hint,
sets `exit_code = EXIT_LOCKED`, `abnormal = False`. Checked *before* the
`reset_at` branch; `_sleep_then_reexec` never called here. Out-of-credits
deliberately keeps the surface-and-pause semantics rate-limits no longer
use.

A terminal auth failure (`_is_terminal_auth_failure`, §3) copies this arm
verbatim — an expired session has no clock-based reset either.

**Auto-resume override persistence.** The re-exec passes only `resume
<id>` as argv. Every sticky choice of the original launch (`--model`,
`--max-workers`, `--confidence-rounds`, `--source-of-truth`, `--clarify`,
`--no-push`, the skip flags) is recorded in `state.json` and continued, so
it survives the auto-resume (§2½ *Run choices on resume*). Per-invocation
choices (`--max-parallel`, the worker ceilings, `--verbosity`) fall back to
`LEERIE_*` env vars and `leerie.toml`, as on any resume.

Ctrl-C (SIGINT) is **resumable** — same contract as every other abnormal
exit. The explicit "throw this away" gesture is `scripts/cleanup.sh
--run-id <id> --branches`, not Ctrl-C.

---

## 5½. Mechanical-feedback loops (CRITIC pattern)

Every worker except the PR writer runs inside `_run_checked_loop` — a
generic async function that calls the worker, runs deterministic
structural checks on the output, and, for callers that pass
`make_feedback_prompt`, re-invokes with formatted feedback if issues
are found. The pattern is grounded in the CRITIC framework (ICLR 2024):
self-correction works only with external tool-verified feedback, not
intrinsic self-review.

Three callers — `wiring_judge`, `provision_judge`, and `integration_judge`
— are single-pass judges: they pass no `make_feedback_prompt`, because
re-asking the judge cannot act on its own finding. (What happens to a
finding is the caller's: `phase_wiring_gate` repairs the plan's edges,
`_run_integration_judge_gate` re-drives the integrator and re-judges in a
fresh call — DESIGN §5, §6.) A round
that finds issues stops the loop immediately — a further round would
attack the identical input with only a fresh, non-deterministic judge
session, which can only *lose* the finding on a lucky re-roll, never gain
information. The oscillation guard below doesn't apply here (no re-drive
between rounds). The `WorkerError` infrastructure-crash retry is
orthogonal and still applies to all callers regardless of
`make_feedback_prompt`.

### Core functions

| Function | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `_replan_domain_closure(plans, targets)` | Domains that must re-plan together with `targets` — the transitive closure across both the id (`depends_on`) and tag (`requires`→`provides`) channels, so a re-plan vanishing every id a domain used never dangles a still-live edge into it. Domains are subtask-id prefixes. Consumed by `phase_overlap_judge`'s unresolvable recovery; `phase_plan(..., domains=…)` takes the result. Pinned by `tests/test_scoped_replan.py`. |
| `_full_suite_rule_patterns(repo_root, prescribed)` | The ONE whole-suite rule list (DESIGN §9 *The whole suite is orchestrator-owned*) that the deny, the strip and the settle-time exemption all read. For each runner spelling R from `_full_suite_runners(_canonical_test_command(repo_root))` — the canonical `test` command (with `resolve_blt`'s precedence, re-implemented without its log line); for a pytest canonical also `pytest` / `python3 -m pytest` / `python -m pytest`; for an npm-family `X test` / `X run test` both; a canonical containing `,()&|;<>`$*` (`*` because the CLI would read it as a wildcard) or empty yields none — and each of the first `_SUITE_MAX_ROOTS` (16) test roots T — a bound that keeps the joined rules far below Linux's per-argument `MAX_ARG_STRLEN`, which ~165 roots would exceed and fail every spawn — (`_test_roots(repo_root)`: pytest `testpaths` from `pytest.ini`/`tox.ini`/`setup.cfg`, read with interpolation off and UTF-8, a read/decode error skipping that file and a root containing `,`/`(`/`)`/`*` dropped; else `tests` when that directory exists; `pyproject.toml` is not read), returns `R`, `R T`, `R T/`, `R T *`, `R T/ *`, `R * T`, `R * T/`. Returns `[]` when a `_prescribed_commands(prescribed)` entry (the whitespace-normalised `commands`, empty unless `is_prescribed` and `commands` is a list) is itself a whole-suite run by the ANCHORED match (`_denied_by_full_suite_rules(..., anchored=True)`) — the user's instruction outranks the default: no deny, strip, exemption or notice for that run. Total: any exception → `[]` plus one `_warn_full_suite_deny_skipped_once` warning, because it runs inside every `claude_p` call against the target repo's files. |
| `_full_suite_denials(repo_root, prescribed=None)` | `_full_suite_rule_patterns` as comma-joined `Bash(...)` rules; `""` when the list is empty. Joined into `claude_p`'s `deny_extra` for every worker `claude_p` spawns, and into the Fly remote integrator's `--disallowedTools` through `_worker_guard` / `scripts/worker-guard.py`; the preflight smoke test (no `deny_extra`) carries neither the deny nor the notice. Probed live (claude 2.1.310 host, 2.1.302 image, `--dangerously-skip-permissions`): `timeout`-wrapped, piped, redirected, `cd … &&` and `-k`/`-m`-filtered runs aimed at a test root are denied; file-targeted runs, loops over files and a flags-only bare runner run. |
| `_denied_by_full_suite_rules(cmd, patterns, *, anchored=False)` / `_shell_subcommands(cmd)` / `_strip_command_prefixes(seg)` / `_rule_matches(text, pattern)` | Whether the rule list refuses `cmd`. `_shell_subcommands` splits it the way the CLI does, with a quote-aware scan (not a regex): single quotes are wholly literal; double quotes are literal except a backslash escape and a command substitution; a substitution (`$(…)` or backticks, quoted or not) becomes a subcommand of its own while the command around it stays whole with a `$_` word in its place; outside quotes the boundaries are `;`, `\|`, `&` (so `&&`/`\|\|`), newline, a subshell's `(`/`)`, and `{`/`}` only as group words, with whitespace or the string's edge on both sides (brace expansion such as `tests/{a,b}.py` stays in its word); a backslash escapes the next character (so a backslash-newline continues the line); redirections outside quotes (`> f`, `2>&1`, `<in`, `> "a b"`, glued or spaced) are dropped with their target unless the target holds a substitution, which is scanned; a here-document operator (`<<word`, `<<-word`, never `<<<`) is recognised only in plain command context — not after an unquoted word-initial `#` on its line, and not inside an unquoted `${…}`, `$[…]`, `$((…))` or `((…))` (tracked by bracket depth; `<`/`>` there are operators, not redirects) — and only with a delimiter that is a plain unquoted word or one wholly in `'…'` or `"…"`, holding no `$`, backquote or backslash (quoted when quoted); the operator and delimiter are then dropped, and at the next unquoted newline the pending bodies — each its lines up to the one equal to its delimiter, leading tabs stripped for `<<-` — are consumed only when every terminating line is present (otherwise the text is scanned as commands, as a `<<` that is not a here-document always is); an unquoted delimiter's body is passed to `_heredoc_substitutions(body) -> list[str]`, which is `_shell_subcommands(body, heredoc_body=True)`: at the body's top level only a backslash escape, `$(` and a backquote are read and all other text is dropped, and each substitution is scanned as commands (quote-aware), its subcommands appended after the command's own; inside any substitution, while a `case` clause (a subcommand whose first word is `case`, until one whose first word is `esac`) is open, a `)` ends a pattern rather than the substitution; differential test against `bash -c`: `tests/test_heredoc_scan_agrees_with_bash.py`; an unclosed substitution still contributes its outer command; whitespace inside quotes is kept as `_QUOTED_SPACE` (`\x00`) so a quoted argument stays one word — unless the scan ends inside an unbalanced quote (an apostrophe in a comment it does not model), where it falls back to plain spaces — and is collapsed per subcommand. Each subcommand is then glob-matched by `_rule_matches` (`*` = any text; a sole trailing ` *` also matches the bare command). Unanchored (strip, settle exemption): every word-suffix is tried, with `_QUOTED_SPACE` turned back into a space so a quoted paraphrase (`Run "pytest tests/" to verify`) still counts, which subsumes the CLI's prefix stripping and also catches a paraphrase ("run pytest tests/ to verify") — over-matching only drops a declared requirement. Anchored (the prescribed check): quoted text stays one word (the CLI ran `"pytest tests/"`), and only the subcommand after `_strip_command_prefixes` — repeatedly removing `_SUITE_WRAPPER_RE` (`env` with `-u NAME`/`--unset NAME`/flags, `timeout` with option arguments, `time [-p]`, `nice [-n N \| -N]`, `nohup`, `stdbuf`, `command`, `builtin`, `noglob`, `exec`, `sudo [-flags]`, `xargs [-flags]`, `then`, `do`, `else`, `!`) and `_SUITE_ASSIGN_RE` (`NAME=value`, a quoted value included) — so `pip install pytest` is not a suite run. Agreement with the CLI is pinned per shape by `tests/test_full_suite_ownership.py::LIVE_PROBED`. |
| `_strip_canonical_suite_commands(plans, repo_root, prescribed)` | Plan repair: removes each `runs_commands` entry `_denied_by_full_suite_rules` refuses, except a `_prescribed_commands` entry, which is never stripped (if the two match modes disagree about it, the worker ends `blocked` loudly instead of the instruction vanishing). Skips non-dict plans and subtasks. Returns the affected sids; mutates in place; never raises. Called in `_run_phases` before the `plan_snapshot` branch — so it runs on a fresh plan and on one reloaded from `plans_after_filters` alike, and a wiring-gate repair that re-schedules on resume re-schedules the stripped plan — logged per sid, and — only when the strip itself uncovered a prescribed command (`check_prescribed_command_coverage`'s uncovered set grew across it) — followed there by `_repair_prescribed_commands(plans, prescribed, reserved_ids=<dropped_subtasks keys>)`: a stripped planner paraphrase of a prescribed command (which the adherence floor had accepted as coverage) makes the floor fail again, and the repair synthesises a subtask carrying the exact, immune commands. |
| settle-time exemption (in `_settle_subtask`) | Before `check_declared_commands_executed`, entries `_denied_by_full_suite_rules` refuses — other than `_prescribed_commands` entries — are dropped from the subtask's `runs_commands` (a copy; the spec on disk is untouched). This is the choke point: it covers specs written before the strip existed (a run resumed past `plan_snapshot`) and anything the strip did not see. |
| `FULL_SUITE_NOTICE` / `_full_suite_notice(repo_root, prescribed)` / `_tools_reach_suite_runner(allowed_tools, repo_root, prescribed)` | `claude_p` computes the deny once and, when it is non-empty and the worker's `allowed_tools` can reach the runner (bare `Bash`, or a `Bash(<runner>…)` grant such as a `_widen_inspect_tools` verb), appends `NOTE FROM ORCHESTRATOR: <FULL_SUITE_NOTICE>` to the user prompt — so implementer, conformer (per-subtask and final), integrator, rebaser and acceptance_writer get it; an inspect-only judgment worker does not, unless `--dangerously-skip-permissions` widened its allowlist with the runner's verb (`_widen_inspect_tools`), in which case it does. The text: the suite is run by the orchestrator on the integrated tree once every wave has merged and is denied to you; record whole-suite criteria `met: false, not_applicable: true` with evidence "orchestrator's whole-tree pass owns this"; use targeted files. Never `None` while a deny is in force (a read error degrades only the named command). Required alongside the deny — replayed against the incident spec, deny alone ended 2/2 workers `blocked`, deny + notice completed 5/5. |
| `_db_reset_rule_patterns(repo_root)` / `_db_reset_denials(repo_root)` / `DB_RESET_NOTICE` | In a Prisma repo (`_prisma_project`, any provider), the bodies `*prisma db push*`, `*prisma migrate reset*`, `*prisma migrate dev*`, `*PRISMA_USER_CONSENT_FOR_DANGEROUS_AI_ACTION*`, and for each package.json script of the Prisma package whose body runs one of those commands (`_prisma_reset_scripts`; names with `,()* ` skipped) `*<pm> <name>*` for `npm run`, `pnpm run`, `pnpm`, `yarn run`, `yarn`, `bun run`, `bun`; `[]` otherwise or on any error (total, like the whole-suite list). `_db_reset_denials` joins them as `Bash(...)` rules into every `claude_p` call's `deny_extra`; when it is non-empty and the worker's `allowed_tools` include bare `Bash`, `claude_p` appends `NOTE FROM ORCHESTRATOR: <DB_RESET_NOTICE>` to the user prompt (DESIGN §8 *Prisma repositories get a real database*; #292's deny-plus-notice pairing). |
| `_worker_guard(allowed_tools, repo_root, state_data, *, worker=None) -> {deny, notices, settings, env}` | The per-worker guard layers, built once for both callers: `claude_p` (`worker=schema_key`) and the Fly remote integrator (`scripts/worker-guard.py`, `worker="integrator"`, printing them as shell assignments). It reads the typed `_forbidden_specs(state_data)`, so each entry's scope (`any` / `whole_suite`) reaches the rules, notice and hook. A `worker` in `NOTICE_FREE_WORKERS` gets `notices == []` and every other layer unchanged. `deny` — the comma-joined whole-suite, database push/reset, forbidden-command and process-kill rules, in that order; `notices` — the whole-suite (when the tools reach the runner and the task does not forbid the canonical test command), forbidden-command, `PROCESS_KILL_NOTICE` (tools reach bare `Bash`) and `DB_RESET_NOTICE` (bare `Bash`) texts, in that order; `settings` — `_forbidden_command_hook_settings`; `env` — `_forbidden_script_shell_env`. `claude_p` lays `env` under its caller's `env_extra`, appends each notice as `NOTE FROM ORCHESTRATOR: <text>`, and joins `deny` after its own repo-write, acceptance-read and system-prompt-read rules. |
| `_repair_missing_requires(plans, defects, warnings=None)` / `_repair_wiring_channels(plans, defects)` / `_fanin_and_fallback(plans, residual)` | The wiring gate's plan repair (DESIGN §5). The tag / id / single-cluster channels first (`_repair_wiring_channels`, returning `(repairs_applied, residual)`), unchanged; the residual then goes through `_fanin_and_fallback`: an in-plan `requires` on a tag with ≥1 other provider (`channel: "fanin"`, `providers`), else — when that would cycle, or the value is a surviving id refused for a cycle — a `depends_on` per provider in sorted order skipping any whose edge would cycle (`channel: "depends_on_fallback"`, `deps_added`, `skipped_cyclic`). Every trial is `_would_cycle_after`, cumulative. No provider, every provider a descendant, or `missing_provides` → a typed warning `{sid, value, kind, why}` appended to `warnings` (`why` ∈ `no_in_plan_provider`, `every_provider_is_a_descendant`, `missing_provides_not_an_edge`). Unrepaired is only a defect whose sid is not in the plan — the gate's sole `die()`. |
| `_serialize_planned_overlap(subtasks, waves, cap)` / `_overlap_first_fit(wave, pairs)` | `_schedule`'s planned-overlap serialisation (DESIGN §5): returns `(waves, serialised_pairs)`; see `overlap_extra_waves`. |
| `_json_key_merge3(base, ours, theirs)` / `_try_json_key_merge(staging, sid)` | The key-level JSON merge at integration (DESIGN §6 *A conflict confined to JSON files is merged by key*). `integrate_wave` calls `_try_json_key_merge` when `integrate.sh` exits 1, before any integrator: only when every conflicted file (`git diff --diff-filter=U`) is `.json`, each stage parses (`:1:` absent → `{}`), and `_json_key_merge3` reports no key conflict, each file's ours side has a faithful renderer (`_json_faithful_renderer(text)`: the `json.dumps` indent — detected, 2, 4 or tab — and `ensure_ascii` setting, plus final newline, that reproduces `text` byte for byte from its parsed value; None otherwise, and the merge is refused), the merged files are written with it, added (`git --literal-pathspecs add -- <files>`) and committed with the merge's own message. Any refusal leaves the merge exactly as git left it (`git --literal-pathspecs checkout -m -- <files>` after a failed commit). No integration judge runs on a key merge. |
| `_integration_dropped_lines(cwd, p1, p2, head, cap=80)` | S3 dropped lines: `{lines: [{file, side, line}], total, excluded_rewritten}` (DESIGN §6). Files both parents changed vs `merge-base(p1, p2)`; added lines stripped, ≥ `_INTEGRATION_LINE_MIN` (8) characters, absent from `head`'s copy; excluded only when the other side's own diff has that exact line as a `-` line. `line` is cut to 200 characters. |
| `_integration_test_failures(st, sid, staging, p1, p2, merge_sha, caps, *, log_path, parent_cache)` / `_conflicted_area_tests(tree, files, globs)` | The conflicted area's tests (DESIGN §6): test files among the files changed `p1..HEAD` plus one-hop importers (`git grep -E` on the module name), run through `_capture_failing_test_ids` (serial, with the command `_acceptance_cmd` renders over the files present in each tree — never the raw test command; a tree whose files render no scoped command gives no IDs; skipped with a logged reason when there is no test command, no test in scope, no scoped runner, or the task forbids the scoped command) on `p1`, `p2` (fresh `worktrees/integ-<sid>-<side>` trees with deps, IDs cached per round scope) and HEAD. Candidate = failing on HEAD and on no parent that ran it; confirmed by `_confirm_new_failures` against the parent it passed on, or `_confirm_still_failing` (every candidate in `needs_rerun`) when no parent has its file. A candidate either confirm leaves `budget_short_unsettled` is listed in `budget_short_unsettled` on the result, never a `test_failure` or `stale`. A confirmed ID is `stale_by_other_side {test_id, home_side, other_side}` when `_confirm_still_failing` also confirms it on the home parent's tree overlaid with the other side's non-test changed files (`_overlay_other_side`), else a `test_failure`. |
| `_incoming_subtask_view(leerie_dir, sid, result)` / `_wave_sids_integrated_before(staging, run_id, sids, rev)` | The integration gate's inputs on every path, resume included: intent and criteria from `subtasks/<sid>.json` when the settle result lacks them; the wave's sids a prior invocation already merged (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` of each `leerie/subtasks/<run-id>/<sid>` branch), seeding `integrated_so_far`. |
| `_repair_prescribed_commands(plans, prescribed, reserved_ids=frozenset())` | Mechanical plan repair for the adherence floor (called by the adherence gate, and again after the whole-suite strip when that strip uncovered a prescribed command; `reserved_ids` — the run's `dropped_subtasks` keys there — are never minted) (DESIGN §8 *Repairing an omitted self-report beats re-driving for it*). Synthesises one subtask carrying every prescribed command, `depends_on` = the plan's current sinks, returns its id — or `None` when the floor is clean, there are no commands, or no plan supplies a valid id prefix. Mutates `plans` in place; never raises; declines rather than guessing (mirrors `_repair_missing_requires`). Called before `check_prescribed_command_coverage` so a repairable gap never reaches the ~125-spawn re-plan path. Deliberately doesn't attach to an existing subtask (a verification-shaped matcher hits 32/36 subtasks on the real incident plan). Pinned by `tests/test_prescribed_command_repair.py`. |
| `check_replan_affordable(st, caps, gate, plans)` | Budget preflight before a re-plan (DESIGN §13) — a re-plan re-runs the whole P1 decomposition and was previously authorised unchecked. Estimates `n_domains × planner_samples + n_subtasks × replan_decompose_estimate` from the **plans the caller passes in** (not `plan_snapshot`, written only after `_schedule()`). `die()`s with `EXIT_BUDGET_INFEASIBLE` when it exceeds what's left.
