Called at the top of the re-planning `_on_feedback` callback in `phase_adherence_gate`, and in `phase_overlap_judge` before `phase_plan`. Honours `skip_budget_check`. Pinned by `tests/test_replan_budget_preflight.py`. |
| `_run_checked_loop(invoke, check, name, max_rounds, make_feedback_prompt)` | Generic loop: call → check → feedback → retry. Returns `(result, warnings)`. Re-invokes on **gating** findings only (see below). Oscillation guard aborts only when a round's issue-signature set is EXACTLY EQUAL to an earlier round's — a proper subset (genuine partial progress) keeps retrying (DESIGN §8). |
| `_partition_issues_by_severity(issues)` | Splits into `(gating, advisory)`, order preserved. Used by `_run_checked_loop` and `_select_best_planner_sample`. |
| `_issue_is_advisory(issue)` | True when the `LABEL` prefix is in `_ADVISORY_ISSUE_LABELS`. Unknown labels/non-strings are gating. |
| `_confidence_axes_clear(conf, axes, threshold)` | Pure predicate: True when every named axis is a number ≥ threshold. Used by the loop and `_settle_subtask`'s implementer confidence check. |
| `_format_check_feedback(issues, rnd, max_rounds)` | Formats issues into the structured feedback block injected on re-invocation. |
| `_confidence_schema(axes)` | DRY helper building the §8 confidence sub-schema. Used by 10 worker schemas (`classifier`, `planner`, `reconciler`, `implementer`, `integrator`, `rebaser`, `conformer`, `provision`, `plan_overlap_judge`, `fit_judge` — not `splitter`, whose output carries no confidence axis). Shape: `required: [*axes, "basis"]`; `falsifiers_tested`/`contradictions_reconciled` optional; no `gap_to_close` field, no `maxLength` caps (both removed as a decoder-corruption mitigation, `anthropics/claude-code#49747`; DESIGN §8). `confidence` is **not** in any of these schemas' top-level `required` — a worker omitting it still validates. Pinned by `tests/test_confidence_not_required.py`; `tests/test_confidence_length_caps.py` covers callers that do emit it. |
| `_subtask_item_schema(*, include_requires, include_migration_targets, include_runs_commands, include_fixes_reported_symptom, include_change_shape, include_verify, include_verification_only, include_claims)` | DRY helper (same pattern as `_confidence_schema`) building the child-subtask item schema shared by `SCHEMAS["planner"]["subtasks"]`, `SCHEMAS["reconciler"]["added_subtasks"]`, `SCHEMAS["splitter"]["children"]` — previously three independently-written literals. Each call site passes its own `include_*` set (`reconciler.added_subtasks` narrowest — no `requires`/`migration_targets`/`runs_commands`/`fixes_reported_symptom`; `splitter.children` — `requires` and `verify`; `planner.subtasks` — all five, `change_shape` among them) rather than converging on one shape, so a future field change is explicit about which sites it reaches. Pinned by `tests/test_shared_subtask_item_schema.py`, including an anti-vacuity check that narrower sites reject the wider ones' fields. |

### Finding severity — gating vs advisory

`_run_checked_loop` partitions each round's findings via
`_partition_issues_by_severity(issues) -> (gating, advisory)` and re-invokes
**only on gating findings**. Advisory findings go to `warnings` (never
hidden) and are logged once, but never consume a round, enter
`_format_check_feedback`, or enter the oscillation guard's signature set.
`_select_best_planner_sample` likewise ranks on the gating subset only.

`_issue_is_advisory(issue)` keys on the mechanical `LABEL` prefix (the same
one `_issue_signature` parses, generated by leerie's own check functions,
not LLM prose — not the natural-language parsing CLAUDE.md forbids). A
`LABEL (subtype):` parenthetical is stripped before lookup.

`_ADVISORY_ISSUE_LABELS` is a **frozenset allowlist**, so the default is
**gating**: an unclassified finding cannot silently disarm a real gate.

| Advisory label | Why it is advice, not a defect |
|---|---|
| `INTRA_DOMAIN_OVERLAP` | Its own text is "consider merging or splitting" — two subtasks touching one file is frequently legitimate (measured 43 → 12 → 6 across both 2026-08-03 runs, never zero). |
| `PHANTOM_PATH` | Fires when no ancestor dir exists for a planned path — exactly what a subtask that *creates* a new module looks like; the dominant driver of the issue-count/plan-size coupling. |
| `OVERSIZED` | Grades a planner self-report, but `fit_judge` in `_recursive_decompose` is the authoritative decomposition gate (DESIGN §5½, §8). |
| `MANY_CATEGORIES` | "typical tasks span 1–3" is a heuristic, not a correctness property. |
| `SAME_WORK_RISK`, `TEST_OWNERSHIP_RISK` | Both end by telling the classifier to apply judgement and keep both categories if deliverables genuinely differ — a remedy that may be "change nothing" cannot gate. |

Everything else — `DANGLING_DEP`, `INTRA_DOMAIN_CYCLE`, `EMPTY_CRITERIA`,
`PROTECTED_PATH`, `MIGRATION_TARGETS_MISSING`, `UNCOVERED_MIGRATION_SURFACE`,
`PRESCRIBED_CMD_UNRUN`, `REQUIRED_ITEM_UNCOVERED`, and every other worker's
codes — remains gating.

Pinned by `tests/test_issue_severity.py`; its most important test is
`test_unknown_labels_default_to_gating` — if that default ever inverts,
every future check silently stops gating until reclassified.

### Per-worker mechanical checks

Each returns `list[str]` — empty when clean. Pure Python, no LLM. Severity
is resolved from the issue code per the table above, not the function.

| Worker | Check function | Issue codes | Max rounds cap |
|--------|---------------|-------------|----------------|
| Classifier | `check_classifier_output(result, repo_root, judge_confirmed=frozenset())` | `CATEGORY_NO_DIR`, `EMPTY_WHY`, `EMPTY_EVIDENCE`, `MANY_CATEGORIES`, `SAME_WORK_RISK`, `TEST_OWNERSHIP_RISK` | `judgment_check_rounds` (3) |
| Classifier (requirement coverage, chained after the row above in `phase_classify`'s check) | `_d1_coverage_holes(result, units, ask_report=True)` | `D1_UNDISPOSED`, `D1_UNROLED`, `D1_UNCOVERED`, `D1_DUPLICATE`, `D1_MISANCHORED`, `D1_BAD_KIND`, `D1_BAD_RESTATES`, `D1_BAD_SUPPORTS`, `D1_RESTATES_ANCESTOR`, `D1_BAD_TABLE_ROW`, `D1_REPORT_WITHOUT_REQUIREMENT` (the last only on the first check of a `phase_classify` call — `ask_report` — so it is asked once) | `judgment_check_rounds` (3) |

An issue in any of these tables **gates** — costing a round and re-driving the worker — unless its label is listed in `_ADVISORY_ISSUE_LABELS`, which is the authority; `_partition_issues_by_severity` splits on it. Read that set rather than a per-row annotation here, which would be a copy of a derived fact. Worth knowing for `CATEGORY_NO_DIR` in particular: it gates, while the two RISK advisories beside it in the `judge_confirmed` suppression do not.
| Planner | `check_planner_output(result, repo_root, domain)` | `PHANTOM_PATH`, `DANGLING_DEP`, `EMPTY_CRITERIA`, `OVERSIZED`, `INTRA_DOMAIN_OVERLAP`, `PROTECTED_PATH`, `INTRA_DOMAIN_CYCLE`, `UNCOVERED_MIGRATION_SURFACE`, `MIGRATION_TARGETS_MISSING` | `planner_check_rounds` (3) |
| Reconciler | `check_reconciler_output(output, plans)` | `RENAME_TO_NOWHERE`, `BAD_PREFIX`, `SELF_DEP` | `judgment_check_rounds` (3) |
| Overlap judge | `check_overlap_judge_output(output, plans, repo_root)` | `PHANTOM_ARTIFACT`, `NO_FILE_OVERLAP`, `DROP_BREAKS_GRAPH`, `DUPLICATE_PAIR` | `judgment_check_rounds` (3) |
| Adherence gate | `check_prescribed_command_coverage(prescribed_procedure, subtasks)` (deterministic floor) + inline `LOW_ADHERENCE` check on the `adherence_judge` result | `PRESCRIBED_CMD_UNRUN`, `LOW_ADHERENCE` | `judgment_check_rounds` (3) |
| Provision | `check_provision_output(result, repo_root)` | `WRONG_PM`, `MISSING_WORKDIR`, `EMPTY_RECIPE` | `judgment_check_rounds` (3) |
| Implementer | `check_implementer_output(result, subtask, actual_files)` | `NO_PLANNED_FILES_TOUCHED` (advisory — excluded from retry by `_gating_issues`), `UNMET_CRITERION`, `OWNED_REGION_FILE_ESCAPE` (gating; sub-file region children only), plus `check_production_evidence`'s four (below) | `implementer_confidence_retries` (2) |
| Integrator | `check_integrator_output(result)` | — | `judgment_check_rounds` (3) |
| Conformer | (`_conformance_clean` on observable signals) | — | `conformance_rounds` (3) |

**`UNMET_CRITERION` must not fire on a criterion the implementer was never
responsible for.** A criterion naming the build is a *conformance-phase*
signal — the conformer runs the build, and one inside a worker's turn
budget can OOM the container and get it reaped mid-turn. With only
`{criterion, met, evidence}` on the schema, an obedient implementer had no
way to say so and every such report became a re-drive.

`SCHEMAS["implementer"]`'s `criteria_results` items therefore carry an optional
`not_applicable` bool, and `check_implementer_output` skips any criterion where
it `is True` (identity, not truthiness) before testing `met`.

**One channel, deliberately.** A second briefly existed —
`_criterion_is_conformance_owned`, substring-matching the repo's resolved
build/lint/test commands inside the criterion text — as a backstop for a worker
that forgot the flag. It is deleted, along with `check_implementer_output`'s
`blt_commands` parameter. `criterion` is planner-authored prose, and the
*Language-to-JSON* rule forbids Python reading meaning out of prose; the
owning worker surfaces it as a JSON field (`not_applicable`) instead.


`check_production_evidence(result) -> list[str]` (DESIGN §9 *Evidence must be
production-grounded*) reads the `production_evidence` object that
`_production_evidence_schema()` puts on the **implementer** and **conformer**
schemas, and emits `NO_PRODUCTION_EVIDENCE` (field absent or not an object),
`UNSUPPORTED_PRODUCTION_EVIDENCE` (`exercised: true` with neither `how` nor
`observed`), `UNEXERCISED_PRODUCTION_PATH` (`exercised: false` with no
`unexercisable_reason`), or `MALFORMED_PRODUCTION_EVIDENCE` (`exercised` not a
bool). The object's optional `unexercisable_resource` names an external
resource no in-container step can supply; it is not checked here, only
routed (`_typed_risks`, below). It has **three call sites with deliberately different severities**.
From `check_implementer_output`, on the `status == "complete"` branch only (a
blocked implementer has no finished path to exercise), it routes through the
existing bounded `implementer_confidence_retries` retry and so never blocks a
run permanently. From `_settle_subtask`'s conformance block and from
`_run_final_conformance` (the whole-tree pass, run after
`_validate_conformance_result`) it is **advisory** — the output extends
`conf_warnings`/`warnings`, never `blocked_reason` — because `solution_defects`
is deliberately the one gating conformer axis (DESIGN §9) and an advisory phase
must not acquire a second way to stop a run. The conformer's copy is read only
when `conf_res is not None`, since a crashed conformer has no result to inspect.

`check_symptom_evidence(result, sid, fixes_reported_symptom) -> list[str]`
(DESIGN §9 *A stale finding is not a bug*) is its sibling for subtasks whose
plan entry declares `fixes_reported_symptom: true`, reading a
`symptom_evidence` object of the same flat shape on the **implementer** schema
only — the conformer neither wrote the fix nor has a base tree to reproduce
against. It emits `NO_SYMPTOM_EVIDENCE`, `SYMPTOM_DID_NOT_REPRODUCE` (the
useful one — the finding may already be fixed) or `MALFORMED_SYMPTOM_EVIDENCE`.
**Advisory**: the output is logged, attached to the result as
`symptom_warnings`, and persisted to `symptom_findings` in `state.json`
(results are in-memory only); it is *never* routed into
`check_implementer_output`, since a retry cannot make a stale finding
un-stale. Scoped by the planner's **declaration**, never by the subtask's id
(a `bugfix-` id prefix is not evidence a symptom exists — ids are re-homed by
merges — and scoping on it produced false positives across the run corpus;
see tests/test_no_id_prefix_dispatch.py). Takes the **orchestrator's** `sid` rather
than the worker's echoed `result["subtask_id"]`. Pinned by
`tests/test_symptom_evidence.py`.

Two shape decisions are load-bearing. The field is **optional in the schema
and gating in the check**: requiring it costs the entire submission on a miss
(measured 40.9%-valid on `plan_overlap_judge` from exactly this mistake), and
gating on absence is what stops optional from meaning ignorable. The object
is **flat with one required inner field, a bare bool** — `how`/`observed`
strings stay optional, since many required params mixed with verbose strings
triggers anthropics/claude-code#49747's decoder corruption.
`tests/test_production_evidence.py` pins both.

`_collect_subtask_risks(impl_res, conf_res) -> list[dict]`
(DESIGN §9 *Self-reported risk is routed, not read*) is the pure routing
helper beside the two checks above. It folds two typed tiers into risk
entries `{kind, detail, where?, source, disposition?, addressed}`: tier 1 is
`production_evidence.exercised == false` on either result (kind
`unexercised_behavior`, detail = the `unexercisable_reason`); tier 2 is the
implementer's optional `self_reported_risks` array
(`_self_reported_risks_schema()`: max 8 items, each a `$ref` to the
implementer schema's `$defs.risk` = `_risk_item_schema()`: `{kind:
RISK_KINDS, detail, where?, gap: RISK_GAPS, where_paths[] (max 10),
settle_by?: RISK_SETTLE_BY, resource?, simulated_interleaving?}`, `kind`,
`detail`, `gap` and `where_paths` required). `RISK_GAPS = (test_missing,
test_weak, unverified_external, none)`; `RISK_SETTLE_BY = (test, typecheck,
install, build)`; `RISK_KINDS` adds `process_note` to the three register
kinds, and `_typed_risks` drops a `process_note` (and any unknown kind) on
ingestion, so it reaches neither the register nor the conformer's challenge
block. An entry without a valid `gap` (a result from before the field) is
typed `none`; the `exercised: false` tier is typed `gap:
unverified_external` with `resource` = its `production_evidence.unexercisable_resource`
(the optional string `_production_evidence_schema()` adds, on both schemas)
when that is non-empty, else `gap: test_missing` with no resource, always
with `where_paths: []`; a tier-2 entry typed `unverified_external` with no
`resource` is re-typed `test_missing` (DESIGN §9 *Self-reported risk is
routed, not read*: only an entry naming the external resource a human must
supply is external). `_verify_risk_paths(entries,
worktree)` then keeps a `where_paths` entry only when it is a relative path
with no `..` naming a file in the subtask's worktree, moving the rest to
`where_paths_unverified`; `_settle_subtask` applies it before writing the
register. Every detail/where is normalized on ingestion by
`_normalize_risk_text` (whitespace runs — including newlines — collapsed;
length-capped at `_RISK_DETAIL_MAX` = 300 / `_RISK_WHERE_MAX` = 120
characters) so a disclosure can never inject markdown structure into the
PR section or bloat it. The conformer's positional `risk_dispositions`
(bare strings, read from `conf_res`) answers the implementer-side entries
in order (index i answers risk i): an entry is marked `addressed: true`
ONLY for `"mitigated"` with the repair recorded in a structured field — a
`fixed: true` `solution_defects` entry or a `kind: "tests"`
`file_updates` entry, and only while the record survives and is
trustworthy: `_run_conformance_phase` sets
`conformer_repair_rolled_back` on the result when its rollback arms
reverted the round's commits (protected path, strict clobber, or the
clean-tree gate exhausted — so no tests entry can point at an
uncommitted path), the cited tests path, canonicalized worktree-relative
first, is absent
from the phase's own diff (`impl_head_sha..HEAD`, ancestor-prefix — a
zero-commit pass citing a pre-existing file records no repair; a
`fixed: true` claim with zero phase commits falls to the same rule),
or the result failed `_validate_conformance_result` — each
neutralizes the act — while
`"accepted"`, `"confirmed_defect"`, an unanswered tail, a non-string or
unrecognised item, or a mitigation with no surviving repair record all
stay unaddressed (the fail-safe union; no prose is ever interpreted,
only set/string comparison on structured fields). `"confirmed_defect"`
never reads as addressed by design: its act is the filed defect, which
the completeness gate owns; a confirmation filed with NO actionable
entry draws an advisory warning at settle (the §12 code check behind
the prompt rule) — see DESIGN §9, which also names the
unrelated-repair residual class and why per-risk linkage was rejected.
`_settle_subtask`'s success path persists the result to
`state.json.risk_register[sid]` with the same set / pop-on-clean shape as
`symptom_findings`, and threads the implementer-side entries into
`_run_conformance_phase` → `_run_conformer`, which renders them as a
`SELF_REPORTED_RISKS` context block the conformer must answer. The register
is routed by type: `gap: unverified_external` with a `resource` reaches the
PR's "Needs human verification" list through `_format_pr_end_state_section`,
and an entry with `simulated_interleaving: true` and no such resource its
"Not verified by this run" list (`_pr_not_verified`); `test_missing` / `test_weak`
feed the coverage re-drive (*Coverage re-drive* below); everything else
stays in `state.json`. Risks never gate; the two *gating*
robustness kinds live on `solution_defects`
(`external_contract_assumption`, `unrevalidated_precondition`) and ride
the existing completeness channel unchanged. Pinned by
`tests/test_risk_register.py`.

`PHANTOM_ARTIFACT` resolves a collision's `artifact` against the union of
every subtask's `files_likely_touched` **as well as** the working tree, not
the tree alone — the judge's charter is subtasks that both *create or
substantially rewrite* an artifact, so a not-yet-existing file is the
canonical subject. Only a path present in neither the tree nor the plan is
flagged. Path comparison is normalized (`_normalize_artifact_path`: leading
`./` stripped, `os.sep` → `/`, no case folding); `NO_FILE_OVERLAP` uses the
same normalizer, plus `_paths_designate_same_file` so a repo-root prefix on
one side does not read as disjoint. **`NO_FILE_OVERLAP` is not emitted when
the two subtasks share a `provides` tag** — the tag is its own grounding,
and for a file neither subtask has created yet each planner invents the
path, so requiring intersection suppressed correct findings (DESIGN §5 *A
deterministic floor underneath the judge*). `DROP_BREAKS_GRAPH` likewise
subtracts tags a **surviving** subtask still provides before flagging an
orphan.

`artifact` is a **logical** label and Python never parses it — the judge
names the files separately in the `artifact_paths` array, and
`PHANTOM_ARTIFACT` does plain set membership on that (CLAUDE.md
*Language-to-JSON*). An empty `artifact_paths` means the artifact has no
file and nothing is flagged; `minLength: 1` on the items makes a blank
entry a schema-gate retry rather than something the check filters at read
time. `artifact_paths` is **asked for but NOT in `collisions[].required`**
(changed 2026-08-03): requiring it drove `plan_overlap_judge`'s valid-output
rate to 40.9% against 99.6–100% for every other worker, almost all failures
the single error `'artifact_paths' is a required property` — a
whole-payload rejection of otherwise-sound collision analysis. Absence is
the designed-for case (`paths = c.get("artifact_paths") or []`; `if not
paths: continue`). See DESIGN §5 *Cross-domain surface overlap*.
`tests/test_phase_overlap_judge.py`'s `TestProsePathParsingAbsent` pins that
neither earlier hand-parsing shape (whole-string checking, whitespace
tokenizing) has returned.

`DUPLICATE_PAIR` covers two collisions naming the same `{a_sid, b_sid}`
pair. This is **coherent** when the pair genuinely overlaps on more than one
artifact (one row per artifact rather than one row listing every path), and
`_apply_overlap_collisions` absorbs the repeat via `skipped_redundant`.
What matters is the resolved **effect** (dropped sid for a `drop_*`, or the
sorted endpoint pair for a `merge`), not the `resolution` string:
identical-effect rows are coalesced by `_validate_overlap_judge_output`
into one collision (artifacts joined, `artifact_paths` unioned) and
applied; rows whose effects genuinely *differ* (e.g. the same pair emitted
twice as `drop_a` with swapped endpoints, dropping both subtasks) surface
as `DUPLICATE_PAIR` from `check_overlap_judge_output`, giving the judge a
retry round.

`LOW_CONFIDENCE` no longer exists. It was emitted by
`_confidence_issues(conf, axes, threshold=9.0)` from a worker's own
self-reported score; every gate that consumed it was replaced by an
independent adversarial verifier (DESIGN §8), and the helper has since been
deleted along with the axis.

The reconciler's size-gate and cycle-gate retry paths also run
`check_reconciler_output` after each retry's `_apply_reconciler_output`,
logging warnings for any structural issues.

### Task-referenced file extraction

When the task string references files (detected by
`_glob_task_references`), the orchestrator names the resolved paths for
the planner via `_format_task_file_references` — a list of paths, and
nothing else; the planner reads the files itself. Whether the plan
covers what they require is `task_coverage_judge`'s call (see
DESIGN.md §8 for the full rationale).

| Function | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `_expand_braces(pattern)` | Pre-expands `{a,b}` brace groups that Python's `glob.glob` does not handle. Recursive for nested braces. |
| `_glob_task_references(task, repo_root)` | Scans the task string for file-path tokens, expands braces, globs each pattern. Returns deduplicated `list[Path]`. Tokens are stripped of markdown emphasis (`*`, `_`, backticks) **before** classification and must still look like a path afterwards — some alphanumeric content plus an extension or a `/` — since a bare `*`/`**` (ordinary markdown emphasis) would otherwise glob to every file in the repo root. Absolute-path tokens are refused, and every glob result is independently re-checked for containment under `repo_root.resolve()` so `../` segments cannot escape either. The task file never appears in its own list (`_is_same_document`). |
| `_is_same_document(path, text_len, text)` | True when `path` holds exactly `text` modulo surrounding whitespace. Keeps a task file out of its own reference list, since the planner already has the task verbatim. A size pre-check (±8 bytes) means only a same-length candidate is ever opened. |
| `_repo_rel(path, repo_root)` | Repo-relative string for a path, falling back to its basename when it resolves outside the repo. Pure path arithmetic. |
| `_git_z_output(argv, *, timeout=None)` | `subprocess.run(argv)` in bytes, `stdout` decoded with `os.fsdecode` (surrogateescape) and `stderr` with `errors="replace"`; returns the `CompletedProcess`. Every git call whose `-z` output carries raw path bytes reads it through this (`_untracked_files`, `_node_lockfile_paths`, `_prisma_project`, `_git_tree_sources`, `_git_paths_at`, `_write_acceptance_set`, `_acceptance_new_files`, `_collect_acceptance_set`): `text=True` decoded strictly and raised `UnicodeDecodeError` on a non-UTF-8 file name (review r2 L2 — out of `_settle_by_execution`, uncaught, killing the wave), and a surrogate-escaped name round-trips to the same file for `unlink`. |
| `_switched_branch_only_paths(repo_root, rel, wb_ref)` | The repo-relative files under `rel` (a file or a directory) that `git ls-tree -r -z --name-only HEAD -- <rel>` lists but the same query against `wb_ref` (from `_working_branch_ref`) does not: content committed only on a branch the operator switched to mid-run. `_stage_worktree_extras` skips exactly these files (a directory or `.claude/` is copied with `_ignore_repo_paths(repo_root, skip)` as `copytree`'s `ignore`), so untracked or `git add`-ed-but-uncommitted files beside them are still staged (DESIGN §12 L2/L4). `ls-tree` reads commits and matches literally. Output is read as bytes and `os.fsdecode`d; `wb_ref` None, or any git failure or exception, gives the empty set (the pre-existing copy) — an exception escaping here would abandon every later task reference. A task-named file skipped this way is named in a WARNING. |
| `_ignore_repo_paths(repo_root, skip)` | A `shutil.copytree` `ignore` callable dropping exactly the repo-relative paths in `skip`. |
| `_porcelain_path(line)` | The target path of one `git status --porcelain` v1 line: `XY <path>`, or the new name of an `R`/`C` line's `<old> -> <new>` (split only on those statuses — porcelain C-quotes any name with whitespace, so an unquoted name never contains ` -> `), with a C-quoted name decoded (`codecs.escape_decode`, then UTF-8 with `surrogateescape`); an undecodable escape (not a whole quoted name) returns the raw text instead of raising. |
| `_working_branch_ref(repo_root, st)` | `refs/heads/<name>` for the run's recorded working branch, trying the recorded name, then the name without a leading `heads/` (what `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` prints when a tag shares the name), then a name already of the form `refs/heads/<name>` (printed when even `heads/<name>` is ambiguous); None when there is no branch to follow (unrecorded, detached start, deleted) or git cannot be run. The same lookup `setup-run.sh` and `planning-worktree.sh` make; `_base_tree_sha` calls it via `asyncio.to_thread`. |
| `_working_branch_arg(st)` | `[working_branch]` for the scripts' optional `<working-branch>` argument, or `[]` when it is empty or `HEAD` (a detached start). |
| `_base_tree_sha(repo_root, st)` | The sha of the tree the planning worktree mirrors — `_working_branch_ref`'s tip, else the checkout's HEAD; the `satisfied_probe_cache` key. |
| `_log_working_branch_fallback(proc, where)` | Logs the scripts' `warning: working branch '<name>' not found; using HEAD` stderr line as a WARNING on a successful run (both callers otherwise print stderr only on failure). Matches that fixed prefix only, so ordinary git stderr is not echoed. |
| `_execute_check_porcelain_only(st)` | `porcelain_only` for the per-wave execute call of `_assert_repo_unchanged`: `True` unless `stop_on_repo_change`, under which HEAD and refs are compared too. |
| `_delta_fingerprint(repo_root, delta)` | Change fingerprint for one `_diff_repo_state` delta, stored in `repo_change_warned`; metadata only, never file contents, symlinks not followed. A working-tree delta's path comes from `_porcelain_path`. A file is its `lstat` `size:mtime_ns:inode`; a directory is the sha256 of the sorted `lstat`s of the untracked, non-ignored entries `_untracked_cmd(repo_root, pathspec="<dir>/")` lists (capped at 5000), so ignored build output and a nested repo's churn do not count; a missing path is `absent`, an `OSError` or failed listing `unreadable`; HEAD/ref deltas `""` (their string carries the sha). The listing is read as bytes and `os.fsdecode`d (`-z` names are unquoted; a non-UTF-8 name must not raise), and the whole computation (`_delta_fingerprint_unguarded`) is wrapped so any exception is `unreadable` — the sentinel must not be able to kill a run. `_assert_repo_unchanged` computes it via `asyncio.to_thread`. |
| `_format_task_file_references(files, repo_root)` | Names the files the task references so the planner reads them itself. A list of paths and nothing else — it must not open them. `None` when the task names no files. |
| `_unreachable_task_references(task, repo_root)` | Advisory sibling of `_glob_task_references`. Scans the same de-emphasized, path-shaped tokens and flags three shapes invisible to the planner for different mechanical reasons: tokens starting with `/` (absolute, dropped as candidates), `~` (home-relative — pathlib never expands `~`; the token must be home-**shaped**, i.e. `~/…` or `~name/…`, since a `~` in task prose is more often approximation notation (`~17.9 MB`, `~2.5/subtask`) whose `expanduser()` raises `RuntimeError` — a `/`-only test is insufficient), and `../` (parent-relative — resolved against the required `repo_root` parameter; flagged when it escapes the root or resolves to nothing). Trailing sentence punctuation is `rstrip`ped (never `strip` — a leading dot or `./`/`../` is meaningful). `_log_unreachable_task_references` (next row) owns the warning line and is `phase_plan`'s only entry point to this check; the check never gates. Both filesystem probes are exception-guarded (`OSError`/`RuntimeError`/`ValueError`), so the function has no raise path; a token that cannot be probed is reported, never propagated. |
| `_log_unreachable_task_references(task, repo_root)` | The only caller of `_unreachable_task_references` (from `phase_plan`). Emits the operator warning and returns the list. Catches **every** exception from the check, logs `unreachable-reference advisory skipped: …`, and returns `[]` — the check gates nothing, so it must never be able to end a run. Added after two runs died in `phase 2: planning` on `RuntimeError: Could not determine home directory.` raised from a `~`-approximation token (2026-08-24). |

**Freeze guard (2026-07-19 incident, root cause A) — resolved by deletion.**
A single incidental dotted token (e.g. `CLAUDE.md` mentioned once in a
task's Verification section) used to make `extract_task_file_structure`
harvest the repo's real CLAUDE.md as spec items, including imperatives that
could never appear verbatim in a subtask — a literal-substring gate that
fired identically every round, burning ~35% of the run's spend on a signal
that could not move. The whole mechanism (`extract_task_file_structure`,
`_is_uncoverable_convention_item`, `_BACKTICK_SPAN_RE`,
`check_task_file_coverage`, `_dedup_frozen_coverage_issues`,
`_format_task_file_structure`, `_MAX_COVERAGE_ITEMS`, and the
`LOW_COVERAGE` issue kind) is deleted. `phase_plan` now names the
referenced files via `_format_task_file_references` and lets the planner
read them; coverage of what those files require belongs to
`task_coverage_judge` (phase 2⅞½). `tests/test_task_file_coverage_freeze.py`
and `TestProseHarvestAbsent` pin that none of the deleted symbols return.

No-op when the task doesn't reference files.

### Instruction-adherence gate (DESIGN §12 sibling — *Instruction adherence
is code-enforced*)

Fully shipped. `SCHEMAS["classifier"]` carries `prescribed_procedure`
(`{is_prescribed, commands, forbid_manual, evidence}`, persisted to
`st.data["prescribed_procedure"]` — see §3 "Worker output schemas"),
`SCHEMAS["planner"]` carries the **required** per-subtask `change_shape`
(`point` | `localized` | `sweep`) — the planner's declaration of how many edit
sites its change needs. Required, not optional, for the same reason
`migration_targets.is_real_identifier` is: a planner must not be able to skip an
attestation a gate depends on by omitting the field. `_subfile_split()` reads it
and refuses to tile anything but a `sweep` (DESIGN §5½ (P1) *Sub-file*
*Gating condition*). It cannot be derived in code — the number of sites a change
needs is not a property of the file — and it must never be read out of
`investigation_notes`, which is planner prose (DESIGN §*Language-to-JSON*).
With it, the planner carries the **required** boolean `independent_sites`
(each site changeable from its own surrounding lines alone) and the optional
`sweep_sites` (`string[]`, the identifiers every site contains — located in the
file by `git grep -w -F`, never read from prose). Absent on
`reconciler.added_subtasks` and `splitter.children`; absence of either typed
field means **no split** (DESIGN §5½ (P1) *Sub-file* — the reversed default).
`_recursive_decompose` copies all three onto splitter children
(`_inherit_split_fields`), and `_inherited_subtask_fields` onto peel, migration
and region children, so a child is gated as its parent was.

`splitter.children` items also carry `verify`
(`_subtask_item_schema(include_requires=True, include_verify=True)`;
`verification_only` is a separate flag, `include_verification_only`, the
planner's alone, and `_inherit_split_fields` drops one a splitter child
carries; DESIGN §8 *A no-op the base already carries*). `_inherited_subtask_fields`
spreads `_inherited_verify(subtask)` — the parent's `verify`, deep-copied,
absent when the parent has none; never `verification_only` — into every
code-built child. `_migration_child(..., verify=None)` takes the label-only
splitter's `verify` for a relabelled chunk (`_label_migration_chunks`
collects it per id), replacing the parent's. After an LLM split,
`_split_children_missing_verify(parent, children)` lists the children
without `verify` under a parent with a verify argv, logged as plan defect
`SPLIT_CHILD_NO_VERIFY`, never repaired.

`SCHEMAS["planner"]` carries the optional per-subtask `runs_commands`
array, the `adherence_judge` worker is fully registered (schema, prompt,
`WORKER_TYPES`, sonnet/`"medium"` model-effort defaults — see "The
`adherence_judge` worker" below), and `phase_adherence_gate` (a
whole-plan gate, "Phase 2⅞", run once per assembled plan rather than
per-subtask) wires all of it together.

`phase_adherence_gate(plans, task, st, caps, models, efforts)` runs in
`_run_phases` immediately after `phase_overlap_judge` and before
`_schedule()`/`_validate_plan` (so a re-plan never rebuilds an
already-scheduled DAG). It short-circuits — free, no worker calls — when
`st.data["skip_adherence_check"]` is set, and again when
`st.data["prescribed_procedure"].is_prescribed` is falsy (the ~90%
goal-only common case never pays for a judge call). Two-stage
composition (corpus-validated: 0/21 false positives on real runs; do not
gate on the judge's score alone, which false-positived ~12% of ordinary
runs in isolation):

1. **Deterministic floor (primary, JSON→verdict, no NL):**
   `check_prescribed_command_coverage(prescribed_procedure, subtasks)`
   computes `set(prescribed_procedure.commands) − ⋃(subtask.runs_commands
   for subtask in plan)` using **normalized token-set matching**
   (lowercase + stopword-filtered token-SUBSET — the planner emits
   paraphrases of the prescribed command, not always the byte-identical
   string), not exact string equality. A non-empty result names a
   prescribed command no subtask runs — a `PRESCRIBED_CMD_UNRUN` issue.
   Silent (and free) when `prescribed_procedure` is absent, `is_prescribed`
   is false, or `commands` is empty.
2. **Adherence judge (secondary, semantic layer):** spawned only when
   `is_prescribed=true`. Scores `instruction_adherence` (0–10) +
   `violations[]` for the case the deterministic floor cannot see: every
   prescribed command runs, but the plan *also* substitutes hand-authored/
   manual work the user's `forbid_manual` signal prohibited. The gate fires
   when `instruction_adherence < _ADHERENCE_GATE_THRESHOLD` (5.0 — chosen
   from the corpus's clean separation: incident plans scored ≤3.0,
   legitimate plans ≥8.5).
3. **Gate wiring.** Either a `PRESCRIBED_CMD_UNRUN` floor issue or a low
   `instruction_adherence` score is fed to the **existing**
   `_run_checked_loop` (bounded by `judgment_check_rounds`), exactly like
   `phase_reconcile` and `phase_overlap_judge`. The retry's
   `make_feedback_prompt` callback **is** the re-plan action: it
   re-invokes `phase_plan` in full with the violation text folded into the
   task string, then re-invokes `phase_reconcile` on the re-planned output
   (short-circuiting to a no-op when the re-plan introduced no new
   unresolved requires), and the loop's next round re-runs the floor +
   judge against the new, reconciled plan. No new pause/resume machinery.
   Exhaustion `die()`s with the unresolved violations and the
   `--skip-adherence-check` escape hatch. `adherence_judge` `WorkerError`
   (every round crashes) degrades: the floor's own (model-independent)
   verdict is re-checked one final time — a clean floor returns the plan
   unmodified, a violating floor still `die()`s — mirroring `fit_judge`'s
   crash-barrier discipline (DESIGN §5½).

On success the gate persists `st.data["adherence_gate"] = {"judge":
<adherence_judge output>, "floor_issues": []}` for audit.

**Settle-time execution check (DESIGN §"A declared command must also have
been executed").** The floor above proves declaration only. At settle time,
`_settle_subtask` runs `check_declared_commands_executed(subtask, executed)`
on every `complete` result whose subtask populates `runs_commands` — on a
copy of the subtask without the entries the whole-suite deny refuses (the
settle-time exemption, §9 table below): `executed` is the list of Bash
commands the worker actually invoked, extracted from its per-worker JSONL
log by `_executed_bash_commands(log_path)` (over `_iter_log_tool_use` —
structured `tool_use` JSON, no prose). Matching is per shell segment
(`_BLT_SEG_RE` split + `_BLT_SEG_LEAD_RE` prefix strip — **no**
cross-segment union, which would credit tokens scattered across unrelated
commands), accepted in either direction: declared token set ⊆ segment's
(literal entry, wrapped execution), or the segment's salient token LIST
appears as a length-≥2 CONTIGUOUS ordered sublist of the declared entry's
salient token list (the paraphrase shape — contiguity rejects non-adjacent
fragments and scattered reassembly while accepting the command wherever it
sits in the paraphrase; the accepted near-miss residual class — parent
sub-commands, flag-dropped variants, `--help`-probed literals,
deliberately-typed adjacent pairs — is documented in DESIGN). Invocation,
not success, is what is verified (DESIGN §"A declared command must also have
been executed"). Each miss yields a `DECLARED_CMD_UNRUN: …` issue: these
join the mechanical-check re-drive (the `implementer_confidence_retries`
budget, feedback naming the unexecuted command); when the budget exhausts
with a command still unexecuted — or at once for a result rescued from
`empty_handoff`, which skips the re-drive — a subtask with its own commits
(`_branch_has_commits_ahead`) or `_verification_only` is settled by
`_settle_by_execution` (§6 *Settle by execution*): `pass` lets the
`complete` stand (the issue is dropped and `declared_unrun_warnings[sid]`
popped); `environment_limit` settles `unconverged`. Otherwise the subtask
settles `status: "blocked"` with the blocker naming the command(s) — never
a silent `complete` — and the wave-end re-drive takes it from the shared
budget, ending `unconverged` when spent. `declared_unrun_warnings` is no
longer written; `phase_finalize` still surfaces one an earlier run
recorded. Skipped for empty/absent `runs_commands` (the ~95% case, free).

### P6 repo-map — `_build_repo_map` + `_rank_repo_map`

Implements DESIGN §5½ (P6) *Codebase structural map*. Both functions are
deterministic, lazy-import tree-sitter (so the module loads on a bare host
Python that lacks the package), and call no LLM.

| Symbol | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `_walk_calls(node)` | Walks a tree-sitter CST recursively, collecting bare-name identifiers from `call` expression function positions. Returns `list[str]`. Attribute callees (e.g. `obj.method`) are skipped — only bare-name callees become ref edges. |
| `_parse_repo_file(path)` | Parses one source file with `tree_sitter_language_pack.process()` (for defs/structure) and a tree-sitter CST walk (for call-site refs). Returns `(defs: list[str], refs: list[str])`. Returns `([], [])` on unsupported language or any error (graceful degrade). On an actual caught exception, stashes `f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"` in the module-level `_last_parse_error` diagnostic (cleared to `None` on success). |
| `_build_repo_map(repo_root, leerie_root)` | Walks all source files under `repo_root` (skipping `.git`, `node_modules`, `__pycache__`, etc.), parses each with `_parse_repo_file`, and builds `{"files": {rel_path: [def_sym, ...]}, "refs": {def_sym: {rel_path, ...}}}`. mtime-caches per-file parse results under `<leerie_root>/<REPO_MAP_CACHE_DIR>/<sha256(abs_path)>.pkl` — only files whose `mtime_ns` changed since the last call are re-parsed. Always returns a valid dict; never raises. **Silent-degrade visibility (DESIGN §12):** if the repo contains source files but the graph comes back empty, `_warn_repo_map_empty_once()` runs a functional probe (`_tree_sitter_extraction_works()`) and emits exactly one warning per process **only if the probe confirms tree-sitter cannot extract symbols**. A genuinely non-code repo, or a working parser on a legitimately symbol-less repo, stays quiet. When the probe failed via a caught exception, the warning appends `" Probe failure: <type>: <message>"` from `_last_parse_error`. |
| `_pagerank(graph, personalization, damping, max_iter, tol)` | Personalized PageRank on a directed `dict[str, set[str]]` graph. Pure stdlib (no networkx). Handles dangling nodes via a dangling-mass redistribution term. Converges when sum of per-node rank deltas < `tol`. Returns `dict[str, float]`. |
| `_render_repo_map_subgraph(repo_map, ranked_files, max_files)` | Renders the top `max_files` files from `ranked_files` as a compact text block: one line per file listing its defined symbols (`path: Sym1, Sym2, ...`). Files with no defs are omitted. |
| `_count_tokens_approx(text)` | Approximate token count: `max(1, len(text.encode()) // 4)` — ~4 bytes per token. Used by `_rank_repo_map`'s binary-search budget fit. |
| `_rank_repo_map(repo_map, seed_files, seed_symbols, token_budget)` | Builds a file→file edge graph via shared symbols (definer → referencing files), runs personalized PageRank biased toward `seed_files` and files that define/reference `seed_symbols`, then binary-searches the largest prefix of the ranked-file list that fits within `token_budget` tokens (default `DEFAULT_CAPS["repo_map_tokens"]`). Returns the ranked subgraph as a plain text string. Returns `""` when the map is empty. |

**Edge direction:** `_build_repo_map` tracks `refs[sym] = {files that call sym}`. `_rank_repo_map` builds a file→file edge from the definer of `sym` to each file that references it — so widely-referenced utility files accumulate high in-degree and surface as structural backbone.

**Personalization in `_rank_repo_map`:** seed files get weight 1.0; files defining a seed symbol get 1.0; files *referencing* a seed symbol get 0.5. When no seed resolves to a known file, uniform personalization is used.

**Skip flag:** `resolve_skip_repo_map` (§2 "Skip flags") gates the call; when `True`, `_build_repo_map` is not called and the planner degrades to the prior grep/glob-only path.

### Phantom-path check

`PHANTOM_PATH` fires when a `files_likely_touched` entry does not exist
and no ancestor directory between the file and `repo_root` exists
either. This catches hallucinated paths (e.g.
`src/totally/invented/dir/file.ts` when `src/totally/` does not exist)
while tolerating greenfield features that create new subdirectories
under an existing parent.

### Migration-surface check

`check_planner_output` includes an `UNCOVERED_MIGRATION_SURFACE` check
(DESIGN §5 *Migration-surface completeness*). The planner **declares** the
migration in its own output — each subtask may carry
`migration_targets: [{old_pattern, replacement, is_real_identifier}]`
(`old_pattern` has `minLength: 3`; `is_real_identifier` is a required
boolean on each entry) — and the check greps `repo_root` for the
declared `old_pattern` string, collects files containing it,
cross-references against `files_likely_touched` across all subtasks in
the domain, and emits the issue when > 5 files are uncovered. The
threshold avoids false positives from comments, type definitions, and
test fixtures.

An earlier version inferred the old pattern from prose
(`_MIGRATION_SIGNAL_RE` matching phrases like "replaces direct `X`" against
`intent`/`investigation_notes`) — forbidden by CLAUDE.md *Language-to-JSON*,
and it did not work: measured on run `19a70d96`, all 27 extractions were
stopwords that grepped to hundreds of files and always cleared the
threshold. Python now greps a symbol the planner handed it directly.

Because `migration_targets` is optional, an omitted field (not a wrong
entry) silently disables `UNCOVERED_MIGRATION_SURFACE` for that subtask.
`_check_migration_targets_declared(subtasks)` closes the common case: the
schema's `performs_replacement: bool` sibling field is a same-worker
self-report of whether the subtask replaces anything at all, and the
check emits `MIGRATION_TARGETS_MISSING` when it's `true` but
`migration_targets` is empty — a same-call internal-consistency check, not
an independent verifier: a planner wrong on both fields together (false +
omitted) is not caught.

Whether `old_pattern` is shaped like a real identifier used to be enforced
by `_BARE_LOWERCASE_WORD_RE` (`^[a-z]+$`) — a regex Python ran against the
planner-populated field, itself a relocated *Language-to-JSON* violation.
It is retired: each `migration_targets` entry now carries a required
`is_real_identifier: bool` field the planner sets itself, and
`_check_migration_surface` trusts that attestation directly (skipping an
entry when it's `false` or absent) rather than re-deriving the judgment.

| Function/constant | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `_MIGRATION_SURFACE_THRESHOLD` | 5 — uncovered file count below which the check stays silent |
| `_grep_old_pattern(pattern, repo_root)` | `subprocess.run` grep for the pattern; returns set of file paths |
| `_check_migration_targets_declared(subtasks)` | `MIGRATION_TARGETS_MISSING` when `performs_replacement: true` and `migration_targets` is empty — same-worker contradiction check, not an independent witness. |

`check_planner_output` (and thus both migration checks) only ever runs on
the planner's raw first-pass sample, inside `plan_one`, before
`_recursive_decompose` expands an oversized subtask into leaf children
(`phase_plan`'s expansion loop reassigns `plan["subtasks"] = leaves` only
after that call returns) — so neither check ever sees a post-expansion
leaf. `_migration_child` (P1 recursive decomposition, DESIGN §5½) still
copies `migration_targets`/`performs_replacement` onto every leaf it
builds, the same way it copies `depends_on`/`requires`/`provides`.

### Multi-sample planning

When `planner_samples > 1`, `phase_plan` runs N independent
`plan_one(category, sample_idx)` calls per domain in parallel
(bounded by `max_parallel`). Each gets a unique `sid`
(`planner-{category}-s{idx}`) so log files don't collide.

`_select_best_planner_sample(samples, repo_root, domain)` mechanically
selects the winner: fewest `check_planner_output` issues, tiebreak on
subtask count (more = better coverage), tiebreak on first sample
(determinism). No LLM merge judge — avoids self-bias. A crashed sample
(worker returned `None`) is dropped from the candidate set before
selection. If all samples for a domain crash, the run aborts.

**Validity gate (runs before scoring).**
`_planner_sample_is_empty_ready(sample, sibling_subtask_counts=None)`
returns True for a `status == "ready"` plan that is exactly empty, or
"near-degenerate" — non-empty but with substantially fewer subtasks than
the largest sibling (`_PLANNER_SAMPLE_DEGENERACY_RATIO`, 4x) — when
`sibling_subtask_counts` is given. `_select_best_planner_sample` drops
those samples **before** ranking — but only while at least one surviving
sibling is not itself dropped; if every sample is empty/near-degenerate
relative to the rest the full set is ranked unchanged, so
`_detect_no_work`'s terminal route still fires.

The gate precedes the scoring rather than joining it as another sort key,
because `check_planner_output` inspects subtasks, so a plan with none to
inspect returns `[]` and scores a perfect zero on the **primary**
criterion — an empty plan is otherwise unfalsifiable and beats every
sibling with real content to critique. Scoped to `ready` only: an empty
`blocked` plan is a planner verdict `_schedule()` must still act on.

Pinned by `tests/test_planner_sample_validity_gate.py`, including an
anti-vacuity control (`test_falsifier_empty_sample_would_win_without_the_gate`)
and `test_selection_is_biased_toward_smaller_plans_when_issues_scale`,
which records the residual bias the gate does **not** fix: per-subtask
findings make issue count grow with plan size, so a larger plan can still
lose to a smaller one.

The selection log line lists **every ranked sample**, not just the
winner (`… — ranked: #0(2i/2s), #2(3i/3s)`), using each sample's index in
the ORIGINAL `samples` list so the number cross-references the
`planner-{category}-s{idx}` worker sid.

### Sweeps (DESIGN §8 *A sweep's instances are items*)

A sweep spec (`_sweep_spec_schema(extra)`) is `{pattern, names?[], paths[],
exclude_paths?[], ignore_calls?[], ignore_attributes?[], markers?[]}`
(required: `pattern`, `paths`); `pattern` is one of `SWEEP_PATTERNS`
(`text_literal`, `call`). The classifier schema's `required_items[].sweeps[]`
adds a required `part` (one of the item's `parts`, or its `item`, verbatim);
the `defect_scope_auditor` schema's `sites[].sweep` is the spec as is, and
every site carries a required `extent` (`one_place` | `pattern`). Grammars read
(`_SWEEP_LANGS`): `tsx`, `typescript`, `javascript`, `python`, by
`tree_sitter_language_pack.detect_language`.

| Function | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `_sweep_glob_re(glob)` | A repo-relative glob as a regex over a `/` path: `**/` and `**` cross directories, `*` and `?` do not; a leading `./` is dropped. |
| `_sweep_is_text(s)` | The text-shape rule over a literal's whitespace-normalised characters: a letter pair required; a URL, or a leading `/`, `./`, `../`, `#`, `@`, `--`, is not text; one token (sentence punctuation stripped from its ends) is text when it holds a non-ASCII letter, or is one capitalised word (`Nombre`, not `ACTIVE`, `idle`, `UserCard`), and is not when it holds `._:/\=<>{}[]|$%^~` or a `-`; several tokens are text unless half or more look like code (a `-:/[]=_.` followed by a character, or `[]{}=`). |
| `_sweep_has_marker(s, markers)` | True with no markers; else a word of `s` equal to a marker (case-folded), or a one-character marker contained in `s`. |
| `_sweep_ignored(node, ignore_calls, ignore_attrs)` | The node's parent is an import/export statement, a literal type, a switch case, a subscript, a module or block (a docstring) or an expression statement it fills alone (a directive); a `===`/`!==`/`==`/`!=`/`in`/`not in` comparison; it is a `pair`'s key; or, walking up to the enclosing function, it sits in the arguments of a call whose callee or callee's last segment is in `ignore_calls`, or under a `jsx_attribute`/`pair`/`keyword_argument` named in `ignore_attrs`. |
| `_sweep_file_instances(path, source, sweep)` | `[{file, line (1-based), node, text}]` in source order, or `None` when no grammar the sweep reads parses the file. `node`: `jsx_text`, `string`, `template` (a template string or f-string; substitutions become a gap) or `call`. A literal's text is whitespace-normalised and capped at 200 characters; a call's is its source text, capped at 120. |
| `_sweep_enumerate(tree, sweep, rev="HEAD")` | `{instances, files, unparsed, error}` over the committed tree `rev` of `tree`: paths from `git ls-tree -r -z --full-tree`, matched by the sweep's globs in Python, blobs from one `git cat-file --batch` (`_tree_git_args`); never reads working files and passes no pathspec. `error` names a failed git call, no paths or an unknown pattern. |
| `_sweep_issues(result, tree, caps, cache=None)` | The classifier-loop check: `SWEEP_PART_UNKNOWN` (part not copied from the item), `SWEEP_EMPTY` (a `call` sweep without `names`, or no instance; the message counts the files under its paths no grammar parsed), `SWEEP_TOO_BROAD` (over `sweep_max_instances` / `sweep_max_files`). An enumeration error raises nothing. |
| `_sweep_derived(out, got, sweep, text, anchor, origin)` | Appends one item per file of an enumeration to `out`, in path order, and returns their indices: `item` = `"<text> — at every instance in <file> (<n>)"`, `anchor` (`span`/`source_ref`), `verifiability: "tree"`, `parts` (`_sweep_part_text`: `file:line node "text"`), `sweep_of` = `origin` + `{file, spec}` (the spec less `part`), `instances`. |
| `_derive_sweep_items(items, tree, caps, cache=None)` | `(items + derived, record)` for the classifier's sweeps: drops every earlier derived item (`sweep_of`; classification precedes the audit), then per item and sweep `_sweep_derived` with text = the part, anchor = the item's `span`/`source_ref`, origin `{item_index, sweep, part}`. `record` rows `{item_index, sweep, part, pattern, instances, files, unparsed[≤50], error, derived[]}`. |
| `_site_sweep_specs(defect_scope)` | `(site, sweep)` per `fix` site (`_scope_sites`) whose `sweep` is well formed. |
| `_tree_dirs(tree, rev="HEAD")` | Every directory of the committed tree (`git ls-tree -r -d -z --name-only --full-tree`), or None when git cannot answer. |
| `_site_sweep_issues(result, tree, caps, cache=None)` | The auditor-loop check, over `fix` sites only: `SWEEP_MISSING: sites[<n>]` (typed `extent: pattern`, no `sweep`), `SITE_IS_A_DIRECTORY: sites[<n>]` (not typed `pattern`, `file` — slashes stripped — is in `_tree_dirs`), then `_sweep_issues` over each site's sweep, named `sites[<n>].sweep`. |
| `_derive_site_sweep_items(items, defect_scope, tree, cache=None)` | `(items + derived, record)` for the audit's site sweeps: drops earlier site-derived items, then per site `_sweep_derived` with text `"Audited defect site D<n> (<symbol>) is resolved: <resolution>"`, anchor `{source_ref: D<n>}`, origin `{site_id}`. `record` rows `{site_id, pattern, instances, files, unparsed[≤50], error, derived[]}`. |
| `_sweep_still_present(items, tree, rev="HEAD")` | `{derived item_index: [instances]}`: each derived item's own `sweep_of.spec` re-enumerated on `tree`; a base instance is still present while its file holds one of the same `node` and `text` (counted as a multiset, lines ignored). |
| `_sweep_evidence_section(items, present)` | The judge's `SWEEP INSTANCES STILL PRESENT` section (per item `item <i>: <left> of <n> still present — …`, at most 40 instances listed), or `""` when nothing is left. |

`phase_classify` runs `_sweep_issues` in its check (on `_judgment_cwd(st)`,
the tree the classifier read), then `_derive_sweep_items` on the returned
items, writes `required_items` and `sweeps`, and logs each sweep's counts.
`phase_defect_scope_audit` runs `_site_sweep_issues` plus `_reading_issues`
as its check-loop check (with a feedback prompt appended to the auditor's user
prompt) and returns the scope; it derives nothing.
`_settle_scope_reading` (below) then appends `_derive_site_sweep_items` over
the audit's sites to `required_items` and its rows to
`sweeps` (replacing earlier site rows), logging each site's counts.

**The scope reading** (DESIGN §8 *A sweep's instances are items*, "When the
task reads two ways"). The `defect_scope_auditor` schema has a required
top-level `reading` `{kind, narrow, broad}`, `kind` one of
`SCOPE_READING_KINDS` (`one_reading`, `narrow_or_broad`), `narrow` / `broad`
one sentence each of what that reading covers (`""` with `one_reading`), and
each site an optional `reading`, one of `SITE_READINGS` (`both`,
`broad_only`; absent means `both`). The run always takes the broad reading;
nothing is asked and no answer key exists.

| Function | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `_reading_issues(result)` | The auditor-loop check on `reading`, for an `applicable` result only: `READING_UNDESCRIBED` (`narrow_or_broad` with an empty `narrow` or `broad`), `READING_BROAD_ADDS_NOTHING` (`narrow_or_broad` and no `fix` site typed `broad_only` that is `extent: pattern` with a `sweep` dict — single files alone do not count), `READING_UNDECLARED: sites[<n>]` (`one_reading` and that site typed `broad_only`). |
| `_settle_scope_reading(st) -> None` | Run by `_run_phases` right after the audit, keyed on the absence of `state.data["scope_reading"]` and skipped once `plans_after_plan` exists. Derives every audited site's sweep items (`_derive_site_sweep_items` — the broad reading keeps every site), logs the reading when the audit found two, and writes `scope_reading` (below). |
| `_pr_scope_reading_lines(state)` | The PR's `## Scope reading` lines, from `scope_reading` when its `kind` is `narrow_or_broad`: both readings, and that the run took the broad one — it did both, and nobody was asked. `[]` otherwise. `_format_pr_end_state_section` renders them under `## Scope reading` (in `_PR_END_STATE_HEADINGS`, after `## Still failing when the run ended` and `## Held-out cases accepted by the operator`). |
Requirement coverage (`_d1_holes`) reads the classifier's result, never the
derived items. `_delivery_judge_unmet` adds `instances` (the item's `parts`)
to a derived item's payload entry; every other entry is unchanged.

### Site claims, blocked domains and forbidden commands (DESIGN §5, §8, §9)

**Site claims (D3).** `phase_defect_scope_audit` stamps every kept site
with `site_id` = `D<n>` in audit order (Python assigns IDs only;
`_scope_sites` fills the same IDs on a `defect_scope` persisted before
the field existed). The auditor types each `fix` site's
`resolution_kind` (one of `SITE_RESOLUTION_KINDS`) and `resolution`; the
planner types each subtask's `change_kind` (`CHANGE_KINDS`: `fix` /
`test` / `docs` / `other`) and `claims.sites[] = {site_id,
resolution_kinds[]}`, and lists sites it leaves alone in the top-level
`sites_not_needed[] = {site_id, reason_kind, reason}` (`reason_kind` one of
`SITE_EXCLUSION_KINDS`: `holds_on_tree`, `covered_by_other_site`,
`outside_task`). On every run the planner also
types `claims.items[] = {item_index, kind}` (`kind`: `deliverable` /
`process`, `ITEM_CLAIM_KINDS`) — the `required_items` indices the
subtask delivers; `claims.sites` may then be empty. The only items a plan
may leave unclaimed are those another category's planner delivers, listed
in the top-level `items_not_needed[] = {item_index, reason_kind, reason}`
(`ITEM_EXCLUSION_KINDS` is `("other_domain",)`; there is no
`already_on_tree`: an item the tree may already carry is claimed, and its
subtask settles as a no-op, DESIGN §5). The item
accounting is checked at plan time (*Item accounting* below);
`_item_claims(plan_subtasks)` reads the claims for the delivery re-drive,
`_site_claim_fields` carries them to split children with the site claims,
and `_merge_subtask_core_fields` unions them when two subtasks merge. The
equivalence table is the code constant `SITE_KIND_CLASS`:

| `resolution_kind` | class | contradicts |
|---|---|---|
| `rerun_flow` | `rerun_flow` | every other class |
| `reraise` | `reraise` | every other class |
| `relink` | `relink` | every other class |
| `guard`, `recompute`, `propagate` | `decide` (one class) | every other class |
| `other` | `other` | nothing — the site is recorded `surface_other: true`, for the delivery gate to settle (`_settle_untyped_sites`) |

| Function | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `_scope_sites(defect_scope)` | The audit's sites, each with a `site_id` (`D1`, `D2`, … by position when absent). Never mutates its input. |
| `_site_claim_rows(plan, defect_scope)` | One row per `fix` site (a site with no `disposition` counts as `fix`): `{site_id, file, symbol, auditor_kind, resolution, claims[{sid, kinds}], not_needed, not_needed_kind, status, surface_other}`. Claims count only from subtasks with `change_kind: "fix"`. `status`: `claimed` (some claimed kind is in the audit kind's class, or either side is `other`), `mismatch` (claimed, every kind outside the class), `not_needed` (unclaimed, with a `sites_not_needed` entry whose `reason_kind` is in `SITE_EXCLUSION_KINDS` and whose `reason` is non-empty; the first such entry per site counts), `unclaimed`. A claim wins over a `not_needed` entry for the same site. An unknown or missing kind reads as `other`. |
| `_check_site_claims(result, defect_scope)` | The planner-loop check: `SITE_UNCLAIMED: D<n> — …` and `SITE_KIND_MISMATCH: D<n> — …` issue strings (gating labels) carrying the site's file/symbol, the audit's kind and `resolution`, and what to do. `[]` for a `blocked` plan and when the audit is inapplicable or has no sites. Wired into `phase_plan`'s `_check_planner` for the `bug-fixing` domain only — the domain the audit belongs to — so the residual rides `planner_check_rounds`; an `unclaimed` residual then stops the run (`_stop_on_unclaimed_sites`). |
| `_stop_on_unclaimed_sites(record)` | DESIGN §5 *An audited site the plan leaves alone is excluded with a typed reason, or the run stops*: `die()`s naming every row of the just-persisted `site_claims` record still `unclaimed` (`D<n>: <file> :: <symbol>`) and the `reason_kind` values; returns when there is none. A `mismatch` never stops. Called by `phase_plan` right after it writes the first-pass record, so nothing is checkpointed (`plans_after_plan`) and a resume plans again. |
| `_site_claim_record(plans, defect_scope)` | `{domain, sites[rows]}` for the `bug-fixing` plan, or `None` when there is none or the audit is inapplicable. `phase_plan` writes it to `state.data["site_claims"]` from the first-pass plans and logs the count still `unclaimed`/`mismatch`, then writes it again over the leaves after recursive decomposition (same verdicts; `claims[].sid` are leaf ids). |
| `_site_claim_fields(subtask)` | `{change_kind, claims}` copied from a split parent (each only when present; `claims` deep-copied). `_inherited_subtask_fields` spreads it into every code-built child (migration chunk, peel, sub-file region) and `_recursive_decompose` stamps it onto every splitter child, whose schema carries neither. Every child carries all of its parent's claims. |

**Item accounting (DESIGN §5 *Required items are claimed too, and the plan
accounts for every one*).** Every planner gets `required_items` as
`_planner_required_items(items)`: each item's `item`, `span`, `parts`,
`source_ref` and `verifiability`, with its code-assigned `item_index` (the
numbering `task_coverage_judge` and the delivery gate use). The check is set
arithmetic on `item_index`, `kind`, `reason_kind` and `verification_only`:

| Function | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `_item_accounting_rows(plans, items)` | One row per required item over the given plans: `{item_index, item, claimed_by[], not_counted[], excluded[{domain, reason_kind, reason}], status}`. A claim counts toward `claimed_by` unless it is a `deliverable` claim from a subtask with `verification_only: true` (such a subtask writes nothing); that subtask's id goes to `not_counted`. An `items_not_needed` entry counts only with a `reason_kind` in `ITEM_EXCLUSION_KINDS` and a non-empty `reason`. `status`: `claimed` (some counted claim), `other_domain` (no counted claim, an `other_domain` exclusion), `uncovered`. Indices outside `[0, len(items))` are ignored here and reported by the check. |
| `_check_item_claims(result, items, n_categories)` | The planner-loop check: `ITEM_UNACCOUNTED: item <i> — …` for a row of this plan that is `uncovered`, or `other_domain` on a run with one category (naming the `verification_only` claimers it did not count, when there are any), and `ITEM_INDEX_UNKNOWN: <i> — …` for a claim or exclusion naming an index outside the list. Each issue quotes the item's wording (truncated to 200 characters) and says what to do. `[]` for a `blocked` plan and when there are no required items. Wired into `phase_plan`'s `_check_planner` for every category unless `skip_coverage_check`, so a residual rides `planner_check_rounds`. |
| `_item_coverage_record(plans, items)` | `{items[rows], uncovered[item_index...]}` for the merged plan, or `None` with no required items. `uncovered` holds every row that is not `claimed`. |
| `_cross_domain_item_gaps(rows)` | The rows with status `other_domain`: items every planner that accounted for them excluded as another domain's, and none claimed. Each one re-plans the domains whose plan excluded it (`_item_gap_domains`). |

`phase_planning_coverage_gate` closes the cross-domain gaps first. It runs
`_run_checked_loop` (`max_rounds = judgment_check_rounds`) whose invoke
re-computes the accounting on the current plan (no worker) and whose check
lists `ITEM_UNCLAIMED_BY_ANY_DOMAIN: item <i> — …` per cross-domain gap. Its
feedback calls `check_replan_affordable(st, caps, "coverage gate", plans)`,
then `phase_plan(..., replan_round=n, domains=_replan_domain_closure(plans,
implicated))` with the gaps folded into the task, merges the fresh plans
with the plans outside the closure, and re-runs `phase_reconcile`,
`phase_overlap_judge` and `phase_adherence_gate`. It then writes
`state.data["item_coverage"]` and logs each `uncovered` item before any
implementation work. A residual never stops the run.

**Blocked domains (D4, shrunk).** The planner returns a top-level
`blocker_kind` (`PLANNER_BLOCKER_KINDS`: `none` / `external_precondition`
/ `evidence_gap`) and, for `external_precondition`, `external_resource`.
Reconciled with the implementer's typed blocker (B1, `BLOCKER_KINDS`, §6
*Typed blocker kinds*): `external_precondition` is the one value the two
share, with the same meaning (only a human outside the run can supply it)
and the same companion `external_resource`; the planner's other two kinds
are plan-level and have no implementer counterpart.
`tests/test_blocker_kind.py` pins the shared value.

| Function | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `_blocked_domain_rows(plans)` | `[{domain, blocker_kind, external_resource, gap}]` for every plan with `status: "blocked"`; `blocker_kind` is `""` when the plan did not type it (a pre-feature checkpoint), `gap` is `_format_blocked_gap(confidence)`. |
| `_settle_blocked_domains(st, plans)` | Writes `state.data["domain_blocked"]` (always — `[]` when nothing is blocked) and `die()`s, before any subtask executes, when a row is `external_precondition`, naming each domain and `external_resource`. Called in `_run_phases` after the `plans_after_plan` checkpoint (fresh and resumed) and again immediately before `_schedule()` (a re-plan can block a domain). No re-plan. |

**Forbidden commands (D5).** The classifier returns
`process_constraints = {forbidden_commands: [{command, evidence_quote,
scope}]}` (`scope` is `any` or `whole_suite`). `phase_classify` persists
`_process_constraints(result, prescribed, sources, repo_root)` to
`state.data["process_constraints"]`. `sources` is the raw task text plus
each referenced report (`units["sections"]` rejoined per report). It is
never the classifier's prompt, so text leerie appended there cannot
qualify. The classifier's entries are unioned with
`forbidden_command_samples` (3) `forbidden_command_extractor` draws taken
beside it (`_forbidden_draw_union(result, samples) -> (union, {draws,
crashed, votes})`, classifier first, so its entry wins a scope tie); the
quote check alone decides what is kept, each kept entry carries `votes`
(draws that typed it; a derived entry, its `derived_from`'s) and the record `draws{draws, crashed}`.
Phase 1 records them through `_record_process_constraints(st, union,
draws, sources, repo_root, provisional=True)`: the record also carries
`provisional: true` and `inputs{union, votes, draws, crashed, sources}`,
because one derivation rule needs the repository's test command, which
`_discover_blt` reads in phase 1½. `phase_provision` calls
`_finalize_process_constraints(st, repo_root)` right after
`_discover_blt`, before the recipe is recorded. It re-derives the record
once from `inputs`, with the same call and `provisional=False` (no
`provisional`, no `inputs`), saves, and logs the entries when they
changed. A record that is not provisional is left alone. Every reader
from phase 1 on (`_worker_guard` among them) reads whichever record is
current (DESIGN §9 *A script's environment is part of what it runs*).

`NOTICE_FREE_WORKERS = {"classifier", "forbidden_command_extractor"}`: `claude_p` appends no
`NOTE FROM ORCHESTRATOR:` (whole-suite, forbidden-command, process-kill,
database-reset) to such a worker. Its deny rules and hook still apply.
The gate lives in `_worker_guard` (`worker=schema_key`), so it binds every
caller of the guard.

Returns the first forbidden command whose normalised argv is a prefix of one of `command`'s. Two package-manager `run` argvs compare from the subcommand on, so `npm test` matches a forbidden `pnpm run test`. Both sides are first canonicalised by `_forbidden_runner_canon`. A `whole_suite` entry naming a `_FORBID_RUNNERS` runner is first split by `_forbidden_suite_head(forb)` into `(runner head, operands)`: the prefix compared is the head alone, the entry's flags are dropped and its operands are added to the roots (DESIGN §9 *A whole-suite forbid matches on the runner alone*), so `go test -race ./...` hits a forbidden `go test ./...`; any other command, or an entry whose own words select, keeps the whole entry as its prefix — and an entry whose own words select is also compared on its runner key alone with no operands (`_forbidden_runner_key`), so the runner's whole-suite run hits it (DESIGN §9 *A whole-suite run contains every selector's run*). Both sides are read by `_forbidden_argvs_env`; a candidate argv is compared only when the forbidden argv's environment is a subset of its own, so an entry that sets an environment hits only a command that sets at least the same one. For a `whole_suite` entry that carries no pnpm `--filter` token itself, a candidate whose environment carries some (`_forbidden_pnpm_filters`: each `--filter`/`-F`/`--filter-prod` value among pnpm's leading options and a `run`'s own, as `pnpm --filter <value>`) is skipped when `_forbidden_filter_scoped(tokens, entry.package_name)` holds — no filter selects the root package: `*`, `**`, a path selector (one starting with `.` or `/`, or braced) whose `_forbidden_operand` is `.` or only `**` segments (`./**`, `{./**}`, `{**}`, `./`, `{.}`; `./*` is not), a name pattern (`fnmatch`, `{}` stripped) matching `package_name`, or, conservatively, an exclusion `!x`, a changed-since `[ref]`, a dependency-closure selector (`...` leading or trailing, or a leading `^`) or an absolute path (DESIGN §9 *A pnpm filter that names one package of several is scoped*); `_forbidden_pnpm_filters(words, vals)` adds the token `pnpm --filter .` when `-w`/`--workspace-root` stands among the same leading options as a filter (the `run` reading scans pnpm's global options and the `run`'s own as one list), since pnpm then also runs the root; `_forbidden_env_render` writes filter tokens as `pnpm --filter <value>… exec` before the argv. `env` (keyword, default empty) is an environment the command runs in (`_forbidden_argvs_env(command, env=env)`), so a script body is read as a call in that environment would run it. A `whole_suite` entry hits only when `_forbidden_whole_suite_rest(rest, roots + operands, runner=_forbidden_runner(forb))` holds for the words after the prefix, so `pnpm test src/a.test.ts` is not a hit; for pytest the runner's `value` is `_PYTEST_VALUE_OPTS` (every option that takes a value — `nargs` other than 0, the optional-value `--cov`/`--debug`/`--cache-show` included, since argparse gives them the next non-option word — read from the parser of pytest 9.2 with pytest-cov 7.1, pytest-xdist 3.8, pytest-timeout 2.4, pytest-rerunfailures 16.7 and pytest-randomly 5.0; `_PYTEST_LONG_FLAGS` is the same parser's `--` options with `nargs` 0; both are pinned against `tests/fixtures/pytest_options.json`, a capture of that parser, by `tests/test_pytest_option_table.py`) when the forbidden argv is `pytest`/`py.test`/`<python> -m pytest`, every other runner's its own `_FORBID_RUNNERS` entry — and the word after such an option is its value, never an operand, so `pytest -p no:cacheprovider` hits. `None` when nothing matches; never raises. |

For `whole_suite` entries: a whole-suite run in any spelling is denied, a run on specific test files is allowed, the same `not_applicable` instruction applies, and the orchestrator runs the coupled tests itself. `claude_p` appends it when the worker's tools reach Bash (bare `Bash`, or a `Bash(<head>…)` grant for a forbidden command's first word) and the worker is not in `NOTICE_FREE_WORKERS`. When any is named, `claude_p` adds `{LEERIE_FORBIDDEN_SCRIPTS: "<names, space-separated>", npm_config_script_shell, pnpm_config_script_shell: <ROOT>/scripts/forbidden-script-shell.sh}` to the worker env (the caller's `env_extra` wins on a clash). The guard (`FORBIDDEN_SCRIPT_SHELL`, mode 755) exits 97 with `leerie: script '<name>' is forbidden for this run` when `$npm_lifecycle_event` is listed, else execs the repository's own script shell: the package manager named by `$npm_config_user_agent` (`npm`/`pnpm`/`yarn`) is asked `config get script-shell` with `npm_config_script_shell`/`pnpm_config_script_shell` unset, the answer cached in `LEERIE_REPO_SCRIPT_SHELL_<pm>` for nested scripts; `undefined`/`null`/empty, the guard itself, or no package manager → `/bin/sh`. Yarn classic reads the npm variable. Benched P10 (bench/f2 `tools/guard.sh`, `runtime_layer.py`). |
| `_blt_shell_argv(cmd, forbidden, *, source=None)` / `ForbiddenByTask` | The one gate for every orchestrator-side launch of a repository command. `cmd` is a shell string → `["bash", "-c", cmd]`, or an exec argv (a list) → that argv as `str`s, checked as `shlex.join(cmd)`; either raises `ForbiddenByTask(hit)` when `_forbidden_command_hit` matches `cmd` or `source` (the command `cmd` was rendered from, e.g. before report flags). Used by `_measure_blt` (its `forbidden` keyword is required; a refusal is the unmeasured record with `skip_kind: "forbidden_by_task"`), `_capture_failing_test_ids` (None, logged), `_run_acceptance_file` (None), `_acceptance_parse_probe` (None with the reason), `_ci_run` (`{rc: None, passed: False, skipped: "forbidden_by_task"}`), `_cov_contained` (`{rc: None, timed_out: False, skipped: "forbidden_by_task"}`; its callers read `rc != 0` as not settled), `_ensure_worktree_deps` (a refused `install` entry makes it return False, a refused `build` entry is skipped; both logged) and `_settle_by_execution`'s launch (verdict `none`). `tests/test_blt_forbidden_gate.py` fails when a shell launch (`["bash"|"sh", "-c", …]`, `shell=True`, `create_subprocess_shell`) appears outside this helper; when any launch (`subprocess.*`, `asyncio.create_subprocess_*`, `os.exec*`/`spawn*`, `_run_proc`, `_run_streaming`, `_run_contained`) runs an argv that is neither a literal led by a `LEERIE_OWNED_HEADS` program nor a name bound from this helper earlier in the same function, outside the test's `EXEMPT` launchers (each with its reason; a stale entry also fails); or when a call passes it an empty forbidden list. |

A matched `tests` axis goes to `_scoped_test_replacement` instead. |
| `_scoped_test_replacement(tree, st, canonical, hit, forbidden, *, log_prefix)` | Replaces a forbidden test command. Otherwise it computes `_changed_files(tree, base)`, then `_coupled_test_files(repo, HEAD, changed, globs)`, keeps the coupled files present in `tree`, and renders them with `_acceptance_cmd`. `_uncovered_item_lines` (one `- [ ] item <i>: <item>` line per `item_coverage.uncovered` index) under "Required items no planned subtask claimed". `_format_pr_end_state_section` renders the second as `## Not verified by this run`, after `## Needs human verification`; the heading is in `_PR_END_STATE_HEADINGS`. `tests/test_needs_human_sources_render.py` derives the written sources from the code (module `*_GAP_SOURCE` constants and literal `"source"` values in dict literals of functions that write `needs_human_verification`), requires each in the table or `{required_item, blocker}`, renders one entry of each, and builds one state holding an entry of every source — the derived ones and the ones read from other state — asserting "Needs human verification" holds exactly the typed external lines. `_untyped_sites(state) -> list[dict]`: the `site_claims` rows with `surface_other: true` and a string `site_id`. `_untyped_site_lines(state) -> list[str]`: one `- [ ] <file> <symbol> (<site_id>): <resolution>[ — the delivery judge: <evidence>]` line per such row whose `settlement.settled` is not true; `_pr_not_verified` lists them (above). `_settle_untyped_sites(st, untyped, samples, tree, record, cache)`: called by `_delivery_judge_unmet` with the contract pack's samples when it asked the contract and `_untyped_sites(st.data)` is non-empty; per row, a vote is a `site_verdicts` entry for its `site_id` with `resolved: true`, a non-empty `cites` of dicts, each `_verify_delivery_cite` status in `_DELIVERY_CITE_OK`; writes `settlement = {settled: 2*votes > len(samples), votes, samples, evidence}` (`evidence`: the first non-vote's `evidence` when it said `resolved: false`, else "claimed resolved, but its citations do not verify on the tree"; 600 chars), then saves. The contract pack's prompt then carries a SITES RESTING ON AN UNTYPED RESOLUTION section (`site_id`, `file`, `symbol`, `resolution` per site) and its turn budget `+2` per site (90 ceiling); `site_verdicts` cites are made relative to the judge's checkout like the items' (`_relative_cites`). Its verdict, with `near_stage`, when `new` is non-empty, else None. None too when `before` is None, `pre_sha` is empty or staging's head is not `post_sha`, and nothing is measured. Recorded by `_measure_axes` for a `carry` `tests` result it would store in the memo: `kept` plus each file of the report's `cases` (a file passed when none of its cases is `failed` or `load_error`) on `tree_sha`. Emptied by a result with no cases or no `failing_ids`, a red one with no failing ID, or a failing case with no file. `_all_carried_result`: `{ran: True, measured: True, passed: True, command: cmd, whole_command, carried, failing_ids: [], failing_id_files: {}, summary}`. |
| `_axis_report_request(st, tree, cmd, label) -> dict \| None`, `_read_axis_report(st, tree, res, request) -> list[dict] \| None`, `_acceptance_report_spec(cmd, path, files=(), *, beside_output=False)`, `_RUNNER_REPORTS_BESIDE_OUTPUT` | DESIGN §9 *Which failures are new*. An axis in `failing_ids_axes` runs `request["run_cmd"]`, its verdict and report one run: `{run_cmd, env, source, kind, report, own}` from `_runner_command` and the `beside_output` spec (vitest `--reporter=default --reporter=json --outputFile.json=<path>`; None for a `stdout:` runner). None too with no runner, a compound script call, or a `pre<name>`/`post<name>` script, and the axis then runs as written with `_attach_failing_ids` on failure. `_measure_blt(..., report=request)` runs it (`_blt_shell_argv(run_cmd, forbidden, source=source)` after the check of `cmd`), its result naming `cmd`. `_read_axis_report` reads and removes the file beneath the measurement directory and sets `failing_ids`, `failing_id_files`, `failing_messages` (each message's first 400 characters) and the file durations, returning the report's cases; None with `res` untouched when the run reached no verdict or left no readable report. |
