With no selection under a `scoped_replacement`, it logs `tests measured whole — running all <n> test file(s) of the scoped replacement`. `carry` on `tests` with a clean tree and a good install: `_carried_selection` after the memo miss and the install, the run `selection["command"]`, the result gaining `whole_command` and `carried`, and stored under `_blt_memo_key(axis, whole_command, tree_sha)`; an empty selection runs nothing (`_all_carried_result`). Passed by `_measure_final`, `_refresh_test_id_diff`, `_ratchet_test_ids` and the acceptance gate's `acceptance-pre`/`acceptance-post` (each also with `failing_ids_axes={"tests"}`); `acceptance-post-again` (`memo=False`, no report) and every per-subtask and baseline call do not. `_orchestrator_results_digest` adds `carried: <n> test file(s) …` beneath a carried axis, and `near stage only: <n> of <m> test file(s) …` beneath a near stage. `_measure_final` passes `near_of` for a round's post measurement: a result with `near_stage` goes to `_confirm_final_test_failures`, and a confirmed new ID makes it the next round's `pre` (no `pre` measurement) and the round's `post`; otherwise `post` is measured again, which runs the closure. |
| `_py_source_graph(repo, rev)` | The Python import graph at `rev` (`files`, `imp`, `importers`), cached in `_SOURCE_GRAPHS` under `(repo, "py:" + rev)`. Sources come from `_git_tree_sources(repo, rev, (".py",))`. `_py_module_index` maps every dotted suffix of a path's package parts to it. `_py_imports` reads `import` / `from … import` with `ast`: `from a import b` names `a.b` when that is a module, else `a`, and relative imports resolve against the importer's package. |
| `_git_tree_sources(repo, rev, exts=_JS_SRC_EXT)` | `exts` selects the source suffixes read. |
| `_jsonc_strip_comments(text)` | `tsconfig.json` text without `//` and `/* */` comments, scanned outside JSON strings only. `_ts_path_aliases` uses it, then drops trailing commas. Before, a regex strip took the `/**/` inside an `include` glob such as `"src/**/*.ts"` for a comment, the JSON stopped parsing, and every alias was lost. Measured on barnacle: no `@/` import edge was resolved, so 0 test files were coupled to `src/lib/random.ts` instead of 4 direct importers. |

The planner ctx carries `process_constraints = {forbidden_commands: [{command, scope}]}` when it is non-empty.

`_confirm_final_test_failures`: when the final `tests` result carries
`scoped_replacement`, the base list is `[]` rather than
`baseline_failing_ids`. Every final failure becomes a candidate, and B\*'s
base reruns keep one the base also fails from being called new.

**Process kills (N8; DESIGN §9 *A worker never kills a process by name*).**
Applied by `claude_p` to every worker whose `allowed_tools` include bare
`Bash` (`_tools_reach_bash`): deny rules, the notice and the hook travel
together.

| Name | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `PROCESS_KILL_DENY_COMMANDS` / `_process_kill_denials()` | `("pkill", "killall", "killall5", "xargs kill")` through `_forbidden_command_denials`: `Bash(<cmd>)` and `Bash(<cmd> *)` each. |
| `PROCESS_KILL_NOTICE` | The paired `NOTE FROM ORCHESTRATOR:` body: kills by name or pattern (`pkill`, `killall`, `fuser -k`, `kill` fed by `pgrep`/`pidof`/`xargs`, wrapped or not) are denied because other workers share the process table; stop your own background command with the `TaskStop` tool, or `kill` a PID saved from `$!`. |
| `_process_kill_hit(command)` | The kill form `command` runs, or `None`: over `_forbidden_argvs(command, keep_xargs=True)` (an `xargs` head is kept as a leading `"xargs"` word instead of unwrapped), a head in `pkill`/`killall`/`killall5`; `fuser` with `-k`/`--kill`; `kill` behind `xargs`; or `kill` in the same command as a `pgrep`/`pidof` argv. `kill -0`, `kill -s 0`, `kill -l`/`-L`/`--list` are never a kill. Reads argv heads only; never raises. |
| `_hook_payload(raw)` | `(forbidden, deny_kills)` from the hook's decoded payload — a dict `{"forbidden", "kills"}`, or a bare list (forbidden only). An entry is a command string or `{command, scope, test_roots, package_name}`. `_forbidden_command_hook_settings` sends only those keys of an entry, never its evidence quote. |
| `_forbidden_command_hook_settings(forbidden, deny_kills=False)` | As above, with the dict payload; `None` only when the list is empty and `deny_kills` is false. |
| `_forbidden_command_hook_main` | Denies a forbidden command first (`forbidden command: <cmd> — the task forbids it`), else, when `kills` is set, a `_process_kill_hit` (`process kill by name or pattern (<form>) — …TaskStop…`). |
| `scripts/forbidden-command-hook.py` | Decodes the payload and the event itself, and for a kills-only payload allows any command whose text contains neither `kill` nor `fuser` without importing leerie (an import costs ~1.7 s where no bytecode cache can be written, and the hook runs before every Bash call of every acting worker). `tests/test_process_kill_deny.py` pins that every recognised kill form passes that prefilter. |

### Existing tests the run changed (DESIGN §8)

Report-only. `phase_finalize` calls `_tracked_test_report(_run_repo(st),
base, run_branch)` once, after `_decide_outcome`, in a thread and
fail-open, and stores it as `tracked_test_report`. It compares each
test-shaped file (`_TRACKED_TEST_RE`) present at the run's own start with the
final tree through `_tt_facts` (`_tt_mask` blanks comments and masks strings
and JS regex literals; `_tt_stmt` reads an assertion statement or a case's
title to its end, whitespace- and trailing-comma-free). `_tt_facts` also returns `lines`, a
Counter of the file's non-blank lines with comments blanked and whitespace
collapsed; `lines_removed` / `lines_added` are the multiset differences
against the base (uncounted: blank, comment-only, moved or reindented lines)
and are stored, and rendered as `setup or other lines changed: N removed,
M added`, only when `lines_removed` exceeds the removed assertions plus
removed cases (`_tracked_test_report`); a file with that alone is listed.
Nothing reads the
record except `_pr_tracked_test_lines`, which `_format_pr_end_state_section`
renders as `## Existing tests changed by this run` (listed in
`_PR_END_STATE_HEADINGS`, so a worker-written copy is stripped), and which
therefore reaches the launcher's fallback through `pr_end_state` and draft
PRs alike. It changes no `outcome`, gate or retry; `_redrive_weakened_tests`
(escalation gate (b)) is separate and untouched. The one thing it shows that
is measured is `existing_behaviour.changed` (below): a file's cases that fail
in their base form are its first entries, `- fails in its base form on this
tree: <id>`; for a case in `existing_behaviour.cause_unkept`, `- the task
changes what this existing test pins, but <why>: <id>`; for one in
`cause_open`, `- fails in its base form; whether the task changes what it
pins is an open question (<qids>): <id>`; else, for a case in
`existing_behaviour.moved_literal`, `- existing test pins text the run moved
to the message files: <id> — <literal> -> <key> in <message file>` (up to 3
literals). A `task_required` row with `cause` is listed before them as `-
existing test changed because the task changes what it pins (<causes>;
<qids>): <id>`.

### Existing tests run in their base form (DESIGN §8)

DESIGN §8 *What an existing test pins on the base holds on the tree that
ships*. Measured, never read: no prompt, judge or text rule.

| Name | Contract |
|---|---|
| `_base_form_case(rel, globs)` | Whether an `_is_test_file` path is a test-case file the check runs: its basename matches one of `_BASE_FORM_CASE_RES` (`_BASE_FORM_JS_RE`: `<stem>.test.`/`.spec.` + `[cm]?[jt]sx?`; `test_*.py`/`*_test.py`; `*_test.go`; `*_test.rb`/`*_spec.rb`/`test_*.rb`) or it is a cargo integration test (`_is_cargo_integration_test`). Not a helper, `conftest.py`, fixture or snapshot. |
| `_base_form_snapshot(rel)` | A JS test-case file's `__snapshots__/<name>.snap` beside it; None for any other file. |
| `_base_form_files(repo, base, head, globs)` | `(files, unsupported)` from `git diff --name-status --no-renames base head`: each `_is_test_file` path present at `base` (status not `A`) that `head` modified or deleted; `unsupported` those whose extension is in `_BASE_FORM_NO_REPORT_EXT` (`.java .kt .kts .scala .groovy .cs .fs .ex .exs .php .swift`: no runner leerie reads a report from, `_RUNNER_REPORTS`), `files` the rest that `_base_form_case` accepts. |
| `_base_form_writable(repo, rev, rel)` | Whether `rel` at `rev` may be written or removed without following a link, read with one `git ls-tree -z rev -- <each directory on the way> rel`: no directory on the way is a row of its own (a directory pathspec lists its contents; anything else is a row), and `rel` is absent or mode `100644`/`100755`. |
| `_base_form_place(st, repo, base, files, trees)` | `(pairs, taken, removed)`: each file's `base` blob written to `<run-dir>/base-form/<base[:12]>/<path>` and paired with its own path, which it replaces; a JS file's base `__snapshots__/<name>.snap` paired the same way when the base had it. A file is `taken`, and never placed, when it or its snapshot is not `_base_form_writable` at one of `trees`. `removed` maps each tree to the paths removed there: every `_base_form_case` file `git diff --name-status base <tree>` shows added (`A`) and writable, and a non-taken JS file's snapshot the tree has and the base did not. |
| `_base_form_regressions(st, caps, staging, before, *, label, log_path, reach_of=None)` | Base `_diff_base(st)`, after staging's branch head. `reach_of` (a round's start): files narrowed to those `reach_of..after` touched or `_change_reach` reaches, all of them when its reach is unknown. One `_capture_failing_test_ids(staging, test cmd, files=<the files not taken>, replace=<pairs>, remove=removed[after], serial=True)` on staging's committed view, in a held-out sandbox (the base form is never on disk). No failing ID: done. Else a `base-form-base` helper worktree at `before` with `_ensure_worktree_deps`, and B\* over the failing IDs, every run of either side with all the pairs and that side's `removed`, whichever files it runs (`_confirm_sized` when every ID has a file, else `_confirm_new_failures` over all of them; a failed checkout or install gives every candidate `no_verdict`). Returns `{base, before, after, files, unsupported, changed: [{id, file, message}], unmeasured: [file], unsettled: [id], verdict, unmeasured_reason?}`: `changed` is B\*'s `new`, IDs as the report names them (the file runs at its own path), `unmeasured` the taken files (`unmeasured_reason` "the base form's path is a link or not a file"), every file when no test or scoped command resolves or the first run gave no report, and the files of `no_verdict` IDs; `unsettled` the `budget_short_unsettled` IDs. A load failure (`<file> :: (file failed to load)`) is a case like any other. |
| `_base_form_reason(changed)` | `"N case(s) an existing test pinned on the base fail when the base's own test file is run against this tree (existing_behaviour_changed): …"`, at most `_BASE_FORM_SHOWN` (5) IDs, each prefixed by its file when the ID does not name it, and `(+k more)`. |
| `_check_existing_behaviour(leerie_dir, st, caps, models, efforts)` | Run before the delivery re-drive and as phase 5's last step before `phase_finalize`, after the final `_refresh_shipping_test_id_diff`: `_base_form_regressions(staging, before=_diff_base(st))` stored as `existing_behaviour` with `tree_sha` (`_view_tree_sha`); when the record has `changed` and no `error`, `_base_form_classify(...)` then `_base_form_questions(..., models, efforts)` (a raise of either is logged; a cause already found stays, its question open); then `_apply_base_form_rulings`, `_existing_behaviour_task_required`, and, without `error`, `literal_restored` = `_base_form_literals_restored(st, rec)`. Reused when that tree is recorded without `error`: the rulings, `_existing_behaviour_task_required` and `literal_restored` are applied again and saved (an answer given since applies). A raise of the measurement is stored as `{error, changed: [], …}`. Then `_set_base_form_gap`. |
| `_redrive_base_form_notes(st, staging)` | The re-drive's `base_form_case` notes, from `existing_behaviour` when its `tree_sha` is staging's `_view_tree_sha` and it has no `error`: one per file of `changed` less the cases in `cause_open` and `cause_unkept`, `{kind, key: "base-form:<file>", file, base, cases[], messages[] (ANSI stripped, ≤ `_REDRIVE_BASE_FORM_MESSAGE` = 300 chars), exercised: [file]}`; `[]` otherwise. Computed once per pass into `delivery_redrive.base_form_open`. |
| `_redrive_base_form_open(rec)` | The notes still to drive: a file with no finished attempt (an `interrupted` one does not count), as found; a file with one finished attempt whose cases are not all in `fixed`, once more for the rest only, `escalation: True`; a file with two finished attempts, none. |
| `_redrive_base_form_attempt(rec, notes, *, rnd, group, model, effort)` | Before a group's worker runs: appends `{round, group, cases, escalation, model, effort, outcome: "interrupted", fixed: []}` to `base_form_driven[key].attempts` (replacing a trailing `interrupted` one). |
| `_redrive_base_form_settled(rec, notes, ge)` | After the group's verdict: the last attempt's `outcome` (`rolled_back` + `reason`, `no_change`, `rollback_failed`, or `kept` + `fixed` = `ge.base_form_fixed` ∩ its cases); the file's `fixed` accumulates. |
| `_redrive_base_form_unkept(rec, rnd, group, reason)` | A kept group the flip rollback (`roll_back_flips`) later rolls back: each of its `kept` base-form attempts (matched by `round`, `group`) becomes `rolled_back` with `reason` and no `fixed`; that file's `fixed` is recomputed from its still-`kept` attempts and its `outcome` is its last attempt's. |
| `_redrive_base_form_fixed(st, caps, staging, notes, *, label, log_path)` | `_base_form_regressions(staging, before=_diff_base(st))` on the group's commit: the notes' cases no longer `changed`, excluding `unmeasured` files and `unsettled` IDs; `[]` when the check raises or measured nothing. |
| `_moved_literal_evidence(repo, base, head, literals, globs=None)` | The message files `git diff --name-only base head` names that match `_MESSAGE_FILE_RE` (`(^|/)(messages|locales?|i18n|translations|langs?)/[^/]+\.json$`, case-insensitive) and exist at `head`, parsed, every string value with its dotted key (`_message_values`). For each literal of `literals` (`{kind: string|regex, text, flags?}`; at least 2 non-blank characters; a regex only when `_PLAIN_REGEX_TEXT_RE` fullmatches its text): (c) a value equal to it (string), or for a regex the first value that is the whole text (case-insensitive only with its own `i` flag), else the first that contains it — that value's file and key are the row's; (a) the production files `git grep -l -F [-i] -e <text> <base>` names that have a `_JS_SRC_EXT` suffix, are not `_is_test_file`, are not message files, and whose base content with comments blanked (`_tt_mask`) holds the text; (b) the first such file that is gone at `head` or whose head content, comments blanked, no longer holds it. Returns `[{literal, kind, ci, file, message_file, key}]` (`ci`: a regex read case-insensitively), at most one row per literal. |
| `_base_form_moved_literals(st, caps, staging, rec, facts_out=None)` | For each `rec["changed"]` row whose file has a `_JS_SRC_EXT` suffix: the file's base blob written once to `<run-dir>/base-form-facts/<base[:12]>/<file>`, the case's facts from `_probe_case_facts_placed(st, _measured_tree(staging), <that copy>, <dir>/`_BASE_FORM_FACTS_PREFIX` (`.leerie-base-form.`)`<basename>, <case title>)` — a sibling path, because a held-out sandbox places a file and refuses one the view already holds, and `_moved_literal_evidence` over its `literals`. `{case_id: evidence}` for the cases with evidence; each case's facts are also put in `facts_out[case_id]` when given. A raise is logged and the cases it did not reach stay unclassified. |
| `_MOCK_MISSING_EXPORT_RE` | `No "([\w$]+)" export is defined on the "([^"]+)" mock`: vitest's fixed message (export, module). |
| `_js_named_imports(code, module)` | The names a `import [type] [default,] { a, b as c } from "<module>"` in `code` imports by name. |
| `_mock_missing_export_evidence(repo, base, head, rel, base_src, message)` | The `mock_missing_export` cause: `_MOCK_MISSING_EXPORT_RE` in `message`, and the production modules `_contradiction_code_files(_js_source_graph(repo, head), [(rel, base_src)])` returns whose head text (comments blanked, `_tt_mask`) imports the export from the module by name (`_js_named_imports`) while their base text, when the base has them, does not. `{kind: "mock_missing_export", module, export, files[], lines[]}` (`lines`: up to 2 head lines per file calling `<export>(`, at most `_BASE_FORM_QUESTION_SHOWN` = 8), or None. |
| `_base_form_cause_key(cause)` | `"moved-literal"` for every `moved_literal` cause; `"mock-<module>-<export>"` (non-`[A-Za-z0-9_.-]` runs as `-`, ≤ 80 chars) for a `mock_missing_export`. The question id is `_BASE_FORM_QID_PREFIX` (`"intent-base-form-"`) + key. |
| `_message_file_values(repo, rev)` | `(file, dotted key, value)` of every `_MESSAGE_FILE_RE` file at `rev` that parses (`_message_values`). |
| `_moved_literal_forms(cause, values)` / `_moved_literal_kept(lits, cause, values)` | The forms a moved literal reads as: the literal, every key whose value equals it (`literal_kind` `regex`: whose value contains it, case-insensitive), that key's last dotted segment, and every value under those keys. Kept when a string literal of `lits` is one of the forms, or a `_PLAIN_REGEX_TEXT_RE` regex literal (its own `i` flag) matches one. |
| `_base_form_run_form_check(base_facts, head_facts, causes, values)` | `""` when the run's form of a case still asserts the new behaviour, else why not: `"its base form's facts could not be read"`; `"the run's form of the test no longer has this case"` (head facts with `error` or no `title`); `"the run's form of it makes <nh> assertion(s) where the base form made <nb>"` (`asserts` counts); `"the run's form of it no longer asserts the moved text `<literal>` or a message key holding it"` (a `moved_literal` cause not `_moved_literal_kept`). |
| `_base_form_classify(st, caps, staging, rec)` | `rec["moved_literal"]` = `_base_form_moved_literals(..., facts_out)`; `rec["causes"]` = per case its moved literals as `{**evidence, kind: "moved_literal", literal_kind}`, plus a `_mock_missing_export_evidence` cause for each JS/TS case whose message matches; `rec["run_form"]` = per caused case `_base_form_run_form_check(base facts, head facts, causes, _message_file_values(repo, after))`, the head facts read from `rec["after"]`'s blob written to `<run-dir>/base-form-facts/<after[:12]>/<file>` and placed beside the test as `_BASE_FORM_RUN_FORM_PREFIX` (`.leerie-run-form.`)`<basename>` (`_probe_case_facts_placed` over `_measured_tree(staging)`), base facts read the same way (`_base_form_case_facts`) when the moved-literal pass did not. Never raises: a case it did not reach has no cause or no check. |
| `_base_form_cause_question(key, rows)` | The question, built from the facts. `moved-literal`: "The run moved user-facing text out of the repository's production code into its message files: N text(s) from M production file(s), for example:" + up to 8 lines `- "<literal>" from `<file>`, now a value in `<message_file>` (key `<key>`)` + "K existing test case(s) assert that text as the base wrote it (for example …) and fail on the run's tree; they can pass only if the production code holds that text again. Does the task ask for this text to move out of the production code into the message files?". `mock-…`: "The run changed production code so it now imports `X` from `M`, which it did not at the run's base: N production file(s), for example … — in lines such as: … K existing test case(s) mock `M` without `X` and fail on the run's tree (for example …); they can pass only if that production code stops using `X`. Does the task ask for the change that makes this production code use `X` from `M`?" |
| `_base_form_questions(st, caps, rec, models, efforts)` | Groups `rec["causes"]` by `_base_form_cause_key`; registers each group's question once per run (`_register_intent_question`, source `base_form`, context `{cause, cases, literals: [[literal, literal_kind, file, ci]]}`; an existing question's `literals` gain the new ones) and `_settle_intent_question`s it (a raise is logged; the question stays open). Never stops. |
| `_apply_base_form_rulings(st, rec)` | Per case of `rec["changed"]` with causes, its questions' `_intent_decision`s: any `no` — it stays; any undecided — it stays and `cause_open[id]` lists the open qids; all `yes` and `run_form[id]` not `""` (or absent: "the run's form of it could not be read") — it stays and `cause_unkept[id]` says why; else it moves to `task_required` as `{**row, cause: [kinds], qids}`. Sets `cause_open` and `cause_unkept` always; whether any moved. |
| `_base_form_literals_restored(st, rec)` | For each `base_form` question decided `yes`, each context literal whose file exists at `rec["after"]` and whose text there, comments blanked, holds it again (`re.I` when `ci`): `[{literal, file, qid}]`. |
| `_literal_restored_reason(rows)` | "N text(s) the task asked to move into the message files are back in the production code they left (literal_restored): `<literal>` in <file>; …" (≤ `_BASE_FORM_SHOWN`, then `(+k more)`). |
| `_base_form_closure(repo, rev, case_files, globs=None)` | The case files' test closure at `rev`: the case files; every runner configuration (basename matching `_RUNNER_CONFIG_GLOBS`) and each repository path its text contains that is test-side, matches `_JS_SUPPORT_PATH_RE`, or has `setup` in its basename; each `conftest.py` on a `.py` case file's directory chain; then, transitively from those, every import (JS/TS and Python graphs at `rev`) that is test-side — `_is_test_file`, the JS graph's `support`, or a `__mocks__` path. |
| `_base_form_closure_breach(repo, base, pre_sha, post_sha, case_files, globs=None)` | Each path `git diff --name-status pre_sha post_sha` changed that is in `_base_form_closure(pre_sha)` and is not, at `post_sha`, the same blob as at `base` ("<path> (its cases' test closure, not put back exactly as at the run's base)"), or is a test file present at `pre_sha` and absent at `base` ("<path> (a test this run added)"); `[]` when none. |
| `_redrive_dropped_cases(st, caps, staging, pre_sha, *, label, log_path)` | The test-case files present at `pre_sha` that staging's commit modified or deleted (`_base_form_files(pre_sha, after)`), their `pre_sha` forms placed in place of the commit's (`_base_form_place(base=pre_sha)`, held-out sandbox) and run once (`_capture_failing_test_ids(serial=True)`), and the commit's own forms run once: the case IDs the start forms pass that the commit's forms do not report. `[]` when nothing moved or no such file; None when a run gives no report, a path is taken, or no scoped test command resolves. |

| `_set_base_form_gap(st, rec)` | One `needs_human_verification` entry, source `BASE_FORM_GAP_SOURCE` (`"base_form"`, group "Regression checks the run could not settle"), naming the `unmeasured` ("gave no verdict"), `unsupported` ("has no runner leerie reads a report from") and `unsettled` entries and an `error`; cleared when there are none. |

Where it runs:

- **Each acceptance repair round and each delivery re-drive group that
  commits** — `_ratchet_exec(…, base_form=True)` calls
  `_base_form_regressions(staging, before=pre_sha, reach_of=pre_sha)` before
  the ID diff, whether or not either side of the diff was measured; when it
  has `changed` and no `error`, `_base_form_classify`, then (when `models`
  is given: the acceptance gate's and the re-drive's calls pass theirs)
  `_base_form_questions`, then `_apply_base_form_rulings` on it — a raise
  there is logged and leaves every case changed. Returned as `base_form`
  with `base_form_changed` (the IDs still `changed`). A raise of the
  measurement is `base_form: {error}` with nothing changed. `_delivery_ratchet`
  carries `base_form_changed` beside `new_failures` (each flags the
  `execution` items); `_ratchet_rollback_reason` gives `"changed what an
  existing test pinned on the base: " + _base_form_reason(...)` after the
  two existing reasons, so `_settle_round` rolls the round back through
  `_roll_back_round` with it. In `_run_delivery_redrive` a group's
  `base_form_changed` is recorded and voids it; `_redrive_rollback_reason`
  names it. `_acceptance_confirm_red_axis`'s call does not pass the flag.
- **Before the delivery re-drive** — `_run_phases` calls
  `_check_existing_behaviour` after the final CI parity and before
  `_run_delivery_redrive`, which turns its `changed` into `base_form_case`
  notes (`_redrive_base_form_notes`; DESIGN §8 *A fix that keeps both, on
  opus when sonnet could not*). They join the pass's notes (the start check,
  the log line, `notes`), are routed by `_redrive_route` like a control, and
  each is live in a group while `_redrive_base_form_open` offers its key and
  no earlier group of the same round drove it. A group holding an
  `escalation` note drives those notes alone, with
  `models["implementer"] = MODEL_BASE_FORM_ESCALATION` and
  `effort = EFFORT_BASE_FORM_ESCALATION` (also for its clean-tree re-ask).
  On a moved HEAD the group records `base_form_fixed`
  (`_redrive_base_form_fixed`), `test_closure_breach`
  (`_base_form_closure_breach` with the base-form notes' files) and
  `dropped_cases`
  (`_redrive_dropped_cases`, `["(not measured)"]` for None); a group with a
  base-form note that fixed none of its cases (and no set case) is
  `zero_progress`; any `test_closure_breach` voids it
  (`_redrive_rollback_reason`: "it changed what a base-form case's test is,
  which only putting the original back may: …"), and so does any
  `dropped_cases`
  (`_redrive_rollback_reason`: "it dropped case(s) of a test it changed
  that still hold on its commit, or could not show it kept them: …").
  `_redrive_note` renders the note as `{kind, test_file, base_form: "git show
  <base>:<file>", failing: [{case, failure}]}`, adds its sentence to the
  kinds paragraph, and a `BASE-FORM CHECK:` paragraph when one is present.
- **The tree that ships** — `_check_existing_behaviour` (above).
  `_decide_outcome` adds `_base_form_reason(existing_behaviour.changed)` to
  the reasons when it is non-empty, and
  `_literal_restored_reason(existing_behaviour.literal_restored)` when that
  is (`unconverged`).
  `_unmeasured_on_shipping_tree` adds, when `existing_behaviour` exists: its
  `error` or a lone `unmeasured_reason`, a `tree_sha` that is not
  `_shipping_tree(st)`, or its `unmeasured` files. No record (the check
  never ran: a state from before it) adds nothing.

### Finalize evidence: site tokens, contract literals, whole-PR review (DESIGN §5, §8, §9)

All three are advisory: none gates, re-drives or changes `outcome`. Order in
`_run_phases` after `phase_execute`: `_warn_site_token_leaks` →
`_extract_contract_literals` → `_run_delivery_prejudge` (sections from
`_delivery_typed_evidence`) → `_run_pr_review` → `_run_final_conformance`
(section from `_format_pr_review_section`) → `_run_delivery_recheck` (evidence
recomputed). Each call there is wrapped so an exception is logged and the run
continues. After the last step that commits (the second
`_check_existing_behaviour`) and `_stop_for_intent_questions`, and before
`phase_finalize`, `_run_shipping_pr_review` runs, wrapped the same way; in
`phase_finalize`, `_record_pr_review_shown` runs after
`_record_unmet_evidence`, before `pr_end_state` is rendered.

**Site tokens (N7a; bench q5/n7a FROZEN.md, v2 boundaries).**

| Function | Contract |
|---|---|
| `_warn_site_token_leaks(st, leerie_dir)` | Tokens: `_site_tokens_from_scope(defect_scope)` (the audit's `ground_truth.inline_examples[].site_tokens`, lower-cased). Added lines: `_diff_added_lines(staging, ["<working_branch>..HEAD"])`. A hit: the first token matching `(?<![A-Za-z0-9])tok(?![A-Za-z0-9])` case-insensitively, one per added line, unless `_site_token_guard_line(path, line)`. No base-tree skip. Persists and returns `site_token_warnings` `[{token, file, added_line (≤200), report_example (≤300, the inline example the token came from, a `site_identifying` one first)}]`; `[]` without tokens, `working_branch` or staging. Called again by `_delivery_typed_evidence(refresh_tokens=True)` at the recheck. |
| `_site_token_guard_line(path, line)` | True only when `path` is a test file (`_SITE_TOKEN_TEST_FILE_RE`: `.test/.spec.[cm]?[jt]sx?`, a `test/`, `tests/` or `__tests__/` directory, `_test.py`/`_test.go`, `test_*.py`) AND the line, after one leading `(export )?(const\|let\|var) X(: T)? = [` and a trailing `];`, splits on `,` into ≥1 parts each a quoted literal or `/re/flags` literal whose inner text is `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+`. |
| `_site_token_evidence_section(hits)` | `None` with no hits. Else the `SITE-TOKEN HITS` section: each hit `{token, file, added_line, token_source: {report_example, audit_marked_site_identifying: true}}`, at most `_SITE_TOKEN_PER_FILE` = 3 per file and `_SITE_TOKEN_SENT` = 30 in all (by file, then diff order), stating "Showing k of N" when cut; aimed at any item forbidding naming the sites, a lead not a verdict. |

**Contract literals (N7d v7e; bench q10 FROZEN_v7.md, `tools/check.py::check7e`).**

| Function | Contract |
|---|---|
| `_contract_risks(st)` | `(key "<sid>#<i>", sid, i, risk)` for every `risk_register` entry of kind `external_contract_assumption`, sids sorted. |
| `_extract_contract_literals(leerie_dir, st, caps, models, efforts)` | One `contract_extractor` call per risk not yet in `contract_literal_checks` (concurrent under `max_parallel`; `bump_workers` each), payload `RISK {sid, kind, detail, where}` + `SUBTASKS [{id, title≤200}]` from `plan.json`. Code sets `counterpart_sid` to null unless it is a plan id other than the owner, and `literal_unverified: true` when the literal is not a substring of `detail + " " + where`. Writes `{owner_sid, risk_index, detail, where, extracted}` or, on `WorkerError`/timeout, `{…, error}`. |
| `_contract_literal_verdict(ext, *, tree_files, grep, own_files, cp_added)` | Pure: `(flag, why)`. In order: a `string_value`/`identifier` literal not matching `^[A-Za-z_$][\w.:\-$]*$` → no flag; no counterpart, no literal, unverified, or kind `other` → no flag. `route_path`: no app-router `app/**/(page\|route).(t\|j)sx?` file → none; a page/route whose trailing non-group, non-dynamic dirs equal the literal's static segments → honoured; the literal (query stripped) on a non-test counterpart added line followed by a char not in `[\w\-/]` → honoured; else FLAG "route not served". `string_value`/`identifier` (matchers: same-quote-delimited, or `(?<![\w$])lit(?![\w$])`): `symbol` on a counterpart added line → honoured; counterpart not integrated (`cp_added` None) → FLAG iff absent from the tree outside `own_files`; on a counterpart added line → honoured; on a final-tree line of a non-test code file (`_CONTRACT_CODE_FILE_RE`) outside `own_files` → honoured unless a non-test counterpart added line carries a near-variant token (`_contract_near_variant`: equal after lower-casing and dropping `-_.:`, a plural, or a ≥4-char raw prefix ≥ half the length ending inside a word) → FLAG; else FLAG "counterpart diff missing". Deviation from the bench: code/test-file patterns also take `.py .go .rb .rs .java .kt .php .cs .swift` and `test_*.py`/`_test.(py\|go)`. |
| `_integration_commit(staging, sid)` | The newest first-parent commit at HEAD whose subject is `leerie: integrate <sid>`, or None. |
| `_check_contract_literals(st, leerie_dir)` | For each record with `extracted`: tree = `git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD`, grep = `git grep -n -F -e <literal> HEAD`, owner/counterpart sides from `_integration_commit` (`_diff_added_lines([sha^1, sha])`, `git diff --name-only`). Writes `flag`, `why`; returns the flagged records; never raises. |
| `_contract_literal_evidence_section(flagged)` | `None` or the `CONTRACT LITERAL FLAGS` section: up to 20 `{owner_sid, counterpart_sid, literal, literal_kind, why, risk}`. |
| `_delivery_typed_evidence(st, leerie_dir, *, refresh_tokens)` | `(sections, {site_token_hits, contract_flags, intermittent_regressions?, sweep_instances_left?})` (the INTERMITTENT REGRESSIONS section, from `test_id_diff`, is added when rows exist; the SWEEP INSTANCES STILL PRESENT section, `_sweep_evidence_section` over `_sweep_still_present(required_items, <run>/worktrees/staging)`, when a derived sweep item has an instance left) for `_delivery_judge_unmet(typed_evidence=…)`; the prejudge uses the recorded hits, the recheck recomputes them; both rerun the contract check. The counts are recorded as `delivery_gate.evidence_before` / `evidence_after`. Never raises. |

`_delivery_judge_unmet(…, typed_evidence=None)` appends each section to every
pack prompt before the closing instruction; with none the prompt is
unchanged.

**Whole-PR review (N2f; bench n2f `harness/review.py`).**

| Function | Contract |
|---|---|
| `_run_pr_review(leerie_dir, st, caps, models, efforts)` | Skipped when `pr_review` exists, the final conformance already recorded `_final`, or `base_sha`/staging is absent. Otherwise `_pr_review_record(st, caps, models, efforts, staging, base_sha, <staging HEAD>, "pr-review")`, persisted as `pr_review`. |
| `_pr_review_record(st, caps, models, efforts, staging, base, head, name)` | One `pr_reviewer` call on commit `head`, returning `{base, head, model, effort, diff_cut, findings[], n_findings, n_verified, at, error?}`. Payload: `TASK`, each `_d1_report_sources` report in full, `REQUIRED ITEMS` (`_pr_review_items`), base and head, the changed files, and `git diff <base>...<head>` cut at `_PR_REVIEW_DIFF_MAX` = 600000 chars (saying so). The payload ends with `COMMANDS YOU MAY RUN`, which lists each granted command prefix, or says none is granted. It then names the canonical test command when a granted prefix covers it, and otherwise says no test runner is granted and not to try running tests. Its `cwd` is `async with _judge_checkout(st, staging, name, rev=head, share_ignored=True)` (DESIGN §8 *A worker that does not commit never runs in a tree leerie measures*), not autonomous, `PR_REVIEW_MAX_TURNS` = 150, tools from `_pr_review_tools(staging, repo_root) -> (allowed_tools, prefixes, canonical)`. That is `_widen_inspect_tools(INSPECT_TOOLS, staging)` plus `Bash(<form>:*)` for each `_full_suite_runners(_canonical_test_command(repo_root))` spelling it lacks. The whole-suite deny and notice still come from `claude_p`, because those tools reach the runner. Nothing is restored afterwards: whatever the reviewer made goes with its checkout. Each finding gets `_verify_pr_finding` against that checkout, inside the same `async with`. A `WorkerError`/timeout is recorded as `error`. |
| `_run_shipping_pr_review(leerie_dir, st, caps, models, efforts)` | DESIGN §9 *The review the PR shows is of the tree that ships*. None, nothing run, when `pr_review` is absent or has no `head`, `base_sha`/staging is absent, `_shipping_commit`/`_shipping_tree` is "", or `_commit_tree(st, pr_review.head)` equals `_shipping_tree(st)`. Returns `pr_review_shipped` unchanged when `_commit_tree` of its `head` equals `_shipping_tree(st)` (resume). Otherwise logs `phase 5: whole-PR review again — the run branch moved from <a> to <b> since the review`, runs `_pr_review_record(..., base_sha, _shipping_commit(st), "pr-review-shipped")` and persists it as `pr_review_shipped`. Read only by `_record_pr_review_shown`. |
| `_shipping_commit(st)` / `_commit_tree(st, commit)` / `_run_repo_rev(st, rev)` | The run branch's head commit; a commit's tree; `git rev-parse --verify -q <rev>` in `<run_dir>/repo` — each "" when it does not resolve. `_shipping_tree` is `_run_repo_rev` of the run branch's `^{tree}`. |
| `_record_pr_review_shown(st)` | In `phase_finalize` after `_record_unmet_evidence`. Removes `pr_review_shown`, then, when a review without `error` exists (`pr_review_shipped` first, else `pr_review`) and `_shipping_commit`/`_shipping_tree` resolve, checks each `verified` finding with `_pr_quote_check` against `git show <shipping commit>:<path>` in the run's own repository and writes `pr_review_shown` `{source, reviewed (its head), reviewed_tree, commit, tree, findings (those whose quote is there, `line_ok` of that file), n_quote_gone}`, logging `pr review: <n> finding(s) of `<source>` quote code the run branch's head <c> no longer has — not listed` when any is dropped. |
| `_pr_advisory(state)` review block | From `pr_review_shown` only: heading `Whole-PR review findings (reviewed on `<commit>`, the run branch's head; each quote checked in the file there)` when `reviewed_tree == tree`, else `Whole-PR review findings (reviewed on `<reviewed>`; each quote checked again in the file at `<commit>`, the run branch's head)` (12-character shas); a line per finding `- `<path>:<start>-<end>` [<kind>] <explanation>`, the range only when `line_ok` is true; at most `_PR_ADVISORY_SHOWN`; then `- <n> more of that review's findings quote code the file at `<commit>` no longer has; not listed (state.json `<source>`)` when `n_quote_gone` > 0. |
| `_pr_review_items(st)` | `[{item_id: "<i>", text}]` over `required_items` by position, plus `{item_id: "contract", text: JSON {defect_shape, sites}}` when the audit is applicable with sites. |
| `_verify_pr_finding(f, staging, items)` | `{path_exists, quote_ok, line_ok, item_id_norm, item_known, span_ok, verified}`: `quote_ok`/`line_ok` are `_pr_quote_check(f, <git show HEAD:<path>>)` (`_pr_finding_path`: `path` without a leading `./`) — the quote, whitespace-normalised, raw or with leading `+`/space diff markers stripped, must occur in the file; `line_ok` whether its first line sits within ±5 of `[line_start, line_end]` (None when not located); `item_id` normalised by `(?:item\s*\|i)?#?\s*(\d+\|contract)`; `span_ok` whether every `...`/`…`-separated piece of `item_span_quote` occurs case-folded in that item's text. `verified` = `quote_ok`. |
| `_format_pr_review_section(st)` | `None` or the final conformer's `ADVISORY WHOLE-PR REVIEW` section: verified findings only, at most `_PR_REVIEW_SHOWN` = 20 `{kind, item_id, path, line_start, line_end, quote, explanation}`, told to check each against the code and fix the real ones; nothing waits on it. Added to every final-conformance round. |

### Intent conflicts — `plan_item_checker`, `intent_resolver`, `set_aside` (DESIGN §11)

DESIGN §11 *Intent conflicts are settled with evidence, else asked*. Every
question is a record in `st.data["intent_questions"][qid]`; its decision is
the user's answer (`st.data["answers"][qid]`, one of `INTENT_ANSWERS` =
`("yes", "no")`) when there is one, else the resolver's `answer` when its
verdict is settled and trusted, else none (pending).

| Function | Contract |
|---|---|
| `_plan_item_check_prompt(items, subtasks)` | The B1 rendering: `REQUIRED ITEMS` (`[item i] text`, each part on a `    part:` line), then `PLAN`, one `=== subtask <id>` block per subtask with each of `PLAN_CONFLICT_FIELDS` = `(intent, scope_note, investigation_notes, success_criteria_seed, verify)` under `--- <field>:` (`(empty)` when empty; `verify` rendered one line per criterion, `criterion: argv joined by spaces`, `_plan_field_text`), closing `Return the conflicts JSON.` |
| `_verify_plan_conflict(c, items, subtasks)` | True iff `item_index` names an item, the whitespace-collapsed `item_quote` is non-empty and inside that item's text or one of its parts, `subtask_id` names a subtask, `field` is in `PLAN_CONFLICT_FIELDS`, and the collapsed `plan_quote` is non-empty and inside that field's text (B1's scoring rule). |
| `_run_plan_item_check(st, subtasks, caps, models, efforts)` | One `plan_item_checker` call (`PAYLOAD_ONLY_TOOLS` in `_payload_only_cwd`, `PLAN_ITEM_CHECK_MAX_TURNS` = 6, never autonomous) when `plan_item_check` is not in state and there are required items. Persists `plan_item_check = {conflicts[], rejected, error?}` (verified conflicts only) and returns the conflicts. A worker failure records `error` and returns `[]`: the check is a source of questions, never a gate. |
| `_plan_intent_check(st, subtasks, caps, models, efforts)` | Runs `_run_plan_item_check`, groups the verified conflicts by subtask, registers one question per subtask (`qid` `intent-plan-<sid>`, source `plan`, text `_plan_conflict_question`) and settles each (`_settle_intent_question`). Called in `_run_phases` right after the plan is scheduled and wiring-checked, before `_validate_plan`/`_write_plan`; followed there by `_stop_for_intent_questions(st)` and `_apply_plan_intent_rulings(st, subtasks)`. |
| `_apply_plan_intent_rulings(st, subtasks)` | For each `plan` question whose decision is `yes`: in its subtask, every conflicting `plan_quote` in a text field is replaced by `[intent ruling <qid>: <decision text>]`, and every `verify` criterion whose rendered line contains one is dropped; the subtask's `_intent_rulings` lists `{qid, decision, evidence}`. Deterministic from state, so a resume re-applies it to the rehydrated `plan_snapshot`. `no` leaves the subtask. |
| `_register_intent_question(st, qid, source, question, context)` | Adds `{qid, source, question, context, at}` when `qid` is new (`source` in `INTENT_SOURCES` = `("plan", "set_aside", "contradiction", "base_form")`); returns the record. |
| `_intent_base(st, tree)` | The commit the resolver reads: `base_sha` once `phase_execute` has cut the run branch; before the cut — the plan check, source (a), runs there on every fresh run — the HEAD commit of `tree`, the planning worktree, which `_ensure_planning_worktree` reset to the working branch's tip and every judgment worker before the cut read. `None` when neither exists. |
| `_settle_intent_question(st, qid, caps, models, efforts)` | When the question has neither an answer nor a verdict: one `intent_resolver` call in `_judge_checkout(st, tree, "intent-resolver", rev=_intent_base(st, tree))` (staging when it exists, else the planning worktree), `INTENT_RESOLVER_TOOLS` (`INSPECT_TOOLS` + `Read,Grep,Glob,Bash(git blame:*)`), `INTENT_RESOLVER_MAX_TURNS` = 60, `add_dirs=[<run-dir>/task-files]`, user prompt `_intent_resolver_prompt`. Records `verdict = {decision, answer, status, evidence[{source, quote, locator, ok}], trusted, model, effort, at}` or `{error}`; a worker failure or an untrusted verdict leaves the question pending. |
| `_verify_intent_evidence(item, *, task, task_files, tree, base)` | `True`/`False`/`None` for one evidence item, whitespace-collapsed containment: `code` in `git show <base>:<path>` (path = locator before the first `:`, backticks and a leading `./` or the checkout's own path stripped, no `..`); `task` in the task text; `report` in the task file(s) whose name the locator names, else in any; `history` in `git show <sha>` (the locator's first 7–40 hex token), raw or with diff markers stripped; `web` → `None` (unchecked). |
| `_intent_verdict_trusted(evidence)` | At least one `code`/`task`/`report`/`history` item and every one of them `ok`. |
| `_intent_decision(st, qid)` | `"yes"`, `"no"` or `None`, as above. |
| `_stop_for_intent_questions(st)` | The questions with no decision. None: returns. On a terminal (`sys.stdin.isatty()`), each is asked once through `_ask_questions` (the question, the resolver's decision text and its quotes; the answer must be in `INTENT_ANSWERS`, re-prompted until it is) and stored in `answers`. Otherwise `_defer_questions(st, pending)` writes them to `pending-questions.json` (`{id, question, choices: ["yes", "no"], why_underivable, evidence[]}`) and exits `EXIT_NEEDS_ANSWERS`. Not gated on `--clarify`. Called after the plan check, after `_run_final_conformance` and before `phase_finalize`. |
| `_set_aside_findings(st, unmet)` | The findings the final conformer is shown, by id: `pr-<k>` for each shown verified `pr_review.findings[k]` (its item from `item_id_norm` when `item_known`), `unmet-<i>` for each confirmed-unmet item `i`, `unmet-contract` for the confirmed-unmet defect contract. |
| `_adjudicate_set_asides(st, res, findings, caps, models, efforts)` | For each `set_aside` entry of a round's result naming a shown finding on a required item: registers `intent-finding-<finding_id>` (source `set_aside`, text `_set_aside_question`), settles it, and when the decision is `yes` appends an unfixed `solution_defects` entry `{kind: "set_aside_refused", where: <path:lines or item>, concrete_case: <finding>, why_ships_a_defect: <decision>}` to `res` and marks the question `driven`. An entry naming no shown finding, or a finding on no required item, is recorded on the question log only. Called in every final-conformance round after `_validate_conformance_result`. |
| `_defect_identity(d)` | `(kind, where, concrete_case)`, stripped. `_run_final_conformance` keeps `settled_res`, the last round's result that reached the end of its round (validated, set-asides adjudicated); when the last round broke before that (malformed, rolled back), `residual_defects` is the last round's actionable defects plus `settled_res`'s, deduplicated by this identity (DESIGN §9 *An unfixed solution defect keeps the final loop going*). |
| `_apply_set_aside_answers(st)` | After `_stop_for_intent_questions` following the final conformance: each `set_aside` question decided `yes` and not `driven` is appended to `conformance._final.residual_defects` (same row shape) and marked `driven`, so the delivery re-drive drives it. Idempotent. |
| `resolve_intent_conflict(st, qid, question, context, caps, models, efforts)` | Source (c), called by `_contradiction_intent`: registers a `contradiction` question, settles it and returns its decision (`None` while open). |
| `_pr_intent_lines(state)` | The body of `## Intent decisions` (in `_PR_END_STATE_HEADINGS`, rendered by `_format_pr_end_state_section` after `## Still failing when the run ended`): one line per question with a decision — the source, the question, the decision (`yes`/`no`, by `resolver` or `user`), the resolver's decision text, its first verified quotes — and one per question still open. |

`_format_pr_review_section` gives each shown finding its `finding_id`
(`pr-<k>`); `_format_unmet_required_items_section` gives each item
`unmet-<i>` and the contract `unmet-contract`; both tell the conformer that
a finding it does not fix goes in `set_aside`.

### Cap resolvers

Same resolution pattern as existing resolvers (CLI → env → TOML →
default): `resolve_judgment_check_rounds`,
`resolve_planner_check_rounds`,
`resolve_implementer_confidence_retries`, `resolve_planner_samples`,
`resolve_token_probe_cache_sec`.
Env vars: `LEERIE_JUDGMENT_CHECK_ROUNDS`,
`LEERIE_PLANNER_CHECK_ROUNDS`,
`LEERIE_IMPLEMENTER_CONFIDENCE_RETRIES`, `LEERIE_PLANNER_SAMPLES`,
`LEERIE_TOKEN_PROBE_CACHE_SEC`.

---

## 6. Caps and their values

Defaults in `DEFAULT_CAPS` and the per-worker `claude_p` call sites.

### Code-enforced caps (the orchestrator counts these)
| Loop | Cap | On cap |
|------|-----|--------|
| subtask continuations (re-spawns of an implementer for the same subtask — both context-exhaustion handoffs *and* mid-execution clarifications consume from the same budget) | 3 (`subtask_continuations`) | return `blocked`; at the wave boundary re-driven from `subtask_redrive_rounds`, then settled `unconverged` |
| corrective retries of a *retryable* failure per subtask (`failed_retries`) | 1 | return `failed` |
| orchestrator-level conformer rounds per subtask (`conformance_rounds`) | 3 | exit the conformance loop; any residuals become `conformance_warnings` on the subtask result — never `failed` / `blocked` (DESIGN §9 *Post-work conformance*). Backgrounding-retry (Pattern B) warnings from round N are injected as structured CRITIC-pattern feedback into round N+1. |
| concurrent orchestrator-run build/lint/test measurements (`blt_parallel`) | 2 | not an escalation — a gate. Distinct from `max_parallel`, which bounds *workers*: a worker is admitted by `_await_worker_memory_admission` and enrolled in a cgroup, while a BLT command `_run_streaming` starts carries no `memory.max`/`pids.max` of its own (DESIGN §6 *Orchestrator-run build/lint/test is bounded, not contained*). Held around the command only — never the memo lookup (a hit must stay free) nor the install. Sized lazily on the running loop by `_blt_semaphore`, since a module-level `asyncio.Semaphore()` binds to whatever loop is current at import. 2 is a floor, not a measured optimum; it matters most under `--subtask-tests full`. |
| implementer completeness re-drives per subtask (`completeness_retry_rounds`) | 1 | the conformer's gating `solution_defects` axis found concrete behavioral gaps in the implementer's diff (DESIGN §9 *The one gating axis: solution completeness*). Each round folds the found defects into the implementer's next attempt as mandatory criteria and re-drives it (a **separate** counter from `implementer_confidence_retries`/`failed_retries`/`subtask_continuations`). Each round **also draws from the shared per-subtask re-drive counter** (`subtask_redrive_rounds`, below): it runs only while `_redrive_allowed(st, caps, sid)` holds and consumes one `redrive_rounds[sid]` via `_consume_redrive`, so the two budgets cannot multiply. On exhaustion the subtask returns `blocked` with the residual defects named; at wave end it is re-driven only if the shared counter has room, else settled `unconverged` — never silently advisory. Independent of `--strict-conformer`, which governs only the advisory build/lint/test/residual axes. |
| shared re-drive rounds per subtask (`subtask_redrive_rounds`) | 2 | one persisted counter per subtask, `state.data["redrive_rounds"][sid]`, drawn by every re-drive kind — the completeness gate's in-settle re-drive, the wave-end re-drive of a `blocked` subtask (`_redrive_blocked_subtasks`) and each coverage re-drive round (`_redrive_uncovered_subtasks`); integration repair rounds do NOT draw from it (they have their own counter, `integration_repair_rounds` below). `_redrive_allowed(st, caps, sid)` is `redrive_rounds[sid] < subtask_redrive_rounds and _redrive_time_left(st, caps)`; `_redrive_time_left(st, caps)` is `redrive_spent_sec < redrive_budget_sec`; `_consume_redrive(st, sid)` increments and saves. Per-attempt budgets (`failed_retries`, `implementer_confidence_retries`, `subtask_continuations`) are not re-drives and do not draw from it. On exhaustion the subtask is settled `unconverged` (`_settle_unconverged`) — never left `blocked` — and its dependents settle `unconverged` without running (DESIGN §13 *One re-drive budget per subtask*). |
| run-level re-drive wall time (`redrive_budget_sec`) | 14400 s (4 h) | the hard stop for every re-drive in the run: `state.data["redrive_spent_sec"]` accumulates, per wave, the longest in-settle re-drive (clock opened by `_open_redrive_clock(st, sid)` at the first in-settle re-drive, closed by `_close_redrive_clock` when the settle returns) plus the wall time of each wave-end re-drive round. Once spent, `_redrive_allowed` is False for every subtask. Measured worst run: 15,017 s. |
| clean-tree re-asks (`clean_tree_reasks`) | 2 | `_clean_tree_gate`: how many times a worker that left its tree dirty (`_tree_dirt` not empty) is re-asked — its own CLI session resumed by `_clean_tree_reasker`, one worker each — before its caller rolls the round back and records the porcelain lines (DESIGN §8 *A worker leaves its tree clean*; IMPLEMENTATION *Clean-tree gate (I1)*). Replaces the caps of the deleted re-drive leftovers commit. |
| final delivery judge crash retries (`delivery_judge_crash_retries`) | 1 | `_run_delivery_detection`: a `final` judge that raises `WorkerError` or times out is asked again up to this many more times; then its unread items are `unknown` and listed under "Needs human verification" (`delivery_judge_unknown`), never `met` (DESIGN §8 *Every post-execution verdict is of the committed tree*; review round 13 claims M1). |
| coverage re-drive threshold (`coverage_uncovered_share`) | 0.25 | `_redrive_uncovered_subtasks`: a completed subtask is re-driven when at least this share of its changed executable lines is executed by no test, after the importing-test settle (DESIGN §9 *Changed lines no test executes are re-driven*). Rounds come from `subtask_redrive_rounds`. |
| B\* host CPU-pressure gate (`confirm_psi_cpu_max`) | 40 | `_confirm_gate` waits until `_host_cpu_psi()` — `some avg10` of the **host** file `_HOST_PSI_CPU_PATH = "/proc/pressure/cpu"`, never a cgroup's `cpu.pressure` — is below this value. |
| B\* gate wait (`confirm_gate_wait_sec`) | 300 s | the gate polls every 2 s for at most this long; a timeout (or an unreadable PSI file, which is logged and treated as a timeout) escalates the pairs below. |
| B\* base/final rerun pairs (`confirm_pairs`) | 3 | interleaved base, final, base, final … reruns per confirm (DESIGN §9 *Which failures are new*). |
| B\* escalated pairs (`confirm_pairs_escalated`) | 5 | pairs used instead when the gate timed out. |
| B\* confirm wall-time budget (`confirm_budget_sec`) | 1800 s | bounds one confirm's or discovery's reruns, its clock started when `_confirm_gate` returns — the gate wait is bounded by `confirm_gate_wait_sec` instead, so one call takes at most `confirm_gate_wait_sec` + `_CONFIRM_GATE_POLL_SEC` + `confirm_budget_sec` (2102 s at the defaults; DESIGN §9 *Which failures are new*, step 2), plus at most 1 s once (the `max(1.0, …)` floor under one rerun's timeout) and the uncharged host build-slot and (test axis) BLT-gate (`blt_parallel`) waits; a sized confirm's later passes (`_confirm_sized`) share it — each gets what the ones before it left, starts only with at least 1 s left and waits on no second gate (CI parity's passes share one base worktree, set up on the first pass and removed after the last, outside the budget); each rerun's timeout is the remaining budget, and `_capture_failing_test_ids`' as-written retry gets only what its rerun has left. A rerun the budget cuts short is not a run and ends the confirm (`budget_exhausted: true`); a candidate every finished rerun agreed on is then `new` / `confirmed` and listed in `budget_short`, or `budget_short_unsettled` where the caller's observation needs a finished pair or rerun (DESIGN §9 step 4); otherwise the usual typing applies. Not an operator setting (no flag, env var or `leerie.toml` key); 0 or less runs no gate and no rerun in every B\* user — the two confirms, `_intermittent_discovery`, `_acceptance_discover` and `_settle_by_execution`: every base-paired candidate is `budget_short_unsettled`. |
| B\* intermittent discovery repeats (`confirm_intermittent_repeats`) | 20 | serial reruns of the import-coupled tests on the final tree, per final-tree ID diff (`_intermittent_discovery`), inside their own `confirm_budget_sec`; 0 disables discovery. Only the files whose 20 repeats all fit the budget by measured duration run; the rest are recorded skipped (never fewer repeats). At a 10.5% per-run failure rate, 20 repeats find the test with p ≈ 0.89; at p = 0.1, 2 repeats only 19%. |
| held-out intermittent discovery repeats (`acceptance_intermittent_repeats`) | 10 | serial reruns, per confirmed set evaluation, of each defect file with held cases that did not end failing (`_acceptance_discover`), inside `confirm_budget_sec`, stopping at the first held case failing with no resource signature (DESIGN §8 *A held case that fails again is a failure, not a flake*). Clamped to 10 (`_ACCEPTANCE_INTERMITTENT_MAX`); 0 disables discovery. At the replay's p = 0.546 per run, a set misses the defect with probability 0.454¹¹ < 0.02%. |
| dependency install retries (`deps_install_retries`) | 2 | per worktree per process: a memo hit in `_ensure_worktree_deps` on a failed install installs again while `_DEPS_FAILED[<tree>]` (failed installs in a row) is at most this; and `_retry_failed_baseline` measures a baseline whose install failed again at most this many times per process (DESIGN §9 *A failed install is no measurement*). 0 never retries. Not an operator setting. |
| total worker invocations per run | 2000 (`--max-workers`, also `LEERIE_MAX_WORKERS` env or `max_workers` in `leerie.toml`) | the cheap, runtime backstop in `State.bump_workers()`: raises `WorkerError`, abort, state saved for `resume`. The complementary early check is `check_budget_feasibility()` at the plan/execute boundary (after `_schedule()`, before `_write_plan()`) — it estimates remaining `claude -p` calls from the planner output and `die()`s with `EXIT_BUDGET_INFEASIBLE=11` and a recommended `--max-workers` value before any implementer spawns. See DESIGN §13 *Budget feasibility — fail fast at the cheapest moment*. |
| per-subtask call-estimate (for the feasibility preflight) | 3.0 (`subtask_call_estimate`) | not a runtime gate; consumed by `check_budget_feasibility()` as the per-subtask multiplier in its remaining-call estimate. Raised from 2.5 to absorb the per-subtask conformer completeness gate (DESIGN §9), whose `solution_defects` finding re-drives the implementer up to `completeness_retry_rounds` times. |
| per-subtask re-plan estimate | 1.5 (`replan_decompose_estimate`) | not a runtime gate; consumed by `check_replan_affordable()` as the per-subtask multiplier when projecting a re-plan's cost. A re-plan re-runs the whole P1 decomposition, not just the planners — the larger half of the cost. Rounded up so the preflight errs toward refusing a marginal re-plan. |
| budget-preflight safety margin | 1.15 (`budget_safety_margin`) | not a runtime gate; consumed by `check_budget_feasibility()` as the multiplier on `total_estimate` before comparison to `max_total_workers`. |
| concurrent workers within a wave | 5 (`--max-parallel`, also `LEERIE_MAX_PARALLEL` env or `max_parallel` in `leerie.toml`) | throughput throttle. Per-worker cgroup memory containment (see row below) keeps an OOM inside one worker's cgroup, so the wave-level parallelism can be high without risking cascade to sshd / lima-guestagent. |
| turns per `claude -p` call | per worker (below) | worker stops; implementer → `incomplete-handoff` |
| per-worker wall-clock (`worker_timeout_sec`) | 5400 s (90 min) global cap, **lowered per worker type by `TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_PER_WORKER` via `resolve_worker_timeout(worker, caps)`** | worker killed; implementer → `incomplete-handoff`. **Two tiers.** With no explicit global (`resolve_worker_timeout_explicit()` re-walks CLI/env/TOML, not a comparison to the default), `resolve_worker_timeout(worker, caps)` applies the table, bounded by the global; a worker absent from it keeps the full 5400 s. With an **explicit** global (`--worker-timeout SEC` / `LEERIE_WORKER_TIMEOUT` / `worker_timeout_sec`), that value wins outright and the table is **bypassed** — tracked as its own cap, `caps["worker_timeout_explicit"]`, mirroring `resolve_worker_memory_max`. The three timeout log/handoff messages (`_run_implementer`, `_run_conformer`, `_run_final_conformance`) report `resolve_worker_timeout(...)`, not the global. **Values are derived, never chosen:** each is `min(cap, max(_WORKER_TIMEOUT_FLOOR_SEC=600, ceil(p99*3), ceil(max*1.2)))` computed from `tests/fixtures/worker_duration/summary.json` (15,951 real calls across 21 worker types, regenerated by `scripts/measure/worker_durations.py <state-root>`; re-executed by `tests/test_worker_duration_distribution.py`). The `max*1.2` term is load-bearing: `planner`'s p99*3 is 5,091 s while its observed maximum is 5,247.6 s, so a p99-only rule would kill a run inside its own derivation corpus — the guard pushes planner to the cap instead. A fired timeout retries once (`_TIMEOUT_RETRY_MAX = 1`), unlike a `WorkerError`, which keeps the full round budget. |
| held-out acceptance sets (`acceptance_sets`) | 5 | number of `acceptance_writer` sets written per run (DESIGN §8 *Held-out acceptance tests*); writers run under a `max_parallel` semaphore. Five so that the two highest-indexed valid sets can stay unseen by the repair rounds. |
| acceptance repair rounds (`acceptance_repair_rounds`) | 2 | at most this many high-effort conformer repair rounds when any held-out set fails on the integrated tree (each failure confirmed under B*); the residual then ships (non-blocking) and feeds the next run. |
| acceptance rewrite rounds (`acceptance_rewrite_rounds`) | 1 | per-set counter (`acceptance.sets[].rewrite_rounds`): at most this many rewrites of a held-out set still failing after the repair rounds, whatever triggered it (M1/M2, the set audit, the surrogate witness); bumped and saved before the writer runs, so a resume never repeats one. Also bounds the writer's own-start retry when no defect case fails (`_write_acceptance_set`). |
| set-audit samples (`set_audit_samples`) | 3 | independent `set_auditor` samples per audit; the verdict is the union of their quote-verified `set_defect` cases (DESIGN §8). |
| defect-scope applicability samples (`applicability_samples`) | 3 | `phase_defect_scope_audit` honours `applicable: false` only when this many independent `defect_scope_auditor` samples all say so; the first `applicable: true` sample is used. A crashed sample is no vote, drawn again within `applicability_samples + 2` attempts in all; if the votes run out first, false stands on the votes cast (DESIGN §5). |
| forbidden-command samples (`forbidden_command_samples`) | 3 | `forbidden_command_extractor` draws per `phase_classify`, run beside the classifier; the persisted list is the union of the classifier's and every sample's entries that pass the quote check (`_forbidden_draw_union` → `_process_constraints`). 0 leaves the classifier's draw alone. |

Not an escalation: it sizes prompts, and every judge-bound item lands in exactly one pack. Bench Q7/D1 arm (c). |

Feedback only: a sweep still over them when the classifier's rounds run out is derived in full. |

One item's samples run in order and stop at the first confirm; 0 disables the falsifier. |

Persisted as `integration_gate[sid].repair_rounds`. |

Each crash: `_rescue_integrator_work` (a new rescue ref, never overwritten), `git merge --abort`, `git reset --hard <pre_sha>`, `integrate.sh` again, a fresh integrator. Spent → `_back_out_unmerged` with a reason naming every rescue ref (`kind: integration_backed_out`, `integration_content_loss` on `risk_register[sid]`) and the wave continues — never `die()` (DESIGN §7 *The integrator* crash paragraph). |
| CI-parity coverage epsilon (`ci_coverage_epsilon_pct`) | 0.01 | `_ci_coverage_fired`: a coverage threshold fires only when the final percentage is below its minimum, below the base's by more than this many points, and its glob covers a file the run changed (DESIGN §9 *The repository's own merge checks run too*). |
| planned-overlap extra waves (`overlap_extra_waves`) | 3 | `_schedule(plans, overlap_extra_waves)` → `_serialize_planned_overlap` splits same-wave subtasks whose planned `files_likely_touched` intersect into sub-waves, keeping a pair (largest overlap first, then wave, then ids) only while the whole plan's extra waves stay within this cap (DESIGN §5 *Planned file overlap is serialised*). 0 disables. |
| per-worker idle-event warning (`worker_idle_warn_sec`) | 300 s (5 min) | log a `no stdout events in <gap>s` warning naming the worker, its PID, and any stderr tail. Observation-only — the worker is NOT killed. |
| per-worker cgroup memory cap (`worker_memory_max_bytes`) | auto-derived via `_auto_worker_memory_max` → `_worker_memory_ceiling(slice_max)` from the shared `leerie.slice/memory.max` budget alone (broker `slice` verb; `_cgroup_slice_info`): `max(_WORKER_BUILD_PEAK_BYTES, min(_WORKER_BUILD_PEAK_BYTES * _WORKER_MEMORY_CEILING_MULTIPLIER, slice_max // 2))` — a **fixed isolation ceiling**, deliberately **independent of the live sibling count and of `max_parallel`**, since `memory.max` is a ceiling, not a reservation (DESIGN §6). Falls back to the legacy `/proc/meminfo`-derived basis (`_auto_worker_memory_max_legacy`, VM RAM split across `max_parallel + 1` slots, floored at 8 GiB) only when no broker/slice budget is readable. **Raised to the repo's measured build peak** once the base-health baseline has measured one: `max(ceiling, 1.25 × peak + 0.3 GiB)` (`_apply_blt_peak`; §6 *Spawn-held enrollment and measured sizing*), re-applied on resume. Contention is handled by admission in **two stages**, never by shrinking caps. Stage 1, `_degrade_max_parallel_for_wave(max_parallel, build_peak_bytes=None)`, runs once at wave entry and is synchronous: it returns the largest N in `[1, max_parallel]` with `slice_max - unreclaimable >= demand * N` and sizes the wave's `asyncio.Semaphore` accordingly. Stage 2 is the per-spawn gate: before spawning, `_await_worker_memory_admission` blocks (polling every 5s, up to 10 min) while measured slice headroom (`slice_max - unreclaimable`, never `memory.current`) is below `demand * (1 + in-flight workers)`. Reservations are bounded by worker LIFETIME — the gate returns a token from `_active_admissions` and `_invoke_admitted` releases it in a `finally`. Pinned by `tests/test_memory_admission_degrade.py`. Overridable via `--worker-memory-max SIZE` / `LEERIE_WORKER_MEMORY_MAX` / `worker_memory_max` in `leerie.toml` (bypasses the derivation only — the admission gate still runs). Suffixes K/M/G/T accepted. **Reconciled against the repo's own declared Node heap** (`resolve_worker_memory_max`, `_declared_node_heap_bytes`): an explicit `--max-old-space-size` in a `package.json` script overrides Node's host-derived default regardless of container size, so `_declared_node_heap_bytes` follows the package-manager indirection through `scripts`, matching all four V8 spellings via `_pm_script_candidates` (splits on shell separators first — a whitespace split alone misses `"build&&node"`). Deliberately over-inclusive: a missed script under-sizes the cage and OOMs the worker; an extra candidate costs nothing. A declared heap overrides whatever `NODE_OPTIONS` leerie injects for that subprocess (P9), sharing the headroom constant `_NODE_HEAP_HEADROOM_BYTES` = 2432 MiB with P9's own injection so both read one name, not a duplicated literal (`tests/test_resolve_worker_memory_max.py` AST-pins it; `test_node_heap_headroom_is_2432_mib` pins the value). When the resolved cap undershoots `declared heap + headroom`: an auto-derived cap is raised unclamped; an explicit override is refused with an actionable `die()`; when even the whole slice can't fit the declared heap, `die()`s naming the shortfall. Regression: `tests/test_worker_heap_ceiling_reconcile.py`, `tests/test_worker_memory_heap_reconcile.py` | the kernel OOM-kills inside the worker's cgroup; sibling workers, the orchestrator, and host-side services are not eligible victims. Enforcement goes through the **cgroup broker** (`scripts/cgroup-broker.py`), driven by the dropped-privilege orchestrator over a descriptor it inherits (no socket path). It creates `<V2_ROOT>/leerie.slice/leerie-w-<sid>` (cgroup **v2** — `V2_ROOT` is `/sys/fs/cgroup` rootful/Fly, or the systemd-delegated user slice under rootless containerd via `LEERIE_CGROUP_V2_ROOT`) or the split `pids/`+`memory/` hierarchies at the fixed `V1_ROOT` (v1/hybrid, never rootless) and sets its `memory.max`. Local nerdctl needs the launcher's cgroup bind-mount (`bind-propagation=rshared` rootful, plain bind rootless) + `--cgroupns=host`; Fly's microVM exposes cgroupfs directly. `_cgroup_probe` asks the broker to round-trip a create+enroll+destroy, and `_enforce_and_record_cgroup_containment` `die()`s before the first worker if it fails (unless `--dangerously-allow-uncapped`). See DESIGN §6 *Memory containment*. |
| per-worker memory demand estimate (`worker_demand_estimate_bytes`) | resolved at run start, and again once phase 1½ (or a resume) has the build/lint/test commands read from the repository, by `_resolve_memory_caps(caps, repo_root)` — which also resolves the ceiling, from `caps["worker_memory_max_cli"]` (the operator's `--worker-memory-max`, recorded at start) — through `resolve_worker_demand_estimate()`: `_WORKER_BUILD_PEAK_BYTES` unless the repo declares a Node heap, else `declared_heap + _NODE_HEAP_HEADROOM_BYTES`. Threaded to both admission surfaces as a parameter, not module state. **Distinct from the ceiling above** — that bounds one worker, this predicts what one will use. | `_degrade_max_parallel_for_wave` shrinks the wave; `_await_worker_memory_admission` blocks the spawn. Both fall back to `_WORKER_BUILD_PEAK_BYTES` when the key is absent, so the three entrypoints that build their own caps (`run_recapture_deps`, `run_rebaser`, `_replay_capture`) are unchanged. |
| per-worker cgroup PIDs cap (`worker_pids_max`) | 2048, or `--worker-pids-max N` / `LEERIE_WORKER_PIDS_MAX`, never `leerie.toml` (positive integer; `resolve_worker_pids_max` `die()`s on bad input). Raised, never lowered, to `ceil(1.5 × measured pids peak)` once the base-health baseline has measured one (`_apply_blt_peak`; §6 *Spawn-held enrollment and measured sizing*) | kernel rejects further `fork()` from any process in the worker cgroup once the count is reached. Sized against measurement (DESIGN §6 *Detecting PID exhaustion*): leerie's own suite peaks at 33 concurrent PIDs, so 2048 sits well above the workload and a worker near it is leaking rather than testing. Raise it per-repo for suites heavier than the default. |
| aggregate container memory cap (`leerie.slice/memory.max`) | auto-derived in `scripts/container-entry.sh` (PID 1) from VM `MemTotal` in `/proc/meminfo`: `MemTotal - max(1 GiB, 12.5%)`, reserving headroom for PID 1 + VM daemons (sshd, lima-guestagent, containerd). Overridable via `LEERIE_CONTAINER_MEMORY_MAX_BYTES` (raw bytes); `0`/`max` opts out. No CLI flag / `leerie.toml` key / `DEFAULT_CAPS` entry — the cap is applied by the shell entrypoint before the Python orchestrator starts. Best-effort: any read/write failure leaves the slice uncapped. Sets `memory.max` (RAM) only, not `memory.swap.max`. | when the slice's aggregate RSS exceeds the cap the kernel triggers a *cgroup-scoped* OOM (`CONSTRAINT_MEMCG`) that kills a process *inside the container*, instead of a VM-wide *global* OOM that would kill unprotected host-session processes and orphan the container. See DESIGN §6 *container boundary's hidden precondition*. |
| auth/quota backoff budget (`auth_retry_max_sec`) | 300 s (5 min) | `claude_p()` retries the worker with `tenacity` exponential backoff (initial 15 s, max 120 s, ±5 s jitter) on 401/429/529/auth-message envelopes. Budget exhausted → `WorkerError` naming the subscription cap (401/429/auth-text) or the transient overload (529). See §3 *Auth/quota backoff*. Terminal auth failures (`_is_terminal_auth_failure`, below) never reach this loop. |
| rate-limit wait ceiling (`max_rate_limit_wait_sec`) | 21600 s (6 h), or `--max-rate-limit-wait SEC` / `LEERIE_MAX_RATE_LIMIT_WAIT` / `max_rate_limit_wait_sec` in `leerie.toml` (positive integer; `resolve_max_rate_limit_wait_sec`, same `_resolve_positive_int_pref` ladder as `resolve_worker_timeout_sec`) | Longest rate-limit reset `main()`'s `except RateLimitedExit` arm will sleep through before it stops auto-resuming and takes the `out_of_credits` disposition instead (worktree-only cleanup, resume hint, `EXIT_LOCKED`). Sized to the subscription's windows: the five-hour session limit is bounded and worth waiting out; the weekly limit resets at a fixed per-account instant that can be days away, and sleeping on it holds the run-directory flock. Keyed on the **computed wait**, never on `rateLimitType`, so a renamed limit type cannot disable it. See DESIGN §6 *A ceiling on the wait*. |
| credential near-expiry warning threshold (`credential_expiry_warn_sec`, proposed 90 min) | 5400 s (90 min) | Launcher-side preflight (`_check_claude_credential_ttl`, staging block) run only when the resolved credential is a *subscription* token — the long-lived `$CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` has no `expiresAt` and is exempt. Parses `claudeAiOauth.expiresAt` (ms epoch) and compares to now. Already expired → refuse to launch, print `claude /login`. Inside the threshold → warn with the exact expiry and point at `claude setup-token`, but still launch. `expiresAt` absent or malformed → proceed silently. Never hard-code a TTL duration; `expiresAt` is the sole source of truth. |
| multi-token probe cache floor (`token_probe_cache_sec`) | 180 s | `resolve_token_probe_cache_sec` (CLI → `LEERIE_TOKEN_PROBE_CACHE_SEC` env → `token_probe_cache_sec` in `leerie.toml` → default), same `_resolve_positive_int_pref` pattern as `resolve_confidence_rounds`. Minimum interval between re-probing a given token's usage/runway (§3 *Multi-token rotation*). |
| mechanical-feedback rounds for judgment workers (`judgment_check_rounds`) | 3 | classifier, reconciler, provision, overlap judge, integrator, adherence gate, and the six independent adversarial verifiers (`classification_judge`, `wiring_judge`, `provision_judge`, `integration_judge` — DESIGN §8; `task_coverage_judge` and `no_work_judge` are NOT bound by this budget: each is invoked directly, exactly once, and never retried). **Feedback-driven** callers (those passing `make_feedback_prompt`: classifier, reconciler, provision, overlap judge, integrator, adherence gate, `classification_judge`) run deterministic checks or an independent judge on the output and re-invoke with structured feedback if issues are found, cutting a round short of exhaustion when a round's issue signatures repeat an earlier round's. On exhaustion, proceed with best result + warnings (or `die()` for the adversarial-verifier gates among them) — except the classification gate, which routes to the cleared-but-empty terminal state instead of `die()`ing when the OR-accumulated `likely_already_satisfied` signal is `True` with evidence (DESIGN §8). **Detect-and-die, single-pass** callers (`wiring_judge`, `provision_judge`, `integration_judge`) stop at the first round that finds issues rather than retrying an unchanged payload. Both families: CRITIC pattern (ICLR 2024). A round that raises `WorkerError` is retried against the same budget regardless of family; any other exception abandons the loop immediately. |
| mechanical-feedback rounds for planner (`planner_check_rounds`) | 3 | Same CRITIC pattern, but higher default because the planner has richer checks (phantom paths, dangling deps, intra-domain cycles, protected paths, migration surface). |
| implementer confidence retries (`implementer_confidence_retries`) | 2 | Separate from `subtask_continuations`. Orchestrator checks confidence scores + scope drift + unmet criteria on complete results and re-invokes as a continuation if issues found. |
| planner samples (`planner_samples`) | 3 | Independent parallel invocations per domain. Mechanical selection: fewest issues, tiebreak on subtask count. Set to 1 to disable. Also `LEERIE_PLANNER_SAMPLES` env or `planner_samples` in `leerie.toml`. CLI: `--planner-samples`. |
| P6 repo-map token budget (`repo_map_tokens`) | 1000 | Token budget for the personalized-PageRank-ranked subgraph injected into the planner/splitter (DESIGN §5½ (P6)). The subgraph is binary-searched to fit within this many tokens. Not user-tunable via CLI / env / toml. |
| P1 recursive decompose max depth (`decompose_max_depth`) | 5 | Maximum recursion depth for `_recursive_decompose()` (DESIGN §5½ (P1)). Recursion terminates at depth ≥ 5 even if `fit_judge` still scores below `decompose_fit_threshold`. A depth-5 tree can represent up to 32 leaves from one subtask. Not user-tunable. |
| P1 fit-judge pass threshold (`decompose_fit_threshold`) | 0.70 | `fit_judge` confidence score at or above which a subtask is accepted as a leaf. Measured on n=24 telemetry-labeled subtasks: oversized mean 0.26 vs well-fit mean 0.84, 88% accuracy at 0.70. Not user-tunable. |
| P1 no-progress guard (`decompose_noprogress_rounds`) | 2 | Consecutive recursion rounds that produce no child with a fit score above the parent's before the subtask is accepted as a leaf with a warning. Prevents a degenerate splitter from looping to `decompose_max_depth`. Not user-tunable. |
| P1 sub-file split span (`subfile_split_max_span`) | 700 | Line-span above which a single-file subtask (tier 1) or a single region (tier 2) is split intra-file rather than left a leaf (DESIGN §5½ (P1) *Sub-file*). Heuristic, not telemetry-calibrated. Not user-tunable. |

### P1 recursive decomposition surface (DESIGN §5½ (P1))

`_partition_files(files: list[str], chunk_size: int) -> list[list[str]]`
Deterministic chunker for the migration-sweep path. Splits `files` into
non-overlapping chunks of at most `chunk_size` (default 8). 100% coverage
and 0 overlap are guaranteed by construction (no LLM). When `chunk_size < 1`,
returns `[list(files)]` (degenerate guard). Used by `_recursive_decompose()`
when `len(files) > 8` so the code — not the LLM — decides the file partition
(the LLM splitter was measured dropping 14/29 migration files in testing);
the splitter worker then only *labels* the pre-computed chunks.

`_remap_vanished_deps(subtasks: list[dict], mapping: dict[str, list[str]]) -> None`
Mutates `subtasks` in place: rewrites every `depends_on` reference to an id that
vanished from the plan, per DESIGN §5 *Id-vanishing operations*. `mapping` is
`{vanished_id: [successor_ids]}`; fan-out (expansion — parent → N leaves) and prune
(drop — id → `[]`) are the same operation over it. Dedups after the rewrite and skips
self-references, mirroring `_apply_overlap_merge`'s discipline. An empty `mapping` is
a no-op; a dep absent from `mapping` passes through untouched. Called from four sites:
`_recursive_decompose()` (intra-generation sibling edges), `phase_plan()` (cross-subtask
edges after expansion), and both phase-3 soft-drop filters (`_filter_offtree_subtasks`,
`_filter_satisfied_subtasks`) with an all-empty mapping to prune dropped ids. This
handles only the **id (`depends_on`) channel**; a *drop* also orphans the tag channel
(see `_prune_orphaned_requires` below).

`_prune_orphaned_requires(plans: list[dict], dropped_provides: set[str]) -> None`
Mutates the subtasks in `plans` in place: removes from each survivor's `requires` any
tag whose only provider was a dropped subtask, per DESIGN §5 *Id-vanishing operations*.
The prune set is `dropped_provides - (union of surviving provides)`: a tag still
provided by a surviving subtask is kept, and a tag no subtask ever provided is left
intact so `_validate_plan` still surfaces it as a genuine planner error. `dropped_provides`
must be captured before the survivor-filter removes the dropped subtasks from
`plan["subtasks"]`. Takes **all plans and operates once over the whole merged set**,
not per-plan, since capability tags are cross-domain and `_validate_plan` checks
provider-existence globally. Called by both phase-3 soft-drop filters once, after the
per-plan `_remap_vanished_deps` loop.

`_recursive_decompose(subtask, depth, st, caps, models, efforts, repo_root, *, repo_map=None, _parent_score, _noprogress_count) -> list[dict]`
Async recursive function implementing DESIGN §5½ (P1) *Task-Context Fit*. For each
subtask: calls `fit_judge` to score Task-Context Fit (0–1); returns `[subtask]`
if score ≥ 0.70 (threshold from `caps["decompose_fit_threshold"]`) or depth ≥
`caps["decompose_max_depth"]` (5); checks the no-progress guard
(`caps["decompose_noprogress_rounds"]` consecutive rounds of no improvement
accept the subtask as leaf); then splits via one of:

- **Migration path** (≥ 9 files): `_partition_files()` owns the file→chunk
  partition (deterministic, 100% coverage). The `splitter` worker is then
  invoked in **label-only mode** (`_label_migration_chunks()`) to write a
