  the sample record's `lead_sets` is those sets' sorted indices), then
  `claude_p(schema_key="falsifier", allowed_tools=ACT_TOOLS,
  max_turns=FALSIFIER_MAX_TURNS (80), autonomous=True,
  sid="falsifier-<name>-s<n>")` — `<name>` is `names[k]`, by default `i<k>` — with `_falsifier_user_prompt` (task,
  referenced files, the item, its anchor and — when it has any — its
  classifier `parts` (`_falsifier_item_parts(item)`: the non-blank string
  parts, in order, as `"parts"` inside THE ITEM TO CHECK), the own start and
  `git diff --stat=160 <own>..<final>`, the lead files, the item's
  `unmet_parts`) — the frozen F+ user prompt line for line but for the
  parts; the record is not passed (DESIGN §8 *What ships is what was
  measured*). With `base_claim=True` (phase 3, `_falsify_satisfied_drops`)
  no start commit or diff stat is computed: the START COMMIT lines are
  `_FALSIFIER_BASE_START` and the closing line `_FALSIFIER_BASE_CLOSE` —
  the working directory is the tree the run starts from, nothing has been
  done on it, a reader judged the item already delivered there — and
  everything else is as above. `_falsify_items`' `names` (index → name,
  default `i<k>`) names each item's samples (sid, confirm label) and its
  saved probe's directory under `probes_root` (default
  `<run_dir>/acceptance/probes`); `persist` (default: write `progress` to
  `delivery_gate.final_progress` and save) runs after each item finishes,
  `None` saves nothing. `prompts/falsifier.md` is the frozen `falsifier_prompt.md` +
  `fplus_addendum.md` with `.q2ctx/` → `FALSIFIER_LEADS_DIR` and bench
  SW's step-1 sentence on the item's parts (DESIGN §8 *The falsifier gets
  the item whole*; `tests/test_falsifier_benched_prompt.py` pins both). `_falsifier_probe_activity(log_path, lane, repo_root)`
  runs after the sample's worker returns and before the next sample's
  `_restore_tree` of that lane. `files` are the lane's own probes: its
  untracked, not-ignored paths (`_untracked_listing(lane)`, git addressed
  by `_tree_git_args`) that are test-shaped (`_is_test_file`), outside
  `FALSIFIER_LEADS_DIR`, and a regular file reached without following a
  link (`_regular_file_beneath`); `created` is `bool(files)`, whatever tool
  wrote them. `ran` reads the Bash commands of the sample's registered
  transcript (`_iter_log_tool_use(kinds=("Bash",))`) through
  `_falsifier_runs_probe(cmd, rel, lane)`: a shell segment
  (`_BLT_SEG_RE`, lead stripped by `_BLT_SEG_LEAD_RE`) whose runner is a
  BLT verb or one of `_FALSIFIER_RUNNER_VERBS` — as its first token, or
  after a Python interpreter's `-m` — and one of whose arguments (quotes
  dropped, a `::` node suffix dropped, a path under the lane made
  relative, normalised) is the probe, its basename, or a directory
  holding it (`.` included). `_falsifier_needs_reask` (could_not_demonstrate
  without both) → one more `claude_p(user_prompt=FALSIFIER_REASK_NOTE,
  resume_session=<_log_session_id(log)>, sid=<sid>-reask)` in the same
  checkout (`claude_p`'s `resume_session` adds `--resume <id>`).
- **Gates** (`_falsifier_gates`; from the placement check through the
  facts read in one `_held_out_section`, so samples queue on the execution
  lock and one confirm holds it across its runs): `new_file` (a safe
  relative path, present in the lane, absent from the final commit),
  `not_a_lead` (not under the leads, not an acceptance path), `runnable`
  (`_acceptance_cmd` renders it), `item_quote` (normalised
  `item_span_quote`, ≥ 8 non-space characters, inside the normalised
  `_falsifier_item_text(item)` — the sentence and its parts, one per line,
  which the coupling check's "the item names the symbol" also reads);
  then the probe — held-out content, its writer read every valid set
  (DESIGN §6 *A held-out evaluation runs alone*) — is copied to a
  `tempfile.mkstemp` file of leerie's own (removed after) and, never
  written into `falsifier-confirm` (refused, `placed: false`, when that
  path exists there), placed in a held-out sandbox over it:
  `_capture_failing_test_ids(serial=True, files=[probe], db=True,
  place=((<copy>, <probe>),))`, which with `place` runs each attempt in
  `_held_out_section` with `HeldOutSandbox(view=tree, place=…,
  report=<its report path>)`, `_heldout_grants` and
  `_acceptance_cmd(…, placed=)`: `case_fails`
  (`_falsifier_case_id` finds the named case among the failing IDs, never a
  load failure), `fails_under_bstar` (`_confirm_still_failing` on that ID;
  with it the sample records `failure_message`, the runner's message for
  that case from the last of its runs that gave one, cut to
  `_UNMET_MESSAGE_MAX` characters, and `failure_line`, the line that message
  names in the probe (`_evidence_line`), or neither when the runner gave
  none — read only by `_record_unmet_evidence`);
  then `_probe_case_facts_placed(st, tree, src, rel, case)` (node
  `scripts/test-case-facts.cjs <tree>/<rel> <case> <report>` through
  `_run_streaming` in the same kind of sandbox, alone, the probe placed,
  env `_ts_script_env()`; the script writes its JSON to its optional
  third argument, the sandbox's report, and the facts are read from it). The
  script finds the case by its title against the runner's full name (the
  case ID's part after ` :: `): equal, or ending in it after a space; a
  parametrised title (`it.each`, `test.each`, a template literal, a `+`
  concatenation) by its whole template — its literal text exactly and in
  order, each placeholder (vitest/jest's printf `%s %d %i %f %j %o %O %p %c
  %# %$`, `%%` a literal `%`, a table's `$name` / `$name.path`, a template's
  `${}`) any text, anchored the same way — the case with the most literal
  text winning. A literal prefix alone, the rule this replaces, missed every
  case whose prefix was 8 characters or shorter (barnacle run e7512406 item
  10: `"skips %s"`, `case_not_found`). A title built with `+` (`titleOf`) is
  read as a template literal is: each string or template operand its text,
  every other operand a `${}` placeholder. The operand is never resolved — a
  loop variable, a constant or a call, whatever the values it takes, is any
  text, as a template literal's `${u}` already was — so `for (const u of
  urls) it("skips " + u, …)` and `urls.forEach((u) => it("skips " + u, …))`
  name `skips ${}`. Before, such a title was no title at all and its every
  case read `case_not_found` (lane SD sweep r2, barnacle e7512406
  bugfix-005-2: a B*-confirmed `::ffff` loopback demonstration rejected by
  `assertion_in_case`, `not_coupled` and `at_assertion` together). A title
  with no literal text (`it(name, …)`, `it(a + b, …)`) names no case. When it
  returns an error starting `facts_failed` (the script crashed, timed out
  or printed no JSON — an infrastructure miss) the sample records
  `facts_read: false` and `facts_error` and stops there:
  `assertion_in_case` and `not_coupled` are not written, so the miss never
  reads as a rejected probe. Otherwise (`case_not_found` included)
  `facts_read: true`, then `assertion_in_case` (normalised
  `assertion_quote`, ≥ 6 characters, inside the case's reachable source,
  and `_falsifier_quoted_assertion_lines(probe_source, assertion_quote,
  facts["asserts"])` non-empty: some probe line the quote names lies in one
  of the case's assertions — DESIGN §8 *The quoted assertion is one the
  test framework makes*). `asserts` is the facts script's list of the
  reachable code's assertion calls, `{start, end}` 1-based lines of the
  outermost call of each chain: a call whose callee chain (through
  property accesses, element accesses and calls) starts at an identifier
  that resolves (`keyOf`, lexical scope) to the global `expect` or
  `assert`, to an import named `expect` or `assert` from any module, or to
  any import (or top-level `require`) of `assert`, `node:assert`,
  `assert/strict` or `node:assert/strict`; for `expect` the chain must
  call `expect(…)`, `expect.soft(…)` or `expect.poll(…)` itself, so
  `expect.any(String)` alone is not one. A facts dict without `asserts`
  has no assertion: the gate fails.
  `not_coupled` (`_falsifier_coupling` returns `coupled: false`: no
  file read but of a JSON path or a fresh one, and no text-tool exec (R1),
  no eval / Function / vm /
  transpile / non-literal import (R2), no import of an in-repo symbol that
  no production code uses outside its own declaration and the item does not
  name, resolved with `_ts_path_aliases` / `_js_resolve`, nor a deep package
  path (R3)). A read is fresh when the facts mark it `fresh: true` and no
  copy makes the directory unsafe. The facts script marks a read `fresh`
  when its first argument is a path inside a fresh directory: a
  `mkdtemp`/`mkdtempSync` result from `fs` or `fs/promises`, extended by
  `path` `join`/`resolve`, a template or `+` only with plain segments. A
  plain segment is a literal that is not absolute and has no `..`
  segment, or a `readdir` entry or its `.name`. Arrays of such paths are
  followed through `filter`/`slice`/`sort`/`map`/`flatMap`/`find`/`at`,
  `for … of` and index access. Each identifier is resolved to its
  declaration by lexical scope. Every value that binding is given must be
  such a path: initialisers, `=` assignments, `push`, a named function's
  call-site arguments, and an array callback's elements. These are
  computed as a greatest fixed point, so a recursive directory walk
  keeps its paths. Anything not followed is not fresh. The facts also
  list `copies`: each `copyFile`/`cp`/`link`/`symlink`/`rename` call,
  sync or not, in reachable code, with `fresh_src`. One whose source is
  not fresh, or an exec whose literal command names a copying tool
  (`_COUPLING_COPY_TOOLS_RE`: `cp`, `ln`, `mv`, `rsync`, `install`,
  `tar`, `ditto`, `dd`, `tee`, `cpio`, `unzip`), makes every read count
  again. Facts without `fresh`, from an older script, count every read as
  before. Whether production code uses an imported symbol (R3) is
  `_coupling_referenced_elsewhere(name, module, repo, sha, tree=, grants=)`:
  the candidates are the tracked non-harness files `git grep -w -F` finds
  naming it at `sha`, its own module among them; a candidate outside
  `_JS_SRC_EXT` counts by that whole word, as no JS/TS parse reads it; the
  JS/TS candidates go to `node scripts/symbol-references.cjs <name> <module>
  <file>...` (`SYMBOL_REFERENCES`, through `_ts_script_run` in the confirm
  checkout with `_measurement_grants`, its caller in `_falsifier_gates`
  holding `_exec_lock().shared()` as every AST script caller does), which lists the files whose syntax
  holds an identifier `name` outside comments, strings and type positions —
  in its module, outside the symbol's own top-level declaration (name and
  body, so a self-recursive call is no use) and its own export of it. A
  caller in the same module is a use: the whole-file match this replaces
  excluded the module, since text cannot tell the definition from a call,
  and so read every helper whose only production caller shares its module
  as test-only (barnacle run e7512406: `scrubSecretEnvInValues`,
  `selectRateLimitTargets`, `withClearBeforeType`, each called in its own
  module, rejected four real demonstrations). When the script cannot run
  (no JSON, an unread file) `_falsifier_coupling` returns `coupled: None`
  with `error: "facts_failed: symbol references"`, and the sample records
  `facts_read: false` as for a failed facts read. Nothing of the probe is
  ever in the checkout.
  A sample is confirmed only when every gate is true. A confirmed sample's
  probe is saved under `acceptance/probes/` (no fixer's grant reaches
  `acceptance/`), re-run only through `_evaluate_acceptance_sets` (placed,
  sandboxed), and what reaches a fixer from it is only the evidence line
  below — the item's own words — never the probe's text, case title or
  the sample's prose.
- **Verdict.** Per item, unmet when the judge record lists it (`by`:
  `judge`, or `untouched_paths`) or a sample is confirmed (`falsifier`).
  A confirmed sample's evidence is `a falsifier probe of the item's words
  "<_scope_norm(item_span_quote)>" fails under B* on the final tree` —
  never its `probe_path`, `case_id` or `reason` (DESIGN §8 *Nothing a
  held-out evaluation produces reaches a fixer*).
  Written as `delivery_gate.items` / `unmet_final` (see State).
  `_decide_outcome` and `_prior_delivery_residual` read `unmet_final` first.
  The final judge's retry loop treats any `Exception` as a crash (its items
  `unknown` when every attempt fails), not only `WorkerError` / timeout.
  The verdict records `final_tree` (`_shipping_tree(st)`), and
  `_delivery_judged_record(sha, unmet, details, tree)` records the pre-pass's
  and the recheck's `tree` (`_shipping_tree(st)` too); the delivery
  re-drive's re-key sets `final_tree` (`_shipping_tree(st)`) with
  `final_sha`.

### CI parity — `ci_checks`

DESIGN §9 *The repository's own merge checks run too*. Two halves, both
advisory (an exception is logged, never fatal) and resume-idempotent:

- **Baseline** — `_capture_ci_parity_baseline(leerie_dir, st, caps, models,
  efforts)`, called in `phase_execute` right after
  `_capture_conformance_baseline` (same `skip_base_baseline` opt-out). On the
  untouched staging base: `_ci_discover` spawns `ci_checks` once (its
  `cwd` `async with _judge_checkout(st, staging, "ci-checks")`, no
  install; DESIGN §8 *A worker that does not commit never runs in a tree
  leerie measures*) when
  `_ci_config_files` finds a `CI_CONFIG_GLOBS` file (else
  `ci_parity.skipped`); `_ci_select(checks, tree, forbidden=())` keeps a check only when it
  is not `kind: test` (left to the test axis), one `trigger` is in
  `CI_GATING_TRIGGERS` (`pull_request`, `pre_push_hook`, `pre_commit_hook`),
  no `requires` is in `CI_EXTERNAL_REQUIRES` (`browser`, `network`,
  `secrets`, `cloud_credentials`, `gpu` — `database` is not), and
  `_ci_check_problems` is empty, and its `argv` does not run a command the
  task forbids (`_forbidden_command_hit` over `shlex.join(argv)` against
  `_forbidden_specs(st.data)`; else `reason: "forbidden_by_task"`, `forbidden: <hit>`) — a
  forbidden `strict_argv` is dropped (`strict_forbidden: <hit>`) and the
  check judged on its plain argv; so is a selected check's `strict_argv`
  with a non-empty `_ci_strict_problems(check, tree) -> list[str]`
  (`strict_problems: [...]`, `strict_argv` then `null`, and the baseline
  logs the drop) — a strict form never deselects the plain check. A check
  that would be selected but runs exactly what an earlier selected one runs
  (`_ci_run_key(check) -> str`: `kind`, `argv`, `cwd`, `env`, each
  prerequisite as it runs (`_ci_prereq_argv` and its `cwd`; one that runs
  nothing is left out), `requires`, `coverage`; never `id`, `trigger`,
  `source`, `path_filters`, `notes` or `strict_argv`)
  is not selected: `reason: "duplicate"`, `duplicate_of: <that check's
  id>`; when the kept check has no strict form left and the duplicate
  does, the kept one takes it (`strict_from: <the duplicate's id>`) (DESIGN §9 *A check is the command its file runs* — the worker
  lists each file's commands apart; code merges only identical runs).
  Provenance (`_ci_check_problems`): the
  `source.file` and `cwd` lie inside the repo; every `argv`, prerequisite
  `argv` and `env` name/value token appears, whitespace-collapsed, in the
  source file; a prerequisite typed `root: part` has a rootless form
  (`_ci_rootless_form(pre) -> list[str] | None`: `rootless_argv` non-empty,
  shorter than `argv`, and an ordered subsequence of it); no token carries a `${{` placeholder; a coverage check names an existing
  `config_file`, a `summary_path` and thresholds whose glob (`**` exempt),
  metric and minimum each appear in that config. Strict provenance
  (`_ci_strict_problems`): every non-flag `strict_argv` token appears in the
  source file or a `CI_STRICT_MANIFESTS` file in the check's cwd or the
  root. The selected checks then
  run in a detached `worktrees/ci-base` worktree at the base sha
  (`_ci_worktree` / `_ci_teardown`; deps and prerequisites via
  `_ci_prepare`, which runs each prerequisite's `_ci_prereq_argv(pre) ->
  list[str] | None` — `argv` for `root: none` or a record without `root`,
  `_ci_rootless_form(pre)` for `part`, nothing for `all` (logged: needs root,
  its packages belong in `setup_packages`); DESIGN §9 *A prerequisite runs
  in the form that needs no root*). Per check: `kind: coverage` → `ratchet: coverage` when the
  summary yields a percentage (`_ci_coverage_pcts`, else
  `coverage_unmeasured`); a run that changed tracked files →
  `writes_tracked_files`; otherwise a `strict_argv` green at the baseline →
  `gate: strict`, red → `ratchet: diagnostic` with the base's
  `_ci_diagnostic_keys`; a plain run green → `gate: plain` (when no strict
  gate); neither → `red_at_baseline`.
- **Browser channel** (DESIGN §8 *A repository's browser suite is a channel
  the run provisions*) — after the selected checks, still in the baseline,
  `_establish_browser_suite(st, caps, ci, base_sha)`.
  `_browser_suite_candidate(recs, tree, forbidden=()) -> dict | None`: the
  first record with `kind: test`, `"browser"` in `requires`, a
  `CI_GATING_TRIGGERS` trigger, `cwd` the root, no `_ci_runs_db_reset`, no
  `_forbidden_command_hit`, empty `_ci_check_problems`, whose
  `shlex.join(argv)` resolved by `_runner_command(cmd, tree,
  BROWSER_SUITE_RUNNERS)` names a runner (`_acceptance_runner`) and is bare
  by `_browser_suite_words_bare(words, prefix)` (exactly one occurrence of
  the prefix; after it only `-…` words, a non-path value after a `--flag`
  without `=` counting as that flag's); returns `{check_id, argv, runner,
  template: shlex.join(argv) + " {test_files}", env, prerequisites,
  requires, source}`. `BROWSER_SUITE_RUNNERS = {"playwright": ("playwright",
  "test")}`. `_establish_browser_suite` records the candidate as
  `ci["browser_suite"]` with `viable: False`, makes `worktrees/ci-browser`
  at the base (`_ci_worktree`), runs `_ci_prepare` over
  `_browser_suite_rec(suite)` (`{id: "browser-<check_id>", prerequisites,
  env, requires}`), resolves the suite's command (`_runner_command`), asks
  for its report (`_acceptance_report_spec` into
  `<measure-dir>/reports/browser-suite-<hex>`), and runs `bash -c <cmd>`
  through `_ci_run` (`MEASURE_KIND`, its database when `requires` names
  one) with the report request's and the path overlay's variables and
  `_browser_suite_env(suite)` — `BROWSER_SUITE_CI_ENV = {"CI": "true"}`
  then the declared `env`. `base` counts `_runner_report_cases` by status
  (or `why`: `no base worktree`, `its runner's report cannot be
  requested`, `not run: <forbidden>`, `no report was written`);
  `viable = passed > 0`; the worktree is torn down. Nothing else is caught:
  an exception propagates out of `_capture_ci_parity_baseline` as any CI
  parity error does (phase 4 logs it and proceeds without CI parity, and
  `baseline_done` is not saved). `_browser_suite(st)` is
  `ci_parity.browser_suite` when `viable`, else None.
  `_browser_suite_cmd(suite, files)` renders `template` over the
  `shlex.quote`d files. `_browser_suite_payload(suite)` is the text a
  worker is told: the one-file command (`<file>`), that it runs a real
  browser and starts what its configuration starts, a database per run,
  `_browser_suite_env` as `K=v` pairs — less `TEST_DB_ENV_NAMES =
  ("DATABASE_URL", "DIRECT_URL")` when `"database"` is in `requires`, with
  "its URL is already in your environment (DATABASE_URL, DIRECT_URL): never
  set those" — and what it is for (layout, what is on screen, viewport,
  hover, touch).
  `_falsify_items`: with `_browser_suite(st)`, `_ci_prepare` over the suite
  in the confirm checkout and in every lane; `_falsifier_user_prompt(…,
  suite=)` appends the payload plus the steer — a part about layout, what
  is visible on screen, viewport, hover or touch is one only this suite can
  show (a test the test command runs renders without layout), so it is
  probed with a file for the suite, run on its own with the command above;
  the held-out files and a reviewer's parts say where to look, not how to
  observe — after the reviewer's parts (no suite: unchanged); a sample whose
  logged Bash commands (its session and its re-ask) ran its `probe_path`
  through the suite's runner (`_browser_suite_ran_probe(cmds, rel, tree,
  suite)`: a segment, package-script calls resolved, holding the runner
  prefix and naming the probe, its basename or a directory above it) is
  recorded `via_browser_suite: true` and gated with
  `_falsifier_gates(…, suite=suite)`, which renders
  `_browser_suite_cmd(suite, [rel])` and calls `_capture_failing_test_ids(…,
  suite=suite)` (the scoped command is `_browser_suite_cmd`; the run's
  environment gains `_browser_suite_env`). `_observability_verdicts` passes
  `suite=_browser_suite(st)` to `_observability_user_prompt(task, payload,
  test_cmd, suite=None)`, which with a suite inserts the payload and the
  third-way sentence after the test command line. Reports:
  `_RUNNER_REPORTS["playwright"] = ("playwright-json", "pwenv")` — `pwenv`
  appends `--reporter=json` and sets both `_PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_ENV`
  (`PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT_FILE`, `PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT_NAME`) to the
  path; `_runner_report_cases("playwright-json", …)` adds one
  `"<file or (playwright)> :: (file failed to load)"` `load_error` per
  top-level `errors[]` entry (its `location.file`, when it names one), and
  one case per `"<rootDir-relative file> :: <describe titles and spec
  title, space-joined>"` across `tests[]` (`unexpected` → `failed`,
  `skipped` → `skipped`, `expected`/`flaky` → `passed`; a second project's
  row turns the case `failed` when it failed, carrying its error message).
  `_SERIAL_RUNNER_FLAGS["playwright"] = "--workers=1"`; `playwright` is in
  `_FALSIFIER_RUNNER_VERBS`. A playwright case's `message` is its last
  result's error: `at <location.file>:<line>:<column>\n` first when the
  error has a location, then its `message`, then its `stack` when not
  already in it. `_falsifier_gates` (either channel) records every failing
  run's message per case ID and, after `not_coupled`, sets `at_assertion =
  _falsifier_failed_at_assertion(messages, rel, probe_source,
  assertion_quote, steps=facts["steps"], asserts=facts["asserts"])`: True
  when some message names no line of `rel` (`_evidence_line` None, an empty
  list included), or names a quoted assertion line
  (`_falsifier_quoted_assertion_lines`: a line whose `_scope_norm` text, at
  least 6 characters, is inside the quote's or holds it, and that lies in
  an `asserts` span), or names a line inside the span of a statement of the
  assertion's binding slice. `steps` is the facts script's list of the
  reachable code's statements, nested ones included (`{start,
  end, fn, binds[], reads[]}`: 1-based lines, the start offset of the
  innermost enclosing function, the names a variable statement declares or
  an assignment statement assigns, the identifiers it reads outside
  property names). The slice's anchors are the innermost statements holding a quoted
  assertion line (`_falsifier_assertion_slice`); a statement joins an anchor's
  slice when it starts before that anchor, in the same function, and binds
  a name the slice reads, to a fixpoint. With no
  `steps` (facts that carry none) the slice is empty: the line rule alone,
  as before. `confirmed` is the conjunction of every gate.
- **Final** — `_run_ci_parity_final(leerie_dir, st, caps) -> list[dict]`,
  called in `_run_phases` after `_run_acceptance_gate` and before
  `phase_finalize`, in a detached `worktrees/ci-final` worktree at the
  staging HEAD. The checks it runs are `_ci_gating_recs(st)` (selected,
  with a `gate` or a `ratchet`, in recorded order), measured by
  `_ci_measure(st, caps, wt, recs, *, label) -> {id: raw}` — every check
  once, in order, in the one prepared tree; a gate's raw `{rc, passed,
  dirty, timed_out, duration_sec, log}`, a diagnostic ratchet's
  `{strict_rc, diagnostics}`, a coverage ratchet's `{rc, coverage}`; logs
  `logs/ci/<label>-<id>[-strict].log` (`label` `final` here). Each commit's
  raw result is kept by `_ci_remember(st, sha, raw, label)` in
  `ci_parity.measured[sha] = {label, results}` (logs dropped; the last
  `_CI_MEASURED_KEEP = 4` commits). When `_ci_remembered(st, sha, recs)`
  holds the HEAD's measurement with every gate `passed` (a kept repair
  round measured it, below), no worktree is made and nothing runs:
  `final.reused` names that measurement's label and the ratchets are read
  from it. A gate (`_ci_gate_argv`) that fails is confirmed by
  `_ci_confirm_red(st, caps, base_sha, final_tree, recs, *, durations=None,
  label="confirm")` — `_confirm_new_failures` with base reruns in a fresh
  `ci-confirm-base` worktree and final reruns in `ci-final`, with
  `seen_failing=True`; `label` prefixes the reruns' logs
  (`<label>-base<n>-<id>`, `<label>-final<n>-<id>`) and the base's
  prerequisites (`<label>-base`). The red checks are sized by `_confirm_sized` over
  their final-run `duration_sec` (recorded on `final.results[id]`; one
  unit per check, no overhead, shortest first); a check never rerun is
  `budget_short_unsettled` (and `sized_out`, kept on `final.sized_out`),
  and `_ci_confirm_chosen(st, caps, base, final_tree, recs, *,
  prior_gate=None, label="confirm", setup=None, upto=0, **pairs)` confirms
  each pass's checks. Sizing chooses a pass's checks, not their order
  (DESIGN §9 *A merge check's rerun sees what its measurement saw*):
  `_ci_confirm_red` orders the measurement's checks as `_ci_gating_recs(st)`
  then any check of `recs` not among them, hands each pass its checks in
  that order, and as `setup` the checks of that order from `base["upto"]`
  up to the pass's last one (`upto` its index plus one). Before the reruns
  `_ci_confirm_chosen` runs `setup` once on the base tree,
  `_ci_measure(…, label="<label>-base-setup")`, results unread, after
  `_ci_prepare` over `setup` and the pass's checks; then `base["upto"] =
  upto`. Each rerun runs the pass's checks in that order; `final_tree` is
  the measured tree, so it needs no set-up.
  `base` is `_ci_confirm_red`'s one `{"sha", "wt", "prepared", "prereqs",
  "upto"}` record
  for the whole sized confirm: the first pass creates `ci-confirm-base`
  (`_ci_worktree`, tried once; `wt` stays None when that fails, and every pass is then
  `_confirm_new_failures` over no-verdict runners), each pass runs
  `_ci_prepare(…, done=base["prereqs"])` over only the checks (`setup` and the pass's) whose ids are not yet in `prepared`
  (deps install once — `_DEPS_INSTALLED` — and the throwaway database
  only when the tree has none), and `_ci_confirm_red` tears it down
  (`_ci_teardown`) when the confirm ends. One rerun runs
  every chosen check serially; each check's
  `_ci_run` gets `_budget_caps(caps, rem)`, `rem` being what is left of the
  `left` the rerun was handed. With `rem <= 0` before a check, or a check
  `timed_out` once that `left` is spent, the rerun returns
  `_RerunCut(failing, measured)` over the checks it finished (a budget cut,
  DESIGN §9 step 4); a check timed out with budget left returns None (no
  verdict). Only `new` ids
  become `unmet` (`why: red`); `final.pre_existing` and `final.no_verdict`
  record the B\* split of the rest, `final.resource_affected` the mixed
  ones, `final.budget_short_unsettled` the ones the budget left unsettled
  (`_set_confirm_budget_gap(st, "CI parity", <not sized out>,
  sized_out=final.sized_out)`). A diagnostic
  ratchet is `unmet` (`why: new_diagnostics`) when a key's final count
  exceeds the base's in a file the run changed
  (`_ci_new_diagnostics(rec, keys, ref, touched)` over `_ci_touched(staging,
  base_sha, final_sha)` — `git diff --name-only` — relative to the check's
  cwd). A coverage ratchet
  is `unmet` (`why: coverage_ratchet`) per `_ci_coverage_fired`: final <
  `min`, final < base − `ci_coverage_epsilon_pct`, and the glob matches a
  changed file.

**Database-backed checks** (DESIGN §8 *Prisma repositories get a real
database*). `_ci_run` wraps a check (and its prerequisites) that
`requires` `database` in `scripts/sandbox-db.sh <pkg> leerie_<…>_test`
(§ *Isolation and the held-out sandbox (I3)*, *The per-command
database*), so each such command has its own cluster; `_CI_DB_URLS` and
`_ci_teardown`'s drop are deleted. In a Prisma repo a prerequisite or check argv that
`_ci_runs_db_reset` matches (its joined argv against
`_db_reset_rule_patterns` — the workers' deny list) is never run
(`{rc: None, skipped: "db_reset"}`; a check so matched is unselected,
`reason: "db_reset"`), so the push `scripts/sandbox-db.sh` makes inside
the command's own confinement is the only one.

`_ci_run(argv, *, tree, rec, st, caps, label)` execs the argv (never a
shell; gated by `_blt_shell_argv`, a refusal is `{rc: None, skipped:
"forbidden_by_task"}` and never run — a forbidden prerequisite included) through `_run_contained` at the worker caps (spawn-held, broker
cgroup) inside `_build_class_slot`, with the check's `env` over the
orchestrator's (and the tree's test database over both, as above), timeout `worker_timeout_sec`, the whole output in
`logs/ci/<label>.log` (read back by `_ci_diagnostic_keys`), and resets a
run that changed tracked files. `_ci_diagnostic_keys(output, tree, cwd)`
counts `file\ttext` keys from fixed tool output — `path:line[:col] rest`
lines and, under a bare path header, indented `line:col rest` lines —
keeping only paths that exist under the check's cwd and dropping positions.
`_ci_coverage_pcts` aggregates an istanbul `json-summary` per
`glob|metric` from `covered`/`total` (`_ci_glob_match`: `fnmatch`, also with
`/**/` read as `/*`).

`_ci_parity_unmet(st)` returns `ci_parity.final.unmet` — the record
`_decide_outcome` reads and a delivery re-drive consumes; and
`_prior_delivery_residual` hands it to the next same-task run's planners as
`ci_unmet` (`{id, why, argv, cwd, diagnostics[≤5], thresholds[≤5]}`, at most
5).

### A kept round's merge checks — `_ci_round_regressions`

DESIGN §8 *A kept repair keeps the repository's merge checks green*.
`_ci_round_regressions(st, caps, staging, pre_sha, post_sha, *, label) ->
dict`, called by `_delivery_ratchet` (below) for every round it gates,
first, unless `exec_result` already carries `new` or `base_form_changed`.
`{}` when `_ci_gating_recs(st)` is empty, either sha is missing, or
`pre_sha == post_sha`. Otherwise, in a fresh `worktrees/ci-round` at
`post_sha` (`_ci_worktree`; none → `unmeasured: "no worktree of the
round's commit"`, nothing broke): `_ci_prepare(…, "<label>-post")`,
`_ci_measure(…, label="<label>-post")`; the gates not `passed` go to
`_ci_confirm_red(st, caps, pre_sha, wt, <those>, durations=…,
label="<label>-confirm")`, and each `new` id is broke `{id, kind, why:
"red", argv: _ci_gate_argv, cwd, rc, lines}`; `pre_existing`,
`resource_affected`, `no_verdict`, `budget_short_unsettled` and `b_star`
are recorded as B\* split them, none a rollback. Ratchets read the start's
raw values from `_ci_remembered(st, pre_sha, <ratchets>)`, else measure
them in `worktrees/ci-round-pre` at `pre_sha` (label `<label>-pre`;
neither → `ratchets_unmeasured[]`): a diagnostic ratchet broke `{…, why:
"new_diagnostics", argv: strict_argv, diagnostics[≤_CI_DIAG_LIMIT],
lines}` on `_ci_new_diagnostics(rec, post keys, pre keys,
_ci_touched(staging, pre_sha, post_sha))`; a coverage ratchet broke `{…,
why: "coverage_ratchet", thresholds, lines}` on the `_ci_coverage_fired`
thresholds (against the base, `_ci_touched(base_sha, post_sha)`) whose
`(glob, metric)` did not fire on the start's percentages
(`_ci_touched(base_sha, pre_sha)`). `lines` is
`_ci_first_error_lines(log text)` for a gate — up to `_CI_ERROR_LINES = 5`
non-empty lines matching `_CI_ERROR_LINE_RE` (`\berror\b`, any case),
else the last 5, the `=== ci ` header never one, each cut at
`_CI_ERROR_LINE_MAX = 300` — the new keys for a diagnostic ratchet, a line
per threshold for coverage. The commit's raw measurement is kept
(`_ci_remember(st, post_sha, raw, "repair <label>")`). Returns `{pre_sha,
post_sha, checks[], broke[], pre_existing[], resource_affected[],
no_verdict[], budget_short_unsettled[], b_star?, unmeasured?,
ratchets_unmeasured?}`. `_ci_broke_text(broke)` is each id with its first
line in parentheses, `; `-joined.

### Per-round rollback of acceptance repair rounds

DESIGN §8 *A repair round that fixes nothing is rolled back*. In
`_run_acceptance_gate_inner`, before each round's worker the staging HEAD is
saved as `gate.round_pre`; the round's entry carries it as `pre_sha`.
`_settle_round(entry, prev, prev_sha)` records every round, the errored one
included: when the round has a verdict on a commit other than `pre_sha`,
`fixed_cases = _acceptance_fixed_cases(prev, results)` —
`_acceptance_failing_keys` (`"<index>:<file>"` → `{failing_cases}`) over the
sets measured on both sides, counted by `_redrive_fixed_cases`; None when no
such set failed before — and `[]` sets `rollback_reason: "fixed no failing
case"`. Otherwise `broken_cases = _acceptance_broken_cases(prev, results)`
(the same keys, counted by `_redrive_broken_cases`; a set passing before
contributes every case it now fails, and a file that failed with named
cases before and fails as a whole after contributes its key, unless its
entry carries `no_case_evidence`) is recorded, and a non-empty list sets
`rollback_reason: "broke previously passing held-out case(s)"` (DESIGN §8:
worse is counted in cases). The entry is saved, then `_undo_round` resets
(`_restore_tree(staging, pre_sha)`, *One restore*) and `final`/`final_sha` return to the verdict before the round. A
failed reset sets `rollback_failed` on the entry and the gate and ends the
rounds. On resume, a last entry with `rollback_reason` and no `rolled_back`
is reset first. The gate-wide rules (test axis red, sets unmeasurable)
still run after the rounds.

A moved round that fixed a case and has a readable `sha` then goes through
the delivery ratchet (below) before it is recorded: `_round_ratchet(entry)`
runs `_ratchet_exec` with the test IDs at `pre_sha` and at `sha`, then
`_delivery_ratchet`, and stores the result as `entry.ratchet`. A
`_ratchet_rollback_reason` (`"turned the repository's merge check(s) red:
<_ci_broke_text>"`, else `"regressed a previously met required item"`,
else `"broke an existing test"`) becomes the round's `rollback_reason` and
`_undo_round` resets it like a no-gain round; a kept round calls
`_ratchet_kept` (unless the ratchet raised) and then
`_ratchet_mark_unverified(st, _ratchet_unverified(st, rat), sha, label)`.
A ratchet that raises is recorded as `{error}`, the round is kept, and
every prior met item is unverified on its commit (below). The test IDs
come from `_ids_at(sha, label)`: one `_ratchet_test_ids` run per commit,
in staging's committed view (`_capture_failing_test_ids`), kept in `gate.test_ids[sha]` (`{ids, files, kind,
messages, command}` or `{unmeasured: true}`). It measures only while
staging's HEAD is that commit. Each round's start is measured before
its worker runs.

### Final-conformer held-out flip — `_conformer_flip_check`

DESIGN §8 *A final-conformer round that turns a passing held-out case
failing is rolled back*. `_run_final_conformance` records each round's
starting HEAD in `_final.round_starts` and staging's HEAD after the pass in
`_final.end_sha`. In `_run_acceptance_gate_inner`, right after a fresh
`initial` is measured (`gate-initial`, never on a resume that reuses it)
and while `gate.conformer_flip` is absent,
`_conformer_flip_check(st, caps, staging, sets, initial, initial_sha) ->
dict | None` returns None unless `_final.round_starts` is non-empty,
`_final.end_sha == initial_sha`, `_acceptance_any_fails(initial)` and some
round committed (`start != end`, a round's end being the next round's
start, the last one's `end_sha`). Then the sets are evaluated on the first
committing round's start (label `conformer-start`), and the record is
`{start_sha, end_sha, broken_cases}` with `broken_cases =
_acceptance_broken_cases(start verdict, initial)`, logged when empty. When
not empty, `_conformer_flip_culprit(st, caps, staging, sets, moved, before,
end_res) -> (round, start, verdict at start)` evaluates each committing
round's commit in turn (label `conformer-r<round>`; the last round's is
`initial`) and returns the first whose `_acceptance_broken_cases(verdict at
its start, verdict at its commit)` is non-empty, else the first committing
round; the record gains `culprit_round` and `rollback_to`. The record (less
the start verdict) is saved as `gate.conformer_flip` before
`_conformer_flip_undo(st, staging, gate, flip)` resets staging with
`_roll_back_round(worker="final conformer", label="round <n>",
reason="broke previously passing held-out case(s)", where="final conformer
held-out rollback")` and records `rolled_back` (and `rollback_failed` when
the reset did not land). A landed reset makes the culprit's start verdict
the gate's `initial` and `rollback_to` its `initial_sha`, in the same save
that records `rolled_back`. On resume, a
`conformer_flip` with `rollback_to` and no `rolled_back` is reset first and
`initial`/`initial_sha` are dropped, so the restored tree is measured
afresh.

### Acceptance repair round probe flip — `_acceptance_item_flips`

DESIGN §8 *A held-out repair round that turns a confirmed probe from
passing to failing is rolled back*. `_run_phases` calls
`_acceptance_item_flips(leerie_dir, st, caps, models, efforts)` right after
`_run_delivery_detection` (advisory: an exception is logged and finalize
proceeds). `_acceptance_kept_rounds(gate) -> list[dict]` is every
`gate.rounds` entry kept by `_acceptance_round_kept` with `pre_sha`,
`results` and a `sha` other than `pre_sha`, in order — none when
`gate.rolled_back`. The check runs only when there is one, when
`delivery_gate.final_sha` is staging's HEAD, and when
`gate.item_flip_checked` is not that HEAD. Each `delivery_gate.items` row
with `verdict: "unmet"` and a sample `_redrive_flip_probe(row)` returns
goes to `_probe_flip_culprit(st, caps, steps, i, smp, where=) -> dict |
None`, the culprit search `_redrive_flip_culprit` also calls, over `steps
= [({round}, "acc-r<round>", pre_sha, sha)]`: `_redrive_probe_flips` per
step in order, the first `flip` returned as `{item_index, round, pre_sha,
post_sha, case_id, probe_saved, b_star}`. With no culprit,
`gate.item_flip_checked = HEAD`. Otherwise the earliest culprit's round
(in `_acceptance_kept_rounds` order) is decided: `gate.item_flips[]` gains
`{round, rollback_to: its pre_sha, from_sha: HEAD, culprits[], reason:
"its commit turned the confirmed falsifier probe of item(s) from passing
on its start to failing on its commit (B*): item <i> (<case_id>)" (that
round's culprits), notes[_redrive_flip_note(i, item, smp, who="acceptance
repair round", short="round")], landed: None}`, saved before
`_roll_back_round(worker="acceptance repair", label="round <n>",
reason=…, where="acceptance repair rollback")`. `landed` records the
reset; a reset that did not land also sets `rollback_failed` and the
check stops. After a landed one, the culprit round and every kept round
after it get `rollback_reason` (a later one "built on round <n>, rolled
back: …") and `rolled_back: true`, a culprit's round also
`flip_regressed[culprits]`; the notes join
`delivery_redrive.pending_controls` (unless their key is there), in the
same save. Then `_acceptance_remeasure_final(…, rollback_to,
"gate-item-flip")` over every set, `_refresh_shipping_test_id_diff(label=
"test-id-diff-item-flip")` and `_run_delivery_detection`, and the check
loops. On entry, an `item_flips` entry with `landed: None` is reset first
(no probe runs), then finished as above.

### Delivery ratchet — `_delivery_ratchet`

DESIGN §8 *A repair that regresses met work is rolled back* (bench Q4 N5,
frozen config C + vote change V; its execution route on B\*). Called by
`_run_acceptance_gate_inner` per round (above) and by
`_run_delivery_redrive` per group that committed and is neither `worse`
nor void.

- **Merge checks first.** Unless `exec_result` has `new` or
  `base_form_changed`, `_ci_round_regressions(st, caps, staging, pre_sha,
  post_sha, label=label)` runs before any item route; a non-empty result is
  `merge_checks`, one that raises is `merge_checks: {error}` (logged, the
  round not rolled back for it). A non-empty `broke` sets
  `merge_checks_broke` (the broke rows) and the ratchet returns there, no
  item read (`prior_met` empty): it is a rollback.
- **Previously met** (`_ratchet_prior_met(st) -> {item_index: evidence}`,
  `_ratchet_prior_met_all(st, items)` less every index in
  `delivery_ratchet.unverified`):
  `delivery_gate.items` rows with `verdict: met` once final detection ran
  (evidence `judge.met_evidence`), else the latest of `judged_after` /
  `judged_before`: every item that is not `external` and not in its
  `unmet`, with evidence from its `details[].met_evidence` (the last
  sample's met verdict, `_delivery_judge_unmet`). An entry in
  `delivery_ratchet.evidence` replaces it. `{}` with no required items,
  under `skip_coverage_check`, or with no recorded verdict.
- **Routes.** An item with `untouched_paths` is settled by
  `_d1_untouched_verdict` on staging (unmet → regressed). The rest are
  typed by `_ratchet_verifiability` (one `verifiability_classifier` call per
  run, cached; an untyped item is `in_tree`; a failed call skips the judge
  route for this ratchet, recorded as `judge.skipped`); a
  `_test_id_diff_item` is `execution` without the classifier, which is
  not called when every item left is one. An `execution`
  item is flagged (`exec_flagged`) when `exec_result.new` is non-empty. The
  `in_tree` items go to `_ratchet_judge`.
- **Judge** (`_ratchet_judge`): every sample's verdicts go through
  `_drop_test_outcome_parts` first; `git diff pre post` (cut at
  `RATCHET_DIFF_MAX_BYTES` = 80,000 with a note) and its `--name-only` set;
  items cut by `_d1_judge_packs`. Per pack, sample 1
  (`claude_p(schema_key="delivery_ratchet", system_prompt=delivery_judge.md
  + delivery_ratchet.md, allowed_tools=SATISFIED_PROBE_TOOLS,
  max_turns=min(30 + 6×pack, 90), sid="delivery_ratchet-<label>-p<k>-s<n>")`)
  over TASK, PREVIOUSLY VERIFIED ITEMS (`{item_index, item,
  prior_verified_evidence}`), CHANGES SINCE THAT VERIFICATION, the
  INTERMITTENT REGRESSIONS section when `exec_result` typed any, and the
  benched closing instruction. Candidates = items sample 1 marks `met:
  false` ∪ items whose `evidence_files` (`_ratchet_norm_path`: staging
  prefix, `./` and `:line` stripped) meet the changed files. With
  candidates, samples 2 and 3 run; a candidate is `confirmed` on ≥ 2 of 3
  unmet votes. A pack whose judge raises confirms nothing (`errors[]`)
  and its items go to `unverified[]`. Returns `{judged, diff_files,
  diff_bytes, sample1_flags, touched, candidates, per_sample_regressed,
  confirmed, samples, met_evidence, errors, unverified?}`.
- **Execution** (`_ratchet_exec(st, caps, staging, pre_sha, before, after,
  *, label, log_path, base_form=False, models=None, efforts=None)`): with
  either side unmeasured,
  `{unmeasured: true}`; with `base_form` it also carries `base_form` and
  `base_form_changed` (*Existing tests run in their base form*, above).
  Otherwise `_ratchet_exec_in` on staging (its test runs read staging's
  committed view): `_redrive_new_failures` confirms `after`'s candidates
  under B\* against a worktree at `pre_sha` (it also returns the whole B\*
  `verdict`). With none new and `after` no `near_stage`,
  `_intermittent_discovery(partial_ok=False)` from `pre_sha` (the tests that
  directly import a file the repair changed, rerun
  `confirm_intermittent_repeats` times if all fit); IDs it fails that neither
  `before` nor `after` holds join `after`'s, and all are confirmed again.
  `_type_intermittent_regressions` types the evidence rows.
  Returns `{new, pre_existing, no_verdict, resource_affected,
  budget_short_unsettled, unmeasured, files, intermittent_regression[],
  discovery}` (the first five as B\* split them). `_redrive_new_failures(
  …, *, intermittent=())` gets discovery's IDs that `after` did not fail as
  `intermittent`, and sizes the candidate files as
  `_confirm_final_test_failures` does (`_confirm_sized`; a file never
  rerun has its IDs `budget_short_unsettled`, listed in `sized_out`), also
  returning `sized_out` and `unsettled_files {id: file}`. A group kept
  with `budget_short_unsettled` candidates records `kept_unsettled` on the
  group and appends `{group, ids, sized_out, files, unchecked_items}`
  (`unchecked_items` the ratchet's `exec_unchecked`) to
  `delivery_redrive.kept_unsettled`, then `_set_redrive_unsettled_gap`. The re-drive calls it in place of `_redrive_new_failures`.
  `_ratchet_test_ids(st, caps, tree, *, label, log_path)` is the test axis
  with IDs: `_measure_axes(tree, {"tests": <the BLT command>}, failing_ids_axes={"tests"}, carry=True)`,
  so its `_scoped_test_replacement` when the task forbids it, the memo, and
  the ledger; `{ids, files, command, messages}`, None with no command, an
  unmeasured result or no report.
- **Staging is the committed test tree** (review round 13 claims M1;
  DESIGN §8 *The final diff describes the tree that ships*): the ratchet's
  execution route, `_redrive_test_ids` and the acceptance gate's `_ids_at`
  measure in staging's committed view (`_committed_view`): the run
  branch's tree plus the environment its committed ignore rules share in.
- **Unverified** (review round 13 claims M1). `unverified[]` is the
  `rest` items (all but `untouched_paths` ones) when the classifier
  failed, else the judge's `unverified` less `regressed`.
  `_ratchet_unverified(st, rat) -> list[int]`: every
  `_ratchet_prior_met(st)` index when `rat.error`, else `rat.unverified`.
  `_ratchet_mark_unverified(st, items, sha, label)` adds `{str(i): {sha,
  label}}` to `delivery_ratchet.unverified`, rewrites those `met` rows of
  `delivery_gate.items` to `{verdict: "unknown", by: [], reason}` and
  calls `_set_ratchet_unverified_gap(st)`: one `needs_human_verification`
  entry, `source: RATCHET_UNVERIFIED_GAP_SOURCE = "ratchet_unverified"`,
  through `_set_delivery_unknown_gap(st, source, items, why)`, cleared when
  none is left. `_run_delivery_detection` pops `unverified` (and rewrites
  the gap) once it has read every item. At the end of
  `_run_delivery_redrive`, when HEAD moved, the unverified items are
  re-read by `_redrive_recheck_items` on the final commit; a result
  without `crashed` (set on every item of a re-judge that raised) is
  applied by `_redrive_apply_item_verdicts` (which also appends an item
  re-read unmet that `unmet_final` lacks) and removed from `unverified`.
  The `final_sha` re-key requires `unverified` to be empty.
- **Result.** `{pre_sha, post_sha, prior_met[], untouched[], execution[],
  exec_flagged[], exec_unchecked[], judge, regressed[], unverified[],
  new_failures[], intermittent_regression[], merge_checks?,
  merge_checks_broke?[]}`. `exec_unchecked` lists the `execution`
  items when `exec_result` was `unmeasured` (no ID diff on either side) or
  carries `budget_short_unsettled` candidates — not a rollback, but logged, so an unmeasured execution route never reads
  as the items holding (DESIGN §8 *A held case that fails again*).
  `unverified` is derived, not listed per failure: `prior_met` less every
  item a route read on `post_sha` (the `untouched` ones; with the
  classifier's kinds, the `execution` ones not in `exec_unchecked` and the
  judged ones not in the judge's `unverified`) and less `regressed` — so
  an `exec_unchecked` item is `unverified` (review round 14 M3). `regressed` or `new_failures` non-empty is
  a rollback (`_ratchet_rollback_reason`). `_ratchet_kept(st, rat)` stores
  the judge's `met_evidence` under `delivery_ratchet.evidence[i] = {sha,
  evidence}` and appends new `intermittent_regression` rows to
  `delivery_ratchet.intermittent_regression`, which
  `_intermittent_regression_rows` reads after `test_id_diff`'s.
- **Re-drive.** A group whose ratchet regressed an item records
  `ratchet_regressed`, is void and rolled back, and each such item becomes
  a pending note `{kind: control_regression, key: met-item-<i>, test:
  "required item <i>", detail}`. A group whose ratchet has
  `merge_checks_broke` records their ids as `merge_checks_broke`, is void
  and rolled back (`_redrive_rollback_reason` adds "it turned the
  repository's merge check(s) red: <_ci_broke_text>"), and each check not
  already pending becomes `_redrive_merge_check_note(b)`: `{kind:
  control_regression, key: ci-<id>, test: "merge check `<id>` (<command>)",
  detail}` — the detail says an earlier attempt turned it red, confirmed
  against the tree before it, and was reverted, "Keep it passing.", then
  "Its first error lines:" and `b.lines`, one per line.

### Delivery re-drive — `_run_delivery_redrive`

DESIGN §8 *Delivery re-drive*. `_run_phases` calls
`_run_delivery_redrive(leerie_dir, st, caps, models, efforts)` right after
`_run_ci_parity_final` (advisory: any exception is logged and finalize
proceeds). It returns at once when `delivery_redrive.done` is set, without
a staging worktree or a readable HEAD, and records `done` with nothing
driven when nothing is open. A recorded `in_flight` group (a crash
mid-group) is rolled back to its `pre_sha` first; its rounds stay spent.

- **Open work.** Sets: the shown/held-back split is
  `_acceptance_shown_indices` over **every** valid set, broken ones
  included, so the held-back identity is the one the run held back all
  along (re-splitting over the unbroken sets would move a held-back set to
  shown and name it, I3); shown and held-back are then that split's sets
  not typed broken, and only they are measured or given to a self-check.
  `_redrive_failing(results, sets, indices)` receives every valid set,
  broken ones included (`by_index` in `_run_delivery_redrive`, which
  `set_note` reads too), and keys each failing file of a measured set in
  `indices` that has work (`_acceptance_result_has_work`) as
  `"<index>:<file>"` → `{set_index, file, kind: defect | control,
  failing_cases[]}`; in a bounded set only a defect file with work
  (`_acceptance_file_has_work`, per case) is kept. A result whose index has
  no set record is skipped, never looked up as `{}` (which
  `_acceptance_result_has_work` reads as unbounded and unbroken); the same
  holds in `_acceptance_work_fails`. **Reproducibility check** (DESIGN §8
  *Delivery re-drive* rule 4): before routing each round,
  `_redrive_unreproducible(notes, shown) -> list[str]` (pure) returns the
  key of every `defect` / `control_regression` note with a `set_index`
  (the round's notes and `pending_controls`) whose set is not a shown set
  not typed broken or whose file is not among that set's defect and
  control files — the `run_files` `_selfcheck_prepare(…, shown, …)` gives
  the group — and of every `unmet_item` note
  `_redrive_item_note_reproducible(n, shown_idx)` fails over those shown
  sets' indices: `by` not a non-empty list, or naming a source in
  `_REDRIVE_UNREPRODUCIBLE_BY = frozenset({"falsifier"})` while the note
  carries no `probe` with `dir`, `file` and `lead_sets` ⊆ the shown
  indices; any such key
  raises `RuntimeError` (a leerie defect, never a note handed to a worker;
  `_run_phases` logs it as advisory). The start verdict is `acceptance.gate.final`
  when `gate.final_sha` is the staging HEAD, else one
  `_evaluate_acceptance_sets` of the shown sets (B*-confirmed). Items:
  `delivery_gate.unmet_final`, split by `_redrive_item_notes(unmet_final,
  claims, n_items, rows, *, shown_idx=(), contested=(), suite=None,
  probe_owners=None) -> (notes, records)` (`rows` is
  `delivery_gate.items`; `shown_idx` the indices of the shown sets not
  typed broken; `contested` the item indices of
  `delivery_redrive.contested_probes`, a measured conflict, through
  `_redrive_contests_by_item`; `suite`, the run's browser channel,
  `_browser_suite(st)`). `_falsifier_shown_probe(row, shown_idx,
  suite=None) -> dict | None` reads the row's confirmed sample: `{dir,
  file, lead_sets, case_name, assertion_quote, reason, item_span_quote,
  via_browser_suite?}` (texts cut to `_REDRIVE_PROBE_TEXT_MAX = 600`;
  `via_browser_suite: true` when the sample has it) when its `lead_sets`
  is a list of integers ⊆ `shown_idx`, `probe_saved.dir/file` is a
  regular file (not a link, `file` relative without `..`) and, for a
  sample with `via_browser_suite`, `suite` is not None; else None. An entry's
  `by` (`["judge"]` when absent) less `_REDRIVE_UNREPRODUCIBLE_BY` —
  keeping `falsifier` when the item is not contested and its probe is
  shown — is its reproducible sources. With none, the item is no note:
  it is a record `{item_index, item, reason: "unreproducible", probed}`
  (`probed`, `_redrive_probed(row)`: the confirmed falsifier sample's
  `item_span_quote`, `_scope_norm`ed, from its `items[]` row; `""` when
  none), or nothing when it is contested (it was driven). An item every
  claimer types `process` (`_item_claims`) has one reproducible source at
  most: `falsifier`, when its probe is shown, not contested, and
  `probe_owners(probe)` is non-empty — in `_run_delivery_redrive`, the
  subtasks (`subfiles` order) whose `subfiles` files or
  `_redrive_kept_files(staging, rec, sids)` files (sid -> the source files
  `git diff --name-only <pre_sha> <post_sha>` of every group in
  `rec.rounds` with both, not `rolled_back`, that it was a member of,
  filtered as `_redrive_subtask_files` filters) meet
  `_redrive_exercised(_js_source_graph(run repo, staging HEAD), {dir,
  defect_files: [file]}, file)`; its note's `claimed_by` is those owners
  and it carries `process: true`. With none, it is a record `{item_index,
  item, reason: "no_code_target"}` — `unreproducible` with `probed` when
  its only source is a falsifier whose probe is not shown — or nothing
  when its only source is a contested falsifier. Otherwise the note is
  `{kind: "unmet_item", key: "item-<i>", item_index, item, evidence, by:
  <reproducible sources>, claimed_by[], evidence_keys[], process?,
  probe?}` (`probe` the shown probe when `falsifier` is among them;
  `evidence_keys` the `_redrive_evidence_keys({by: <its sources>}, row)`),
  its `evidence` the `" | "` join
  of `evidence_by[<source>]` over those sources; an entry with no
  `evidence_by` keeps its `evidence` when every source is reproducible,
  else `""` (code does not split the joined prose). The records are never
  routed or driven, are re-checked with the rest at the end
  (`start_items` holds them), and are accounted by
  `_redrive_unrouted_items` — also when they are the only open work,
  where the re-drive ends before any round. Evidence keys
  (`_redrive_evidence_keys(u, row, *, contested=False) -> list[str]`): one
  per source of the entry's `by` (`["judge"]` when not a list); a
  falsifier source is `_redrive_probe_key(row)` — `"falsifier:"` + the
  first 16 hex of the SHA-256 of the confirmed sample's `probe_saved.file`,
  a NUL and the file's bytes (`_read_beneath`, at most
  `_REDRIVE_PROBE_KEY_MAX = 1 MiB`), else `"falsifier"` when no saved
  probe can be read — and none when the item is contested; any other
  source is its name. Right after a group's implementer returns, the keys
  of every `unmet_item` note it held join `evidence_handed` as
  `"<i>:<key>"`; at each round's start the open notes' keys join an
  in-memory `seen`.
  Merge checks: `_ci_parity_unmet(st)`. Residual solution defects:
  `conformance._final.residual_defects`, each a note `{kind:
  "solution_defect", key: "solution-defect-<j>", defect_kind, where,
  concrete_case, why, exercised: [_solution_defect_file(where, files)]}`
  until its key is in `defects_driven` (read at each round's start and
  again before each group, below); `_solution_defect_file` is the
  integrated source file that `where` names (the whole string, or its part
  before a `:`), else none.
- **Routing** (`_redrive_route(notes, subfiles, *, fallback, pending)`,
  pure). `subfiles` maps each planned subtask — plan order, status not
  `blocked` / `accepted_external`, not accept-blocked; an `unconverged` one
  is included (DESIGN §8 *An unmet item reaches its owner, or is recorded
  as reaching none*) — to
  `_redrive_subtask_files`: the source files (`_CONTRACT_CODE_FILE_RE`, not
  `_is_test_file`) its `leerie: integrate <sid>` merge changed
  (`_integration_commit`, `git diff --name-only <merge>^1 <merge>`), else
  its `files_likely_touched`. A set file's exercised files are
  `_redrive_exercised(graph, set, file)`: the in-repo production modules
  its import / `require` / `vi.mock` / `jest.mock` specifiers resolve to
  (`_js_source_graph` of the staging HEAD, `_js_resolve`; JS/TS only). All
  defect notes go to the union of subtasks whose files meet any defect
  file's exercised files, else `fallback` (the audited fix sites'
  claimers; in a held-back round the subtasks earlier groups drove), else
  every subtask. A control note (a failing set control, a held-back
  control, a red check via `_redrive_ci_files`: its diagnostics' files
  under its cwd, a coverage glob matched with `_ci_glob_match`; a
  `solution_defect` by its `where` file) goes to the
  subtasks it touches, else the defect claimers, else every subtask. An
  item goes to every claimer (`_item_claims(plan_subtasks)` over
  `claims.items`; for a `process` note, its `claimed_by`, the owners of its
  probe), else the defect claimers, else every subtask. Subtasks
  sharing a file are unioned into one group; groups and members keep plan
  order; every group also carries the pending `control_regression` notes.
- **Rounds.** At most as many as the members' shared counters allow, and
  none once `redrive_spent_sec` reaches `redrive_budget_sec`, checked
  before each round. With the budget already spent on entry (a resume after
  that stop), the pre-round baseline `_redrive_test_ids(…, "redrive-ids0")`
  is not measured either. A
  round is held-back when no shown file fails, held-back sets exist and the
  held-back round has not run: the held-back sets are measured and their
  failing files become names-only notes (`HELD-BACK ACCEPTANCE FAILURES`).
  Per group, in order: the notes still open are kept (a set note only when
  its file still fails; a `ci_check` note only when
  `_redrive_checks_cleared(st, caps, notes, head, touched) -> set[str]` does not
  name its key — `head` the group's start, read from staging; the keys of
  the checks whose kept measurement of `head` (`_ci_remembered`) reads
  them green: a gate `passed`, a diagnostic ratchet with no
  `_ci_new_diagnostics` key against the base over `touched` (`_ci_touched`
  base..`head`, read only when such a note is open), a coverage ratchet
  with no `_ci_coverage_fired` threshold; no kept measurement clears
  nothing, and nothing is run; recorded as the group's `checks_cleared`
  and logged; a `solution_defect` note only while its key is not in
  `defects_driven`, which an earlier kept group of the same round may have
  added — the keys dropped recorded as the group's `defects_closed` and
  logged; items always), and a group with none is
  skipped (`skipped: nothing_left`, no counter consumed); members whose `_redrive_allowed` is
  false are dropped (`skipped: budget` when none is left, its unmet items
  added to `items_budget_skipped`); a group that drives adds its items to
  `items_driven`; each member's
  counter is consumed (`_consume_redrive`); `in_flight {pre_sha, round,
  group}` is saved; with shown sets, in a Prisma/PostgreSQL repo the
  implementer is spawned through `scripts/sandbox-db.sh`
  (`_redrive_drive(…, db=True)` → `claude_p(…, db=True)`: its own cluster
  for its session, which its self-check uses through its environment) and
  the self-check prepared
  (DESIGN §8 *A held-out set never enters a tree a worker commits from*):
  `_selfcheck_prepare(st, caps, staging, shown, label, probes=()) -> dict`
  writes `<run>/selfcheck/<label>/` holding `sets/set-<index>/<rel>` (a
  read-only copy of each shown set's files, the source the note points
  at; never under the read-denied `acceptance/`) and
  `sets/probe-i<k>/<rel>` for each of `probes` — `_redrive_probe_sets(live)`:
  per item whose note carries a shown `probe`, `{index: "probe-i<k>",
  item_index, dir, defect_files: [file], control_files: [],
  support_files: [], via_browser_suite?}` (`via_browser_suite: true` when
  the probe has it); the self-check is prepared (and the implementer
  given a database) when the group has shown sets or such probes —,
  `config.json` (`{tree,
  repo_root, sets[{index, dir, defect_files, control_files,
  support_files}] with `dir` the copy, snap_root
  (`_selfcheck_copies(st.run_dir, label)`), env (empty), suite,
  forbidden, timeout, log}`; `suite` is None, or, when a probe has
  `via_browser_suite`, `{template, files, env}`: `_browser_suite(st)`'s
  `template`, those probes' files, and `_browser_suite_env(suite)` less
  `TEST_DB_ENV_NAMES` when `"database"` is in its `requires` — with no
  `_browser_suite(st)` it raises `RuntimeError`, a leerie defect, since
  `_falsifier_shown_probe` shows such a probe only with the channel) and
  `bin/leerie-selfcheck` (a bash wrapper: `exec python3
  <leerie>/scripts/selfcheck.py <config.json> "$@"`), and returns `{dir,
  bin, command, src, run_files, name_flag, probes{item_index: path}}` —
  `run_files` the shown sets' defect and control files and each probe's
  file, `probes` each probe's copy, `command` the wrapper when either
  channel has files, `name_flag` the runners' own test-name flag
  (`_SELFCHECK_NAME_FLAGS`: vitest/jest `-t`, pytest `-k`, playwright
  `-g`) when every channel's runner — the one read off
  `_acceptance_cmd(st, <run_files not on the suite>, staging)`, the
  suite's `runner` — has the same one, else None; the
  bin directory is put first on the implementer's `PATH` (`env_extra`).
  Before a group whose `probe_sets` hold a `via_browser_suite` probe, with
  `_browser_suite(st)` set, the drive runs `_ci_prepare(staging,
  [_browser_suite_rec(suite)], st, caps, "redrive", done=<one set per
  pass>)`: the copy shares staging's ignored paths and tree stores.
  `scripts/selfcheck.py` imports the orchestrator and calls
  `selfcheck_main(argv) -> int` (public: its caller is `scripts/selfcheck.py`, a separate process, like `run_rebaser`'s `host-finalize.sh`): `_selfcheck_args(args, run_files)`
  splits the arguments into a subset (each argument naming exactly one
  set test file: its path, its file name or a unique path suffix; one
  naming several is a usage error, exit 2), a name filter
  (`-t`/`--testNamePattern`/`-k`/`-g` with a value, `=`-joined or not) and the
  rest, passed through to the runner (bench I3-3's selection); SIGTERM,
  SIGHUP and SIGINT raise `SystemExit(128 + signum)`, so the copy's
  deletion runs on every exit. `_selfcheck_snapshot(tree, snap)` copies every path of
  `_untracked_listing(tree, cached=True)` that exists (gitlinks
  skipped) through one `tar --null --no-recursion -T - -cf - | tar -xf -`
  pipe (symlinks as symlinks) — no temporary index, so it writes no git
  object; `_share_ignored_paths(tree, snap, set_files) -> {paths, linked,
  copied}` gives the copy every path of `_untracked_listing(tree,
  which="ignored", directory=True)` as its own (DESIGN §8 *The
  self-check's copy is a tree of its own*) except one that is a set file
  or an ancestor of one, or that holds `snap` (realpaths): reached from
  `tree` and `snap` without following a link (`_open_dir_beneath`, the
  copy's missing parents made), each entry made by `_link_entry_at(sfd,
  dfd, name, counts)` relative to the two open directories — a directory
  made (`0700`, then the source's mode `| 0o700`) and filled by
  `_link_tree_at(sfd, dfd, counts)`, a link made again with the same
  target (`readlink`), anything else `os.link`ed (`follow_symlinks=False`);
  a link refused with `EXDEV`, `EPERM` or `EMLINK` (`_NO_LINK_ERRNOS`) of a
  regular file copies its bytes instead (`O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`, its mode),
  any other error raises; `linked` and `copied` count the files; a path
  gone since the listing is skipped; a set path already present in the copy is refused (exit 3,
  listed); `_place_set` places every shown set, files `0444`; the files
  to run (the subset, else every test file) split by channel: those not
  in the config's `suite.files` through `_acceptance_cmd(st, files,
  snap)`, those in it through `_runner_command(_browser_suite_cmd(suite,
  files), snap, _RUNNER_REPORTS, files)` with its path overlay and
  `suite.env` (DESIGN §8 *A probe is re-run through the channel that
  confirmed it*); for each, the name filter (the channel's runner's
  `_SELFCHECK_NAME_FLAGS` flag; exit 2 when it has none) and the rest
  appended by `_append_runner_flags`
  (exit 2 when they cannot be placed); then, in turn, each is bound
  through `_blt_shell_argv` against the config's forbidden specs right
  before its launch — one the task forbids is never launched: `SELF-CHECK
  UNMEASURED: <files> not run — <reason>`, the call record gains
  `unmeasured{<file>: "forbidden_by_task"}` and `forbidden` (kept by
  `_selfcheck_calls`), and the other channel still runs — and run in the
  copy under `bash -c` with the config's `env`, the channel's and
  `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES=<snap_root>`, each printed `SELF-CHECK: <cmd>`,
  all inside one budget, the config's timeout (exit 124, which ends the
  call). The call's exit is the first non-zero run's, else 2 when a
  channel was refused (no verdict, never a pass), else 0. It prints
  the runner's output, then `SELF-CHECK PASSED|FAILED (exit N) …`, deletes the copy
  (`_rmtree_owned`) and appends `{ts,
  args, subset, name_filter, files, shared, linked, copied, rc, secs_*}`
  to the config's `log` (`shared` the number of paths shared). After the
  drive the group records the calls (`selfcheck_calls`, first 50) and
  `_selfcheck_cleanup(sc)` removes `<run>/selfcheck/<label>/` and
  `_selfcheck_copies(<run>, <label>)`; a resumed crash removes
  `<run>/selfcheck/` and `<run>/worktrees/.selfcheck/` whole. `_selfcheck_prepare`
  removes both for its label first and makes `<run>/selfcheck/<label>/run/`
  (0700). The span fingerprints of the
  shown sets (`_heldout_fingerprints(staging, [{dir, files}], pre_sha) ->
  dict[int, frozenset[bytes]]`, the anti-cheat of DESIGN §8): per set file
  (its first `_HELDOUT_SOURCE_MAX =
  1 MiB`), its normalised lines (`_heldout_pieces(readline)`: pieces of at
  most `_HELDOUT_LINE_MAX = 4096` bytes, `\s+` collapsed to one space and
  trimmed, kept only when they hold `[A-Za-z0-9]` and no NUL and, once
  `_HELDOUT_LITERAL_RE` (quoted strings with an optional `r`/`b`/`u`/`f`
  prefix, unterminated included; numbers; `True False None true false
  null nil undefined`) is stripped, still hold `[A-Za-z_]` — a literal-only
  line is never in a span, review round 13 M1), and every window of
  `_HELDOUT_SPAN_LINES = 4` of them — or one window of all of a file with
  fewer, when it has at least `_HELDOUT_SPAN_MIN = 2` — as a 16-byte
  `blake2b` digest (`_span_digest`), keyed
  by window length; less every window all of whose lines the base holds:
  the files of `pre_sha` holding any of the lines (`git grep -l -z -I -F -f
  <temp pattern file> pre_sha --`), read through one `git cat-file --batch`
  up to `_HELDOUT_BASE_SCAN_MAX = 64 MiB`, normalised the same way, their
  lines compared whole; a base it could not read drops nothing.
  `_holds_heldout_span(pieces, prints)` slides each length over the
  pieces; `_history_heldout_hits(staging, pre_sha, post_sha, staged,
  prints) -> list[str]` is every path of `git log --raw -m --no-abbrev
  --no-renames -z pre..post` (`-m`: a merge's blobs against each parent)
  that is a set file's path or whose new blob, read through one `git
  cat-file --batch`, holds a span (unreadable history → the set files). A
  value the test asserts — a literal, an identifier, a path — is never a
  span on its own (`tests/test_heldout_bytes_never_reach_history.py`).
  The probes the group holds are staged files here too (their source is
  fingerprinted and their paths checked like a shown set's).
  The commits' set paths and those hits are unioned
  into `committed_staged`; one implementer runs in staging (`_redrive_drive`:
  `_implementer_base_prompt` of the first member + `NOTE FROM
  ORCHESTRATOR:` `_redrive_note(...)`, `claude_p(schema_key="implementer",
  allowed_tools=ACT_TOOLS, max_turns=120, autonomous=True,
  sid="delivery-redrive-r<round>-g<group>")`, effort the resolved
  implementer effort or `EFFORT_REDRIVE_ESCALATION`, with the self-check's
  bin first on `PATH`; it returns `{status, summary, probe_objections?}`,
  the worker's raw `probe_objections`, first 10). `_redrive_note` renders
  an `unmet_item` note's `probe` as `{test_file, failing_case,
  failing_assertion, why_it_fails}` and, when any note has one, a PROBES
  paragraph naming the self-check, the rollback of a commit that leaves
  the probe failing or breaks a case an existing test pins, and the
  `probe_objections` fields. `_redrive_probe_objections(raw, probes) ->
  list[dict]` keeps each `{item_index, probe_test_file, kind, reason}`
  (first 10, `reason` cut to 1200) whose `probe_test_file` is a probe of
  `probes` (its relative path, or a path ending in `/<path>`) and whose
  `kind` is in `PROBE_OBJECTION_KINDS = ("input_outside_domain",
  "contradicts_task", "breaks_existing_test")`; nothing in it is checked
  as true. They are recorded on the group (`probe_objections`) and
  appended, with `round` and `group`, to
  `delivery_redrive.probe_objections`; they change no routing and no
  verdict. Then the clean-tree gate runs (a group
  left dirty past its re-asks is rolled back), and, when HEAD moved, the shown sets (and, in a
  held-back round, the held-back ones) are re-measured, each shown probe
  the group was handed is re-run on the commit
  (`_redrive_probe_verdicts(st, caps, staging, probe_sets, label, *, rev)
  -> {item_index: pass | fail | unmeasured}`: each probe as
  `_falsifier_probe_set(item_index, dir, rel, *, via_browser_suite=False)`
  — `{index: 1000000 + item_index, dir, defect_files: [rel],
  control_files: [], support_files: [], cases: {}, via_browser_suite?}`,
  `via_browser_suite` from the probe, the shape `_redrive_recheck_items`
  re-runs too, with the sample's —
  through one `_evaluate_acceptance_sets`; recorded as `probes_after
  {"<i>": verdict}`), and the repo's test
  command re-run for failing IDs (`_redrive_test_ids`, which is
  `_ratchet_test_ids` on staging, measured in its committed view, with the re-drive log: a command the task
  forbids is replaced by its `_scoped_test_replacement`, or no verdict when
  there is nothing to run — never run raw), new ones confirmed
  against a `redrive-base` worktree at `pre_sha` by `_confirm_new_failures`
  (`_redrive_new_failures`, through `_ratchet_exec`, which then runs the
  intermittent discovery if none is new and types `intermittent_regression`
  rows, recorded on the group), after the group's near stage
  (`_near_rejection`), whose verdict stands for all of this when it rejects
  the group. `_redrive_verdict` (pure): `worse` when any set
  case newly fails (`broke_cases`, from `_redrive_broken_cases(before,
  after)`: every case of a key failing only after — the key itself when it
  has no per-case record — plus, for a key failing on both sides with
  per-case records, the IDs that joined its list, plus the key itself for
  a key that failed with a per-case record before and fails with none
  after: a whole-file failure, an import or collection error — never for
  an after entry marked `no_case_evidence`), a control file newly
  fails, or a test is confirmed newly failing — in a held-back round also
  when a held-back case newly fails (`held_broke_cases`), a held-back
  control newly fails, or none is fixed; a set or held-back
  measurement that produced nothing carries the earlier verdict
  (`resource_affected`), and the held-back rules then do not apply. A group
  is `zero_progress` when a set note it drove names a set that produced a
  verdict after it (a held-back note: the held-back sets did), or a probe
  it was handed has a `pass` or `fail` verdict, and it fixed no set case,
  shown or held-back, and no probe of it passes — `_redrive_fixed_cases(before, after)`:
  every case of a key no longer failing (the key itself when it has no
  per-case record) plus, for a key failing on both sides with per-case
  records, the IDs that left its list; `_redrive_verdict` returns them as
  `fixed_cases` / `held_fixed_cases`, and the held-back "none is fixed" rule
  reads `held_fixed_cases` too. When a probe of the group passes,
  `_redrive_pinned_breaks(repo, base, post_sha, newv) -> [{id, file}]`
  (sorted by id) reads the cases an existing test pins that fail on the
  commit: the `newv["base_form"]["changed"]` rows, and each confirmed
  `newv["new"]` ID whose `newv["files"]` file exists at the run's
  `_diff_base` and is not in `git diff --name-only base post_sha`. These
  are read right after the group's `_ratchet_exec(..., base_form=True)`
  (or near stage), before `new_failures` / `base_form_changed` are
  recorded. When any is found, `_redrive_task_required(st, caps, models,
  efforts, staging, rec, pinned, probes, *, rnd, gi) -> {case id:
  verdict}` asks the contradiction judge (DESIGN §8 *Delivery re-drive*
  rule 4, *A pinned case a required item's probe contradicts is
  task-required*), `probes` being item index -> the `probe` of each
  passing item's `unmet_item` note in the group: per pinned case, in
  order, items ascending, `_contradiction_verdict` until one is
  `exclusive`; the first case with none ends it with `{}`; more than
  `_REDRIVE_CONTEST_TESTS_MAX` pinned cases, no `_diff_base`, or no probe
  is `{}` with no call. A raise is logged and is `{}`. When it returns
  every pinned case, the group records `task_required[{id, item_index}]`,
  drops those IDs from `newv["base_form_changed"]`, and `pinned` becomes
  empty (no conflict); a settled ID still in `newv["new"]` (its test file
  left as the base had it) stays a new failure, and its pending
  `control_regression` note's `detail` is
  `_redrive_task_required_detail(verdict)` ("required item <i>
  contradicts this existing test case … Change this test case to what the
  item requires; do not leave it failing, and do not restore the old
  behaviour."). Otherwise, when any pinned case remains, the group records
  `probe_conflict{items, tests}` (tests
  first `_REDRIVE_CONTEST_TESTS_MAX = 10`) and each passing probe's item
  is appended to `delivery_redrive.contested_probes` as `{item_index,
  probe_test_file, tests[], round, group}`. Such a group is already
  rolled back (each pinned case is in `new_failures`, making it worse, or
  in `base_form_changed`, voiding it); `_redrive_rollback_reason` names
  the conflict, and the zero-progress words add "(a shown falsifier probe
  counts as one)" when the group has `probes_after`. A group that is none of the below then
  runs `_delivery_ratchet` (`ratchet`). A group that is worse, zero-progress,
  committed staged material (`committed_staged`), fails the escalation gate, or whose ratchet
  regressed a previously met item or turned a merge check red is
  rolled back (`_roll_back_round(st, staging, pre_sha, ...)`, *A rollback says why*); the controls it broke become pending `control_regression`
  notes. A `trade` (something fixed and something broken) records its
  `(fixed, broken)` pairs in `trade_pairs`; a pair seen before is a
  `conflict` — `{pairs, round, reason}` with `reason` a sentence naming
  both sides — and the re-drive stops; each pair whose broken side is a
  test whose file is tracked at the own start is appended to
  `contradictions`. Wall time is charged with `_charge_redrive_time`.
- **Contradiction judge** (DESIGN §8 *Delivery re-drive* rule 4, *A pinned
  case a required item's probe contradicts is task-required*):
  `_contradiction_verdict(st, caps, models, efforts, staging, rec, *, base,
  case, item_index, probe, rnd, gi) -> dict` appends to and returns from
  `rec["contradiction_verdicts"]` one `{case, file, item_index,
  probe_test_file, round, group, status, key?, model?, effort?,
  code_files?, same_entry_point?, same_input_by_meaning?, same_observable?,
  mutually_exclusive?, evidence?[{test, quote}] (first
  `_CONTRADICTION_QUOTES_KEPT` = 12, each cut at `_CONTRADICTION_TEXT_MAX`
  = 1200), explanation?, failures[], quotes?{pinned, independent}, error?}`.
  `key` = sha256 of the case ID, `base`, the two paths and the probe's text
  (first 16 hex); a verdict with the same `key` and no `error` is returned
  as is (no call). The pinned file is `_git_blob_text(run repo, base,
  file)` — never a later form — and the probe is read with
  `_read_beneath(dir, dir/file, limit=READ_LIMIT_TEXT)`; either unreadable
  is `unsettled` with no call. `_contradiction_code_files(g, [(path,
  text), ...]) -> [path]` over `_js_source_graph(repo, base)`: each test's
  imports and mocks (`_JS_IMPORT_RE`, `_JS_MOCK_RE`, `_js_resolve`), then
  `g["imp"]` transitively, keeping only production files (in `g["files"]`,
  not `_js_is_test`, not `g["support"]`). The payload `<run_dir>/
  CONTRADICTION_DIRNAME ("contradiction")/<key>/` (`_mkdir_private`,
  files by `_write_beneath`) holds `pinned/<file>`, `independent/<probe
  file>` and `code/<path>` (text from `g["src"]`), and is removed
  (`_rmtree_owned`) after the call whatever happens. The two cases' facts
  are `_contradiction_facts(st, view, src, rel, case)`:
  `_probe_case_facts_placed` over `_measured_tree(staging)` with the file
  placed beside `rel` (`_BASE_FORM_FACTS_PREFIX`), the pinned case named
  by its ID after ` :: `, the probe by its `case_name`; a facts error (a
  file the TS parse cannot read: every other language) is `unsettled`
  with no call. The call: `claude_p(user_prompt=
  _contradiction_user_prompt((file, title), (probe file, title), code),
  system_prompt=_load_prompt("contradiction_judge"),
  schema_key="contradiction_judge", cwd=<payload>,
  allowed_tools=CONTRADICTION_JUDGE_TOOLS ("Read,Grep,Glob"),
  max_turns=CONTRADICTION_JUDGE_MAX_TURNS (60), autonomous=False, model,
  effort, sid="contradiction_judge-r<r>g<g>-i<i>-<key[:8]>")`, titles the
  facts' `title` (else the name given); `WorkerError` or a timeout is
  `unsettled` with `error`. `_contradiction_check(res, srcs, code,
  asserts) -> (failures, first)`: every quote `_ws_norm`ed is non-empty
  and a substring of its `test`'s file (`code`: of some code file); each of
  `pinned`/`independent` needs one quote with
  `_falsifier_quoted_assertion_lines(src, quote, asserts)` non-empty
  (`first[test]`, stripped). `_contradiction_status(res, failures)`:
  `unsettled` on any failure; `exclusive` when `mutually_exclusive` and the
  three `same_*` are all true; `unsettled` when `mutually_exclusive` is
  true without them; else `both_can_hold` (`CONTRADICTION_STATUSES`).
  `_contradiction_rule(verdict) -> "task_required" | "regression"` is the
  one place a status becomes a rule (`task_required` on `exclusive`, and on
  `unsettled` with `intent_decision == "yes"`). In `_redrive_task_required`
  each verdict first goes through `_contradiction_intent(st, caps, models,
  efforts, v)`: an `unsettled` verdict without `error` becomes the intent
  question `intent-contradiction-<case, [^A-Za-z0-9_.-] → ->-i<item>`
  (`_contradiction_question(v, item_text)`), settled by
  `resolve_intent_conflict`; an open one is asked at once
  (`_stop_for_intent_questions`); the verdict records `intent_qid` and
  `intent_decision` (DESIGN §11 source (c)).
