  `_redrive_task_required_cases(rec) -> {case id: verdict}`: the first
  `task_required` verdict per case. `_redrive_base_form_open` drops those
  cases from every base-form note (a note left with none is not offered).
- **Escalation** (`_redrive_escalate`): every member is on its last round
  (`redrive_rounds + 1 >= subtask_redrive_rounds`), the group's notes name
  a failing set, every such set is from the own-start writer
  (`acceptance.validity_base == _acceptance_own_start(st)`) and
  `_redrive_audit_blocks(set) is False` (its `audit.sample_kinds` exist and
  no strict majority of the samples typed a case `contradicts_task`), and
  `_redrive_ast_available(staging)` (`node`, `REDRIVE_AST_GATE`, and
  `_ts_resolvable(staging)` — a compiler API from staging's `typescript`
  or the bundled copy, so always true in the image). After the round
  `_redrive_escalation_gate(staging, pre_sha, head)` voids it on any of:
  `_redrive_weakened_tests` — a test-shaped file (`_REDRIVE_TEST_RE`)
  present at `pre_sha` deleted, or with fewer `expect(`/`assert(` call
  sites, fewer `it(`/`test(` cases, or more `.skip(`/`.only(`/`.todo(`/
  `xit(`/`xdescribe(`/`xtest(`; `_redrive_schema_hits` — the Q3 schema
  gate v2 over added lines of changed JS/TS production files: required
  fields from `schema.prisma` models the file names, base `z.object` keys
  without `.optional/.nullable/.nullish/.default/.catch`, and base
  interface/type members without `?`/`| null`/`| undefined`; rules C1
  (`.f ?? x`, `.f || x`), C2 (`!x.f ||`, `x.f == null ||`), C3 (`x.f ? a :
  b`), C1C2 on destructured aliases, C4 (a required member made optional),
  C5 (a required relation key removed from a `where:` object); a (rule,
  field) also matched on a removed line of the same hunk is exempt, as is
  an `if` line whose next four head lines throw or return an error, a
  default of `[]`/`{}`/`new Map()`/`new Set()`, and a C1 on `A ?? <read of
  f> ?? ""` whose `A` is optional; `_redrive_ast_hits` — `node
  scripts/redrive-ast-gate.cjs <base> <head> <name>` per changed JS/TS
  production file (cwd staging, env `_ts_script_env()`): D1 a null-guarded throw or error return
  of the base missing under the same (function, condition), D2 a new
  success-shaped `if (<null test>) return …` before an error in the same
  function, D3 a new catch that swallows an error class some changed file
  throws under a null guard; a script that yields no JSON voids the round.
- **Re-check and record.** At a round's end, when HEAD differs from the
  commit the verdict being replaced was made on (`items_rechecked_sha`,
  which starts as `delivery_gate.final_sha` — never empty, so a round that
  changed nothing re-judges nothing): routed items
  are re-checked (`_redrive_recheck_items`: judge-unmet and
  untouched-paths items through `_delivery_judge_unmet(<all required
  items>, phase_label="redrive", only=<those indices>,
  full_vote=_judge_majority_items(<unmet_final>))` with
  `_delivery_record`, falsifier-confirmed items by
  re-running their saved probe — the first `falsifier.samples[]` with a
  `probe_saved`, its `via_browser_suite` carried — as a one-file set
  through `_evaluate_acceptance_sets`; unmet if either says
  so, and a crashed or unmeasured check keeps the item unmet; then
  `_redrive_falsify_met(st, caps, models, efforts, staging, out)` runs
  `_falsify_items(sha=<HEAD>, indices=<the re-checked items now met and
  not unknown, crashed, external, test_id_diff or untouched_paths>,
  parts_by_idx={}, progress={"items": {}})` — a met has detection's bar,
  DESIGN §8 *A re-check replaces a verdict only on a tree that changed,
  and only by the vote that made it* — and a confirmed item is unmet again
  with `by` + `["falsifier"]` and evidence `a falsifier probe of the
  item's words "<quote>" fails under B* on the re-checked tree`; every
  item it ran carries its record as `falsifier`, which
  `_redrive_apply_item_verdicts` writes onto the row, so the next re-check
  re-runs the new probe; `delivery_gate.final_progress` is restored to
  what it was, and a falsifier that cannot run leaves the re-check's
  verdict), and `_run_ci_parity_final` re-runs when a check was routed. When the re-drive
  ends on a HEAD other than its start, every valid set is measured once:
  `acceptance.gate.final` / `final_sha` and `residual`
  (`_acceptance_residual_of`) are rewritten, or kept when nothing measured;
  `_run_ci_parity_final` runs; `_redrive_refresh_test_id_diff(leerie_dir,
  st, caps, staging)` calls `_refresh_test_id_diff` (below, *The final
  diff describes the tree that ships*) with `label="redrive-final"`; every
  item still open at the start is re-checked unless that HEAD was already
  re-checked, and `delivery_gate.unmet_final` / `items[]` are rewritten
  (`_redrive_apply_item_verdicts(st, verdicts, sha, tree_sha)`, which
  settles each re-checked row on its stored `test_outcome_part` and then,
  given `tree_sha`, calls `_resettle_test_outcome_rows`); then
  `_resettle_test_outcome_rows(st, tree_sha)` re-reads every row's
  `test_outcome_part` the same way (a row the part alone made unmet, `by
  == ["test_id_diff"]`, is first restored to met), so no row carries
  detection's test-outcome verdict onto another tree. Then `done`.
  Before that resettle, and after the unverified items are read again,
  `_redrive_met_unread(st, final)` lists the items still to read. Each
  one's `delivery_gate.items` row has `verdict == "met"` or
  `other_parts == "met"`, its item passes `_falsifier_item` (not
  `external`, not `_test_id_diff_item`, no `untouched_paths`; detection's
  `f_idx` and `_redrive_falsify_met` use the same predicate), and its
  `redrive_recheck.sha` is not `final`. Those items go through
  `_redrive_recheck_items` (cited judge, then `_redrive_falsify_met`).
  The verdicts that did not crash are applied with
  `_redrive_apply_item_verdicts(st, ..., final, final_tree)`. A crashed
  item goes to `_ratchet_mark_unverified(st, crashed, final, "the
  delivery re-drive")`, which makes it `unknown`, lists it and blocks the
  re-key of `final_sha`. See DESIGN §8 *Every item the tree that ships
  reports met passed detection's bar on it*.
  Then, for every item that re-check made unmet with a confirmed falsifier
  sample (`_redrive_flip_probe({"falsifier": verdict["falsifier"]})`: the
  first sample with `confirmed`, `case_id` and `probe_saved{dir, file}`),
  `_redrive_flip_culprit(st, caps, rec, i, smp)` walks
  `_redrive_kept_groups(rec)` — every group with `pre_sha`, a different
  `post_sha` and no `rolled_back`, in landing order — through
  `_probe_flip_culprit` (steps `({round, group}, "r<r>g<g>", pre_sha,
  post_sha)`) and returns the first
  whose `_redrive_probe_flips(st, caps, smp, pre_sha, post_sha, label=)`
  says `flip`: the saved probe, copied to a temp file, placed in a held-out
  sandbox over a pristine installed checkout of each commit
  (`_falsifier_checkout(st, "flip-post"|"flip-pre", sha)`,
  `_ensure_worktree_deps`, the browser suite's prerequisites when the
  sample has `via_browser_suite`; no channel then: no verdict), run by
  `_capture_failing_test_ids(serial=True, files=[rel], db=True, place=)`
  under `_held_out_section` — once on `post_sha`, then on `pre_sha` (a
  start whose report does not list the case as `passed` is a fail) — and
  only `post: fail, pre: pass` goes to `_confirm_new_failures([case_id],
  <pre runner>, <post runner>, caps, seen_failing=True)`; `flip` when the case is `new`.
  Returns `{flip, pre, post, b_star?}`. With any culprit, the closure
  `roll_back_flips` resets staging to the earliest culprit's `pre_sha`
  through `_roll_back_round` (reason "its commit turned the confirmed
  falsifier probe of met item(s) from passing on its start to failing on
  its commit (B*): item <i> (<case_id>)"), marks it and every kept group
  after it `rolled_back` (a later one's reason "built on r<r>g<g>, rolled
  back: …"), stores each culprit on its group as `flip_regressed`, appends
  `flip_rollbacks`, and adds `_redrive_flip_note(i, item, smp, *,
  who="re-drive attempt", short="attempt")` — `{kind: control_regression,
  key: met-item-<i>, test: "required item <i>", detail}`, the detail
  ("an earlier <who> made this required item, met before it, unmet: …")
  naming the case, then the item, the sample's
  `assertion_quote` and `failure_message` — to `pending_controls` unless
  that key is pending. A reset that does not land sets `rollback_failed`
  and the pass ends as for any group. After a landed one, the items open at
  the start, `items_driven` and the flipped items are re-checked on the new
  HEAD (`_redrive_recheck_items`, applied with `_redrive_apply_item_verdicts`,
  a crashed one `_ratchet_mark_unverified`), `items_rechecked_sha` moves
  there, the shown sets and the test-ID baseline are measured again, and
  the round loop resumes: a member with a round left gets the note, and
  the end of the pass runs again even on the start commit. See DESIGN §8
  *A kept group that turns a met item's confirmed probe from passing to
  failing is rolled back*.

### Report-bounded has-work — `_acceptance_scope_judge_sets`

DESIGN §8 *A task that points at a report is bounded by the report's own
scenarios*. `phase_acceptance_write` calls `async
_acceptance_scope_judge_sets(task, st, caps, models, efforts, sets)` on its
valid sets when `_d1_report_sources(task, repo_root)` is non-empty (a
report-pointer task); `_acceptance_audit_and_rewrite` calls it again for a
set its rewrite replaced. Per set, per defect file with a case in
`base_failing_cases`, one `scope_judge` call (`allowed_tools="Read"`,
`max_turns=3`, cwd an empty `<run_dir>/scope-judge/`, budget-counted)
receives the task, the reports, the test file's source (first 60,000
characters) and the file's own-start cases numbered `[i]` with status and,
for a failing case, its runner message (first 600 characters,
whitespace-normalised). `_scope_judge_counted(out, haystack, cases,
failing) -> dict` is the decision, all in code: a range is verified when its
`span_quote` is a non-empty substring of the haystack (task + reports) after
`_scope_norm` (NFC, whitespace runs to one space, stripped); `ms`/`s` convert
to `ms`; each verified range is widened to the hull of the verified ranges of
its unit it overlaps; a case counts when it is in `failing`, its `origin` is
not `other_scenario`, its own `span_quote` verifies, and every param whose
`range_ref` names a verified range of the same (converted) unit lies inside
that hull (a param naming an unverified or out-of-list range, or another
unit, is neutral); a case of `failing` the judge's answer does not type
counts (`typed: false`). The set records `scope = {bounded: true,
counted_cases{file: [case ids]}, judged{file: {case id: {origin, in_range,
quote_ok, typed, counted}}}}`; a judge that raises (other than budget exhaustion) or
returns no cases leaves that file unbounded — the set records `scope =
{bounded: false, error}` and every failing file counts. The collected set
also carries `base_case_status{file: {case id: status}}` and
`base_failure_messages{file: {case id: message}}`, the judge's inputs.

`_acceptance_counted_files(set_) -> set[str] | None` (None when unbounded)
and `_acceptance_result_has_work(set_, failing_files, failing_cases=None) ->
bool` (not broken, and unbounded or some failing file has work by
`_acceptance_file_has_work(set_, rel, failing_cases)`: the file holds a
counted case and, when `failing_cases[rel]` is a non-empty list, one of
those IDs is in `counted_cases[rel]` — per case; a file with no per-case
record counts whole) are what every has-work reader uses: `_decide_outcome`
(passing each result's `failing_cases`), `_acceptance_residual_unbroken`
(drops a set whose recorded `files_by_set[index]` — with
`failing_cases_by_set[index]` — has no work; a residual without
`files_by_set` falls back to the set's own bound), `_acceptance_work_fails
(results, sets)` (the no-work settle in `_settle_pending_no_work`,
`_acceptance_passes_on_head` and `_fix_ids_held_out_sets_protect`, which on
the validity base passes each set's `base_failing_cases`), and
`_redrive_failing`. The repair rounds and the set audit still read
`_acceptance_any_fails`, so a variant set is repaired in the same pass. The
residual gains `files_by_set{index: [failing files]}` and
`failing_cases_by_set{index: {file: [case ids]}}`. The per-case record comes
from evaluation: `_acceptance_run_placed` calls `_run_acceptance_file(...,
cases_out=obs)`, which requests the runner's report as validation does
(`_acceptance_report_spec`) but keeps the exit-code verdict, and stores
`obs["failing_cases"]` (the report's `failed` case IDs; nothing on no report,
a collection error or zero executed cases), and `obs["resource"] = True`
when the run timed out, or exited by a signal (`_rc_is_resource_signal`:
a negative return code, or 128 + SIGKILL/TERM/SEGV/ABRT/BUS/HUP) with no
readable report. Each failing run of a file — the first and every vote
rerun — is kept, and `_acceptance_vote_cases(runs) -> list[str] | None`
derives the file's cases (DESIGN §8 *Delivery re-drive* rule 4):
`_acceptance_run_case_evidence(obs)` is None for a run with a resource
signature (`obs["resource"]`, or every failing case's non-blank message
matching `_RESOURCE_FAILURE_RE`), else the run's `failing_cases` (`[]`
for a collection error); the file's cases are the intersection over the
runs naming cases, their union when that is empty, `[]` when evidence
runs exist but none named a case, and None when no run gave evidence. A
confirmed failing file with IDs lands in the result's
`failing_cases{file: [ids]}`; one with None is listed in the result's
`no_case_evidence_files` (absent when empty). A file settled by an
`asserted` held case takes the asserting run's IDs instead, and an
intermittent file its held cases. `_acceptance_failing_keys` and
`_redrive_failing` carry `no_case_evidence: True` on such a file's entry
(the key absent otherwise), and `_redrive_broken_cases` then does not
count it as a whole-file collapse.

**Held cases (DESIGN §8 *A held case that fails again is a failure, not a
flake*).** `_acceptance_held_cases(set_, rel) -> set[str]` is the defect
file's `base_failing_cases[rel]`, intersected with `counted_cases[rel]`
when the scope judge bounded the set (`_acceptance_counted_files` not
None); empty for a control or a set recorded without
`base_failing_cases`. `_run_acceptance_file(..., cases_out=obs)` also
stores `obs["failing_messages"]{case id: message}` (the report's per-case
message, `_parse_runner_report`'s `messages`). `_acceptance_held_signals(
set_, rel, obs) -> (asserted, seen)`: `seen` the held cases among
`obs["failing_cases"]`, `asserted` those whose message is non-blank and
does not match `_RESOURCE_FAILURE_RE`. With `confirm`,
`_acceptance_run_placed` takes a failing file with any `asserted` case as
failing without a vote; the rest go to `_confirm_still_failing`, whose
reruns now pass `cases_out` too and run every file under one deadline of
the remaining budget they are given (`_budget_caps`; a file that budget
cut short ends the rerun as a `_RerunCut` — not a run, never a pass; a
file every finished rerun failed is confirmed and listed in
`budget_short_files`; a vote file whose first run set `obs["resource"]` —
a timeout or a signal death — goes in `needs_rerun`, so with no finished
rerun it is `budget_short_unsettled`, listed in
`budget_short_unsettled_files` and counted with `resource_affected` for
the unmeasured rule; an unmeasured result records why in
`unmeasured_reason` / `unmeasured_files`, codes of `ACCEPTANCE_UNMEASURED_WHY`,
which `_acceptance_unmeasured_lines` renders for the PR), and a rerun with an `asserted` case
settles its file failing whatever the vote says. Then discovery
(`_acceptance_discover`): for each defect file with held cases that did
not end failing, up to `acceptance_intermittent_repeats` (clamped to
`_ACCEPTANCE_INTERMITTENT_MAX = 10`) serial reruns under `_confirm_hold()`
and `_confirm_gate`, inside `confirm_budget_sec` counted from when the
gate returns — each rerun runs with `worker_timeout_sec` lowered to what
is left of the budget (`_budget_caps`), and a round whose run that
lowered timeout cut short is not counted, `budget_exhausted` set —
stopping at the first `asserted` case; a file that got one is failing. Whenever discovery had files to rerun, the result carries `discovery{files, repeats_required, repeats_run, budget_exhausted, found[], incomplete, reason, disabled?}`, found or not: `repeats_run` counts only rounds every pending file finished; `incomplete` is true and `reason` is `"budget_exhausted"` when the budget ran out before every round with files still pending, else false and `""`; with `acceptance_intermittent_repeats` 0 the record is `disabled: true, reason: "disabled"`, `incomplete: false` — neither logged nor listed. An incomplete discovery logs `acceptance <label> set <i>: discovery_incomplete — <run> of <required> rerun round(s) (<reason>)`, and `_pr_advisory` lists every `acceptance.gate.final` result whose discovery stopped short (`_acceptance_discovery_stopped_short`: `incomplete` true, not `disabled`, and `repeats_required` not 0 — a `state.json` saved before the `disabled` record carries `incomplete: true, reason: "repeats_disabled"`, `repeats_required: 0` for repeats of 0, which is read as disabled) under "Held-out discovery that did not finish". It is the only reader of the record; the run outcome does not read it. A held case `seen` in
any run of a file that ends neither failing nor passing cleanly — every
held failure carried a resource signature or no message — makes that
file failing with `intermittent_cases{file: [case ids]}` on the result
(its `failing_cases[file]` the same IDs). The result therefore counts as
a failing measured set everywhere (`_acceptance_any_fails`,
`_acceptance_work_fails`, `_decide_outcome`, `_redrive_failing`).
`_acceptance_residual_of` adds `intermittent: [set indices]` when any
failing result carries `intermittent_cases`. The gate's closing log says
`held-out sets pass on the integrated tree` only when no set is
unmeasured; otherwise `N of M held-out set(s) pass, K unmeasured (no
evidence either way)`. `confirm=False` (the report-base measurement) runs
neither the vote nor discovery.

`fixed_on_head_by_execution`: when the writer's one own-start retry still
leaves every declared defect file passing, `_write_acceptance_set` records
that reason on the (invalid) set — the only writer of the string.
`phase_acceptance_write` returns every invalid set as
`discarded[{index, reason}]` (`reason` the set's own, `"invalid"` when it
has none), persisted with the record; `_settle_pending_no_work` reads it
(DESIGN §8 *No work is declared on executed evidence*).

### The settled bar — `_record_settled_bar`, `_settled_bar_check`

DESIGN §8 *Done is a fixed bar per task, not re-sampled each run*. Every task
with a key; no worker takes part.

**Key.** `_settled_bar_key(task, repo_root) -> str | None` is the first 32 hex
characters of the sha256 of the JSON of `{task: task.strip(), reports: sorted
[path, sha256 of the bytes]}` over `_d1_report_paths(task, repo_root)`, the
references and filter `_d1_report_sources` reads: `_glob_task_references`, a
markdown suffix, not tracked; `reports` is `[]` for a task that points at none,
which is then keyed by its text alone. None, logged, when any report is over
`D1_REPORT_MAX_BYTES` or cannot be read (`_read_beneath`, `READ_LIMIT_TEXT`), and
None for an empty task: no bar applies. `phase_acceptance_write` computes it
once, before the writers run, and keeps it as `acceptance.settled_bar_key`, on
the non-`bug-fixing` path too (beside `skipped`). `_record_settled_bar` reads that, never the file
again, so a report edited during a run is a new bar for the next run. The same-
task lookups (`_prior_delivery_residual`, `_prior_acceptance_dispute_record`)
do not read it.

**Store.** `_settled_bar_dir(leerie_root, key) -> Path` is
`<state-root>/settled-bars/<key>` (`SETTLED_BARS_DIRNAME`).
`_load_settled_bar(leerie_root, key) -> dict` reads `bar.json` (`SETTLED_BAR_FILE`) through `_read_text_beneath`
(`READ_LIMIT_CONFIG`), `{"entries": []}` when absent or unreadable;
`_save_settled_bar` writes it through `_write_beneath`. An entry is `{run, set,
recorded_at, own_start, tree, defect{file: [case ids]}, control[], support[],
modes{}}`, its files under `<run>/set-<k>/` (`_settled_bar_entry_dir`). The bar's
`change` (absent when none) is `{run, own_start, tree, recorded_at, patches[{path,
test, patch}], tests[], run_tests[], known_failing{file: [case ids]},
backfilled}`, its files under `<run>/change/` (`_settled_change_dir(leerie_root,
key, run)`, `SETTLED_CHANGE_DIRNAME`): `patches/<i>.patch`, one per file the diff
touches, and `files/<path>`, each test file (`_is_test_file` with
`resolve_test_file_globs`) the diff added or changed, as the shipped tree has it.
`run_tests` is the subset still run (a dropped file stays placed: it may be a
helper another one imports).

**The change.** `_settled_change_capture(git_dir, own_start, tree, leerie_root,
dest, globs, failing_ids) -> dict | None` writes it from any repository holding
both commits (`git diff --no-renames --binary`, `git cat-file blob`, bytes); None,
writing nothing, when the diff is empty, a git call fails, or one file's patch
or test is over `READ_LIMIT_TEXT`. `known_failing` is the `failing_ids` (a run's
`final_failing_ids`) whose part before ` :: ` is one of its test files' path
(vitest, jest) or dotted module (pytest's report), keyed by that file; the check
compares a failing case's ID against all of them.
`_settled_change_hunks(patch: bytes) -> list[bytes]` splits one file's patch into
its header plus each `@@` hunk (a binary patch, or one with no hunk, is one unit).
`_settled_change_landed(st, leerie_root, key, change, base) -> bool` is True when
every non-test hunk (every hunk, when the change touched only tests) passes
`git apply --cached --check -R` against `base` read into a private index
(`<run-dir>/.settled-change-index`) of the run's own repository; False on any
failure, a missing patch, or no hunk. `_settled_change_backfill(st, key, task,
bar) -> dict | None`, for a bar with no `change`: the newest (`run.json`
`finished_at`) sibling run directory whose `run.json` has `outcome: "done"` and
the same stripped task, limited to the runs of `bar.entries` when it has any;
from its `state.json`, `acceptance.settled_bar_key` equal to `key` when present,
else, for a task with reports, each report's mtime before its `started_at`; its
own start (`repo_state_before_planning.head`, else `base_sha`) and its
`refs/heads/<_compute_run_branch(run)>` in `<run-dir>/repo`. Only that newest run
is tried: logged and None when its repository, own start or branch is gone.
`backfilled: true`.

**Recording.** `_decide_outcome` calls `_record_settled_bar_safely(st)` when the
outcome is `done` (never raising; what was kept goes to
`acceptance.settled_bar_recorded`). `_record_settled_bar(st) -> dict | None`
returns None, changing nothing, with no `acceptance.settled_bar_key`, or when
another run's entries or change exist and this run's
`acceptance.settled_bar.status` is not `unlanded`: the bar is fixed. The change is
`_record_settled_change(st, leerie_root, key)`: `_settled_change_capture` on the
run's own repository from `acceptance.validity_base` (else
`repo_state_before_planning.head`) to its run branch (else
`acceptance.gate.final_sha`), with `final_failing_ids`. Otherwise,
for each set of `acceptance.sets` that is not broken and not itself a bar set
(`settled_bar` key), with a measured `acceptance.gate.final` result, the
counted IDs (`scope.counted_cases` when bounded, else `base_failing_cases`)
minus those still failing (`failing_cases[file]`; a failing file without a
per-case record keeps none), with the set's control files not failing; a set
with no such counted case is not recorded. Files are copied beneath the state
root (`_copy_beneath(..., src_anchor=st.run_dir, limit=READ_LIMIT_TEXT)`). The
new entries and change replace every old one, whose directories are removed;
when there are neither, the old bar stays. The return is `{entries, cases}` plus
`change{files, tests}` when one was recorded.

**At the own start.** `phase_acceptance_write`, after `_acceptance_scope_judge_sets`
and `_record_report_reproduced`, calls `_settled_bar_at_own_start(key, st, caps,
sets, base, written=n)` (fail-open: any exception gives `{status: "error",
error}` and leaves the sets as typed) and returns its record as `settled_bar`
(absent when None: no key, or no bar under it). When the categories
lack `bug-fixing` it makes the same call with no sets if there is an own start
and a scoped test command, returning `{skipped, settled_bar_key, settled_bar}`, or a full record
with `written: 0` when a regression injected sets. `--skip-acceptance-check` and
no scoped test command return as they did, with no check. `_settled_bar_check`
takes the bar's `change`, or `_settled_change_backfill` (saved into `bar.json`),
returns None with neither entries nor change, and when there is a change records
`change{run, landed, backfilled}` from `_settled_change_landed`; a change not
landed with no entries is `unlanded` at once, with entries it is set aside and
the entries decide as before. It then sets up one `_acceptance_tree` at the own start (`acceptance-bar`; `{status:
"unmeasured"}` when it cannot) and runs each entry's defect and control files
with `_run_settled_bar_file` (`_run_acceptance_file(..., validating=True,
place=<the entry's files>)`, so per case, in the held-out sandbox, never on
disk; a failing file runs once more, and a case stays `failed` only when it
failed both times). An entry any of whose paths the tree already has is not run
(`skipped`). A file with no verdict for which `_run_acceptance_file` set
`observed["ran_nothing"]` (a collection error, no test executed, the runner's
no-verdict exit) or `load_failure` is dropped from the entry; any other with no
verdict is listed in `unmeasured` and kept. A defect case the runner's report no
longer names is dropped; any drop rewrites `bar.json` (entries left with no
defect case removed) and is logged. A landed change's `run_tests` then run
(`_settled_change_tests`): every file of `tests` is written onto the
`acceptance-bar` tree (`_write_beneath`, after the entries ran; the shim never
places over a tree path), and each runs unplaced through `_run_settled_bar_file`
(label `settled-bar-<run>-change`), never `skipped` for a path the tree has: each case
reported passed counts as a passing bar case, each failed one not in
`known_failing` as a failure (a file with no per-case record by its verdict; a
failing one in `known_failing` is not one), and a file that ran nothing or did
not load leaves `run_tests` for good, rewriting `bar.json`. The record is
`{status, entries, passed, failed, dropped[], skipped[], unmeasured[],
advisory[], injected[], change, change_failed[]}`, `status`:

- `empty` — no defect case of the bar ran, none unmeasured, and no landed change;
- `unmeasured` — the tree could not be set up, or a file could not be run and no
  regression was seen;
- `unlanded` — the change is not on the own start and no entry ran, or there is
  no landed change and every defect case that ran failed;
- `regressed` — some case failed, and some defect case passed or the change is
  landed. A change failure is not injected: its IDs are `change_failed[]`, which
  `_settled_bar_settles_run` names in `no_work_dispute` and `no_work_acceptance.cases`
  after the injected sets' cases. Entry failures are injected:
  `_inject_settled_bar_sets(st, sets, failures, written)` appends, per entry
  with a failure, a set indexed past `max(written, every set index)`, its
  files copied to `<run_dir>/acceptance/bar-<index>/`, `defect_files` the
  entry files with a failing case, `control_files` the rest that ran,
  `base_failing_cases` / `cases` / `scope.counted_cases` those failing IDs
  (`scope.by = "settled_bar"`), `settled_bar{run, set}`. Such a set is always in
  `_acceptance_shown_indices`, does not count toward its four, and is skipped by
  `_acceptance_audit_and_rewrite`;
- `holds` — every case that ran passed, or none ran and the change is landed:
  `_settled_bar_withdraw(sets) ->
  list[dict]` sets each fresh set's `scope.counted_cases` to `{}` (an unbounded
  set becomes bounded, `by: "settled_bar"`, `unbounded_error`) and returns the
  withdrawn cases as `advisory[{set, file, case}]`, `case` null for a file that
  counted whole with no per-case record.

**Acting on it.** `_run_phases`, right after the `acceptance` checkpoint, calls
`_settled_bar_settles_run(st) -> bool` when `plans_after_plan` is not in state;
it is idempotent, so a resume killed between its first save and `finished_at`
ends the same way. On `holds` it pops `no_work_pending`, sets
`no_work_acceptance = {verdict: "settled_bar_holds", advisory: <count>}`, calls
`_finish_no_work_run` with the key `<settled bar holds>` and returns True. On
`regressed` it pops `no_work_pending`, sets `no_work_acceptance = {verdict:
"settled_bar_regressed", cases}` and `no_work_dispute` naming the injected
counted cases (first 20), so `phase_plan` reads them and
`_settle_pending_no_work` and its dispute bound are not reached, and returns
False. Any other status returns False. `_decide_outcome` adds a reason, so
`unconverged`, when `settled_bar.status` is `regressed` and there are no commits.

**Advisory surfaces.** `_settled_bar_advisory(state) -> list[dict]` reads the
list; `_settled_bar_advisory_lines(state) -> list[str]` renders the statement
(`SETTLED_BAR_ADVISORY_NOTE`) then `  set <k>: <file> :: <name>` per case.
`_finish_no_work_run` logs them after its final line; the `no_work_reasons` value
carries the note and the list; `_decide_outcome` writes `run.json`
`settled_bar_advisory{note, cases[]}`; `_pr_advisory` lists them all, uncapped.
A held bar's run has no gate, so `_prior_delivery_residual` hands nothing on.

**Replay:** not in this repository (lane scratch); DESIGN §8 *What was measured*
carries its numbers.

---

### Operator-accepted held-out cases — `accept-heldout`

DESIGN §8 *An operator accepts a held-out case the task does not require*.

- **`leerie accept-heldout <run-id> <set>[/<case>] ... [--runtime fly|ec2|local]`**
  (launcher arm `accept-heldout`, beside `accept-blocked` and
  `accept-integration`, whose local/Fly/EC2 machinery — runtime
  auto-detection, run-id allowlist, wake-mutate-pause, `ACCEPTED:` /
  `NOOP:` / `ERROR:` sentinels, the best-effort host mirror — it mirrors).
  Each case argument is base64-encoded by the launcher before it reaches the
  mutation program `_ah_mutate` (`python3 -I -c` locally, `python3 -I -`
  over stdin on Fly/EC2), so free text never meets a remote shell; every
  line it prints passes a non-printable character as `?` (a case title is
  worker-written text, DESIGN §6 *No text leerie did not write reaches the
  operator's terminal as a control sequence*). Usage on a missing argument:

  ```
  accept-heldout requires <run-id> and at least one <set> or <set>/<case>
    Usage: leerie accept-heldout <run-id> <set>[/<case>] ... [--runtime fly|ec2|local]
      <set>         every case of that held-out set (its number, as the PR shows it)
      <set>/<case>  one case of it, by the name the PR shows, or <file> :: <title>
  ```
- **The lock.** `_ah_mutate` takes `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB)` on the
  run directory — the lock `State._acquire_lock` holds for an
  orchestrator's life — and refuses with "an orchestrator owns this run"
  when it is held. It writes `state.json` by temp file and `os.replace`,
  keeping the file's mode.
- **Validation, all before any change** (one bad argument changes nothing):
  `<set>` must be digits naming a set in `acceptance.sets`; a set carrying
  `settled_bar` (a regressed bar's) is refused; `<set>/<case>` needs a
  bounded set (`scope.bounded: true`) and a case the run recorded for that
  set — in `scope.counted_cases`, `base_failing_cases`,
  `base_case_status`, a gate result's `failing_cases` (`initial`, `final`,
  `rounds[].results`) or `residual.failing_cases_by_set` — named by its
  whole ID, its ID with an absolute file part made relative, or its title
  (the part after ` :: `, which the PR shows); a name matching cases in two
  files is refused, asking for the whole ID. The error lists up to eight of
  the set's case titles.
- **The change**, per argument: a case is removed from
  `scope.counted_cases[file]` and appended to the set's
  `operator_accepted.cases` (`was_counted` records whether it was counted);
  a whole set records `whole_set: {at}` and empties `counted_cases`,
  bounding a set that was not bounded. `scope_before` keeps the first scope
  seen; `pending: true` is set. `NOOP:` for a set typed `broken`, a case or
  set already accepted.
- **Readers.** Every has-work reader reads `scope.counted_cases`
  (`_acceptance_counted_files`, `_acceptance_file_has_work`,
  `_acceptance_result_has_work`, `_settle_case_names`, the held signals,
  `_collect_unmet_evidence`), so the withdrawal alone takes the case out of
  the no-work settle, the already-fixed check, the satisfied-probe
  protection, the delivery re-drive, `_decide_outcome`, the unmet evidence,
  `_record_settled_bar` and `_acceptance_residual_unbroken`. Read from
  `operator_accepted` itself (`_acceptance_operator_accepted(set_) ->
  (whole, {file: ids})`):
  - `_acceptance_failure_unaccepted(set_, result)` / `_acceptance_repair_fails(results, sets)`:
    the gate's repair starts and each round runs only while a measured
    failure holds a failing file with no per-case record or a failing ID
    outside the accepted ones (a gate whose every failure is accepted logs
    so and repairs nothing); `_acceptance_audit_and_rewrite` leaves such a
    set out of its `todo`.
  - `_acceptance_name_accepted(set_, file | None, name)`: a declared name
    matches an accepted ID whose title is the name or ends with it right
    after a non-identifier character (jest's space, pytest's dot).
    `_format_acceptance_failures_section` skips a result with no unaccepted
    failure and drops accepted names; `_acceptance_residual_unbroken` drops
    them from the `cases` it hands on.
  - `_acceptance_operator_pending(data)`: a set's `operator_accepted.pending`;
    `_decide_outcome` clears every one.
  - `_pr_operator_accepted_lines(state)`: the
    `## Held-out cases accepted by the operator` section
    (`_OPERATOR_ACCEPTED_HEADING`, in `_PR_END_STATE_HEADINGS`, rendered by
    `_format_pr_end_state_section` after `## Still failing when the run
    ended`): a statement that the operator, not leerie, decided, then one
    line per case — set, file, title, time — or per whole set.
- **Resume.** An unfinished run reads all of the above where it resumes. A
  finished one (`_run_has_nothing_left` and not `no_work_required`) with
  `_acceptance_operator_pending` calls `_redecide_after_operator_acceptance(st)`
  before answering "nothing to resume": `_decide_outcome(st,
  any_commits=True)` (which records the settled bar when the outcome is now
  `done`), `_record_unmet_evidence`, `_format_pr_end_state_section` into
  `run.json.pr_end_state` (swapped into `pr_body` when it holds the old
  text) and, when `run.json` has `pushed_at` and `pr_url`, `pr_refresh`
  (above, *Host-side finalize*). No worker is called.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_accept_heldout.py` — the launcher verb on a real
  run directory whose run branch lives in a real run repository, then the
  real `_run_phases` resume: outcome `unconverged` → `done`, the PR section,
  `pr_refresh` holding the old text, no worker; controls (no acceptance, no
  re-decision; a variant accepted alone, still `unconverged`); refusals
  (live run, unknown set or case, malformed argument beside a good one,
  ambiguous name, a case of an unbounded set, a regressed bar), each leaving
  `state.json` byte-identical; the next same-task run's residual; the real
  gate on a real pytest repository repairing nothing when every failure is
  accepted, and naming only the unaccepted sibling when one case is; the
  host refresh. `tests/test_accept_verbs_keep_their_evidence.py` checks
  `_ah_mutate` carries no apostrophe.

## 6½. Per-repo dependency provisioning

Implements DESIGN §6½. The provision phase fires once per run, between
classify and plan; on `resume` it is guarded on the presence of
`st.data["provision"]["recipe"]` (key-presence, not truthiness — an
empty recipe is a valid completed state) so a resume that already
persisted a recipe does not re-fire `mise install` (DESIGN §6
"Resumable planning").

### Worker registration

`WORKER_TYPES` gains `"provision"`. `SCHEMAS["provision"]` is the JSON
schema for the LLM-fallback recipe:

```python
{
    "type": "object",
    "required": ["recipe"],
    "properties": {
        "recipe": {
            "type": "array",
            "items": {
                "type": "object",
                "required": ["kind", "command", "working_dir"],
                "properties": {
                    "kind": {"enum": ["install", "build", "none"]},
                    "command": {
                        "type": "array",
                        "items": {"type": "string"},
                        "minItems": 1,
                    },
                    "working_dir": {"type": "string"},
                    "timeout_s": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1},
                },
            },
        },
        "confidence": {"type": "string"},
        "notes": {"type": "string"},
    },
}
```

`_detect_recipe_from_lockfiles(repo_root) -> list[dict]` is the
deterministic table. It returns a list of `{kind, command, working_dir,
timeout_s}` dicts — possibly empty (table miss → LLM fallback), possibly
multi-entry (polyglot repos like Rails-with-frontend emit *all* matches,
not first-wins).

| Detected file | Emitted command | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `pnpm-lock.yaml` | `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` | takes precedence over yarn.lock and package-lock.json |
| `yarn.lock` (no pnpm-lock.yaml) | `yarn install --frozen-lockfile` | |
| `package-lock.json` (neither above) | `npm ci` | |
| `uv.lock` | `uv sync` | |
| `poetry.lock` | `poetry install` | |
| `Pipfile.lock` | `pipenv install` | |
| `go.mod` + `go.sum` | `go mod download` | |
| `Cargo.lock` | `cargo fetch` | |
| `Gemfile.lock` | `bundle install` | |
| `composer.lock` | `composer install --no-interaction` | |
| `packages.lock.json` | `dotnet restore` | NuGet lockfile |
| anything else | (no entry — caller falls back to LLM worker) | bare `requirements.txt`, bare `pyproject.toml`, Maven (`pom.xml`), Gradle, polyglot Makefile |

The table matches the files above at the repo root. In addition, one Node
entry per **independent package root** below it (DESIGN §6½ *One install
per independent package root*), after the root Node entry:
`_nested_node_roots(repo_root)` returns `(dir, lockfile)` for each
directory holding a `pnpm-lock.yaml` / `yarn.lock` / `package-lock.json`
(`_node_lockfile_paths`: `git ls-files` with `:(glob)**/<lockfile>`
pathspecs when the root is a work tree, else a walk skipping
`node_modules` and dot-directories), excluding any path with a
`node_modules` segment and any directory matched by the root's workspace
globs (`_workspace_globs`: `pnpm-workspace.yaml` `packages:` items and
`package.json` `workspaces`, list or `{packages}`; `!glob` excludes;
`_workspace_glob_matches`: `*` within a segment, `**` across segments).
pnpm > yarn > npm within a directory; sorted; at most
`_NESTED_NODE_ROOTS_MAX` (16). Each entry is the root's command
(`_NODE_LOCKFILE_INSTALL`) with `working_dir` = that directory.

`_validate_provision_recipe(recipe) -> None` enforces (raises `ValueError`
on violation):
- `command[0]` is a program's bare name (`_PROVISION_PROGRAM_RE`,
  `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._+-]*$`) or a relative path
  (`_PROVISION_PROGRAM_PATH_RE`, no leading `/`, no `..` segment). There
  is no list of programs (DESIGN §6½ *The §12 carve-out*).
- No `sudo` anywhere in the argv.
- No shell metacharacters (`|`, `&`, `;`, `$`, backticks, `>`, `<`, `\n`)
  in any argv element.
- `working_dir` is either `"."` or a relative path with no `..` segments
  and no leading `/`.

`_recipe_program_issues(recipe, repo_root, bin_paths, path) -> list[str]`
is the provision worker's check, run with `check_provision_output` in its
`_run_checked_loop` (the table's recipe is code's and is not checked): one
`UNKNOWN_PROGRAM` issue per non-`none` entry whose bare program has no
executable regular file of that name in `bin_paths`
(`st.data["provision"]["bin_paths"]`) or on `path` (the orchestrator's
`PATH`), `<MISE_DATA_DIR>/shims` left out — a shim exists for every tool
any run installed, active here or not; or whose path program is not a
regular file beneath `repo_root/<working_dir>` (`_regular_file_beneath`).
`bin_paths` is captured by `_run_mise_install` after the version capture:
`mise bin-paths` confined under the same toolchain grant in the
provisioning checkout, bounded by `MISE_LS_TIMEOUT`, one directory per
line; a timeout or nonzero exit is logged and leaves it unrecorded, so a
bare program then resolves on `PATH` alone. Pinned by
`tests/test_provision_recipe_validation.py`.

### Phase implementation (`phase_provision`)

Insertion point in `_orchestrate()`: inside the `else:` (fresh-run)
branch, after the `_write_run_json(...)` block and before
`gather_answers(st, supplied)`. Step order:

1. **The provisioning checkout.** Every task is provisioned, whatever
   its categories: no category skips the phase (DESIGN §6½ — every
   measurement installs from the recipe, a docs-only task's included).
   Steps 2–4 run in `_provision_hook_and_toolchain(tree, log_dir, st)`,
   inside `_judge_checkout(st, <planning worktree>, "provision")`: `tree`
   is a throwaway checkout of the planning tree's commit, removed
   afterwards, and is the `repo_root` steps 2–4 see. Never the user's
   checkout, which is read-only in the container (DESIGN §6 *The explicit
   channel*). A missing planning worktree or a checkout that cannot be
   made `die()`s.
1½. **Tool discovery.** `_discover_tools(st, caps, models, efforts)`,
   called by `phase_provision` before the provisioning checkout (DESIGN
   §6½ *The tools a repository needs are read from it*). Spawns the
   `tool_discovery` worker (`prompts/tool_discovery.md`,
   `SCHEMAS["tool_discovery"]`: `tools[]` of `{tool, version, evidence}`,
   `tool` matching `TOOL_NAME_PATTERN` and `version`
   `TOOL_VERSION_PATTERN` — an exact version, a prefix, `latest` or
   `lts`; optional `confidence` on `tool_completeness`) with
   `TOOL_DISCOVERY_USER_PROMPT`, `cwd=_judgment_cwd(st)`, `INSPECT_TOOLS`,
   `max_turns=30`, `autonomous=False`, through `_run_checked_loop` with
   `check=_check_tool_discovery_output(result, registry)` (one
   `UNKNOWN_TOOL` issue per `tool` absent from `_mise_registry_names()`,
   naming registry names that contain it or that it contains) and
   feedback rounds bounded by `judgment_check_rounds`.
   `await _mise_registry_names(st)` is the first column of `mise
   registry`, read once per process (30 s), confined like every `mise`
   leerie runs: `_run_proc(_confined_argv(_measurement_grants(st, tree),
   …))` in the planning tree (`_judgment_cwd(st)`), under the execution
   lock shared; empty when mise cannot run, and then discovery is skipped
   with a log line. `_mise_tools_toml(tools,
   registry)` writes one `"<tool>" = "<version>"` line under `[tools]` per
   registry name, first occurrence wins, to `<run_dir>/mise-tools.toml`
   (`MISE_TOOLS_NAME`, via `_write_beneath`); `_use_run_tools_file(env,
   path)` sets `MISE_GLOBAL_CONFIG_FILE` on `os.environ`, so `mise install`
   (step 4), every confined command and every worker read it beneath the
   repository's own pins. Recorded at `st.data["provision"]["tools"]` (the
   worker's list) and `["tools_file"]`; on `resume`, `_resume_provision_env(st, env)` re-applies `tools_file`
   A worker that returns no
   answer (`_run_checked_loop` gives `None`, or a `WorkerError`) logs and
   leaves the run on the repository's own pins (`tools: []`, no file). Pinned by
   `tests/test_tool_discovery.py`.
2. **Setup hook.** `_run_setup_hook(repo_root, log_dir, st)` execs
   `<repo>/.leerie-setup.sh` if present (10-min timeout, streams to
   `<state-root>/runs/<id>/logs/setup-hook.log`). Idempotent via
   `st.data["provision"]["sh_hook_ran"]`. Nonzero exit → `die()`.
   **Runs as the non-root `leerie` container user; no sudo.** The hook
   can install user-space tooling (`mise install <lang>@<version>`,
   anything writing to `~/.local/bin`) and pre-populate fixtures, but
   cannot `apt-get install` or write to system directories. Repos
   that need root-level system packages maintain a fork of the leerie
   Dockerfile and override `IMAGE_TAG`; out of scope for the hook.
   Its pip user base is its own home's (DESIGN §6 *Every confined process
   has its own home*), and `_measurement_grants` sets its `XDG_CACHE_HOME`
   to the checkout's own, and no worker reads either, so a
   tool for the workers goes beneath `~/.local/bin` (`pip install --target`
   and a launcher script, DESIGN §6½ step 1). It installs no git hooks.
4. **Mise install.** `_run_mise_install(repo_root, log_dir, st)`:
   runs `mise install` in that checkout. (The go override that step 3
   once synthesized from `go.mod` — `_synth_mise_go_override`, its
   `MISE_OVERRIDE_CONFIG_FILENAMES` export and its parsers of idiomatic
   files — is deleted: Go's version comes from step 1½ like every other
   tool's.) mise
   reads `.tool-versions` natively, and reads `.nvmrc` /
   `.python-version` / `.ruby-version` / `rust-toolchain.toml` /
   `.go-version` / `.java-version` / `global.json` / … because the image's
   `/etc/mise/config.toml` enables the idiomatic files of every tool mise
   ships. It runs whatever the tree holds — there is no file-presence
   gate (`_MISE_SIGNAL_FILES` and `_repo_has_version_signal` are gone).
   `_trust_run_mise_configs(env, run_dir) -> None` sets
   `env["MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS"] = str(run_dir)` (replacing any value);
   `main()` applies it to `os.environ` right after `_leerie_stores`, so
   every confined command and worker trusts the configuration files beneath
   the run directory — the trees' `mise.toml` and the run's tools file —
   and nothing else.
   Ruby uses precompiled binaries (`MISE_RUBY_COMPILE=false` in the
   image) to avoid requiring the full ruby-build toolchain.
   Streams to `<state-root>/runs/<id>/logs/provision.log`. Nonzero exit
   surfaces the failing tool+version to `die()`. The install's env sets
   `MISE_NODE_COREPACK=false` whatever the image says; after a zero exit
   `_enable_corepack_shims(grants, env, cwd, log_path, verbosity)` runs,
   for each real directory `v` (not a symlink alias) under
   `$MISE_DATA_DIR/installs/node/` holding `bin/corepack` but no
   `bin/pnpm`, `[v/bin/corepack, "enable", "--install-directory",
   v/bin]` through `_run_streaming` under the same toolchain grant
   (label `corepack enable <version>`); a nonzero exit `die()`s, as mise's
   own failed enable failed the install. Never a directory under
   `MISE_SYSTEM_DATA_DIR` (DESIGN §6 *Each Node version's corepack shims
   go in its own `bin`*). Pinned by `tests/test_corepack_shim_dir.py`.
   The install and the enables run inside `_mise_install_lock(st)` (an
   async context manager): an exclusive `flock` on
   `_host_shared_dir(st) / MISE_INSTALL_LOCK_NAME` (`"mise-install.lock"`,
   opened `O_RDONLY | O_CREAT`), tried `LOCK_NB` every
   `MISE_INSTALL_LOCK_POLL_SEC` (1 s) and logged once while it waits;
   released (the descriptor closed) on exit, `die()` included; the version
   capture below runs after it. The toolchain grant's env names
   `MISE_CACHE_DIR` beneath `MISE_DATA_DIR`, so mise's own install lock and
   `incomplete` markers are shared with the data (DESIGN §6 *One toolchain
   install at a time on a host, against mise's own completeness record*).
   Pinned by `tests/test_mise_install_lock.py`, whose real-container test
   (opt-in, `LEERIE_TEST_CONTAINER_IMAGE`) runs two runs' installs of one
   version with the first frozen mid-extract and then killed.
5. **Version capture.** Runs `mise ls --current --json` (the
   subcommand `mise current --json` does not exist; verified
   against mise.usage.kdl) via `_run_proc` bounded by
   `MISE_LS_TIMEOUT` (30s) — a timeout or non-zero exit is logged and
   skipped, the same fail-open disposition as any other capture
   failure, since workers install their own tools via prompt
   injection regardless. Output is object-keyed-by-tool, each
   value an array of `{version, install_path, source}` objects.
   Raw blob stored at `st.data["provision"]["mise_versions"]`;
   `tools[name][0].version` is the value rendered in `leerie list`
   and one-line log summaries.
6. **Table-first detection.** `_detect_recipe_from_lockfiles(
   repo_root)`. Non-empty result is the recipe (marked
   `source: "table"` in state).
7. **LLM fallback.** Empty table result → `_gather_provision_fixtures(
   repo_root)` assembles inputs (see below), `claude_p("provision",
   prompt, fixtures, SCHEMAS["provision"], model)` returns a
   recipe (marked `source: "llm"` in state).
8. **Validate.** `_validate_provision_recipe(recipe)`. Reject →
   `die()`.
8½. **Normalize pip installs.** `_normalize_pip_installs(recipe)` adds
   `--break-system-packages` to every `pip`/`pip3`/`python -m pip`
   *install* entry that lacks it (`_is_pip_install` finds the `install`
   subcommand as the first non-option token after the pip prefix, so a
   leading global flag like `pip -v install` still matches; `uv pip
   install` and `pipx install` are exempt — they manage their own
   environments). The container's system Python is Debian-13
   externally-managed (PEP 668) — a bare `pip install` exits non-zero,
   silently breaking every recipe consumer (most visibly
   `_capture_conformance_baseline`, whose failed `pip install` leaves
   the base test axis recording `command not found`). Normalizing at
   this one chokepoint fixes the baseline installer *and* the
   `PROVISION_RECIPE:` prompt block at once. The flag is a no-op on a
   non-externally-managed interpreter, so it is applied unconditionally.
9. **Persist (do not execute).** Full recipe + `source` + resolved
    versions saved to `st.data["provision"]`. The recipe is not
    executed by `phase_provision` — the implementer and conformer
    workers run install commands from their own worktrees, given the
    recipe via prompt injection
    (`_format_provision_recipe_section()`), and every tree leerie
    measures installs from it (`_ensure_worktree_deps`). See
    "Worker-driven install" below.

### Helper functions

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `_gather_provision_fixtures(repo_root) -> dict` | Assembles the LLM-worker input set under a 24KB total ceiling. README extracted by `_extract_readme_sections()`; root manifests (`package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `go.mod`, `Cargo.toml`, `Gemfile`, `Makefile`, `pom.xml`, `build.gradle*`) included if present; workspace child manifests capped at 3 (1KB each) for monorepos; up to 2 `.github/workflows/*.yml` files matching `(?i)ci\|test\|build\|release` (skip `codeql\|stale\|dependabot`); optional `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` capped at 4KB. |
| `_extract_readme_sections(text) -> str` | **Size-bounding only** — returns the leading slice of the README, ≤ `_README_EXTRACT_BUDGET` (12KB), cut back to the last section boundary so the worker never receives a header with its body sheared off (never discarding more than 25% of the budget chasing one; a headerless document still gets its first three-quarters of the budget, i.e. ~9KB at the current 12KB setting). Under budget the README is returned verbatim. **It does not decide which sections are install-relevant** — that is a judgment about prose and belongs to the `provision` worker, which is told so in `prompts/provision.md`; no keyword filter is applied. `_gather_provision_fixtures` additionally reports `readme_bytes_unseen` / `readme_sections_unseen`, and `_format_provision_user_prompt` renders them as an explicit `[TRUNCATED: …]` note under an `UNFILTERED` header — a slice the worker cannot tell is a slice reads as the whole README. Reporting the size of the gap is mechanical; guessing at its contents would be back to classifying prose. |
| `_run_setup_hook(repo_root, log_dir, st)` | Execs `<repo>/.leerie-setup.sh` if present with a 10-min timeout via `_run_streaming` (live output to terminal + persistent log at `<log_dir>/setup-hook.log`); sets `st.data["provision"]["sh_hook_ran"] = True` on success. |
| `_run_mise_install(repo_root, log_dir, st)` | Runs `mise install` + `mise ls --current --json` at `repo_root`. The install streams via `_run_streaming` so the user sees per-tool progress on a first-run Python/Ruby/Rust install. |
| `_format_provision_recipe_section(recipe, *, audience) -> str \| None` | Renders the persisted recipe as a `PROVISION_RECIPE:` block for injection into implementer or conformer prompts. Audience-specific framing ("decide whether your subtask needs them" vs "ensure deps before BUILD/LINT/TEST"). Returns None when the recipe is empty or all-`none`. |
| `phase_provision(repo_root, st, models)` | Orchestrates all of the above. Detects + persists the recipe; does NOT execute it (workers run installs in their worktrees per DESIGN §6½). |
| `_run_streaming(cmd, ..., log_path, verbosity, ...)` | Async subprocess helper with live-streamed stdout+stderr, persistent log file, bounded tail deque, and `TimeoutExpired` carrying the tail in `.output`. Used by `_run_mise_install` and `_run_setup_hook`; replaces the previous `_run_proc` calls that buffered output for the entire run duration. |

### Caches

One host cache is mounted into the container, `rw`: `~/.cache/leerie/toolchains`
at `/leerie-toolchains`, the host's toolchains and the toolchain home layer
(§0.5 "Bind-mount table"). Package stores and caches (pnpm, pip,
Go, Cargo, Bundler, corepack) are not mounted from the host: they live in the state
mount, each run's own at `<run-dir>/worktrees/.stores/stores/` and its workers'
at `<run-dir>/worktrees/.stores/cache/` (the held-out side's at
`<run-dir>/worktrees/.stores/cache-held-out/`; DESIGN §6 *The pnpm store shares the
worktrees' mount*). Concurrency-safety verdicts, for whichever directory
each tool writes:

- **mise installs** — Safe. Version dirs are immutable once installed;
  mise renames atomically on install.
- **pnpm store** — Safe (CAS, atomic ops; pnpm/discussions#10702).
- **Go modules** — Safe (`flock` per module-version in
  `cmd/go/internal/modfetch`).
- **Cargo** — Safe (flock on index + per-crate locks). No `CARGO_HOME`
  is set: cargo's home is `~/.cargo`, whose `bin` is the toolchain home
  layer's and whose registry a tree's install keeps in that tree's home
  layer (DESIGN §6 *Every confined process has its own home*, 4).
- **pip** — Mixed. Most races fixed (pypa/pip#9470, #12361, #13540
  closed). The wheel-build race #9034 (concurrent `pip install` of
  the same sdist into the same wheel-cache slot) is still open; in
  practice leerie runs a small number of concurrent workers and the
  collision window is narrow. A worker that does hit the race retries
  once via pip's own retry, and a persistent failure surfaces as a
  conformer warning (DESIGN §9), not a silent corruption.
- **Bundler** — Per tree (`BUNDLE_PATH`, `_TREE_STORE_VARS`), so no two
  trees share an installed bundle.

### Worker-driven install

`scripts/new-worktree.sh` does just the `git worktree add` and prints
the worktree path. The image holds no dependency (DESIGN §6½ *The
repository image holds no dependency*), so a worktree starts with none.
There is **no orchestrator-driven install** in a worker's tree after it
is created; the orchestrator installs in the trees it measures
(`_ensure_worktree_deps`).

How dependencies reach the worker:

1. `git worktree add` checks out the worktree (tracked files only).
   It starts with no `node_modules/` / `.venv/` / `target/` by
   design.
2. The orchestrator parses the worktree path from the script's stdout.
3. `_run_implementer` (and later `_run_conformer`) read
   `st.data["provision"]["recipe"]` and inject it as a
   `PROVISION_RECIPE:` block in the worker's user prompt via
   `_format_provision_recipe_section(...)`.
4. The worker's prompt (see `prompts/implementer.md` §2 and
   `prompts/conformer.md` §Input) instructs it to decide whether the
   subtask needs the install and to run the commands from its worktree
   if so. The block carries every `install` and `build` entry, for
   every ecosystem.
5. If the recipe is missing or empty, no `PROVISION_RECIPE:` block is
   injected and the worker proceeds without one.
6. Install failures inside a worker surface through the worker's
   normal exit machinery — a hard-failing build/test in the
   implementer becomes a `failed` or `blocked` status; in the
   conformer it surfaces as a `tests-failed: …` advisory warning
   (DESIGN §9). `_summarize_residuals` writes a failing axis as
   `<axis>-failed: <summary> — '<command>'`, the command cut to
   `_RESIDUAL_COMMAND_CHARS` (160) characters with its full length named,
   and, for tests, `; failing: <files>` from the axis's own report
   (`failing_id_files`, else the `failing_ids`), at most
   `_RESIDUAL_FAILING_FILES` (10) and `(+N more)`. A cleanup failure is
   logged through `_exc_text` (message, or the exception type when the
   message is empty).

Why this shape (worker-driven install):

- The host's repo is bind-mounted at `repo_root`, so an
  orchestrator-driven install there would write linux-arm64 native
  binaries into the host's darwin `node_modules`, corrupting the
  host's checkout.
- Per-worktree pre-install wastes work for subtasks that don't need
  built deps (config-only, doc-only, non-test refactors).
- `claude -p`'s built-in stream-event plumbing surfaces Bash tool I/O
  to the orchestrator log live, so an install inside a worker is
  visible without any special streaming code.

The `MISE_GLOBAL_CONFIG_FILE` env var naming the run's tools file
(`_discover_tools`) is exported to `os.environ` once in `phase_provision`
(and re-exported from persisted state on `resume`); worker subprocesses
inherit it without any per-worker plumbing because `_invoke` does
not pass an explicit `env=` to `create_subprocess_exec`.

**Convention-doc injection (`CONVENTION_DOCS:` block).** Alongside the
recipe, `_run_implementer` injects the repo's authoritative convention docs
so the implementer writes to the repo's design conventions on the first try
rather than drifting and relying on a post-hoc conformer catch (DESIGN §9).
It calls `_discover_rules_files(st.repo_root)` — the same discovery the
conformer uses — and renders the surviving paths (relative to `repo_root`)
as a `CONVENTION_DOCS:` line, matching `_run_conformer`'s `RULES_FILES:`
formatting. Paths only, not contents: the implementer opens the docs
relevant to its subtask itself, avoiding inlining a large design-system
doc into every prompt. When discovery returns nothing, no block is
injected. The `prompts/implementer.md` §3 evidence gate and §4 Implement
step name this block so the worker reconciles the pattern it followed
against the discovered conventions.

### Auto-capture of repo dependencies

Implements DESIGN §6½ *Auto-capture of repo dependencies*. All Python
surface lives in `orchestrator/leerie.py`.

#### Capture functions

| Function / Constant | Signature / Value | Role |
|---------------------|-------------------|------|
| `_DEPCAP_TOTAL_BUDGET` | `307200` (bytes) | Byte ceiling for the install-command hint fed to the dep_capture worker (~300 KB ≈ 75k tokens). Mirrors the `_gather_provision_fixtures` add_bytes/hit_ceiling idiom. |
| `_DEP_MANIFEST_NAMES` | tuple | Fixed tuple of dependency-manifest filenames gathered as the PRIMARY corpus — matched by exact name, **not** a glob (`requirements.txt`, `requirements-dev.txt`, `requirements-test.txt`, `pyproject.toml`, `Pipfile`(`.lock`), `setup.py`/`setup.cfg`, `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `package-lock.json`, `yarn.lock`, `go.mod`, `Cargo.toml`(`.lock`), `Gemfile`(`.lock`), `composer.json`(`.lock`)). |
| `_DEPCAP_MANIFEST_FILE_BUDGET` / `_DEPCAP_MANIFEST_TOTAL_BUDGET` | `16384` / `131072` (bytes) | Per-file and total byte caps for the gathered manifest corpus. |
| `_DEPCAP_INSTALL_RE` / `_DEPCAP_TEXT_TOOLS` / `_DEPCAP_SEGMENT_RE` | regex / frozenset / regex | Install-verb matcher (verb at a command boundary), the set of text-scanning command words (`grep`/`git`/`sed`/…) excluded from the command hint, and the shell-separator splitter (`\n ; && \|\| \| &`) used to evaluate a chained command per-segment. |
| `_is_install_command` | `(cmd: str) -> bool` | True iff **some shell segment** of `cmd` (split on `_DEPCAP_SEGMENT_RE`) invokes a package-manager install verb (`_DEPCAP_INSTALL_RE`) while that segment's leading word (after an optional `sudo`) is not a text tool. Per-segment evaluation keeps a genuine install chained after a text tool (`echo hi\npip install x`, `git log && pip install x`) while still dropping the leak where the verb is inside the text tool's own arg (`grep "apt-get install intents"`). |
| `_gather_dep_manifests` | `(repo_root: Path) -> str` | Reads the repo's dependency-manifest files (`_DEP_MANIFEST_NAMES`) present in `repo_root`, bounded per file and in total; returns a labeled `### <filename>` block per manifest. The PRIMARY dep_capture corpus (DESIGN §6½). |
| `_extract_depcap_commands` | `(log_dir: Path) -> tuple[str, bool]` | Iterates `_worker_transcripts(log_dir)` (the registered transcripts only, newest mtime first — never another `*.log` there, which may be a command's output; DESIGN §8 *What a worker ran is read from its own transcript*); calls `_iter_log_tool_use` on each; collects distinct `command` values from `kind == "Bash"` tool-use blocks **that pass `_is_install_command`** into an insertion-order dict. Admits commands under `_DEPCAP_TOTAL_BUDGET` bytes (separator `\n---\n`). The SECONDARY hint (system/native deps) — manifests are primary. Returns `(commands_text, hit_ceiling)`. |
| `_normalize_setup_packages` | `(pkgs: list[str]) -> str` | Renders a package list in the canonical persisted form: order-preserving dedup, space-joined. Shared by `_merge_setup_packages` (union) and the `replace` path so both emit byte-identical TOML values. |
| `_merge_setup_packages` | `(existing: str, captured: list[str]) -> str \| None` | Parses `existing` (space- or comma-separated, per DESIGN §6½); takes the union with `captured`; returns the merged string (via `_normalize_setup_packages`) only if it grew (else `None` → no write). Preserves user-narrowed lists: only genuinely-new packages are appended; nothing is removed. |
| `_toml_value` | `(val: str) -> str` | Renders `val` as a TOML string for `_write_config_toml_keys`. A value containing `"` and no `'` is wrapped in a TOML *literal* (single-quoted) string. Both readers already `.strip("'")`, so it round-trips with no unescaping; plain values keep the `"..."` basic-string form. Prevents invalid TOML from inner quotes. |
| `_write_config_toml_keys` | `(cfg_path: Path, updates: dict[str, str]) -> None` | Minimal deterministic TOML upsert. Creates the file with a leerie header (matching the launcher's `config --init` heredoc tone) if absent; otherwise replaces the first *uncommented* `key =` line for each key, or appends if absent. Values rendered via `_toml_value`. Never touches commented lines. Writes via temp-file + `os.replace()` (State.save atomicity discipline). |
| `capture_repo_deps` | `async (repo_root: Path, st: State, caps: dict \| None, models: dict[str, str] \| None, efforts: dict[str, str \| None] \| None, replace: bool = False, record_in: Path \| None = None) -> None` | Main entry point. Guards: `resolve_capture_deps`, caps/models/efforts availability, `log_dir` existence, committed `.leerie/Dockerfile` skip. Builds a **manifests-first** corpus: `_gather_dep_manifests` (primary) + `_extract_depcap_commands` (secondary install-command hint); if BOTH are empty, returns. Checks worker budget; invokes `claude_p(schema_key='dep_capture', cwd=_payload_only_cwd(st), allowed_tools=PAYLOAD_ONLY_TOOLS, ...)` (never `repo_root`, the user's checkout; DESIGN §8 *A worker that does not commit never runs in a tree leerie measures*) with `_load_prompt("dep_capture")`, composing a two-section user prompt (manifests, then install-command hint). Takes `setup_packages` from the result. **`record_in`** (every in-container seam: `phase_finalize`, `_best_effort_capture_deps`, `_backstop_capture_prior_runs`, each with the current run's directory; the host's `run_recapture_deps`, with the target run's): appends the capture to `<record_in>/captured-deps.json` (`_record_capture`) and writes nothing in `repo_root` (DESIGN §6 *The explicit channel*, §6½ *The operator applies a capture*). **None:** records nothing (logged). Then the `dep_capture.done` sentinel and `dep_capture_done`. Non-fatality is enforced at each call site's `try/except`, not inside the function. |
| `DEBIAN_PACKAGE_PATTERN` | `str` | `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9+.-]+$`. The `dep_capture` schema's `setup_packages` item `pattern` and `_capture_problems`' rule (DESIGN §6½ *A capture names packages, never commands*). |
| `_capture_problems` | `(setup_packages: object) -> list[str]` | Each reason a capture cannot be recorded or applied: `setup_packages` not a list, or an item not matching `DEBIAN_PACKAGE_PATTERN`. `[]` when it can. |
| `_merge_capture_into_config` | `(cfg_path: Path, setup_packages: list[str], replace: bool) -> dict[str, str]` | Refuses (logs, writes nothing, returns `{}`) a capture `_capture_problems` rejects. The merge, against `cfg_path` as it is now. **`replace=False`:** `setup_packages` via `_merge_setup_packages` (never-clobber). **`replace=True` (only `--recapture --force`):** wholesale-replaces `setup_packages` from the capture; an empty capture leaves the config untouched. Writes via `_write_config_toml_keys` when there is an update; returns the updates. |
| `_record_capture` | `(record_in: Path, from_run: str, setup_packages: list[str], replace: bool) -> None` | Appends `{from_run, setup_packages, replace}` to the JSON list in `<record_in>/captured-deps.json` (`CAPTURED_DEPS_FILE`), temp file + `os.replace`, and logs `leerie config --apply-capture <record_in name>`. Nothing is recorded for an empty capture, nor for one `_capture_problems` refuses (logged). |
| `_config_capture_problems` | `(cfg: Path) -> list[str]` | `_capture_problems` of the `setup_packages` items `cfg` holds now (`_split_setup_packages`). |
| `apply_captured_deps` | `(run_dir: Path, repo_root: Path) -> int` | The operator's `config --apply-capture` (via `host_apply_captured_deps`, scripts/host-finalize.sh), its only caller. `die()`s, applying nothing and keeping the file, when any entry fails `_capture_problems`; an entry's `language_installs` (recorded by an earlier leerie) is not read. Otherwise applies every entry of `<run_dir>/captured-deps.json`, in order, with `_merge_capture_into_config(repo_root/.leerie/config.toml, ...)`, logs the change as a unified diff (`difflib`, reading the file beneath the checkout before and after), then appends them to `captured-deps.applied.json` (`CAPTURED_DEPS_APPLIED_FILE`) and removes the pending file, so a second call is a no-op. Returns the number applied. An absent, unreadable or malformed file is logged and kept; returns 0. |
| `resolve_capture_deps` | `(repo_root: Path) -> bool` | env `LEERIE_CAPTURE_DEPS` > `.leerie/config.toml` `capture_deps` key; default `True`. No CLI flag and no `leerie.toml` tier (env → config → default only). |

#### dep_capture worker

`dep_capture` is a non-WORKER_TYPES worker (like `pr_writer`) registered in
`SCHEMAS`, `_allowed_schema_keys`, `EFFORT_DEFAULT_PER_WORKER` (medium), and
`resolve_models`/`resolve_efforts`. It is **absent** from
`MODEL_DEFAULT_PER_WORKER`; its `sonnet` default comes from the global
`MODEL_DEFAULT` fallback. Its model override is env-var-only (no CLI flag, no
`leerie.toml` key): `MODEL_DEP_CAPTURE_ENV = "LEERIE_MODEL_DEP_CAPTURE"`.
System prompt is `prompts/dep_capture.md`. Output schema:

```json
{
  "setup_packages": ["string"],
  "dockerfile_notes": "string | null"
}
```

`setup_packages` is required, and its items carry `pattern:
DEBIAN_PACKAGE_PATTERN`. The worker names no language install: the image
holds no dependency (DESIGN §6½ *The repository image holds no
dependency*). A pattern also rules out the empty item, which would render to `""` and, under
`--recapture --force` (replace path), blank the persisted config. The schema is the enforcement layer (DESIGN §12); the replace
path additionally gates the write on the rendered value being non-empty.

#### Capture trigger seams

`capture_repo_deps` is called from three seams; all are non-fatal (wrapped in
`try/except`):

1. **Finalize (clean finish).** Called with `await` from `phase_finalize`,
   after `finished_at` is written and run-branch verification completes.
   `caps`, `models`, and `efforts` are forwarded from `phase_finalize`'s
   parameters. The resume-of-finished guard in `_run_phases` returns before
   `phase_finalize` is reached, so capture never re-fires on a completed
   resume; a partial resume that reaches finalize re-runs capture, and the
   union merge makes this a no-op when nothing new was found.

2. **Cancel / SIGTERM arm (catchable signals).** In `main()`'s
   `KeyboardInterrupt` and `InterruptedBySignal` exception handlers, after
   `st.save()`, a best-effort `asyncio.run(capture_repo_deps(...))` runs in
   its own event loop — the same post-loop pattern as the `RateLimitedExit`
   arm. Non-fatal: any exception is logged and suppressed. Covers Ctrl-C and
   `nerdctl stop`, where the orchestrator gets a real Python window before
   the `finally` cleanup block.

3. **Host-side (`run_recapture_deps` / run-start backstop).** Two host-side
   seams funnel to the same worker:
   - **`run_recapture_deps(leerie_root, repo_root, force, run_id)`**: the
     on-demand recapture entrypoint invoked by `leerie config --recapture`.
     When `run_id` is given, targets that run only; otherwise consolidates
     across **all** finished runs with `logs/` (newest-first). Each target
     run's `State` is flocked (skipped on `StateLockedError`); with
     `force=True` the sentinel is dropped before capture **and**
     `capture_repo_deps(replace=True)` wholesale-replaces the persisted deps
     (vs. the default never-clobber union). Exits 1 if no runs directory or no
     finished run found; per-run errors are logged and skipped (non-fatal for
     multi-run consolidation).
   - **`_backstop_capture_prior_runs(leerie_root, repo_root, caps, models,
     efforts)`**: called at run-start (in `_run_phases`, before
     `phase_classify`) to cover SIGKILL / crash cases where the cancel arm
     could not fire. Scans `leerie_root/runs/` for run dirs that have `logs/`
     but no `dep_capture.done` sentinel and calls `capture_repo_deps` over
     each via a lightweight ad-hoc state object.

**Idempotency sentinel.** `capture_repo_deps` writes `<run_dir>/dep_capture.done`
(a one-line file) and sets `st.data["dep_capture_done"] = True` after a
successful write. The run-start backstop skips runs whose sentinel file is
present. The `dep_capture_done` state field is defined in `STATE_FIELDS` and
documented in the state-schema table above.

#### Generated Dockerfile (launcher)

When the launcher generates the repository image's Dockerfile from `setup_packages`
(see *Per-repo derived image* above), the file is the apt layer
(`USER root; apt-get install ...`) and nothing else, and ends with the
image still at `USER root` — it does **not** append a trailing `USER
leerie`. The base image's ENTRYPOINT (`scripts/container-entry.sh`) is
inherited by the derived image and **must** run as PID-1 root to set up
cgroup containment and launch the cgroup broker before dropping to leerie
via `runuser` (DESIGN §6 *Memory containment*; the base Dockerfile omits
`USER leerie` for the same reason). A trailing `USER leerie` here would
override that — cgroup writes, the broker's cgroup setup, and `runuser`
would then all fail EACCES and the container would exit 1. The Fly path
builds the same generated bytes (`$_REPO_DF_GEN`, `_set_fly_per_repo_image`),
so there is no second hash site.

#### Config knobs

One config key, with no CLI flag:
- `capture_deps` (orchestrator, `resolve_capture_deps`): env
  `LEERIE_CAPTURE_DEPS` > `.leerie/config.toml` > default. Does **not**
  consult `leerie.toml`.

| Key | Env override | Default | Meaning |
|-----|-------------|---------|---------|
| `capture_deps` | `LEERIE_CAPTURE_DEPS` | `true` | Enable finalize-time dependency capture. Set to `false` to disable entirely. |

`bake_language_deps` / `LEERIE_BAKE_LANGUAGE_DEPS` are no longer read
(DESIGN §6½ *The repository image holds no dependency*). The key is
resolved by `resolve_capture_deps` before the finalize hook fires. It is
not emitted into `leerie config --init` output — that heredoc
documents only `build`/`lint`/`test`/`setup_packages` — but they are
documented in the `CLAUDE.md` quick-start and here.

Conforms to DESIGN §6½ *Auto-capture of repo dependencies*.

---

## 7. Git worktree mechanics (`scripts/*.sh`)

Every script takes a `RUN_ID` as its first positional argument (after any flags) so the per-run namespacing is explicit at the shell boundary, not implicit through `cwd`. Every script names the run's own repository, `<run-dir>/repo`, through `LEERIE_GIT_DIR` (`leerie_repo_git`; it is never discovered from the working directory, DESIGN §6 *Named, never discovered*); `_run_script` sets it and `LEERIE_STATE_DIR` absolute (see *The run's own repository* below). Staging and each subtask tree are worktrees of their own tree repositories (`leerie_tree`, DESIGN §6 *A repository per committing tree (I6)*).

| Script | Behavior |
|--------|----------|
| `setup-run.sh <run-id> [<working-branch>]` | Creates `leerie/runs/<run-id>` **only if absent** — never force-resets it (an existing branch carries completed waves; resetting it would destroy resume state). When `<working-branch>` is given (by `phase_execute`, via `_working_branch_arg(st)` — `st.data["working_branch"]` unless empty or `HEAD`), it is recorded verbatim (so the file agrees with the orchestrator's `working_branch`, the diff and PR base) and, when it names a local branch — tried as given, then without a leading `heads/` (the form `--abbrev-ref` prints when a tag shares the name), then as an already-full `refs/heads/<name>` — the run branch is cut from it, so an operator's mid-run branch switch cannot re-base the run (DESIGN §12 L4); a branch that no longer exists warns on stderr and falls back to `HEAD`. With no argument (`collect-subtrees.sh`, a detached start) the run branch is cut from `HEAD` and `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` is recorded. The record goes to `${LEERIE_STATE_DIR:-.leerie}/runs/<run-id>/working-branch` on first run only. Adds the run-branch worktree at `${LEERIE_STATE_DIR:-.leerie}/runs/<run-id>/worktrees/staging` if missing. Canonicalizes the staging path to absolute (`pwd -P`) before comparing against `git worktree list --porcelain` output (which always uses absolute, symlink-resolved paths); under `leerie_repo_lock`, reclaims an unregistered-but-present staging directory (`rm -rf`) and calls `prune_leerie_worktrees "$RUN_DIR"` (scoped to this run; see above), so a directory left behind by a SIGKILLed run (Fly `machine stop` — `_cleanup_on_abnormal_exit` never runs) does not make `git worktree add` fail with `fatal: '<path>' already exists`. A staging worktree that is still registered (a SIGKILLed predecessor skipped `_cleanup_on_abnormal_exit`) is reused but restored by `leerie_reset_worktree <staging> leerie/runs/<run-id>` (*One restore*: checked out on the run branch — `reset --hard HEAD` alone kept a HEAD a worker detached, review round 15 H2 — at its tip, nothing uncommitted, ignored files kept; under `set -e` a failure stops setup with the porcelain). Every subtask worktree of the run is restored the same way onto `leerie/subtasks/<run-id>/<sid>`: found by path — each registered worktree directly in the run's worktree directory (not staging) whose name, minus the `leerie_worktree_name` prefix, is a `<sid>` with an existing subtask branch — never by the branch line of `git worktree list --porcelain`, which a detached worktree lacks; helper checkouts name no subtask branch and are left alone. Hooks off throughout (`leerie_git_hooks_off`). Safe on `resume`. |
| `planning-worktree.sh <run-id> [<working-branch>]` | Creates (`git worktree add --detach`, hooks off by `leerie_git_hooks_off`) or resets (`leerie_reset_worktree <wt> "" <target>`, *One restore*: ignored installs survive) the per-run judgment-worker worktree at `${LEERIE_STATE_DIR:-.leerie}/runs/<run-id>/worktrees/<run-id[:12]>-planning`, mirroring the given working branch when it resolves — the same lookup as `setup-run.sh` and `_working_branch_ref` (the name, then without a leading `heads/`, then an already-full `refs/heads/<name>`) — else the checkout's `HEAD` (a missing branch warns on stderr). Called by `_ensure_planning_worktree()` with `_working_branch_arg(st)`; that function logs the script's fallback warning (`_log_working_branch_fallback`), then stages task-referenced files and `.claude/` the worktree lacks via `_stage_worktree_extras`, skipping, file by file, only files committed on a branch the operator switched to and absent from the working branch (`_switched_branch_only_paths`). Under `leerie_repo_lock`, prunes (scoped to this run) **before** reclaiming an orphaned directory, as `new-worktree.sh` does. |
| `new-worktree.sh <id> <run-id>` | Makes (or reuses) the subtask tree at `${LEERIE_STATE_DIR:-.leerie}/runs/<run-id>/worktrees/<run-id[:12]>-<id>` (`leerie_worktree_name`), hooks off (`leerie_git_hooks_off`). Under `leerie_repo_lock` (`<run-dir>/repo/leerie-worktree.lock`: the run's own repository, so shared by that run's scripts and helpers only): `prune_leerie_worktrees` (scoped to this run) of the run repository's registry; `leerie/subtasks/<run-id>/<id>` cut in the run repository from the current `leerie/runs/<run-id>` tip when absent, kept when present (resume after handoff); then `leerie_tree <run-dir>/tree-repos/<name> <branch> <worktree>` (DESIGN §6 *A repository per committing tree (I6)*): a present tree of that tree repository is reused after its branch is taken; otherwise it is made afresh. Prints the absolute worktree path. The run-branch (`leerie/runs/…`) and subtask-branch (`leerie/subtasks/…`) prefixes are deliberately disjoint so neither is an ancestor ref of the other. |
| `integrate.sh <id> <run-id>` | From repo root, inside the run-branch worktree (`${LEERIE_STATE_DIR:-.leerie}/runs/<run-id>/worktrees/staging`): `git merge --no-ff leerie/subtasks/<run-id>/<id>` (hooks off: `leerie_git_hooks_off`, DESIGN §6½). Exit 0 clean; exit 1 on conflict, leaving the worktree mid-merge for an integrator; exit 2 on precondition failure (run-branch worktree or subtask branch missing) — `integrate_wave` treats exit 2 as fatal via `die()` and does *not* spawn an integrator, since the worktree-less case would fail in confusing ways. |
| `finalize.sh <run-id> [<base>]` | Run-branch verifier.
