Exits 0 if `refs/heads/leerie/runs/<run-id>` exists and contains at least one commit beyond `<base>` when given (`base_sha`, which `phase_finalize` passes), else beyond the working branch; exits non-zero with a diagnosis otherwise. The working branch is **never** modified — leerie does not merge into it locally; the PR is the proposed integration. The push and PR step lives in the **host launcher** (`leerie` bash script), not in the container — it runs after `nerdctl run` exits cleanly, using the host's own `git push` + `gh pr create` against the host's auth state. See "Host-side finalize" below. |
| `cleanup.sh [--run-id <id> \| --all-runs] [--branches \| --subtask-branches]` | Each run is cleaned inside its own repository (`<run-dir>/repo`) when it has one, whatever the caller's cwd; a run made before per-run repositories, in the cwd's. Default (no flag): scans `<state-root>/runs/*/state.json` for the most-recently-failed run (most recent without `finished_at`), confirms y/N, then removes only that run's worktrees + prunes git metadata. State dir stays as audit. `--run-id <id>` is an explicit single-run cleanup (worktrees only). `--all-runs` runs the same per-run cleanup across every run dir under `<state-root>/runs/`. `--branches` (combinable with `--run-id` or `--all-runs`) additionally deletes the matching run branches *and* subtask branches (`leerie/runs/<id>` and `leerie/subtasks/<id>/*`). `--subtask-branches` deletes only the subtask branches and keeps `leerie/runs/<id>`. `phase_finalize` passes neither: its cleanup removes worktrees only, and the run's branches go with its repository. Without either flag, all branches are kept as an audit trail. State dirs are always preserved by `cleanup.sh`. Ctrl-C and every other abnormal exit in the orchestrator also preserve state — they call `_cleanup_on_abnormal_exit(full_purge=False)`. There is no `full_purge=True` call site today; the flag is retained as a future hook for an explicit-purge gesture, but no current code path uses it. |

A run branch `leerie/runs/<run-id>` is never reset once created — this is the invariant `resume` depends on. See `DESIGN.md` §6 ("the run branch is the resume contract").

### The run's own repository (RC4, I4): code surface

DESIGN §6 *The run's own repository* is canonical. Every branch of a run
lives in `<run-dir>/repo`. The planning worktree and leerie's detached
checkouts are worktrees of it; staging and each subtask tree are worktrees
of their own tree repositories, whose branches leerie takes back into it
(DESIGN §6 *A repository per committing tree (I6)*). The user's
repository receives only `leerie/runs/<id>`, by the host-side bring-back.

**Functions (`orchestrator/leerie.py`).**

| Function | Contract |
|---|---|
| `_run_repo(st) -> Path` | `Path(st.run_dir) / RUN_REPO_NAME` (`"repo"`): the one spelling of the path. `State.run_repo` returns it. |
| `_git_at(path) -> list[str]` | `["--git-dir", path]` when `path` holds a `HEAD` file and an `objects/` directory (a git directory: the run's repository), else `["-C", path]` (a work tree). Every orchestrator git call on a path that may be the run's repository builds its argv with it, so none relies on discovering a bare repository, which `safe.bareRepository=explicit` refuses (review round 17 M3). |
| `_run_repo_of(run_dir) -> Path \| None` | `<run_dir>/repo` when it has a `HEAD` file and `git --git-dir <repo> rev-parse --git-dir` succeeds, else None: a run made before per-run repositories, or not yet started. It never reads `core.bare`, which a worker's `git init` in a linked worktree rewrites (round 17 H1). The prune and abnormal-exit cleanup use it to pick the registry a run's worktrees are in. |
| `_run_repo_unusable(st, repo) -> str` | "" when `repo/HEAD` exists and `git --git-dir repo rev-parse --verify <anchor>^{commit}` succeeds, where `<anchor>` is `st.data["base_sha"]`, else `refs/leerie/user-head`; otherwise the reason. |
| `_ensure_run_repo(st) -> Path` | When `st.data["run_repo"]` is set: returns the repository if `_run_repo_unusable` is "", else raises `RunRepoError` naming its path and saying it will not be deleted or rebuilt. It never deletes or rebuilds a recorded repository (round 17 H1). Otherwise: removes every `.repo.tmp-*` under the run directory (creation holds the run's flock, so none is live; round 17 L2); if `repo` exists unrecorded, records it when `_run_repo_unusable` is "" and raises otherwise, deleting nothing; else runs `git init --bare --object-format=<the user's>` in `.repo.tmp-<pid>`, `_carry_repo_config(st.repo_root, tmp)`, `_refresh_run_repo_base(st, tmp)`, and renames it into place. A failed creation removes the scratch directory and raises `RunRepoError`. It sets `st.data["run_repo"] = "repo"`. Called through `_ensure_run_repo_or_die` (off the event loop, `die()` on failure; there is no fallback to the user's repository) by `_run_phases` before the `waves` guard, by `_ensure_planning_worktree`, and by `phase_execute`. |
| `_carry_repo_config(user, repo) -> None` | Reads `git -C user config --local --list -z` and copies each key with `git config -f repo/config --add`, except `core.bare`, `core.worktree`, `core.repositoryformatversion`, `extensions.*`, `include.*`, `includeif.*` (`_RUN_REPO_UNCARRIED_*`) and any key `git init` already wrote. A key with no `=` is copied as `true`. If `git -C user config core.hooksPath` is empty, it sets `core.hooksPath` to `git -C user rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path hooks`. Both reads use `_git_hooks_on(os.environ)`, since leerie's hooks-off entry would otherwise be the answer. It also runs host-side, for the rebaser's repository. |
| `_refresh_run_repo_base(st, repo=None) -> str` | Runs `git --git-dir <repo> fetch --quiet --no-write-fetch-head --no-recurse-submodules --update-head-ok <user> [+HEAD:refs/leerie/user-head] [+<wb ref>:<wb ref>]`, where `<wb ref>` comes from `_working_branch_ref` and `repo` defaults to `_run_repo(st)`. `+HEAD:refs/leerie/user-head` is in the fetch only when the repository has no `refs/leerie/user-head` yet (its creation) or there is no `<wb ref>` (a detached start); then it also sets `update-ref --no-deref HEAD <user-head>`. So a mid-run branch switch brings no other branch's history in (round 17 L1). Tag auto-follow is on. Returns the commit of `<wb ref>`, else of `refs/leerie/user-head`. The hooks-off entry is in the environment (`main()`). Called through `_refresh_run_repo_base_or_die` before `planning-worktree.sh` (in `_ensure_planning_worktree`) and before `setup-run.sh` (in `phase_execute`). |
| `_run_repo_commit(st, sha, ref) -> bool` | True when `sha` is a commit in the run's repository. Otherwise it fetches it by SHA from the user's repository into `ref` first. Used for the acceptance own start (`refs/leerie/own-start`, before `_acceptance_writer_checkout`'s clone) and a sibling's start (`refs/leerie/report-base`, `_acceptance_report_base`). Never raises. |
| `_ref_less_clone(src, wt, rev) -> str` | A `--shared --no-checkout --no-tags` clone of `src` at `wt`, detached at `rev`, with every ref, the remote and the reflog deleted. Returns "" on success, else why not, removing `wt`. Used by `_acceptance_writer_checkout` (`src` = the run's repository) and `_replay_capture` (`src` = the replayed repository, in the replay's temporary directory; no linked worktree of it). |
| `_diff_base(st) -> str \| None` | `st.data["base_sha"]`, else None. |
| `_record_run_id_for_launcher(run_id) -> None` | Writes `run_id` to the path in `LEERIE_RUN_ID_FILE` (a temporary file in the same directory, then `os.replace`), so the launcher knows which run its container ran (DESIGN §6 *Which run the container ran*). `main()` calls it right after `State(...)` takes the run directory's flock: a fresh run, a `resume <id>` and an auto-picked `resume` alike. It is a no-op when the variable is unset (Fly/EC2, tests, direct invocation). A failed write is logged and the run goes on; the branch then comes back at the run's finalize or `prune`. |
| `_refuse_other_run_layout(st, verb) -> None` | `RUN_LAYOUT_VERSION = 4` (the layout before the field, which recorded none, counts as 1; 3 moved worker transcripts into `logs/transcripts/` and `logs/held-out/transcripts/`; 4 moved every store a tree installs from — `stores/`, `tree-stores/`, `workers/cache/`, `workers/cache-held-out/` — into `worktrees/.stores/`, DESIGN §6 *The write grants on one mount are one mount*). Returns when `st.data.get("run_layout") == RUN_LAYOUT_VERSION`; otherwise calls `die()` naming the run, its layout (`run_layout`, or "none recorded"), whether it is older or newer, the `leerie_version` that made it, and the fix: finish it with that leerie, or start the task again as a fresh run. `main()` calls it for `resume` and for `--phase judge|heal` (whose `--run-id` names the run `State` opened) right after `State(...)` takes the run's flock and `st.load()` reads its `state.json`, before `_record_run_id_for_launcher`, the run-directory `mkdir`s, the log tee and the `try:` whose exit arms stamp `finished_at` and run `_cleanup_on_abnormal_exit` — so a refused run directory is left exactly as it was (DESIGN §6 *A run directory is continued only by a leerie of its layout*). A `resume` whose run has no `state.json` passes, for `_run_phases`' "nothing to resume". |
| `_run_script(name, *args, st)` | `cwd=_run_repo(st)`, with `LEERIE_STATE_DIR` set to the run directory's state root (`run_dir/../..`, resolved) and `LEERIE_GIT_DIR` set to `_run_repo(st)`, on every runtime. |

**State and `run.json`.**
- `run_repo`: `"repo"`, set by `_ensure_run_repo`.
- `base_sha`: the commit `setup-run.sh` cut the run branch from. `phase_execute` records it once, from `git --git-dir <repo> rev-parse refs/heads/leerie/runs/<id>^{commit}` right after the script, before anything is integrated; it `die()`s if that branch is missing.
- `run.json` `brought_back_sha`: written by the host only.
- Refs of leerie's own in the run's repository: `refs/leerie/user-head`, `refs/leerie/own-start`, `refs/leerie/report-base`, plus `refs/leerie/rescue/*` as before.

**Readers of the base.** These read `_diff_base(st)`, and skip (as they skipped without `working_branch`) when it is None:
- `_run_final_conformance`: the guard, the merge-base and the DIFF_BASE line;
- the acceptance-repair conformer's DIFF_BASE line (`_run_acceptance_gate_inner`);
- `_warn_site_token_leaks`, `_run_pr_review`;
- the delivery gate's two guards and the coverage check's guard;
- `_confirm_final_test_failures`' merge-base;
- `_compose_pr_via_llm`'s range (`<base or HEAD>..<run branch>`, read in the run's repository);
- `phase_finalize`'s ahead count.

`finalize.sh <run-id> [<base>]` counts from `<base>` when given; `phase_finalize` passes it. `working_branch` stays the PR-facing name in `run.json`.

**Git on the run's repository.** Everything below runs in `_run_repo(st)`, not the process cwd `/work`, named with `--git-dir` (`_git_at`), never `-C`:
- every `worktree remove` that named `st.repo_root`, and `_finish_no_work_run`'s;
- `_reset_subtask_worktree`, `_prune_subtask_worktree`;
- `_create_empty_subtask_branch`'s caller, `_undo_interrupted_redrives`' `update-ref`, `_settle_subtask`'s `_ref_sha`;
- `_shipping_tree`, `_falsify_items`' `diff --stat`;
- `_worktree_add_detached` (default `repo`; with no `repo` given and `_run_repo_of(st.run_dir)` None it `die()`s — the run's repository is missing only through a leerie bug, never degraded into a gate's "no evidence");
- `_cleanup_on_abnormal_exit`'s removals;
- `_prune_leerie_worktrees(root)` (the registry of `_run_repo_of(root)`, else the cwd's; the `git worktree prune` argv is unchanged, the repository passed as `GIT_DIR` in its environment).
- reads of a commit's objects:
  - `_record_settled_head` and `_fork_point` (the implementer's base);
  - the acceptance audit's `_js_source_graph` / `_repo_test_harness`;
  - `_acceptance_mechanical_findings`, `_prisma_db_context`, `_prisma_mock_hits`;
  - `_falsifier_coupling`;
  - the delivery re-drive's `_js_source_graph`.

  `_coupled_test_files` reads the measured tree's own repository (`tree` / `staging`), which is the run's.

Unchanged, on `st.repo_root` (the user's checkout, read-only git): `_preflight_repo`, the `working_branch` read, `_snapshot_repo_state`/`_assert_repo_unchanged`, `_stage_worktree_extras`, `_switched_branch_only_paths`, `_working_branch_ref`, `_base_tree_sha`.

**Shell.**
- The worktree scripts act on the repository `LEERIE_GIT_DIR` names, else on the one at their cwd. `worktree-lib.sh`'s `leerie_repo_git` runs `git --git-dir="$LEERIE_GIT_DIR"` when it is set and plain `git` otherwise; every repository-level git command in `setup-run.sh`, `planning-worktree.sh`, `new-worktree.sh`, `finalize.sh`, `integrate.sh`'s `show-ref`, `prune_leerie_worktrees` and `leerie_repo_lock` goes through it (round 17 M3). Git run inside a worktree is unchanged. Two more:
  - `finalize.sh` takes the optional `<base>`.
  - `cleanup.sh`'s `clean_one_run` cleans with `LEERIE_GIT_DIR=<run-dir>/repo` when that repository exists, whatever its caller's cwd (no `cd`); its `worktree remove` is `git ${LEERIE_GIT_DIR:+--git-dir="$LEERIE_GIT_DIR"} worktree remove --force`. A run made before the change is cleaned in the cwd's repository, with `LEERIE_GIT_DIR` unset.
- `scripts/host-finalize.sh`:
  - `host_bring_back_run_branch <run-dir>`: needs `<run-dir>/repo` with `refs/heads/leerie/runs/<id>` (else a no-op), read with `git --git-dir`.
    - If the user's ref already equals the tip, it records `brought_back_sha`.
    - Else, if the user's ref is not `brought_back_sha` (or absent when nothing was recorded), it refuses: it returns 0 when the tip is what was last brought back, and 2 otherwise.
    - Else it fetches into `refs/leerie/incoming/<id>` (`-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null`, `--no-tags --no-write-fetch-head --no-auto-maintenance`). When the user's ref exists and `merge-base --is-ancestor <old> <tip>` fails, it deletes the incoming ref, says the tip "does not descend" from the user's ref, and returns 2 (round 17 H1: only a fast-forward is brought back). Else it runs `update-ref refs/heads/leerie/runs/<id> <tip> <old>` (`<old>` empty for "must not exist"), deletes the incoming ref and records `brought_back_sha`.
    - It returns 1 when the fetch or the swap fails.
  - `host_finalize` calls it first, before the `no_push` check.
  - `_host_finalize_rebase_repo <dir> <run-branch> <pr-base>` makes the rebaser's repository:
    - `git clone --bare --shared --no-tags --single-branch --branch <run-branch> $USER_REPO`, then every git on it with `--git-dir`;
    - `remote remove origin`;
    - fetches the user's `refs/heads/<pr-base>` and `refs/remotes/origin/<pr-base>` when present.

    `run_rebaser` then carries the user's repository-local config into it (`_carry_repo_config`; its `origin` among it), in the python seam the step already runs, and never when the worktree's common directory is the user's own.

    `run_rebaser`'s prompt names the run's commits as `<base_sha>..<run-branch>` (`st.data["base_sha"]`, else `working_branch` for a state that predates it): that repository has the run branch and the PR base, and the working branch only when it is the PR base (round 17 M1).

    The rebase worktree is added there, and nothing is registered in `$USER_REPO`. The scratch-ref fetch-back runs with hooks off. After `rebased`, `refs/remotes/origin/<pr-base>` is fetched from it into `$USER_REPO`. `rm -rf` of the scratch directory removes the repository with the worktree.
- `leerie` launcher:
  - `_read_ran_run_id` reads the run-id file (local runtime only) into `_ran_run_id`. A first line that is not a run id (`[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, no leading dot) counts as no file. Every post-exit step reads that variable, and nothing else names the run:
    - `_bring_back_ran_run` (`_read_ran_run_id`, then `host_bring_back_run_branch` for that run when it has `repo/HEAD`; never fails) runs in the container arm's EXIT trap, before the run-id file is removed, so every exit brings the branch back: clean, failed, `--no-push`, and Ctrl-C/TERM, whose traps `exit 130`/`143` through it (round 17 M2). Every step of that EXIT trap ends `|| true`;
    - the "finalize: skipped … (run <id>)" line, which carries no run when there is no file;
    - the auto-finalize, which calls `host_finalize` on `runs/<_ran_run_id>` when its `run.json` has `finished_at`, `branch` and `working_branch` and no `pushed_at`, and otherwise says why and exits 0. It replaced the scan for the newest unpushed finished `run.json` under the state root, which with two runs could push the other one.

    The run is the one named in the run-id file, and no other. The file is `$LEERIE_STATE_HOST_DIR/.runid-$$`. It is removed before `nerdctl run` and by the EXIT traps, and passed as `-e LEERIE_RUN_ID_FILE=/leerie-state/.runid-$$`;
  - `finalize` (local), before its branch-exists check;
  - `prune --apply` (`_bring_back`, the same bash function through `LEERIE_PRUNE_HOST_FINALIZE`), before deleting a terminal run directory that has `repo/`. On a non-zero return the directory is kept and reported. `prune` keeps its user-registry deregistration and `leerie/subtasks/*` deletion for runs made before the change.
- `scripts/remote/fetch-branch.sh` and `ec2-fetch-branch.sh` read the run branch and subtask refs, and bundle, from `git --git-dir=/work/.leerie/runs/<id>/repo`. Their state tar has `--exclude=<id>/repo`.
- `scripts/remote/collect-subtrees.sh` sets `LEERIE_STATE_DIR=/work/.leerie` (it defaulted to `/leerie-state`, absent on a machine) and runs in `<run-dir>/repo`, with `LEERIE_GIT_DIR` set to it and its own `for-each-ref`/`merge-base` on `--git-dir`. It reports `COLLECT-ERROR` when that repository is missing.

**Deleted.**
- `_redrive_exclude_clear`, `_redrive_exclude_path`, `_REDRIVE_EXCLUDE_TAG` and their call in `_run_delivery_redrive`.
- `phase_finalize`'s `--subtask-branches` (both cleanup calls are worktrees-only now) and the run-branch-survived `show-ref` check.
- `_cleanup_on_abnormal_exit`'s `full_purge` `for-each-ref`/`branch -D` loop. The purge removes the run directory, the run's repository with it.

**Tests.**
- `tests/test_run_repo.py`, real git, through the real scripts and helpers:
  - creation: bare, no alternates, no remote, only the working branch, `refs/leerie/user-head` and the tags in that history, the same object format, idempotent, and nothing left behind on failure;
  - the config carry and its substance: a run-repository commit runs the user's `pre-commit`;
  - refresh: follows the user's tip, restores a moved copy, keeps the run's HEAD, and gives a detached start a detached HEAD;
  - round 17: a worker's `git init` in staging (`core.bare` becomes false) costs the run nothing; a recorded repository failing its check raises and is not deleted; a crash-left `.repo.tmp-*` is removed and an unrecorded complete repository adopted; a mid-run branch switch brings no other commit in; every tree kind works under `safe.bareRepository=explicit`; the rebaser's prompt range resolves in its own repository;
  - r16 H2's two drivers as I4 tests;
  - every tree of a run hangs off `<run-dir>/repo`, while the user's `git worktree list` names only the user's checkout;
  - `base_sha` read by `_warn_site_token_leaks` and `finalize.sh` against a moved name;
  - the resume refusal and its order;
  - the full purge leaves the user's repository alone;
  - finalize's cleanup deletes no branch.
- `tests/test_run_repo_bring_back.py` (`HAS_JQ`): bring-back with hooks off and no `FETCH_HEAD`; advancing; the compare-and-swap refusing a rebased ref (rc 0) and unbrought work (rc 2); a tip that is no fast-forward refused (rc 2); a deleted ref is not recreated; a no-op without `repo/`; the call sites; the launcher's own traps under SIGINT (exit 130, branch brought back, a dead keepalive); `prune` keeping, then deleting, a run.
- `tests/test_checkout_ignore.py`: no function resolves `info/exclude` any more.
- Harness (`tests/conftest.py`):
  - `relocate_into_run_repo(leerie, st)` turns a hand-built layout (run branches and staging in the test's "user" repository) into the run's repository: it moves the `leerie/*` branches and the worktrees under the run directory, and records `base_sha` as the cut point.
  - The autouse `_no_run_repo_without_a_git_repo` makes `_ensure_run_repo_or_die` / `_refresh_run_repo_base_or_die` no-ops for a state whose `repo_root` is no git repository (stubbed-git phase tests, `Mock` states). A real repository gets the real functions.
- Rewritten to the layout, 51 test files plus `tests/conftest.py`. Each test's builders make the run's repository (`_ensure_run_repo` or the helper above) and do their git there. Three things changed besides the builders:
  - the pins of the deleted surfaces were rewritten: full-purge branch deletion, the run-branch-survived check, `--subtask-branches`, `_redrive_exclude_*`;
  - the `working_branch` skip tests now drop `base_sha`;
  - two argv-shape pins follow `git -C <repo>`.
- Round 17 (the repository named, never discovered): three pins follow the `--git-dir` spelling — `test_cleanup_run_scoped`'s `worktree remove`, `test_fetch_branch_sh`'s machine stub (it maps `--git-dir=<machine repo>` to the fixture) and `test_worktree_prune_scoping`'s locale probe (`LC_ALL=C LANGUAGE='' leerie_repo_git worktree prune`).

### A repository per committing tree (I6): code surface

DESIGN §6 *A repository per committing tree (I6)* is canonical.

**Layout.** `<run-dir>/tree-repos/<tree>/` (`TREE_REPOS_NAME =
"tree-repos"`), `<tree>` the worktree's directory name. Staging's holds the
run branch, a subtask tree's its subtask branch.

**Shell (`scripts/worktree-lib.sh`).**
- `leerie_take_tree_branch <tree-repo> <branch>`: `leerie_repo_git fetch
  --quiet --no-tags --no-write-fetch-head --no-auto-maintenance <tree-repo>
  +refs/heads/<branch>:refs/heads/<branch>`.
- `leerie_tree_branch_of <run-id> <tree-name>`: the branch by the name
  alone (`_tree_branch_of` in Python).
- `leerie_tree <tree-repo> <branch> <worktree>`, under `leerie_repo_lock`:
  - the worktree present and a worktree of `<tree-repo>` (its
    `--git-common-dir` is `<tree-repo>`): take its branch, reuse it;
  - otherwise: a tree of the run repository at that path (a run made before
    tree repositories) is deregistered there and removed; a stale
    `<tree-repo>` that holds `<branch>` has it taken first, then is
    removed; then `git init --bare --quiet --template=
    --object-format=<the run repository's>`, `objects/info/alternates` =
    `<run-repo>/objects`, `config` and `info/` copied from
    `<run-dir>/repo-settings` (`<run-dir>` being `<tree-repo>`'s
    grandparent; with no copy, the run repository's own `config` with
    `core.bare=true`), `git --git-dir <tree-repo> fetch --quiet --no-tags
    --no-write-fetch-head --no-auto-maintenance <run-repo>
    +refs/heads/<branch>:refs/heads/<branch>`, and `git --git-dir
    <tree-repo> worktree add <worktree> <branch>`.
- `leerie_drop_tree <tree-repo> <worktree>`: removes the worktree
  directory and the tree repository (the caller takes first when it keeps
  the work).
- `leerie_run_settings` maps a tree of a tree repository to the run's
  `repo-settings` too.
- `new-worktree.sh`: the run-scoped prune of the run repository's own
  registry, the subtask branch created in the run repository when absent
  (from the run branch's tip), then `leerie_tree`. The orphan-directory
  removal and the add's repair-and-retry are gone: a tree's registration is
  private to its tree repository, made under the lock, so no sibling races
  it; the pre-prefix worktree move is gone with them (such a run predates
  per-run repositories, and its resume is refused).
- `setup-run.sh`: staging through `leerie_tree`; on resume, every tree under
  `worktrees/` with a tree repository has its branch taken before it is
  reset.
- `integrate.sh`: in a staging of a tree repository, fetches the subtask
  branch from the run repository into it before the merge, and takes
  staging's branch after the merge (and after `merge --abort`).
- `cleanup.sh`: a tree with a tree repository is taken, then dropped.
- `collect-subtrees.sh` (Fly): takes staging after its integrator and after
  `_back_out`.
- `fetch-branch.sh`, `ec2-fetch-branch.sh`: the state tar also has
  `--exclude=<id>/tree-repos`.

**Python (`orchestrator/leerie.py`).**

| Function | Contract |
|---|---|
| `_common_dir_of(tree) -> Path \| None` | `git -C tree rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir`, None when that fails. |
| `_tree_repo_of(tree) -> Path \| None` | The common directory of `tree` when it is `<run-dir>/tree-repos/<name>` of a run with a repository (`_run_repo_of`), else None (a tree of the run repository itself, or of no run). |
| `_run_repo_for_tree(tree) -> Path \| None` | The run repository a tree belongs to, by the layout alone (`<run-dir>/repo` for a tree repository's tree, the common directory when that is a run repository), never by the tree repository's alternates file, which its worker can write. |
| `_tree_branch_of(tree_repo) -> str` | The branch leerie takes from it, by its name alone (never the tree's HEAD, which the worker sets): `staging` → `leerie/runs/<run-id>`, `<run-id[:12]>-<sid>` → `leerie/subtasks/<run-id>/<sid>`; `<run-id>` is the run directory's name. |
| `_take_tree_branch(tree) -> str \| None` | For a tree of a tree repository: `_take_tree_repo` of it; None for any other tree. `_take_tree_branch_async` runs it off the event loop; `_take_after_worker(cwd)` first puts leerie's settings back (`_restore_settings`, logged) and `die()`s when `_settings_dirt(cwd)` is still non-empty, then takes, and `die()`s when the take raises. |
| `_take_tree_repo(tree_repo) -> str \| None` | The fetch above into `<run-dir>/repo`, then the run repository's commit of that branch. Raises `RunRepoError` when the fetch fails. |
| `_drop_tree_repo(run_dir, name, *, take) -> bool` | Removes `<run_dir>/tree-repos/<name>` (a no-op when absent), after `_take_tree_repo` when `take`; False, with everything kept, when that take fails. |
| `_branch_commit_for_tree(tree, name) -> str` | `name` (the run branch) as the run repository's commit when `tree` is a tree of a tree repository, else `name`. `_branch_commit_for_tree_async` off the event loop. |
| `_bring_commit(tree, sha) -> None` | A commit leerie made in a tree repository on no branch (a synthetic merge, a rescue) into the run repository: a no-op when the run repository has it; else `fetch --upload-pack="git -c uploadpack.allowAnySHA1InWant=true upload-pack" <tree-repo> +<sha>:refs/leerie/kept/<sha>`. |

Where leerie takes:
- `claude_p`, in a `finally` after the worker call, for its `cwd`
  (`_take_tree_branch_async`); a failed take `die()`s.
- `_restore_tree`, at its end, for `tree`.
- `_integrate_merge`, at its end (integrate.sh took after the merge; the
  JSON-key merge and the subject amend come after it).
- `_reintegrate_settled_head` moves the subtask branch in the run repository
  (`update-ref` there, never in staging).
- `_prune_subtask_worktree`, before it drops the tree; `_reset_subtask_worktree`
  drops it without taking (it deletes the branch).
- `_cleanup_on_abnormal_exit`: each tree with a tree repository is taken,
  then dropped (directory and tree repository).
- `_reap_idle_worktrees`: each reaped run's trees are taken into that run's
  repository before its `worktrees/` and `tree-repos/` go.

Reads:
- `_ancestor_codes`, `_wave_sids_not_integrated`, `_next_rescue_ref` read
  the run repository (`_git_at(_run_repo_for_tree(staging))`).
- `_rescue_integrator_work` stores its commit with `_bring_commit` and its
  ref in the run repository.
- `_synthetic_merge`'s commit is brought (`_bring_commit`) before the
  integration judge's checkout.
- `_judge_checkout` and `_committed_view` add their checkouts in the run
  repository (`repo` default), at a commit brought or taken there; the view
  reads its tip from the run repository after taking the tree.
- The run branch is read by commit, never by name, inside a subtask tree:
  `_branch_commit_for_tree(tree, <run branch>)` is passed where a subtask
  tree's diff, log or show was given the name: `check_diff_scope`,
  `_branch_has_commits_ahead`, `check_branch_has_commits`, the settle's
  name-only diff, `_run_conformance_phase` (its `_changed_files`,
  `_clobbered_owned_files` and the conformer's `DIFF_BASE`), and the
  external-claim checks (`_env_template_local_service`, `_repo_mentions`).
  Coverage reads its base in the committed view, a worktree of the run
  repository, where the name resolves.
- `_undo_interrupted_redrives`, rolling a subtask branch back in the run
  repository while its tree is gone, drops a surviving tree repository
  untaken (`leerie_tree` takes a stale one).
- `_run_settings_of(tree)` returns `(<tree-repo>, <run-dir>/repo-settings)`
  for a tree of a tree repository, so `_settings_dirt` and
  `_restore_settings` check and restore its `config` and `info/` against
  the run's copy.

`_seal_run_repo_config` also sets `gc.auto=0`, `gc.pruneExpire=never`,
`gc.worktreePruneExpire=never` and `maintenance.auto=false`. leerie's
fetches into the run repository pass `--no-auto-maintenance`.

**Tests.** `tests/conftest.py::worker_exit(tree)` runs the real
`_take_tree_branch`: what a worker's exit does, for a test that stands in
for a worker by committing in its tree. `tests/test_tree_repos.py`, real git
through the real scripts:
the tree repository's shape (alternates, one ref, the run's settings, no
copied objects); a worker confined to its tree and tree repository (the
run repository made read-only) commits, and cannot move the run branch or a
sibling's; leerie takes exactly the tree's own branch (a ref the worker
made elsewhere in its repository never reaches the run repository); a
worker that moves its HEAD to another branch does not change what is
taken; integrate merges a sibling into staging and takes it; a rollback
through `_restore_tree` reaches the run repository; a resume takes a
crashed worker's commits before the reset; the run repository's gc
settings; a judge checkout at a synthetic merge and at a detached HEAD
staging was left on; a tree made before this
change is remade from a tree repository.

### The user's checkout is read-only in the local container: code surface

DESIGN §6 *The explicit channel: the user's checkout is mounted read-only*
is canonical. Locally nothing in the container writes the user's checkout.

- **Mount.** The launcher's `_run_argv` mounts `-v "$USER_REPO:/work:ro"`.
  Fly and EC2 are unchanged: `/work` there is the machine's clone and the
  state root's home, read-write.
- **`scripts/container-entry.sh`.** The rootful guard's `chown leerie: /work`
  runs only when `/work` is not a read-only mount
  (`_work_is_read_only`: `/proc/self/mounts`' entry for `/work` has `ro`
  among its options). Locally `/work` is always read-only, so it never runs;
  on Fly it re-owns the volume root as before.
- **Dependency capture** records instead of writing (`capture_repo_deps`
  `record_in`, `_record_capture`, `apply_captured_deps` above). Only the
  operator applies it (DESIGN §6½ *The operator applies a capture*):
  - `leerie config --apply-capture <run-id>` (a run id of
    `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, not `.`/`..`; else usage, exit 1; exit 1 too when
    `<state>/runs/<run-id>/captured-deps.json` is absent) sources
    `scripts/host-finalize.sh` and runs `host_apply_captured_deps
    <run-dir>`: host `python3` loads `orchestrator/leerie.py` of the tree
    the file was sourced from (`_HOST_FINALIZE_CODE`; for this verb, the
    install) by path (as the rebaser and `--recapture` seams do) and calls
    `apply_captured_deps(run_dir, $USER_REPO)`, which logs the change as a
    unified diff. Returns 1 (the verb exits 1) when the seam fails or the
    capture is refused.
  - The launcher's `_note_ran_run_captures` (`_read_ran_run_id`) runs in the
    container arm's EXIT trap, after `_bring_back_ran_run`, `|| true` like
    every step there: when the ran run has a `captured-deps.json` it prints
    `[leerie] capture: run <id> recorded dependencies …; review and apply
    them with: leerie config --apply-capture <id>`. It applies nothing.
  - `fetch-branch.sh` and `ec2-fetch-branch.sh` step 4 log the same line
    after the state stream-back when the run directory has the file, and
    stream nothing from the machine's `/work/.leerie/` back.
- **Phase 1½.** `phase_provision` runs `_run_setup_hook` and
  `_run_mise_install` with `repo_root` = a `_judge_checkout(st,
  <planning worktree>, "provision")` of the planning tree's commit, removed
  afterwards; a checkout that cannot be made `die()`s. The recipe
  detection still reads the user's checkout.
- **Status reads of the checkout** run `git --no-optional-locks status
  --porcelain`: `_snapshot_repo_state` and `_preflight_repo`'s clean check.
- **No registry fallback.** `_prune_leerie_worktrees(root)` returns when
  `_run_repo_of(root)` is None, touching no registry and creating no lock
  file. `_cleanup_on_abnormal_exit` runs `git worktree remove` only in the
  run's own repository; without one it removes the directories only. A
  pre-change run's registrations in the user's repository are deregistered
  by the host's `leerie prune`, as before.
- **The state-root fallback** (`resolve_leerie_root`'s `<repo>/.leerie`) is
  unchanged and unreachable in the local container: `_run_argv` always
  passes `-e LEERIE_STATE_DIR=/leerie-state`.
- **Kept, by reachability:** `_repo_write_denials` (the host seams
  `run_rebaser`, `run_recapture_deps`) and `_assert_repo_unchanged` (Fly/EC2;
  its baseline feeds the acceptance own start).

**Tests.**
- `tests/test_work_read_only.py`:
  - the launcher's `_run_argv` mounts `$USER_REPO:/work:ro`, passes
    `LEERIE_STATE_DIR=/leerie-state`, and mounts nothing else at `/work`;
  - a worker-style write to a read-only checkout fails while the run's
    reads succeed (a real read-only bind mount when the host can make one,
    the real container probe when `LEERIE_TEST_CONTAINER_IMAGE` names an
    image);
  - the entry script's chown is guarded by the mount check, and the check
    reads `ro` from a mounts line;
  - capture inside the container records into the run directory and leaves
    the checkout untouched; `apply_captured_deps` merges into the host's
    current config (keeping a key the user edited), is a no-op the second
    time, and keeps a malformed file;
  - the launcher's EXIT trap names the ran run's capture and applies
    nothing; `config --apply-capture` applies it;
  - phase 1½'s hook and `mise` run outside the checkout;
  - the snapshot's status passes `--no-optional-locks`;
  - with no run repository the prune and the abnormal-exit clean-up create
    nothing in the cwd's `.git`.

### Host-side finalize (bash + jq in the `leerie` launcher)

The push + PR step runs on the **host** in the launcher, after `nerdctl
run` exits cleanly. The container's `phase_finalize` writes
`finished_at` to `run.json` and exits 0; the launcher polls that
sentinel and proceeds. See DESIGN.md §6 *Finalization* for the
architecture (auth state lives in host processes the container can't
reach; the boundary is structural).

The launcher's finalize block in `leerie` (bash) does, in order:

1. **Skip if `--no-push`.**
2. **Read run state** via `jq` from `$LEERIE_STATE_HOST_DIR/runs/<run-id>/run.json` and
   `state.json` (run branch, working branch, finished_at).
3. **Push the run branch.** `git push -u origin leerie/runs/<run-id>`
   (with `--no-verify` if the flag was set). On failure: print a
   multi-line message (run branch + working branch, captured push
   output — stderr plus any pre-push hook stdout — and the exact retry
   command), update `run.json` with `push_error`, exit non-zero.
4. **Compose PR title + body.** Primary path: read `pr_title` /
   `pr_body` from `run.json` — written by the `pr_writer` worker that
   `phase_finalize` invokes when the run will be pushed (`not no_push`), or
   that a resume of a finished run invokes when it continues with a push,
   the run has no `pushed_at` and `run.json` has no `pr_title`
   (`_compose_pr_for_a_push_chosen_after_finalize`) (see
   DESIGN §6 *Finalization* and §9 *Structured-output schemas*
   `pr_writer` entry). Fallback path (pr_writer skipped or crashed): a
   bash heredoc reads `state.json` fields with `jq` and emits the
   deterministic body shape `compose_pr_body` produces (task, category,
   source-of-truth, run timestamps, wave + subtask + worker counts,
   when `external_preconditions` is non-empty a `⚠ Deploy-ordering`
   section rendered via `jq`, byte-identical to the Python renderer —
   see "Deploy-ordering notes" — and then run.json's `pr_end_state`,
   the end-state section `phase_finalize` rendered, appended as-is). The launcher branches on whether
   `pr_title_llm` / `pr_body_llm` are non-empty.
5. **Open PR.** Before calling `gh pr create`, validate that
   `working_branch` still exists on origin via `git ls-remote
   --exit-code --heads`. If deleted (a stacked run's parent squash-
   merged mid-flight), fall back to the repo's default branch (`git
   remote show origin | sed 's/.*HEAD branch: //'`). Then:
   `gh pr create --base <working-branch> --head
   leerie/runs/<run-id> --title "leerie: <pr_title>" --body-file -`
   with the composed body piped on stdin, plus `--draft` when `run.json`'s
   `outcome` is `unconverged` (DESIGN §6 *The run outcome is decided
   once*). On failure: log a warning
   with the pushed-branch URL and a retry command (using the resolved
   base); update `run.json` with `pr_error`. **Non-fatal** — exit 0.

**An open PR follows its run's re-decided outcome** (DESIGN §6). When
`run.json.pushed_at` is set, `host_finalize` first calls
`_host_finalize_refresh_pr <run.json>`, which acts only when `pr_refresh` is
an object and `pr_url` is set: `gh pr view <url> --json body,isDraft`; the
body with every occurrence of `pr_refresh.end_state_was` replaced by
`pr_end_state` (jq `split`/`join` on the literal text; appended after a
blank line when the body does not hold it, or `end_state_was` is empty);
`gh pr edit <url> --body-file -`; `gh pr ready <url>` when
`pr_refresh.outcome` is not `unconverged` and the PR is a draft; then
`pr_refresh` is set null. Every `gh` runs from `/` with `GIT_DIR` /
`GIT_WORK_TREE`, as `gh pr create` does. A failing step prints a warning,
keeps `pr_refresh` and returns 0, so the next `finalize` tries again; nothing
is pushed and no PR is created. The local launcher's post-exit block, which
otherwise stops at "already pushed", calls `host_finalize` when
`pr_refresh` is an object; Fly and EC2 reach it through `decide_teardown`'s
`host_finalize`, and every runtime through `leerie finalize <run-id>`.
Pinned in `tests/test_accept_heldout.py` (real git origin, stub `gh`: body
swapped, draft marked ready, nothing pushed; a failing `gh pr ready` keeps
the request).

**Local runtime only.** The inline finalize block above runs only when
`LEERIE_RUNTIME != "fly"`. On Fly the run dir is not yet on the host
when this block would otherwise execute (it's on the Fly Machine and
gets streamed back inside the EXIT trap `decide_teardown` that fires
*later*). The Fly path runs the same `host_finalize` function from a
different call site — see *Remote execution mode* below.

**Preflight (`leerie` bash, before `nerdctl run`):** the launcher
checks `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`, `shutil.which gh`,
`gh auth status`, and `git remote get-url origin` before spinning up
the container, with actionable messages plus the `--no-push` escape
hatch. The orchestrator no longer runs these checks; they moved to the
host where the auth state actually lives.

`--no-push` skips the entire push + PR step. CLI flag, `LEERIE_NO_PUSH`
env, `no_push = true` in `leerie.toml`. **The launcher resolves `no_push`
from CLI → env → TOML** (its inline TOML fallback mirrors
`_read_toml_key`'s flat grep — no `tomllib` dependency, since the launcher
runs on the user's host where Python 3.9 is still common) and hands a fresh
run the result as `--no-push`. The in-container `resolve_no_push()` sees
only the CLI flag and an in-tree `leerie.toml`, since `LEERIE_NO_PUSH` is
not forwarded to the container. Disagreement on a TOML-only opt-out would
make the launcher's host-side checks and the run's record disagree (the
launcher hands its resolved choice to a fresh run as `--no-push`; the
orchestrator records it, gates `pr_writer` and writes `run.json.no_push`).
`--no-verify` is CLI-only and only affects the push step (worker
`git commit`s inside worktrees still run all hooks).

### Remote execution mode

`--runtime fly` (or `LEERIE_RUNTIME=fly`) routes
execution to Fly.io Machines instead of the local `nerdctl run`. The
Colima/containerd preflight block is gated on `RUNTIME=local` and skipped
entirely when `RUNTIME=fly`. `--runtime` flows through `REWRITTEN_ARGS`
to the orchestrator's argparse. The launcher's bash-side resolution block
also accepts `ec2` so `--runtime ec2` is not rejected before a
container/instance starts; EC2 provisioning itself, and the
orchestrator-side argparse enum, are out of this launcher knob's scope.

Resolution order (highest priority first):

1. **`--runtime local|fly|ec2`** CLI flag. Passed through to the
   orchestrator so both the launcher and the orchestrator share the same
   resolved value.
2. **`LEERIE_RUNTIME`** environment variable, values `local` | `fly` | `ec2`.
3. **Default `local`** — local `nerdctl run` is used when unset. A
   `runtime` key in `leerie.toml` stops the launcher instead (§2
   *Repository configuration chooses no operator authority*).

Invalid values in env or TOML are rejected immediately with an error
message and exit 1 before any preflight runs.

**Runtime auto-detection on run-id-bearing verbs:** the shared
`_auto_detect_run_runtime(run_id, explicit_runtime)` helper checks
`$LEERIE_STATE_HOST_DIR/runs/$run_id/` for `fly-machine.json` (Fly) then
`ec2-instance.json` (EC2 — the sidecar `ec2-provision.sh`'s
`provision_instance()` writes unconditionally on a successful create). If
`explicit_runtime` is empty and either sidecar is present, it echoes the
detected runtime (`"fly"` or `"ec2"`) to stdout and returns 0; the caller
promotes its local runtime variable to that value. `_auto_detect_fly_runtime`
remains as a thin Fly-only wrapper (returns 0 only when the detected runtime
is `"fly"`) for call sites not yet migrated to EC2 handling.
Applied to `stop`, `kill`, `accept-blocked`, and `finalize` (all four
now accept `ec2` in their `--runtime` enum validation, alongside `local` and
`fly`), and to `resume` (which also appends `--runtime fly` to
`REWRITTEN_ARGS` and tracks the `_RUNTIME_EXPLICIT` flag). When the user
explicitly passes `--runtime local` on a Fly-originated run, `resume` warns
but respects the choice; the fast-path verbs reject it as before.

Every verb wires a real EC2 *action*: `kill`, `stop`, `accept-blocked`,
`list` (see the rows above), and `resume` / `finalize`. Detecting or
being explicitly passed `--runtime ec2` routes to the EC2 path rather
than falling through to the Fly path (which would misdirect an EC2
instance id to `flyctl`) or defaulting to `local` (which would
mislabel the run).

`resume` promotes `RUNTIME=ec2` exactly as it promotes `RUNTIME=fly` two
lines above, so the `RUNTIME=ec2` dispatch branch's sidecar →
`resume_instance()` path is reachable from a real `resume` invocation
(`grep -c "not yet wired" leerie` is 0). `tests/test_ec2_launcher_resume.py`
drives the real `leerie` binary to assert the promotion fires.

**`kill`'s EC2 action.** Resolves `ec2_instance_id` from the run dir's
`ec2-instance.json` (preferred) or `run.json` via the new
`_resolve_ec2_instance_id_from_run_dir` helper (the EC2 counterpart to
`_resolve_volume_id_from_run_dir` — unlike Fly, the run-id is NOT the
instance id for EC2 runs, so it must always be read from a sidecar). Dies
with "no ec2_instance_id found ..." if neither sidecar carries one. Prompts
for confirmation (bypassed by `--force`, same convention as the Fly/local
paths) before sourcing `aws-credentials.sh` + `ec2-lib.sh` +
`ec2-provision.sh` + `ec2-resume-instance.sh`, resolving credentials via
`resolve_aws_credentials` (same precedence and `--profile`/`--region`
passthrough as the `RUNTIME=ec2` fresh-provision branch), and gating on
`require_aws`. Sets `LEERIE_EC2_INSTANCE_ID` and re-resolves
`LEERIE_EC2_SSH_TARGET` from the instance's current `PublicIpAddress` via
`ec2-resume-instance.sh`'s `_resolve_ssh_target_from_instance` (EC2 hands
out a new public IP on every stop/start cycle). Then calls
`_try_fetch_state_for_ec2_teardown` — the same hook
`decide_ec2_teardown`'s clean-exit branch uses, reused rather than
duplicated — to sync the run branch and state dir back to the host BEFORE
calling `terminate_instance()`: the one-way-ratchet invariant
(`ec2-provision.sh:262-272`) that destroy-then-fetch would make paid-for
LLM work unrecoverable. A failed sync leaves the instance running and dies
with a "LEFT RUNNING" message pointing at a retry (`leerie kill <id>
--force`) rather than escalating to termination. On success, writes
`killed_at` + `ec2_instance_id` onto the run sidecar (bootstrapping
`run.json` from `ec2-instance.json` first via the widened `_ensure_run_json`
helper, which also handles an EC2-only run dir the same way it already
handles a Fly-only one). `flyctl` is never invoked on this path.

When `RUNTIME=fly`, the launcher skips the per-OS nerdctl preflight, the
image-build check, the auth/cache mount assembly, and the `nerdctl run`
invocation, and instead calls the remote dispatch path via
`scripts/remote/provision.sh`.

#### Machine lifecycle (`scripts/remote/provision.sh`)

The provision script is **sourced** (not exec'd) by the launcher so the
machine ID and destroy trap live in the launcher's process. It provides
four functions:

- **`provision_machine()`** — creates a Fly Machine from `$FLY_IMAGE_TAG`
  (set by the launcher; see below), polls `flyctl machine status` until the
  machine reaches state `started`, and registers `decide_teardown` as an
  EXIT/INT/TERM trap. Exports `$LEERIE_MACHINE_ID`. Returns 0 on success;
  destroys the machine and returns 1 on failure. Writes `fly_machine_id`
  and `image_tag` (from `$FLY_IMAGE_TAG`) to the run sidecar
  (`$LEERIE_STATE_HOST_DIR/runs/<run-id>/run.json`) when `$LEERIE_RUN_ID`
  is set — written immediately after provision succeeds so a launcher
  crash before classification still leaves a recoverable pointer. The
  `image_tag` field lets `resume_machine()` detect version drift on
  `resume` and update the machine's image before starting it.
- **`stop_machine()`** — runs `flyctl machine stop $LEERIE_MACHINE_ID
  --app $FLY_APP`, tolerant of already-stopped machines. Preserves the
  machine's filesystem on its Fly volume so `resume-machine.sh` can wake
  it later.
- **`destroy_machine()`** — runs `flyctl machine destroy $LEERIE_MACHINE_ID
  --app $FLY_APP --force`, with a stop-then-destroy fallback for machines
  already in a terminal state.
- **`decide_teardown()`** — the trap entry point. Classifies
  `$LEERIE_REMOTE_EXIT_RC` (set by the launcher just before exit) and
  dispatches one of three ways:
  - `destroy_machine` for genuine terminal exits (rc=0, EXIT_NEEDS_ANSWERS=10,
    EX_TEMPFAIL=75): the orchestrator exited cleanly and the machine has no
    further value.
  - **Detach** for rc=130/143 (host-side SIGINT/SIGTERM): the user pressed
    Ctrl-C or the local stream broke (laptop closed, WiFi dropped). Since
    the orchestrator on the machine was started detached (Python
    `subprocess.Popen(start_new_session=True, user="leerie", ...)`, see
    *Worker auth + config seeding* below), it is still running. The function
    leaves the machine alone, prints a one-line "detached" banner with the
    reattach / pause / kill commands, and returns.
  - `stop_machine` for unknown non-zero failures (worker error, orchestrator
    exception): preserves the machine's filesystem on its Fly volume so the
    user can attach to inspect and then `leerie resume`. Writes `paused_at`
    and `pause_reason` to the run sidecar.

  Idempotent (the trap fires on every exit, including success).

The classification table is the canonical authority on which exit
codes are treated as which disposition; DESIGN §6 *Detached orchestrator
(remote mode)* and *Remote pause-on-failure (Fly.io)* document the
rationale.

Environment variables consumed by `provision.sh`:

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `LEERIE_FLY_APP` | — (required) | Fly.io app name. Fly app names are globally unique; set via `--fly-app` or env. |
| `FLY_IMAGE_TAG` | `registry.fly.io/<app>:<version>` | Full image tag to launch (set by the launcher) |
| `FLY_REGION` | `iad` | Fly.io region |
| `FLY_VM_CPUS` | `4` | vCPU count for the machine. Setting >8 auto-promotes to Fly's `performance` CPU class (much more expensive — ~14x per CPU-second). |
| `FLY_VM_MEMORY` | `8192` | Memory in MB for the machine. Setting >16384 auto-promotes to Fly's `performance` CPU class. |
| `FLY_VM_DISK_GB` | `8` (on Fly runtime) | Per-machine Fly volume size in GB, mounted at `/work` — the path where the seeded repo, `.leerie/runs/<id>/` state, and per-subtask worktrees all live (and grow). The launcher defaults to `8` when `RUNTIME=fly` and no explicit value is given (CLI / env; never `leerie.toml`). The volume is destroyed when the machine is destroyed (clean exit or `kill`). Override to a larger value for runs that hit ENOSPC (the rootfs is hard-capped at 2,000 IOPS / 8 MiB/s — N-wide worktree fans-out hit both the IOPS ceiling and the size cap fast). `/home/leerie` (caches + the `.claude` auth bundle) stays on the rootfs — `seed_auth` runs unconditionally on every resume, so the auth bundle is refreshed from host `$STAGE` regardless of pause length. |
| `LEERIE_MACHINE_START_TIMEOUT` | `120` | Seconds to wait for `state=started` |

`FLY_IMAGE_TAG` is resolved by the launcher (`resolve_fly_image_tag()`)
using `$LEERIE_FLY_APP` and `$LEERIE_VERSION`, or overridden by setting
`LEERIE_FLY_IMAGE` in the environment.

`provision_machine` requires `flyctl` on `PATH` and `flyctl auth status`
to succeed. The launcher's `RUNTIME=fly` preflight calls `require_flyctl`
from `scripts/remote/lib.sh` *before* sourcing any other remote script —
that helper detects missing `flyctl` and prompts for `brew install
flyctl` (macOS) or the Fly install script (Linux), then prompts for
`flyctl auth login` if unauthenticated. The auto-install mirrors the
local-runtime auto-install in `scripts/install.sh:200-208` and respects
`--no-runtime-install` / `LEERIE_NO_RUNTIME_INSTALL=1` (falls back to
hint-and-exit-1). By the time `provision_machine` runs, `flyctl` is
guaranteed to be on PATH and authenticated.

#### Private ssh-agent isolation (`_leerie_fly_agent_ensure`)

Before any `flyctl ssh ...` call can run, the launcher's `RUNTIME=fly`
branch invokes `_leerie_fly_agent_ensure` (in `scripts/remote/lib.sh`)
to spawn — or reuse — a leerie-owned ssh-agent at
`${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/leerie/agent/ssh-agent.sock` and
export `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` to point at it for the rest of the process
tree. The user's main ssh-agent is never touched.

This isolation matters because `flyctl ssh issue --agent` is
**additive** — it appends a fresh 24h cert to the agent and never
deletes prior certs. With multiple `require_fly_ssh` callers per
leerie run (seed-auth + two seed-repo paths), aiming flyctl at the
user's main agent accumulates dozens of certs, which OpenSSH then
offers to every ssh destination (including `github.com`); after
~5 failed auth attempts per connection GitHub rate-limits the account.
Containing all Fly certs in a private agent reachable only by leerie's
process tree eliminates the failure mode.

The private agent is persistent (lazy-spawned, never auto-killed) so
the 24h cert is reused across leerie runs — re-issuing on every
invocation was what produced the original accumulation. Reboot wipes
the socket inode; the next run lazy-spawns fresh. Parallel leerie
invocations serialize on `~/.cache/leerie/agent/.spawn.lock` via
`mkdir`-as-mutex (portable across darwin/linux without the non-stdlib
`flock` binary macOS lacks); only the first spawn wins, the rest see a
live socket and reuse it.

The reuse check probes the socket with `ssh-add -l` and reuses it on any
exit code **other than 2**: rc 0 (has keys) and rc 1 (reachable, no keys
yet) both mean the agent is alive; only rc 2 (cannot connect) means the
socket is stale. Treating rc 1 like rc 2 would unlink a live agent's
socket out from under the still-running process.
The exit code is captured (`ssh-add -l … || rc=$?`), never read from `$?`
after a bare statement: the function runs under the launcher's
`set -euo pipefail`, where a bare `ssh-add -l` returning 1 ends the launcher
before the check. The function releases `.spawn.lock` on every return; a
failed `ssh-agent` spawn returns its exit code with a `remote_log` line, and
the launcher and `require_fly_ssh` stop on it.

Any newly-spawned agent carries `-t 24h`, matching the 24h Fly cert
(`flyctl ssh issue --agent`) — this bounds only the lifetime of
**identities** added to the agent (`man ssh-agent`), not the agent
process itself (killing it is the separate `ssh-agent -k`). An
orphaned agent leaks indefinitely holding an empty keyring; there is
no reaper for it today.

#### Worker auth + config seeding (`scripts/remote/seed-auth.sh`)

After `provision_machine()` returns successfully, the launcher sources
`scripts/remote/seed-auth.sh` and calls `seed_auth()`. This is the remote
equivalent of the `AUTH_MOUNTS` bind-mount block (launcher lines ~542–726):
instead of mounting `$STAGE` as container volumes, the same content is
delivered via `flyctl ssh console -C` tar-pipe + small shell-command
invocations. (`flyctl machine exec` is NOT used — current flyctl removed
both `--stdin` on `machine exec` and the post-`--` argv form; `ssh
console -C` is the only flyctl transport that takes the remote command
as a single string AND forwards host stdin.)

`seed_auth()` performs six steps:

1. **Hallpass readiness probe.** Calls `require_fly_ssh` (ensures the
   leerie-private ssh-agent — see above — holds a valid Fly cert,
   issuing only if none exists) and `wait_for_fly_ssh_ready` (polls
   `flyctl ssh console --pty=false -C true` until success; hallpass
   takes 5-30 s to come up after `flyctl machine start` reports
   "started"). This is the *only* hallpass probe in a run — subsequent
   transports (`seed_repo_clone` parent + submodule bundles,
   `seed_repo_dirty` rsync) rely on each pipe's own
   `LEERIE_SEED_TIMEOUT_S` wrapper (rc 124/137) as the authoritative
   failure detector; an extra probe before each pipe would only
   manufacture false-positives once the channel is warm. Bound: ~175 s
   total (12 attempts × 10 s per-probe timeout + 11 × 5 s sleep); on
   success emits `remote: hallpass ready on <machine>`; on the rare
   exit-137 exhaustion (timeout's SIGKILL or an external SIGKILL like
   macOS Jetsam under host pressure), the warning includes a "killed
   externally" diagnostic so the operator can distinguish client-side
   pressure from a real Fly outage.

2. **Tar-pipe delivery of `$STAGE` to /home/leerie.** `tar -czC $STAGE`
   (gzip-compressed; excluding `.gitconfig`, `.gitconfig.local`,
   `.gitignore`, `.gitignore_global`, `.git-credentials`, `.netrc`,
   `.ssh`, `.gnupg`, `.config`; with `COPYFILE_DISABLE=1` host-side to
   silence macOS BSD tar's per-file
   `LIBARCHIVE.xattr.com.apple.provenance` warnings on the remote GNU
   tar) is piped to `flyctl ssh console --pty=false -C "sh -c
   'tar -xzC /home/leerie && chown -R leerie: /home/leerie'"`. The
   `chown -R leerie:` is necessary because the ssh-console session
   lands as root with default umask; without it the orchestrator
   (running as leerie) couldn't read its own credentials. The
   `leerie:` (trailing colon, no group name) uses leerie's numeric
   primary group rather than a hard-coded group name — leerie's
   primary GID is `HOST_GID` (defaults to 20 / staff on macOS) and the
   group is not necessarily called `leerie`.

   The launcher's `$STAGE` build skips `.claude/local` (the host npm
   install of `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` — the image installs claude
   globally via the Dockerfile, so shipping the host's local install
   is dead weight) plus `.claude/plugins/cache/` and
   `.claude/plugins/marketplaces/` (rebuilt on the remote in step 6
   from the small JSON metadata files that ride along). This keeps the
   stage well under the size where the `ssh console -C` stdin pipe
   starts hitting EOFs.

   On transient "tunnel unavailable" failure from a freshly-spawned
   flyctl agent, the seed retries once after `flyctl agent restart`.

3. **Token fallback.** If `$STAGE/.claude/.credentials.json` was not
   written (Linux, or macOS Keychain extraction failure) but
   `$CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` is set, `seed_auth()` writes a
   credentials JSON
   `{"claudeAiOauth":{"accessToken":"<token>","scopes":["user:inference"]}}`
   (the `scopes` field is mandatory — CLI 2.1.210's file-auth rejects a
   scope-less blob; see the `_extract_claude_credentials_json` row
   above) directly to `/home/leerie/.claude/.credentials.json` via
   `flyctl ssh console -C "sh -c 'cat > .../credentials.json
   && chmod 600 ... && chown leerie: ...'"`. If neither source is
   available, `seed_auth()` returns 1 with an actionable error.

4. **Git identity.** Reads `user.name` and `user.email` from the
   host's git config and writes them to `/home/leerie/.gitconfig` on
   the machine via `flyctl ssh console -C "sh -c 'IFS= read -r n;
   IFS= read -r e; git config --file /home/leerie/.gitconfig user.name
   \"\$n\" && git config --file /home/leerie/.gitconfig user.email
   \"\$e\" && chown leerie: /home/leerie/.gitconfig'"` with the two
   values piped on stdin — NOT `git config --global`, which under the
   ssh-console session's default root user would write to
   `/root/.gitconfig` where leerie can't read it. Worker commits carry
   the host user's identity.

5. **Pre-warm `claude --version`** once as the leerie user via
   `flyctl ssh console -C "su leerie -c 'HOME=/home/leerie PATH=... claude
   --version'"`. The first `claude --version` on a freshly-booted Fly
   machine takes ~17 s (Node runtime + statsig client cold-start);
   subsequent calls return in <0.2 s. Paying this upfront means the
   orchestrator's preflight `_check_claude_cli_version` call hits warm
   caches.

6. **Rebuild plugin cache.** The tar pipe excludes `plugins/cache/`
   and `plugins/marketplaces/` (step 2); the small JSON metadata files
   (`installed_plugins.json`, `known_marketplaces.json`) ride along
   and are the source of truth for rebuilding. Inside one
   `flyctl ssh console` invocation (running as the leerie user via
   `runuser -u leerie -- env HOME=... PATH=... sh -s` — not
   `su -c 'sh -s'`, which has implementation-specific stdin-forwarding
   under util-linux) a shell heredoc runs two phases: (a) read
   `known_marketplaces.json` with a python3 one-liner (jq isn't in the
   image), emit each `source.repo`, and run `claude plugin marketplace
   add <owner>/<repo>`; (b) read `installed_plugins.json` keys (e.g.
   `vercel@claude-plugins-official`) and run `claude plugin install`
   per entry. Output is appended to
   `/home/leerie/.cache/leerie/plugin-install.log`. Per-plugin
   failures are logged (`WARN: <spec> install failed (continuing)`)
   but non-fatal — a missing plugin only matters if a user-supplied
   task explicitly invokes it, in which case the Claude CLI's existing
   "plugin not found in cache" skip-with-warning behavior applies. The
   invocation is bracketed with the same `$(_seed_timeout_prefix)` +
   `_seed_progress_bg "plugin_rebuild"` heartbeat the main tar pipe
   uses (step 2), so a stalled `flyctl ssh console` produces a clean rc
   124/137 instead of hanging, and the user sees `plugin_rebuild: still
   streaming (Ns elapsed)` lines on the happy path. The rc is captured
   via `|| _rebuild_rc=$?` (grabs the rc and suppresses file-level
   `set -e`); the trailing `remote_log` line branches on rc —
   `complete` on 0, "timed out after Ns" on 124/137, "rc=N —
   continuing" otherwise. Replaces shipping ~200 MB of plugin contents
   over the WireGuard pipe with ~30–90 s of public-egress git-clone +
   bun-install on the Fly machine.

Git-push auth (SSH keys, `.netrc`, `~/.config/gh`) is **not** seeded — that
auth lives on the host per DESIGN §6 *Finalization* and is not needed inside
the remote machine for `claude -p` worker authentication or `git commit`.
The host pushes the run branch via `leerie finalize` after `fetch_branch`
streams the branch + state directory back; the machine never sees a
GitHub credential.

After seeding completes the launcher starts the orchestrator inside the
machine **detached** — see DESIGN §6 *Detached orchestrator (remote
mode)* for the rationale. The launcher generates the run-id host-side
(slug + suffix, same pattern as today's orchestrator-side generator)
and passes it explicitly via `--run-id <id>`, so it knows the
`orchestrator.log` path before the orchestrator has produced any output.
The detach is done by piping a Python wrapper script via stdin to
`flyctl ssh console -C "python3 -"`:

```bash
# Wrapper script built host-side with the argv JSON literal embedded
# (so no remote shell quoting touches the orchestrator argv).
_launch_argv_json="$(python3 -c '
import json, sys
print(json.dumps(sys.argv[1:]))
' "$LEERIE_RUN_ID" "${REWRITTEN_ARGS[@]}")"
_launch_script="$(cat <<PY
import fcntl, os, pwd, subprocess, sys, time
argv = ${_launch_argv_json}
run_id = argv[0]
orch_args = argv[1:]
run_dir = "/work/.leerie/runs/" + run_id
os.makedirs(run_dir, exist_ok=True)
leerie_pw = pwd.getpwnam("leerie")
# os.makedirs above created these as root; chown so the orchestrator
# (running as leerie) can write state files later.
for d in ("/work/.leerie", "/work/.leerie/runs", run_dir):
    try: os.chown(d, leerie_pw.pw_uid, leerie_pw.pw_gid)
    except OSError: pass
child_env = dict(os.environ)
child_env["HOME"] = "/home/leerie"   # ssh-console default is /root
child_env["USER"] = "leerie"
child_env["LOGNAME"] = "leerie"
# Host-side $(basename "$USER_REPO") expansion (heredoc is unquoted) —
# keeps orchestrator log() prefix consistent with host-side remote_log().
child_env["USER_REPO"] = "$(basename "$USER_REPO")"
# Host IANA TZ so in-machine log() offsets match host-side remote_log();
# _host_tz computed via `readlink /etc/localtime | sed 's|.*/zoneinfo/||'`.
# Empty value -> Python astimezone() falls back to UTC.
child_env["TZ"] = ${_host_tz_json}
# Bedrock activation. Every value is JSON-encoded host-side (not a raw
# quoted-var substitution — a bearer token could contain a quote/backslash
# that breaks out of the Python string literal). Bearer-token block takes
# precedence over the SSO/profile block. NOTE: heredoc is unquoted (<<PY) —
# never put a backtick pair in a comment here (command-substitution delimiter).
if "${_BEDROCK_BEARER_ACTIVE}" == "true":
    child_env["AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK"] = ${_bedrock_bearer_token_json}
    child_env["CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK"] = ${_bedrock_use_bedrock_json}
    if ${_bedrock_bearer_region_json}:
        child_env["AWS_REGION"] = ${_bedrock_bearer_region_json}
elif "${_BEDROCK_ACTIVE}" == "true":
    child_env["CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK"] = "1"
    if ${_bedrock_profile_json}:
        child_env["AWS_PROFILE"] = ${_bedrock_profile_json}
    if ${_bedrock_region_json}:
        child_env["AWS_REGION"] = ${_bedrock_region_json}
extra_path = "/usr/local/share/mise/installs/node/lts-current/bin"
if extra_path not in child_env.get("PATH", ""):
    child_env["PATH"] = extra_path + ":" + child_env.get("PATH", "")
log_path = run_dir + "/orchestrator.log"
pid_path = run_dir + "/orchestrator.pid"
with open(log_path, "ab") as log_f:
    p = subprocess.Popen(
        ["python3", "/opt/leerie-image/orchestrator/leerie.py",
         *orch_args],
        stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=log_f, stderr=log_f,
        start_new_session=True,    # bash setsid equivalent; portable
        cwd="/work",                # avoid stale-cwd ENOENT cascades
        user="leerie", group=leerie_pw.pw_gid,
        env=child_env,
    )
# Poll briefly before recording the pid. If this Popen lost the
# State.__init__ flock race against an already-running orchestrator for
# this run (DESIGN §6 *Single owner per run dir*), the child exits 75;
# writing its pid before the race resolves would overwrite the winner's
# pid with a dead one (the stale-pid contagion in DESIGN §6). Budget 2 s
# (Popen -> flock attempt is ~300-500 ms normally, ~1 s under disk
# pressure); the reader-side /proc cross-check catches any residual case.
for _ in range(10):
    if p.poll() is not None:
        break
    time.sleep(0.2)
if p.poll() == 75:
    # Stillborn — winner still owns the run; leave the pid file alone.
    sys.exit(75)
with open(pid_path, "w") as pid_f:
    pid_f.write(str(p.pid) + "\n")
PY
)"
printf '%s' "$_launch_script" \
  | flyctl ssh console --app "$FLY_APP" --machine "$LEERIE_MACHINE_ID" \
      --pty=false -C "python3 -"

# Separately tail the orchestrator log via a second ssh-console session
# (its death — Ctrl-C, broken pipe, laptop disconnect — does NOT
# propagate to the orchestrator).
printf '%s' "$_tail_invocation" \
  | flyctl ssh console --app "$FLY_APP" --machine "$LEERIE_MACHINE_ID" \
      --pty=false -C "sh -s"
```

The remote orchestrator never pushes, on any runtime: the push is the
host's, run inline by `decide_teardown` after stream-back (see *Run branch
stream-back* below) or — as a recovery path — via `leerie finalize
<run-id>` after reattach. So the machine gets no push flag of its own: it
receives the same `--no-push` a local container would (on a fresh run, when
the launcher resolved `NO_PUSH=true`; on a resume, only the resume's own
`--no-push` / `--push`), records the choice in `state.json.no_push`, gates
`pr_writer` on `not no_push`, and writes `run.json.no_push`, which the
stream-back brings home unchanged (DESIGN §6 *One push choice per run, on
every runtime*).

When the tail's ssh-console session ends (the orchestrator wrote its
final log line and exited, or the user pressed Ctrl-C, or the laptop
disconnected), the launcher's EXIT trap classifies the rc via
`decide_teardown` per the table above — **sync-then-destroy** for
clean terminal exits (rc=0/10/75: `_try_fetch_branch_for_teardown` runs
`fetch_branch` BEFORE `destroy_machine`; on sync failure leaves the
machine RUNNING for user recovery), **detach** for SIGINT/SIGTERM,
**pause** for other non-zero rc.

**Pre-classify resume — `resume` is host-only, task is recovered
from `task.txt`.** `leerie resume` on the host means "wake the paused
Fly machine"; the in-machine orchestrator interprets the same flag as
"resume state from disk." Since the run-id is the machine ID from the
start (DESIGN §6), the launcher always has a valid run-id at resume time.
If classify never ran (no `state.json` exists), the orchestrator's
`resume` branch needs a `task` positional, which is gone from the
user's resume argv. The launcher persists the user's original task
argument to `$LEERIE_STATE_HOST_DIR/runs/$LEERIE_RUN_ID/task.txt` on
first launch, and on pre-classify resume — when `LEERIE_TASK_ARG` is
empty in this invocation's argv — reads it back and appends to
`REWRITTEN_ARGS`. Both writes are idempotent (`! -f` and "no task in
argv" guards), so an explicit re-supplied task on the resume command
line wins. `task.txt` is launcher-side; the orchestrator never reads it.

The launcher's task extractor walks `$@` once at startup, skipping
the value of any `--flag` that takes one. The list of value-taking
flags (`_value_flags` literal in `leerie`) is source-coupled to the
orchestrator's argparse by `tests/test_launcher_value_flags_coupling.py`
— a value-taker added upstream that is not mirrored in the launcher
would silently misclassify its value as the task and persist the wrong
string. Per-worker `--model-<W>` / `--effort-<W>` overrides are matched
by prefix pattern (`--model-*` / `--effort-*`) rather than enumerated.

Maps to `DESIGN.md` §6 (container boundary / teardown / finalization)
and §6 *Remote execution* (the one-microVM-per-run model and the
host-as-the-only-credential-holder contract).

#### Repo seeding (`scripts/remote/seed-repo.sh`)

Two-phase bundle-then-rsync seeding: the host has the full repo, so
pack its committed state as a `git bundle` and pipe it to the
machine; the machine clones from the bundle on its local disk; the
host then rsync's the small dirty/untracked delta to fill in
uncommitted edits, untracked files, and forced-in `.claude/`. No
in-machine `git clone` from origin — Fly machines deliberately receive
no GitHub credentials (DESIGN §6 *Finalization*: the host pushes via
`leerie finalize`, not the machine).

**Phase 1: bundle clone (`seed_repo_clone`).**

1. **Parent repo bundle.** Host runs `git -C "$USER_REPO" bundle
   create - --all 2>/dev/null` and pipes the output stream straight to
   `flyctl ssh console --pty=false -C "sh -c 'cat > /tmp/leerie-seed.bundle'"`
   on the machine (`--all` packs every ref into one pack-format binary
   stream). The `sh -c '...'` wrapper is load-bearing — bare
   `-C "cat > /tmp/..."` is parsed by flyctl as if `>` were a `cat`
   argument and fails with `cat: invalid option -- 'c'`.

2. **Submodule bundles, recursive.** Host lists the submodules with
   `_seed_submodule_dirs` (NUL-terminated records, §0) and, for each,
   runs `git -C <dir> bundle create - --all | flyctl ssh console -C
   "sh -c 'cat > /tmp/leerie-subs/<bn>'"`, so each submodule's pack data
   lands as its own file on the machine. `<bn>` is
   `_seed_bundle_name <displaypath>`, the hex of the path's bytes and
   `.bundle`: a name of `[0-9a-f]` only is never shell syntax, and no two
   paths share one.

3. **Machine-side clone + submodule update.** A single
   `flyctl ssh console -C "bash -c '<script>'"` call:
   - `git clone /tmp/leerie-seed.bundle /work` (treats the bundle file
     like a remote; recreates `.git/` and checks out HEAD).
   - `_seed_machine_submodules /tmp/leerie-subs` (§0): for each
     submodule listed NUL-safely from `.gitmodules` whose bundle was
     sent, `git config submodule.<name>.url /tmp/leerie-subs/<bn>`
     (sets the URL in `.git/config`, NOT `.gitmodules` — the committed
     file is never modified), then
     `git --literal-pathspecs -c protocol.file.allow=always submodule
     update --init -- <path>` (clones it from its bundle file), then the
     same inside it for nested submodules. The
     `protocol.file.allow=always` flag is load-bearing — git 2.38+
     blocks the `file` protocol by default per CVE-2022-39253, which
     would otherwise abort with `fatal: transport 'file' not allowed`.
   - `chown -R leerie: /work` (orchestrator runs as leerie).
   - `rm -rf /tmp/leerie-seed.bundle /tmp/leerie-subs` (bundles served
     their purpose; tmpfs space reclaimed).

Before the clone runs, `/work` is emptied via `find /work -mindepth 1
-maxdepth 1 -exec rm -rf {} +`. Note the `find ... -exec rm` form
preserves the `/work` inode itself — a naive `rm -rf /work && mkdir
-p /work` would replace the inode and leave any process holding a
prior fd (the ssh-console shell, the orchestrator about to be
spawned) with a stale cwd, producing `getcwd: ENOENT` cascades.

**Why bundles instead of tar:** macOS BSD `tar -c` normalizes filenames
NFC → NFD when archiving, which desyncs a macOS-built git index (NFC)
from the Linux-written tree (NFD) and shows unicode filenames as
untracked + missing on the machine. Bundles avoid this — they store
pack-format binary objects, so filenames materialize natively on the
receiving Linux git from raw tree-object bytes with no transport-layer
normalization step.

**Phase 2: dirty delta (`seed_repo_dirty`).** Same call path as
`re-seed.sh` (Phase 4 mid-run re-rsync) but called automatically by
`seed_repo` immediately after the bundle clone succeeds. Computes the
dirty set from `git status --porcelain` on the host:
- Modified-but-uncommitted tracked files
- Untracked-not-ignored files
- Defensive filter drops `.git/*`, non-whitelisted `.leerie/*` paths, and worktree paths
  (`.leerie/runs/*/worktrees/*`) before handing the list to rsync; exception: `.leerie/config.toml`,
  `.leerie/Dockerfile`, `.leerie/.leerie-setup.sh` pass through
- Forced-in `.claude/` (workers need it, often gitignored) —
  enumerated via `find .claude -type f` host-side and appended to
  the dirty list before the defensive filter

The dirty set is rsync'd over `flyctl ssh console -C "rsync --server
..."` via `fly_rsync_wrapper` (lib.sh). NFC byte preservation is
free with rsync; the bundle path doesn't need it (filenames don't
transit), but the delta does.

The script is **sourced** (not exec'd) by the launcher — same
pattern as `provision.sh` — so `seed_repo()` runs in the launcher's
process after `provision_machine()` exports `$LEERIE_MACHINE_ID`.

Environment variables consumed by `seed-repo.sh`:

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `LEERIE_MACHINE_ID` | — | ID of the started Fly Machine (exported by `provision.sh`) |
| `LEERIE_FLY_APP` | — (required) | Fly.io app name. Fly app names are globally unique; set via `--fly-app` or env. |
| `USER_REPO` | — | Absolute path to the local git repo (set by launcher) |

Requires: `flyctl` on `PATH` (authenticated); `git`; `python3`; `rsync`.

#### Run branch stream-back (`scripts/remote/fetch-branch.sh`)

Stream-back path that makes the completed run available on the host
so the existing host-side finalize block can push it and open a PR.
Runs in two contexts:

- **Sync-before-destroy** (the load-bearing safety net):
  `decide_teardown`'s clean-exit branch sources `fetch-branch.sh`
  via `_try_fetch_branch_for_teardown` and runs `fetch_branch`
  BEFORE calling `destroy_machine`. On sync failure the machine is
  left RUNNING with `sync_failed_at` written to the sidecar.
- **`leerie finalize`** (user-driven recovery / re-attempt). The
  launcher's `finalize` handler also detects "already synced to
  host" state and short-circuits past `fetch_branch` entirely. Two
  flavors qualify: (a) **normal run** — `finished_at` set, state.json
  present, AND the run branch exists locally (auto-sync's `git
  bundle` step landed); (b) **no-work run (DESIGN §8)** —
  `finished_at` set, state.json present, `run.json.no_push=true`, and
  the run branch was NEVER materialized (so it cannot exist locally).
  In flavor (b), `host_finalize`'s `no_push` gate short-circuits
  the push cleanly; its rev-parse defense-in-depth guard backstops
  the case where `no_push` was lost upstream.

The mechanism is the same in both contexts:

1. **Discover the completed run** — scans `.leerie/runs/*/run.json`
   on the machine via a python -c snippet through
   `flyctl ssh console -C`. Picks the entry with `finished_at` set,
   no `pushed_at`, and the most recent mtime, then prints four lines
   on stdout: run_id, branch, working_branch, no_push.

   CRITICAL: stderr is captured to a separate tmpfile, NOT merged
   into stdout via `2>&1`. `flyctl ssh console` prints "Connecting
   to fdaa:..." to stderr; merging it would shift every parsed line
   by one, corrupting the discovered run_id and branch name.
   Downstream `git bundle create` would silently produce an empty
   bundle against a nonexistent branch.

   We do NOT use the `no_push` flag from `run.json` as a proxy for
   "no branch was materialized." A `--no-push` run has a run branch;
   `no_push=true` says only that the host does not push it.

3. **Run branch via git bundle** — `git -C /work bundle create -
   leerie/runs/<run-id>` on the machine, piped to a host tempfile,
   then fetched via `git fetch <bundle> +<branch>:<branch>` into
   the host repo. Resolves cleanly because both repos share the
   same origin history.

4. **Run state directory** — tars `/work/.leerie/runs/<run-id>`
   on the machine and extracts it under `$LEERIE_STATE_HOST_DIR/runs/`
   on the host, so `run.json` and `state.json` end up present exactly
   as after a local run.

5. **`run.json` arrives unchanged.** The stream-back never edits
   `run.json.no_push`, and `host_finalize` reads it as written on the
   machine. Its one writer, `_record_run_push_choice(st, choice)`, writes
   `choice or _run_has_nothing_to_push(st.data)` — `true` for a run whose
   `current_phase` carries `_finish_no_work_run`'s `done:` stamp (no run
   branch), whatever a later invocation's choice. `main()` (every
   non-`--phase` invocation), `phase_finalize` and `_finish_no_work_run`
   are its callers. `ec2-fetch-branch.sh` behaves the same.

The script is **sourced** (not exec'd) by the launcher and exports
`LEERIE_REMOTE_RUN_ID` on success (the discovered run-id, in case the caller
needs it for diagnostics).

Environment variables consumed by `fetch-branch.sh`:

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `LEERIE_MACHINE_ID` | — | ID of the started Fly Machine (exported by `provision.sh`) |
| `LEERIE_FLY_APP` | — (required) | Fly.io app name. Fly app names are globally unique; set via `--fly-app` or env. |
| `USER_REPO` | — | Absolute path to the local git repo (set by launcher) |

Exports: `LEERIE_REMOTE_RUN_ID` — the run-id of the completed run on the machine.

Requires: `flyctl` on `PATH` (authenticated); `git`; `tar`; `python3` (on the machine — always present in the leerie image).

Maps to `DESIGN.md`: §6 *Finalization* (remote-finalize stream-back variant).

#### Smart resume (`leerie resume`)

`leerie resume [<run-id>] [--shell] [--auto-finalize]
[--app <app>] [--runtime fly]` re-engages with a remote run regardless
of state. The launcher routes by observation:

| Machine state | Orchestrator state | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Stopped (paused) | n/a | Wake via `resume_machine` → re-seed → launch orchestrator → tail |
| Running | Dead | (Re-)seed if needed → launch orchestrator → tail |
| Running | Alive | Skip seed + launch → attach: tail orchestrator.log (default) or open bash shell (`--shell`) |

The "alive orchestrator" case is detected by a two-layered flock probe.
**Early probe (resume path only):** on the `_resumed=true` path, the
launcher runs a lightweight Python flock snippet via `flyctl ssh console`
immediately after `resume_machine` — before `seed_auth`. rc=75 (lock
held) skips `seed_auth`/`re_seed`/launch entirely, pivoting straight to
`_attach_to_live_orchestrator` (lib.sh) — SSH readiness is not a concern
since an alive orchestrator means the machine was never stopped and
hallpass is already warm; any other rc falls through to `seed_auth`.
**Launch-time probe (belt-and-suspenders):** the in-machine Python
launch wrapper takes its own fast-path flock probe (DESIGN §6 *Single
owner per run dir*) and exits 75 when the lock is held, covering fresh
provisions and any race the early probe missed. `flyctl ssh console`
doesn't forward remote exit codes, so the launcher parses the real code
from stderr via `_extract_flyctl_remote_rc`. Both probes pivot via
`_attach_to_live_orchestrator`: `tail_with_optional_autofinalize()`
(default) or a `flyctl ssh console` bash payload (`--shell`), and set
`container_rc=130` so `decide_teardown` leaves the machine alone. The
attach transport is `flyctl ssh console` proxied through Fly's
hallpass + WireGuard mesh — no sshd, no key management, no public
exposure. Auth inherits from `flyctl auth status`.

Run-id resolution:

1. `leerie resume <id>` → look up
   `$LEERIE_STATE_HOST_DIR/runs/<id>/fly-machine.json` first, then
