A replacing rewrite moves it to `rewrite.original.operator_accepted`. An invalid set from the writer's own-start retry whose defect files all still pass carries `reason: "fixed_on_head_by_execution"`. `{"skipped": reason}` when the run is not a defect fix (no `bug-fixing` category), there is no scoped test command (also `skip_kind: "no_scoped_runner"`, `reason`, `test_command`), `--skip-acceptance-check` is set, or writing raised anything but a budget-exhaustion `WorkerError` (which stops the run). `gate` is `{initial[], initial_sha?, rounds[{round, results?, sha?, error?, retried?, pre_sha?, fixed_cases?, ratchet?, rollback_reason?, rolled_back?, rollback_failed?, flip_regressed?}], round_pre?{round, sha}, test_ids?{sha: {ids[], files{}, kind, messages{}, command} | {unmeasured: true}}, final[], final_sha?, before_sha?, pre_tests_passed?, post_tests_confirm?, residual?, rolled_back?, rollback_reason?, rollback_failed?, final_unremeasured?{sha, label}, conformer_flip?{start_sha, end_sha, broken_cases[], culprit_round?, rollback_to?, rolled_back?, rollback_failed?}, item_flips?[{round, rollback_to, from_sha, culprits[], reason, notes[], landed, rollback_failed?}], item_flip_checked?}` (`conformer_flip`: `_conformer_flip_check`'s decision, saved before its reset; `item_flips`: each `_acceptance_item_flips` decision, saved before its reset, `landed` None until the reset ran; `item_flip_checked`: the HEAD on which that check last found no flip) (`final_unremeasured` written by `_acceptance_remeasure_final` when re-measuring `sha` measured no set, so `final` stays of `final_sha`; dropped when a re-measure succeeds) (`round_pre` the in-flight round's own start, saved before its worker runs and dropped when the round is recorded; a round's `pre_sha` is that start, `fixed_cases` `_acceptance_fixed_cases(verdict before, its verdict)`, `ratchet` the round's `_delivery_ratchet` result (or `{error}`), `test_ids` the test axis's failing IDs per measured commit, and `rollback_reason: "fixed no failing case"` | `"regressed a previously met required item"` | `"broke an existing test"` | an `_acceptance_item_flips` reason (with `flip_regressed[]` on the culprit round) marks a round reset to `pre_sha` — `rolled_back` the confirmed reset, absent while the decision is on disk but the reset not yet done, which a resume finishes; `_acceptance_round_kept` skips such a round wherever the latest or last measured verdict is read) (`initial` persisted before any repair; `initial_sha`/`rounds[].sha` the commit each verdict was measured on, `final_sha` the staging HEAD when `final` was written — rewritten with `final` by the delivery re-drive, and by `_acceptance_remeasure_final` when a resumed gate finds `final` of another commit than staging's HEAD: the sets are measured again on HEAD with no repair round, and the gate otherwise skips only while `final_sha` is HEAD — absent from a state saved before they existed, which then always counts as moved), each result `{index, passed, unmeasured, failing_files[], failing_cases?{file: [case ids]}, resource_affected_files?[], intermittent_cases?{file: [held case ids]}, budget_short_files?[], budget_short_unsettled_files?[], no_case_evidence_files?[], discovery?, unmeasured_reason?, unmeasured_files?{file: reason}}` (`failing_files` confirmed under B*; on an unmeasured result, `unmeasured_reason` a whole-set cause and `unmeasured_files` the per-file causes, both codes of `ACCEPTANCE_UNMEASURED_WHY`; `failing_cases` the runner report's failing case IDs per confirmed failing file, where one was readable); `residual` `{failing_sets, held_back_failing_sets, total_sets, cases[], sets[], cases_by_set{index: [names]}, files_by_set{index: [failing files]}, failing_cases_by_set{index: {file: [case ids]}}, intermittent?[set indices whose failure is a held case seen failing only with resource signatures], unmeasured_final?, rollback_failed?}` — from the last MEASURED verdict when the final one measured nothing (`unmeasured_final: true`, forwarded to the planner) — feeds the next same-task run via `_prior_delivery_residual` as `acceptance_unmet`, after `_acceptance_residual_unbroken` drops the sets typed broken, and the variant sets (no counted case among their `files_by_set` files), at read time (None when none is left and no rollback failed; a residual without `sets` is used with `cases` emptied). `cases` and `cases_by_set` hold the shown sets' declared names only (`_acceptance_shown_indices(sets)`), a failing held-back set counted in `held_back_failing_sets`; `_acceptance_residual_unbroken` re-derives `cases` (and `held_back_failing_sets`) from the shown sets at read time, and only `cases` is handed on (`cases_by_set` is copied unchanged), so a residual recorded before that rule hands on no held-back name, and `acceptance_unmet` carries `held_back_failing_sets` beside `cases` (DESIGN §8 *Nothing a held-out evaluation produces reaches a fixer*). Presence of the key is the write half's resume checkpoint (skipped when `plans_after_plan` is present, like `defect_scope`); `gate.final` is the gate half's sentinel. |
| `skip_acceptance_check` | bool | whether the held-out acceptance sets and gate are suppressed. Resolved from `--skip-acceptance-check` / `LEERIE_SKIP_ACCEPTANCE_CHECK` / default `False`; seeded in both the fresh and resume branches. |
| `no_work_pending` | bool | set by `_confirm_no_work_on_converged_gate` when the `no_work_judge` confirms and `_acceptance_can_check(st)` holds (acceptance not skipped, `bug-fixing` category, a scoped test template): the confirmation is held instead of finishing, and `_settle_pending_no_work` decides it after `phase_acceptance_write` (DESIGN §8 *No work is declared on executed evidence, and a dispute is bounded*). Cleared on a dispute. |
| `no_work_acceptance` | dict | `_settle_pending_no_work`'s verdict, or `_settled_bar_settles_run`'s when the bar settled it first: `{verdict: pass \| dispute \| accepted after dispute \| fixed_on_head_by_execution \| no valid sets \| not measurable \| error: <type> \| settled_bar_holds \| settled_bar_regressed, results?, cases?, discarded?, advisory?}` — `fixed_on_head_by_execution` (an executed basis, with `discarded` copied from `acceptance.discarded`) when there is no valid set, `acceptance.written` ≥ 1 and every one of the `written` sets is in `acceptance.discarded` with that reason; its presence is the settle step's resume sentinel. |
| `acceptance_dispute` | dict | `{failing_sets, total_sets, cases[], accepted?, unacted?, redispute?}` written when held-out sets fail on HEAD — as a new dispute when the previous completed same-task run had NOT already disputed, and again with `accepted: true` when it had (the carry-forward); `_prior_acceptance_dispute` reads it from that sibling on the next run, which then accepts no work instead of disputing again. `unacted: true` is set by `_mark_dispute_unacted` when the disputing run still ended as no work by another exit (empty plans, or the satisfied-probe sweep emptying the plan); `_prior_acceptance_dispute` does not count such a dispute unless it also carries `redispute: true` — written when the dispute was raised because the previous run's dispute was unacted (`_prior_acceptance_dispute_record`), so a second unacted dispute counts and the wrong-tests loop stays bounded at two extra runs (DESIGN §8 *A dispute counts only once it is acted on*). |
| `declared_unrun_warnings` | dict | per-sid list of `DECLARED_CMD_UNRUN` issues on an `empty_handoff`-rescued subtask that settled `complete` without running them. No longer written — such a rescue is now settled by execution or re-driven (DESIGN §8 *Settled by execution*) — but still read by `phase_finalize`, so a run recorded before the change keeps surfacing it. |
| `settled_by_execution` | dict[str, dict] | per-sid record of `_settle_by_execution` (DESIGN §8 *Settled by execution*): `{verdict, why, commands: [{argv, rc, attempts, passed, resource_affected, environment_limit, tail}], dirty, removed_untracked?, forbidden?}` (`forbidden[{argv, forbidden}]` only when a verify argv runs a command the task forbids — then nothing ran), written on every execution whatever the verdict; `no_op: true` when `_settle_nothing_to_change` ran it for a no-op claim (the one-re-drive rule). |
| `ci_parity` | dict \| absent | CI parity (DESIGN §9 *The repository's own merge checks run too*), written by `_capture_ci_parity_baseline` and `_run_ci_parity_final`: `{baseline_done, config_files[], excluded_by_worker[], skipped?, base_sha, checks[], final?}`. Each check `{id, kind, argv, cwd, env, prerequisites, trigger, requires, strict_argv, source, coverage, selected, reason?, problems?, duplicate_of?, strict_from?, forbidden?, strict_forbidden?, strict_problems?, gate?: plain \| strict, ratchet?: diagnostic \| coverage, base?{rc, dirty, strict_rc?, diagnostics?{"file\ttext": count}, coverage?{"glob\|metric": pct}}}`; `reason` one of `left_to_test_axis`, `not_merge_gating`, `external_resource`, `db_reset`, `forbidden_by_task` (with `forbidden`, the entry the argv hits), `provenance` (with `problems`), `duplicate` (with `duplicate_of`, the id of the selected check that runs the same thing — `_ci_run_key`), `no_base_worktree`, `writes_tracked_files`, `red_at_baseline`, `coverage_unmeasured`; `strict_forbidden` is the entry a selected check's `strict_argv` hit, and `strict_problems` the `_ci_strict_problems` of one that failed provenance (that `strict_argv` then `null`; the check stays selected). `final` `{sha, results{id: {...}}, unmet[{id, kind, why: red \| new_diagnostics \| coverage_ratchet, argv, cwd, rc? \| diagnostics? \| thresholds?}], resource_affected[], pre_existing[], no_verdict[], budget_short_unsettled[], sized_out?[], b_star?, skipped?}, reused?}` (`reused`: the label of the kept measurement it was read from). `measured` `{<commit sha>: {label, results{id: raw}}}` — `_ci_measure`'s raw results per commit, the last `_CI_MEASURED_KEEP`, written by `_ci_remember` from the final pass and `_ci_round_regressions`. `baseline_done` is the baseline's resume sentinel; `final.sha` equal to the staging HEAD is the final half's. `browser_suite` (present only when `_browser_suite_candidate` found one, DESIGN §8 *A repository's browser suite is a channel the run provisions*): `{check_id, argv, runner, template, env[{name, value}], prerequisites[], requires[], source, viable, base{rc, timed_out, passed, failed, skipped, load_error, why?} | {why}}`, written by `_establish_browser_suite` before `ci_parity` is saved; `_browser_suite(st)` returns it only when `viable`. |
| `blt_peak` | dict \| absent | the base-health baseline's measured peak (DESIGN §6 *The repo's own build peak*): `{memory_bytes, pids, axis, slots, worker_memory_max_bytes, worker_pids_max}` — the largest `memory.peak` / `pids.peak` across the measured axes, the host build-semaphore slot count sized from it, and the raised caps `_apply_blt_peak` applied. Re-applied on resume. |
| `answers` | dict[str, str] | user answers to classifier questions (and source-of-truth) |
| `artifact_registry` | list[dict] | shared artifact vocabulary (DESIGN §5 *Artifact-registry worker*). |
| `needs_source_of_truth` | bool | whether classifier asked for source-of-truth disambiguation. |
| `source_of_truth_pref` | str | resolved preference (`codebase` / `research` / `both`) |
| `clarify` | bool | whether asking the user is allowed for this run (resolved from `--clarify` / `LEERIE_CLARIFY` / `leerie.toml` / default `False`) |
| `dangerously_skip_permissions` | bool | the operator's tooling escape hatch. Resolved from `--dangerously-skip-permissions` / `LEERIE_DANGEROUSLY_SKIP_PERMISSIONS` / default `False`. |
| `dangerously_force_strict_output` | bool | whether this run forced constrained decoding via the per-run loopback proxy (`--dangerously-force-strict-output` / `LEERIE_DANGEROUSLY_FORCE_STRICT_OUTPUT`). |
| `skip_overlap_judge` | bool | whether the phase 2¾ `plan_overlap_judge` worker is suppressed even on multi-planner runs (DESIGN §5 *Cross-domain surface overlap*). |
| `skip_adherence_check` | bool | whether the instruction-adherence gate (the deterministic prescribed-command-coverage floor + the `adherence_judge` worker in the planner check loop) is suppressed. |
| `skip_coverage_check` | bool | whether required-items checking is suppressed — one flag governs every side: the planner-loop item accounting (`_check_item_claims`), the phase 2⅞½ task-coverage gate (its item accounting and its single advisory `task_coverage_judge` invocation; the deterministic `check_required_items_coverage` floor it used to compose with was deleted) and the phase 5 delivery gate (`_run_delivery_prejudge`/`_run_delivery_recheck` — DESIGN §8 *The delivery gate*). |
| `skip_completeness_check` | bool | whether the conformer's gating `solution_defects` completeness axis (DESIGN §9 *The one gating axis: solution completeness*) is demoted to advisory. |
| `skip_integration_check` | bool | whether `integrate_wave`'s `integration_judge` behavioral-defect gate (DESIGN §8 *Independent adversarial verification*) is suppressed entirely — no worker spawn for any subtask in this run. |
| `skip_budget_check` | bool | whether `check_budget_feasibility()` (DESIGN §13 *Budget feasibility — fail fast at the cheapest moment*) is suppressed. Resolved from `--skip-budget-check` / `LEERIE_SKIP_BUDGET_CHECK` / default `False`. |
| `skip_classification_check` | bool | whether `phase_classification_gate` (DESIGN §8 *Independent adversarial verification*) is suppressed. Resolved from `--skip-classification-check` / `LEERIE_SKIP_CLASSIFICATION_CHECK` / default `False`. |
| `stop_on_blocked` | bool | whether a subtask still blocked after its re-drives from the shared budget halts the run instead of being settled `unconverged`. Resolved from `--stop-on-blocked` / `LEERIE_STOP_ON_BLOCKED` / `leerie.toml` / default `False`. |
| `stop_on_repo_change` | bool | whether a change to the real checkout halts the run (`_assert_repo_unchanged` die()s, and the execute-wave check also compares HEAD and refs) instead of being logged as a WARNING. Resolved from `--stop-on-repo-change` / `LEERIE_STOP_ON_REPO_CHANGE` / `leerie.toml` / default `False`. |
| `repo_change_warned` | dict[str, str] | `{delta: fingerprint}` for every `_diff_repo_state` delta `_assert_repo_unchanged` has already warned about (fingerprint from `_delta_fingerprint`). A delta that persists across later phases and waves (the baseline is never refreshed) is warned once; it re-warns, marked `(changed again)`, only when its fingerprint changes, so a later write to an already-warned path is not hidden. Absent until the first warning. A `list[str]` written by an earlier build of this feature is converted in place to `{delta: current fingerprint}` (those deltas were already warned, so they stay quiet). |
| `skip_satisfied_check` | bool | whether `_filter_satisfied_subtasks()` (DESIGN §8 *Already-satisfied subtask elimination*) is suppressed. Resolved from `--skip-satisfied-check` / `LEERIE_SKIP_SATISFIED_CHECK` / default `False`. |
| `strict_conformer` | bool | whether the conformer phase is blocking instead of advisory (DESIGN §9 *Post-work conformance*, "Opt-in strict mode" paragraph). Resolved from `--strict-conformer` / `LEERIE_STRICT_CONFORMER` / `leerie.toml` / default `False`. |
| `test_ledger` | dict[str, dict] | test file → `{tree, passed}`: the tree each file's result on the tree that ships was last measured on (`_test_ledger`, DESIGN §8 *What ships is what was measured, once per change that can affect it*). |
| `subtask_tests` | str | How much of the repo's suite each per-subtask conformance round measures (DESIGN §9 *Per-subtask scope: a delta proxy, not the suite*). |
| `skip_base_baseline` | bool | whether the base-tree health baseline (DESIGN §9 *Base-tree health baseline*) is suppressed. Resolved from `--skip-base-baseline` / `LEERIE_SKIP_BASE_BASELINE` / default `False`. |
| `skip_repo_map` | bool | whether the P6 repo-map structural context (DESIGN §5½ (P6) *Codebase structural map*) is suppressed. Resolved from `--skip-repo-map` / `LEERIE_SKIP_REPO_MAP` / `skip_repo_map` in `leerie.toml` / default `False`. |
| `no_push` | bool | the orchestrator's resolved `--no-push` (after `--push`), a sticky run choice (§2½ *Run choices on resume*), the same on every runtime; `_record_run_push_choice` derives `run.json.no_push`, the record the host reads, from it (`true` regardless while the run has nothing to push). |
| `pr_template` | str \| None | the resolved `--pr-template` / `LEERIE_PR_TEMPLATE` / `pr_template` in `leerie.toml`; None means the discovery default. A sticky run choice. |
| `run_caps` | dict[str, int] | the sticky caps, keyed as in `DEFAULT_CAPS` — exactly the keys of `RUN_CAPS_STICKY` (`max_total_workers`, `confidence_rounds`, `planner_samples`, `judgment_check_rounds`, `planner_check_rounds`, `implementer_confidence_retries`). Continued per entry on `resume`. |
| `models` | dict[str, str] | `resolve_models`' result, per worker, as the run uses it. Continued per entry on `resume`. |
| `efforts` | dict[str, str \| None] | `resolve_efforts`' result, per worker. Continued per entry on `resume`. |
| `run_choice_overrides` | list[dict] | one `{choice, recorded, now, at}` per sticky choice a `resume`'s command line changed (`choice` is `<key>` or `<key>.<entry>`), appended by `main()` in order. |
| `cgroup_containment` | dict | recorded by the fail-closed gate (`_enforce_and_record_cgroup_containment`, in `_run_phases` just before the first worker spawns) (DESIGN §6 *Memory containment*): `{enforced: bool, hierarchy: "v2"\|"v1"\|null}`. |
| `verbosity` | str | resolved verbosity level (`quiet` / `normal` / `stream` / `debug`); re-resolved fresh on every run, including `resume`, so the user can dial up or down without editing state |
| `inspect_dirs` | list[str] | extra absolute paths granted to inspect-bucket workers (classifier, planner, reconciler, plan_overlap_judge, provision) via `--add-dir`. |
| `integrator_warnings` | dict[str, str] | non-fatal commit warnings from `integrate_wave` (non-fatal signal log) |
| `scope_warnings` | dict[str, dict] | oversized-diff warnings from `check_diff_scope` (non-fatal signal log) |
| `under_scope_warnings` | dict[str, dict] | `{touched, declared, reason}` per subtask that committed work but touched **none** of its `files_likely_touched`, from `check_diff_scope` (non-fatal signal log; DESIGN §9 *Scope is checked in both directions*). Comparison via `_declared_path_covers` — component-wise, absorbs a repo-root prefix on either side, and a directory-shaped declaration covers files beneath it. |
| `conformance` | dict[str, dict] | per-subtask conformer output and `conformance_warnings` (non-fatal signal log). `conformance["_final"] = {result, warnings, blocked, tree_sha, round_starts[], end_sha, residual_defects?[]}` (`round_starts`: each round's starting HEAD; `end_sha`: staging's HEAD after the pass — read by `_conformer_flip_check`) is the final-tree pass's record (`residual_defects`: the actionable solution defects still unfixed after the last round — re-drive notes and an `unconverged` reason, never a stop) and its resume sentinel: `_run_final_conformance` skips on resume only when `_final` is present with `blocked` false (or absent — an orchestrator-exception record), and runs again when `blocked` is true (DESIGN §9, final-tree pass). |
| `blt_results` | dict[str, dict] | Per-run memo of orchestrator-measured build/lint/test verdicts (DESIGN §9). |
| `unreviewed_subtasks` | list[str] | subtask ids whose conformer produced no result at all (worker crash, or the 5400 s timeout), so a subtask that was never reviewed is distinguishable from one that passed. |
| `symptom_findings` | dict[str, list[str]] | subtask id -> `check_symptom_evidence` findings, for subtasks whose plan entry declares `fixes_reported_symptom: true` (NOT those whose id begins `bugfix-`: ids are re-homed by plan merges and synthesised for verification-only work, so the prefix is not evidence a symptom exists) (DESIGN §9 *A stale finding is not a bug*). |
| `risk_register` | dict[str, list[dict]] | subtask id -> `_collect_subtask_risks` entries after `_verify_risk_paths` (`{kind, detail, where?, source, gap, where_paths[], where_paths_unverified?, settle_by?, resource?, simulated_interleaving?, disposition?, addressed}`): every worker self-reported risk (typed `self_reported_risks`, `process_note` excluded, plus the `production_evidence.exercised == false` tier, typed `unverified_external` with its `resource` only when it names `unexercisable_resource`, else `test_missing`); entries the conformer's `risk_dispositions` cleared through a verifiable act carry `addressed: true` and the rest stay unaddressed (DESIGN §9 *Self-reported risk is routed, not read*). Set and popped on the same settle path as `symptom_findings`. Routed by `gap`: `unverified_external` with a non-empty `resource` (or `simulated_interleaving`) to the PR's "Needs human verification", grouped by that resource (an `unverified_external` entry stored with none, by an older leerie, is not rendered); `test_missing` / `test_weak` to the coverage re-drive. Also carries `integration_content_loss` entries (`_record_integration_loss`), rendered under the PR's "Integration content loss". |
| `coverage_redrive` | dict[str, dict] | per-sid coverage re-drive record (`_redrive_uncovered_subtasks`, DESIGN §9 *Changed lines no test executes are re-driven*): `{rounds[{round, share, uncovered, gaps_open, pre_sha}], last, final, uncovered, open_gaps?, rolled_back?{status, reason}}`; `last` is the latest `_measure_subtask_coverage` record plus its `gaps`; `final` `covered` / `untested` / `rolled_back` / `unmeasured`, set once (the resume skip). |
| `existing_behaviour` | dict | the existing tests the run changed, run in their base form on the tree that ships (`_check_existing_behaviour`, DESIGN §8 *What an existing test pins on the base holds on the tree that ships*): `{tree_sha, base, before, after, files[], unsupported[], changed: [{id, file, message}], moved_literal?{id: [{literal, kind, ci, file, message_file, key}]}, causes?{id: [cause]}, run_form?{id: "" \| why}, cause_open?{id: [qid]}, cause_unkept?{id: why}, literal_restored?[{literal, file, qid}], task_required?[{id, file, message, item_index, probe_test_file, quote} \| {id, file, message, cause[], qids[]}], unmeasured[], unsettled[], verdict, unmeasured_reason?, error?}`. `task_required`: the `changed` rows whose case `_redrive_task_required_cases(delivery_redrive)` names, moved there by `_existing_behaviour_task_required(st, rec) -> bool` (on a fresh measurement before it is stored, and on a reused one, saved when any moved), `quote` the verdict's `quotes.independent`; `_pr_tracked_test_lines` lists each first under its file as "- existing test changed because required item <i> contradicts it: `<id>` — the item's probe `<file>` asserts `<quote>`", and nothing counts it. `changed` makes the run `unconverged` (`_decide_outcome`); `error`, `unmeasured` or another tree is a reason of `_unmeasured_on_shipping_tree`. |
| `tracked_test_report` | dict | existing tests the run changed (`_tracked_test_report`, DESIGN §8 *Existing tests the run changed are listed in the PR*): `{files: [{file, deleted?, removed[], cases_removed[], added[], cases_added[], skips_added?, lines_removed?, lines_added?, omitted?}], files_omitted}`, stored once at `phase_finalize` (base to final tree), report-only; rendered by `_pr_tracked_test_lines` under `## Existing tests changed by this run`. Lists are source-ordered and bounded by `_TRACKED_TEST_ITEMS_MAX` / `_TRACKED_TEST_FILES_MAX`; the PR shows at most `_PR_TRACKED_TEST_SHOWN` entries and counts the rest. |
| `settled_heads` | dict[str, str] | per-sid subtask branch tip at the moment the subtask settled `complete` (`_record_settled_head`, DESIGN §6 *Integrated means the settled commit is on the run branch*); `integrate_wave` requires it to be an ancestor of staging after the merge; reset to the round's `pre_sha` by `_undo_interrupted_redrives`. |
| `redrive_in_flight` | dict[str, dict] | per-sid write-ahead marker of a wave-end re-drive round on the subtask's branch (`_mark_redrive_in_flight`, DESIGN §6 *A re-drive interrupted mid-round is undone, never integrated*): `{kind: "coverage" \| "blocked", pre_sha, round, status}`, saved before the round's settle and dropped once it is decided; a resume rolls the branch back to `pre_sha` and restores `status` (`_undo_interrupted_redrives`). |
| `integration_unjudged` | dict[str, str] | per-sid write-ahead marker of an integrator merge not yet judged (`_mark_integration_unjudged`, DESIGN §6 *A committed resolution is not a judged one*): the merge's first parent, saved before the integrator is spawned and dropped once the integration is decided (`_clear_integration_unjudged`); a resume that finds it with no `integration_gate[sid]` and the sid merged runs the integration gate on the committed merge. |
| `delivery_ratchet` | dict \| absent | the delivery ratchet's run-wide record (DESIGN §8 *A repair that regresses met work is rolled back*): `{verifiability?{item_index: in_tree \| execution}, evidence?{item_index: {sha, evidence}}, intermittent_regression?[], unverified?{item_index: {sha, label}}}` (`unverified`: items a failed ratchet did not read on the commit it kept, `_ratchet_mark_unverified`) — `verifiability` the cached `verifiability_classifier` result (`_ratchet_verifiability`); `evidence` the met evidence each kept repair's ratchet judge gave, the next ratchet's prior evidence; `intermittent_regression` the rows kept repairs typed, read by `_intermittent_regression_rows` after `test_id_diff`'s (evidence only). Per-repair verdicts live on `acceptance.gate.rounds[].ratchet` and `delivery_redrive.rounds[].groups[].ratchet`. |
| `round_rollbacks` | list[dict] \| absent | every worker round rolled back (`_record_round_rollback`, DESIGN §8 *A rollback says why*): `[{site, worker, label, reason, pre_sha, post_sha, rolled_back}]`; `rolled_back` false when the reset did not land. |
| `delivery_redrive` | dict \| absent | the delivery re-drive record (`_run_delivery_redrive`, DESIGN §8 *Delivery re-drive*): `{start_sha, rounds[{round, held_mode, groups[{group, members[], notes[kinds], skipped?, escalated?, pre_sha?, post_sha?, implementer?{status?, summary?, error?}, fixed[], broke[], ctl_new[], new_failures[], resource_affected[] (B\* mixed evidence only), pre_existing[], unmeasured[] (a set or the test IDs with no verdict, and B\* `no_verdict` IDs), selfcheck_calls?[{args[], subset[], name_filter, rc, secs_total}] (the group's self-check calls, first 50), unclean_tree?[] (the porcelain lines a group's implementer left past `clean_tree_reasks`; the group is then `rolled_back`), rollback_reason? (why a group was rolled back, in words: `_redrive_rollback_reason`, or the unclean tree), committed_staged[] (shown set paths a commit names — `git log --name-only -m pre..post` — and paths whose committed blob holds a span of a shown set's source — `_history_heldout_hits`), worse?, zero_progress?, trade?, gate?{void, weakened[], schema[], ast[] \| null}, intermittent_regression?[], ratchet?, ratchet_regressed?[], base_form_fixed?[case IDs], test_closure_breach?[paths in words], dropped_cases?[case IDs], items_driven[item indices a group drove], items_budget_skipped[item indices a group held with no member left a re-drive round], evidence_handed["<item index>:<evidence key>" a driven group's notes carried, `_redrive_evidence_keys`], unrouted_items?[{item_index, item, reason: no_owner | budget | unreproducible | no_code_target | after_last_round, probed?}] (at the end, `_redrive_unrouted_items(open_items, handed, budget_skipped, stopped_on_budget, seen=None)` over `_redrive_open_evidence(unmet_final, n_items, rows, notes, records, *, contested=())` — per still-open note or record `{item_index, item, keys, drivable, reason, probed}`: `keys` every evidence key of the item, `drivable` its note's `evidence_keys`, `reason` a record's own, else `unreproducible` when a key outside the note is a falsifier's and the note has no `probe`, else `no_code_target` for a `process` note, else `unreproducible`; `probed` the record's, or `_redrive_probed(row)` when `unreproducible` — in item order: an item with every key in `handed` (`evidence_handed`) is not listed; else, when a missing key is `drivable`, `budget` if the item is in `budget_skipped` or `stopped_on_budget`, else `after_last_round` if `seen` is not None and a missing drivable key is not in it, else `no_owner`; else the entry's `reason`, with `probed` when `unreproducible`; read by `_decide_outcome`'s reasons — one line naming every unrouted item and reason, then per item: `unreproducible`, that a confirmed falsifier probe of the item's words `probed` fails under B\* and the probe is held-out content no fixer could see, so no re-drive round was spent on it, or, for an item in `items_driven`, so no re-drive worker was handed it (the item's other evidence was driven); `no_code_target`, "item <i> is a constraint over the whole change whose unmet evidence names no code a subtask changed, so no re-drive worker could be handed it"; `after_last_round`, "item <i>'s unmet evidence was confirmed on the tree that ships after the re-drive's last round, so no re-drive worker was handed it"; any other reason for an item in `items_driven`, "item <i> was driven on earlier evidence; its latest confirmed evidence reached no re-drive worker (<reason>)" — and `_prior_delivery_residual`'s `unrouted_items`), kept_unsettled?[], probes_after?{"<item>": pass \| fail \| unmeasured} (`_redrive_probe_verdicts`), probe_conflict?{items[], tests[{id, file}]} (`_redrive_pinned_breaks`), probe_objections?[] (`_redrive_probe_objections`), flip_regressed?[{item_index, round, group, pre_sha, post_sha, case_id, probe_saved{dir, file}, b_star}] (`_redrive_flip_culprit`: a met item's confirmed probe passed on the group's start and failed on its commit under B\*, read after the last round; the group is then `rolled_back`), defects_closed?[] (`solution_defect` keys an earlier kept group drove, not handed on), defects_driven?[] (the `solution_defect` keys the group was handed, when it was not rolled back), rolled_back?, rollback_failed?}]}], pending_controls[], trade_pairs[[fixed, broken]], contradiction_verdicts[] (every `_contradiction_verdict`, DESIGN §8 *Delivery re-drive* rule 4; a group's `task_required?[{id, item_index}]` names the pinned cases it broke that every one settled `exclusive`), contested_probes[{item_index, probe_test_file, tests[{id, file}], round, group}] (a measured conflict: a group's commit made the probe pass and broke a case an existing test pins; the item is passed to `_redrive_item_notes(contested=)`, so its probe is never handed on again; `_decide_outcome` adds, per still-unmet item, `_redrive_contest_text` of its first record — "item <i>: its falsifier probe <file> conflicts with existing tests — the re-drive change that made it pass (round <r>, group <g>) broke <n> case(s) they pin: <ids> …; the change was rolled back and the probe is not driven again — a person decides; the item stays unmet" — and `_collect_unmet_evidence` its `conflicts_with`), probe_objections[{item_index, probe_test_file, kind, reason, round, group}] (every kept objection, unverified; `_decide_outcome` adds, per still-unmet item, `_redrive_objection_text` of each of its first 3 — "item <i>: a re-drive fixer objected to its falsifier probe <file> (<kind>): "<reason>" — its own words, not verified by leerie; it exempts nothing" — and `_collect_unmet_evidence` its `objections`), held_round_done?, flip_rollbacks?[{group, pre_sha, items[], landed}] (each reset a flip caused: staging back to the earliest culprit group's `pre_sha`), conflict?{pairs[], round, reason}, contradictions[{fixed, tracked_test, file, round}], defects_driven?[keys of `conformance._final.residual_defects` driven by a group that was not rolled back: a group not rolled back adds the `solution_defect` keys it was handed, also recorded as its own `defects_driven[]`; a flip's rollback (`roll_back_flips`) then drops, through `_redrive_defects_unkept(rec)`, every key a now rolled-back group's `defects_driven` names and no group still not rolled back does], base_form_open[`_redrive_base_form_notes`], base_form_driven{key: {file, cases[], fixed[], outcome, attempts[{round, group, cases[], escalation, model, effort, outcome: interrupted | kept | no_change | rolled_back | rollback_failed, fixed[], reason?}]}}, kept_unsettled?[{group, ids[], sized_out[], files{id: file}, unchecked_items[]}] (a kept group's `budget_short_unsettled` candidates and its ratchet's `exec_unchecked` items, listed by `_set_redrive_unsettled_gap`), items_rechecked_sha?, in_flight?{pre_sha, round, group}, rollback_failed?, final_sha?, done}` (`rollback_failed`: a group's reset did not land; the re-drive stopped with its commits on staging); `done` is the resume sentinel; `conflict.reason` is `_decide_outcome`'s reason verbatim. |
| `provision` | dict | output of `phase_provision` (DESIGN §6½), plus `gate` (`skipped` \| `degraded` \| `passed`, `_record_provision_gate`) once `phase_provision_gate` has a result. `_run_phases` runs both after the `plans_after_classify` block, keyed on `recipe` and on `gate` (DESIGN §6 *Resumable planning*). |
| `external_preconditions` | list[dict] | planner-declared `extent: external` `requires` entries collected during `phase_reconcile` (DESIGN §5 `requires.extent`). Each item is `{tag, reasons: [{sid, reason}, …], originating_subtasks: [sid, …]}`, deduped by tag. |
| `dropped_subtasks` | dict[str, dict] | subtasks soft-dropped pre-schedule, and subtasks settled `complete` without a diff (`_settle_already_satisfied`). A no-diff settle's `reason` is one of `already_satisfied_pre_spawn`, `settled_by_execution`, `satisfied_by_sibling` (`satisfied_by: [{sid, commit, files}]`, `executed?`; §*Sibling-delivered no-op*) or `satisfied_on_base` (`executed?`, `claimed_locations?`). |
| `provider_subset_sids` | list[str] | sids flagged at plan time by `_warn_provider_subset_subtasks()` — every file in the subtask's `files_likely_touched` is already owned by an ordered predecessor it depends on (DESIGN §5 *Provider-subset subtasks*). |
| `conditional_drops` | dict[str, dict] | planner-emitted consumer subtasks dropped by the reconciler's `conditional_drop` resolution op (DESIGN §5) — i.e. the planner authored the subtask as "no-op if X" and X turned out to be unresolvable. |
| `external_twin_demotions` | list[dict] | `unresolvable` entries rescued by `_demote_unresolvable_with_external_twin` (DESIGN §5 *The external twin*) — a consumer declared a tag `in_plan` while another subtask declared the same capability `extent: external`. |
| `speculative_collapse_drops` | list[str] | subtask sids mechanically pruned by dead-subtask elimination (DESIGN §5) — fully-speculative subtasks whose every `in_plan` requires was unresolvable because the provider domain returned 0 subtasks. |
| `overlap_replan_done` | bool | set once when `phase_overlap_judge` answers an `unresolvable` collision with a **scoped re-plan** instead of `die()`ing (DESIGN §5). |
| `plan_overlap_judge` | dict | full output of the phase 2¾ `plan_overlap_judge` worker (DESIGN §5 *Cross-domain surface overlap*) — `{collisions: [{a_sid, b_sid, artifact, resolution, reason, merge_feasibility?}, …]}`. |
| `plan_overlap_applied` | list[dict] | post-apply mutation summary for the phase 2¾ judge. |
| `duplicate_provider_merge_applied` | list[dict] | post-apply mutation summary for merges the deterministic `check_duplicate_providers` floor synthesized and applied via `_duplicate_provider_merge_collisions` + `_apply_overlap_collisions` (M11 DECISION — see "Phase 2¾ checks" above). |
| `adherence_gate` | dict | audit record from the phase 2⅞ instruction-adherence gate (`phase_adherence_gate` — see "Instruction-adherence gate" above) — `{judge: <adherence_judge output>, floor_issues: list[str]}`. |
| `coverage_gate` | dict | audit record from the phase 2⅞½ task-coverage gate (`phase_planning_coverage_gate`, DESIGN §8 *Independent adversarial verification*) — the final `task_coverage_judge` output `{task_covered, coverage_gaps, rationale}`. |
| `item_coverage` | dict \| null | the merged plan's required-item accounting (DESIGN §5 *Required items are claimed too, and the plan accounts for every one*), written by `phase_planning_coverage_gate` before execution: `{items[{item_index, item, claimed_by[], not_counted[], excluded[{domain, reason_kind, reason}], status}], uncovered[item_index...]}`, `status` one of `claimed`/`other_domain`/`uncovered` (`_item_accounting_rows`). Not written when the run has no required items or `skip_coverage_check` is set. Never gates; each `uncovered` item is listed in the PR's *Not verified by this run* (`_uncovered_item_lines`). |
| `classification_coverage_gate` | dict | audit record from `phase_classification_gate` (DESIGN §8 *Independent adversarial verification*) — the final `classification_judge` output `{categories_reviewed, miscategorizations, rationale}`. |
| `wiring_gate` | dict | audit record from `phase_wiring_gate` (DESIGN §5 *A wiring re-check on the fully-merged plan*, §8) — the final `wiring_judge` output `{plan_reviewed, wiring_defects, rationale}` plus a `repairs` array of `{sid, tag, provider, channel}` for every edge the gate added (`channel` is `"tag"`, `"id"`, or `"cofile_cluster"`; on the id channel `tag` and `provider` are both the named subtask id). (`"fanin"` and `"depends_on_fallback"` entries come from `_fanin_and_fallback` and add `providers` / `deps_added` + `skipped_cyclic`), and a `warnings` array of `{sid, value, kind, why}` for the findings no edge can order (DESIGN §5). `phase_wiring_gate` saves it only when `repairs` is empty; with repairs it sets the key and `_run_phases` saves it in the same `st.save()` as the re-`_schedule()`d `plan_snapshot`, so a resume never finds the verdict without the repaired snapshot. |
| `provision_recipe_gate` | dict | audit record from `phase_provision_gate` (DESIGN §8, §6½) — the final `provision_judge` output `{recipe_reviewed, recipe_failures, rationale}`. |
| `integration_gate` | dict[str, dict] | per-sid audit record from `integrate_wave`'s `integration_judge` gate — `{sid: {defects: list[str], advisories: list[str], merge_commit_sha: str, accepted: bool}}`, plus the repair loop's `repair_rounds`, `rounds`, `superseded`, `outcome` (`clean` / `repaired` / `backed_out`), `fallback_reason`, `reset_to`, `residual_lines`, `residual_total` (DESIGN §6 *When integration cannot succeed*). |
| `integration_defects` | dict[str, list[str]] | per-sid flat mirror of `integration_gate[sid]["defects"]` for the sids with a currently-gating (not-yet-accepted) finding — the record `accept-integration` clears (popped, along with the whole key when it empties, once accepted or once a re-invoked judge comes back clean). |
| `no_work_required` | bool | set to `True` by `_finish_no_work_run` when every planner returns `status: "ready"` with `subtasks: []` (DESIGN §8 *The cleared-but-empty terminal state*). |
| `no_work_reasons` | dict[str, str] | per-domain `confidence.basis` quoted from each planner's empty-but-ready output, recorded alongside `no_work_required` for audit. |
| `working_branch` | str | the user's branch at the moment `phase_classify` runs (`git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`). |
| `pr_base_branch` | str | the final branch this run's PR merges into — overridable via `--pr-base-branch` / `LEERIE_PR_BASE_BRANCH` / `pr_base_branch` in `leerie.toml` (resolved by `resolve_pr_base_branch`, CLI > env > file precedence, mirroring `resolve_pr_template`). |
| `run_repo` | str | `"repo"` once the run's own repository `<run-dir>/repo` exists (`_ensure_run_repo`; DESIGN §6 *The run's own repository*). |
| `run_layout` | int | `RUN_LAYOUT_VERSION` at the run's fresh start, never rewritten by a resume. Absent on every run directory made before the field (an older layout). `resume` and `--phase` refuse a run whose value differs (`_refuse_other_run_layout`), and `leerie list` shows such a run with work left as `other-leerie` (DESIGN §6 *A run directory is continued only by a leerie of its layout*). |
| `base_sha` | str | the commit `setup-run.sh` cut the run branch from, recorded once by `phase_execute`; every comparison leerie makes against the base reads it (`_diff_base`), never the working branch's name. |
| `leerie_version` | str | the leerie version string from `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, seeded once at the run's original start and **immutable across resumes** (N38) — a resume no longer overwrites it with whatever is installed at resume time, since doing so made a resumed run's failures read as attributable to the wrong release. |
| `leerie_commit` | str \| null | short sha of the commit the launch's code snapshot holds (`<sha>-dirty.<tree>` for a checkout with edits; `_snapshot_leerie_code`), forwarded by the launcher as `LEERIE_COMMIT`, seeded once at the run's original start and **immutable across resumes** (N38), same rationale as `leerie_version`. |
| `leerie_versions` | list[dict] | append-only resume history (N38), distinct from the immutable `leerie_version`/`leerie_commit` pair above. |
| `dep_capture_done` | bool | set to `True` in `state.json` by `capture_repo_deps` after a successful write. |
| `requirement_coverage` | dict | the requirement-coverage gate's record, written by `phase_classify` (DESIGN §8 *Requirement coverage*): `{spans[{id, parent}], sections[{id, source}], reports[], closure[], holes{}}`. `spans`/`sections` are the IDs `_d1_split_spans`/`_d1_split_sections` assigned (no text); `parent` is the mechanical nesting link `_d1_judge_packs` groups by; `reports` the inlined report paths; `closure` the S/R ids `_d1_closure` derives; `holes` the residual `_d1_coverage_holes` findings after the check rounds (`{}` when none). |
| `needs_human_verification` | list[dict] | items no in-container step can verify, for the PR's "Needs human verification" list: `[{source, item_index, item, span, source_ref}]`, `source` `"required_item"` for a `required_items` entry typed `verifiability: "external"` (written by `phase_classify`; never handed to the `delivery_judge`), and `source` `"blocker"` — `{source, subtask, resource, blocker}`, plus `via` (the accepted-external predecessors) for a dependent settled without running — for a subtask settled `accepted_external` on an implementer's `external_precondition` or as such a dependent (`_settle_accepted_external`; `phase_classify` rewrites only the `required_item` entries). A third source, `"regression_check"` (`{source, detail}`, at most one), comes from `_set_regression_gap`: the task forbids the test command, and its scoped replacement could not run on the latest measured tree. A fourth, `"test_outcome"` (`{source, detail}`, at most one), from `_set_test_outcome_gap`: required items decided by the failing-test-ID diff whose verdict was `unknown` at final delivery detection. A sixth, `"final_test_diff"` (`{source, detail}`, at most one), from `_set_final_diff_gap`: the failing-test-ID diff could not be measured on the tree that ships. A fifth, `"confirm_budget"` (`{source, site, detail}`, at most one per site), from `_set_confirm_budget_gap`: final-tree B\* candidates left `budget_short_unsettled`. |
| `site_claims` | dict \| null | the site-claims record (DESIGN §5 *Every `fix` site is claimed*), written by `phase_plan` from the first-pass `bug-fixing` plan and rewritten over its leaves after decomposition: `{domain, sites[{site_id, file, symbol, auditor_kind, resolution, claims[{sid, kinds[]}], not_needed, not_needed_kind, status, surface_other}]}`, `status` one of `claimed`/`mismatch`/`not_needed`/`unclaimed` (`_site_claim_rows`); `surface_other` marks a site resting on an `other` kind; the delivery gate adds `settlement{settled, votes, samples, evidence}` to such a row (`_settle_untyped_sites`). Not written when there is no `bug-fixing` plan or the audit is inapplicable. An `unclaimed` row stops the run in planning (`_stop_on_unclaimed_sites`). |
| `scope_reading` | dict | which reading of the task the run took (DESIGN §8 *A sweep's instances are items*), written once by `_settle_scope_reading` after the audit: `{kind}` with `kind` `none` (no applicable audit) or `one_reading`; `{kind: "narrow_or_broad", narrow, broad, chosen: "broad"}` otherwise. Its presence is the step's resume checkpoint. Rendered under the PR's `## Scope reading`. |
| `sweeps` | list[dict] | per sweep (DESIGN §8 *A sweep's instances are items*): the classifier's, written by `phase_classify` (`{item_index, sweep, part, pattern, instances, files, unparsed[] (at most 50 paths), error, derived[item_index...]}`), then the audit's sites', appended by `_settle_scope_reading` (`{site_id, pattern, instances, files, unparsed[], error, derived[]}`) — what each enumeration found on the base tree and which derived `required_items` it appended. `[]` when nothing carries a sweep. |
| `domain_blocked` | list[dict] | every planner domain that exited `blocked`, `[{domain, blocker_kind, external_resource, gap}]` (`_settle_blocked_domains`; DESIGN §8 *A partially blocked plan is recorded*). Written after planning and again before scheduling; `[]` when none. A row typed `external_precondition` stops the run before execution. |
| `process_constraints` | dict | the classifier's typed process constraints (DESIGN §9 *A command the task forbids*): `{forbidden_commands[], entries[{command, scope, evidence_quote, test_roots?, package_name?, derived_from?, votes}], dropped[{command, reason, evidence_quote}], draws{draws, crashed}}` from `_process_constraints` over the union of the classifier's and the `forbidden_command_extractor` samples' entries. A state written before scopes existed carries `{forbidden_commands[], evidence}`; `_forbidden_specs` reads that as `scope: "any"`. Read by `claude_p` (deny rules, notice, hook), `_measure_axes`, the plan strip and the planner ctx. |
| `committing_worker_started` | bool | True once `claude_p` has started the first worker whose `schema_key` is in `_COMMITTING_WORKERS`; `_run_setup_hook` `die()`s rather than run the hook when it is set and `provision.sh_hook_ran` is not (DESIGN §6 *Leerie's runs of the repository's commands are confined too*) |


`pending-questions.json` (written by `gather_answers` on non-TTY exit, read by
the plugin skill in `commands/leerie.md`):

| Field | Shape | Notes |
|-------|-------|-------|
| `questions` | array of `{id, question, why_underivable?, choices?, evidence?}` | the classifier-surfaced intent questions not already in `--answers`; or the open intent conflicts (`_stop_for_intent_questions`), each with `choices: ["yes", "no"]` and the resolver's verified quotes |

`answers.json` (written by the plugin skill, passed back via
`--answers <state-root>/answers.json`):

| Field | Shape | Notes |
|-------|-------|-------|
| `<question id>` | string | one entry per question id from `pending-questions.json.questions[].id`; for an intent question one of its `choices` (another value leaves it open) |
| `source_of_truth` | `"codebase"` / `"research"` / `"both"` | optional; overrides the resolved preference for this run |

The checkpoint schema — seven required sections, enforced by
`_validate_checkpoint()`: *Frozen success criteria*, *Current status*, *Files
touched*, *Decisions made*, *Evidence gate status*, *Next action*, *Open
unknowns*. Three layers: (a) every header present; (b) every section
non-whitespace; (c) the five handoff-context sections reject single-token
placeholders (`none`/`n/a`/`na`/`tbd`/`nothing`/`unknown`/`todo`/`pending`/`—`/`--`/`-`/`?`,
trailing punctuation stripped first) — *Decisions made* and *Open unknowns*
accept them. When `worktree_root` is passed, a freshness check also requires
every *Files touched* path to still exist or carry a `[deleted]` annotation.

`claude_p()`'s CLI-reported `num_turns` is unreliable against `--max-turns`
(computed from two different counters depending on which exit path fired).
`terminal_reason` is the trustworthy cap signal; `tests/test_turn_cap_signal.py`
guards against reintroducing the `num_turns` comparison.

Maps to `DESIGN.md`: §10 (handoff, coordination-artifact location), §9 (criteria
locking).

---

## 9. Structured-output schemas

`claude_p()` validates each worker's payload against a schema keyed by worker
type. `confidence` is optional on every worker schema (a required object
shape would corrupt payloads under anthropics/claude-code#49747) but when
present follows `_confidence_schema(...)`: axis score(s) 1–10, `basis`
(string, required), `falsifiers_tested` / `contradictions_reconciled` (arrays
of strings, optional). There is no `gap_to_close` field — a low score's gap
is stated in `basis`.

Required fields, current shape:

- **classifier** — required: `categories` (array). Optional: `questions`
  (`{id, question, why_underivable?}[]`), `source_of_truth_question` (bool —
  flags relevance only; the orchestrator's preference resolution supplies the
  value, default `both`), `prescribed_procedure` (`{is_prescribed, commands[],
  forbid_manual, evidence}` — language→JSON signal for an explicit procedure
  vs. a goal description; `check_classifier_output` requires non-empty
  `evidence` when `is_prescribed`; persisted to `st.data["prescribed_procedure"]`,
  default `{}`), `likely_already_satisfied` (bool) + `likely_already_satisfied_evidence`
  (required non-empty when true — DESIGN §8; OR-preserved across
  `phase_classification_gate` re-classify rounds so a silent round never
  clears an earlier true finding). `process_constraints` (optional, via
  `$defs`) is `{forbidden_commands: [{command, evidence_quote, scope: any |
  whole_suite}]}` — commands the task forbids running, each with the task's
  own words; persisted by `_process_constraints` (quote-checked).
- **planner** — required: `domain`, `subtasks`, `status` (`ready` / `blocked`
  — DESIGN §8 planner gate; a `ready` plan may carry empty `subtasks`, the
  cleared-but-empty terminal state). `confidence` keys when present:
  `task_understanding`, `decomposition_quality` (1–10), `basis`. Each subtask:
  `{id, title, success_criteria_seed, intent, scope_note, files_likely_touched,
  depends_on, requires, provides, size, investigation_notes, runs_commands,
  verify, verification_only}`. `verify` (optional, planner and
  splitter children — `include_verify`) is `{criterion, argv: string[]}[]`, one entry per success
  criterion, `argv` empty for a criterion no command decides;
  `verification_only` (optional boolean, absence = false, planner only —
  `include_verification_only`) is the planner's
  claim that the subtask writes nothing and every criterion is decided by its
  argv — `_verification_only(subtask)` counts it only when every entry has a
  non-empty argv (DESIGN §8 *Settled by execution*). Merges
  (`_apply_overlap_merge`, the planner-overlap merge) carry both through
  `_merge_verify_fields`: the entries are unioned and `verification_only`
  survives only when both sides had it.
  `requires` is `{tag, extent: "in_plan"|"external", reason (required
  non-empty when external)}[]` — `in_plan` is satisfied by a sibling's
  `provides` (a graph edge); `external` is a planner-declared prerequisite
  outside *this run's* graph — either outside the build graph entirely
  (another repo, ops runbook, manual step), or producible by code but owned
  by another run the task names (sibling phase document, earlier phase), or
  fenced off by the task itself (the task declares a surface out of scope
  and the capability's only implementation site lies on it) — surfaced in
  `plan.json`'s `preconditions` (DESIGN §5 `requires.extent`). In every case
  `reason` must name the owner; the discriminating test is "is it in this
  run's graph?", not "could any code produce it?".
  `change_shape` (required), `independent_sites` (required boolean) and
  `sweep_sites` (optional `string[]`) gate the sub-file split (DESIGN §5½
  (P1) *Sub-file*; `_subfile_split_gate`, `_sweep_site_lines`).
  `provides` is bare strings. `size` is `small`/`medium`/`large` — `large`
  triggers the size-resolution retry loop, `_validate_plan` OVERSIZED-dies if
  it survives. `runs_commands` (optional strings) feeds
  `check_prescribed_command_coverage(prescribed_procedure, subtasks) ->
  list[str]`, the deterministic primary layer of the instruction-adherence
  gate (token-subset match of `prescribed.commands` against the union of
  `runs_commands`, emitting `PRESCRIBED_CMD_UNRUN: ...`; short-circuits to
  `[]` with no prescribed procedure). Tested in
  `tests/test_prescribed_cmd_coverage.py`; wired into `phase_adherence_gate`.
  Also required: top-level `blocker_kind` (`none` / `external_precondition` /
  `evidence_gap`) and per subtask `change_kind` (`fix` / `test` / `docs` /
  `other`). Optional: top-level `external_resource` (string) and
  `sites_not_needed` (`{site_id, reason_kind: enum SITE_EXCLUSION_KINDS,
  reason: string (minLength 1)}[]`) and `items_not_needed`
  (`{item_index: integer, reason_kind: enum ITEM_EXCLUSION_KINDS, reason:
  string (minLength 1)}[]`); per subtask `claims`
  (`{sites: {site_id, resolution_kinds: string[] (minItems 1)}[]}`). These
  five live in the planner schema's `$defs` and are referenced with `$ref`
  (the CLI resolves and validates `$ref`, probed live on 2.1.310: a value
  outside a referenced enum was rejected).
- **defect_scope_auditor** — required: `applicable`, `sites`. Each site:
  required `{file, symbol, role, disposition, resolution_kind}`, optional
  `{line_hint, note, resolution}`; `resolution_kind` (a `$ref` into the
  schema's `$defs`) is one of `rerun_flow` / `reraise` / `relink` / `guard`
  / `recompute` / `propagate` / `other` (`other` with an empty `resolution`
  on a `ruled_out` site). Optional `defect_shape`, `chokepoint`,
  `ground_truth`, `rationale`. `site_id` is assigned by code, never by the
  worker.
- **implementer** — required: `subtask_id`, `status` (`complete` /
  `incomplete-handoff` / `blocked` / `failed` / `needs-clarification`).
  `confidence`: `root_cause`, `solution` (1–10), `basis`. Optional: `branch`,
  `criteria_results` (`{criterion, met, evidence, not_applicable?,
  locations?}[]` — does not gate; `locations` items are `$ref:
  #/$defs/location` = `{path, start_line?, end_line?}`, the files and lines
  the evidence was read from, which a no-op claim's settle probe is shown
  by `_no_op_claim_evidence`), `checkpoint_path`, `blocker`, `summary`, `clarification_question`
  (DESIGN §11: `{id, question, why_underivable}`, all required together with
  `checkpoint_path`), `artifacts` (DESIGN §5: `{name, kind: "markdown"|"json"|"text",
  content, summary?}[]` — deliverables for downstream subtasks),
  `self_reported_risks` (DESIGN §9 *Self-reported risk is routed, not read*:
  max 8 items, each `$ref: #/$defs/risk` — `{kind:
  unexercised_behavior|external_contract_assumption|untested_change|process_note,
  detail, where?, gap: test_missing|test_weak|unverified_external|none,
  where_paths[], settle_by?: test|typecheck|install|build, resource?,
  simulated_interleaving?}` — routed by `_collect_subtask_risks` into the
  `risk_register` and the conformer's challenge context, never parsed from
  prose), `blocker_kind` (`$ref` into the schema's `$defs`: `nothing_to_change`
  / `external_precondition` / `environment_limit` / `upstream_missing` /
  `cannot_reproduce` / `regression_unresolved` / `other`),
  `external_resource` (string, the resource an `external_precondition`
  needs) and `external_resource_claim` (`$ref` into `$defs`: `{kind:
  env_var|network|file|binary|service_credential|human_action, name?,
  host?, port?, path?, description?, quote?}`, the typed resource
  `_verify_external_claim` checks) — routed by `_route_blocker_kind` (§6 *Typed blocker kinds*);
  and `probe_objections` (array of flat objects, required `probe_test_file`
  and `kind` — `PROBE_OBJECTION_KINDS` —, optional `reason`), read only
  from a delivery re-drive implementer and only through
  `_redrive_probe_objections` (DESIGN §8 *Delivery re-drive* rule 4).
- **integrator** — required: `incoming_subtask`, `status` (`resolved` /
  `design-conflict` / `failed`). `confidence`: `_confidence_schema(["resolution"])`.
  Optional: `resolution_summary`, `diagnosis` (fallback on non-`resolved`).
- **rebaser** — required: `status` (`rebased` / `irreconcilable` / `failed`),
  `final_branch_state`. `confidence` mirrors `integrator`. Optional:
  `resolution_summary`, `diagnosis` (required in practice when
  `irreconcilable`). A scoped, fully-agentic §12 exception (DESIGN §6
  *Finalization* "Rebase-onto-base before push") — the worker performs the
  whole rebase workflow itself, and `check_rebaser_worktree_state(worktree,
  status, pre_rebase_sha, base_ref=None)` mechanically re-verifies the
  claimed status against actual git state (`run_rebaser` passes
  `base_ref=origin/<pr_base_branch>`). On `rebased`, a conflict marker is
  a `(path, line)` that `_introduced_conflict_markers` reports against
  **both** `pre_rebase_sha` and `base_ref`; an unresolvable `base_ref`
  drops only the second scan. That helper reads `git diff --check
  <since>` (git's own marker rule: `conflict-marker-size`, diff3's
  `|||||||`), then re-diffs with `--text -U0` each path `--check` skipped
  as binary (`-\t-\t` in `--numstat -z`; a `-diff` lockfile still
  receives merge markers) unless the file has a NUL in its first 8000
  bytes, applying the same rule (`_is_conflict_marker`) to its added
  lines. In-progress rebase state is located with `git rev-parse
  --git-path rebase-merge|rebase-apply` (`_rebase_state_dirs`), since
  `.git` is a file in the disposable worktree. Every git failure —
  `--check` exiting other than 0/2, `--numstat`, the per-path diff, or
  `--git-path` — returns a "could not scan/verify" mismatch.
- **acceptance_writer** — required: `files[]`, each `{path, kind: defect|control,
  cases[], failure_mode: assertion|import}`; optional `notes`. Python keeps a
  defect file only if one of its cases fails on the validity base (the run's
  own start) and a control file only if none of its cases fails — and a set
  only with at least one kept control file — judged by
  `_run_acceptance_file(..., validating=True)` — the repo's scoped test
  template rendered over that one file, per case from the runner's structured
  report where one can be written (exit code otherwise), and `failure_mode`
  honoured only as the Phase 2 row describes (not `_measure_blt`); `cases` are
  the only thing the repair rounds are shown (DESIGN §8 *Held-out acceptance
  tests*).
- **set_auditor** — required: `cases[]`, each `{case, verdict:
  implementation_gap|set_defect, defect_kind: none|harness_unreachable|coupling|
  contradicts_task|overspecified_mechanism|environment|test_bug, test_quote{file,
  quote}, prod_quote{file, quote}, task_quote, failure_quote, reason}`. A
  `set_defect` counts only when `_verify_set_audit_case` finds every quote its
  kind requires (`_SET_AUDIT_QUOTES`) verbatim, whitespace aside, at least 12
  characters: `test_quote` in the named SET file, `prod_quote` in a repository
  file of the audited tree that is not a set file, `task_quote` in the task
  and its referenced files, `failure_quote` in the case's failure message.
  One verdict per identical assertion (DESIGN §8 *Identical assertions get
  one verdict*):
  - When it took at least one sample, `_acceptance_audit_in` also returns
    `verdicts`, one per failing case: `set_defect` when the case is a
    counted finding, else `implementation_gap`. It also returns
    `case_keys` from `_audit_case_key(set_, file, case, graph)`.
  - `_audit_case_key` finds the case's own block. In JS/TS
    (`_AUDIT_JS_BLOCK_RE`), that is the longest `it`/`test` title the
    case ID ends with, the block running to the next opening. In Python
    (`_AUDIT_PY_BLOCK_RE`), it is the `def` named by the case ID's last
    dotted part (parameters stripped), running to the next `def` at the
    same or lesser indent. It keeps the block's lines matching
    `_AUDIT_ASSERT_RE` (`expect(`, `assert`, `.assert…(`), each
    whitespace-collapsed. The target is the repository modules the set
    file imports: resolved non-test JS/TS imports, or Python module names.
    The key is the first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of `[assertion,
    target]`. It is None when no block or assertion is found.
  - `_acceptance_audit_and_rewrite` audits every set in `todo` first, then
    calls `_reconcile_audit_verdicts(audits)`, then acts on the triggers
    per set. A set's re-audit after its rewrite is reconciled against deep
    copies of the other sets' audits.
  - `_reconcile_audit_verdicts` groups the cases of all audits by key. For
    a key typed both `set_defect` and `implementation_gap`, it removes the
    `set_defect` cases from their sets' `findings` (recomputing `kinds`,
    appending to `reconciled`) in place. It returns one conflict per such
    key, `{key, assertion, target, cases[{set, case, verdict}], kept:
    "implementation_gap"}`, appended to `acceptance.audit_conflicts`.
  - `_AUDIT_RECORD_KEYS` names what a set's `audit` record keeps.
- **surrogate_fixer** — required: `summary`, `files_changed[]`.
- **ci_checks** — required: `checks[]` and `excluded[]`, every field of both
  required (shape in the worker table). `kind`: `CI_CHECK_KINDS`; `trigger`:
  `CI_TRIGGERS`; `requires`: `CI_REQUIRES`; `metric`:
  `CI_COVERAGE_METRICS`; `excluded[].reason`: deploy|release|schedule_only|
  manual_only|push_only|reporting_only|duplicate|external_action|other. No
  maps and no nullable fields: `env` is a list of `{name, value}`,
  `strict_argv` is `[]` when the tool has no strict form, and a non-coverage
  check carries `coverage: {summary_path: "", config_file: "", thresholds:
  []}`.
- **scope_judge** — required: `report_ranges[]`, each `{param, min, max (a
  single value has min = max), unit: ms|s|count|bytes|percent|other,
  span_quote}`, and `cases[]`, each `{case_index, origin: report_example|
  report_regression_test|report_symptom|other_scenario, params[{range_ref,
  value, unit}], span_quote, reason}`. Facts only; `_scope_judge_counted`
  decides which cases count (see *Report-bounded has-work* in §6).
- **pr_reviewer** — required: `findings[]`, each `{item_id: string|null,
  kind: unmet_requirement|bug|regression, path, line_start, line_end, quote,
  item_span_quote: string|null, explanation}` (`additionalProperties: false`
  at both levels; `PR_REVIEW_KINDS`). A finding reaches the final conformer
  only when `_verify_pr_finding` finds its quote in the file at HEAD.
- **intent_resolver** — required: `decision` (string, non-empty), `answer`
  (`yes`|`no`, `INTENT_ANSWERS`), `evidence[]` (at least one), each
  `{source: code|history|task|report|web, quote, locator}`, and `status`
  (`settled`|`unsettled`); `additionalProperties: false` at both levels.
  B2's schema plus `answer`, the typed direction code applies.
- **plan_item_checker** — required: `conflicts[]`, each `{item_index
  (integer ≥ 0), item_quote, subtask_id, field (PLAN_CONFLICT_FIELDS),
  plan_quote, kind: preserve_vs_change|narrowing|pinned_test_contradicts,
  test_file}` (`additionalProperties: false` at both levels; B1's schema).
- **contract_extractor** — required: `counterpart_sid: string|null`,
  `literal: string|null`, `literal_kind: string_value|identifier|route_path|
  other` (`CONTRACT_LITERAL_KINDS`), `symbol: string|null`.
- **falsifier** — required: `verdict` (`unmet_demonstrated` |
  `could_not_demonstrate`), `probe_path`, `case_name`, `assertion_quote`,
  `item_span_quote`, `entry_point`, `reason` (strings, `""` when none).
  Facts only; `_falsifier_gates` decides.
- **forbidden_command_extractor** — required: `forbidden_commands[]`, the
  same `_FORBIDDEN_COMMANDS_ARRAY_SCHEMA` the classifier's
  `process_constraints.forbidden_commands` uses (`{command, evidence_quote,
  scope: any|whole_suite}`, all required).
- **verifiability_classifier** — required: `items[]`, each `{item_index,
  verifiability: in_tree|execution (RATCHET_VERIFIABILITY), reason}`
  (`additionalProperties: false` at both levels).
- **observability_judge** — required: `items[]`, each `{item_index,
  parts[]}`, each part `{part_index, observable (OBSERVABLE_KINDS), needs
  ("" or OBSERVABILITY_NEEDS), reason, cites[{path, line_start, line_end,
  quote}]}` (`additionalProperties: false` at every level).
- **contradiction_judge** — required: `same_entry_point`,
  `same_input_by_meaning`, `same_observable`, `mutually_exclusive`
  (booleans), `evidence[]` (`minItems` 1) each `{test:
  pinned|independent|code (CONTRADICTION_SOURCES), quote}` (`quote`
  `minLength` 1), `explanation` (`minLength` 1); `additionalProperties:
  false` at both levels — lane B3's `h/schema.json`. Facts only;
  `_contradiction_status` decides.
- **delivery_ratchet** — `_delivery_ratchet_schema(SCHEMAS["delivery_judge"])`:
  the delivery judge's schema with `evidence_files: string[]` added to each
  verdict's properties and `required`; derived, so the two never drift.
- **delivery_judge** (parts) — every verdict requires `parts[]`, each
  `{requirement, kind: static|behavioral|test_outcome, status: met|unmet|not_inspected,
  cites[]}` with `cites[]` `{path, line_start, line_end, quote}` (`$defs`
  `part` / `cite`). `path` is repo-relative, `"RECORD"`, or `"ABSENT"` /
  `"ABSENT:<pathspec>"` (the quote is then an extended regex).
- **conformer** — required: `subtask_id`, `rules_files_read` (strings, empty
  when none found), `rule_violations` (`{status: fixed|residual, rule, fix,
  evidence, why_not_fixed}[]`), `file_updates` (`{kind: docs|tests, path,
  reason}[]`), `build`/`lint`/`tests` (each `{"$ref": "#/$defs/blt"}`, the
  one shape `_CONFORMER_BLT_PROP` = `{ran, passed, command, summary?}` in the
  schema's `$defs` — `ran: false` when not applicable; one definition instead
  of three keeps the hardened wire form at 2,826 bytes with
  `unexercisable_resource` added, under the 3,178-byte compiler failure point
  `tests/test_conformer_schema_size.py` pins), `summary`, and `solution_defects`
  (`{kind: unhandled_input|unhandled_path|missing_guard|sibling_site_unedited|
  wrong_selector|decoy_or_shortcut|external_contract_assumption|
  unrevalidated_precondition, concrete_case, where, why_ships_a_defect}[]`,
  all three fields non-empty). `solution_defects` is the **gating** axis
  (DESIGN §9 *The one gating axis: solution completeness*) — the conformer's
  independent adversarial attack on the diff; non-empty retries the
  implementer with the defects as mandatory criteria (bounded by
  `completeness_retry_rounds`), or blocks on exhaustion. The last two kinds
  extend the attack beyond the planner-authored criteria (DESIGN §9 *The
  success criteria are not the ceiling of this attack*). Optional:
  `risk_dispositions` — a positional array of BARE STRINGS
  (`"confirmed_defect"` / `"mitigated"` / `"accepted"`; no enum on the
  wire, no item object, no rationale field — both were rejected for the
  grammar budget, see `_risk_dispositions_schema`), where entry i answers
  the i-th `SELF_REPORTED_RISKS` challenge item; a short or absent array
  leaves the tail unanswered, which `_collect_subtask_risks` keeps on the
  `risk_register` — the fail-safe union, DESIGN §9 *Self-reported risk is
  routed, not read*.
  Optional: `set_aside` — `{finding_id, reason_kind, quote}[]`, all three
  required: the shown findings (`pr-<k>`, `unmet-<i>`, `unmet-contract`)
  the final conformer leaves unfixed, `reason_kind` one of
  `SET_ASIDE_REASON_KINDS` (`deliberate`, `out_of_scope`, `larger_change`,
  `incorrect`), checked in code rather than by an enum on the wire, and
  `quote` the words the set-aside rests on. No `item_index`: the item is
  the finding's own. Both omissions are the grammar budget: with them the
  hardened form is 3,226 bytes, over the 3,178 the compiler rejects;
  without, 3,097 (dumped 2,658). `_adjudicate_set_asides` reads it
  (DESIGN §11 *Intent conflicts are settled with evidence, else asked*).

  `rule_violations`/`file_updates` are wire-flattened discriminated arrays
  (mirroring `SCHEMAS["reconciler"]`'s `tag_ops` technique) to keep the
  schema small for the strict-output proxy's grammar compiler.
  `_expand_conformer_output()` fans them back into `rule_violations_fixed`,
  `rule_violations_residual`, `docs_updates`, `tests_updates` right after the
  worker call (an unrecognised `status`/`kind` is dropped; pinned by
  `tests/test_conformer_schema_shrink.py`). `_validate_conformance_result()`
  then enforces cross-field invariants on the expanded shape: a residual
  with no `axis` requires non-empty `rules_files_read` (an `axis` residual
  is leerie's own `build/lint/tests must pass` rule, from the prompt, not a
  repository file), every `rule_violations_fixed` cites
  a `rule`, every `docs_updates`/`tests_updates` `path` exists in the
  worktree, every `solution_defects` item carries non-empty
  `concrete_case`/`where`. `confidence`: `conformance` (1–10), `basis`.
- **judge** — required: `passed` (bool, true only when all three dimensions
  are true), `dimensions` (`{schema_ok, factual_ok, hallucination_ok}`),
  `rationale` (1–3 sentences), `suggested_fixes` (empty when `passed: true`).
  Used by `phase_judge()` / `_judge_capture()`, post-run. `prompts/judge.md`
  carries the rubric.
- **patch_generator** — required: `anchor` (exact substring of the current
  system prompt, validated against live prompt text before applying),
  `replacement`. Optional: `strategy`, `pivot_reason`. Used by the self-heal
  skill's patch-generation worker, post-run.

Schemas are embedded as Python dicts in `leerie.py` and serialized inline.

Maps to `DESIGN.md`: §7, §14.

---

## 10. Telemetry — NDJSON envelope and call_type mapping

Maps to `DESIGN.md`: §14.

### NDJSON envelope schema

Every `claude_p()` invocation appends one JSON object (one line) to
`<state-root>/runs/<run-id>/calls.ndjson`, opened for append at run start and
never truncated. Not read by the orchestrator at runtime — reading is a
post-run operation performed by the judge and heal skills.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| `call_id` | str (UUID v4) | unique identifier for this invocation; referenced by judge verdicts |
| `run_id` | str | matches the run directory name under `<state-root>/runs/` |
| `call_type` | str | one of the `WORKER_TYPES` schema keys, plus the post-run/finalize workers `pr_writer`, `judge`, `patch_generator`, `dep_capture` |
| `model` | str | the model alias passed to `--model` (e.g. `opus`, `sonnet`) |
| `system_prompt` | str | the full system prompt injected via `--append-system-prompt` |
| `user_content` | str | the user-turn content passed to the worker |
| `response_content` | str | the worker's raw text response (before schema parsing) |
| `parsed_ok` | bool | whether `structured_output` was present and schema-valid |
| `input_tokens` | int | total input via `_usage_input_tokens(usage)` — `input_tokens` plus `cache_creation_input_tokens` plus `cache_read_input_tokens` (every worker runs with prompt caching, so the bare API field alone understates weight) |
| `output_tokens` | int | `usage.output_tokens` from the CLI envelope |
| `latency_ms` | int | wall-clock milliseconds from subprocess start to return |
| `success` | bool | whether the call produced a schema-valid result |
| `failure_kind` | str \| null | derived by `_classify_failure_kind`: `api_error` (`:auth`/`:quota`/`:overload`/`:transport` suffix), `incomplete` (non-`completed` `terminal_reason`), `malformed_tool_call` (CLI tool-call-parse-failure diagnostic — `anthropics/claude-code#49747`), or `schema_parse_failed` (the dominant case). Rate-limit/out-of-credits/hard-crash failures raise `RateLimitedExit`/`WorkerError` past the capture block and get no record. |
| `cgroup_applied` | bool | whether per-worker cgroup memory/PID containment was active for this spawn |
| `ts` | str (ISO-8601) | UTC timestamp when the line is written |

The judge skill consumes `system_prompt`/`user_content`/`response_content`/
`parsed_ok`; the heal loop replays a call against a patched prompt using
`system_prompt`/`user_content`. `call_type` partitions calls for per-type
analysis.

### Capture file path

```
<state-root>/runs/<run-id>/calls.ndjson
```

One file per run. Written by the orchestrator; the judge and heal skills
read it as a post-run harvest.

### Reporting — the `--report` verb

`resume` takes its run-id positionally OR as `--run-id`; both are
equivalent. `main()` pops the bare verb from `argv[0]`, then — for `resume`
only — takes an optional leading non-flag positional via
`_extract_resume_run_id()` before `ap.parse_args()` and assigns it to
`args.run_id`; passing both with different values `die()`s. `list` is
excluded (it has its own positionals: `list status paused`, `list chains`).
Pinned by `tests/test_resume_positional_run_id.py`.

`leerie --report [RUN_ID]` is a read-only telemetry report for a single run;
like `list` it exits without running orchestrate. Run selection reuses
`resolve_run_id` (exact-match a passed id, else auto-pick the most recent
run, else die). Unlike `resume`, `--report` does not pass
`resumable_only=True` — reporting on a finished run is the normal case. It
prints a header (status, duration, `state.json`'s `telemetry` aggregate —
calls, `$cost`, in/out tokens); a per-`call_type` breakdown from
`calls.ndjson` (count, tokens, average latency, failure count, sorted by
call count via `_aggregate_calls`); a `failures by kind` rollup when any
failed; and a memory-peak line (peak `rss_kb`, max `open_fds`/`thread_count`)
from `memory.ndjson` via `_memory_peak`. All inputs already exist on disk;
`--report` adds no new telemetry.

### call_type → prompt-resolution table

Each `call_type` maps to exactly one system-prompt source; no call_type is
ever spawned without one, and no prompt is shared between call types.

| call_type        | Prompt source | Notes |
|------------------|---------------|-------|
| `classifier`     | `prompts/classifier.md` | read from disk |
| `planner`        | `prompts/planner.md` | read from disk |
| `reconciler`     | `prompts/reconciler.md` | read from disk |
| `plan_overlap_judge` | `prompts/plan_overlap_judge.md` | cross-domain surface-overlap analysis, phase 2¾ (DESIGN §5) |
| `fit_judge`      | `prompts/fit_judge.md` | per-subtask decomposition fit verdict (DESIGN §5½) |
| `splitter`       | `prompts/splitter.md` | coupled-minority subtask splitter (DESIGN §5½) |
| `adherence_judge`| `prompts/adherence_judge.md` | whole-plan instruction-adherence score, phase 2⅞ (DESIGN §12 sibling) |
| `satisfied_probe`| `prompts/satisfied_probe.md` | per-subtask base-tree already-satisfied probe, phase 3 (DESIGN §8) |
| `no_work_judge`  | `prompts/no_work_judge.md` | independent verifier of the classifier's already-satisfied claim on the converged gate path, phase 1½ (DESIGN §8 *The healthy-path consumer*) |
| `delivery_judge` | `prompts/delivery_judge.md` | finalize-side required-items verifier on the integrated staging tree, phase 5 delivery gate (DESIGN §8 *The delivery gate*) |
| `defect_scope_auditor` | `prompts/defect_scope_auditor.md` | pre-planning defect-shape site enumeration on defect-fix tasks, phase 2 (DESIGN §5 *Defect-scope audit*) |
| `provision`      | `prompts/provision.md` | LLM fallback when the lockfile table misses (DESIGN §6½) |
| `implementer`    | `prompts/implementer.md` | read from disk |
| `integrator`     | `prompts/integrator.md` | read from disk |
| `conformer`      | `prompts/conformer.md` | read from disk; carries the gating `solution_defects` section |
| `classification_judge` | `prompts/classification_judge.md` | independent adversarial verifier of the classifier's category set (DESIGN §8) |
| `wiring_judge`   | `prompts/wiring_judge.md` | independent semantic-wiring verifier of the reconciled plan (DESIGN §5, §8) |
| `provision_judge`| `prompts/provision_judge.md` | independent verifier of the install recipe vs image/runtime (DESIGN §6½, §8) |
| `task_coverage_judge`| `prompts/task_coverage_judge.md` | independent adversarial verifier of plan coverage (DESIGN §8); wired into `phase_planning_coverage_gate` |
| `artifact_registry` | `prompts/artifact_registry.md` | pre-planning shared-vocabulary worker, phase 2 (DESIGN §5) |
| `integration_judge` | `prompts/integration_judge.md` | post-merge behavioral-correctness verifier inside `integrate_wave` (DESIGN §8) |

`resolve_prompt(call_type: str) -> tuple[str, str, str]` loads a worker's
system prompt: given any member of `WORKER_TYPES`, returns `(source_kind,
content, location_hint)` where `source_kind` is `"file"` and `location_hint`
is `"prompts/<call_type>.md"`. Raises `ValueError` for an unknown
`call_type`.

### _replay_capture — primitive for judge and heal-loop replays

```python
async def _replay_capture(
    record: dict,
    *,
    override_system_prompt: str | None = None,
    cwd: str | None = None,
) -> tuple[dict, dict]:
```

Given one NDJSON record, reconstructs the `claude_p()` invocation with the
captured `system_prompt`, `user_content`, `call_type` (used as `schema_key`),
and `model`, and returns `(envelope, structured_output)` from the new
invocation. `override_system_prompt` lets the heal loop replay with a
patched prompt in place of the captured one. Replays use a throwaway
in-memory `_ReplayState` and `_suppress_capture=True` — they never write to
`calls.ndjson`. The replayed call reads the repository at `cwd` (default
the current directory, the user's checkout) only through
`_ref_less_clone(cwd, <tmp>/replay-checkout, HEAD)`: a ref-less `--shared`
clone of that repository at its HEAD under the replay's temporary run
directory, removed with it; INSPECT_TOOLS run there, never in the checkout
itself (DESIGN §8 *A
worker that does not commit never runs in a tree leerie measures*). A
`cwd` that is no git repository (no HEAD commit) has no clone to make:
the replay raises `WorkerError`, which `_replay_and_judge_sample` records as an empty
envelope. Both judge (n=1 replay, then score) and heal (n=N replays,
baseline vs patched) build on this primitive.
