## 11. Verification status of the code

Mirrors `DESIGN.md` §15, at the code level.

enforcement functions. No coverage target is set. It covers, by subsystem:
core resolvers and validation (incl. `test_state_fields.py`, pinning
`STATE_FIELDS` parity against both the §8 field table and every
`st.data[...]` write); planning (P6 repo map, P1 recursive decomposition);
worker isolation/prompts/tool scoping (incl. `test_judgment_worker_isolation.py`,
which pins that judgment workers never receive
`--dangerously-skip-permissions`); orchestrator wiring (incl.
`test_no_undefined_names.py`, a whole-module `symtable` scan for undefined
names — ruff F821 without the dependency); conformance (DESIGN §9, incl.
`test_conformance_clean_delta.py`'s delta-not-verdict discipline and the
three `{test_files}`-proxy files detailed below); container image/provisioning;
the `leerie config` verb; judge/heal skills; the group verb (DESIGN §20); and
finalize/host-side bash (`test_host_finalize_sh.py`'s no-push/already-pushed
idempotency and PR-base-branch-override contract). The full per-file,
per-incident inventory — which test covers which surface, and the specific
traps each one pins against regressing — is in `docs/TESTING.md`, not
duplicated here.

The `{test_files}`-proxy files carry the per-file detail a reader scans to
find what is already covered:

| Test file | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `test_test_files_proxy.py` | `_is_test_file` / `_render_scoped`'s `{test_files}` tier / `_select_subtask_axes`' deferral (DESIGN §9). The load-bearing case is the empty-AFTER-filter one: `files` is NON-empty so the pre-existing empty-list guard does not fire, yet every member is a non-test path — rendering there yields a bare `pytest`, which runs EVERYTHING, the same inversion the `{files}` rule forbids reached by a different route. Also pins that the shipped vitest/jest `{files}` templates take SOURCE files on purpose, the `lstrip("./")`-vs-`removeprefix` case, and declared `test_file_globs` REPLACING rather than extending the built-ins. |
| `test_near_tests_first.py` | DESIGN §8 *A round's near tests are measured first*, §9 *Discovery on a tree that may not ship*, over real repositories and a real pytest: the stage's files, memo and ledger; rejection and flake; no stage for an unknown reach or a forbidden scoped command; a keeper pays no file twice; the final conformer's loop, the acceptance gate and the re-drive driven whole; phase 5 running the closure and the deferred discovery; the log lines. |
| `test_one_measurement_per_change.py` | DESIGN §8 *What ships is what was measured, once per change that can affect it*, over real git and a real confined pytest: a red run's verdict and IDs from one run, an identical tree and the ratchet's read of one not run, a leaf change running only its coupled tests with each carried file's own tree, a hub running what it reaches, a lockfile, config, fixture, document, deleted file, unknown language or test-less source running the whole command, a carried failure re-run, staleness by tree diff through a revert and a rollback, a forbidden command replaced then narrowed and never run, the round loop's regression compare across a narrowed result, and the real `_run_final_conformance` plus phase 5. |
| `test_scoped_proxy_corpus.py` | The measured basis for the `{test_files}` tier, frozen against `tests/fixtures/scoped_proxy_corpus/corpus.json` — 36 REAL per-subtask diffs recovered from leerie's own run branches. Exists because the ratio was first taken from the planner's `files_likely_touched` and was badly wrong (40% test-touching predicted vs 94% real). Each row must be ONE subtask's work (an integration merge's FIRST-PARENT diff, not a cumulative two-dot diff), and the fixture must retain its source-only rows or the render-nothing safety property (a test-less diff defers rather than rendering a bare runner) goes untested. |
| `test_scoped_degrade_warning.py` | `_warn_scoped_degraded_once` (DESIGN §9): `scoped` is the default and an unresolvable `tests` proxy now defers that axis to the whole-tree pass, so a repo with no test proxy gets no per-subtask test signal at all — and must be told so once (an unresolvable `build` proxy still runs the canonical build, which the warning also states). The anti-vacuity partner `test_silent_when_a_proxy_resolves` is mandatory: without it a warning that fired unconditionally would pass, turning the signal into noise on the ~99% of repos where scoping works. Two wiring guards — the call precedes the baseline block, and an AST check that it is NOT nested under the `skip_base_baseline` guard (sentinel-skipped on resume, i.e. silent on exactly the runs that most need telling). |
| `test_full_suite_ownership.py` | DESIGN §9 *The whole suite is orchestrator-owned*: the matcher against a set of commands whose deny verdicts were observed live on the CLI (`LIVE_PROBED`; the rest of the verdicts gathered in review agree by offline replay only, including subshell, `$(…)`, unspaced-redirect, quoted-bracket, line-continuation and brace-group-vs-expansion shapes) plus paraphrase/compound/wrapper shapes and npm-family negatives; the anchored match with the CLI's prefixes (environment assignments with quoted values, `env` and its options, `timeout` options, compound-command keywords) and the `is_prescribed` gate (a prescribed command that merely names the runner, or a drifted classifier, never lifts the deny); a prescribed command never stripped or exempted, and a stripped paraphrase of one resynthesised exactly through the real `_run_phases`; the emitted `Bash(...)` string being exactly the pattern list; testpaths, hostile ini files and a failing derivation degrading without raising; `_strip_canonical_suite_commands` against the 2026-10-26 incident's real `runs_commands` (and a prescribed whole-suite command lifting strip, deny and notice together); the settle-time exemption through the real `_settle_subtask` (an old spec settles complete; a prescribed one still blocks); deny and notice reaching the real `claude_p` together for every Bash-capable worker, not for an unwidened inspect-only one, and for one whose allowlist a runner grant widened; the strip running inside the real `_run_phases` before `_schedule()`; a resume past `plan_snapshot` whose wiring gate repairs keeping the stripped plan and any resynthesised subtask; the root cap, wildcard decline and malformed-`commands` guard; and an end-to-end `_run_conformance_phase` on a docs-only diff where the canonical suite is never measured and a conformer's self-reported green suite does not survive. |

**CI workflows:**

| Workflow | Coverage |
|----------|----------|
| `.github/workflows/syntax.yml` | AST-parses every Python file under the repo plus `tests/`; runs `pytest tests/test_no_undefined_names.py` for the undefined-name scan (one implementation, not reimplemented in the workflow). Path-filtered to the Python source trees. |
| `.github/workflows/shellcheck.yml` | `shellcheck -x scripts/*.sh`. Path-filtered to `scripts/**/*.sh`. |
| `.github/workflows/release.yml` | On a `chore(release): X.Y.Z` commit landing on `main`, creates the `vX.Y.Z` tag and matching GitHub Release, or fails loudly if either is missing at job end; both idempotency checks gate independently. |

Most workflows carry a `concurrency:` block keyed on `github.ref` with
`cancel-in-progress: true`; `release.yml` is the exception
(`cancel-in-progress: false`, since cancelling mid-release is worse than
letting it finish). Dependabot tracks the GitHub-Actions ecosystem weekly.

**Not tested.** No worker has run against a live `claude -p` as part of
automated CI. The flag contract in §3 is from CLI documentation, not
observed runs. `claude_p` itself is not unit-tested directly — meaningful
testing requires a stub or live `claude` binary, a separate end-to-end tier
exercised manually.
